2238836.title: Veterinary Assistant Instructor
2238836.description:
## Veterinary Assistant Instructor

The Maritime College
Location: Halifax, Nova Scotia (On-site)
Fall Intake (October)

## Position Summary

The Veterinary Assistant Instructor is responsible for delivering high-quality instruction within the Veterinary Assistant diploma program in accordance with Nova Scotia Private Career Colleges (PCC) regulations and Department of Advanced Education requirements. The instructor ensures students achieve required learning outcomes through engaging instruction, practical skills development, and academic support aligned with current industry standards.

## Key Responsibilities

• Deliver instruction aligned with approved program curriculum and learning outcomes

• Provide theory and practical training relevant to veterinary assistant practice

• Evaluate student performance, assignments, and practical competencies

• Maintain accurate academic records including attendance, grades, and progress reports

• Support students during practicum/OJT preparation and employer communication as required

• Ensure compliance with PCC standards, institutional policies, and regulatory requirements

• Maintain professional currency in veterinary assisting practices and industry standards

• Collaborate with academic administration to support student success and program delivery

Instructor Qualifications & Registration Requirements (PCC Nova Scotia Compliance)

To be eligible for instructor registration with the Nova Scotia Private Career Colleges Division, applicants must meet one or more of the following criteria:

• A bachelor's degree in a related field and at least 1 year of directly related occupational experience; or

• A college diploma/certificate in a related field and at least 2 years of directly related occupational experience; or

• A Bachelor of Education degree or valid Nova Scotia teaching certificate and at least 2 years of directly related occupational experience; or

• Equivalent combination of education and directly related occupational experience acceptable to the Director under PCC regulations

## Additional Requirements:

• Demonstrated current and directly related occupational experience in veterinary assisting, animal health, or veterinary clinical practice specifically with Office procedures and experience with the Veterinary Software, cloud-based software (Neo by IDEXX).

• Strong instructional, communication, and student engagement skills

• Proficiency with MS Office and learning management systems (LMS)

• Commitment to student-centered learning and regulatory compliance

• Ability to work independently in a contract-based instructional environment

## Preferred Assets

• RVT, CVT, or equivalent veterinary clinical certification (if applicable)

• Prior teaching, mentoring, or training experience in a post-secondary or clinical setting

• Experience supervising students in practicum or on-the-job training environments

• We encourage applications from experienced Vet professionals who are passionate about student success, workforce development, and preparing graduates for successful careers in the Vet profession.

## Contract Details

• Daytime classroom delivery

• Fall 2026 program start

• Competitive instructional rates based on qualifications and experience

• Located in downtown Halifax

## What We Are Looking For

We are seeking a professional who:

• Is passionate about sharing Vet knowledge and experience.

• Enjoys mentoring and supporting adult learners.

• Brings real-world Vet expertise into the classroom.

• Demonstrates professionalism, reliability, and strong organizational skills.

• Is committed to student success and educational excellence.

## How to Apply

Interested candidates are invited to submit:

• Cover Letter

• Resume/Curriculum Vitae

• Summary of relevant Vet and instructional experience

Applications will be reviewed as received. We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

The Maritime College is committed to creating an inclusive and accessible learning and working environment and encourages applications from all qualified candidates.

## Details:

The Halifax Regional Centre for Education is accepting applications for the Educational Program Assistant Substitute List for the 2026-2027 school year.

Substitute employees are eligible to accept day-to-day and short term assignments to provide support to schools when permanent employees are away. HRCE has 136 school locations so, depending on where you live, there is potential for steady and frequent substitute work.

Candidates must create an online resume in order to apply. Please ensure your resume is completed in full, including the questionnaire section of the online resume, and outlines any relevant qualifications and experience.

Applicants invited to participate in the hiring process (such as an interview or testing) and who require accommodation, should discuss their request for accommodation when invited to the assessment process

Applicants MUST meet the following criteria :

• High School Completion Certificate or equivalent;

• Valid Emergency First Aid CPR/AED Level C Certificate;

• Experience working with children;

• Physical ability to lift up to 50 pounds and move quickly;

• Trained or Willing to be trained in Toileting/Personal Care

• A related diploma or certificate from a recognized post secondary institution, including a formal practicum placement will be considered an asset.

Rate of Pay is $26.22 per hour.

Incomplete applications will not be accepted.

Should your application be considered, qualified candidates will be contacted by the Halifax Regional Centre for Education for a confidential interview. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Following completion of a successful interview and positive reference checks, candidates will be contacted and required to provide the following before being added to the substitute list:

• Current Vulnerable Sector Check - available from your local Police or RCMP detachment, please print this letter and submit it with your VSS application to the Police/RCMP detachment or online via https://secure.tritoncanada.ca/v/public/landing/HalifaxPoliceService/home ). Must be issued within the past six months. Please wait until after the interview process to apply for a Vulnerable Sector Check.

• Current Child Abuse Registry Search results - issued within six months of employment start date (you will be mailed your CAR results to provide to HRCE as part of your new hire package). CAR applications may be made online https://beta.novascotia.ca/apply-child-abuse-register-search

If you have previously applied within the last three months you do not need to re-apply.

Current sub EPA's are not required to apply to this posting, please complete the sub confirmation on myHRCE. Returning Substitutes & Term Employees wishing to substitute do NOT need to apply to the substitute posting. Confirm your intent to return to active substituting by completing the online Substitute Confirmation Form accessible via myHRCE .

If you have previously been approved for the Educational Program Assistant Substitute List but have been inactive, please contact careers@hrce.ca.

You do NOT have to be a substitute to apply and be considered for term and permanent job postings with HRCE.

## Please refer to job description for further details.

Nova Scotia's Regional Centres for Education and the Conseil scolaire acadien provincial (CSAP) are committed to an inclusive education system that supports the well-being and achievement of every student and is high-quality, culturally and linguistically responsive.

The Halifax Regional Centre for Education (HRCE) is actively working to hire individuals from under-represented groups, particularly people of African Nova Scotian, African Canadian and African ancestry and Mi'kmaw/Indigenous ancestry, to work toward equitable representation within all employee groups. Equitable hiring strengthens the knowledge and expertise in our schools, and supports our public education system in establishing schools as safe, caring, and accessible learning spaces that support all students. 2239096.title: Lending Officer (Member Experience Officer)
2239096.description:
Member Experience Officer (Lending Officer)
New Minas Branch

Valley Credit Union, Nova Scotia, is a full-service financial institution with 7 branch locations, 60 employees, and over $300 Million in assets.
Located in Nova Scotia, within the Beautiful Annapolis Valley.

At Valley Credit Union (Valley CU), you make a real impact on the community every day. Join a team dedicated to exceptional service, doing the right thing, and exceeding member expectations.
Be part of something meaningful!

Reporting to the Branch Experience Leader, the candidate will be responsible for providing superior member service, evaluating authorizing, and recommending approval of members applications for all consumer credit products. They will identify members investment opportunities including the licensing and sale of a full array of mutual funds and selling various deposit products that meet members needs.

## Key Responsibilities (the position):

• Conduct in-person and/or virtual interviews with applicants to obtain personal and financial data to determine lending and/or investment needs.

• Analyze applicant financial status, credit, and property evaluation to determine feasibility of granting loan. Approve or decline loan within approved lending limits prefer to the next higher approving position level with recommendations.

• Compile loan packages and negotiate loan structure with applicants, including rates, terms, and repayment options.

• Prepare documentation for loan renewals, loan payment extensions and substitution of loan securities.

• Manage and grow a small mutual fund investment portfolio; evaluate each situation to provide appropriate advice, and products to meet member needs.

• Provide individual financial counselling and information to members on loans and deposit products, and other services available through the Credit Union. Make referrals to those requiring financial planning advice.

• Analyse current local market and potential trends to plan and develop relationship building activities and educate members on Credit Union product and services offerings.

• Monitor account overdraft activity to ensure accounts operate within limits and ensure appropriate action is taken to minimize losses to the Credit Union.

• Ensure adherence to Credit Union policies and procedures as well as legislative requirements.

• Participate in community events.

• Complete reports and other duties as assigned.

## Successful Candidate will possess the following qualifications:

• Successfully completed a certificate or diploma in Business Administration and have 3-5 years of experience in credit and in a financial institution; or an equivalent combination of training and experience in credit.

• Will have three to five years experience in credit and collections in a financial institution; or an equivalent combination of behaviours, training and experience and a desire to learn.

• Exceptional communication and relationship building skills with the proven ability to exercise sound judgement and discretion.

We're so excited to get to know you!

## Comprehensive Benefits:

• Enjoy peace of mind with our employer's health and dental plan coverage, designed to keep you and your family healthy.

## Retirement Savings:

• Secure your future with our Registered Pension Plan, featuring a generous employer match of up to 6%.

## Employee Perks:

• Enjoy no service fees and exclusively reduced rates on employee loans and mortgages for a more affordable financial journey.

## People Helping People:

• Empowering employees to make a meaningful impact at work through a strong commitment to community and member services.

If you are interested in joining a Team that believes in going the extra mile, please submit your cover letter and resume outlining your qualifications to, Human Resources.

All offers of employment are condition upon the acceptance of an Individual Fidelity Bond Application, which includes a criminal records and credit checks.

Valley Credit Union is an equal opportunity employer, who embraces diversity, all persons are encouraged to apply.

Applications will be accepted until the position is filled, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

• Strong understanding of aviation weather, airport performance, flight plan calculations, fuel planning?and?weight and balance.

• Strong client service mindset with the ability to build effective relationships.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

• Make an Impact: Help shape the future of a growing aviation company.

• Be Part of a Winning Team: Work with talented professionals who value collaboration and excellence.

• Grow Your Career: Access opportunities for personal and professional development.

• We Love What We Do: Passionate about aviation, we craft exceptional experiences with precision and pride.

• We Explore with Intention: We are energized by the pursuit of better. With curiosity and purpose, we seek new ideas, challenge assumptions, and continuously improve how we serve our clients and each other.

• We Are a Team: We are a coordinated and resourceful team that embraces a healthy debate culture, encouraging open dialogue and diverse perspectives.

• We Grow Together: We are committed to continuous growth - for our people and our organization. We invest in learning, embrace challenges as opportunities, and celebrate developing talent from within.

Diversity & Inclusion: We respect and value the diversity of our people. We strive to create an environment where employees can be themselves and where our differences are celebrated. We welcome all applicants and encourage individuals who identify with any of the protected grounds under the human rights legislation to apply to any open role. 2228214.description:
POSITION: Support Services
START DATE: To be determined
TYPE: Casual
RATE: $20.48-$20.80 per hour

## POSITION SCOPE:

The Support Service staff person is accountable to the residents to ensure a high quality of work is maintained while balancing tasks with residents' needs and relationships. They work under the direction of the Neighbourhood Manager, Dietitian, and Support Service Assistant as a member of the multidisciplinary team. The Support Service staff person works in providing an Eden Alternative approach to resident-directed care. The staff person works within the framework, policies and objectives as set out by Tideview Terrace and the Department of Seniors & Long-Term Care.

## QUALIFICATIONS:

Required:

• Completion of High School or GED

• Knowledge of infection control guidelines, food safety and WHMIS

• Knowledge of how to maintain a clean and safe work environment following proper cleaning techniques and OH&S safe work practices, including use of chemicals and equipment

• Demonstrated ability to work closely with the CCAs and as a member of the multidisciplinary team

• Ability to work independently in a household for any extended period of time if necessary with the awareness of human resources available to call upon throughout the building

• Demonstrated commitment in providing an Eden Alternative approach

• The ability to balance tasks with residents' needs

• Actively promotes activities that are meaningful to the residents' needs

• Demonstrated interest in building resident relationships with the importance of providing simple pleasures

• Adaptable, responsible and takes initiative

• Displays positive attitudes and behaviours

• Displays problem solving and decision-making techniques

• Clear written and verbal communication skills and excellent interpersonal skills

• Must be able to perform duties that involve lifting, bending and stretching and meet the overall physical and cognitive demands of the job

• Maintains confidentiality in all aspects of on and off duty

• Outstanding work history inclusive of good attendance, demonstrated availability to work, available to work all shifts, weekends and holidays, and willingness to work all Neighbourhoods and all Support Service areas in current and past employment

Please submit your application via this link: https://jbtmz.me/s/?e=Ff4P3rY3

Tideview Terrace is an EDEN Registered facility dedicated to eliminating the plagues of loneliness, helplessness, and boredom of our residents.

## Creating Homes Where Life is Worth Living http://www.edenalt.org/

The Eden Alternative shows how companionship, the opportunity to give meaningful care to other living things, and the variety and spontaneity that mark an enlivened environment, can succeed where pills and therapies often fail. Places that have adopted the Eden Alternative typically are filled with plants, animals, and are regularly visited by children.

The Eden Alternative is also about changing the culture of long-term care organizations. The departmentalized, task-orientation of the current institutional model has created a culture that is characterized by pessimism, cynicism and stinginess. By moving away from the top-down bureaucratic approach to management and moving decision making closer to the Elders, Edenizing organizations are helping to support a meaningful life for their Elders.

2237966.title: Senior Software Developer
2237966.description:
## Career Opportunity

GeoSpectrum is growing and has a new career opportunity for an experienced Senior Software Developer.

As a Senior Software Developer, you will design and deliver high-quality, scalable solutions for the software applications that support and operate our integrated sonar products. You'll join an established, cross-functional Scrum team to translate technical concepts and align with organizational goals. With a strong technical foundation and commitment to quality, you will mentor others, contribute to best practices and drive continuous improvement across development processes and product quality.

## About Us

GeoSpectrum Technologies was founded in 1994 by friends who wanted to work together and build a collaborative workplace where employees take pride in contributing to cutting?edge technology from concept to delivery. Based in Dartmouth, Nova Scotia, we design and manufacture state?of?the?art underwater acoustic components, transducers, and end?to?end systems for maritime surveillance and exploration. Serving clients across ocean science, defence, and oil and gas industries, we are known for our innovation and for delivering reliable, customized solutions that exceed customer expectations. Over three decades, our core values have shaped a supportive and creative environment that emphasizes employee engagement, technical excellence, and strong customer relationships.

To learn more about who we are and what it's like to work at GeoSpectrum, we invite you to watch our company video by visiting www.geospectrum.ca.

## Responsibilities
Software Development and Delivery

• Design, develop, and implement high-quality software solutions that address complex business and technical challenges.

• Lead the delivery of major projects and initiatives, ensuring solutions are scalable, maintainable, and aligned with organizational objectives.

• Balance short-term delivery goals with long-term product quality, technical sustainability, and operational excellence.

• Apply deep technical expertise to guide architectural, design, and implementation decisions.

• Identify, assess, and proactively manage technical and project risks.

## Ownership & Accountability

• Take full ownership and accountability for the successful delivery of significant features, projects, and technical initiatives.

• Independently gather, analyze, and refine business and technical requirements.

• Ensure work produces measurable business value and meets established quality standards.

• Drive issues to resolution while maintaining a focus on outcomes and customer impact.

## Collaboration & Communication

• Collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams, including product managers, business stakeholders, customers, and external partners.

• Communicate technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

• Build trusted relationships across teams and contribute to a positive, collaborative work environment.

• Facilitate discussions that align technical solutions with business needs and strategic priorities.

## Leadership & Mentorship

2239637.title: Mobile Service Mechanic (Year Round) (Shelburne)
2239637.employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
2239637.description:
Competition # : 49868

Department: Public Works

Location: SHELBURNE

Zone: 32

Type of Employment: Year Round

Union Status: CUPE - NSPG

Closing Date: 23-Sep-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

Under Article 13 of the Collective Agreement between the Nova Scotia Department of Public Works and the Canadian Union of Public Employees, Local 1867, the following opportunity is being posted.

Please quote the competition number and the Zone you are applying for as noted above on your application.

About Us
At the Department of Public Works, we are responsible for building and maintaining a sustainable provincial infrastructure for Nova Scotians. From highways and bridges to government buildings and registration of vehicles, safety and quality of life are top of mind. We support Nova Scotia's 23,000 kilometers of roads and highways, 4,100 bridges, and 9 provincial ferries.

Our Fleet Services Division is pivotal in ensuring the Public Works Fleet is running smoothly; ensuring the safety of our provincial road network.

About Our Opportunity
As the Mobile Service Mechanic, you will have the opportunity to work on our wide variety of equipment that maintains our roads and highways. You will be responsible for maintaining Utility Tractors, Rubber Tire Loaders, Graders, Tandem Trucks and all associated attachments including wings, plows, and sweepers.

Primary Accountabilities
You will not only repair, rebuild and make adjustments to our fleet, but also determine the reasoning for equipment malfunctions. To minimize such occurrences, preventative maintenance is a critical component in this role.
We will ensure you have the right tools to do the job, and there is nothing more important than your safety. You have a clean workspace, and your ideas and input are valued and considered. Your coveralls and other personal protective equipment (PPE) are provided. We also have an annual footwear and tool reimbursement allowance as you must bring your own mechanical tools.

Qualifications and Experience
Some high school and an Inter-Provincial Red Seal Certificate of Qualification in Truck and Transport plus a minimum of five (5) years of diversified mechanical experience.

Upon hire, applicants will be required to successfully complete Nova Scotia Motor Vehicle Inspection (MVI) training as part of their probationary requirements.

A valid Class 5 drivers' license is a condition of employment, and an acceptable driver abstract must be submitted before employment begins. Air Brake endorsement is an asset.

Knowledge and experience of computer-controlled engine diagnostic technology, electrical schematics, dealer purchased engine programs, online service manuals, and safety inspections are considered assets.

Air Conditioning Certification and a Motor Vehicle Inspection license would also be considered assets.

You consistently demonstrate initiative in your role, remaining up to date in changes to equipment, methods and technology within the mechanical field. Strong communication skills are necessary for the times when you will be helping staff diagnose and resolve equipment issues. You must also be able to work effectively with minimal supervision as most of your time will be spent working independently. Professionalism and a high standard for client and customer service is required.

You will be assessed on the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, interview, and reference checks.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
Work is performed in a mechanical repair environment occasioned by noise, smoke and gas fumes and at times adverse weather conditions while operating in a field environment. Considerable standing, lifting, carrying and moving about is a requirement of this position.

Additional Information
There is one (1) opportunity in Shelburne in Zone 32 covering the Bridgewater Fleet Services Area including Zones 25, 28, 30, 32 and 34.

Normal hours of work are 8am - 4:30pm. If equipment breaks down, we will count on you to help things get up and running again. Therefore, you will be on-call outside of your regular work schedule.

This opportunity is for a 52-week Year-Round position – the duties of which are full time and continuous in nature.

You must bring your own mechanical tools.

What We Offer
• Career Development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career.

• Engaging workplace. Our Employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in. We have forward-thinking policies and strategies.

• Countless Career Paths.

Pay Grade: MBS MECH

Salary Range: $38.02 Hourly

The Government of Nova Scotia has an Employment Equity Policy, and we welcome applications from Indigenous People, African Nova Scotians, Persons of African Descent, Racialized Persons, Persons with Disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+ Persons and Women in occupations or positions where they are under-represented. If you are a member of one of these equity groups, you are encouraged to self-identify on your electronic application.

2236693.title: Business Analyst
2236693.description:
Business Analyst

Eastlink

Work Location: 33 Alderney Drive, Dartmouth, NS (On-site, 5 days per week)

Department: Customer Care

Reports To: Director, Customer Service & Accounts Receivable

Employment Status: Full time, 40 hours per week

At Eastlink, our Business Analysts are driven by curiosity, problem-solving, and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact. By transforming data into actionable insights, they help us improve performance and enhance the customer experience to move the business forward.

In this role, you'll support our Customer Care and Accounts Receivable teams by providing analysis that helps leaders understand performance and anticipate future business needs. You'll work across teams to evaluate trends, support planning activities, and recommend improvements that contribute to operational effectiveness and business success.

What You’ll Be Doing

As a Business Analyst, you'll help the business better understand performance, identify opportunities, and make informed decisions. You will:

• Monitor and analyze key operational, customer service, and Accounts Receivable metrics.

• Create and maintain reports, dashboards, and performance scorecards.

• Present findings in a clear way to help teams prioritize actions and achieve results.

• Support forecasting, workforce planning, and sales performance tracking.

• Partner with leaders to evaluate challenges, answer business questions, and recommend solutions.

• Contribute to improvement initiatives that enhance efficiency and support business goals.

What We’re Looking For

We're looking for someone who enjoys working with information, asking thoughtful questions, and finding practical solutions. You’ll succeed in this role if you:

• Are naturally curious and enjoy understanding the story behind the numbers.

• Take ownership of your work and can confidently manage priorities independently.

• Approach challenges with strong analytical and critical-thinking skills.

• Can identify trends, evaluate impacts, and make well-supported recommendations.

• Are comfortable working with both detailed information and the bigger business picture.

• Build strong working relationships and collaborate effectively with different teams.

• Communicate clearly and can adjust information to different audiences.

• Have a strong commitment to accuracy, quality, and continuous learning.

What You’ll Bring

• Three or more years of experience in an analytical, financial, operational, or business support role.

• Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including experience working with large and complex datasets.

• Demonstrated experience gathering, analyzing, and interpreting business data.

• Strong reporting and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate findings effectively.

• Experience working with performance metrics, forecasting, and operational reporting.

• Excellent attention to detail, organizational skills, and time management abilities.

• Experience with business intelligence, analytics, or data visualization tools.

• A results-oriented mindset and a desire to contribute to team and organizational success.

• Post-secondary education in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Economics, Analytics, or a related field, is considered an asset.

• Experience in a customer service, collections, call centre, or telecommunications environment is considered an asset.

About Eastlink

Eastlink is proudly family-owned and headquartered in Halifax, Nova Scotia. After more than 50 years, we’ve grown from a small-town startup into one of Canada’s Best Managed companies without losing our entrepreneurial edge. We move fast. We try new things. We care about doing right by our customers, and we’re not afraid to take a different approach to make that happen.

Why Work with Us

We could say we’re not your typical telecom, but what makes us different is how we operate day to day. At Eastlink, we’re a tight-knit team all working toward common goals. We’re big enough to do meaningful work, but small enough that you can actually make your mark. You won’t get stuck waiting for layers of approval or years of tenure to make an impact! We believe in getting involved, speaking up, and figuring things out together. We’re always listening, learning, and adapting because our customers (and our people) expect us to. And just like we invest in our network, we invest in you, with intention and for the long run.

When you join Eastlink, you'll enjoy:

• Opportunities for internal growth and promotion

• Paid vacation and holidays

• Comprehensive health and dental benefits

• Company pension plan with employer contributions

• Employee discounts on Eastlink products and services

We’re committed to building a workplace where everyone feels they belong. We embrace diversity, inclusion, equity, and accessibility throughout all levels of the organization and encourage members of equity groups to self-identify during the application process. Need an accommodation during the hiring process? We encourage you to reach out and let us know how we can support your participation.

## Senior Accountant

## Stewiacke, NS

## Manager, Finance

## Corporate Services

Location: New Minas, Nova Scotia
Type of Employment: Full Time, Term (up to 1 year)
Union Status: Excluded (non-union)
Competition # COR 26081A
Closing Date: September 17, 2026

## The Opportunity

Reporting to the Director of Finance, the District Finance Manager is accountable for the development, maintenance, implementation, and management of the financial administration activities for budget planning and expenditure control, revenue accounting, operating cost management, financial reporting and analysis, internal controls, procurement and payment oversight, year-end financial activities, and audit requirements for assigned District(s), in accordance with Agency, Departmental and Federal/Provincial policies, regulations, and procedures.

Qualifications

## Must Have

• Bachelor's degree in business administration, Finance, Accounting, or Commerce

• Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation (or legacy designations such as CMA, CGA, or CA)

• 3-5 years of progressive experience in financial management or a similar leadership role, preferably in a unionized environment and overseeing diverse corporate functions

• Working knowledge of Canadian GAAP and PSAB

• Advanced Excel skills (modelling and data analysis)

## The Fine Print

An equivalent combination of training, education and experience may be considered.

This position requires a valid driver's license and access to a reliable vehicle. Some travel within the district is required.

Responsibilities
• Manage the financial administration of the assigned District, including accounts payable, accounts receivable, cash handling, revenue accounting, inventory-related financial processes, budget administration, forecasting, and expenditure control, ensuring financial activities are accurate, timely, and compliant with established policies and procedures

• Lead the preparation, implementation, monitoring, and analysis of annual operating and support the capital budgeting process, including reviewing budgeted and actual expenditures, identifying variances, preparing forecasts, and providing financial advice, reporting, and recommendations to support effective decision making by District management.

Type of Employment: Permanent, Full-Time

Group Affiliation: SMUFU, Rank of Assistant Professor

Applications are invited for a probationary, tenure-track position in Public Policy and Governance at the rank of Assistant Professor, beginning July 1, 2027. Applicants should hold a completed or nearly completed PhD in Political Science or Public Administration and have a demonstrable commitment to the values of equity, diversity, and inclusion as it pertains to service, teaching, and research.

In support of the University's commitment to a diversified professoriate and in accordance with the University Employment Equity and Diversity policy, preference will be given to scholars who identify as Indigenous, Black or racialized. All applicants will be asked to complete and return a mandatory faculty self-identification form as part of the recruitment process. Indigenous applicants are required to document their Indigenous identity in their application and should be aware that the University may verify the community connections of applicants.

We seek highly qualified applicants who can enrich our program with research and teaching excellence in the field of Public Policy and Governance. We are particularly interested in scholars who employ comparative politics methodologies and engage critically with structures of power and inequality. While the area of research expertise for this position is open, consideration will be given to applicants with expertise in one or more of the following areas: 1) Environmental justice and resource management; 2) Politics of representation, party politics and governing; 3) Inter-provincial politics and/or Crown-Indigenous governance in Canada; and 4) Social policy and public healthcare governance. The successful candidate must demonstrate a capacity to teach our existing Public Policy and Public Administration courses, as well as to develop new course offerings in the field of Public Policy and Governance. We also welcome candidates who demonstrate an interest in, or capacity for, providing students with experiential learning opportunities, such as community-engaged learning or practice-based projects connecting political science concepts to real-world contexts.

## Application Details

At Saint Mary's University equity and diversity are integral to excellence and enrich our community. As an institution committed to fostering an environment of inclusion and respect, we welcome applications from women, Indigenous peoples, racialized persons/visible minorities, persons with disabilities, persons of minority sexual orientation or gender identity and others who might contribute to the growth and enrichment of our community. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, preference will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents.

If you require accommodations during the recruitment process, please contact hr@smu.ca. Teaching loads, employee benefits, and salary scales are governed by the Saint Mary's University Collective Agreement: https://www.smufu.ca/. All positions are subject to budgetary approval.

## Applications should consist of the following (7) items merged into ONE file:

1) application form (application form link);

2) cover letter describing how the candidate's areas of teaching and research expertise are relevant to the position;

3) curriculum vitae;

4) complete teaching dossier including teaching philosophy, evidence of teaching effectiveness, and relevant sample syllabi;

5) statement of research interests;

6) one piece of published or ongoing research, as well as links to other papers; and

Candidates may also include a statement detailing career interruptions or other special circumstances relevant to their applications (one page, maximum). This statement is optional.

## Job Title: Junior Project Manager

## Location: Dartmouth, Nova Scotia

## TP-CGC-9383

The Cherubini Group of Companies (Cherubini) is a Dartmouth-based leader in steel fabrication, widely recognized for delivering complex bridges, buildings, and infrastructure projects. As one of Canada's Best Managed Companies, Cherubini brings more than fifty years of expertise, modern fabrication facilities, and an unwavering commitment to quality, innovation, and safety. The organization plays a vital role in transportation, industrial, and renewable energy projects across Atlantic Canada and beyond.

## Role Description

The Junior Project Manager supports the successful delivery of steel fabrication projects from contract award through completion. Working closely with Senior Project Managers and Project Coordinators, this role develops hands-on experience in the technical, financial, and operational aspects of projects. You will gain exposure to contract management, fabrication processes, and client relations, building a strong foundation for a career in project management.

This role is ideal for early-career professionals who are motivated to learn, eager to take on responsibility, and thrive in a collaborative, fast-paced construction and fabrication environment.

## Your responsibilities will include:

Safety - Support Cherubini's Safety Program by promoting safe work practices and contributing to a culture of health and wellbeing in the office, shop, and on project sites. Follow established safety procedures and reinforce safety expectations during project activities.

Finance - Assist with project budgeting, cost tracking, and basic financial reporting under the guidance of a Senior Project Manager. Support the preparation of progress billings, track contract changes, and assist with purchasing requisitions and invoice reviews in accordance with project budgets and authorization limits.

Technical - Develop a working knowledge of project contracts, drawings, and specifications. Assist with the review and coordination of shop drawings and erection plans. Prepare and track requests for information (RFIs), support document control, and help issue work packages to the shop floor.

Leadership - Support customer relationships through professional communication and timely follow-up. Collaborate with Project Managers, Project Coordinators, shop personnel, and site teams to help monitor progress and resolve issues. Participate in shop and site visits to gain hands-on exposure to fabrication and construction activities.

Administration - Assist with project documentation, record keeping, and closeout activities. Support the solicitation and review of supplier and sub-trade quotations. Help coordinate purchasing activities to ensure materials and services align with project requirements, schedules, and budgets.

## Your Qualifications

We are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented early-career professional who is interested in steel fabrication and project management. The successful candidate will bring strong organizational skills, a willingness to learn, and the ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams.

## Your qualifications include:

• 1-3 years of experience in steel fabrication, construction, engineering, or project coordination, or a relevant co-op/internship background. Experience in steel fabrication is strongly preferred.

• Post-secondary degree or diploma in Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Working knowledge of steel fabrication processes, terminology, and shop workflows.

• Basic understanding of construction drawings, specifications, and project documentation.

• Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work collaboratively with internal teams, clients, and suppliers.

• Comfort using project management software and standard office applications to track documents, schedules, and costs.

• Awareness of workplace safety practices and a willingness to learn applicable regulatory requirements, including the Nova Scotia OH&S Act.

• Must be able to work on-site at Cherubini's Dartmouth, Nova Scotia office.

## Why Cherubini?

This is an opportunity to launch and grow your project management career with one of Atlantic Canada's most respected structural steel fabricators. At Cherubini, Junior Project Managers work alongside experienced professionals, gaining hands-on exposure to complex bridge and building projects while developing core project management skills. With modern facilities, a strong safety culture, structured mentorship, and the stability of a Canada's Best Managed Company, Cherubini offers a supportive environment for professional growth and long-term career development.

To express interest in this opportunity, please apply online by clicking "Apply Now" below.

For more information contact Thomas Pugh, Partner, at 902-818-4506 and tpugh@kbrs.ca or Heather Simmons, Consultant at 902-421-2335 and hsimmons@kbrs.ca. If you require accommodation to participate in the recruitment process, please let us know.

Meridia Recruitment Solutions connects leading organizations with top talent by building strong relationships and creating ideal matches with candidates because we are only successful when you are. We appreciate your interest in this opportunity.

To learn more about Meridia Recruitment Solutions, our job opportunities, and career advice we invite you to explore our site and subscribe for career alerts.

Under Article 13 of the Collective Agreement between the Nova Scotia Department of Public Works and the Canadian Union of Public Employees, Local 1867, the following opportunity is being posted.

Please quote the competition number and the Zone you are applying for as noted above on your application.

About Us
Building and maintaining our provincial infrastructure is no small job. We're recruiting for people like you to help our province achieve big things.
The Department of Public Works supports Nova Scotia's 23,000 kilometers of roads and highways, 4,100 bridges, and 9 provincial ferries. There are a lot of exciting developments on the horizon in our Province, and this is your opportunity to get involved with supporting the efficient flow of communications pertaining to summer and winter road construction, snow and ice control activities, and maintenance operations.

About Our Opportunity
As the Baseperson I, you are responsible for the effective flow of communications within a geographic area of the province; ensuring the efficient dispatch of human, material, and equipment resources pertaining to snow and ice control activities and highway maintenance/operations.
You receive and record incoming calls and activities at the local maintenance base and provide general information with regards to Department policies. You provide top notch customer service and aid in resolving customer inquiries and concerns.

Primary Accountabilities
You are responsible for monitoring weather conditions and updating the electronic Road Condition Reporting System (511) on a regular basis. You maintain daily log records of all winter maintenance activities including equipment status, operator hours of work, material payloads from weigh scales, weather conditions, etc. You ensure equipment operators are dispatched to proper plow routes and support them by providing information and monitoring locations through radio contact and AVL technology. You are also a key contact in supporting Supervisor(s) by reporting equipment breakdowns and initiating emergency response procedures as required. General maintenance/organization of the base and light janitorial duties are required at times.
The successful candidate may also be required to perform the duties of other job positions as outlined in Group I of the CUPE Collective Agreement for which they are qualified.

Qualifications and Experience
Some High School and two (2) years of related experience in a dispatch or customer experience environment; an acceptable equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.
You have experience around heavy equipment and construction, including the use of TMR/operational radio systems.
You are familiar with computer applications including Windows, internet, word processing, spreadsheets, data entry and email applications. Knowledge of the geographical area is required to respond effectively to staff and public inquiries, and to respond appropriately in emergency response situations.
Training or certification in the following subject areas are considered assets: SAP, WHMIS, First Aid and CPR, Transportation of Dangerous Goods, and knowledge of department policies and procedures.
You are a self-motivated individual who works independently with minimal supervision and participates fully as an effective team player.
You are accurate in your work, have a mathematical aptitude, and have well developed time management and organizational skills to meet established deadlines and priorities. You have strong communication skills, along with a strong customer service focus.

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
An equivalent combination of training, education and experience will be considered. Equivalencies may include, but are not limited to:

• At least 3 years of related experience.

Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
Work is performed in the office environment of an operation base, which may be occasioned by diesel fumes from equipment, noise and dust. Some outside work is required in varying weather conditions. Shift work is required, including nights and weekends.

Additional Information
There is one (1) opportunity available based out of Zone 6 (Port Hawkesbury).

This opportunity is for a 17-week Winter Works Period position. Applicants who are successful in a Winter Works Period opportunity are always required to be available and guaranteed a minimum ninety (90) hours for every two calendar weeks during the Winter Works Period.

For all employees on the Winter Wage Guarantee, the regular hourly rate will include a winter premium per hour throughout the Winter Works period.

What We Offer
• Career Development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career.

• Engaging workplace. Our Employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in. We have forward-thinking policies and strategies.

• Countless Career Paths.

Location: Truro, Nova Scotia
TP-JDS-9844
Meridia Recruitment is proud to partner with Irving Woodlands in their search for a Woodlands Operations Manager. This is a key leadership role responsible for overseeing harvesting, trucking, and road construction activities within a complex environment supporting regional mill operations.

## Role Description

The Woodlands Operations Manager will take ownership of day-to-day woodlands operations in Nova Scotia, ensuring reliable fibre flow from harvest through to mill delivery. The role leads a small team of supervisors responsible for harvesting and trucking operations and works closely with mill leadership and regional stakeholders to align production with demand.
This is a highly operational, hands-on leadership role in a fast-paced environment supported by a large contractor network and continuous production activity. You will be responsible for production planning, scheduling, KPI tracking, and overall operational performance across multiple harvesting systems and trucking operations.

The successful candidate will work directly with harvesting crews, trucking operators, contractors, and landowners, ensuring safe, efficient, and cost-effective execution of operations. A key focus of the role is strengthening and growing the contractor base to support long-term operational capacity.

## Your Qualifications

• 8+ years of experience in forestry, woodlands operations, construction, transportation/logistics, or a related heavy operational environment

• Bachelor's Degree or College Diploma in a relevant field, such as Forestry, Natural Resources, or a related discipline.

• At least 5 years of supervisory experience, demonstrating effective leadership and people management skills.

2239485.title: Director, Project Delivery
2239485.employer: Build Nova Scotia Healthcare Infrastructure Division
2239485.description:
The Director, Project Delivery is accountable for leading the planning, execution, control, commissioning and operational turnover of assigned infrastructure projects. The position ensures projects are delivered safely, within approved scope, schedule and budget, and in accordance with Build Nova Scotia governance, quality and reporting requirements. The Director, Project Delivery provides day to day leadership to the assigned project delivery team and coordinates internal and external partners to achieve approved project and operational outcomes.

Located in Sydney, NS, this position reports to the Senior Director, Project Delivery and works collaboratively with our healthcare infrastructure division. This is a full-time five (5) year term position.

Qualifications
• As the ideal candidate, you have a post-secondary degree in Engineering, Construction Management or other relevant discipline, along with ten (10) plus years of progressive experience in a leadership role in construction operations or project management, preferably with a good understanding of healthcare or similar scale public infrastructure projects.

• A relevant professional designation or certification, such as P.Eng., Architect, C.E.T. or PMP, is considered an asset. An equivalent combination of education, professional credentials and directly related experience may be considered.

• You are a results-oriented leader with demonstrated success creating alignment across diverse organizations and leading high-performing teams of employees, consultants, specialists and contractors. You have a proven record in project governance, cost and schedule control, procurement, contract administration, risk management, change management, claims resolution and the implementation of effective project delivery practices. You understand the legislation, regulations, codes, standards and commercial considerations applicable to major public-sector construction.

• You can translate complex project information into concise, decision-ready reporting for senior leaders and government partners. You demonstrate sound judgment, strong written and verbal communication, disciplined prioritization and the ability to make timely decisions in a high-pressure, multi-project environment. You build trusted relationships while maintaining clear accountability for performance and results.

Responsibilities
• Leads projects to operational completion by leading both the internal and external parties to desired outcome.

• Develops and maintains project plans including scope, budget, and schedule to ensure project related policy objectives are realized as efficiently as possible.

• Supervises assigned project staff pursuant to Build NS human resource practices and oversees the works of contracted external resources to ensure the cost-effective delivery of work in accordance with the scope of negotiated contracts.

• Monitors project deliverables and provides direction to staff so that deliverables meet defined Build NS Healthcare quality standards.

• Manages project risk by prioritizing potential risk areas and recommending appropriate mitigation strategies to program management.

• Communicates regularly with sponsors and stakeholders to maintain positive working relationships, including participating in and leading federal/provincial/academic scientific, regulatory and technical advisory committees and community based committees and directing the development of Build NS program status reports consistent with organizational reporting processes and standards.

• Manages procurement of project resources according to Build NS procurement policy including contract management of Build NS project suppliers.

• Supports, or in the absence of the Senior Director acts as, spokesperson for the project with media and in public forum

• Provide leadership and direction to ensure the effective management of human and financial resources by setting and evaluating staff performance targets, promoting diversity and a healthy, respectful workplace, demonstrating the leadership competencies, respecting corporate human resources practices, promoting teamwork and individual development.

• Maintain internal communications, monitor revenues and expenditures, adhere to procurement guidelines, acquire goods and services in the most cost effective manner and accurately forecast budget requirements for the fiscal year.

• May perform other related duties as assigned.

2238040.title: Shift Engineer
2238040.description:
## THE ORGANIZATION:

At Events East Group, we proudly manage and operate the Halifax Convention Centre, Scotiabank Centre and Scotiabank Centre Box Office. Our people and our community make us the favoured event destination for our guests. Whether we're attracting large delegations or hosting an elite group of athletes for an international competition, we are a catalyst for new opportunities and connections between Nova Scotia and the world.

## THE POSITION:

Events East Group is now inviting applications for the position of Shift Engineer with our Building Services team.

Reporting to the Chief Engineer, the Shift Engineer is accountable for the operation and maintenance of mechanical systems used to provide Heat, Ventilation, Air Conditioning (HVAC) in the Halifax Convention Centre (HCC) and Scotiabank Centre (SBC). Flexibility is essential, as shift scheduling is based on operational needs.

## THE DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

## Operations:

• Program Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning, and lighting control computer to satisfy the day-to-day event and operational needs, through the Honeywell EBI computerized system.

• Ensure facilities are ready to welcome events and respond promptly to all service requests.

• Work with outside contractors as required.

• Operate and maintain the ice plant to optimal conditions, troubleshooting systems integration as required.

• Operate and maintain boilers and cooling system.

• Complete preventive maintenance work orders as required to include, but not be limited to filtration system changes, greasing and oiling of motors, gears, etc., inspection and adjustment of belts and pulleys, replacement of motor bearings, alignment of shafts, boiler tube cleaning, and related building fixtures and equipment repairs.

• Perform a daily inspection of all mechanical and electrical rooms.

• Repair and maintain kitchen equipment and plumbing components.

• Maintenance of motor driven entrance systems such as roll up doors and sliding doors.

• Respond to emergency issues such as sewer back-ups, leaks or extended power outages.

• Support building maintenance team in the completion of projects.

• Other related duties as assigned.

## Administration:

• Weekly measuring and recording of water treatment chemical levels; add chemicals as required.

• Assist in the development or updating of departmental Standard Operating Procedures.

## Health & Safety:

• Adhere to all departmental standards, guidelines, and procedures to ensure the safety of oneself, team members, and guests.

• Report safety hazards, near misses, and incidents promptly, taking appropriate action to address hazards when safe, and actively participating in the investigation process.

• Wear, use, and ensure the appropriate use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) as required, reporting any violations or damaged PPE within the team or onsite.

## THE PERKS AND BENEFITS:

• 3 weeks of vacation starting

• Sick and personal days

• Employee and Family Assistance Program (EFAP) available through Telus Health
• Discounts

• Free counselling services

• Resources available for personal life needs

• Medical & Dental benefits through Medavie BlueCross as soon as you start!

• Short Term Illness (STI) and Long Term Disability (LTD)

• Participation in the Province of Nova Scotia Public Service Superannuation Plan

• 13 paid holidays or Time in Lieu for working on the holiday

• Paid bereavement leave

• Discounted transit bus pass through SmartTrip

• Discounted gym membership at Goodlife Fitness

## THE PROFESSIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

## Education and Experience:

• 5+ years of experience in physical plant operations

• 1st or 2nd class Refrigeration Plant Operator - Stationary Engineer

• Emergency or Standard First Aid training is an asset

About Us
Nova Scotia is rich in natural resources – including biodiversity, forests, geological resources, provincial parks and the land we manage. The Department of Natural Resources is responsible for the development, management, conservation and protection of forest, mineral, parks and wildlife resources and the administration of the province's Crown land. Together we are working with Nova Scotians to build a better future through sustainable natural resource management as we all benefit from the natural health and wealth of the province.

About Our Opportunity
Working under minimal supervision, you will perform a variety of responsible and complex clerical assignments requiring independent analysis, exercise of judgement, and a detailed knowledge of procedures, rules, acts and regulations. You will perform duties involving more technical clerical tasks.

Primary Accountabilities
Some of your key responsibilities will include:

• Compiling complex reports and drawing data from a variety of sources from within and outside of the work group.

• Preparing reports from statistical and financial information to ensure management receives appropriate information in an accurate and timely manner.

• Maintaining statements, accounts, and database records within established procedures, taking appropriate action to secure or make payment or resolve discrepancies.

• Preparing letters, memoranda, and reports for approval, while following up on pending issues.

• Maintaining filing system of original source documents for audit and other legal or organizational requirements.

• Dealing with internal clients or external sources, such as clients or suppliers, to resolve non-routine queries and problems.

• Have strong communication and interpersonal skills and the ability to present information in a clear, concise manner (both verbally and written).

• Have proficiency in data entry and in the use of a variety of computer applications including: Word, Outlook, Excel, Power Point.

You consistently maintain a professional and courteous disposition and hold a high standard for client and customer service. • Completion of secretarial/office administration training/program.

• Experience and/or training in radio communication.

• Knowledge and experience with the department/government financial processes and policies.

• Familiarity with many department/government programs, regulations, statutes, and procedures.

• Working knowledge of time entry using SAP or a similar program.

We will assess the above qualifications using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

An equivalent combination of training, education and experience will be considered. Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

This is a permanent, full-time position based in GUYSBOROUGH, Nova Scotia.

2225245.title: Managing Director
2225245.description:
Higher Talent Inc. has partnered with Pilot° in their search for a Managing Director reporting to their St. John's, NL office.

## ABOUT THE ROLE:

Reporting to the President & Executive Chair, the Managing Director (MD) is the senior operational and leadership executive responsible for the day-to-day performance, stability, and growth of Pilot°. The MD translates vision into execution, ensuring the agency operates profitably, efficiently, and with strategic clarity. This role is ideal for a seasoned leader who combines business acumen, people leadership, and operational discipline, and who thrives in a creative, client-driven environment. The MD must be a confident, credible leader internally and with senior clients. The Managing Director is central to Pilot's next chapter-ensuring the agency is strong, stable, scalable, and future-ready, while preserving the values, reputation, and creative excellence that define the brand for more than three decades.

## WHO THEY ARE:

Pilot° is a full-service marketing and communications agency with more than 30 years of experience supporting long-standing clients across the private, public and non-profit sectors. Small by design, Pilot° brings together a tight-knit team of uniquely talented and experienced professionals who leverage their individual expertise, networks, and trusted relationships to deliver exceptional value and meaningful results for clients.

With a strong, respected brand and a reputation for quality, collaboration, and impact, Pilot° is known not only for outstanding client work but also for treating employees exceptionally well, offering a supportive culture and highly competitive benefits.

Located in the heart of downtown St. John's, NL, the role offers an inspiring work environment surrounded by historic charm, vibrant streets, and the perfect setting for scenic lunchtime strolls and local shopping.

## DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Agency Leadership & Management
• Provide strong, steady leadership to the leadership team and staff.

• Set clear priorities, expectations, and accountability across the agency.

• Foster a high-performance culture grounded in respect, collaboration, and excellence.

• Act as a trusted partner to the President & Executive Chair in decision-making and execution.

• Operations & Workflow Oversight
• Own the operational rhythm of the agency: resourcing, scheduling, workflow, and delivery.

• Ensure projects and retainers are delivered on time, on budget, and to scope.

• Oversee project management systems, internal workflows, and process improvement.

• Champion consistency and discipline across tools, templates, and reporting (e.g., project management, time tracking, financial reporting).

• Financial Performance & Profitability
• Be accountable for agency financial health, including:
• Revenue targets

• Gross margin

• Utilization and recoverability

• Cost control

• Work closely with finance/accounting to review monthly financials and forecasts.

• Identify risks and opportunities early and take corrective action as needed.

• Ensure pricing, resourcing, and scope decisions support long-term sustainability.

• Client Leadership & Relationship Management
• Provide senior oversight on key client accounts.

• Step in as an escalation point when needed to protect relationships and outcomes.

• Ensure client work aligns with Pilot's strategic and creative standards.

• Support account leaders in managing scope, expectations, and value delivery.

• Business Development & Growth Support
• Support new business development efforts alongside senior leadership.

• Help evaluate opportunities for strategic fit, capacity, and profitability.

• Contribute to proposals, pitches, and pricing strategies as required.

• Strengthen Pilot's reputation as a trusted, high-calibre agency partner.

• People Leadership & Talent Development
• Has direct leadership responsibility for senior operational and client-facing roles.

• Lead, coach, and support the leadership team (Account, Strategy, Creative, Operations).

• Ensure clear role definitions, performance expectations, and development plans.

• Support recruitment, onboarding, and retention of high-quality talent.

• Champion succession planning and leadership development within the agency.

• Governance & Strategic Alignment
• Execute against the strategic direction set by the President & Executive Chair.

• Ensure decisions align with Pilot's values, brand, and long-term vision.

• Prepare briefing materials, operational updates, and performance reporting as required.

• Contribute to strategic planning and annual goal-setting.

## QUALIFICATIONS

• Senior leadership experience in a professional services, agency, consulting, or complex client-service environment.

• Demonstrated success managing teams, budgets, and operational performance.

• Experience working with founders, boards, or executive leadership is an asset.

• Exposure to marketing, communications, creative, or adjacent industries preferred (but not mandatory).

## Skills & Attributes

• Strong operational and financial acumen.

• Excellent people leadership and communication skills.

• Calm, decisive, and credible under pressure.

• Strategic thinker who can also execute at a detailed level.

• High emotional intelligence and sound judgment.

• Comfortable navigating complexity, ambiguity, and competing priorities.

## Mindset

• Values collaboration over ego.

• Comfortable leading in a smaller market with big-market standards.

• Motivated by building something enduring, not just personal advancement.

• Respects creative cultures while bringing structure and discipline.

If you're seeking meaningful, creative and entrepreneurial work in a senior leadership role, apply today with Pilot°.

Rebecca Furey, Recruitment Specialist | rebecca@highertalent.ca

Higher Talent Inc. | www.highertalent.ca

We embrace diversity. Individuals that represent a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills are encouraged to apply. We thank all applicants for their interest, however; only those candidates being considered for an interview will be contacted. Applicants considered for the position will be subject to a background check. This opportunity is only available for candidates legally entitled to work in Canada.

The successful candidate will support the PMO by supporting the optimization and standardization of our project management processes including the corporate project controls and risk management frameworks. They will also act as a key connector across the PMO's functions, ensuring workstream actions are coordinated and tracked through to completion.

The Enterprise Risk & Controls Officer will monitor project planning and delivery efficiency, quality, and adherence to established best practices. This role involves oversight of enterprise risk management, project controls implementation, and governance activities. This is an excellent opportunity for a junior professional to develop their project management skills. This is a full-time five (5) year term position.

## Education

• Post-secondary education (degree or diploma) in business administration, project management or a related field.

• Exposure to the construction industry would be an asset.

## Experience

• 2+ years of experience in project management or a related field.

• Experience working in a PMO or change management environment is an asset.

• Experience using Power BI, Microsoft SharePoint, and other Microsoft tools.

• Experience using Project Management Information Systems is an asset.

• Experience in Public Sector Infrastructure Delivery is an asset.

## Certifications

• A project management designation (e.g. CAPM, PMP) would be an asset.

• Change management certifications (e.g., Prosci) would be an asset.

## Skills

• Excellent communication, organizational, interpersonal skills, and attention to detail.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to think enterprise wide.

• Ability to adapt to change and work under pressure.

• Knowledge of project management methodologies (e.g., Agile, Waterfall).

• Business acumen with an understanding of dealing with project lifecycles, budgets, and schedules.

• Must demonstrate strong initiative and ability to proactively manage work.

• The role of a Enterprise Risk & Controls Officer comes with a high level of autonomy; they must be able to work autonomously upon receiving direction and use professional judgment as to when items/situations require escalation.

Responsibilities

## PMO Leadership

• Understand and continually communicate the PMO's value proposition and ensure alignment with corporate objectives.

• Facilitate communication between the PMO and other departments where appropriate.

• In coordination with the PMO team, contribute to the achievement of goals under the Build NS strategic plan.

• Foster a culture of collaboration, innovation, and professional development within the PMO.

## PMO Support

• Assist in drafting communication materials, presentations, briefing notes and information reports and summaries.

• Assist in the development of executive reporting and performance insights related to organizational risk, controls, and governance.

• Maintain PMO project controls framework and documentation.

• Aid in the refinement and maintenance of PMO standards, methodologies, and best practices.

• Support development of reports on project status, performance, and key performance indicators.

• Coordinate and maintain the corporate Enterprise Risk Management framework, including risk identification, assessment, monitoring, and reporting activities.

• Support enterprise risk management across the organization, including the production of monthly reports on risk management activities.

• Facilitate stakeholder engagement, training, and awareness activities related to risk management and project controls.

• Identify and support implementation and continuous improvement of the Project Controls Framework.

• Assist in the development and maintenance of process maps to visualize and improve business processes.

• Collaborate with stakeholders to implement process changes and monitor their effectiveness.

As an integral part of our Projects team, the Project Manager will play a key role in leading construction initiatives, managing project scope, schedule, and budget, and fostering strong client and subcontractor relationships.

## How you'll spend your day:

• Prepare contracts and negotiate revisions, changes and additions to contractual agreements.

• Select trade subcontractors and plan, schedule and co-ordinate their activities.

• Manage project budgets and submit monthly progress billings.

• Focus on managing the project schedule along with the team through the use of MS Project.

• Ensure projects are built to drawing specifications and the timely completion of all site activities.

• Communicate regularly with Site Managers and all stakeholders.

• Provide leadership to labour force to ensure timely completion of all activities and deliverables.

• Develop and maintain positive relations and with clients, consultants, architects and subcontractors.

## What will help you thrive:

• Post-secondary education in construction management or a related field or equivalent work experience.

• Minimum of 5 years' project management experience with a General Contractor.

VON Canada is a not-for-profit organization providing home and community care services for over 125 years. Focusing on person-centred care, we provide people with the support they need and want, at home and in the community, so they can live healthier, happier lives surrounded by loved ones.

## VON - At the heart of care.

As a Continuing Care Assistant (CCA), you'll use your training to provide person-centred care, support daily living, and help clients stay comfortable and independent in their own homes. You'll travel between clients' homes throughout the day, making every visit matter. Bring your skills to where they're needed most!

## What we offer:

• Work to your full scope of practice

• Ongoing professional development to enhance your skills and knowledge

• Competitive salary and vacation time

• Comprehensive benefits package (health, dental, LTD) and an Employee Assistance Program

• Defined Benefit Pension Plan with company contributions

## What you'll do:

• Provide care to clients in the comfort of their own homes

• Help develop the client's care plan

• Assist with personal care, such as bathing, grooming, and dressing

• Aide with mobility and transfers to ensure safety and comfort

• Plan and prepare nutritious meals and perform light housekeeping duties

• Offer respite care to families, allowing them a much-needed break

• Monitor and maintain a safe home environment

• Collaborate with healthcare teams

VON Canada: Careers that fit your life. Join our team today!

CCA Recognizing Prior Learning (RPL) Program
