United Way Maritimes - with teams located in and serving the regions of Central New Brunswick, Colchester & Cumberland Counties, Halifax, Lunenburg County, Pictou County, Prince Edward Island, and Saint John, Kings & Charlotte - is a for-impact organization that brings donors, volunteers, and partners together to create lasting social change. We believe everyone matters and deserves to belong, be safe, and live a life of their choosing. To help, United Way Maritimes alleviates and reduces local poverty by funding, partnering, convening, and advocating for solutions. United Way Maritimes is part of a federated movement of 50+ United Ways across the country.

The staff at United Way Maritimes takes pride in bringing together people who have a range of experience, talents, and backgrounds. We share a passion for each of the places we call home and bring many different skills and strengths to the work we do. Our community and social change priorities include poverty, social isolation, affordable housing, people experiencing marginalization and vulnerability, and recovery and resilience to environmental, mass casualty and public health emergencies. We provide a supportive and flexible work environment filled with opportunity, balance, and laughter.

The Housing Team is focused on creating and stewarding a sustainable, equitable, and community-driven parallel housing system that provides opportunities unavailable in the general market. This includes supportive housing, affordable rental, and attainable homeownership models that support people exiting homelessness, strengthen housing stability, and address gaps such as missing-middle housing.

Reporting to the Director, Affordable Housing, the Resident Relations Coordinator, working in coordination with the Property Manager and team, plays a dual role in supporting both the successful leasing of rental units, and the sale of attainable homeownership units, while fostering a positive, inclusive, and supportive community for residents. This position is responsible for coordinating intake, leasing processes, and occupancy targets, while also building strong relationships with residents to support housing stability, well-being, community connection, and growing social/economic opportunity.

## The key responsibilities of the role include:

• Leasing & Tenant Coordination: Manage the full tenant leasing lifecycle, including inquiry response, application and waitlist administration, lease preparation, tenant onboarding and move-outs, property showings, compliance with residential tenancy legislation and community standards, potential evictions, and maintenance of accurate occupancy and leasing records.

• Attainable Homeownership Support: Support the administration of affordable homeownership programs by promoting the project, managing prospective buyer inquiries, coordinating application intake and eligibility assessments, maintaining applicant records, facilitating the home sale process with legal stakeholders, and supporting homeowner communications and transitions.

• Resident Relations & Community Building: Foster positive resident relationships and community engagement by serving as a trusted point of contact, supporting a safe and inclusive living environment, encouraging resident participation, and promoting a culture of belonging and mutual respect within housing communities.

• Operations & Documentation: Support effective housing operations by working collaboratively with colleagues across teams, maintaining secure and accurate records, and contributing to reporting for leadership and external stakeholders.

## Qualifications

• Post-secondary education in social services, business administration, property management, or related field (or equivalent experience)

• Experience in leasing, property management, or customer service (or ability to learn quickly)

• Familiarity with Residential Tenancy legislation (or ability to quickly learn).

• Experience working with vulnerable populations and diverse communities.

• Ability to manage sensitive situations with professionalism and empathy.

• Ability to source and manage all supply and contracted service needs.

• Demonstrated ability to prioritize tasks based on comparative importance and urgency.

• Ability to work with minimal supervision and direction.

• Strong verbal and written communication skills and a strong attention to detail.

• Confident communication and active listening skills

• Knowledge of common software such as Microsoft Office and Office 365 and property management software (i.e., Yardi)

• WHIMIS certified.

• Demonstrated enthusiasm for continuous learning relevant to the role.

• Detail oriented and strong problem-solving abilities.

Our ideal candidate is someone whose values and approach align with United Way Maritimes' commitment to strengthening communities, advancing equity, and addressing the root causes of poverty through collaboration and community impact. The ideal candidate is a relationship-focused professional with strong interpersonal, communication, and conflict resolution skills who can build trust with tenants, colleagues, and community partners. They bring a trauma-informed, equity-informed, and tenant-centred perspective to their work, balancing administrative responsibilities with genuine care for people and their unique circumstances. Empathetic, respectful, and inclusive, they approach challenges with sound judgment, professionalism, and appropriate boundaries while remaining calm and solutions-focused in complex situations. They thrive in collaborative, fast-paced environments, are adaptable to change, and demonstrate a high degree of accountability and self-motivation. Most importantly, they share a deep commitment to equity, inclusion, dignity, and community well-being, helping create opportunities for individuals and communities to thrive.

Interested candidates are encouraged to reach out to our Administrative & HR Assistant, Aleks Wilson, for a conversation about the role, salary range, and total compensation package. To contact Aleks, please email jobs@unitedwaymaritimes.ca or phone 902-298-3702.

• Guaranteed 90 hours of pay every two weeks

• $0.95/per hour premium

• Opportunities for overtime

You are responsible for operating snow removal equipment such as snowplows, graders, and loaders. This includes general maintenance of the equipment, pre-and-post trip inspections, and daily logs. You may also be required to perform other work, such as maintaining signs, road surface repairs and traffic control.

Qualifications and Experience
Two years of experience or an acceptable equivalent of education, training, and relevant experience.

Minimum of Class III license with air brake endorsement.

The following is not required but considered helpful:

• A professional driving course from a recognized truck driving training facility

• Knowledge of hydraulic systems and mechanical skills

• Training completed at any accredited heavy/commercial equipment training institute

• Previous experience driving a manual transmission, operating trucks with salt and plow equipment, and/or knowledge of salt spreading systems

You are flexible, self-motivated, and comfortable working in all weather conditions. You are respectful and understand the value of good customer service. You will be working around environmental hazards, various traffic conditions and occasional work performed in a mechanical environment.

Competition # : 49588

Department: Service Nova Scotia

Location: DARTMOUTH

Type of Employment: Permanent

Closing Date: 15-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
At Service Nova Scotia, we impact every citizen, business and municipality in Nova Scotia. Our mandate is to design and deliver programs and services to meet the needs of our clients and the public good through a culture of excellence. Our vision is to be a recognized leader in service and public protection that delivers trusted, accessible, modern programs, and contributes to Nova Scotia as a safe and desirable place to live, work and do business.

The Alcohol, Gaming, Fuel and Tobacco (AGFT) Division of Service Nova Scotia is the regulatory body charged with administering Part II of the Gaming Control Act, parts of the Liquor Control Act, and the Theatres and Amusements Act. The AGFT issues approximately 13,000 licenses annually, and provides in counter service to approximately 3,100 annually.

About Our Opportunity
Reporting to the Director of Investigation and Enforcement, the Senior Gaming Analyst provides operational leadership, technical expertise, and regulatory oversight for gaming investigations, compliance activities, and gaming technology within the province. The Senior Gaming Analyst supports the planning, development, implementation, and ongoing enhancement of policies, procedures, standards, and regulatory frameworks related to lottery schemes and gaming operations.

The Senior Gaming Analyst is responsible for supervising analytical and investigative staff, coordinating complex regulatory and technical activities, and providing subject matter expertise related to gaming systems, gaming integrity, cybersecurity, and emerging technologies. The role contributes to divisional planning, operational priorities, risk management, and strategic decision-making.

Lottery schemes include, but are not limited to, casinos, slot machines, Video Lottery Terminals, online gaming systems, electronic raffle systems, bingo, table games, lotteries, games of chance, and associated hardware, software, networks, and cloud-based technologies that may impact the integrity of gaming within the province.

Primary Accountabilities
Provide leadership for the division's gaming compliance, investigative, and technical oversight programs to ensure lottery schemes within the province operate in accordance with legislation, regulatory standards, and integrity requirements. Support divisional planning, operational priorities, resource allocation, and continuous improvement initiatives related to gaming regulation and enforcement.

Lead, supervise, and mentor staff engaged in regulatory, investigative, analytical, and technical activities. Establish operational priorities, assign work, monitor performance, provide technical direction, support staff development, and ensure consistency in investigative practices, inspections, reporting and regulatory decision-making.

Provide senior expertise and decision-making support related complex gaming investigations, integrity concerns, compliance matters, enforcement actions and emerging regulatory risks.

Lead and develop, implementation and ongoing enhancement of policies, procedures, technical standards and regulatory frameworks related to gaming systems, lottery schemes, investigations, compliance activities, and gaming integrity within the province.

Provide strategic oversight of compliance monitoring, audits, inspections and technical reviews related to casinos, video lottery terminals, online gaming systems, charitable gaming, electronic raffle systems, and other regulated lottery schemes. Identify emerging trends, integrity concerns, and operational risks requiring regulatory response or enhanced oversight.

Develop and maintain collaborative relationships with gaming operators, independent testing laboratories, law enforcement agencies, financial institutions, regulatory organizations, vendors, and other government agencies to support information sharing, regulatory consistency, compliance activities, and investigations involving gaming integrity or emerging technologies.

Prepare and present technical reports, briefing materials, risk assessments, recommendations, and policy analysis for senior management related to gaming integrity, regulatory compliance, operational risks, enforcement matters, and emerging gaming technologies.

Represent the division on internal and external committees, working groups and interjurisdictional initiatives related to gaming regulation, investigations, cybersecurity, compliance monitoring and technical standards.

Qualifications and Experience
To be considered for this opportunity, you are registered as a Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) and hold membership in good standing with Engineers Nova Scotia. You hold a Bachelor of Engineering in addition to a minimum of 6 years of related experience. You are registered with Engineers Nova Scotia as Licensed to Practice.

In addition, you hold extensive experience providing operational leadership, technical expertise, and regulatory oversight for investigations, and compliance activities. You also have experience in planning, developing, implementing, and enhancing policies, procedures, standards, and regulatory frameworks. .

In addition, you demonstrate:

· Strong leadership and communications skills

· Experience supervising staff

· A high degree of judgment and accuracy

· Strong interpersonal and relationship building skills

· Diplomacy, resourcefulness with a focus on clients

· Strong organizational skills and the ability to work with minimum supervision

· A professional attitude at all times.

The following would be considered assets: experience within the regulated areas of Liquor, Gaming, Smoke, Theatres and Amusement, and a good working knowledge of data spreadsheet and work processing software.

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
The primary hours of work will be determined by the employer and the hours of operation of premises and events licensed by the Alcohol Gaming Fuel & Tobacco Division. Will include varied hours of shift work to include evenings, nights and weekends.

Additional Information

## This is a full-time permanent position based in Dartmouth, Nova Scotia.

Note that this competition is being reposted. For any candidates who previously applied, thank you for your interest - note that your application has been received and considered and there is no need to reapply.

Wasoqopa'q First Nation (formerly Acadia First Nation) is governed as a custom band under the provisions of the Indian Act with established bylaws, policies and procedures. The First Nation's electoral system constitutes an election once every five (5) years with positions for one Chief and eight (8) councillors. Chief and Council elect, are the governing body responsible for making decisions for the overall health and well-being of communities, Elders, youth and families.

Wasoqopa'q First Nation is unique in its geographical composition, spread throughout the Southwestern regions of Nova Scotia spanning five counties from Yarmouth to Halifax, encompassing six (6) reserves - Yarmouth, Ponhook, Medway, Wildcat, Gold River, and Hammonds Plains, in both rural and urban settings. To support administration and business operations, Wasoqopa'q First Nation, with supporting staff, provides programs and services within two (2) Health Centres, a Youth Centre, two (2) Community Centres, six (6) administration offices, and six (6) business establishments, including economic development, education, employment, fishing, forestry, health, housing & maintenance, human resources, and social.

## Position Overview and Objective

WFN is currently recruiting for a Community Healing Coordinator, reporting to the Health Director, responsible for fostering culturally safe, strength-based community led initiatives that build capacity, resilience, wellness and crisis readiness, through the facilitation of engagement, coordinating resources, supporting shared learning through a Community of Practice. Working collaboratively with community leadership, Health Director, wellness teams, Elders, Knowledge Keepers, service partners, and the Tajikeim Mental Wellness Team, the Coordinator contributes and advances the Healing Through Loss Framework development work.

## Essential Functions and Duties

• Coordinate access to information, resources, and culturally safe supports during crisis situations

• Promote culturally grounded approaches to grief, loss, traditional healing, resilience, and shared access to Mi'kmaw resources

• Act as a primary point of contact for employees requesting support related to addressing client crisis, grief, loss, trauma, and wellness concerns

• Support WFN in identifying immediate needs, long-term wellness and crisis response goals for healing

• Work with the Healing Through Loss Tajikeim'k Lead to support WFN community engagement, implementation, and evaluation of the Healing Through Loss Framework

• Facilitate engagement sessions, plan meetings, follow-up activities, and implementation plans that reflect community priorities

• Build relationships with wellness teams, community organizations, service providers, and external partners.

• Serve as a liaison between WFN, Tajikeim'k, and regional service providers

• Support knowledge sharing, collaboration, and ongoing Community of Practice meetings focused on crisis response, healing, and mental wellness

• Work with community, and other Community Healing Coordinators in the development of community support mapping work

• Identify training, education, coaching, mentorship, and resource-sharing opportunities that strengthen community wellness and crisis response

• Assist in co-developing culturally relevant tools, resources, and educational materials

• Promote trauma-informed, culturally safe, and community-led practices for loss, grief, crisis, and healing to support front line teams in their wellness

• Maintain records of engagement activities, implementation progress, outcomes, and identifying emerging community needs

• Collect feedback to support continuous improvement and identify service gaps

• Prepare reports, briefing materials, recommendations, and updates for leadership and partners

• Work with the Tajikeim'k Mental Wellness Team to plan, implement, and evaluate workforce wellness initiatives

• Foster peer learning, mentorship, collaboration, and strategies to address vicarious trauma impacts, compassion fatigue, psychological safety and workplace stress

• Work with community partners, Elders, and Knowledge Keepers to strengthen staff wellness, self-care, reflective practice, resilience, and crisis preparedness

• Adhere to all Wasoqopa'q First Nation (WFN) Policies, Procedures and necessary procedures, as required

• Working in a team environment, other duties, training and activities, as required

## Qualifications

• Degree in Social Work, Public Health, Community Development, Indigenous Studies, Mental Health and Addictions, or a related field

• Minimum 2-3 years' experience in community mental wellness, crisis response, Indigenous health, or community development

• Experience working respectfully with Elders, Knowledge Keepers, community members, and partners

• Strong understanding of mental wellness, grief, loss, trauma-informed care, suicide intervention principles, crisis response, and community healing practices

• Knowledge of L'nu culture, traditions, healing practices, and culturally safe service delivery

• Knowledge of the Mi'kmaw language is an asset

• First Aid CPR, WHMIS and OHS are considered an asset

• Criminal Record Check and Vulnerable Sector Check required

• Child Abuse Registry Check required

## Required Abilities, Skills and Competencies

• Strong interpersonal, facilitation, and communication skills

• Ability to collaborate with communities, health teams, educators, service providers, and external partners

• Ability to evaluate programs and activities and adjust approaches to support positive outcomes

• A commitment to fostering, cultivating, and preserving a culture of diversity, equity and inclusion

## Working Conditions

• Office Hours of work occur 8:00 am to 5:00 pm, Monday to Thursday, inclusive, circumstances may arise that require evenings and or weekends, altering weekly work schedules

• Travel may be required to attend meetings

• A valid driver's license is required, as is access to a vehicle

• Occasionally, travel and meetings may fall outside of the regular office hours

• Travel to the other location requires driving for significant periods of time

## Application Requirements

Submit Cover Letter and Resume to resumes@wasoqopaq.ca

**Please quote #COMMUNITYHEALINGCOORDINATOR on your cover letter and indicate your salary expectations for this position.

WFN appreciates the interest of all applicants, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. WFN does not assume candidate expenses related to this recruitment process.

In accordance with the Aboriginal Employment Preference Policy of the Canadian Human Rights Commission, if all qualifications are equal, preference will be given to persons of Aboriginal ancestry and if a Wasoqopa'q First Nation Band member.

Deadline to Apply
Deadline to Apply: OCTOBER 22, 2026

Wasoqopa'q First Nation is committed to fostering a safe workplace that provides an equitable, diverse and inclusive environment, where employees are treated professionally and with dignity and respect. We value the contributions that each person brings, and are committed to ensuring equal opportunity and participation as part of the WFN team.

We are a community. We make a difference.

You must be willing to participate in on-the-job training or training programs that support the development of additional skills.

• You will be accountable for environmental performance as it relates to the environmental management system processes and initiatives.

We understand that experience comes in many forms, and we're dedicated to adding new perspectives to the team. So, if your experience is close to what we've listed above, please consider applying.

Work Conditions and Physical Capabilities

• Must be able to lift a range of 17-66 lbs. from waist to overhead on a minimal to frequent basis

• Able to carry 25-66 lbs. with one or two hands

• Use a range of grip strength from simple to firm grasp with turning motions

• Use upper and whole-body strength to push and pull 20-50 lbs.

• Perform static reaching from shoulder to overhead occasionally and frequently at waist and lateral level

• Perform frequent walking

• Occasionally perform standing, bending, stooping, and forward flexional movements, squatting, twisting while balancing with neck flexion, extension, and rotation movements

• Perform sitting, kneeling, crouching, and crawling on a minimal basis

• Able to discriminate colours through vision and adjust to warm temperatures and confined spaces

Learn more about our culture and values

At the Emera Group of Companies, you'll be part of an inclusive, respectful workplace where everyone is welcomed and supported. Your experience and perspective will help us to safely deliver cleaner, more reliable energy to our customers. Diversity, Equity & Inclusion at Emera

As one of Atlantic Canada's largest publicly traded companies, we are ranked one of Canada's Top 100 Employers, Top Employers for Young People and Top Diversity Employers. Applicants from these equity groups may self-identify through the online application process. We support candidates and employees with access and accommodation needs and encourage you to let us know when you require accommodation.

Recruitment & Promotion Policy

The success of the Emera Company is driven by its people: a strong team with a shared commitment to support the Emera Company mission and values. 2240988.description:
Competition # : 50004

Department: Opportunities and Social Development

Location: TRURO

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: Exclusion - Non Union - NSPG

Closing Date: 07-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
At the Department of Opportunities and Social Development (OSD), we are a large and diverse department providing a broad portfolio of programs and services including Child and Family Wellbeing (CFW), Employment Support Services (ESS), Income Assistance (IA), Supportive Housing and Homelessness, and the Disability Support Program (DSP).

Through our services, we advocate and help vulnerable Nova Scotians be independent, self-reliant, and secure. We work collaboratively across the province with a strong dedicated network of supports and staff, to achieve desired and shared outcomes for all.

About Our Opportunity
Wood Street Campus is a cornerstone in providing specialized treatment services for children in the care of the Minister. We are passionate about supporting children and enhancing their development into successful young people in the community. The experience of fostering positive outcomes for children is very rewarding and requires a highly motivated and energetic individual!

Reporting to the Director, Service Delivery, Child & Youth Caring Services, as the Program Manager, you will be part of the leadership team at Wood Street Campus. You will be accountable for the recruitment, supervision, and leadership of your professional staff, who all work together to provide diagnostic, assessment and treatment services, and programming for children with complex emotional and/or behavioural issues in the care of the Minister.

About You
You are a highly motivated, energetic, and collaborative individual whose passion is positively contributing to experiences for children in care. Through your leadership, you aspire to shape the future of children through your impact on positive outcomes and working in partnership with other organizations to ensure best practices in service delivery. If this is you, this is your team!

Primary Accountabilities
You will oversee the program and human resource management at Wood Street Campus, including assessment, treatment, education, programming, safety and security. Your key responsibilities include:

• Interpreting and administering the Children and Family Service Act

• Collaborating with Clinical Services to ensure the effective delivery of services, youth programming, treatment plans, and case management

• Quality management through monitoring, assessing, and reviewing incidents and treatment plans

• Leading the enhancement and development of various policies, committees and initiatives

• Ensuring the effective management of human resources and supervising a team of employees

Qualifications and Experience
As our Wood Street Campus Program Manager, you have completed your Bachelor's degree, or an acceptable equivalent, combined with several years of progressive experience supervising and/or managing a child and youth caring program. A valid driver's license, ability to travel, and access to a reliable vehicle are required.

Knowledge of human behaviour, trauma-informed care and considerable insight into the motivation of young people to implement change in their lives is required. You also have an understanding of child and youth caring treatment programs and demonstrated knowledge of safety and staffing issues in a child and youth caring treatment setting. Strong organizational skills, experience in program development and a proven ability to provide effective problem-solving techniques in an intense treatment setting are required.

You possess strong leadership abilities and communication skills, both verbal and in writing. You are a collaborative leader and have the ability to foster partnerships and strong working relationships with a variety of professionals and stakeholders. You have a proven ability to provide inspirational leadership, individual and group supervision of staff, as well as direction, guidance, coaching and modelling on effective treatment strategies for children. Proven ability to work as a member of an Interdisciplinary Team, along with the ability to prepare and maintain staff shift schedules, and recruit, motivate and train staff within a 24/7 program are essential. A working knowledge of the Department's policies and procedures, as well as relevant acts and legislation, such as the Children and Family Services Act and the Occupational Health & Safety Act, is a definite asset.

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examinations, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
We recognize equivalent combinations of training, education, and experience, providing opportunities for individuals with diverse backgrounds to contribute their skills and expertise. Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
Wood Street Campus, Secure Treatment operates twenty-four (24) hours a day, seven (7) days per week, with an Interdisciplinary Team who provide stabilization, assessment, and treatment services to children with complex emotional and/or behavioural issues. These children may also demonstrate harmful/aggressive behaviours, and the Nonviolent Crisis Intervention Model (NCI) is utilized to manage these behaviours. You must be physically able to implement NCI techniques.

Your hours of work may include evenings and weekends to ensure the safe and effective operation of the campus.

What We Offer
• Career Development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career

• Engaging workplace: our Employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in; we have forward-thinking policies and strategies

• Countless career paths

2117142.title: Occupational Therapist (OT)
2117142.description:
East Cumberland Lodge is a licensed long-term care facility with 74 beds, providing both Level I and Level II care to its residents. Situated in the scenic coastal village of Pugwash, Nova Scotia, the Lodge offers a supportive environment within a vibrant and close-knit community.

Position Summary

The Occupational Therapist (OT) reports to the Director of Resident Care and plays a critical role in enhancing the quality of life for residents by facilitating their participation in meaningful, everyday activities. The OT will provide comprehensive clinical services including initial and ongoing assessments, referrals, treatment interventions, and participation in care planning with a multidisciplinary team. The role is integral to care conferences and involves planning and implementing strategies for activities of daily living (ADL) assessments, restorative care, and a wide range of therapeutic interventions.

In a progressive long-term care (LTC) setting, the OT's scope will also encompass advanced dementia care through cognitive assessments and behavioral support, adaptive equipment recommendations, mobility and seating assessments, splinting, and feeding, eating, and swallowing interventions. The OT will actively contribute to restraint reduction efforts, falls prevention strategies, and lead in pressure wound management and prevention. As part of the multidisciplinary care team, the OT will work closely with residents, their families, and other healthcare professionals to deliver individualized care plans that optimize resident independence and well-being.

2240245.title: Commercial Leasing Manager
2240245.description:
## Join Us in Creating the Best Places to Live, Shop, Work & Play

As Commercial Leasing Manager, you will be responsible for the strategic leasing, financial performance, tenant relations, and operational oversight of Southwest Properties' commercial portfolio.

We believe in going beyond the necessary to create inspiring environments. To us, a building is so much more than just a collection of walls under a single roof. At Southwest, we believe an innovative, exceptional, thoughtfully designed building can inspire great things to happen inside and around it.

____________________________________________________________________________________

## Here's a Few Reasons Why We Love Where We Work

• Customizable Plan Options for Health & Dental Coverage (Single/Family Plan Options)

• Employee & Family Assistance Program

• 4% Matching GRRSP program

• Annual Health and Wellness Incentives

• Employee Transit Allowance

• Educational Reimbursement for Eligible Employees/Programs

• Social Events

• Charitable Donation Matching Program

• 1 Paid Volunteer Day for an Organization of your Choice

• 2 Personal Days Annually

• Employee Discount Program

• Vacation Purchase Program Options for Eligible Employees

____________________________________________________________________________________

## What Your Day Will Look Like

You will lead all commercial leasing activities, including lease negotiations, tenant retention, portfolio optimization, landlord representation, and commercial property performance. You will work collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders, tenants, property management providers, legal counsel, and service providers to maximize occupancy, revenue, tenant satisfaction, and long-term asset value.

This position will work with members of the senior management team and property operations to support the strategic objectives and performance of the commercial portfolio.

Hours of Work: Full-time day hours Monday to Friday, with occasional evening and after-hours commitments.

Work Location: Southwest Properties Main Office (1315 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS), with regular visits to commercial properties and tenant locations.

____________________________________________________________________________________

## Compensation

In addition to a competitive base salary, the successful candidate will participate in a performance-based commission program tied to commercial leasing activities and the achievement of established leasing objectives. This incentive structure is designed to reward strong performance in areas including business development, tenant acquisition, lease negotiations, and occupancy growth.

____________________________________________________________________________________

## What You'll be Responsible For

## Commercial Leasing & Tenant Relations

• Develop and implement leasing strategies that maximize occupancy, revenue, tenant retention, and long-term portfolio value.

• Lead the negotiation and administration of all commercial leasing transactions, including new lease agreements, licenses, amendments, renewals, extensions, assignments, and terminations.

• Act as the primary point of contact for commercial tenants, ensuring a high standard of customer service and tenant satisfaction.

• Review, negotiate, and finalize leasing documentation in collaboration with legal counsel.

• Proactively prospect for new tenants and leasing opportunities to minimize vacancy and maximize portfolio performance.

• Establish and maintain strong relationships with existing tenants, prospective tenants, brokers, and industry stakeholders.

• Conduct market research and provide subject matter expertise on commercial leasing trends, market conditions, and competitive positioning.

• Provide advice and recommendations regarding tenant mix, tenant quality, customer experience, and overall commercial property performance.

• Manage and resolve conflicts of interest between tenants, landlords, and other stakeholders while maintaining positive business relationships.

• Represent Southwest Properties at industry events, networking functions, and professional associations.

## Portfolio Performance & Financial Management

• Establish leasing and financial performance objectives for commercial properties.

• Set and manage market rents, discounted rents, license fees, operating costs, recoveries, and other lease-related financial terms.

• Oversee rent collection, accounts receivable, arrears management, tenant defaults, and collection processes.

• Monitor budgets and prepare financial and operational reports.

• Analyze leasing performance, occupancy trends, market activity, and revenue opportunities.

• Prepare rent rolls, tenant abstracts, leasing forecasts, budget inputs, and portfolio performance analyses.

## Property Operations & Landlord Representation

• Work collaboratively with the Operations team to ensure commercial properties are maintained and operated to a high standard.

• Act on behalf of the ownership group to provide guidance, support, and oversight to third-party property management providers.

• Manage landlord relationships and ensure landlord obligations under lease agreements are fulfilled.

• Procure, negotiate, and manage third-party vendor contracts.

• Manage external service providers and contractors.

• Monitor tenant compliance with lease obligations and building requirements.

## Strategic Planning & Reporting

• Monitor market conditions, competitor activity, and emerging trends.

• Provide strategic recommendations regarding portfolio performance and asset optimization opportunities.

• Support acquisitions, development projects, redevelopment initiatives, and other strategic projects.

• Collaborate with Finance, Construction & Development, Operations, and Market teams.

• Prepare and present leasing, financial, and operational reports to leadership and committees.

____________________________________________________________________________________

## Your Environment

This role operates across a variety of settings, including the Southwest Properties Main Office, on-site property locations, and tenant-facing environments. Southwest Properties Main Office is located at 1315 Lower Water Street, Halifax, Nova Scotia.

____________________________________________________________________________________

## What Will Help You Succeed

You don't require all the listed qualifications to add incredible value to our team. If you feel energized thinking about what you could accomplish at Southwest, we would love to hear from you.

Our ideal candidate has a Bachelor's Degree in Business Administration, Commerce, Real Estate, Finance, Property Management, or a related discipline, combined with 5-7 years of progressively senior experience in commercial leasing, real estate asset management, commercial property management, or a comparable field.

• CPM, RPA, CCIM, or equivalent designations are considered an asset.

• Ability to build strong, professional relationships with internal and external stakeholders.

• Professional written and verbal communication.

• Highly organized, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines.

• Proactive and solutions-oriented mindset.

• Strong negotiation and influencing skills.

• Customer-focused approach with a commitment to service excellence.

Position requires: Criminal Records Check Completion.

____________________________________________________________________________________

## People are at the Heart of Everything We Do

Southwest Properties is committed to attracting and retaining a diverse team, who values your experiences, perspectives, and unique identity. We are committed to creating and maintaining an environment that is inclusive, equitable, and welcoming.

____________________________________________________________________________________

Thank you for your interest in Southwest Properties. Those chosen for an interview will be contacted.

We are a team of individuals who get joy from bringing joy to others.

2239631.description:
## Behaviour Specialist – Full-Time Permanent Position

Location: Central Office Location – Bedford Hwy (flexibility to be located elsewhere in Nova Scotia)

Hours: 35 hours per work week (8:30AM – 4:30PM)

## What we offer:

## NSECDIS offers a competitive compensation package including:

As well as:

• $86,565/annually or $47.56/hour

• 105 hours Vacation, 105 hours Sick time

• Group Health Benefits Plan (including Extended Healthcare, Dental and Wellness services)

• Contributory Defined Benefits Pension Plan

• Paid holidays (provincial & federal) as well as a paid winter holiday shutdown

• Continuous Professional Development

• A chance to support families and educators in your community

## Who we are:

Nova Scotia Early Childhood Development Intervention Services (NSECDIS) provides province-wide services for families of children, birth to school entry, who may be at risk for, or with a diagnosis of, developmental delay. Our goal to promote improved developmental outcomes for children through consultation, coaching, information sharing, support and services designed to meet the individual needs of the child and family. Services emphasize the enhancement of skills and ability through planned interactions to promote child development and family capacity and are delivered in the child's home and community-based programs.

We also facilitate Early Learning and Child Care program and Early Childhood Educator capacity building through coaching within Child-care and Pre-primary programs with use of The Pyramid Model for Supporting Social Emotional Competence in Infants and Young Children.

As an employer we offer a supportive environment where staff are encouraged to follow their passion within our field. We believe in continuous Professional Development and growth. Our teams are comprised of compassionate, trained professionals who enjoy serving their communities.

The Behaviour Specialist for NSECDIS is responsible for collaboratively shaping and leading the strategic planning, consultative support and professional development related to the building of NSECDIS staff and their associated families and programs, capacity to support young children's social emotional development and self-regulation. This role will work collaboratively with Developmental Interventionists, Inclusion Coaches, as well as regional and provincial NSECDIS leadership to support core training, program planning, and staff capacity building through coaching.

This role will report to the Executive Director and will be collaboratively supported by the Learning and Development Specialist.

## Duties Include:

• Provide specialized expertise in the development, implementation, and evaluation of positive behaviour support plans and programming for young children (birth to school entry).

• Collaborate with NSECDIS teams and community partners to support children's social-emotional development and self-regulation across home and community settings.

• Plan, develop, and deliver professional learning opportunities for NSECDIS staff, families, and early childhood professionals.

• Provide targeted support to Intervention and Pyramid Model teams for children with developmental delays, disabilities, trauma histories, and behavioural or emotional challenges.

• Offer consultation, problem-solving support, and coaching to Developmental Interventionists and Inclusion Coaches related to individual case files using evidence-based practices.

• Model and coach functional assessment, program planning, and behaviour support strategies.

• Collaborate with staff, families, and community partners in the development, implementation, and review of individualized program plans.

• Participate in positive behaviour support planning meetings, providing guidance and modeling best practices as needed.

• Support the interpretation of assessments and reports, and promote effective use of evidence-based tools, resources, and strategies.

• Review and evaluate intervention effectiveness and recommend adjustments as needed.

• Guide staff in collecting and analyzing behavioural data to identify triggers and understand the function of behaviour.

• Support staff in connecting families with appropriate community, mental health, and other external resources.

• Maintain knowledge of NSECDIS policies, procedures, and guidelines.

• Uphold confidentiality in all aspects of practice.

• Promote inclusive, culturally responsive, and trauma-informed practices.

• Stay current with emerging research, trends, and best practices in behaviour support.

• Participate in quality improvement and innovation initiatives.

• Perform other duties as assigned.

## Qualifications & Skills:

• Master Degree in Special Education, Diverse Learners; Psychology (Clinical or School); or Human Communication Disorders;
• Candidates with a Masters Degree in Special Education or Diverse Learners must have BCBA Certification in good standing with the Behaviour Analyst Certification Board OR completion of a Masters level program in Applied Behavioural Analysis and currently undergoing supervision to obtain BCBA certification;

• Candidates with a Masters Degree in Psychology (Clinical or School) must be registered with NSBEP (Registered Psychologist or Candidate Register Psychologist);

• Candidates with a Masters Degree in Human Communications Disorders must be registered with the Nova Scotia College of Audiologists and Speech Language Pathologists and must have BCBA Certification in good standing with the Behaviour Analyst Certification Board OR completion of a Masters level program in Applied Behavioural Analysis and currently undergoing supervision to obtain BCBA certification;

• Minimum of three years of successful practice;

• Relevant training and/or experience with implementing evidence-based interventions with young children with developmental delays or disorders;

• Experience and/or training in functional behaviour assessment procedures

• Experience developing and delivering effective training using a variety of formats (e.g., in-person, online, recorded)

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills

• Demonstrated effective relationship building skills

• Demonstrated ability to work within an inter-professional collaborative practice framework; and ability to work independently with minimal supervision

• Strong project management skills with an ability to manage multiple priorities

• Proficiency with technology including data management systems and Microsoft office suite

Please apply using our Applicant Tracking System though the link provided via this website with a Resume & Cover Letter

2240328.title: Saltwater Aquaculture Worker
2240328.description:
Kelly Cove Salmon Ltd., a division of Cooke Aquaculture Inc., a dynamic and growing east coast family company, with Platinum Member status in the Canada's Best Managed Companies Program, is offering a unique opportunity for highly motivated individuals to join the Company's Saltwater Team in Shelburne, NS and surrounding areas.

Cooke is a global seafood company with operations in North America, Europe, and South America. Our company's success is driven by our dynamic, highly-skilled and innovative management team, supported by dedicated employees who live in coastal communities and contribute to the local area's economy and sense of community.

## The Role

As a result of our robust growth, we are hiring Saltwater Aquaculture Workers to join our team. The ideal candidates will be self-motivated team players willing to work flexible work hours and schedules.

The primary duties include, but are not limited to:

• Monitoring and operating the feeding systems.

• Report any observed irregularities in stocks.

• Grid installation and inspection/repair.

• Marine cage and net installation and removal.

• Operate, maintain, and clean aquaculture equipment and enclosures.

• General site maintenance including net washing.

• Operation of boats for aquaculture operations.

• Grade and weigh aquaculture stock.

• Harvest assistance as required.

*Applicants must hold or be willing to obtain a Marine Emergency Duties (MED) certificate .

This is a labour-intensive position, requires standing for long periods of time; applicants must be comfortable working in outside weather conditions on both aquaculture sites and aboard maintenance vessels.

Experience within the aquaculture field would be considered an asset but not required as on the job training is provided.

Join our team and enjoy the benefits of full-time year-round employment with competitive rates and a comprehensive benefits package tailored to support your well-being and career growth.

## Benefits Package

• Health Benefits: Includes coverage for dental, vision, and extended medical care.

• Insurance: Life and disability insurance provided for financial security.

• Support Services: Access to an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

• Financial Planning: Opportunity for RRSP matching to support your retirement savings.

• Wellness: Wellness programs.

• Career Development: Professional growth opportunities and avenues for advancement.

• Perks: Employee discounts on company products or services.

*As per company policy, a criminal background check is required.

## The Opportunity

The role description is just one part of the story. This is an opportunity to grow, to work within the parameters of the role but to reach your fullest potential. 2239111.title: Talent Acquisition Partner
2239111.description:
Work Location: 6080 Young Street, Halifax, NS (On-site, 5 days per week)

Department: People & Culture

Reports To: Senior Manager, Talent Management

Employment Status: Full time, 40 hours per week

At Eastlink, our people are at the heart of everything we do. As part of our People & Culture team, you'll help shape the future of our organization by attracting and connecting great talent with meaningful career opportunities.

As a Talent Acquisition Partner, you'll do more than fill roles. You'll be a trusted advisor to leaders, an advocate for candidates, and one of the first people prospective team members meet when exploring a career at Eastlink. Every conversation is an opportunity to share our story, showcase our culture, and help candidates envision their future with us. If you're passionate about recruitment, enjoy building relationships, and thrive on connecting people with opportunities where they can succeed, this is a role where you can make a real impact.

What You’ll Be Doing

As a Talent Acquisition Partner, you will:

• Deliver an exceptional recruitment experience that reflects Eastlink's culture and values.

• Lead the full recruitment lifecycle from intake and sourcing through to offer and hire.

• Partner with leaders to understand their talent needs and develop effective hiring strategies.

• Provide guidance and coaching throughout the recruitment and selection process.

• Build strong talent pipelines through sourcing, networking, community partnerships, and career events.

• Identify creative approaches to attract top talent in competitive markets.

• Collaborate with People & Culture partners to support key people initiatives and business goals.

What We’re Looking For

We're looking for someone who is energized by helping people find meaningful career opportunities and who enjoys building strong partnerships across the business. You'll succeed in this role if you:

• Build strong relationships and earn trust through collaboration and accountability.

• Proactively communicate progress, market insights, and recommendations so leaders feel supported and informed throughout the hiring process.

• Enjoy finding creative solutions and thinking beyond traditional recruiting methods.

• Stay organized and manage competing priorities with confidence.

• Balance attention to detail with a focus on the bigger picture.

• Take pride in representing Eastlink and creating a welcoming experience for every candidate.

You’ll Also Bring

• A post-secondary degree or diploma in Business, Human Resources, or a related field.

• Two or more years of recruitment experience in an in-house environment.

• Experience sourcing and attracting talent through a variety of channels.

• Strong relationship-building, communication, and interviewing skills.

• Experience with HRIS or applicant tracking systems; Dayforce experience is considered an asset.

About Eastlink

Eastlink is proudly family-owned and headquartered in Halifax, Nova Scotia. After more than 50 years, we’ve grown from a small-town startup into one of Canada’s Best Managed companies without losing our entrepreneurial edge. We move fast. We try new things. We care about doing right by our customers, and we’re not afraid to take a different approach to make that happen.

Why Work with Us

We could say we’re not your typical telecom, but what makes us different is how we operate day to day. At Eastlink, we’re a tight-knit team all working toward common goals. We’re big enough to do meaningful work, but small enough that you can actually make your mark. You won’t get stuck waiting for layers of approval or years of tenure to make an impact! We believe in getting involved, speaking up, and figuring things out together. We’re always listening, learning, and adapting because our customers (and our people) expect us to. And just like we invest in our network, we invest in you, with intention and for the long run.

When you join Eastlink, you'll enjoy:

• Opportunities for internal growth and promotion

• Paid vacation and holidays

• Comprehensive health and dental benefits

• Company pension plan with employer contributions

• Employee discounts on Eastlink products and services

We’re committed to building a workplace where everyone feels they belong. We embrace diversity, inclusion, equity, and accessibility throughout all levels of the organization and encourage members of equity groups to self-identify during the application process. Need an accommodation during the hiring process? We encourage you to reach out and let us know how we can support your participation.

2237677.title: Technical Project Manager
2237677.description:
## We're Hiring!

CarteNav Solutions, a PAL company, is an international leader in situational awareness solutions for the maritime, land, and air environments. We deliver leading-edge software solutions that support mission-critical operations for government and defense customers. We're looking for a Technical Project Manager to join our growing team—someone who can move fluently between the discipline of formal program management and the rhythm of agile software delivery.

As a Technical Project Manager, you'll be the bridge between our software engineering teams and our customers, translating technical progress into business confidence and business requirements into technical plans. You'll own the planning, coordination, and execution of complex software delivery projects. You'll also influence delivery best practices and help shape the future of how we scale and operate.

## What You'll Do

• Own end-to-end delivery of complex, technical projects from kickoff through deployment and acceptance

• Develop project plans, risks, budgets, and deliverables, while managing the formal schedules, budgets, and reporting requirements

• Translate customer and contractual requirements into clear technical specifications and actionable plans that engineering teams can execute against

• Ensure deliverables meet contractual, security, and compliance requirements, including export control, documentation, and acceptance testing obligations

• Represent the project delivery function in leadership planning and customer engagements

• Serve as the primary point of contact as a trusted advisor to customers and senior stakeholders

• Coordinate efforts across engineering, QA, product, and support teams to keep priorities aligned and dependencies visible

• Drive continuous improvement of delivery practices, tooling, and templates across the project management function

• Support proposal development and project estimation for new opportunities

## What We're Looking For

• 7+ years of experience in project management, with meaningful time spent managing software delivery

• Experience managing projects for government, defense, or other highly regulated customers

• Technical fluency — comfortable in conversations about architecture, integrations, and the software development lifecycle, even without a hands-on engineering background

• Proven ability to manage large-scale software initiatives, within a multi-stakeholder technical environment

• Proficiency with project management delivery tools like Jira, Microsoft Planner, Azure DevOps, or similar

• Clear, precise written and verbal communication, including formal status reporting and documentation

• Eligible to obtain and maintain a government security clearance, or ability to meet applicable export control and citizenship requirements

• PMP, Agile, or similar certifications are preferred

## Nice to Have

• Experience with defense, aerospace, or public sector procurement processes

• Familiarity with regulatory or safety-critical software standards

• Experience mentoring or leading other project managers

## Why Join Us?

• Work on software that supports real, high-stakes missions for government and defense customers

• Sit at the intersection of technical delivery and customer strategy, with real influence over how projects get built

• Join a global team that values clarity, ownership, and getting the details right

• Advance your career in a forward-thinking environment

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who is passionate about creating great software, cares about client engagements, and takes pride in successful project delivery. If you're an experienced project leader ready to help deliver mission-critical software and shape how we work—let's talk.

## What We Offer:

• Comprehensive health benefits including medical, dental, vision, and life insurance

• Pension Plan with employer matching

• Employee Stock Purchase Plan

• Tuition Assistance Program

• Personal travel privileges with PAL and interline agreements with multiple airlines

• Employee and Family Assistance Program

• Industry discounts (hotels, rental cars, etc.)

PAL Aerospace is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment that celebrates and encourages diversity, equity, and inclusion whereby individuals are recognized, supported, and respected. Candidates of all backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

Only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. Thank you.

## #PALAerospace

## Developmental Interventionist – Part time (21 hours, 3 days per week), Permanent

Location: 5-28 Aberdean Dr., Kentville NS Hours: 21 hours, 3 days per week (8:30AM – 4:30PM)

## What we offer:

## NSECDIS offers a competitive compensation package including:

• Salary: $34.20 per hour ($62,244.00 per year) with annual adjustments up to 8 years

• 105 hours Vacation, 105 hours Sick time

• Group Health Benefits Plan (including Extended Healthcare, Dental and Wellness services)

• Contributory Defined Benefits Pension Plan

As well as:

## Who we are:

Nova Scotia Early Childhood Development Intervention Services (NSECDIS) provides province-wide services for families of children, birth to school entry, who may be at risk for, or with a diagnosis of, developmental delay. Our goal to promote improved developmental outcomes for children through consultation, coaching, information sharing, support and services designed to meet the individual needs of the child and family. Services emphasize the enhancement of skills and ability through planned interactions to promote child development and family capacity and are delivered in the child's home and community-based programs.

We also facilitate Early Learning and Child Care program and Early Childhood Educator capacity building through coaching within child care and Pre-primary programs with use of The Pyramid Model for Supporting Social Emotional Competence in Infants and Young Children.

As an employer we offer a supportive environment where staff are encouraged to follow their passion within our field. We believe in continuous Professional Development and growth. Our teams are comprised of compassionate trained professionals who enjoy serving their communities.

## Duties include:

• In home coaching with families and community consultations to establish and implement family led meaningful goals and strategies

• Supporting capacity building in families and educators by providing participatory experiences and opportunities that strengthen knowledge and skills and promote a positive sense of competence and confidence

• Connect families with community partners/resources and support navigation within service systems

• Maintaining positive relationships and continual communication with families and their support teams to facilitate joint programming

• Tracking of child and family progress and goals through timely and accurate documentation of all caseload observations and data within our internal database system and support files

• Other related duties as required

## Qualifications & Skills:

• A minimum Bachelor's Degree in Early Childhood Development or related field

• Experience working with children from birth to school age with developmental disabilities and their families is essential

• Strong planning, organizational and time management abilities are required

• Excellent communication (oral & written)

• Strong interpersonal skills

• Adaptable and dependable

• Valid driver's license and access to own reliable vehicle is required daily

2234814.title: System Support Technician
2234814.description:
Position Type:
Permanent
*

## Closing date:

Emergency Medical Care Inc. (EMC) is a wholly owned subsidiary of Medavie Health Services (MHS) that manages and operates ground ambulance, air medical transport and the medical communications operations in Nova Scotia through a performance-based contract with the provincial government's Emergency Health Services (EHS) Operations division and the Department of Health and Wellness. As well, EMC operates TeleHealth/811 medical communications for Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island for the Department of Health.

We access all communities in Nova Scotia in a timely and efficient manner with our fleet of more than 180 ambulances and support vehicles operating out of 60+ stations. We respond to 165,000+ calls annually across the province, which are actively managed through the EHS Operations Medical Communications Centre, the hub of all emergency (911) and non-emergency (hospital transfers) medical calls.

The EHS Operations LifeFlight program provides even greater accessibility by responding to patients on scene or through inter-facility transports by our critical care team via helicopter, fixed wing, or ground ambulance.

In addition, paramedics in Nova Scotia participate in various programs both urban and rural such as community-based paramedic programs, collaborative emergency centres, and emergency preparedness and special operations, to name a few.

There are lots of opportunities waiting for you in Nova Scotia. Apply now to learn more about our service and available positions.

## Nature and Scope:

Reporting to the Manager, Fleet & Physical Resources, the System Support Technician (SST) is a key part of the EMC team that provides a well maintained, safe, effective and efficient fleet of vehicles; designed to give optimal customer service and patient care.

## DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

The position entails, but is not limited to the following:

• Completes light mechanical repairs as directed.

• Completes required Ambulance Base Station facilities repairs which includes but not limited to; Base Station cleaning, painting, yard maintenance, lighting repairs and general maintenance requirements.

• Ensures all system vehicles based out of the Fleet Centre are stocked and in a ready state in accordance to EMC and EHS Fleet Policy and Procedures at all times.

• Conducts all cleaning required to the vehicle interior or exterior in accordance with proper decontamination policies.

• Conducts reasonable on-going cleanliness the fleet centre during scheduled shift and at least once a week fleet center deep clean.

• Performs other such similar, comparable or related duties as may be required or assigned.

• Will require an element of Fleet on-call duty as per schedule

## QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS:

• Minimum Grade 12

• WHMIS

• Class 4 License required

• First Aid an asset

• Good dexterity, good general health, good eyesight and physical coordination.

• Effective oral and written communication skills.

• Displays good decision-making skills and takes initiative

Our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative of the citizens we serve. We are committed to building an inclusive team that represents a variety of backgrounds, cultures, races, perspectives and skills. We encourage applications from all qualified candidates including women, persons of any sexual orientations and gender identities and/or expressions, Indigenous persons, African Canadians, other racialized groups, persons with disabilities. Candidates who identify as being from any of these groups are encouraged to voluntarily self-identify.

2239075.title: 2627-178 - Faculty, Aviation (AME-M,E,S) - Ivany Campus
2239075.description:
## Faculty - Aviation

## Education

## Ivany Campus

## Dartmouth, Nova Scotia

## Applied Innovation and Technology

Three (3) Continuing Full-time Positions (one position in Mechanical, one position in Structures and one position in Avionics): Commencing approximately October 26, 2026

## Application deadline is 11:59PM, October 10, 2026

## Competition No. 2627-178

From Industry Expert to Instructor - Help Train the Next Generation of Skilled Aircraft Maintenance Engineers

Are you an experienced Aircraft Maintenance Engineer (AME) looking for a new challenge; one that keeps you connected to the work you love, while offering more balance, stability, and long-term security?

At Nova Scotia Community College, you can take the knowledge and experience you've built in industry and use it to mentor the next generation of AMEs, all while enjoying predictable hours, excellent benefits, and a career that's easier on the body.

**Secondment opportunities may be available, subject to approval from your current employer. This can be an excellent option for those interested in gaining teaching experience or exploring a new professional pathway while maintaining their existing employment and salary. If you are interested in exploring secondment options, please contact Jaclynn at jaclynn.kelly@nscc.ca.**

## Why Make the Move to Teaching?

This is an opportunity to stay hands-on in the trade without the physical demands, long shifts, emergency callouts, or unpredictable schedules that often come with industry work.

As a Faculty member with NSCC, you'll enjoy:

• The opportunity to share your industry expertise and help shape the next generation of AMEs

• Meaningful work that makes a lasting impact on students, industry, and communities

• A supportive team environment focused on collaboration, mentorship, and continuous learning

• The ability to stay connected to your trade while transitioning into teaching

• Predictable work hours that support work-life balance

• A stable and rewarding career in education with opportunities for professional growth

• Support and training to help transition successfully into teaching

Whether you're looking to slow down physically, spend more time with family, take your work experience in a new direction, or transition into a rewarding second phase of your career, this role offers the chance to do all of that while remaining deeply connected to the AME community.

Qualifications
We're seeking experienced tradespeople who are passionate about the industry and interested in helping others succeed.

Ideal candidates will have:

• Valid Transport Canada Aircraft Maintenance Engineers (AME) License: M1 or M2 or equivalent, AME-E and/or AME-S.

• A minimum of five years (full-time equivalent) of recent occupational experience.

• Clear understanding of Manufacturer's and Regulatory Documentation (CARS 566), including SRM, Service Bulletins, Engineering Drawings, etc.

• Comfortable using computer applications such as the Microsoft Office Suite, including Outlook

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

• A commitment to safety, mentorship, and lifelong learning

Previous teaching experience or related experience in the delivery of educational program or training adults would be an asset, but not required. If you've coached apprentices, trained coworkers, or shared your knowledge on the shop floor, you already have valuable experience to build on.

NOTE: Two years of your training will be counted towards the educational requirements and cannot be included as part of your occupational experience.

## Compensation & Benefits

The salary scale for NSCC Faculty is based on steps that range from $81,760.18 - $104,267.58 annually.

In addition to salary, NSCC offers:

• A defined benefit pension plan to support long-term financial security

• Comprehensive health and dental coverage, including vision, paramedical services, life insurance, Employee Family Assistance Program (EFAP), and more

• Up to 45+ days of paid vacation and recognized holidays, including paid time off between Christmas and New Year's

• Professional development and training opportunities to support ongoing learning and career growth

## Make an Impact

The aviation industry need experienced professionals willing to pass on their knowledge. This is your opportunity to shape the future of industry while building a healthier, more balanced future for yourself.

If you're ready to bring your experience into the classroom and help develop the next generation of AMEs, we'd love to hear from you.

Responsibilities
As part of the Applied Innovation & Technology faculty team in the Aircraft Maintenance Technology/Aircraft Maintenance Technician programs, you will:

• Deliver theoretical and hands on practical shop training along with classroom instruction

• Share real-life industry knowledge and troubleshooting experience

• Mentor and support students entering the trade

• Help students build the skills employers are looking for

• Promote and ensure health and safety practices and procedures are consistently followed in classrooms, shops, and labs

• Work collaboratively with fellow instructors and industry partners

• Stay current with evolving technology and industry practices

• Participate in student advising, curriculum development, program promotion, committee work, and work placement support

• You may also coordinate the aviation hangar and lab operations by setting up/taking down and maintaining the organization of the hangar and labs and its materials, equipment, and inventory

This role combines shop instruction with modern teaching tools and blended learning approaches, including in-class, online, and off-site instruction, as well as occasional evening and weekend sessions.

As a condition of employment, you are required to provide proof of a valid AME licence, prior to your start date.

As a condition of employment, Faculty at NSCC must complete a part-time adult education program delivered by NSCC. This adult education program is a significant investment on the part of NSCC in the learning and development of new employees. To achieve regular status, all probationary, full or part-time Faculty of the College must successfully complete the program within their probationary period. Term full-time Faculty whose term appointment is twelve or more months are also required to participate in this program.

Candidates selected for interviews will be expected to provide at least three recent occupational references. The successful candidate will be expected to provide official transcripts to show proof of academic achievements.

NSCC is committed to the full inclusion of all applicants. As part of this commitment, NSCC will ensure that applicants are provided reasonable accommodations, as required. If accommodation is needed to participate in the job application process, please contact Jaclynn Kelly, HR & Talent Consultant at jaclynn.kelly@nscc.ca. Our Employee Workplace Accommodation Policy can be found here: Employee Workplace Accommodations Policy | NSCC

Unfortunately, we cannot accept late or paper applications.

2240777.title: Child Protection Social Worker 1-2 (Multiple Positions)
2240777.employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
2240777.description:
Competition # : 49977

Department: Opportunities and Social Development

Location: YARMOUTH

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: NSGEU - NSPG

Closing Date: 05-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
At the Department of Opportunities and Social Development (OSD), we are a large and diverse department providing a broad portfolio of programs and services including Child and Family Wellbeing (CFW), Employment Support Services(ESS), Income Assistance (IA), Homelessness and Supportive Housing, and Disability Support Program(DSP).

Through our services, we advocate and help vulnerable Nova Scotians be independent, self-reliant, and secure. We work collaboratively across the province with a strong dedicated network of supports and staff, to achieve desired and shared outcomes for all.

About Our Opportunity
We're hiring dedicated Child Protection Social Workers to join our team in the following program areas, including Assessment, Ongoing Support, and Children in Care. In this vital role, you will provide a wide array of professional child and family wellbeing services. You will be involved in planning for and supervising children in the care of the Minister, liaising with various partners and communities, and advocating on behalf of children and families.

As a role model, you will support and demonstrate a workplace culture that is inclusive, respectful, safe, and supportive. Under the provisions of the Children and Family Services Act (CFSA) and An Act respecting First Nations, Inuit, and Métis Children, Youth, and Families (FNIM), your role will actively work towards ensuring children's safety and wellbeing, provide ongoing supports to parents and children, and collaborate with program areas to determine appropriate and safe places for children to live.

Primary Accountabilities
Daily, you actively work to engage people and communities to build resilience, address challenges and trauma, and create change. Every day is different, and you will encounter unique challenges with responsibilities ranging from:

• Assessing child safety and wellbeing concerns and working with families and communities to address them

• Collaborating with and supporting individuals and families

• Planning and developing case plans with families

• Working closely with the community and advocating for connections to community resources

• Participating in risk assessments, court testimonies, and evaluations

• Planning with and supervising children in care of the Minister

Qualifications and Experience
A completed Master of Social Work, or a Bachelor of Social work with at least two (2) years of related experience, along with a driver's license are required. You must be eligible for registration with the Nova Scotia College of Social Workers (NSCSW). If you are a current social work student with anticipated graduation this year, with at least two (2) years of related experience, we encourage you to apply!

You are:

• A strong team player

• Empowered to drive positive change

• Compassionate, reliable, and resourceful

You possess a deep understanding of child development, family dynamics, trauma-informed care, and community resources. You are well-versed in effective intervention strategies. Your excellent problem-solving skills, combined with creative thinking, enhance the support provided to children and families, contributing to their overall well-being and growth.

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Working Conditions
A typical workday is between 8am - 5pm. Most of your work will involve meeting with clients in their homes or with service providers, requiring substantial driving time, sometimes in adverse weather conditions.

On a rotating schedule, you may be required to provide child and family wellbeing services for your designated area, after regular business hours. This will include working on weekends and reporting to the provincial after-hours response team.

You may also be called upon to work beyond regular business hours on short notice.

Personal resilience is crucial to meet the physical and emotional demands of this position. You will be immersed in high-stress and crisis situations, with extensive support and resources at your disposal. You must be able to work under pressure and be both personally and professionally committed to working inclusively with culturally diverse individuals.

Additional Information

## Several Opportunities are available, including:

• Two (2) Permanent positions

• One (1) Term position with an anticipated end date of August 20, 2027

• One (1) Temporary position with an anticipated end date of June 11, 2027.

The appointment status ('term', 'temporary' or 'casual') is dependent on the start date of the successful candidate.

What We Offer
We offer many perks and benefits, based on your employment status including:

• A social work career without limits; endless opportunities to grow and develop within the Province of Nova Scotia through coaching, training, and advancement opportunities

• Reimbursement for your registration fees to the NS College of Social Workers.

• Out-of-province applicants may be eligible to apply for moving expenses.

• Ability to earn overtime and shift premiums for weekend and after-hours work.

• Travel and car allowance.

• Three (3) weeks vacation to start, and annual pay progression.

• Employee and Family Assistance Programs (EFAP)

• Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability

• Defined Pension Benefit Plan.

Click here to learn more about our various benefits offerings and eligibility criteria.
