2241060.title: Director, Operational Services
2241060.description:
Job Title: Director, Operational Services
Location: Truro, Nova Scotia
TP - CHI - 10141

Meridia Recruitment Solutions is pleased to partner with Chignecto-Central Regional Centre for Education (CCRCE) in the recruitment of a Director, Operational Services to join their Executive Leadership Team in Truro, Nova Scotia.

CCRCE serves approximately 20,000 students and employs more than 4,000 staff across 65 schools throughout central and northern Nova Scotia. As one of the province's largest public education organizations, CCRCE is committed to providing inclusive, safe, healthy, and supportive learning environments that enable student success. The Operational Services Department oversees a diverse operational portfolio that includes school facilities, student transportation, health and safety, capital projects, infrastructure planning, and responsibilities as landlord for several leaseholds, in support of schools and communities across the region.

## Role Description

Reporting to the Regional Executive Director, the Director, Operational Services provides strategic leadership and oversight for Property Services, Student Transportation, infrastructure, and Health & Safety across the region. Leading a team of approximately 500 employees and overseeing an operational budget of approximately $60 million, the Director is responsible for ensuring the effective delivery of operational services that support schools, students, staff, and communities.

This role serves as a key member of the Executive Leadership Team and requires a leader who can balance strategic planning with a visible, hands-on approach to leadership. Working closely with senior administrators, school leaders, government partners, contractors, consultants, and community stakeholders, the Director will help shape the future of CCRCE.

## Your responsibilities will include:

• Providing leadership and oversight for Property Services, Student Transportation, and Health & Safety.

• Serving as a key member of the Executive Leadership Team, contributing to organizational planning and decision-making across the Regional Centre.

• Leading and developing multidisciplinary operational teams while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, safety, and continuous improvement.

• Overseeing transportation services supporting more than 13,000 students daily through a fleet of approximately 200 buses.

• Directing facilities operations, maintenance programs, custodial services, and infrastructure investments across more than 3.8 million square feet of educational and support facilities.

• Developing and managing significant operational and capital budgets while ensuring responsible stewardship of public resources.

• Leading long-range capital planning, major repairs, renovations, construction projects, and infrastructure renewal initiatives.

• Monitoring operational performance, service levels, and departmental effectiveness to ensure high-quality service delivery.

• Ensuring compliance with procurement requirements, purchasing policies, tendering processes, regulatory obligations, and health and safety standards.

• Building strong relationships with principals, school communities, contractors, municipalities, consultants, government agencies, and other stakeholders.

• Providing leadership within a unionized environment, including labour relations matters and participation in collective bargaining activities.

• Supporting emergency management planning, operational continuity, school closure decisions, and transportation service interruption protocols across the region.

## Your Qualifications

As the ideal candidate, you are a collaborative and highly visible operational leader who combines strategic thinking with a practical, solutions-oriented approach. You have experience leading large teams, managing complex operations, and building strong relationships within public-facing organizations.

## Your qualifications include:

• Post-secondary education in engineering, operations management, facilities management, business, public administration, or another discipline relevant to operational leadership.

• 5+ years of management experience, combined with 5+ years of experience overseeing large-scale operations, infrastructure, facilities, transportation, fleet management, public works, healthcare operations, education operations, or similar complex environments.

• Demonstrated success leading large, diverse teams and managing significant operational budgets.

• Experience working within a unionized environment and a strong understanding of labour relations and collective agreements.

• Working knowledge of provincial building and fire code requirements, accessibility standards, environmental and regulatory compliance, and the Occupational Health and Safety Act.

• Experience with procurement, purchasing policies, tendering processes, contract administration, and supplier management.

• Strong project management, strategic planning, and organizational leadership capabilities.

• Exceptional communication, stakeholder engagement, and relationship-building skills.

• Ability to lead organizational change while maintaining a strong focus on service delivery and operational excellence.

• Valid driver's licence and ability to travel throughout the region.

## Assets include:

• Engineering background.

• A professional designation, such as P.Eng., CPMM, FMP or PMP, or eligibility for professional registration, is an asset.

• Experience in public education, municipal government, public works, healthcare, transportation, fleet management, facilities management, or other large public-sector organizations.

• Experience leading major capital construction, infrastructure renewal, or asset management programs.

## Why CCRCE?

This is a unique opportunity to lead one of the largest operational portfolios in Nova Scotia's public education sector. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, you will help shape the infrastructure, transportation systems, and operational services that support approximately 20,000 students and 4,000 employees across the region.

CCRCE offers a comprehensive total rewards package, including a competitive salary, defined benefit pension plan, comprehensive health and dental coverage, generous vacation entitlement, and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact within a values-driven public service organization.

2239102.description:
## Occupational Therapist (OT) - Disability Support Outreach Team (DSOT)

## Meaningful Work | Flexible FTE | Permanent Full-Time | 37.5 hours/week

Make a difference where it matters most. Breton Ability is looking for a Occupational Therapist (OT) to join our brand-new Disability Support Outreach Team (DSOT) and help people with disabilities live with greater choice, dignity, and independence. This is an opportunity to bring your clinical expertise into a collaborative, community-based role where your work has a visible impact on individuals, families, teams, and communities across Cape Breton.

Be part of something new from the beginning. DSOT is a brand-new team being built to bring Remedy to life, and this role offers a rare opportunity to help shape how innovative, community-based disability supports are delivered across Cape Breton.

This is a chance to do meaningful clinical work in a setting where your expertise directly improves everyday life. You will provide occupational therapy assessment, consultation, and intervention services supporting individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, autism spectrum disorder, acquired disabilities, physical disabilities, mental health needs, and dual diagnosis. As part of an interdisciplinary team, you will develop practical supports focused on accessibility, participation, independence, health, safety, and quality of life.

Flexible by Design: Funding is available for one full-time equivalent (FTE) Occupational Therapist position. The organization is committed to flexibility and is open to a range of scheduling arrangements, including full-time, part-time, shared, or customized schedules. Candidates are encouraged to apply regardless of their preferred hours, as we are willing to explore options that support both service delivery and work-life balance. Benefit eligibility may vary based on hours worked.

## What you'll do:

• Provide occupational therapy assessment, consultation, and intervention to support participation, independence, and quality of life.

• Complete functional, sensory, accessibility, environmental, and activities of daily living assessments.

• Recommend adaptive equipment, assistive technology, and environmental supports.

• Collaborate with individuals, families, teams, and community partners to create person-directed solutions.

• Support Individual Program Plans and Positive Behaviour Support Plans through a human rights-based, trauma-informed approach.

• Provide education and consultation on accessibility, sensory supports, supported decision-making, and Remedy-aligned service delivery.

## What you bring:

• Master's Degree in Occupational Therapy, from an accredited program.\

• Eligibility for registration or current registration with the College of Occupational Therapists of Nova Scotia.

• Experience supporting individuals with disabilities, complex support needs, and/or diverse abilities.

• Knowledge of occupational therapy assessment, sensory supports, accessibility, assistive technology, adaptive equipment, and participation-focused interventions.

• Strong consultation, communication, documentation, and interdisciplinary collaboration skills.

• Commitment to trauma-informed, rights-based, and person-directed practice.

Where you'll work: The Occupational Therapist works across community, office, residential, educational, and alternate settings as required. Travel within the service region is required and a valid driver's license must be maintained.

Why you'll want to join us: At Breton Ability, your expertise will be valued, your ideas will matter, and your work will help build more inclusive supports across Nova Scotia. We offer a supportive interdisciplinary team, comprehensive benefits, a pension plan, wellness programs, professional development, and opportunities to grow and lead.

Join us in creating a future of choice, independence, and dignity for all individuals!

About the Opportunity

The Medical Laboratory Technologist performs analytical tests and procedures offered by the Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine using appropriate methodologies and quality assurance techniques. The Medical Laboratory Technologist possesses the technical ability and problem-solving skills to perform all tests (both manual and automated) in the clinical and environmental laboratories. Performs laboratory tests with a network of steps and variables according to established protocols and works with little or no supervision in emergency and weekend/night situations. Operates instruments that are often computer integrated and networked and uses computerized information systems. Compares test results to pre-established criteria (reference intervals) and makes decisions regarding the reportability of results, thus exercising independent judgment. Stressful working conditions require the Medical Laboratory Technologist to be tactful, sensitive and able to communicate effectively and professionally. Maintains patient confidentiality at all times as deemed essential by the Medical Laboratory Technologist Code of Conduct.

About You

We would love to hear from you if you have the following:

Must be a graduate from a recognized Medical Laboratory Technologist program or equivalent (as determined by NSRMLS)

Candidates must have successfully completed the Medical Laboratory Technologist Examination in all five disciplines

Licensure (active) with Nova Scotia Regulator of Medical Laboratory Sciences (NSRMLS)

Personal Liability Insurance (PLI) required

Ability to work shiftwork (weekends and holidays as required)

Willingness to travel when required

Competencies in other languages an asset, French preferred

Please ensure your resume is up to date and includes all relevant education, experience, training, and certifications.

Hours

Permanent full-time position; 75 hours biweekly

Compensation and Benefits

$33.20 - $42.47 hourly

Successful candidates may be eligible for our benefits package which includes health, dental, travel, long-term disability, and life insurance coverage as well as a defined benefit pension plan.

What You'll Love About Nova Scotia Health

Nova Scotia Health is more than the province's largest provider of health services; we're a team driven by excellence in health, healing and learning. Across hospitals, health centres and community programs, our people deliver innovative, high-quality care that impacts lives across Nova Scotia and Atlantic Canada.

From vibrant city life to scenic coastal communities, Nova Scotia offers a lifestyle as rewarding as the work itself. At Nova Scotia Health, you'll find meaningful career opportunities, supportive teams and the work-life balance to enjoy everything our beautiful province has to offer. Join us and discover why so many people are choosing to call Nova Scotia home.

• You demonstrate understanding of and skill in interviewing techniques and professional boundaries, including privacy and confidentiality.

• You are known for your superior customer service skills and are able to create a relationship of trust beyond the immediate interaction.

• Your superb team working skills enable you to contribute positively to a team environment

• You have specific technical occupational knowledge and skill in assistive technology and developing accommodation plans.

• You have specific knowledge and understanding of diverse populations including Indigenous populations.

For example, you will:

• Provide learning strategies to complement student accommodation plans including, but not limited to, improving learning skills, integrating technology, accessing learning resources and tools and developing communication plans with faculty.

• Organize services, refer students to appropriate learning supports, assess eligibility for funding programs, facilitate government mandated funding applications, and comply with external government partners' processes and legislation.

• Contribute to and participate in campus initiatives and signature events.

As part of the Student Supports team, you will participate in, or at times lead, the organization of campus events, activities, or committees that contribute to the distinctive student experience, such as Orientation, Wellness Week, and Convocation. You are passionate about supporting students and providing excellent customer service.

As a condition of employment, Professional Support employees at NSCC must complete a part-time adult education program delivered by NSCC. This adult education program is a significant investment on the part of NSCC in the learning and development of new employees. To achieve regular status; all probationary, full or part-time Professional Support employees of the College must successfully complete the program within their probationary period. Term full-time Professional Support employees whose term appointment is twelve or more months are also required to participate in this program.

Candidates selected for interviews will be expected to provide at least three recent occupational references. The successful candidate will be expected to provide official transcripts to show proof of academic achievements.

NSCC is committed to the full inclusion of all applicants. As part of this commitment, NSCC will ensure that applicants are provided reasonable accommodations, as required. Payroll Specialist
Location: Dartmouth, NS

Position Summary
Maritime Paper Products LP is a dynamic, team-oriented company and is honored to be one of Canada's Best Managed Companies. We believe that hiring the best people is a key part of our success. Providing excellence in both our packaging solutions and the relationships we build with our clients, we offer superior capabilities, including in-house graphic and structural design, platemaking, and manufacturing for retail-ready display. We support our customers through operations located in NS, NB, NL, and PE.

We are seeking a detail-oriented and experienced Payroll Specialist to join our team. • Prepare annual payroll reporting, including T4s and other required government filings.

• Assist with payroll-related financial reporting and account reconciliations.

• Assist with payroll audits and support continuous improvement initiatives.

## Qualifications & Experience

## Required Qualifications

• Minimum of 3-5 years of payroll experience, including full-cycle payroll and T4 processing.

• Experience working in a unionized environment with demonstrated knowledge of collective agreements.

• Knowledge of Canadian payroll legislation, remittances, and payroll compliance requirements.

• Advanced report writing, data analysis, and HRIS experience, including the development of payroll and workforce reports and the analysis of data to support operational and strategic decision-making.

• Experience administering employee benefits programs.

• Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

• High level of accuracy and attention to detail.

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

## Preferred Qualifications

• Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and payroll reporting tools.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced payroll professional who enjoys working in a collaborative environment and takes pride in delivering accurate, compliant, and employee-focused payroll services.

About Our OpportunitySuccessful candidates will begin with two weeks of paid training designed to build the knowledge and skills required for effective snow and ice control operations. Following training, you will complete 45 hours of paid plowing experience under the guidance of an experienced Operator. Candidates must also successfully complete a driving assessment using a one-person-truck-plow equipped with a front plow, wing, and salt controls. There may be an opportunity to participate in the Winter Wage Guarantee, which provides guaranteed work for a minimum of two weeks and may continue for the duration of the winter season. • Guaranteed 90 hours of pay every two weeks

• Opportunities for overtime

• Scheduled days off (2 days bi-weekly)

You may also be required to perform other work, such as maintaining signs, road surface repairs and traffic control.

Qualifications and Experience
Two years of experience or an acceptable equivalent of education, training, and relevant experience.

Minimum of Class III license with air brake endorsement.

Reading and writing skills are required to understand department documentation and to complete daily logs, inspection reports, etc.

• A professional driving course from a recognized truck driving training facility

• Knowledge of hydraulic systems and mechanical skills

• Training completed at any accredited heavy/commercial equipment training institute

• Previous experience driving a manual transmission, operating trucks with salt and plow equipment, and/or knowledge of salt spreading systems

You are flexible, self-motivated, and comfortable working in all weather conditions. You are respectful and understand the value of good customer service. You will be working around environmental hazards, various traffic conditions and occasional work performed in a mechanical environment.

Applicants who are unable to apply online are invited to stop by the local Area Office located at 4 Ivey Lane, Windsor to complete a paper application. Staff will be on site between 8:30 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. Monday to Friday to assist you. Please bring a current copy of your Drivers Abstract.

2240901.title: Water Treatment Plant Operator (Float)
2240901.description:
Halifax Water is inviting applications for one (1) Term Full-time Water Treatment Plant Operator (Float) for up to six (6) months in the Operations department. The Water Treatment Plant Operator will work under the direction of the designated supervisor, who may or may not be on site, to operate water treatment plants, and perform maintenance of equipment associated with water supply plant facilities.

The Operator will work 12-hour shifts, day and night shifts, or operate and maintain small systems plants at the location to which he or she is assigned.

Interested, qualified candidates are asked to submit a cover letter and up-to-date resume quoting Competition #HW26-106E confirming their interest by 12:00 pm on October 3rd, 2026. As part of the conditional offer process, candidates will be subject to a satisfactory background check and satisfactory pre-employment testing.

Qualifications
Minimum Qualifications for this position include:

• Two (2) year technical program related to Water Treatment; an equivalent combination of formal education and related experience in a water treatment environment may be considered.

• The successful incumbent must successfully complete Operator-in-Training Water Treatment Certificate within six months of date of hire and pass the Level 1 examination within twelve months of the date of hire.

• Must also possess a valid NS driver's license.

A copy of the job description and required qualifications for this CUPE Local 227 bargaining unit position may be viewed on our corporate website at https://halifaxwater.ca/

Responsibilities
The Operator will perform preventative maintenance on all facility mechanical equipment, ensure all responsibilities are met as it pertains to the ISO 14001 compliant Environmental Management System, control all operational processes during the designated shift period, check mechanical equipment, making adjustments as required, take samples and conduct routine tests for process control, transport and mix chemicals and operate equipment used for unloading chemicals. They will also take daily readings and log any irregularities in process operations, monitor and take daily readings of weather station instruments, maintain adequate records as required, perform maintenance checks on all equipment which form part of the treatment facility, and perform mechanical maintenance as directed, on any equipment that forms part of the treatment facility.

In addition to a collegial work environment that promotes a work-life balance, Halifax Water offers its employees a challenging and rewarding career with a competitive compensation and benefits package, opportunities for professional development, and incentive programs. As a member of the team at Halifax Water, you will be contributing to the success of the utility while delivering world class customer service for water, wastewater and stormwater services in an integrated, cost effective and environmentally sound manner with a commitment to long-term sustainability.

1713568.description:

JOB LOCATION: Meteghan, NS

Villa Acadienne is an 86 bed long term care facility that has adopted the Eden Alternative Philosophy of Care. We believe in a resident centered care approach and strive to make life for our residents' worth living. We are moving away from a medical model of care and transforming our home into a place where residents can continue to grow and live full lives. We are situated in Meteghan, NS. We are about 30 minutes from Yarmouth, 40 minutes from Digby and about 3 hours from Halifax. We invite you to come join our team and enjoy life along the coast of Saint Mary's Bay. For more information on who we are and the services we provide, please visit our website at www.villaacadienne.com.

## JOB PURPOSE:

• Working within the full RN scope of practice - conducting resident assessments, care planning and evaluation.

• Appraising, coaching and supervising other care staff.

• Addressing resident and family issues.

• Playing a leadership role by inspiring, demonstrating and encouraging staff to create/enhance a life worth living and mitigate loneliness, boredom and helplessness for residents.

• Working collaboratively within a multidisciplinary setting.

## QUALIFICATIONS:

The ideal candidate will have the following qualifications, experience and abilities:

• RN currently licensed to work in the Province of Nova Scotia.

• Current certificate in Standard First Aid and CPR (or willing to obtain)

• Knowledge and experience in a unionized LTC environment or health environment (preferred).

• Able to communicate in French and English (an asset).

• A "people person" who wants to make a difference in the lives of residents and staff and who is respectful of all people.

• A "big picture" thinker and change agent with a propensity for continuous learning.

• Service oriented with the ability to build relationships and create win/win solutions.

• Excellent communication skills and proven ability to coach, lead and work with others.

• Excellent listening, negotiating, team building and problem-solving skills.

• Proven ability to make timely decisions, multi-task and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

## WHAT WE OFFER:

• Excellent wage and benefit package with participation in the Nova Scotia Health Employees' Pension Plan (NSHEPP)

• A competitive salary with shift and weekend premiums

• Many education opportunities

2238791.title: Procurement Manager
2238791.description:
With more than 50 years of Aerospace industry experience, IMP Aerostructures, an Operating Unit of IMP Aerospace and Defence, is a leader in the Aerospace industry providing top quality, structural components and assemblies to clients such as Bombardier, Bell Helicopter, Boeing, Spirit Aerosystems and Lockheed. Located in the quaint town of Amherst, NS, just a short trip from Moncton, NB, you'll enjoy a lifestyle that offers all of the amenities of big city living in a rural setting. Recognized as one of Canada's Best Managed Companies, IMP Group takes enormous pride in the diligence and hard work its employee groups provide. Known for providing its employees with a supportive and challenging atmosphere, fostering growth and personal development, IMP Aerostructures has an immediate opening for a motivated individual to join its winning team!

Position Overview:
The Procurement Manager is responsible for planning, managing, and delivering all procurement activities for the IMP Aerostructures manufacturing operation. This role ensures the timely acquisition of raw materials, components, and services required to support production while optimizing costs, maintaining supplier relationships, and ensuring compliance with quality standards and company policies.

What You Will Do:
• Lead, mentor, and develop purchasing and procurement personnel.

• Establish performance goals and conduct employee evaluations.

• Promote continuous improvement and best practices within the procurement team.

• Develop and implement purchasing strategies to support manufacturing operations.

• Source, evaluate, negotiate, and manage relationships with suppliers and vendors.

• Negotiate pricing, delivery, and payment terms - and issue purchase orders, contracts, and service agreements to achieve cost savings and meet operational requirements.

• Monitor MRP messages / requisitions with buyers to ensure items are purchased on a timely basis to meet the requirements.

• Monitor supplier performance, including quality, delivery, responsiveness, and cost competitiveness.

• Monitor inventory levels and forecast purchasing requirements.

• Develop strategies to minimize stock shortages, excess inventory, and obsolete materials.

• Identify and implement cost-reduction initiatives without compromising quality or delivery requirements.

• Track purchasing metrics and savings initiatives.

• Ensure compliance with company policies, industry regulations, and ethical procurement standards.

• Develop and maintain purchasing procedures and controls.

What You Will Bring:
• University degree or combination of education and experience in a related field.

• SCMP or PLog designation or related work experience.

• 5-10 years of procurement experience – ideally in a manufacturing environment.

• 3+ years of leadership experience.

• Experience with ERP/MRP systems and inventory management.

• Strong negotiation and contract management skills.

• Knowledge of manufacturing processes and supply chain operations.

• Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities.

• Experience with ERP systems (JD Edwards. SAP, Oracle, etc.).

• Strong communication, organizational, and leadership skills.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

• Strong knowledge of MS Office and proficiency in Microsoft Excel and data analysis.

• Occasional travel to supplier locations, trade shows, and manufacturing facilities.

• Ability to work extended hours when required to support operational needs.

• Must be eligible to meet requirements for Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP), and Canadian government security clearances.

• Demonstrate a personal commitment to IMP Occupational Health, Safety and Environment policies.

What We Will Do For You:
We offer a comprehensive Benefits Package, including RSP Program, Tuition Reimbursement Program, Long Service Awards, Volunteer Grant Program, Scholarship Program, and more!

Applications for the above position will be accepted until the position has been filled. We thank all applicants for their interest; however only individuals selected for an interview will be notified.

Marine Atlantic is currently looking for a Certified Engineroom Assistant to work onboard our vessels that operate from the ports of Port aux Basques NL and North Sydney NS year round; and Argentia NL during the summer season. These positions are permanent full-time spare and relief positions that are scheduled across our fleet and each tour based on operational requirements.

Marine Atlantic is committed to a diverse, equitable and inclusive workplace. Preference may be given to members of the following equity deserving groups: women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, visible minorities and 2SLGBTQIA+ community members. If you are a member of one or more of these groups, please state to which group(s) you identify in your application.

• Keeping all machinery spaces and equipment clean and free of hazards to ensure a safe working environment
• Understanding the tasks to safely discharge or receive fuel, lube and dirty oils, and in handling engine room chemicals
• Performing all watchkeeping duties assigned, standing fire watches, and becoming familiar with the layout of the vessel
• Performing or assisting in all maintenance activities
• Maintaining good mechanical skills and judgment, with the ability to follow written and oral instructions
• Working diligently to promote a safe working environment.
• Assisting in the accomplishment of vessel functions by performing other related duties as required.

Education, Certification and Experience:
• 4th Class Motorship OR Engine Room Rating
• Valid STCW 6.1 and 6.2 Certificates
• Transport Canada mandated Marine Medical Examination
• 3 years of relevant work experience

## Additional Qualifications

• Ability to lift, handle, and carry heavy objects up to 22.3 kg

• Passenger Safety Management
• Marine Basic First Aid

Come experience the pride of working with an organization with newly constructed and revitalized infrastructure that has positioned itself for the future.

There is a monthly tour pattern for regularly assigned positions of 15 days on and 15 days off, normally commencing the 1st and 15th of each month. Marine Atlantic is a Federal Crown Corporation that provides a vital ferry service link between Newfoundland and Labrador and mainland Canada.

Headquartered in Atlantic Canada with a global presence in over 40 countries and a dedication to innovation over 50 years, the PAL Aerospace team thrives at the forefront of aviation technology and expert crew skills. As a rapidly growing company, we've built a reputation for delivering airborne special mission solutions that enable our customers to address today's complex security, safety, economic, and environmental threats - we need exceptionally talented marketers to help us do that. On the PAL Aerospace marketing team, you're working alongside a tight-knit group of passionate marketers who get to merge bold creativity and effective strategy with incredibly talented engineers, operators, pilots, and ambitious customers to make the world a safer and more sustainable place.

Our marketing team is looking for a Senior Product Marketing Specialist to introduce the future of C4ISR special mission products such as the PAL Aerospace mission system and CarteNav's AIMS-ISR and AIMS-C4. PAL Aerospace's target audience is technical and demanding. In this highly impactful role as a product marketer, you must be confident in delivering succinct, highly valuable, and actionable marketing to operators, government customers, and OEMs tackling today's threats, including domestic affairs, public safety, environmental, civil operations, and defence. This role will report directly to the Director of Marketing to coordinate sales enablement, campaigns, product news, go-to-market strategies, market research, and other demand-generating activities. As a Senior Product Marketing Specialist, you will heavily collaborate with internal stakeholders and external partners to build working relationships to drive meaningful growth and compelling storytelling.

Learn how PAL Aerospace is delivering the future of C4ISR special mission products here: https://palaerospace.com

## At PAL Aerospace in this role, you'll get to:

• Drive value proposition, positioning, and messaging development for mission system software, special mission aircraft, contracted ISR operations solutions, and productized engineering/design/modification programs.

• Own the cadence and outcomes of our partner-facing broadcasts and thought leadership program. From topic selection and SME prep through promotion, execution, and post-event reuse into evergreen demand and enablement assets. This role is public-facing; you should be comfortable presenting live to technical audiences and facilitating SMEs.

• Be PAL's internal connective hub for product story and GTM readiness: run a recurring cross?BU cadence that keeps Sales/BD & Marketing aligned with engineering, mission software (CarteNav), global mission ops, technical services, and aircrew training: turning program reality into one narrative, proof points, and priorities the org can execute.

• Aggressively uncover and validate USPs through customer/partner interviews, win/loss insights, competitive review, internal SME discovery, and field feedback. Then turn it into a story Growth-marketing/Sales/BD can use.

• Collaborate with the PAL Aerospace marketing and BD teams on the enablement system: pitch narrative, decks, one-pagers, competitive talk tracks, product briefs, and evergreen assets used in real sales conversations. Additional growth marketing content that you may collaborate on includes case studies, product videos, white papers, web copy, and more.

• Lead go-to-market planning for product launches and major updates: narrative, proof points, announcements, partner coordination, and integrated campaign planning.

• Become a product expert and power-user of current products for effective communication internally with sales & BD as well as externally with collaborating partners.

• Work with the marketing team on events to ensure products are represented correctly, effectively, and interactively at all in-person and online events PAL Aerospace and its subsidiaries participate in.

## You'll particularly love it here if:

• You have 1-5 proven years in product marketing, solutions marketing, or a similar role (B2B/SaaS experience is a plus) and can prove you've built positioning, ICPs, and value props that Sales actually used.

• You are eager to accelerate your product marketing career in the demanding yet highly rewarding fast-paced aerospace and defence market.

• Are independent, accountable, and energized by high-ownership roles.

• Have opinions on what makes a product shine above the rest and how to target and capture a market segment.

• You see the game of marketing as a fun pursuit with a keen focus on ambitious goals and the challenges it takes to achieve them.

## What you can expect from PAL Aerospace:

• Results-oriented culture: Flexible hours and remote working options empower our marketing team to focus on doing amazing things that move the needle in society, not the clock.

• Diversity & inclusivity: We believe varied backgrounds and perspectives are a competitive advantage. PAL Aerospace is committed to being an inclusive workplace that celebrates diversity and promotes critical thinking.

• Free flow of communication: From co-op students to executives, there are no barriers to sharing knowledge and, most importantly, ideas. Transparency and ease of communication across all levels and teams are encouraged.

• Travel Privileges: Full-time employees enjoy travel passes with many domestic and international partner carriers.

PAL Aerospace is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment that celebrates and encourages diversity, equity, and inclusion whereby individuals are recognized, supported, and respected. Candidates of all backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

Only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. Thank you.

2240980.title: General Manager
2240980.description:
General Manager

Portland Custom Millwork Ltd.

## Position Summary

Portland Custom Millwork is seeking an experienced General Manager to oversee the day-to-day operations of its custom millwork projects. The General Manager will coordinate projects from estimating through production, installation, and completion, ensuring work is properly planned, accurately priced, completed on schedule, and delivered to a high standard.

## Key Responsibilities

## Estimating and Project Planning

• Review drawings, specifications, site conditions, and customer requirements.

• Prepare accurate estimates for materials, labour, subcontractors, and installation.

• Develop project scopes, budgets, timelines, and production requirements.

• Identify potential design, pricing, scheduling, or installation issues before work begins.

• Coordinate changes to project scope and prepare change-order pricing.

## Project Management

• Manage multiple millwork projects from award through final completion.

• Coordinate with customers, contractors, designers, architects, suppliers, and installers.

• Monitor project costs, progress, deadlines, and quality.

• Ensure drawings, approvals, measurements, materials, and site conditions are ready before production or installation.

• Resolve project issues promptly and keep customers informed.

• Review completed work and ensure deficiencies are addressed.

## Scheduling and Production

• Develop and maintain the overall production and installation schedule.

• Prioritize projects based on customer deadlines, available labour, material lead times, and shop capacity.

• Assign work and provide clear direction to shop and installation employees.

• Hold regular scheduling meetings and communicate changes to the team.

• Monitor workflow and adjust schedules when delays or conflicts arise.

## Purchasing and Materials

• Determine material and hardware requirements for each project.

• Order materials accurately and on time.

• Monitor supplier pricing, availability, and lead times.

• Confirm materials are received, inspected, and allocated to the correct projects.

• Minimize waste, rush orders, and excess inventory.

## Operations and Leadership

• Oversee the daily activities of the shop and installation teams.

• Set clear expectations for productivity, workmanship, safety, and professionalism.

• Support, coach, and hold employees accountable for performance.

• Help recruit, train, and retain skilled employees.

• Maintain organized and efficient shop and project-management processes.

• Promote a positive, respectful, and solutions-focused work environment.

## Financial and Business Management

• Monitor estimated versus actual labour and material costs.

• Identify and address project overruns.

• Support project billing by confirming progress, completed work, and approved changes.

• Review project profitability and recommend operational improvements.

• Provide regular updates to the Owner on schedules, project risks, staffing, cash-flow requirements, and overall performance.

• Help develop pricing standards, operational procedures, and growth plans.

## Qualifications

• Experience managing custom millwork, cabinetry, construction, or a related manufacturing operation.

• Strong estimating and project-management experience.

• Ability to read architectural drawings, shop drawings, and specifications.

• Knowledge of millwork materials, hardware, manufacturing, finishing, and installation.

• Strong organizational and scheduling skills.

• Ability to manage several projects and competing deadlines.

• Strong leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills.

• Comfortable working with estimating, scheduling, and accounting software.

• Valid driver's licence.

## Key Measures of Success

• Projects are accurately estimated and profitable.

• Materials are ordered correctly and available when required.

• Production and installations are completed on schedule.

• Labour and material overruns are minimized.

• Customers receive consistent communication and quality workmanship.

• Employees understand priorities and are held accountable.

• The shop operates safely, efficiently, and with minimal downtime.

## Position Details

• Reports to: Owner/President

• Employment: Full-time

• Location: Portland Custom Millwork Ltd.

• Compensation: Based on experience

2241310.title: Buyer/Purchaser Intermediate
2241310.description:
Requisition ID: 2634

Why Choose IMP Aerospace & Defence:
IMP Aerospace & Defence is not only one of the leading companies in the Aerospace field, but we are also one of the most engaging and equality advocating companies to work for. We believe that regardless of where you work at IMP Aerospace & Defence, you are a part of our ever-growing team. IMP is able to achieve success through this teamwork mindset. That is why at IMP, you are not defined by your role.

Position Overview:
The primary responsibility of the Buyer – OWSS will be to monitor / review requirements based on IMP's Selection Notice and Priority Summary (SNAPS) and action Special Instructions (SPIN) based on an established induction forecast. The position requires liaison with Department of National Defence (DND) for arrangements of transportation of Repairable components from Main Operating Bases (MOBs) into IMP's Subcontractors. Notify the Sub-Contractor of the incoming shipments. Review quotes for best value and ensure all costs captured are within the Maximum Repair Cost (MRC). Provide Purchase Orders to authorize the induction of components into the repair lines with value within the MRC. Provide options to stakeholders and recommendation to maximize Budget and components availability. The position also carries out all required aspects of the procurement function for the acquisition of aerospace supply items; ensuring value is maximized at all times and that all supplies and parts are ordered in accordance with specifications as provided by requestor. The Buyer - OWSS MRO is a main member of an integrated team supporting DND operations. During demanding periods required to support in-house aircraft programs as well.

What You Will Do:
• Coordinate the shipment, delivery, repair, and return of assigned aircraft components between subcontractor repair facilities and the Canadian Forces Supply System (CFSS).

• Monitor subcontractor and supplier performance, including cost, turnaround time (TAT), quality, and procurement efficiency, and recommend improvements.

• Monitor CFSS usage and stock levels; initiate procurement actions, Priority Repair Requests (PRRs), and recommendations for obsolete or surplus inventory.

• Expedite outstanding PRRs and provide Canadian Forces/MOB stakeholders with repair and item status updates.

• Review RFQs and purchase orders, research suppliers, obtain and evaluate quotations, determine economic order quantities, and negotiate procurement terms.

• Prepare and release RFQs and purchase orders within approved signing authority.

• Manage assigned stock codes, SNAP list changes, inventory levels, distribution, and logistics to prevent stock-outs and High Priority Requirements (HPRs).

• Collaborate with Buyers, Asset Managers, Materiel Support representatives, CF base/depot personnel, and suppliers to ensure timely replenishment and fleet support.

• Review and recommend improvements to procurement and inventory policies, procedures, and processes.

• Investigate recurring supply issues, identify root causes, and implement or recommend corrective actions.

• Interpret and communicate moderately complex aerospace drawings and specifications with suppliers.

• Participate in Materiel Review Boards, departmental/program meetings, and meetings to resolve supply and procurement issues.

• Provide required reports, correspondence, customer support, training, and special assignments while maintaining professional relationships with internal and external stakeholders.

What You Will Bring:
• Professional Logistics (P. Log) or Supply Chain Management Professional (SCMP) or working towards designation would be beneficial

• Ideally, an undergraduate degree or College diploma in, Supply Chain, Industrial Engineering, Operations Management or Business Administration

• 3 - 5 years relevant experience in purchasing/procurement ideally in the aerospace and / or aviation industries; or equivalent experience in a similar type of complex and dynamic technical environment and education

• Working knowledge of the Canadian Forces Supply System (CFSS) Defence Resource Management Information System (DRMIS) would be beneficial

• Highly proficient in MS Office Suite of applications Experience with MRP/ERP systems (e.g. JD Edwards, PeopleSoft., etc)

• Excellent oral and written communication skills

• Proven organizational ability and an aptitude for working with numbers

• Strong analytical skills and the ability to work independently

• Strong time management and organizational skills

• Strong influencing skill and the ability to meet objectives working with colleagues

• The ideal candidate would have the qualities of a good team member, keen problem solving and organizational abilities.

• Familiarity or experience with inventory management is an asset

• Respect for accuracy and detail Incumbents must be able to pass and maintain Public Services & Procurement Canada (PSPC) and Transport Canada security clearances

• All successful applicants must be eligible to meet requirements for U.S. International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP) and Canadian government security clearance

What We Will Do For You:
• All IMP's benefits become effective on your first day of work, regardless of your position.

• Employees are entitled to 3 paid personal days and 12 statutory holidays per year.

• We offer a comprehensive Benefits Package, including RRSP Program, Tuition Reimbursement Program, Long Service Awards, Volunteer Grant Program, Scholarship Program, and more!

•

IMP is committed to Employment Equity and our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative at all job levels. We welcome applicants from Indigenous People, Visible Minority Groups, Persons with Disabilities and Women in occupations or positions where they are under-represented. If you are a member of one of these equity groups, you are encouraged to self identify on either your cover letter or resume.

2215480.title: Technical Records Specialist
2215480.description:
Requisition ID: 2418

Why Choose IMP Aerospace & Defence:
IMP Aerospace & Defence is not only one of the leading companies in the Aerospace field, but we are also one of the most engaging and equality advocating companies to work for. We believe that regardless of where you work at IMP Aerospace & Defence, you are a part of our ever-growing team. IMP is able to achieve success through this teamwork mindset. Position Overview:
The Technical Record Specialist reports to the CH149 Technical Record Supervisor for the duties of CH149 Technical Records Management, covering the CH149 fleet and also the -519 variant of the AW-101 aircraft. Primary tasking for this role is on maintaining the structure and conducting data updates in the CH149 Electronic Record Keeping System, along with a key secondary focus on data analysis and reporting.

What You Will Do:
• Configuration management and implementation of data updates of the CH149 Electronic Record Keeping System (ERKS), GOLDesp, and the Compound - Interactive Electronic Technical Publication (C-IETP).

• Assist the CH149 Technical Record Supervisor in providing CH149 HUMS data for ASIP and ILS activities in support of the CH149 fleet and facilitating these activities with the aircraft OEM and IMP Solutions.

• Provide expertise and advice to in-house CH149 Engineering Life Cycle Specialists in retrieving trend data available in the Oracle/HUMS systems to assist technical investigation on aircraft systems.

• The conversion of ATO and AMO policy and technical directives into GOLDesp and C-IETP data elements.

• TAM-compliant management of the Electronic Record Keeping System required for the support of the CH149 Cormorant helicopter.

• Coordinate the delivery of GOLDesp and C-IETP updates to the user units.

• Support to parts Repair & Overhaul activity and Structure Building in GOLDesp for HIA heavy maintenance (PIM) aircraft.

• Conduct data gathering and analysis on the CH149 fleet and fleet operations in support of CSH program metrics and Key Performance Indicators.

• Conduct additional data gathering and analysis as part of CSH program initiatives.

• Provide reports to the CSC on CH149 materiel, upgrades, modification and component usage trends.

• Other duties as assigned by the CH149 CIS & Technical Record Supervisor.

What You Will Bring:
• CET (Diploma in Engineering Technology) or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• 4 or more years experience in an aircraft engineering and maintenance environment with directly related experience in aircraft systems.

• Knowledge of rotary-wing aircraft systems and components is desirable.

• Ability to manage projects and tasks.

• Database and general computer skills are essential, with the ideal candidate possessing both experience with enterprise level databases (Oracle) as well as common applications such as MS-Access.

• Must be proficient in the use of Microsoft Office Suite of programs including at least MS Word and Excel.

• A working knowledge of GOLDesp is desirable.

• Knowledge of airworthiness regulations, standards and military modification processes is desirable.

• Sound interpersonal skills and an ability to work effectively with people at all levels within the organization. Capable of providing clear and detailed written and verbal communication.

• Must possess good self-discipline with an ability to work independently when required.

• Hold or have previously held an Aircraft Maintenance Engineers license or equivalent qualification as an aircraft technician within the Canadian Armed Forces, CSH or commercial aviation organization.

• Demonstrate a personal commitment to IMP Occupational Health, Safety and Environment policies. Continually focusing on your individual safety and the safety of others who may be affected by your work and to fully comply with all Federal Health and Safety Legislation.

• Participate in Continuous Improvement, Lean & 5S activities in your area.

• Must be eligible to meet requirements for Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP), Secret Level II Security Clearance through PSPC- Contract Security Program, and Transport Canada RAIC clearance.

Are you an Electrical Engineering student looking to apply your classroom learning to real-world infrastructure that powers communities across Nova Scotia?

As an Engineering Co-op with our Energy Delivery Distribution Engineering team, you'll gain hands-on experience supporting the operation and design of the electrical distribution network that delivers reliable energy to homes and businesses every day.

During the Winter 2027 term, you'll work alongside experienced engineers and technical professionals while developing practical knowledge of distribution systems, electrical protection, customer servicing, engineering records, and asset management. You'll have the opportunity to contribute to meaningful projects, participate in technical reviews, and gain valuable insight into how utility engineering supports safe and reliable service for customers.

This is an exciting opportunity for students who enjoy problem-solving, technical analysis, and learning how engineering principles are applied in the field.

## What you'll do:

• Support the operation and design of Nova Scotia Power's electrical distribution network.

• Gather and analyze field and historical asset data to support engineering decisions and system planning.

• Develop an understanding of distribution equipment, electrical protection systems, and overcurrent protective devices.

• Assist with customer servicing reviews and technical assessments, including fault level requests.

• Help maintain the accuracy of engineering records through updates to underground distribution drawings.

• Support the review and markup of new drawing revisions and engineering documentation.

• Contribute to projects that improve the reliability and effectiveness of the distribution system.

• Collaborate with engineers, technical staff, and cross-functional stakeholders to solve engineering challenges.

• Are currently pursuing a degree in Electrical Engineering, ideally in your second, third, or fourth year of study.

• Have strong analytical and problem-solving skills and enjoy working with technical information.

• Are comfortable using computer applications and engineering-related software and tools.

• Demonstrate strong organizational skills and can manage multiple tasks effectively.

• Work well both independently and as part of a collaborative team.

• Take initiative, show accountability, and approach challenges with a positive attitude.

• Communicate clearly and effectively with a variety of audiences.

2238143.description:
RISK MANAGEMENT

Environmental Services Worker (Housekeeper)

Department: Environmental Services
Location: Berwick, Nova Scotia
Union: Unionized
Responsible to: Director of Facilities

## Position Summary

The Environmental Services Worker supports the delivery of high-quality environmental services throughout Grand View Manor by maintaining a clean, safe, and comfortable environment for residents, tenants, visitors, and team members. The Environmental Services Worker contributes to resident quality of life by ensuring resident rooms, common areas, washrooms, equipment, and furnishings are cleaned and maintained according to established standards. The position plays an important role in infection prevention and control, workplace safety, resident satisfaction, and maintaining a welcoming environment that respects the dignity, privacy, and comfort of all residents.

## Key Accountabilities

## Resident Room Cleaning

• Clean resident rooms according to established schedules and procedures.

• Clean beds, bed rails, mattresses, furniture, mirrors, windows, window ledges, light fixtures, walls, pictures, chairs, and baseboards.

• Shampoo fabric chairs and clean upholstered furniture as required.

• Respect resident privacy, dignity, personal belongings, and individual preferences while performing duties.

• Report concerns related to resident room cleanliness, safety, or maintenance needs.

## Bathroom Cleaning and Sanitation

• Complete thorough cleaning and sanitization of resident bathrooms.

• Clean tubs, sinks, toilets, mirrors, walls, floors, vents, fixtures, and related surfaces.

• Replenish paper products, soap, and other supplies as required.

• Follow infection prevention and control standards when cleaning and disinfecting resident care areas.

## Floor Care and Facility Maintenance

• Sweep, mop, scrub, strip, wax, buff, and polish floors using approved equipment and procedures.

• Operate Taskis, vacuums, carpet extractors, and other cleaning equipment safely and effectively.

• Maintain cleanliness of corridors, common areas, entrances, exits, nursing stations, and assigned work areas.

• Check exit doors when used and report any concerns.

## Cleaning and Sanitation

• Collect garbage and recycling throughout the shift and ensure timely disposal.

• Participate in departmental cleaning schedules and sanitation programs.

• Clean and maintain hopper rooms, housekeeping carts, storage areas, and utility rooms.

• Ensure all cleaning equipment and supplies are properly cleaned, stored, and maintained.

• Follow infection prevention, environmental cleaning, and workplace safety standards.

## Equipment and Supply Management

• Maintain a clean, organized, and properly stocked housekeeping cart.

• Monitor inventory levels and report supply shortages to the appropriate supervisor.

• Report damaged equipment, maintenance concerns, or unsafe conditions promptly.

• Demonstrate proper care and handling of all cleaning equipment and supplies.

## Teamwork and Communication

• Read and review Environmental Services communication logs, communication boards, and assigned notices at the beginning of each shift.

• Communicate effectively with Nursing and other departments regarding room access, cleaning schedules, and resident needs.

• Work collaboratively with Environmental Services team members and other departments.

• Follow oral and written instructions accurately and efficiently.

• Demonstrate flexibility in performing assigned duties and learning new tasks.

• Participate in orientation, training, and educational opportunities as required.

• Perform other related duties as assigned.

## Qualifications

## Education Required:

• Grade 10 education or equivalent.

## Experience Preferred:

• Previous housekeeping, environmental services, hospitality, healthcare, long-term care, or commercial cleaning experience.

• Experience operating commercial cleaning equipment.

## Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

• Ability to read, write, and follow oral and written instructions.

• Ability to complete routine cleaning and sanitation duties independently.

• Good communication and interpersonal skills.

• Ability to organize work effectively and manage competing priorities.

• Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

• Knowledge of WHMIS, Safety Data Sheets (SDS), and safe chemical handling practices.

• Knowledge of infection prevention and control practices is considered an asset.

• Ability to maintain confidentiality regarding residents and organizational information.

• Commitment to resident-centered service and quality outcomes.

• Willingness to learn new skills, procedures, and equipment operation.

## Working Conditions

## Physical Demands

• Frequent standing and walking throughout the shift.

• Frequent lifting, carrying, pushing, and pulling of cleaning equipment, supplies, garbage, and linen.

• Frequent bending, twisting, reaching, kneeling, squatting, and repetitive movements.

• Ability to move furniture and equipment as required.

• Ability to safely operate cleaning equipment and tools.

## Mental Demands

• Ability to maintain attention to detail while working independently.

• Ability to prioritize tasks and complete work within established timelines.

• Ability to adapt to changing priorities and operational needs.

• Ability to follow detailed cleaning schedules and procedures.

## Environmental Conditions

• Exposure to cleaning and disinfecting chemicals.

• Exposure to bodily fluids and infectious materials in accordance with infection prevention protocols.

• Exposure to varying temperatures, odors, noise, and cleaning equipment.

• Work performed throughout resident care areas, common spaces, administrative areas, and service departments.

## Interpersonal Relationships

The Environmental Services Worker maintains positive and professional working relationships with:

• Residents and families

• Environmental Services team members

• Nursing and clinical staff

• Food Services staff

• Maintenance staff

• Leadership team members

• Volunteers, visitors, contractors, and community partners

Teamwork, communication, and mutual respect are essential to providing exceptional resident care and service.

## Core Competencies

• Resident-Centered Service

• Infection Prevention and Control

• Environmental Cleaning and Sanitation

• Teamwork and Collaboration

• Accountability

• Communication

• Attention to Detail

• Adaptability

• Professionalism

• Time Management

• Workplace Safety

• Continuous Learning

2228797.description:
The Maritime Odd Fellows Home is a 47 Bed Long Term Care Facility located in the town of Pictou, overlooking picturesque Pictou Harbour. The Odd Fellows Home has a long history providing quality care to our valued Residents and is in need of a Full-time LPN to join our care team.

The Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN) utilizes the nursing process, critical thinking and problem solving skills to provide holistic care to individuals, families, and groups. The LPN is responsible for planning nursing care in an assigned area as required by individualized Resident needs and according to dependent and independent nursing functions while adhering to recognized nursing techniques, procedures, and established standards based on the scope of practical nursing, under the direction of the Registered Nurse.

The LPN contributes to the efficient and effective functioning of the Home, coordination of Resident care and staffing. The LPN accepts responsibility for maintaining and continually enhancing competencies through ongoing professional development including participation in education programs, research and continuous quality activities. The LPN practices according to the College of Licensed Practical Nurses of Nova Scotia Code of Ethics for Licensed Practical Nurses, Standards of Nursing Practice, specialty standards as applicable and the policies and procedures of the Maritime Odd Fellows Home. Working collaboratively as a member of the health care team by respecting and acknowledging the roles of all those within the healthcare system in contributing to safe, competent and ethical care, the LPN provides Resident-centred care that responds appropriately to the physiological, psychological, social, cultural, and spiritual needs.

## Qualifications

• Graduate of an accredited school of nursing

• Successful completion of Physical Assessment and Pharmacology certifications

• Current certificate of registration with CLPNNS

• Recent Long Term Care experience preferred

• Experience caring for individuals with dementia an asset

• Current CPR certification

• Demonstrated clinical skills

• Effective communication skills

• Current Criminal Records Check with Vulnerable Sector

• Resident Focus

• Influence, impact and leadership

• Team Work

• Problem Solving

• Accountability and Dependability

• Operating Equipment

• Ethics and Integrity

2240811.title: Supervisor, Production
2240811.description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is transforming the future?

## Who We Are

We are Vale Base Metals – a global supplier of the critical minerals transforming the future.

With industry-leading reserves of copper and nickel in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia, and state-of-the-art infrastructure in the U.K., Canada, and Japan, VBM delivers a secure and responsible supply of high-quality products to customers across Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

Global demand for critical minerals is growing exponentially. From energy to aerospace, batteries to magnets, robotics to artificial intelligence, a secure and responsible supply of critical minerals is fundamental to power modern technologies. And at Vale Base Metals, we are transforming our business to provide a secure and responsible supply of these minerals.

Join our diverse team of 13,000 talented individuals committed to providing mineral security to a world in transition. We invite you to put your skills to work, driving meaningful and enduring change while enjoying a rewarding career.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking an operations Supervisor to join our Creighton mine Team in Sudbury, Ontario.

The role is a permanent onsite position, working 5/4 rotating days and afternoons. This posting is for an existing position vacancy.

As a Supervisor, Production you will continuously improve the work team performance through the effective use of established processes and procedures in achieving assigned objectives following Vale's Safety Policies, Programs, and Legislative Standards.

Additionally, in this position you will:

• Lead and manage operations to achieve safe, efficient, and cost-effective production and maintenance targets.

• Promote a Zero Harm culture by ensuring compliance with safety programs, procedures, and risk management practices.

• Monitor production, quality, cost, and capital performance, taking corrective action as needed to meet targets.

• Conduct crew line-ups, communicate risks, manage incident reporting, and participate in investigations.

• Support injury management and employee return-to-work programs in collaboration with healthcare providers.

• Manage workforce performance through training, qualification tracking, coaching, mentoring, discipline, and grievance resolution.

• Coordinate resources, inventories, materials, overtime, and work schedules to support operational requirements.

• Plan, assign, monitor, and continuously improve work execution while ensuring accurate reporting, work order completion, and effective shift handovers.

## What We Offer You

• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare online

• Online training and career development opportunities

## About You

## Education:

• Grade 12 level education or GED equivalency is required

• Common Core: First Line Underground Mine Supervisor Common Core (770121) or Common Core for First Line Production Supervisor Underground Hard Rock Mining (770120) is preferred.

## Experience:

• Minimum 3 years of leadership experience in an industrial setting.

• Experience working underground is preferred.

• Experience with Microsoft Office Products is required.

## Skills:

• Ability to work with minimal supervision and work well with others in a team environment.

• Must have strong written and oral communication skills.

• Must be obsessed with safety and risk.

• Must demonstrate open and transparent dialogue in all aspects of work

## Why Sudbury

Greater Sudbury is a vibrant city in northeastern Ontario, renowned for its rich mining history and significant role in Canada's mineral production. The city sits atop one of the world's largest and oldest meteorite impact sites, the Sudbury Basin, which is exceptionally rich in nickel, copper, and other critical minerals that are required for modern technologies such as AI and defence. The mining sector is a cornerstone of Sudbury's economy, driving both employment and economic growth, and Vale Base Metals plays a pivotal role in this regard. Our commitment to the community is as deep as our mines.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people can act like owners, being their authentic selves and empowering them to deliver results. Vale Base Metals encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

In accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Employees engaged by the Company must be lawfully able to work for the Company in the country where the role is located. The Company does not provide immigration, work permit, or permanent residence sponsorship or assistance.

Vale uses artificial intelligence to screen, assess, and/or select applicants for this position.

Pay Grade: 17 V

Minimum Starting Salary: 108,000

Apply by: October 6, 2026

## #ValeBaseMetals

Interested applicants must submit their application online at https://vale.eightfold.ai/careers.

2240269.description:
Job Advertisement: Property Manager

Type of Employment: Permanent, Full-time

Work Location: Based in Colchester & Cumberland counties (Hybrid work environment; on-site at housing communities)

Application Deadline: Tuesday, September 29, 2026

United Way Maritimes - with teams located in and serving the regions of Central New Brunswick, Colchester & Cumberland Counties, Halifax, Lunenburg County, Pictou County, Prince Edward Island, and Saint John, Kings & Charlotte - is a for-impact organization that brings donors, volunteers, and partners together to create lasting social change. We believe everyone matters and deserves to belong, be safe, and live a life of their choosing. To help, United Way Maritimes alleviates and reduces local poverty by funding, partnering, convening, and advocating for solutions. United Way Maritimes is part of a federated movement of 50+ United Ways across the country.

The staff at United Way Maritimes takes pride in bringing together people who have a range of experience, talents, and backgrounds. We share a passion for each of the places we call home and bring many different skills and strengths to the work we do. Our community and social change priorities include poverty, social isolation, affordable housing, people experiencing marginalization and vulnerability, and recovery and resilience to environmental, mass casualty and public health emergencies. We provide a supportive and flexible work environment filled with opportunity, balance, and laughter.

The Housing Team is focused on creating and stewarding a sustainable, equitable, and community-driven parallel housing system that provides opportunities unavailable in the general market. This includes supportive housing, affordable rental, and attainable homeownership models that support people exiting homelessness, strengthen housing stability, and address gaps such as missing-middle housing.

Reporting to the Director, Affordable Housing, the Property Manager is responsible for protecting the long-term value, performance, and sustainability of United Way Maritimes' housing portfolio. Working closely with housing team members and organizational partners, this role provides strategic and operational leadership to ensure housing assets are operated safely, efficiently, and in accordance with United Way Maritimes' values and applicable legislation.

The successful candidate will oversee building operations, maintenance programs, capital planning, contracted service providers, financial performance, regulatory compliance, insurance administration, and risk management while helping create housing communities where residents can thrive.

## The key responsibilities of the role include:

• Asset Management: Develop and implement long-term asset management strategies to ensure the sustainability, performance, and value of United Way Maritimes' housing portfolio. This includes supervising property coordinators, managing capital and lifecycle planning, coordinating preventative maintenance and asset assessments, and supporting the transition of new developments into operations.

• Property Operations: Oversee the day-to-day operation and maintenance of housing assets to ensure buildings are safe, secure, clean, and well-maintained. This includes monitoring building performance, completing minor repairs when appropriate, developing operational standards, and coordinating emergency preparedness and business continuity planning.

• Contract & Vendor Management: Manage the procurement, contracting, and performance of maintenance contractors and service providers to support effective property operations. This includes overseeing RFP processes, negotiating service agreements, monitoring quality standards, and ensuring all contracted work complies with legislative and organizational requirements.

• Compliance & Risk Management: Ensure housing operations comply with Residential Tenancy legislation, Occupational Health & Safety requirements, fire and accessibility standards, insurance obligations, and other regulatory requirements. This includes coordinating inspections and reporting, managing insurance claims, and proactively identifying and mitigating operational risks.

## Qualifications

• Experience: Minimum five years of progressive experience in property or asset management.

• Education: Post-secondary education in Property Management, Facilities Management, Business Administration, Engineering Technology, Construction Management, or a related discipline.

• Demonstrated repair, maintenance and construction skills.

• Experience supporting direct reports, providing guidance, mentorship and accountability.

• Experience managing affordable or multi-unit residential housing preferred.

• Experience managing operating budgets and capital planning.

• Experience procuring and managing contracted services.

• Knowledge of building systems and preventative maintenance.

• Knowledge of Occupational Health & Safety requirements.

• Familiarity with Residential Tenancy legislation.

• Strong contract administration and negotiation skills.

• Excellent organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

• Possess construction/repair tools and access to reliable vehicle.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office, SharePoint, Excel, and property management software.

Our ideal candidate is a strategic and collaborative leader who combines strong planning and systems-thinking skills with a practical, hands-on approach to property and asset management. They are financially and operationally disciplined, an excellent communicator and relationship builder, and are able to balance long-term planning with day-to-day operational demands. Calm, solutions-focused, and committed to continuous improvement, they thrive in collaborative environments and are dedicated to supporting organizational learning and excellence.

United Way Maritimes is committed to a comprehensive compensation package including salary, group retirement savings plan contribution, health and dental benefits, generous vacation time, additional time-off during the December holiday period, and professional development and training opportunities. The salary for this position is $81,984 per year.

Interested candidates are encouraged to reach out to our Administrative & HR Assistant, Aleks Wilson, for a conversation about the role, salary range, and total compensation package. To contact Aleks, please email: jobs@unitedwaymaritimes.ca or 902-298-3702.

If this sounds like you, let us know by sharing your resume and cover letter outlining why you could be the right fit for United Way Maritimes and this role. Submit your application to jobs@unitedwaymaritimes.ca by Tuesday, September 29, at 11:59pm (AST).

United Way Maritimes deeply values equity and is committed to ensuring our staff community reflects the diversity of the wider community. We welcome applications from African Nova Scotian people, people of African descent, Indigenous peoples, racialized people, women, people with disabilities, people of varied sexual and gender identities, and others with the skills and knowledge to productively engage with diverse communities. True North Salmon , a division of Cooke Aquaculture Inc., a dynamic and growing east coast family company, with Platinum Member status in the Canada's Best Managed Companies Program, is hiring a Delivery Driver at our Dartmouth, NS facility.

• Deliver fresh and frozen seafood products to retail and wholesale customers in a safe, timely, and professional manner.

• Adhere to company safety policies, driving regulations, and commercial vehicle operating procedures.

• Maintain cleanliness and organization of the delivery vehicle and delivery equipment.

## Qualifications:

• Valid Class 5 driver's license and a clean driving abstract.

• Minimum two years delivery driving experience.

• Excellent Customer Service skills.

• Strong work ethic.

• Ability to work flexible hours.

• Ability to drive a vehicle with air brakes is desirable.

*As per company policy, a criminal background check is required.

Join our team and enjoy the benefits of full-time year-round employment with competitive rates and a comprehensive benefits package tailored to support your well-being and career growth.

• Insurance: Life and disability insurance provided for financial security.

## The Opportunity

The role description is just one part of the story. This is an opportunity to grow, to stretch, to work within the parameters of the role but stretch to your fullest potential. We are a team that counts performance, we reward contribution, and we recognize talent. It is about being at the center of one of the fastest growing Atlantic Canadian based companies and knowing you are part of that growth. The ability to bring your passion for learning, desire for growth, and energy for moving your career forward is what we offer.

Why Cooke? Simple because we are a company that rewards initiative, resourcefulness and work ethic. We will champion your growth and provide you with the platform to create your path, your career, and your future.

2240619.description:

Connection is everything. It drives us to innovate, explore, and stay close to what matters to us most. At Bell, we're building a more connected future through world-class networks, AI-powered solutions, and digital experiences that elevate how people live, work, and play every day.

We believe in empowering people. That's why we equip our teams with cutting-edge technology, AI tools, and a collaborative environment that supports creativity and growth.
