2240233.title: Engineer-in-Training - Rotational Program (Energy Delivery)
2240233.description:
The Opportunity

Job Title: Engineer-in-Training - Rotational Program (Energy Delivery)
Company, Department: Nova Scotia Power, Energy Delivery
Location: Halifax Regional Municipality, NS
Type of Employment: Regular, Full Time

Closing Date: September 29, 2026

Reference Number: 2026-5871

## The Opportunity

Nova Scotia Power's 3-year rotational Engineer-in-Training program is designed to develop technical and leadership skills, preparing participants to become future technical and people leaders who help shape the future of our company and the service we provide our customers. Throughout this three-year program, EITs will continue to develop their knowledge base by working with a variety of teams across the business, including the operational areas of Energy Delivery. Upon completion of the program, you will have fulfilled 36 months of engineering experience required toward obtaining your Professional Engineer (P.Eng) designation.

EITs benefit from structured onboarding, mentorship from business leaders, ongoing professional development, and opportunities to build leadership skills in a collaborative and inclusive environment.

## Energy Delivery

As an EIT in Energy Delivery, you may work across a variety of teams involved in the planning, design, operation, and maintenance of transmission and distribution lines, as well as substations. You will contribute to monitoring and improving system performance, ensuring compliance with safety, environmental, and regulatory standards, and supporting the integration of renewable energy sources. Through this work, you will help enhance the reliability of Nova Scotia's electricity system and the experience of our customers.

We are currently looking to fill six (6) Engineer-In-Training positions as part of our EIT Rotational Program for Energy Delivery to start work in June 2027. In this role you will mainly work out of Halifax Regional Municipality with some travel to other areas of the province as required.

Key elements of this role include:

## Engineering Design & Technical Work

• Prepare plans, designs, calculations, cost estimates, and bills of materials for a variety of engineering projects.

• Complete tasks in accordance with established codes, standards, engineering practices, drawings, and specifications.

• Perform routine technical surveys, inspections, and assessments.

• Support design, maintenance, and improvement of systems related to the transmission and distribution of electricity.

• Contribute to monitoring and improving system performance and reliability.

## Program Participation & Rotations

• Participate in rotational assignments across a variety of roles and locations within Energy Delivery (i.e. Field Operations, Major Projects, Reliability, and Asset Management)

• Gain experience in both office and field-based engineering work.

• Work alongside engineers and technical staff supporting electricity transmission and distribution.

• Contribute to projects involving system planning, risk mitigation, and project tracking.

• Participate in professional development activities, including semi-annual learning sessions and mentorship opportunities.

## Operations Support & Response

• Support operational activities related to electricity delivery for our customers.

• Respond to storm events and participate in power restoration efforts as required.

• Travel as necessary to support operational and project requirements.

## Health, Safety & Environmental Compliance

• Adhere to all Occupational Health and Safety rules and regulations.

• Promote and ensure personal safety and the safety of co-workers.

• Comply with organizational policies, including safety-sensitive requirements.

• Support environmental performance in alignment with environmental management system processes and initiatives.

These skills will make you successful:

## Education & Experience

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering (Electrical and Industrial) with graduation aligned with program start timing.

• Registered member or eligible for membership with Engineers Nova Scotia.

• An equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant experience may be considered.

## Technical/Job Specific Knowledge and Abilities

• Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to work effectively both independently and in a team environment.

• Strong communication and interpersonal skills.

• Adaptability and willingness to learn new tools, systems, and applications.

• Demonstrated commitment to continuous learning and professional development.

• Ability to work in both office and field environments.

• Valid driver's license and willingness to support emergency restoration efforts outside normal working hours.

• Willingness and ability to travel as required.

This position is considered a safety sensitive position. As such, the successful candidate must comply with the Emera Alcohol and Drug Policy which requires a confidential pre-employment alcohol and drug test in accordance with the Emera Alcohol and Drug Procedure.

You will be responsible for personal safety and that of co-workers by observing all Occupational Health and Safety Rules and Regulations. You will be accountable for environmental performance as it relates to the environmental management system processes and initiatives.

Learn more about our culture and values

At the Emera Group of Companies, you'll be part of an inclusive, respectful workplace where everyone is welcomed and supported. Come build a career as unique as you are: making an impact from Atlantic Canada to the world. Your experience and perspective will help us to safely deliver cleaner, more reliable energy to our customers.

If working in an innovative environment, challenging yourself, and shaping a cleaner energy future inspires you, we want to hear from you. Apply by September 29, 2026 and let us know why this role is right for you.

The perks of joining our team? We offer:

• Health & Wellbeing: A comprehensive benefits plan, 24/7 access to virtual health care services for you and your family through Dialogue, access to a free on-site fitness centre, Employee and Family Assistance Program, parental leave top-up plan and wellness benefits.

• Grow Your Career: Opportunities to advance within and between our affiliate companies, a focus on employee development and available sponsored education programs.

• Community Engagement & Care: Corporate investments in the places where our people live and work, mentoring opportunities, fundraising-matching & volunteer programs, various committees and employee resource groups, and scholarships for children of employees.

• Competitive Compensation: Short-term incentive plans and a Defined Contribution Pension Plan.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion at Emera

As one of Atlantic Canada's largest publicly traded companies, we are ranked one of Canada's Top 100 Employers, Top Employers for Young People and Top Diversity Employers. We know our success is driven by our dedicated teams and we strongly encourage applications from all qualified candidates, including persons who identify as racially visible, Indigenous, persons with disabilities, women in underrepresented roles and members of the 2SLGBTQ+ community.
Applicants from these equity groups may self-identify through the online application process. We support candidates and employees with access and accommodation needs and encourage you to let us know when you require accommodation.

Recruitment & Promotion Policy

The success of the Emera Company is driven by its people: a strong team with a shared commitment to support the Emera Company mission and values. The purpose of our recruitment policy is to provide a consistent framework to support fair and equitable attraction, hiring, and retention of the best talent for vacant positions. We are dedicated to maintaining a fair hiring process that provides equitable opportunities to all our applicants and is guided by our company values.

2238529.title: Senior Analyst, Market Intelligence
2238529.description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is growing?

## Who We Are

We are a global mining company dedicated to safely delivering nickel, copper, cobalt, and platinum group metals essential for the world's energy transition.

Our mission is to improve lives and shape a better future together.

From utensils to cellphones to satellites, our operations simplify daily life and enhance connectivity. Our metals are integral to life-saving medical equipment and the electric vehicles driving the fight against climate change – our work truly matters.

Join our diverse team of 15,000 talented individuals committed to transforming critical minerals into prosperity and sustainable development in countries like Canada, Brazil, Indonesia, the United Kingdom, and Japan. We invite you to use your skills with us and contribute to something meaningful and enduring.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking a Senior Analyst,Market Intelligence, to join our Commercial Team in Toronto, Ontario.

This is a permanent hybrid position.

As a Senior Market Analyst, you will provide market intelligence and strategic insights across Vale Base Metals' portfolio. You will conduct macroeconomic, commodity, and pricing analysis, develop market supply and demand forecasts, and assess competitive dynamics to support business planning and commercial decision-making.

Reporting to the Senior Manager, Market, you will play a key role in identifying market opportunities and risks while helping shape strategic initiatives through data-driven analysis and research.

## Key Responsibilities

• Develop and maintain commodity market supply and demand models, including market balances, market segments and regional trends.

• Analyze macroeconomic indicators, commodity prices, premiums, derivatives, and policy developments impacting global markets.

• Conduct competitive intelligence research on industry participants, projects, and market developments.

• Participate in discussions around market opportunities and risks to support short-term and long-term business and strategic planning

• Collaborate with other teams to develop market insights and recommendations.

• Prepare and deliver presentations, reports, and executive briefings on market trends and outlooks.

• Contribute to weekly, monthly, and quarterly reporting for internal and external stakeholders.

## About You

## Experience

• 3-5 years of experience in market intelligence, market research, commodity analysis, consulting, investment research, or capital markets.

• Experience within mining, metals, natural resources, energy, or related industries is considered an asset.

• Experience interpreting market, economic, and financial data to support business decisions.

## Education

• Undergraduate degree in Economics, Finance, Business, Engineering, Statistics, Commerce, or a related discipline.

## Skills & Competencies

• Strong understanding of commodity markets, economic analysis, and finance fundamentals.

• Excellent analytical and quantitative problem-solving abilities.

• Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills with the ability to communicate complex concepts clearly.

• Advanced proficiency in Excel and data modeling tools.

• Ability to synthesize large datasets into meaningful business insights.

• High attention to detail and strong organizational skills.

• Demonstrated initiative, curiosity, and strategic thinking.

## What We Offer You

• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans, and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare online

• Online training and career development opportunities

## Why Toronto

Toronto, Canada's largest city and financial hub, is a center of innovation, commerce, and culture. Known for its diverse economy and vibrant urban environment, Toronto offers unparalleled access to talent, technology, and global connectivity.

Our Toronto office serves as a strategic hub for corporate functions, technology development, and business operations. Here, we drive initiatives that support Vale Base Metals' global operations, leveraging advanced analytics, digital transformation, and strategic planning to ensure operational excellence across all regions.

Toronto's dynamic ecosystem enables collaboration with leading technology partners, universities, and research institutions, fostering innovation in mining and metals processing. This location is integral to shaping the future of sustainable mining and advancing our commitment to responsible resource development.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people feel comfortable to be themselves. Vale encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all.

We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

Accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Vale uses artificial intelligence to screen, assess, and/or select applicants for this position.

Pay Grade: F5T

## Minimum Starting Salary: CAD $89,000

Apply by: Friday, Oct 08, 2026

## #ValeBaseMetals

About Us
At the Department of Opportunities and Social Development (OSD), we are a large and diverse department providing a broad portfolio of programs and services including Child and Family Wellbeing (CFW), Employment Support Services(ESS), Income Assistance (IA), Homelessness and Supportive Housing, and Disability Support Program(DSP).

Through our services, we advocate and help vulnerable Nova Scotians be independent, self-reliant, and secure. We work collaboratively across the province with a strong dedicated network of supports and staff, to achieve desired and shared outcomes for all.

About Our Opportunity
Access Support Workers are responsible for transporting and supporting children, youth, and parents for family access visits, attendance for appointments, and other miscellaneous transportation needs as requested by the Social Workers in our various Child and Family Wellbeing Programs.

This is an exciting and rewarding career opportunity that works collaboratively to positively impact the lives of children, youth, and their families. You will join a dynamic and creative environment that celebrates diversity, promotes continued professional growth, and provides you with the opportunity to utilize your full range of skills, knowledge, and experience.

Primary Accountabilities
You will ensure the safety of children and provide basic childcare and transportation services. You may also provide oversight during contact between children and their immediate and extended families and support networks. You may be required to complete documentation confirming interactions as well as raising any issues that arise, along with other related duties to help ensure the smooth and efficient operation of the Provincial Access and Transportation Program.

Qualifications and Experience
You have completed an approved child & youth care worker diploma from a provincially approved post-secondary institution, or have at least two (2) years of related experience supporting children, youth, and/or families.

Experience in child welfare or other social services, including daycare or youth services, is desirable.

You must have a valid driver's license, have the ability to travel, and access to a reliable vehicle. You will use your personal vehicle, and your vehicle must be properly equipped for the transportation of infants and children.

You must have the ability to communicate in a professional manner using tact and diplomacy when dealing with sensitive situations as you support foster parents, social workers, in-care youth, daycare providers, schools, birth parents, and guardians.

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
We recognize equivalent combinations of training, education, and experience, providing opportunities for individuals with diverse backgrounds to contribute their skills and expertise. Equivalencies include, but are not limited to:

• A completed diploma or bachelor's degree in a related field (early childhood education (ECE), social sciences, social work, child and youth, social/ human services, disability support services, etc.)

Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
Extensive travel is required and necessitates considerable driving time, sometimes in adverse weather conditions. Visits are often scheduled at various times throughout the day, week, and weekends. Sometimes, hours and schedules will change requiring you to be flexible and willing to accommodate client's needs.

Your personal resiliency is essential to meet the physical and emotional demands of this position. You will be immersed in high stress situations and encounter distraught youth and family members.

Additional Information
This is a Part-time 50%, TEMPORARY employment opportunity with an anticipated end date of June 14, 2027. The appointment status ('term', 'temporary' or 'casual') is dependent on the start date of the successful candidate.

What We Offer
• Career Possibilities; you will have access to multiple career paths, career guidance, and ongoing training for every stage of your career.

• Rewarding and versatile work; daily, you will get to see the impact you have in and around your community.

• Engaging workplace; you are respected, supported, and valued. We have forward-thinking policies and strategies and incorporate your feedback to enhance our services.

About Our OpportunitySuccessful candidates will begin with two weeks of paid training designed to build the knowledge and skills required for effective snow and ice control operations. Following training, you will complete 45 hours of paid plowing experience under the guidance of an experienced Operator. Candidates must also successfully complete a driving assessment using a one-person-truck-plow equipped with a front plow, wing, and salt controls. This is a spare position, and hours of work are not guaranteed. Employees are called in as operational needs require. There may be an opportunity to participate in the Winter Wage Guarantee, which provides guaranteed work for a minimum of two weeks and may continue for the duration of the winter season. If placed on the Winter Wage Guarantee, the following will apply:
• Guaranteed 90 hours of pay every two weeks

• $0.95/per hour premium

• Opportunities for overtime

• Scheduled days off (2 days bi-weekly)

You are responsible for operating snow removal equipment such as snowplows, graders, and loaders. This includes general maintenance of the equipment, pre-and-post trip inspections, and daily logs. You may also be required to perform other work, such as maintaining signs, road surface repairs and traffic control.

Qualifications and Experience
Two years of experience or an acceptable equivalent of education, training, and relevant experience.

Minimum of Class III license with air brake endorsement.

Reading and writing skills are required to understand department documentation and to complete daily logs, inspection reports, etc.

The following is not required but considered helpful:

• A professional driving course from a recognized truck driving training facility

• Knowledge of hydraulic systems and mechanical skills

• Training completed at any accredited heavy/commercial equipment training institute

• Previous experience driving a manual transmission, operating trucks with salt and plow equipment, and/or knowledge of salt spreading systems

You are flexible, self-motivated, and comfortable working in all weather conditions. You are respectful and understand the value of good customer service. You will be working around environmental hazards, various traffic conditions and occasional work performed in a mechanical environment.

Additional Information
Applicants who are unable to apply online are invited to stop by the local Area Office located at 449 Jubilee Road, Hebbville to complete a paper application. Staff will be on site between 8:30 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. Monday to Friday to assist you. Please bring a current copy of your Drivers Abstract.

About Us
The Department of Municipal Affairs is dedicated to working with municipalities to build healthy, vibrant, and safe communities throughout Nova Scotia. Municipal Affairs provides programs, grants, and funding opportunities for municipalities and community groups. The Department also provides services and guidance to municipalities in many areas including land use planning, budget planning and finance, infrastructure development, policy and program development.

About Our Opportunity
The Director, Building Codes and Standards provides strategic leadership for Nova Scotia's building code system and serves as the department's senior authority on building code policy, governance, adoption, interpretation, and implementation. This is a unique opportunity to lead the continual improvement of a provincial regulatory program that influences public safety, housing supply, accessibility, affordability, energy efficiency, and economic growth across the province.

As a trusted advisor to government and municipal partners, you will lead the development of recommendations on building code adoption and implementation, oversee key governance bodies, and represent Nova Scotia in national and intergovernmental forums. You will work at the intersection of technical expertise, public policy, partner engagement, and government decision-making to ensure Nova Scotia's building code framework remains effective, responsive, and aligned with provincial priorities.

Primary Accountabilities
In this role, you will:

• Lead the strategic direction, governance, administration, and continual improvement of Nova Scotia's building code program.

• Provide executive-level advice to senior leadership and government on building codes, regulatory modernization, and associated policy matters.

• Lead analysis, consultation, and recommendations regarding the adoption and implementation of national model codes and related standards.

• Oversee the governance and effective operation of associated agencies, boards, and commissions responsible for building code matters.

• Represent Nova Scotia in federal, provincial, territorial, and national forums related to building codes and regulatory development.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with municipalities, building officials, industry associations, professional bodies, and other collaborators.

• Lead consultation and engagement processes to support balanced, practical, and informed regulatory decisions.

• Collaborate with associations, municipalities and building officials to make available improved guidance, tools, training, and implementation supports.

• Identify emerging issues, risks, and opportunities and provide timely strategic advice on matters with technical, policy, operational, and political implications.

• Lead a high-performing team and manage assigned human, financial, and project resources.

Based on operational requirements, the position may supervise professional, technical, policy, administrative, or project staff.

Qualifications and Experience
You have significant experience in building codes, construction standards, regulatory development, public administration, or a closely related field. You are recognized for your ability to navigate complex technical and policy issues, provide strategic advice, and build credibility with diverse stakeholders.

You bring:

• Extensive experience interpreting and applying complex legislation, regulations, standards, technical requirements, or building codes.

• Demonstrated experience providing strategic advice to senior leaders, executives, or government decision-makers.

• Experience leading complex initiatives involving multiple collaborators with competing interests and priorities.

• Strong understanding of regulatory development, governance, public policy, and government decision-making processes.

• Exceptional communication and relationship-management skills, with the ability to translate technical issues into clear and practical advice.

• Proven ability to lead consultation processes, build consensus, and manage sensitive issues with policy, technical, operational, and political considerations.

• Strong judgment, strategic thinking, and problem-solving abilities.

The following would be considered assets:

• Experience working with municipalities, municipal building officials, or development and construction partners.

• Experience participating in national standards development, intergovernmental forums, advisory committees, or regulatory bodies.

• Professional designation as a Professional Engineer or Registered Architect.

• Certification or significant experience as a Building Official or building code professional.

• Experience leading organizational, regulatory, or governance modernization initiatives.

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: interviews, presentations, written exercises, and reference checks.

Equivalency
We recognize equivalent combinations of training, education, and experience, providing opportunities for individuals with diverse backgrounds to contribute their skills and expertise. Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

This position operates in a fast-paced and highly visible environment involving competing priorities, tight timelines, and complex issues. Occasional travel, as well as evening or weekend meetings, may be required.

Please quote the competition number and the Zone you are applying for as noted above on your application.

About Us
Maintaining our Provincial Infrastructure is no small job.

The Department of Public Works supports Nova Scotia's 23,000 kilometers of roads and highways and 4,100 bridges.

If you enjoy operating Heavy Equipment, and seeking your next opportunity where you will directly contribute to the safety of our province, we want to hear from you.

About Our Opportunity
Under the supervision of the Area Manager, the Equipment Operator Trainer supports the development of Equipment Operators. This role plays an essential part in Equipment Operator onboarding, seasonal preparation, documentation quality, and ensuring procedures are followed correctly.

Trainers are expected to work proactively and independently, using structured work plans aligned with operational priorities and seasonal demands. They collaborate closely with Area Managers, Operations Supervisors, Equipment Operators, and Equipment Instructors/Inspectors (EQIIs) to ensure training and documentation efforts are consistent, useful, and responsive to District needs.

This position provides structured and assigned training support and does not replace supervisory functions or routine peer-to-peer coaching that occurs among Equipment Operators as part of normal operations.

Primary Accountabilities
As an Equipment Operator Trainer, your role is pivotal in helping the public arrive safely at their destination. The main responsibilities of this position include:

• Actively monitoring and supporting Equipment Operator development, documenting progress and offering feedback to Supervisors

• Supporting the coaching of new and existing Equipment Operators on the safe performance of tasks such as plowing, ditching, ice blading, grading, and other equipment operations. Tracking progress of new Equipment Operators and supporting scheduling OPTP testing with EQII when Equipment Operators have achieved sufficient experience

• Ensuring Equipment Operators are following safety protocols while operating, including trip inspections, hazard assessments, protective equipment, and safe use of attachments

• Reporting serious or repeated performance concerns to the Operations Supervisor for action

• Preparing equipment for training, including ensuring it is operationally fit, trip inspections are complete, equipment is fuelled, attachments installed, etc.

• Providing hands-on instruction and demonstrations to ensure Equipment Operators are proficient in the safe and effective operation of machinery

Qualifications and Experience
To be eligible, you must have a High school diploma or GED equivalent and minimum 5 years of experience operating relevant equipment.

You must have access to a reliable motor vehicle and a class 3 Driver's License with Air Brake Endorsement and Condition 15 is required. Applicants must possess this license at the time of hire. A Class 1 license is considered an asset.

You must be able to demonstrate the ability to operate a wide variety of heavy equipment in all seasons and to work independently and manage priorities using structured task planning.

As the ideal candidate, you are flexible, self-motivated, and comfortable working in adverse weather conditions. As part of our team, you bring professionalism and hold a high standard for client service with proven organizational skills, including tracking training-related records and reviewing documentation such as logs and inspection forms and Computer literacy (e.g., digital forms, spreadsheets, email).

You will be assessed on the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: practical driving test on a tandem truck, written examination, interview, and reference checks.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
You will be working in a range of weather conditions, from extreme heat to cold, and managing environmental hazards such as uneven terrain and slippery surfaces. The Equipment Operator Trainer may also need to work near moving traffic, which presents safety risks.

Occasionally, work may take place in areas with machinery, resulting in exposure to smoke and fumes. The role also involves environments with elevated levels of noise, dust, and vibration. These conditions require a high level of adaptability and situational awareness to ensure safety and efficiency.

Additional InformationYour designated work location is 18 Hardscratch Road, Yarmouth. Based on operational requirements, you may be required to travel to and work from locations within Shelburne (Zone 32), Yarmouth (Zone 34), and Saulnierville (Zone 35).

WHO WE ARE
Mariner innovates always and everywhere, turning novel ideas into practical solutions. From products and services to venture creation, we build better futures powered by people. Our purpose has always been to be a great, everlasting technology company for those who make an impact - elevating people, data, and technology in the best way to solve hard problems. We partner with people embracing change, leveraging data, cybersecurity, cloud, and change management to drive successful business outcomes that matter to our customers.

Mariners build for change. Like SHIFT Energy, our energy management and decarbonization company. Or East Valley Ventures, created to scale social economic impact in our communities through investment and mentorship of emerging change-makers and their companies.

Mariner s purpose has always been to be a great, everlasting technology company and the core values that guide us every day are:

## OUR VALUES

• We care for our team.

• We care about the impact we have on our community.

• We serve by solving complex problems.

• We grow because growth fuels opportunities.

• We innovate always and everywhere.

• We build a business that lasts.

## OVERVIEW OF THE ROLE:

We are seeking an experienced and dynamic Project Manager to join our team. In this role, you will lead and oversee complex technology projects, collaborating with cross-functional teams to ensure successful project delivery and client satisfaction. Your ability to manage projects from initiation to completion, mitigate risks, and drive results will be crucial in shaping our project management practice.

## WHAT YOU LL BE DOING IN THE ROLE:

• Plan, lead, coordinate, and oversee the implementation of complex client-based projects and deliverables.

• Identify program/project milestones, critical success factors, and resource requirements.

• Ensure that risks are proactively identified with mitigation strategies developed and monitored while also ensuring that project issues are resolved and appropriately escalated; maintain data related to key risks and issues including the status and progress.

• Engage project stakeholders regularly by keeping them informed of delivery progress, risks and issues and manage expectations on deliverables.

• Lead initiatives involving a significant level of business or technology transformation and organizational change.

• Collaborate efficiently with partners and vendors to deliver projects according to plan.

• Manage budgets and align project deliverables to expected business benefits.

• Negotiate changes in scope, budget or schedule with sponsor and steering committees.

• Analyze, problem solve, and research project elements as required.

• Provide proactive leadership and direction to Project Management and Delivery teams.

## WHAT SKILLS / QUALIFICATIONS YOU LL NEED TO DO THE JOB:

• 10+ years of project management experience in large sized projects.

• Demonstrated experience within a team environment where the candidate was called on to perform tasks in a mixture of collaborative and autonomous modes.

• Demonstrated and verifiable experience in developing and delivering tailored written and verbal communications to a varied stakeholder base; including senior and executive-level, technical, and business resources.

• A minimum of five years of demonstrated and verifiable experience as a project manager on projects with multiple stakeholder communities.

• Strong understanding of the consulting process, project management, organizational change management.

• Ability to communicate effectively with a broad range of audiences (technical, management, executive).

• Bachelor s degree in business, engineering, computer science, or related technical area.

• Experience working in client-based consulting role is highly desirable.

• Relevant industry certifications are an asset (PMP, PROSCI).

• Ability to work hybrid or onsite model is preferred.

• Ability to meet any security screening and Controlled Goods Program requirements associated with the role.

## AND YOU ARE...

• Always improving your skills and knowledge: you want to be the best at what you do

• Curious and creative; comfortable taking on new problems and challenges

• A self-starter with the ability to recommend priorities to the project leader

• Comfortable working through problems and figuring things out with minimal supervision

• Great problem-solving skills: thorough and reliable

• Able to work in a team: share knowledge and assist other team members

• A good communicator: able to explain your ideas and recommendations

• Well organized and dependable under pressure: you manage your time effectively

• Energized by our company values!

## MARINER OFFERS YOU:

• A values-driven workplace where people really matter

• Hybrid work environment.

• Competitive salary, retirement savings program, and rewards program

• Comprehensive health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance plans and access to e-health care

• Paid vacation, maternity/parental leave, paid sick leave and paid Mariner MyLife days

• Unlimited training

## WHY MARINER?

We believe in making a positive impact in the communities where we live and work! 2197862.description:
## Job Title: Industrial Mechanic/Millwright

## Location: Oxford, Nova Scotia

## TP-OFF-9048

Oxford Frozen Foods, a member of the Bragg Group of Companies, is a family-owned international business that has over 1200 employees across eight manufacturing facilities and two large farming operations in Atlantic Canada and the United States. As the world's largest provider of wild blueberries and one of North America's leading producers of premium frozen carrots, onion rings, and battered appetizers, they continue to grow their impact through innovation and quality.

Partnered with Meridia, Oxford Frozen Foods is looking for an Industrial Mechanic/Millwright to provide support within their flagship facility based in Oxford, Nova Scotia.

## Role Description

As the Industrial Mechanic/Millwright, you will perform preventative and predictive maintenance on highly automated equipment while also troubleshooting and repairing robotic, mechanical, and PLC-driven systems. Working as part of a skilled maintenance team, you will be responsible for ensuring equipment operates safely and efficiently. This position involves a rotating shift schedule of two weeks on days and two weeks on nights, with every other weekend off.

## Your responsibilities will include:

• Troubleshooting, repairing, replacing, and installing various types of automated production equipment.

• Performing preventive maintenance on the equipment to ensure smooth operations.

• Work closely with fellow technicians, operators, and supervisors to prioritize repairs and share technical knowledge. Participate in shift handovers and team meetings to ensure continuity, communicate ongoing concerns, and support coordinated efforts across departments.

• Support sustainability efforts by monitoring production areas for energy and material inefficiencies such as compressed air leaks, water waste, or product spills. Take initiative by helping implement solutions that align with environmental sustainability goals.

• Actively contribute to a safety-first culture. Follow all safety protocols and ensure that workstations and surrounding environments remain organized and hazard-free.

## Your Qualifications

The ideal candidate will have proven experience working with automated production equipment in an industrial maintenance or manufacturing environment. You bring hands-on experience with preventative and predictive maintenance practices, and a strong technical understanding of mechanical systems. You are comfortable interpreting schematics and using diagnostic tools. You are a team player who can also work independently. You also have the ability to excel in a fast-paced environment and are adaptable to changing priorities.

## Your qualifications include:

• Completion of an Industrial Mechanic/Millwright diploma; Red Seal certification is an asset (third or fourth-year apprentices may be considered).

• Applicants with significant hands-on experience in mechanical or electro-mechanical roles may also be considered in place of formal education.

• Prior experience in a manufacturing setting or industrial maintenance is preferred.

• Comfortable reading and interpreting schematics, blueprints, and equipment manuals.

• Familiarity with preventative and predictive maintenance practices.

• Stainless steel welding and fabrication experience is considered an asset

• Familiarity with safety best practices is an asset.

• Able to work in a fast-paced environment and multitask effectively.

Oxford Frozen Foods offers more than just a job, it's a chance to build a stable, long-term career with a company that invests in its people. With competitive wages, annual profit sharing, health and dental benefits, a matching pension plan, and a unique housing loan program, Oxford supports both your professional development and personal wellbeing. Employees gain hands-on experience with cutting-edge automation in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment, while contributing to a company that values sustainability, innovation, and community.

To express interest in this opportunity please apply online by clicking "Apply Now" below.

For more information contact Thomas Pugh, Partner, at 902-818-4506 and tpugh@kbrs.ca or Heather Simmons, Senior Recruitment Specialist at 902-421-2335 and hsimmons@kbrs.ca. If you require accommodation to participate in the recruitment process, please let us know.

Meridia Recruitment Solutions is pleased to partner with MCA Consultants in the search for a Director of Electrical Engineering within their Dartmouth, NS office.

MCA Consultants is a multidisciplinary mechanical and electrical consulting engineering firm with offices in Charlottetown, Prince Edward Island, and Dartmouth, Nova Scotia. With an established client base and extensive project work in the region, MCA Consultants is now investing in a dedicated local Electrical team to better support its Nova Scotia partnerships.

This is a rare opportunity for an engineering leader to take ownership of MCA Consultants' growing electrical engineering portfolio in Nova Scotia. As Director of Electrical Engineering, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the firm's regional growth strategy, developing client relationships, and building a high-performing team to support an expanding Nova Scotia project portfolio.

## About MCA Consultants

With a team of nearly 60 engineers, designers, technologists, and support professionals, MCA Consultants delivers practical, innovative, and cost-effective engineering and project management solutions to clients throughout Atlantic Canada. Their electrical engineering team designs building systems for educational, healthcare, recreational, residential, commercial, pharmaceutical, food-processing, and industrial facilities, as well as municipal infrastructure projects including underground electrical distribution, street lighting, and pumping stations. Their services include electrical power distribution, lighting and lighting controls, fire alarm, security, structured cabling, audiovisual systems, emergency power generation, electric vehicle charging infrastructure, and photovoltaic (solar) systems, and industrial instrumentation and control cabling.

Their projects typically begin in conceptual or preliminary design and continue through detailed design, tendering, contract administration, and construction support. MCA Consultants works closely with architects, developers, building owners, and municipal, provincial and federal government agencies to deliver successful projects throughout Atlantic Canada.

Role Description
You will play a key role in delivering high-quality building services design while also helping to expand MCA's existing footprint in Halifax. This role offers a combination of technical leadership, client engagement, and business development, with a strong emphasis on relationship-building and project delivery. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to take ownership of MCA Consultants' local electrical engineering portfolio and contribute directly to the firm's continued growth throughout Nova Scotia.

Key Responsibilities:

• Design electrical systems for commercial, institutional, multi-residential, and industrial projects.

• Lead projects from concept through construction, ensuring quality, efficiency, schedule adherence, and budget performance.

• Prepare and review design drawings, specifications, technical reports, and system analyses, including load calculations and equipment selection.

• Conduct site visits, attend project meetings, and liaise with clients, consultants, contractors, and other project stakeholders.

• Coordinate multidisciplinary project teams, including CAD Technicians and junior staff.

• Review shop drawings and support contract administration during construction.

• Build and maintain strong client relationships while identifying and pursuing new business opportunities.

• Provide leadership, mentorship, recruitment support, workforce planning, and professional development for the Nova Scotia electrical engineering team.

• Contribute to strategic planning, business growth, and MCA Consultants' presence within the engineering, development, and construction communities across Nova Scotia.

• Foster a culture of technical excellence, collaboration, and innovation.

Your Qualifications
The ideal candidate is a technically proficient and relationship-oriented Electrical Engineer who is energized by the opportunity to help lead the continued growth of MCA's Electrical Engineering practice in Nova Scotia.
Your qualifications include:

• Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering.

• Registered (or eligible for registration) as a P.Eng. with Engineers Nova Scotia.

• Extensive experience in electrical building systems design.

• Strong knowledge of applicable codes and standards (Canadian Electrical Code, National Building Code).

• Experience with power distribution, lighting systems, and fire alarm design (power generation experience is an asset).

• Proven ability to manage projects and collaborate across multidisciplinary teams.

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build lasting client relationships.

• Self-driven, adaptable, and capable of working independently in a flexible environment.

• Interest in business development and leadership is considered a strong asset.

Why Join MCA Consultants?
This is more than a leadership role. It is an opportunity to build and shape the future of MCA Consultants' electrical engineering practice in Nova Scotia while helping drive the continued growth of a respected Atlantic Canadian consulting firm. For an ambitious Electrical Engineer with a passion for leadership, client development, and business growth, this role offers the opportunity to make a lasting impact. You'll have the autonomy to influence strategy, build a team, strengthen client partnerships, and help shape the future direction of MCA Consultants' electrical engineering practice across Nova Scotia.
MCA Consultants offers:

• Flexible, hybrid-friendly work environment

• Competitive compensation

• Comprehensive health and dental benefits

• RRSP matching

• Generous paid time off

• A collaborative, non-corporate culture where your input matters

• Exposure to a wide variety of exciting and impactful projects

• A clear pathway to leadership, and potential ownership, for the right individual

Competition # : 49855

Department: Service Nova Scotia

Location: TRURO HEIGHTS

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: NSGEU - NSPG

Closing Date: 29-Sep-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
At Service Nova Scotia, we impact every citizen, business and municipality in Nova Scotia. Our mandate is to design and deliver programs and services to meet the needs of our clients and the public good through a culture of excellence.

Service Nova Scotia's vision is to be a recognized leader in service and public protection that delivers trusted, accessible, modern programs, and contributes to Nova Scotia as a safe and desirable place to live, work and do business. To learn more about our Department, please click here: Department of Service Nova Scotia - Government of Nova Scotia. Department of Service Nova Scotia - Government of Nova Scotia

About Our Opportunity
Under the supervision of the Senior Property Mapper, you maintain, and upgrade property mapping using information from the Registry (title documents and plans of survey or subdivision).

Primary Accountabilities
• Maintaining and revising property boundaries (as described in parcel descriptions and survey plans) and the Land Information Network (LIN-NS) database by interpreting and verifying property ownership information (from documents affecting title/ownership).

• Maintaining Land Registration documents pertaining to subdivision/consolidation plans and instruments of subdivision, creating the required relations between new and existing PIDs.

• Reviewing parcel descriptions (PDCA), verifying mapping graphics, and creating new parcels as required through interpretation of registered documents/plans (RPA) for Land Registration migration.

• Providing support to Property Valuation Services Corporation (PVSC) and Municipal Units by resolving linkages between the LIN-NS and IASWorld (PVSC) databases and maintaining the currency of land ownership, property location and lot size changes of real property accounts in the Provincial Property Assessment Roll and in Municipal databases.

• Working collaboratively with other government agencies and the public, you will help to improve the quality of the NSPRD and IASWorld databases through daily processes and special projects as required.

Qualifications and Experience
To be considered for this position, you have completed a Technical program in a related field (approved courses in drafting or graphics, survey principles, or property law) or an acceptable equivalent. A solid working knowledge of mapping techniques (as it applies to property mapping) is essential. A working knowledge of Provincial Statutes (Land Registration Act, Registry Act, Municipal Government Act) relating to real property is also required. Completion of courses in computer/windows operating systems, computer software used in the digital mapping updating process is also important. In addition, you possess excellent communications skills, the ability to interact with people in a professional manner with a customer-focused approach and you are a collaborative team player. You also have excellent communication skills, attention to detail with superior analytical thinking and problem-solving skills.

Direct knowledge of the LIN-NS and IASWorld databases, additional education/experience in software, and the handling and maintaining of files contained in a map library will be considered definite assets. A working knowledge of Departmental programs and related legislation, and/or experience working in a legal setting (with title searching) as well as bilingualism in French and English would be considered assets.

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Additional Information
This competition will be leveraged to fill multiple vacancies in Truro, Nova Scotia.

What We Offer
• Career Development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career.

• Engaging workplace. Our Employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in. We have forward-thinking policies and strategies.

• Countless career paths.

Pay Grade: TE 17 - TE 23

Salary Range: $1,967.62 - $2,944.94 Bi-Weekly

Employment Equity Statement: Our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative, at all job levels, of the citizens we serve. The Government of Nova Scotia has an Employment Equity Policy, and we welcome applications from Indigenous People, African Nova Scotians, Persons of African Descent, Racialized Persons, Persons with Disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+ Persons and Women in occupations or positions where they are under-represented. If you are a member of one of these equity groups, you are encouraged to self-identify on your electronic application.

Accommodation Statement: We are committed to providing an inclusive and accessible recruitment process. Candidates may request accommodations based on any grounds protected by the Human Rights Act. If you require an accommodation throughout the recruitment process, please contact us at competitions@novascotia.ca.

Failure to apply correctly means that your application will not be given first consideration as a bargaining unit applicant, and will only be included if external applications are pursued.

External applicants and current casual employees will only be considered if there are no qualified civil service bargaining unit candidates. PLEASE NOTE: Candidates will not be considered for an interview if applications are incomplete or are missing information.

If you accept a position that requires PSSP contributions, your pension payments must be stopped. Please contact the Nova Scotia Pension Services Corporation for more information.

## DIETITIAN

## Position Identification

TITLE: Dietitian
DEPARTMENT: Department of Support Services
REPORTS TO: Administrator

## Position Objective

To ensure the effectiveness and efficiency of the Department of Support Services

## Position Specification

## Qualifications:

• Bachelor of Science in Applied Human Nutrition (Dietetics) or Nutrition Major

• Approved Dietetic Internship Program

• Professional Dietitian Membership with the Nova Scotia Regulator of Dietetics (NSRD) and/or Canadian Association

• Management/Leadership Certificate

• Minimum of three years senior leadership experience in a Health Care Facility, preferably in a long term care setting or a minimum of five years management experience in nutrition in a medium to large size team

• Extensive knowledge and experience in Labour Relations and applying the terms of a Collective Agreement

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook)

• Experience in Strategic Planning (asset)

## Competencies

• Thinking Capabilities

• Decisiveness

• Strategic Orientation

• Leadership Effectiveness

• Development of People

• Team Leadership

• Organizational

• Time Management

• Nutritional Services Management

• Detailed Orientated

• Thorough

• Achievement Orientated

• Human Resource Management

## Characteristics & Behaviors:

• Accountable

• Disciplined

• Initiative

• Adaptable

• Enthusiastic

• Motivated

• Approachable

• Flexible

• Professional

• Compassionate

• Friendly

• Reliable

• Cooperative

• Honest

• Responsible

## Position Summary

Reporting to the Administrator, the Dietitian is responsible for defining and for the direction, coordination, quality, safety, planning and delivery of all matters related to Nutritional Services for the facility. As a member of the Senior Leadership Team, the Dietitian assists in the development, administration and coordination of the departmental policies and procedures and makes reports and recommendations to the Administrator regarding the function of the Nutritional Services Department.

The Dietitian is responsible for assessing the Clinical Nutritional needs of all residents of Glen Haven Manor upon admission and complete assessment follow up annually and as required. The Dietitian is also responsible for the planning, organizing of the menu and then reviewing or making changes based on the Nutritional Guide of Canada and all therapeutic diet programs. The Dietitian collaborates with all departments to ensure activities are planned and coordinated appropriately, integrates suggestions identified through Resident and Family Council, participates in all planning related to the priorities of the facility and the needs of residents.

The Dietitian conducts periodic evaluations and survey inspections to identify deficiencies and develops and implements a corrective action plan. The Dietitian ensures all information related to nutritional service requirements and keeping a resident's environment safe and clean are implemented in accordance with the commitment to providing exceptional individualized quality care.

## Duties & Responsibilities

## Management and Leadership:

• Assesses the Clinical Nutritional needs of all residents of Glen Haven Manor upon admission and complete assessment follow up annually and as required. The Dietitian is also responsible for the planning, organizing of the menu and then reviewing or making changes based on the Nutritional Guide of Canada and all therapeutic diet programs.

• Recommends therapeutic diets, oral nutritional supplements, and texture modifications.

• Participates in resident care conferences and contributing to interdisciplinary care planning.

• Works closely with the nursing staff, including Director of Care; nurses and additional members of the care team, using an interdisciplinary approach to ensure coordinated nutritional support for residents.

• Educates residents, families, and staff on nutrition-related topics.

• Establishes and maintains high standards for employee performance and conducts performance reviews.

• Participates in the development and coordination of strategic planning.

• Provides effective leadership by ensuring that best practices protocols are implemented, practiced, upgraded, and maintained by duly qualified and licensed professionals.

• Responsible for the direction of site-based operations staff. This includes responsibilities regarding disciplinary matters, training, retraining, quality assurance and client satisfaction.

• Coordinates and provides accountabilities for all departmental activities to insure the effective and efficient delivery of services of the department including matters related client admissions, client service, family liaison, governmental liaison, accreditation, licensing, professional standards, and professional outsourcing of services required by the department.

• Accounts for the smooth, effective, and efficient operation of the department, and more particularly, to create and support a work environment conducive to a positive staff morale and a profession staff approach in all their interactions with clients, client families, co-workers, and the public at large.

• Facilitates coordination and communication of matters that have inter-departmental implication or impact.

• Provides leadership and participates in the various standing or ad hoc committees and teams with a commitment to continuously improve the standard of care or the general environment conducive to the delivery of quality care.

• Actively participates in the planning, organizing, and directing of the activities in Departments within the designated span of control. Observe all by-laws, rules, and regulations and the Facility's compliance with federal and provincial statutes and regulations.

• Communication on a routine basis with Senior Leaders/Managers, to advise the Administrator on matters pertinent to services and care within the organization.

• Participate in the public relations programs within the facility and community, with other facilities and community agencies.

• Participate in personal professional development.

• Develops, implements, and modifies policies and procedures.

• Instills a positive service-minded attitude and feeling of pride and responsibility in the Support Services staff by demonstrating a personal enthusiasm and team spirit.

• Accounts for the overall comfort and satisfaction of residents as it relates to departmental services.

## Quality Assurance and Compliance:

• Ensures departmental compliance with all requirements imposed including matters related to information management, policies, procedures, statutory requirements, and professional standards.

• Establish and maintain the standards of the Canadian Council on Accreditation for Health Care Facilities that are relevant to the profession for which there is line authority and ensures active participation in the Quality Assurance Programs of the facility.

• Performs an important role in the quality assurance process by performing inspections of all Nutritional services provided, and ensure compliance with all applicable statutory, regulatory or industry standards and codes. Reporting responsibilities include inspection reports, client satisfaction surveys, equipment inspections, daily team reports, project completion reports, and other quality assurance tasks.

## Safety Health & Environmental Affairs

• Complete all job tasks in accordance with the Standard Operating Procedures and Safe Work Practices and acknowledge health and safety as everyone's responsibility.

• Active participation in activities associated with the management of workplace safety, health and environmental affairs as endorsement of a progressive safety culture.

• Applies infection control practices and standards precautions, as required.

## Working Conditions

• Hours of Work - Monday to Friday (including evenings, weekends and holidays as determined by department & organizational need)

• Lead staff corrective action and disciplinary processes.

• Interface with residents, families, and visitors

• Report and respond to emergency situations.

## Physical Requirements

• Light to moderate working conditions

## Direct Reports

• Support Services Supervisor, Support Services Team consisting of Cooks and Nutritional Services Workers.

## Acknowledgement

This job description has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this classification. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities and qualifications required of employees assigned to the role.

2237686.title: Senior Vice President & Chief Financial Officer
2237686.description:
IMP Group is a privately-held investment corporation, working to support our diverse business divisions to develop and deliver substantial value and growth in industries ranging from aerospace to healthcare. At IMP, we know our employees are central to our business success and so we cultivate and support our teams to be strategic, competitive, forward-thinking, resilient and innovative. If you are searching for a distinctive professional challenge, the exciting next step in your career is here at IMP.

About IMP Group
Founded in 1967 and headquartered in Halifax, Nova Scotia, IMP Group is a privately held investment corporation with a diversified portfolio of operating companies spanning aerospace and defence, aviation, information technology, healthcare, industrial services, financial services, and customer experience solutions industries.

IMP Group's decentralized operating model empowers entrepreneurial leadership within its portfolio companies while providing strong governance, strategic oversight, and disciplined capital allocation at the corporate level. The organization has built a reputation for operational excellence, long-term value creation, and meaningful economic impact across Canada and select international markets.

Guided by its core values of Safety, Integrity, Engagement, Diversity, Respect, Security, and Passion, IMP Group fosters a culture of accountability, collaboration, and long-term partnership with employees, customers, suppliers, and communities.

Position Summary
Our CFO is retiring after more than 30 years with the Company, and we are seeking a strategic financial leader to become our next Senior Vice President & Chief Financial Officer.

Reporting to the President & Chief Executive Officer, the CFO is a key member of the executive leadership team responsible for the overall financial stewardship, strategic planning, capital allocation, and risk management of IMP Group and its diverse portfolio of businesses.

The CFO will serve as a trusted advisor to the President & CEO, Board of Directors, shareholders, and business leaders across the organization. This executive will provide financial leadership that supports sustainable growth, drives operational excellence, and ensures the organization maintains the financial strength and flexibility required to execute its long-term strategy.

The successful candidate will possess the experience and business acumen to navigate a complex, multi-company environment while balancing strategic vision with disciplined execution.

Key ResponsibilitiesFinancial Accountability
• Lead all aspects of corporate finance, accounting, treasury, tax, financial planning and analysis, reporting, and internal controls.

• Ensure the integrity, accuracy, and timeliness of financial reporting across the organization.

• Oversee budgeting, forecasting, performance measurement, and financial reporting processes.

• Maintain strong financial governance and compliance frameworks across all operating companies.

• Monitor business performance and recommend actions to improve profitability, cash flow, and return on invested capital.

• Utilize data, analytics, and key performance indicators to drive decision-making.

• Challenge assumptions constructively and provides clear, fact-based recommendations.

• Maintain focus on profitability, cash flow, operational efficiency, and return on investment.

Financial Governance and Risk Management
• Provide executive oversight for company risk management procedures and reporting.

• Ensure robust financial controls, compliance programs, and governance practices are maintained throughout the organization.

• Partner with legal, audit, and operational leaders to mitigate financial, operational, cybersecurity, regulatory, and reputational risks.

• Work closely with IMP's external audit firm to ensure the integrity, accuracy and transparency of the company's financial statements.

• Support Board and Audit Committee governance responsibilities through effective reporting and communication.

• Create and maintain a culture where risk is appropriately identified, assessed, and managed.

• Ensure compliance, transparency, and accountability while enabling business growth.

Strategic Leadership
• Partner with the CEO and executive team to develop and execute IMP Group's strategic and financial plans.

• Provide financial insight and analysis to support major business decisions, investments, acquisitions, divestitures, and growth initiatives.

• Think beyond individual business units to align the overall company and shareholder perspective.

• Evaluate market opportunities, economic trends, and business performance to identify strategic risks and opportunities.

• Support business unit leaders in achieving financial and operational objectives while maintaining accountability and autonomy within the decentralized operating model.

• Develop and execute financial strategies across multiple industries and business models.

• Lead and develop a high-performing finance organization capable of supporting a complex and diversified business portfolio.

• Foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, collaboration, and operational excellence.

• Mentor finance leaders across the company and strengthen succession planning and talent development.

• Champion IMP Group's values and promote a culture of integrity, respect, engagement, and inclusion.

• Create an environment that empowers operational finance leaders while maintaining strong accountability for results.

Capital Allocation and Investment Management
• Develop and execute capital allocation strategies aligned with shareholder objectives and long-term value creation.

• Lead financial evaluation and due diligence activities related to acquisitions, investments, partnerships, and strategic transactions.

• Optimize capital structures across the portfolio and oversee relationships with lenders, financial institutions, and external advisors.

• Understand the operational drivers of business performance and translate financial insights into actionable business decisions.

• Evaluate opportunities through both a financial and strategic lens.

• Possess a strong understanding of capital-intensive businesses, regulated industries, and growth-oriented enterprises.

• Demonstrate sound judgment in evaluating risk, investment opportunities, acquisitions, and resource allocation.

Executive Influence, Board and Stakeholder Relations
• Serve as a principal financial advisor to the President & CEO, Board of Directors, and shareholders.

This role will maintain leadership continuity while overseeing engineering priorities, infrastructure safety and reliability, lifecycle planning, maintenance, rehabilitation, and capital investment.

## WHAT YOU LL BE DOING IN THE ROLE:

• Build effective relationships with employees, executives, government representatives, regulators, contractors, and other stakeholders.

• Minimum of 15 years of progressive experience, or an equivalent combination of education and senior-level experience, in engineering, construction, infrastructure, or asset management.

• Executive- or Director-level leadership experience within a complex environment.

• Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary engineering and operational teams and deliver results in evolving environments.

• Knowledge of public-sector governance, procurement, regulatory compliance, and safety requirements.

• Strong executive communication, stakeholder-management, relationship-building, and decision-making skills.

## AND YOU ARE...

• Curious and creative; comfortable taking on new problems and challenges

• A self-starter with the ability to recommend priorities to the project leader

• Comfortable working through problems and figuring things out with minimal supervision

• Great problem-solving skills: thorough and reliable

• Able to work in a team: share knowledge and assist other team members

• A good communicator: able to explain your ideas and recommendations

• Well organized and dependable under pressure: you manage your time effectively

• Energized by our company values!

## MARINER OFFERS YOU:

• A values-driven workplace where people really matter

• Onsite work environment.

• Competitive salary, retirement savings program, and rewards program

• Comprehensive health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance plans and access to e-health care

• Paid vacation, maternity/parental leave, paid sick leave and paid Mariner MyLife days

• Unlimited training

## WHY MARINER?

We believe in making a positive impact in the communities where we live and work! Not only are we passionate about nurturing a thriving technology sector here in Atlantic Canada, but we are also committed to solving technology challenges that will make an impact worldwide. Technology is everlasting, and we take pride in connecting world class talent to world class projects and business solutions.

If you are an IT Professional, Software Professional, or Management Consultant, that is passionate about career development, data, and problem solving, we want to hear from you! If this sounds like someone you know, share this with them so they do not miss the opportunity to experience Mariner!

To achieve this, we know we need to be all in on training and development of our team so we can continue to move the needle in the technology sector together. Of course, we offer competitive compensation and benefits packages to our team, but our competitive edge is the development and training that our team experiences every day.

Be part of our vibrant community that values diversity and embraces inclusion at every level. We are committed to fostering a culture where individuals from all backgrounds and walks of life feel empowered to contribute their unique perspectives. Our collaborative environment celebrates the richness of ideas and experiences, and we believe that by embracing diversity, we can achieve greater innovation and excellence together. Come and help us create a workplace that reflects the beautiful tapestry of our global community.
