• You demonstrate a commitment to the principles of human rights equity and diversity, and experience promoting a respectful work and learning environment for students, staff and faculty.

• You possess excellent interpersonal skills that enable you to interact with a diversity of people and support resolution of issues.

• Your superb team working skills enable you to contribute positive to a team environment.

• You are known for your problem solving and critical thinking skills.

• You are a strong communicator.

• You possess excellent coordination skills specifically related to coordinating service, work, events, logistics, etc. and managing priorities and time management.

• Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively and independently and display a high degree of initiative.

• Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to respond to a variety of needs of various stakeholders.

• Ability to foster and maintain partnerships with providers, internally and externally, for purposes of liaising, referrals, health promotion, support planning and system navigation.

• Highly developed assessment skills.

• Ability to work independently to manage crises happening on campus.

• You are dedicated to life-long learning.

Responsibilities
Reporting to the Manager, Student Services, with functional reporting to the Manager, Student Wellbeing, you will:

• Provide short term, individual counselling for personal and career issues to NSCC students using various evidence based therapeutic approaches. You will assess students for risk, to self and/or others, make the appropriate intervention for support and follow up, which may include linkages with community agencies. You will maintain accurate and timely case notes.

• Work collaboratively with Student Supports including, Student Accessibility, Student Care Navigator and College and Career Prep staff to ensure seamless services for students presenting with a variety of concerns and needs.

• Participate in monthly Community of Practice and weekly clinical consults for Student Services Counsellors across the Province.

• Demonstrate a commitment to the principles of human rights, equity and diversity, providing culturally sensitive, accessible, responsive, high-quality service and supports.

• Implement student-centred care, trauma-informed approaches for the purpose of supporting student wellbeing.

• Maintain current knowledge and comprehensive understanding of relevant College policies, procedures, and practices, providing accurate information about supports available to students both on and off campus.

• Assess students in need of emergency housing, using a provided framework

• Support a variety of student concerns including sexual violence, depression, anxiety, psychosis and grief as examples.

• Support and collaborate with the work of the Student Care Navigator, academic partners, housing, and others in addressing behaviours of concern, supporting students with individualized plans.

• Create, assess and modify counselling support plans, including for those in crisis and/or at risk, as required, based on student needs and in collaboration with on and off campus resources/ agencies.

• Complete accurate and timely documentation according to NSCC practices.

• Assess for, and when appropriate, recommend accommodations related to mental health issues, liaising with other NSCC staff as required.

• Collaborate on the development of resource materials and lead or support the delivery of student wellbeing initiatives

• Develop relationships with various on and off campus partners and community resources to foster support services for our students.

• Engage in continual professional development and relevant learning to remain current and responsive in practice, including best practices in post-secondary mental health

• Support the work of the Students Association, Housing and others by being available to offer workshops/presentations as required.

• Assist with Campus events such as Wellbeing Activities, Orientation, and Open House.

• Participate in responses to critical incidents happening on a campus, in collaboration with others, working to ensure students are supported.

As a condition of employment, Professional Support employees at NSCC must complete a part-time adult education program delivered by NSCC. This adult education program is a significant investment on the part of NSCC in the learning and development of new employees. To achieve regular status; all probationary, full or part-time Professional Support employees of the College must successfully complete the program within their probationary period. Term full-time Professional Support employees whose term appointment is twelve or more months are also required to participate in this program.

NSCC is committed to the full inclusion of all applicants. As part of this commitment, NSCC will ensure that applicants are provided reasonable accommodations, as required. If accommodation is needed to participate in the job application process, please contact Jaclynn Kelly , HR & Talent Consultant, at jaclynn.kelly@nscc.ca. Our Employee Workplace Accommodation Policy can be found here.

Unfortunately, we can not accept late or paper applications.

2239476.title: Women's Counsellor (Relief/Casual)
2239476.description:
Bryony House is seeking a Relief or Casual Women's Counsellors to join our team and play an important role in supporting women and children experiencing intimate partner violence. If you are passionate about crisis intervention, trauma-informed support, and have a flexible schedule, we would love to hear from you.

We are currently hiring for both relief and casual positions:

• Relief: Relief staff are unionized and are eligible for an hourly wage of between $30.52 - $38.27/hour. Relief staff are the first to be scheduled in advance for vacation coverage and are on call first for emergency shift coverage. Hours of work can include days, evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays. Relief staff can be mandated to work certain shifts if there is no other casual coverage available.

• Casual: Casual staff are non-unionized and are eligible for an hourly wage of $29.50/hour. Casuals are scheduled if no other relief staff are available. Casual staff are not mandated to work if there is no other coverage available, it is based purely on their availability.

Neither position are guaranteed hours. Please specify in your application which role type you are interested in being considered for.

Qualifications
• Undergraduate degree in Social Work, Community Studies, Psychology, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.

• Current First Aid, NVCI, and CPR certification.

• Experience and knowledge of working with women and children who have experienced violence and trauma.

• Demonstrated knowledge of crisis intervention and de-escalation strategies.

• Experience supporting individuals who use drugs and/or are in recovery from addiction.

• Experience supporting individuals living with mental illness and the impacts of trauma.

• Proven dependability, reliability, and professionalism in an employment setting.

• Demonstrated ability to manage workplace conflict professionally.

• Basic proficiency with Google Workspace and willingness to learn HIFIS case management software.

Responsibilities
Reporting to the Shelter Manager, the Women's Counsellor is responsible for providing crisis intervention, supportive counselling, advocacy, and shelter support services for women and children affected by intimate partner violence. Specific responsibilities include:

• Provide crisis intervention and support, safety planning and case management to residents.

• Advocate for clients and assist with referrals to community services and resources.

• Support women and children throughout their stay in shelter using a trauma-informed approach.

• Answer the 24-hour distress and crisis line and provide immediate support to callers.

• Complete intake assessments for women and children entering the shelter.

• Assist with household duties, and tasks to ensure the needs of the house and residents are met.

• Maintain accurate case documentation and statistics using organizational systems.

• Work collaboratively with colleagues while upholding organizational values and promoting a respectful workplace.

This role provides the right candidate with the opportunity to work with an amazing team of people dedicated to providing women and children a safe haven away from violence. If this sounds like the right fit for you, we'd love to hear from you!

Bryony House is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to building an inclusive and diverse workplace where everyone feels valued, respected, and empowered to contribute their unique perspectives. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities.

Bryony House is an equal opportunity employer and a Unionized work environment: Public Service Alliance of Canada Local #80022.

2241192.title: Developmental Interventionist - Halifax - 14 month term - Sept 24, 2026
2241192.employer: Nova Scotia Early Childhood Development Intervention Services
2241192.description:
## Developmental Interventionist – 14 month term, Full Time

Location: 3400 Dutch Village Rd., Suite 103, Halifax Hours: 35 hours per week (8:30AM – 4:30PM)

## What we offer:

## NSECDIS offers a competitive compensation package including:

• Salary: $34.20 per hour ($62,244.00 per year) with annual adjustments up to 8 years

• 105 hours Vacation, 105 hours Sick time

• Group Health Benefits Plan (including Extended Healthcare, Dental and Wellness services)

• Contributory Defined Benefits Pension Plan

• Paid holidays (provincial & federal) as well as a paid winter holiday shutdown

As well as:

• Continuous Professional Development

• A chance to support families and educators in your community

## Who we are:

Nova Scotia Early Childhood Development Intervention Services (NSECDIS) provides province-wide services for families of children, birth to school entry, who may be at risk for, or with a diagnosis of, developmental delay. Our goal to promote improved developmental outcomes for children through consultation, coaching, information sharing, support and services designed to meet the individual needs of the child and family. Services emphasize the enhancement of skills and ability through planned interactions to promote child development and family capacity and are delivered in the child's home and community-based programs.

We also facilitate Early Learning and Child Care program and Early Childhood Educator capacity building through coaching within child care and Pre-primary programs with use of The Pyramid Model for Supporting Social Emotional Competence in Infants and Young Children.

As an employer we offer a supportive environment where staff are encouraged to follow their passion within our field. We believe in continuous Professional Development and growth. Our teams are comprised of compassionate trained professionals who enjoy serving their communities.

## Duties include:

• In home coaching with families and community consultations to establish and implement family led meaningful goals and strategies

• Supporting capacity building in families and educators by providing participatory experiences and opportunities that strengthen knowledge and skills and promote a positive sense of competence and confidence

• Connect families with community partners/resources and support navigation within service systems

• Maintaining positive relationships and continual communication with families and their support teams to facilitate joint programming

• Tracking of child and family progress and goals through timely and accurate documentation of all caseload observations and data within our internal database system and support files

• Other related duties as required

## Qualifications & Skills:

• A minimum Bachelor's Degree in Early Childhood Development or related field

• Experience working with children from birth to school age with developmental disabilities and their families is essential

• Strong planning, organizational and time management abilities are required

• Excellent communication (oral & written)

• Strong interpersonal skills

• Adaptable and dependable

• Valid driver's license and access to own reliable vehicle is required daily

Please apply using our Applicant Tracking System though the link provided via this website with a Resume & Cover Letter

Our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative of the families we serve. If you are a member of one or more equity groups, you are encouraged to self-identify on your cover letter or resume.

2240411.title: Social Media Strategist – 18-Month Term
2240411.description:
## Join Our Team as a Social Media Strategist at Atlantic Lottery!

Reporting to the Manager, Creative & Content Strategy, the Social Media Strategist is responsible for shaping and growing Atlantic Lottery's social media presence across corporate, brand, and product channels. This role develops and executes social media strategies that strengthen brand awareness, engage audiences, and support business objectives.

In this 18-month term, you will be working closely with marketing, communications, creative teams, and external partners. The Social Media Strategist creates compelling content, fosters meaningful audience engagement, and uses performance insights to continuously optimize results. This is an exciting opportunity for a strategic and creative professional who is passionate about storytelling, social trends, and building strong digital communities.

## Why Join Our Team?

• Help shape the social presence of one of Atlantic Canada's most recognized brands and connect with audiences across the region.

• Join a collaborative team of marketers, communicators, and creative professionals who are passionate about delivering exceptional experiences.

• Bring innovative ideas to life through engaging campaigns, content, and digital storytelling.

• Influence business decisions and brand growth through audience insights, emerging trends, and social media expertise.

Application Deadline: October 9, 2026

Qualifications
Education and Experience:

• Post-secondary education in Marketing, Communications, Public Relations, or a related field. Equivalent combinations of education and experience will be considered.

• 5+ years of experience in social media, digital marketing, communications, content marketing, or a related field

• Experience developing and executing social media strategies and managing social media channels for a brand, organization, or agency

• Experience creating and delivering engaging content across digital and social media platforms

• Experience analyzing performance metrics and using insights to optimize content and audience engagement

• Must be 19 years of age or older and reside in Atlantic Canada.

Professional Skills:

• Strong understanding of social media platforms, audience behaviors, emerging trends, and industry best practices

• Exceptional storytelling, copywriting, and content planning skills

• Proficiency with social media management, monitoring, and analytics tools

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to translate data into actionable recommendations

• Excellent communication, collaboration, and relationship-building skills

• Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment

Assets:

• Experience working with external agencies, vendors, or creative partners

• Experience supporting brands in a regulated industry

• Experience with photography, video production, or other digital content creation

• Bilingualism in English and French.

## Work Location & Flexibility

This role may be based out of one of our Atlantic Canadian offices: Moncton, NB; Dartmouth, NS; or St. John's, NL.

• During probation: Full-time, in-office (Moncton preferred for onboarding)

• After probation: Choice of full-time in-office or hybrid (2-3 days per week onsite)

## Compensation

• Salary Band: $75,200 - $122,200

• Expected Hiring Range: $79,900 - $82,000 (based on experience, skills, market conditions, and internal equity)

## AL Benefits

• Extended health coverage (medical, dental, vision)

• Basic life insurance and disability coverage

• Defined Benefit Pension Plan

• Three weeks' vacation annually (pro‑rated), 13 paid statutory holidays, and a vacation purchase program

• Wellness support, including wellness programs, 3 personal care days, and a 24/7 Employee & Family Assistance Program

• Two paid volunteer days per year

• Career advancement opportunities

## Recruitment Process

We've made meaningful enhancements to our hiring practices in recent years. Our typical recruitment process includes:

• Two in‑person interviews

• An assignment and/or scenario‑based questions

• Behavioral or cognitive assessments

• Verification of relevant certifications (as applicable)

All interviews are conducted in English, our primary working language, unless otherwise specified.

Only those selected for an interview will be contacted. Successful candidates will undergo reference checks and a mandatory criminal background check. Additional financial, educational, or credential verifications may be required depending on the role.

## Role Commitment

To support employee development, business continuity, and knowledge transfer, individuals who accept this position are expected to remain in the role for a minimum of 18 months before being eligible to apply for or transfer to another position within Atlantic Lottery.

This expectation applies to both external hires and employees moving into the role from another position.

## Internal Candidates

Internal applicants must be in good standing, including meeting expectations on their most recent performance review, and must not be on probation. Consideration may also include factors such as performance improvement plans, disciplinary actions, attendance, and completion of mandatory training.

A Predictive Index (PI) assessment will be completed or shared with the hiring leader as part of the evaluation process.

## Eligibility to Work in Canada

Candidates must have all required work permits, visas, and authorizations and be eligible to work in Canada at the time an offer is made. It is the candidate's responsibility to secure these requirements.

Atlantic Lottery welcomes applications from all qualified candidates. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in Canada. Atlantic Lottery is not participating in the Temporary Foreign Worker (Labour Market Impact Assessment) Program, Provincial Nominee Programs, or the Atlantic Immigration Program at this time. Support for any other immigration programs for new hires is subject to internal policies, operational needs, and program restrictions and is not guaranteed.

Responsibilities
What You'll Do:

• Develop and execute social media strategies that support brand awareness, audience engagement, and business goals.

• Create and deliver compelling content and campaigns that connect with audiences across social platforms.

• Build and strengthen online communities by fostering meaningful interactions and positive brand experiences.

• Use performance data and audience insights to optimize content, engagement, and channel effectiveness.

• Collaborate with internal teams and external partners to support integrated marketing and communications initiatives.

• Identify emerging trends and opportunities to keep Atlantic Lottery's social media presence innovative and relevant.

We are committed to fostering an inclusive, accessible environment, where all employees and customers feel valued, respected and supported. We are dedicated to building a workforce that reflects the diversity of our customers and communities in which we live and serve. If you require an accommodation for the recruitment/interview process (including alternate formats of materials, or accessible meeting rooms or other accommodations), please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

2237734.title: General Manager
2237734.description:
General Manager - Northeast Nutrition Inc.
Location: Truro, Nova Scotia
Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
Work Setting: On-site
Experience Level: Senior Leadership

## About Cooke Aquaculture

Cooke Aquaculture is a global seafood company with operations across North America, Europe, South America, and Australia. Our success is driven by a dynamic, highly skilled, and innovative team supported by dedicated employees who live and work in coastal communities and contribute to the strength of the local economy. As an integrated seafood company, Cooke is committed to delivering high-quality, responsibly produced seafood while continually investing in our people, operations, and communities.

## About Northeast Nutrition Inc.

Northeast Nutrition Inc., a member of the Cooke family of companies, operates an integrated feed manufacturing facility in Truro, Nova Scotia. The facility produces high-quality, nutritionally optimized aquaculture feed that supports Cooke farming operations in New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Newfoundland and Labrador, and Maine. We are seeking an experienced and results-oriented General Manager to provide strategic and operational leadership for the facility. This is a key leadership position responsible for ensuring safe, reliable, efficient, and cost-effective operations while delivering consistent feed quality and performance to support Cooke's farming operations.

## The Opportunity

As General Manager, you will have overall responsibility for the performance of the Northeast Nutrition facility. You will lead a multidisciplinary team, establish operational priorities, drive continuous improvement, manage costs, and ensure the highest standards of safety, quality, regulatory compliance, and customer service. This is a highly visible leadership role with significant influence on operational performance and the broader success of Cooke's integrated aquaculture business.

## Key Responsibilities

• Lead Plant Operations
• Provide overall leadership and accountability for day-to-day plant operations.

• Oversee production, quality, maintenance, shipping and receiving, health and safety, labour management, training, and operational planning.

• Develop and execute production plans to meet the needs of Cooke's farming operations while maximizing plant capacity and efficiency.

• Establish performance objectives, monitor key operating metrics, and take decisive action to address gaps.

• Ensure effective coordination between production, maintenance, quality, logistics, and other functional areas.

• Drive Operational Excellence
• Lead a culture of continuous improvement across the facility.

• Champion Lean Manufacturing principles and identify opportunities to improve throughput, productivity, reliability, and overall plant performance.

• Reduce waste, unplanned downtime, production losses, and operating costs.

• Partner closely with Maintenance to improve equipment reliability, preventative maintenance, and asset utilization.

• Use operational data and performance metrics to identify trends, solve problems, and drive sustainable improvements.

• Ensure Feed Quality, Food Safety & Regulatory Compliance
• Maintain the highest standards of feed quality, nutritional performance, and product consistency.

• Ensure compliance with applicable HACCP, CFIA, FDA, environmental, occupational health and safety, and other regulatory requirements.

• Lead the investigation and resolution of quality or feed-performance issues through effective root-cause analysis and corrective action.

• Promote a culture where quality and food safety are embedded in every aspect of the operation.

• Build and Lead High-Performing Teams
• Lead, coach, and develop managers, supervisors, and plant employees.

• Establish clear expectations and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, respect, and continuous improvement.

• Support workforce planning, recruitment, onboarding, training, performance management, and succession planning.

• Develop strong relationships with employees, operational leaders, and key stakeholders across Cooke.

• Encourage employee engagement and participation in safety, quality, and continuous improvement initiatives.

• Manage Financial & Business Performance
• Develop and manage operating budgets and financial targets.

• Maintain strong control over labour, raw materials, energy, maintenance, and other operating costs.

• Identify and implement initiatives that improve productivity and profitability without compromising safety or quality.

• Analyze operational and financial performance to support informed business decisions.

• Balance short-term operational requirements with long-term capacity, reliability, and business objectives.

• Champion Health & Safety
• Provide visible leadership in health and safety and ensure compliance with all applicable legislation and company standards.

• Establish and maintain a proactive, prevention-focused safety culture.

• Ensure employees are appropriately trained and equipped to perform their work safely.

• Lead by example and hold leaders and employees accountable for safe work practices.

## What You Bring

• 5+ years of progressive leadership experience in feed manufacturing, aquaculture, food manufacturing, or a closely related process-manufacturing environment.

• Previous experience leading a manufacturing facility or large-scale production operation.

• Strong knowledge of plant operations, production planning, maintenance, reliability, quality, and cost management.

• Demonstrated success leading teams and delivering measurable improvements in productivity, efficiency, safety, and financial performance.

• Experience with Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement, root-cause analysis, and operational performance management.

• Strong understanding of HACCP, CFIA, FDA, and other applicable food/feed safety and regulatory requirements.

• Experience managing budgets, operating costs, capital requirements, and business performance.

• Excellent leadership, communication, problem-solving, and relationship-building skills.

• Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, highly integrated operating environment.

• Post-secondary education in business, engineering, manufacturing, food science, aquaculture, or a related discipline would be considered an asset.

## Working Environment

This is an on-site leadership position based at the Northeast Nutrition facility in Truro, Nova Scotia. The General Manager is expected to maintain a strong presence on the production floor and actively engage with employees and operational teams. The role involves working in a manufacturing environment that may be fast-paced, noisy, and subject to varying temperatures. Appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) is required in designated areas.

## Why Join Cooke?

At Cooke, we believe our success comes from people who take initiative, demonstrate resourcefulness, and are committed to getting the job done well. We provide our leaders with the opportunity to make meaningful decisions, solve complex challenges, develop high-performing teams, and build a career within a growing global seafood company. You'll be joining an organization where your leadership can have a direct impact-not only on the performance of a facility, but on an integrated aquaculture operation spanning multiple regions.

NOTE: The recruiter is reviewing and interviewing eligible applicants for this position as they are received. If you are interested in this posting, you are encouraged to apply as soon as possible.

Company Website: https://www.cookeseafood.com

2240914.title: Estimating Department Manager - Dartmouth, NS
2240914.description:
Black & McDonald is seeking an experienced Estimating Department Manager to lead its estimating function for the Atlantic Region. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced construction and estimating leader who enjoys building strong teams, guiding complex bids, developing relationships across the industry, and helping shape how projects move from opportunity to execution.

You'll lead a skilled estimating team supporting projects across the commercial, government, industrial, utility, and institutional sectors while contributing to bid strategy, risk assessment, operational planning, and long-term business success.

## Role Overview

Reporting to the Regional Vice President, Maritimes, the Estimating Department Manager will oversee the estimating function for the region, providing leadership, technical oversight, and strategic direction to the team.

The successful candidate will balance strong estimating expertise with people leadership, business judgment, and relationship management. You'll be responsible for ensuring estimates are accurate, competitive, and complete while developing the team, strengthening processes, and supporting Black & McDonald's continued growth in Atlantic Canada.

## Key Responsibilities

Team Leadership & Development: Lead, coach, and mentor a team of Estimators, assign work, support professional development, and foster accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Estimating Oversight: Oversee and, where required, prepare estimates for labour, materials, equipment, and subcontracted work based on drawings, specifications, tender documents, and contract requirements.

Bid Strategy & Risk Assessment: Review estimates, assess project risks and opportunities, support bid strategy, and ensure final submissions are accurate, competitive, and commercially sound.

Supplier & Subcontractor Engagement: Work closely with suppliers, subcontractors, owners, consultants, designers, and architects to develop pricing, clarify scope, and support successful tender submissions.

Department Operations: Lead the overall function of the estimating department, including staffing, workflow, performance management, resource planning, and departmental priorities.

Process & Continuous Improvement: Develop and maintain estimating procedures, tools, data, and metrics that strengthen consistency, accuracy, efficiency, and decision-making.

Industry & Client Relationships: Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, consultants, suppliers, subcontractors, and industry partners while representing Black & McDonald within the local market.

Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner closely with Operations and regional leadership to support project handover, planning, execution, and overall business performance.

## What You Bring

• 5-10+ years of progressive construction estimating experience, with strong knowledge of tendering, planning, drawings, specifications, contracts, and project risk.

• Demonstrated experience leading and developing teams.

• Strong analytical, communication, organization, and relationship-building skills.

• Experience with estimating platforms such as Accubid, Autobid, Bid2Win, Excel, or similar.

• Degree, diploma, trade background, or equivalent combination of technical and estimating experience.

• PMP, Gold Seal Certification, construction safety certifications, and/or an MBA would be considered assets.

## Why Black & McDonald?

With more than 100 years of experience, Black & McDonald offers the stability of an established organization with opportunities for continued professional growth. Employees receive a competitive compensation package, Health and Dental benefits, employer-matched Pension Plan, incentive plan, flexible work hours, summer hours, and ongoing career development opportunities. Black & McDonald is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. Accommodations are available throughout the recruitment and selection process. To learn more about Black & McDonald, please visit: their website link: https://blackandmcdonald.com/

## How to Apply

Please submit your resume online by clicking "Apply." If you need accommodation during the selection process, or for more information, please contact Susan Brimble confidentially at sbrimble@facetconnect.com.

## Technical Leadership

• Perform the full range of duties of a Red Seal Truck and Transport Mechanic.

• Diagnose, repair and maintain coaches, buses, support vehicles and related equipment.

• Complete complex troubleshooting and assist other technicians with difficult repairs.

• Perform inspections and preventative maintenance in accordance with regulatory and company standards.

• Strong Diagnostic skills and electrical knowledge

• Ensure repairs are completed safely, efficiently and to a high standard.

• Promote teamwork, collaboration and respectful communication.

• Encourage safe work practices and reinforce company policies and procedures.

• Assist in resolving day-to-day operational issues within the shop.

• Monitor completed work to ensure repairs meet company and regulatory standards.

• Support compliance requirements, provincial inspection standards and applicable legislation.

• Ensure proper documentation of repairs and maintenance activities.

• Maintain a safe, organized and clean work environment.

• Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, quality and safety.

## Administrative Support

• Assist with inventory control and communicate parts requirements.

• Participate in meetings, training and continuous improvement initiatives.

• Recommend improvements to shop processes and procedures.

## Leadership Expectations

The Lead Hand is expected to lead by example by:

• Demonstrating professionalism and accountability.

• Maintaining a positive, solutions-focused attitude.

• Treating employees with respect.

• Supporting employee development through coaching and mentoring.

• Communicating clearly and constructively.

• Promoting a culture of safety, teamwork and continuous improvement.

## Qualifications

• Red Seal Truck and Transport Mechanic Certification.

• Valid driver's licence (Class 2 or 3 with air brake endorsement considered an asset).

• Several years of progressively responsible Truck and Transport/Bus mechanical experience.

• Demonstrated ability to organize work and coordinate multiple priorities.

• Strong diagnostic and troubleshooting skills.

• Effective interpersonal and communication skills.

• Experience mentoring apprentices or leading teams is considered an asset.

## Working Conditions

• Active, hands-on mechanical position performed in a maintenance shop environment.

• Frequent standing, bending, lifting and use of mechanical tools and equipment.

• Exposure to noise, grease, weather conditions and moving vehicles.

• Overtime and flexible hours may be required to meet operational demands.

## Benefits

• Signing Bonus - $5000

• Boot/Tool Allowance - $1000

• Group Health Insurance Benefits package

• Relocation expenses (if applicable)

• Employee RRSP matching program (4% match)

• Rewarding career with a growing company

• on-call premiums

Company, Department: Nova Scotia Power, Regulatory Marketing

• Are currently enrolled in and have completed at least the second year of a Business Administration, Commerce, Communications, Public Relations, Computer Science, UI/UX Design, Web Development, or related program.

At Service Nova Scotia, we impact every citizen, business and municipality in Nova Scotia. About Our Opportunity
The Operational Accounting Division of the Department of Service Nova Scotia has an opening that will provide the opportunity to apply your excellent financial expertise and client service in a setting that offers challenges and values collaborative teamwork and innovative thinking.

Primary Accountabilities
Under the general direction of the Coordinator Corporate Operational Accounting, your responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:

• payment production (cheque/electronic/foreign/recurring - which includes accounts payable, provincial social payments, accounts receivable inflows)

• payment cancellations

• payment replacements

• data entry on computerized accounting and spreadsheet applications

• monitor and reconcile file uploads from departmental sub-systems to SAP

• program areas on business and system processes and as well support to the general public.

In addition, you will coordinate and monitor the accurate and effective use of the Corporate Credit Card Program which includes help desk support, monthly reconciliation and posting to SAP. As part of a team-based environment, you will provide support to the other team members of Operational Accounting and participate on teams assigned to special projects.

• You are proficient in the use of PC computer systems, database systems, internet-based applications, spreadsheets, and word-processing packages.

• Demonstrated ability to set priorities to effectively manage multiple projects in a high volume, fast pace, team-oriented environment with a strong client service focus using superior organizational and time management skills.

• Demonstrated ability to exercise initiative and sound judgement, analyze and reconcile accounts and strong troubleshooting skills.

Hours of work will include rotating evening shift within the team.

We are a global mining company dedicated to safely delivering nickel, copper, cobalt, and platinum group metals essential for the world's energy transition.

Our mission is to improve lives and shape a better future together.

From utensils to cellphones to satellites, our operations simplify daily life and enhance connectivity. Our metals are integral to life-saving medical equipment and the electric vehicles driving the fight against climate change – our work truly matters.

Join our diverse team of 15,000 talented individuals committed to transforming critical minerals into prosperity and sustainable development in countries like Canada, Brazil, Indonesia, the United Kingdom, and Japan. We invite you to use your skills with us and contribute to something meaningful and enduring.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking Mining Engineering Co-op Students to join our Mines Technical Services Department in Sudbury, Ontario.

This is a 4 to 16 month fixed term position starting in January 2027 or May 2027. Please be clear in your application which start date you are looking for.

Stock Room Coordinator
Location: Dartmouth, NS

Position Summary
Maritime Paper Products LP is a dynamic, team-oriented company and is honored to be one of Canada's Best Managed Companies. We believe that hiring the best people is a key part of our success. Providing excellence in both our packaging solutions and the relationships we build with our clients, we offer superior capabilities, including in-house graphic and structural design, platemaking, and manufacturing for retail-ready display. We support our customers through operations located in NS, NB, NL, and PE.

We are seeking a highly organized and detail-oriented Stock Room Coordinator to support plant and equipment reliability through effective spare parts inventory management at our Dartmouth facility. This role is responsible for receiving, storing, issuing, kitting, and restocking inventory. Working closely with Operations, Maintenance, Purchasing, and Accounting, the Stock Room Coordinator will maintain inventory accuracy, support maintenance activities, and drive continuous improvement initiatives in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. The Stock Room Coordinator will report to the Maintenance Supervisor.

## Duties & Responsibilities

• Develop and implement efficient workflows for stock management and spare parts availability, while identifying opportunities for continuous improvement and operational optimization.

• Identify and ensure the availability of critical spare parts.

• Establish inventory controls and maintain stock accuracy through cycle counts, obsolete part removal, and non-moving part reviews.

• Manage processes for returning, restocking, and coordinating repairable parts to maintain inventory accuracy and availability.

• Maintain and optimize CMMS data, including Bills of Material (BOMs), to improve inventory accuracy, organization, and visibility of spare parts.

• Collaborate with the Maintenance team to improve parts management processes.

• Document parts receiving and inspection processes to ensure compliance with specifications.

• Implement systems for kitting, staging, and delivering materials required for planned work orders.

• Maintain accurate records and documentation related to storeroom activities, including requisitions, procurement, receiving, storage, distribution, returns, deliveries, shipping, and obsolescence.

• Maintain a clean, organized, and properly labeled storeroom using LEAN methodologies.

• Develop and deliver training programs for new employees and annual refresher training on storeroom access and best practices.

• Ensure adherence to established policies and procedures to support plant goals and key performance indicators (KPIs).

• Restrict storeroom access to authorized personnel only.

• Prepare and analyze reports related to storeroom activities.

• Utilize strong interpersonal and leadership skills to resolve issues and support a positive work environment.

## Qualifications & Experience

## Required Qualifications

• High School Diploma or equivalent.

• Experience working in storerooms, including handling mechanical and electrical parts.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite.

• Ability to lift up to 50 pounds, use hand carts and dollies, and work on your feet for extended periods.

• Strong organizational skills with the ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities.

• Dependable, task-oriented, and self-motivated.

## Preferred Qualifications

• LEAN training or certification with relevant practical experience.

• Mechanical and/or electrical experience.

• Experience working in a manufacturing environment.

• Experience using a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS).

This is an excellent opportunity for a highly organized and proactive inventory professional who enjoys working in a collaborative manufacturing environment and takes pride in maintaining accurate inventory records and supporting plant reliability.

## About Eating Disorders Nova Scotia

Eating Disorders Nova Scotia is a community-based organization with an audacious belief; that no-one should have to face an eating disorder alone. We draw upon the lived experience of those who have been through an eating disorder to create a welcoming, pro-recovery space and supports that are validating and compassionate. Our services include peer support groups, one-on-one mentoring, skills groups, workshops, family support, and more. We offer programs virtually and at our space at 2711 Agricola Street in Halifax. Learn more at www.eatingdisordersns.ca

## About the Position

The Programs Manager is responsible for overseeing all aspects of our programs including project planning, partnership development, engagement, program implementation, and evaluation. The Programs Manager manages a dynamic and committed team who coordinate our peer support programs, clinician led groups, in-person programs and events, workshops and educational work. The Programs Manager seeks out and responds to community needs, and stays informed on sector trends, eating disorders research, reports, and newsimpacting service delivery. An experienced non-profit leader, the Program Manager builds and nurtures partnerships, manages the sustainable growth of our programs and services, and ensures quality. The Programs Manager reports directly to the Executive Director

## Key Responsibilities

• Lead the planning, development, delivery and evaluation of programs and services, ensuring alignment with organizational goals, funder requirements, and best practices.

• Ensure peer support programs are delivered in alignment with established peer support values, principles, and practices, preserving the integrity and fidelity of the peer support approach.

• Develop and implement detailed work plans for the group or project team including tasks, priorities, accountabilities, resources, schedules and milestones.

• Assist with funding proposal development.

• Oversee accurate documentation, data management, and the use of technology to support decision-making and continuous improvement.

• Implement processes and procedures to regularly and consistently evaluate quality and effectiveness of our work.

• Monitor program outcomes and prepare reports for funders and leadership.

• Proactively build, maintain and enhance working relationships with key partners, collaborations, and sector networks to advance our mission.

• Facilitate change and empower employees to grow while promoting group cohesion, shared purpose and engagement.

• Create a work environment that encourages self-awareness, continuous learning, and sustainable approaches to work.

• Provide coaching, mentorship, training, and performance management for program staff, contractors, students, and volunteers.

• Ensure compliance with organizational policies, health and safety standards, and funder requirements.

• Manage program budgets, monitor expenditures, support funding processes, and ensure financial accountability, including expense approvals and revenue tracking.

## Qualifications

• Post-secondary education in Health Services Management, Human Services, Non-profit Leadership, Project Management, or related field.

• Minimum of 3+ years of progressive leadership experience in program administration/management.

• Proven ability to manage staff.

• Experience managing program budgets.

• Experience in facilitating and driving quality improvement and ensuring excellence in standards of service.

• Ability to develop and cultivate strong strategic relationships with community partners, stakeholders, and external agencies.

• Advanced technical proficiency, including data systems, reporting, and information management.

• Detail-oriented, self-initiating, well-organized, and capable of managing multiple projects simultaneously and independently in a fast-paced environment.

• Strong verbal and written communications skills across a range of technologies and contexts in a manner that builds trust, respect and credibility, including in-person and technology-assisted communication.

Knowledge of the non-profit sector, the mental health landscape in Nova Scotia, peer support and eating disorders recovery an asset.

If this sounds like the ideal role for you, here are more reasons why you should apply:

• An opportunity to be a part of a team dedicated to supporting those impacted by eating disorders in a truly client centred, recovery-oriented approach

• A work culture that prioritizes self-care, professional growth, and development

• A flexible work environment

• Health spending account

• Professional development fund

• 3% RRSP matching

We love to hear from candidates with a passion for the mission and lived experience with eating disorders recovery. Eating Disorders Nova Scotia is committed to the principles of equality and diversity in the workplace. We welcome applications from Indigenous peoples, minority communities, immigrants, persons with disabilities, and the 2SLGBTQIA+ community.

Send your resume and cover letter as one PDF titled "Your Name-Program Manager Application" to

Shaleen@eatingdisordersns.ca

About Us

## Senior Audit Officer, Performance Audit Team

## Two (2) Vacancy

## Permanent, Halifax, NS

Our goal is to build a diverse workforce that reflects the citizens we serve. The Office of the Auditor General has an Employment Equity Policy and welcomes applications from Aboriginal Peoples, African Nova Scotians and Other Racially Visible Persons, Persons with Disabilities, and Women in occupations or positions where they are under-represented. If you belong to one of these groups, we encourage you to self-identify in your cover letter or resume.

Why Join Us?
At the Office of the Auditor General of Nova Scotia, we provide independent assurance to the House of Assembly on the government's use of public funds and performance. With about 40 professionals, we're small enough that you'll quickly build meaningful relationships and have your voice heard, but large enough to give you exposure to complex, high-profile audits that make a real difference in areas like healthcare, education, social services, and public safety. For more information, please visit www.oag-ns.ca.

We offer:

• Career development – We are committed to your professional growth as a CPA. We fund your annual CPD requirements and support participation in CPA Atlantic events and national legislative audit networks. Because our team is small, you won't be siloed. You'll contribute to the full audit lifecycle from planning through to reporting, building depth and breadth that is hard to find in larger organizations. You'll also be mentored by senior CPAs who are invested in your success.

• Comprehensive benefits – Competitive salary, extended health and dental benefits, life insurance, and a defined benefit pension plan

• For more information visit our website: Career Information | Office of the Auditor General of Nova Scotia

The Opportunity
We seek a professional to join our Performance Audit Team as a Senior Audit Officer. This position directly reports to an Audit Principal on the Performance Audit Team.

You are responsible for the planning, fieldwork and reporting on performance audits in accordance with professional standards/guidance and Office methodology. This may include but is not limited to developing detailed audit plans, documenting and evaluating systems, testing transactions, evaluating complex information from a variety of subject areas, identifying and evaluating audit findings, and writing report sections summarizing your assigned audit work. You will also assist in the training and development of our junior staff through direct supervision by acting as a coach or mentor. Limited travel within Nova Scotia may be required.

What We're Looking For
You are a CPA looking for work that goes beyond the numbers – where your findings shape how government serves Nova Scotians. You bring:

• Canadian Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation, or expected to receive it within three to six months of hire (e.g., CFE successfully completed, designation pending). Internationally trained accountants whose credentials are recognized as equivalent by CPA Canada are encouraged to apply.

• Recent experience in internal audit, program evaluation, policy analysis, performance measurement or experience applying analysis and research techniques

• Recent experience in reporting and/or presenting research and analysis findings in written documents (e.g., reports, briefing notes, program or policy etc.)

• Experience in collaborating in working groups and/or projects

• Experience in briefing management on the results of complex research and analysis, both verbally and in writing

• Excellent time management skills to ensure engagements are completed within budget and time constraints

• Analytical skills to assess multi-dimensional problems and audit issues

• Highly proficient in the use of MS Office Suite (i.e. Excel and Word)

Asset Qualifications:

• Knowledge of SAP and CAAT software

• Knowledge of Canadian Standards on Assurance Engagements (CSAE)

• Experience in health administration or public health

Remote in Canada
Reference #JL-PRS-9829

Prosaris is helping industrial organizations transform the way they detect, manage, and prevent equipment failures. Their technology combines advanced ultrasonic sensing hardware with powerful software that identifies compressed air leaks, infrastructure issues, and predictive maintenance opportunities that are often impossible for the human ear to detect. What started as a solution for compressed air leak detection has evolved into a broader industrial intelligence platform supporting some of the world's largest organizations.

As a growing Canadian technology company, Prosaris is at an exciting inflection point. With a proven product, established customers, and ambitious growth plans, the company is evolving from a hardware-focused business into a recurring revenue SaaS-driven organization.

## The Role

The Account Executive will play a critical role in driving revenue growth by identifying new opportunities, managing prospect relationships, and closing both hardware and software subscription business. This is an exciting opportunity for a motivated sales professional who enjoys hunting for new opportunities while also developing long-term customer relationships.

Working closely with company leadership and technical experts, the Account Executive will educate prospective customers on the value of Prosaris' technology and help organizations improve reliability, efficiency, and operational performance.

## Duties & Responsibilities:

• Prospect, qualify, and develop new business opportunities within industrial and manufacturing markets.

• Manage a full sales cycle from initial outreach through contract execution.

• Develop and maintain relationships with operations, maintenance, engineering, and executive-level stakeholders.

• Conduct virtual and in-person sales presentations, product demonstrations, and customer meetings.

• Collaborate with technical team members to deliver effective customer solutions.

• Identify opportunities for software subscription growth and recurring revenue expansion.

• Develop account plans that support customer retention, expansion, and enterprise-level growth.

• Attend industry events and conferences to build market presence and generate leads.

## Qualifications & Experience:

• 5+ years of B2B sales experience.

• Proven ability to generate new business and consistently achieve sales targets.

• Experience managing enterprise accounts and multiple decision-makers.

• Self-motivated individual who thrives in an entrepreneurial environment.

2237543.description:
Job Title: Architectural Technologist & Design Lead
Location: Lower Sackville, Nova Scotia
TP-SBG-10014
For over 50 years, Sealand Building Group (Sealand) has been more than a construction company. They are dedicated partners in progress, creating controlled environments that help shape a better future for their customers, employees, and communities. Specializing in food processing, cold storage, agribusiness, distribution, and advanced manufacturing facilities, Sealand designs and builds reliable, high-performance environments that support some of Canada's most essential industries.
Sealand approaches every project with a foundation of strong values: humility in their work, honesty in their partnerships, a focus on results, kindness in their actions, and honor in their commitments. This philosophy enables them to deliver not only technically sound facilities, but also lasting relationships built on trust and shared success.
Meridia Recruitment Solutions is pleased to partner with Sealand Building Group in the recruitment of an Architectural Technologist & Design Lead to join their team located in Lower Sackville, Nova Scotia.
Role Description
As the Architectural Technologist & Design Lead, you will develop accurate and coordinated technical drawings as well as lead the coordination of the design process from initial project concept through construction and project closeout. Working closely with clients, consultants, project team, field team, and the internal design team, you will help transform conceptual ideas into functional facility layouts and ensure designs are coordinated, constructible, and aligned with project scope, schedule, and budget.
This is a hands-on role that combines technical design expertise with design coordination. While much of your time will be spent drawing, you will also manage consultants, facilitate design meetings, review drawings, and keep projects moving forward. Success in this role requires strong architectural knowledge, excellent communication skills, and the ability to coordinate multiple stakeholders throughout the design process.
Your responsibilities will include:

• Work with clients to understand operational requirements and develop functional building layouts and design concepts.

• Prepare conceptual layouts, design-development drawings, permit packages, and construction documents using AutoCAD, and other applicable design software.

• Develop floor plans, elevations, sections, details, schedules, and building-envelope assemblies.

• Produce accurate as-built drawings and updated drawings at project completion.

• Coordinate the design process from project initiation through construction and project closeout.

• Lead the coordination of architectural, structural, civil, mechanical, electrical and refrigeration disciplines.

• Manage external consultants and facilitate design coordination meetings throughout the project.

• Review drawings, specifications, schedules, and technical documentation for completeness, coordination, constructability, and compliance with project requirements.

• Ensure designs remain aligned with project scope, budget, schedule, and operational objectives.

• Identify design conflicts, missing information, and coordination issues and work with project stakeholders to resolve them.

• Track design decisions, revisions, approvals, and outstanding items throughout the project lifecycle.

• Work closely with design, project and site teams to support the successful transition from design into construction.

• Review RFIs, shop drawings, samples, and other construction submittals for design coordination purposes.

• Participate in site visits to review existing conditions, construction progress, and design-related issues.

• Maintain organized design records, drawing registers, meeting minutes, revision logs, and project documentation.

• Support permit submissions, regulatory approvals, and project closeout activities.

• Promote practical and constructible design solutions that support project quality, safety, schedule, and budget objectives.

Your Qualifications
The ideal candidate is an experienced Architectural Technologist who enjoys bringing people, information, and projects together. You are confident working with multiple stakeholders, comfortable asking questions and challenging assumptions, and thrive in environments where communication, coordination, and problem-solving are critical to success.
Your qualifications include:

• A degree or diploma in Architectural Technology, Structural Engineering Technology, Architecture, Engineering, or a related field.

• 7+ years of experience in architectural design, drafting, design coordination, or construction project delivery.

• Strong proficiency in AutoCAD and the ability to prepare and modify drawings when required.

• Strong working knowledge of applicable building codes and construction standards.

• Ability to read, interpret, and review construction drawings, specifications, contracts, and technical documentation.

• Experience coordinating external consultants and design disciplines throughout the project lifecycle.

• Strong understanding of building construction methods, systems, and design coordination processes.

• Working knowledge of Bluebeam and Microsoft Office.

• Excellent communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities and maintain project momentum in a fast-paced environment.

• Valid driver's license and ability to visit project sites is required.

## Assets include:

• Experience working on industrial, food processing, cold storage, manufacturing, distribution, or other specialized construction projects.

• Experience within a design-build construction environment.

• Site experience and exposure to active construction environments.

## Why Join Sealand Building Group?

• Professional development, education, and training opportunities.

• A collaborative and supportive team environment.

• The opportunity to work on specialized projects that help build Canada's food industry.

• Competitive compensation and benefits.

• Quality vehicles, accommodations, and technology resources.

2238644.description:
Operating with Experience. 50 Years of Flight Operations Driving Mission-Critical Success.

Headquartered in Atlantic Canada with a global presence in over 60 countries and a dedication to special missions excellence for over 50 years, the PAL Aerospace team thrives at the forefront of aviation technology and expert crew skills. As a rapidly growing company, we've built a reputation for delivering airborne special mission solutions that enable our customers to address today's complex security, safety, economic, and environmental threats. On the PAL Aerospace team, you're working alongside a tight-knit group of talented professionals who help make the world a safer and more sustainable place.

Operating for domestic affairs agencies, coast guards, fisheries protection, search and rescue, and other public safety organizations, our Airborne Maritime Surveillance Division (AMSD) offers immediate access to special mission aircraft, sensors, and crew.

To support our mission, PAL Aerospace is looking for Training Managers to join our AMSD team in Campbell River, BC, Halifax, NS or St. John's, NL where no two days are the same!

The Training Manager is responsible for delivering, evaluating, and maintaining pilot training programs to ensure compliance with company standards, Canadian Aviation Regulations (CARs), and approved training programs. This role supports safe, standardized flight operations through effective instruction, mentoring, and performance assessment.

## Key Responsibilities

## Training Delivery

• Conduct ground school, simulator, and line training for flight crew.

• Deliver recurrent, upgrade, and initial aircraft type training.

• Ensure all instruction aligns with Company Operations Manual (COM), SOPs, and approved training programs.

## Evaluation & Checking

• Assess pilot competency through formal evaluations and line checks.

• Identify training deficiencies and recommend corrective actions.

• Provide structured feedback and coaching to trainees.

## Standardization

• Promote adherence to SOPs and operational best practices.

• Support standardization initiatives across fleets and bases.

• Participate in training meetings and calibration sessions.

## Program Development & Support

• Assist in development and revision of training programs, manuals, and courseware.

• Provide input on training improvements based on operational experience.

• Support implementation of new procedures, aircraft, or regulatory requirements.

## Safety & Compliance

• Ensure all training complies with CARs, company manuals, and approved syllabi.

• Contribute to the Safety Management System (SMS) through reporting and hazard identification.

• Maintain accurate training records and documentation.

## Qualifications:

• Must have experience on DHC-8 and/or KingAir

• Valid ATPL

• 3500 hours total time

• 500 multi-engine hours

• 1000 PIC hours

• Instrument Rating

Competition # : 49956

Department: Public Works

Location: MILLER LAKE

Type of Employment: Term

Union Status: NSGEU - NSPG

Closing Date: 04-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
Maintaining our provincial infrastructure is no small job. We're recruiting for people like you to help our Province achieve big things.
The Fleet Services Division of the Department of Public Works supports the backbone of our provincial highway infrastructure. We are located at Miller Lake, the central Fleet Services hub of the province. At Miller Lake, we are pivotal in ensuring the equipment used to maintain, repair, and build Nova Scotia's 23,000 kilometers of roads and highways, and 4,100 bridges, is always ready to go.
If you are focused and committed to ensuring the safety of our roads and helping the public arrive safely to their destination, then we have the perfect opportunity for you.

About Our Opportunity
You will be responsible for the management, planning and coordination of all inventory activities, control of the fleet inventories at the central mechanical stores operations at Miller Lake and the provincial inventory fleet operations in the divisional stores at each provincial district. You are also responsible for the procurement of all the parts for the provincial fleet operation.

Primary Accountabilities
As the Provincial Inventory Coordinator, you will manage and implement enhancements to the SAP on-line inventory system. This includes ensuring that the maintenance, updating and input/output of the SAP inventory system is completed correctly and on a timely basis. Also includes attendance at meetings locally and outside the province in relation to SAP improvements.

## Your main responsibilities will also include:

• Managing the fleet parts inventory operation for the Miller Lake stores and the division stores throughout each provincial district.

• Managing fleet stock for slow-moving and/or obsolete holdings and decides whether stock is redistributed or disposed.

• Preparing requisitions for the Provincial Fleet stock to be processed as provincial standing offers (one-three contracts) for the mechanical branches.

• Formulating policies, implementing controls and guidelines to ensure the Department's fleet inventory of approximately 6.5 million dollars is managed efficiently. This includes the central operation as well as nine division stores throughout the provincial districts.

• Developing realistic short and long-range goals and objectives through the utilization of inventory management techniques and computerization.

Primary Accountabilities Continued
• Providing on-going training for fleet inventory staff across the province in all aspects of the SAP inventory management system (i.e.; Goods Movement, MRP, Physical Inventory Counts). This includes training in all areas of inventory management as well as SAP.

• Establishing and updating material requirements planning procedures and practices for all fleet inventories.

• Conferring with Area Managers, Fleet Service Co-ordinators, Project Manager, Shop Supervisors, Financial Services Officers, District Directors and other Department personnel on problems relating to supply, administration, inventory management, and making recommendations on improvements. Also meeting and conferring with other provincial government departments to discuss methods of inventory procurement.

• Traveling throughout the province to ensure proper procedures are being followed and are consistent; reviewing internal systems and procedures and advising on and assisting in the development and implementation of enhancements.

• Determining procedures and cycles for directing all physical inventory stocktaking throughout the Province.

Qualifications and Experience
As the ideal candidate, you will require a post-secondary certificate or diploma specialized in Business or Supply Chain. A minimum of 7 years of progressive supply chain experience is required, preferably with a well-rounded knowledge of scheduling, planning, procurement, inventory, and disposal functions. A professional with several years of experience in supply chain management including scheduling, planning, procurement, inventory, and disposal functions will be considered.

Experience in managing and directing a computerized heavy parts inventory. Knowledge of inventory management applications and principles of inventory management in an automated and integrated environment with this application relating to the procedures within mechanical repair plants.

An excellent knowledge of the SAP Inventory Management system with respect to Goods Movement, Material Master, Material Requirements Planning, and Physical Inventory Counts. A working knowledge of the Nova Scotia Occupational Health and Safety Act, Movement of Dangerous Goods, and WHIMIS. Knowledge of the Provincial Government's purchasing principles and procedures.

As the ideal candidate, you have:

• A strong commitment to customer service.

• Experience in assisting clients with specification development, scanning the market for suitable goods, purchasing, and following orders through to delivery & deficiency resolution.

• Strong problem solving and project management competencies.

• Experience leading projects.

• Experience in managing inventory systems.

• The ability to process a large volume of work under tight deadlines.

You bring outstanding leadership, diplomacy, project management, and communication skills. You have strong problem-solving skills and a demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities and demands. You are a highly organized individual who is focused on continuously improving quality and has a solution-focused approach. You are responsive and able to prioritize a high volume of competing and sometimes rapid requests. You are an excellent relationship builder, self-starter, and are effective in working in a team-orientated environment, with the ability to undertake complex assignments without supervision.
We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
This is an excellent career opportunity for many, and we do consider an equivalent combination of training, education, and experience. Related equivalencies may include, but are not limited to:

• 9 years of related work experience.

Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
Work is performed in a mechanical repair environment occasioned by smoke, gas fumes, and machinery noise.

Additional Information
This is a Term employment opportunity with an anticipated end date of October 29, 2027. The appointment status (Term, Temporary or Casual) is dependent on the start date of the successful candidate.

What We Offer
• Career development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career

• Engaging workplace: our employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in, we have forward-thinking policies and strategies

• Countless career paths

Pay Grade: TE 23

What started as a general store has evolved into a dynamic, multi-location retail group operating under national banners including Home Hardware Building Centre, The Brick, and Bell, with a diversified portfolio spanning home improvement, building materials, furniture, appliances, electronics, floral, and property management.
Over the last five years, The Wilson Group has entered a significant new chapter of growth. To support this momentum, we are seeking an experienced Controller to join the team in Yarmouth, Nova Scotia. Reporting directly to the CFO, the Controller will lead the day-to-day accounting operations across a multi-entity organization while providing the financial leadership, insight, and structure needed to support continued growth.
This is an opportunity for an experienced accounting professional who enjoys being close to the business. Someone equally comfortable diving into the details and stepping back to understand the bigger picture. Working closely with the CFO and operational leaders, the Controller will play a key role in strengthening financial processes, enhancing reporting capabilities, and translating financial information into meaningful insights that support sound business decisions.
What you'll do:

• Lead day-to-day accounting operations across multiple entities and locations

• Oversee monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting, ensuring accurate and timely preparation of financial statements

• Lead budgeting, forecasting, cash flow management, and financial planning processes

• Develop and strengthen internal controls, accounting policies, and financial procedures

• Analyze operational and financial results, identifying trends, opportunities, and areas requiring attention

• Translate financial information into clear, actionable insights and recommendations for senior leadership and operational teams

• Oversee inventory accounting and reporting across the organization

• Coordinate year-end activities and act as a primary liaison with external accountants and advisors

• Identify and implement opportunities to improve systems, reporting, processes, and overall operational efficiency

• Partner closely with the CFO and business leaders to support strategic initiatives and drive business performance

## The ideal candidate will possess:

• Seven or more years of progressive accounting and financial leadership experience

• A CPA designation or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience

• Strong technical accounting knowledge and financial reporting expertise

• Demonstrated experience leading accounting functions and strengthening financial processes

• Exceptional analytical and problem-solving capabilities with the ability to turn financial information into meaningful business insight

• Strong systems aptitude, including advanced Excel proficiency

• The ability to communicate effectively with operational leaders, executive stakeholders, and team members across the organization

• A hands-on approach and willingness to get into the details while maintaining a broader understanding of the business

• Experience within retail, distribution, inventory-intensive, multi-location, or similarly complex operating environments would be considered an asset

This is an exciting opportunity for a financial leader who wants to have a meaningful impact within a growing, diversified organization. You will work directly with a collaborative executive team, influence important business decisions, and play a key role in strengthening the financial infrastructure that supports The Wilson Group's continued evolution.

• Finance and reporting: Assist with financial information, reconciliations, portfolio and performance reporting, internal controls, business planning, and the preparation of materials that support sound financial management and decision-making.

2236782.employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia

About Us
Nova Scotia is rich in natural resources – including biodiversity, forests, provincial parks and the land we manage. Natural Resources is responsible for the development, management, conservation and protection of forests, parks and wildlife resources and the administration of the province's Crown land. Together we are working with Nova Scotians to build a better future through sustainable natural resource management.

About Our Opportunity
The Forest Technician 4 – Air Attack Officer (AAO) provides specialized, technically complex direction and coordination of aerial wildfire suppression operations across the Province of Nova Scotia. The position ensures that aircraft resources are deployed safely, effectively, and efficiently in support of provincial wildfire suppression strategies. As the AAO, you will also provide operational support to the Fleet and Wildfire Management division including wildfire prevention and mitigation, training and equipment initiatives.

Primary Accountabilities
• Direct, coordinate, and control aerial wildfire suppression operations including airspace management, target selection, and drop evaluation.

• Conduct aerial reconnaissance, post-mission debriefings, and provide clear, concise radio communications.

• Monitor aircraft readiness, base alert levels, weather conditions, and fire danger indices.

• Ensure compliance with aviation policies, safety standards, and operational guidelines.

• Develop, deliver, and evaluate training for Air Attack Officers and wildfire management staff.

• Contribute to annual wildfire preparedness and pre-suppression planning activities.

• Support Provincial Wildfire Coordination Centre operations including duty officer rotations, aircraft dispatch, and situation reporting.

• Wildfire Training, Prevention /Mitigation and Equipment support

Qualifications and Experience
You have graduated from a recognized forestry or related technician diploma program and have a minimum of six (6) years of related experience. You must be able to demonstrate extensive experience with wildfire aerial suppression tactics using fixed? and rotary?wing aircraft operations. You have advanced knowledge and analytical skills to assess wildland fire behaviour and values at risk to develop and adapt aerial attack strategies under dynamic and high?pressure operational conditions. The role requires a strong working understanding of Canadian Aviation Regulations, restricted wildfire airspace procedures, and applicable wildfire legislation to ensure aircraft are deployed safely, effectively, and in compliance with established standards. Effective performance requires clear, concise verbal and written communication, particularly in demanding radio environments, and the ability to remain composed while managing multiple concurrent operational priorities. The position includes leadership responsibilities such as mentoring and developing Air Attack Officer trainees. Proficiency with office productivity software and mobile technology is required, including the use of iPhones, iPads, and operational applications such as ESRI Field Maps, Avenza Maps, and ForeFlight to support situational awareness and decision?making.

You must have:

• Valid class 5 driver's licence or equivalent

• Restricted Radio Operators Certificate (ROC-A) (or can obtain)

• Provincial/Territorial Agency Air Attack Officer certification (with the ability to obtain National Air Attack Officer certification)

• Valid Canadian passport for international deployments (or ability to obtain)

• S-490 Advanced Wildland Fire Behaviour course or equivalent

Assets:

• National Air Attack Officer certification

• Qualified as one or more Incident Command System command and general staff positions

• Experience in the development and delivery of training courses in an adult education environment.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
Normal work week is 35 hours per week. This position often requires extensive travel within province, nationally, and internationally with minimal notification. Extended periods in small aircraft under turbulence, exposure to G forces, and occasional field movement requiring coordination and stamina. Incumbents will perform a rotating shift to provided seven day per week coverage during the wildfire season and on occasion overtime may be required.
