## Faculty - Electrical Construction & Industrial

## Education

## Cumberland Campus

## Springhill, Nova Scotia

## Institute of Skilled Trades

Term, Full-time Position: Commencing approximately November 16, 2026 and ending approximately June 25, 2027

## Application deadline is 11:59PM, October 1, 2026

Competition No. 2627-186

From Industry Expert to Instructor - Help Train the Next Generation of Skilled Trades Workers

Are you an experienced Construction Electrician looking for a new challenge; one that keeps you connected to the trade you love, while offering more balance, stability, and long-term security?

At Nova Scotia Community College, you can take the knowledge and experience you've built in industry and use it to mentor the next generation of skilled trades professionals, all while enjoying predictable hours, excellent benefits, and a career that's easier on the body.

## Why Make the Move to Teaching?

This is an opportunity to stay hands-on in the trade without the physical demands, long shifts, emergency callouts, or unpredictable schedules that often come with industry work.

As a Faculty member with NSCC, you'll enjoy:

• The opportunity to share your industry expertise and help shape the next generation of skilled trades professionals

• Meaningful work that makes a lasting impact on students, industry, and communities

• A supportive team environment focused on collaboration, mentorship, and continuous learning

• The ability to stay connected to your trade while transitioning into teaching

• Predictable work hours that support work-life balance

• A stable and rewarding career in education with opportunities for professional growth

• Support and training to help transition successfully into teaching

Whether you're looking to slow down physically, spend more time with family, take your trade experience in a new direction, or transition into a rewarding second phase of your career, this role offers the chance to do all of that while remaining deeply connected to the trades community.

Qualifications

## What We're Looking For

We're seeking experienced tradespeople who are passionate about the industry and interested in helping others succeed.

Ideal candidates will have:

• Interprovincial Red Seal certification in Construction Electrician.

• A Journeyperson certification as an Industrial Electrician would be consdiered an asset.

• A minimum of five years (full-time equivalent) of recent journeyperson experience in the electrical construction and industrial trade.

• Comfortable using computer applications such as the Microsoft Office Suite, including Outlook

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

• A commitment to safety, mentorship, and lifelong learning

Previous teaching experience or related experience in the delivery of educational program or training adults would be an asset, but not required. If you've coached apprentices, trained coworkers, or shared your knowledge on the shop floor, you already have valuable experience to build on.

NOTE: Two years of your training will be counted towards the educational requirements and cannot be included as part of your occupational experience.

## Compensation & Benefits

Faculty salaries currently range from approximately $81,760 to $104,267 annually, based on experience and qualifications.

In addition to salary, NSCC offers:

• A defined benefit pension plan to support long-term financial security

• Comprehensive health and dental coverage, including vision, paramedical services, life insurance, Employee Family Assistance Program (EFAP), and more

• Up to 45+ days of paid vacation and recognized holidays, including paid time off between Christmas and New Year's

• Professional development and training opportunities to support ongoing learning and career growth

## Make an Impact

The trades need experienced professionals willing to pass on their knowledge. This is your opportunity to shape the future of industry while building a healthier, more balanced future for yourself.

If you're ready to bring your trade experience into the classroom and help develop the next generation of technicians, we'd love to hear from you.

Responsibilities

## What You'll Be Doing

As part of the Institute of Skilled Trades faculty team in the Electrical Construction & Industrial program, you will:

• Deliver theoretical and hands on practical shop training along with classroom instruction

• Share real-life industry knowledge and troubleshooting experience

• Mentor and support students entering the trade

• Help students build the skills employers are looking for

• Promote and ensure health and safety practices and procedures are consistently followed in classrooms, shops, and labs.

• Work collaboratively with fellow instructors and industry partners

• Stay current with evolving technology and industry practices

• Participate in student advising, curriculum development, program promotion, committee work, and work placement support

This role combines shop instruction with modern teaching tools and blended learning approaches, including in-class, online, and off-site instruction, as well as occasional evening and weekend sessions.

As a condition of employment, you are required to provide proof of a valid Red Seal certification, including your Red Seal number for verification with the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency, prior to your start date.

As a condition of employment, Faculty at NSCC must complete a part-time adult education program delivered by NSCC. This adult education program is a significant investment on the part of NSCC in the learning and development of new employees. To achieve regular status, all probationary, full or part-time Faculty of the College must successfully complete the program within their probationary period. Term full-time Faculty whose term appointment is twelve or more months are also required to participate in this program.

Candidates selected for interviews will be expected to provide at least three recent occupational references. The successful candidate will be expected to provide official transcripts to show proof of academic achievements.

NSCC is committed to the full inclusion of all applicants. As part of this commitment, NSCC will ensure that applicants are provided reasonable accommodations, as required. If accommodation is needed to participate in the job application process, please contact (HRG). Our Employee Workplace Accommodation Policy can be found here: Employee Workplace Accommodations Policy | NSCC

Unfortunately, we cannot accept late or paper applications.

Emergency Medical Care Inc. (EMC) is a wholly owned subsidiary of Medavie Health Services (MHS) that manages and operates ground ambulance, air medical transport and the medical communications operations in Nova Scotia through a performance-based contract with the provincial government's Emergency Health Services (EHS) Operations division and the Department of Health and Wellness. As well, EMC operates TeleHealth/811 medical communications for Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island for the Department of Health.

We access all communities in Nova Scotia in a timely and efficient manner with our fleet of more than 180 ambulances and support vehicles operating out of 60+ stations. We respond to 165,000+ calls annually across the province, which are actively managed through the EHS Operations Medical Communications Centre, the hub of all emergency (911) and non-emergency (hospital transfers) medical calls.

The EHS Operations LifeFlight program provides even greater accessibility by responding to patients on scene or through inter-facility transports by our critical care team via helicopter, fixed wing, or ground ambulance.

In addition, paramedics in Nova Scotia participate in various programs both urban and rural such as community-based paramedic programs, collaborative emergency centres, and emergency preparedness and special operations, to name a few.

There are lots of opportunities waiting for you in Nova Scotia. Apply now to learn more about our service and available positions.

## NATURE AND SCOPE:

Reporting to the Integrated Health Operations Supervisor (IHOS), the Clinical Support Paramedic will be responsible for the assessment of health and clinical needs and providing clinical advice, utilizing professional clinical judgment, supported by decision support software within the provincial EHS system.

Must maintain and be accountable for their own professional competencies through participation in continuing education sessions, successful completion of required skills training, and clinical exposure under the oversight and direction of the Medical Director and College.

As an employee of EMC, we are accountable to our patients and coworkers by participating in and supporting all safety related initiatives, as well as acting in a manner that fosters a culture that focuses on patient safety and a safe workplace.

## DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

The position entails, but is not limited to the following:

• Provide telephone triage, medication advice, health information, patient follow up and implement care packages to a range of individuals in a range of emotional states to specific emergency calls, using Clinical Decision Support Software.

• Provide clinical advice to Operational staff when required and proactively promote the use of alternative care pathways to operational staff.

• Provide skilled and effective assessment of patients presenting clinical need, through telephone consultation, with the support of clinical assessment software.

• Apply critical analysis to the combination of complex information during the care process to provide accurate advice and health information to patients in order to empower them to act upon the advice given.

• Keep immediate and accurate records of service user inquiries to the service during the consultation.

• Recognize opportunities for and provide health education during the consultation process referring to Health Care Professionals as required.

• Practice active listening and analytical skills to identify medical issues and provide treatment plans.

• Conduct clinical follow-ups.

• Access databases, email, and approved internet resources and critically appraise sources of information and their evidence base.

• Act as a clinical resource for internal and external non-medical staff.

• Provide advice on clinical issues i.e. clinical requirement for inter-facility transports.

• Undertake audits of the Clinical Desk and produce feedback reports.

## Qualifications and Requirements:

Education/Experience:

• Active CPNS registration as an Advance Care Paramedic.

• ACP - minimum of 5 years recent experience with at least three (3) years in a frontline patient care role in a high volume area

• ACP in either a high call volume ground ambulance position or emergency department.

• Must have working knowledge of window-based computer applications and the ability to accurately type 30 wpm

• Must have or be willing to complete an AEMD course as well as other courses as necessary

• Must have a good clinical record

• Must have a good attendance record

• Current certification/instructor in ACLS, ATLS, PTLS, PALS an asset

• Completion of a leadership course, an asset

• Other current and past leadership roles within the organization, an asset

Knowledge & Skills:

• Advanced patient assessment skills

• Demonstrated high standards of competence in practices to protect health and safety including clinical governance, infection control and scene safety

• Excellent understanding and must follow the EHS CPGs, protocols, and policies.

• Methodical and systemic approach to working including ability to prioritize

• Ability to convey information in a simplified and easily understandable way

• Ability to identify, assess and prioritize complex problems

• Previous experience with tele-triage considered an asset

While Medavie may use automated tools, including AI, to support application screening, candidates are expected to complete all recruitment interactions independently-without AI assistance-to ensure a fair and equitable process.

Our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative of the citizens we serve. We are committed to building an inclusive team that represents a variety of backgrounds, cultures, races, perspectives and skills. We encourage applications from all qualified candidates including women, persons of any sexual orientations and gender identities and/or expressions, Indigenous persons, African Canadians, other racialized groups, persons with disabilities. ## Commercial Business Development Manager
Nova Scotia
Reference #JL-MNI-10039

For more than 100 years, MUNN Insurance has been helping Atlantic Canadians protect what matters most. As one of Atlantic Canada's leading independent insurance brokerages, MUNN provides personal, commercial, and specialty insurance solutions through a client-focused and relationship-driven approach.

With a strong reputation built on trust, expertise, and exceptional service, MUNN partners with industry-leading insurers to deliver tailored solutions that meet the evolving needs of businesses and individuals. Their success is driven by a collaborative culture, deep community connections, and a commitment to helping clients navigate risk with confidence.

As MUNN continues to grow its commercial presence across Atlantic Canada, they are seeking a Commercial Business Development Manager to lead commercial growth initiatives throughout Nova Scotia.

## The Role

Reporting to the Commercial Leadership Team, the Commercial Business Development Manager is responsible for developing new commercial business opportunities, building strategic relationships, and expanding MUNN Insurance's presence throughout Nova Scotia.

This is a highly visible, client-facing role focused on generating new business and cultivating long-term relationships within the business community. The successful candidate will identify opportunities, develop trusted advisor relationships, and work closely with internal commercial insurance professionals to deliver customized solutions that support client success.

This opportunity is ideal for a motivated business development professional who enjoys networking, building relationships, creating opportunities, and contributing directly to organizational growth.

## Duties & Responsibilities:

## Business Development & Market Growth

• Develop and execute a strategic business development plan focused on commercial growth throughout Nova Scotia.

• Identify and pursue new commercial insurance opportunities through prospecting, networking, referrals, and community engagement.

• Build strong relationships with business owners, executives, and key decision-makers.

• Develop referral partnerships and centres of influence to support long-term growth.

• Maintain an active pipeline of qualified opportunities and manage prospects through the sales process.

• Consistently achieve business development and revenue objectives.

• Identify opportunities for account expansion and cross-selling.

## Client Relationship Management

• Conduct consultative discussions to understand clients' businesses, operations, risks, and goals.

• Develop trusted advisor relationships with prospective and existing clients.

• Analyze insurance programs and identify opportunities to improve coverage and risk management strategies.

• Present tailored insurance solutions that align with client needs and objectives.

• Support a seamless transition from prospect to client while maintaining key relationships.

## Market Presence & Community Engagement

• Establish a strong presence within Nova Scotia's business community.

• Participate in professional associations, industry events, and networking opportunities.

• Enhance MUNN Insurance's visibility and reputation throughout the province.

• Build relationships with industry partners, community organizations, and referral sources.

• Identify emerging market opportunities and industry trends.

## Collaboration & Commercial Strategy

• Collaborate closely with Commercial Account Managers and insurer partners to develop competitive client solutions.

• Support the preparation and presentation of proposals for new opportunities.

• Maintain a strong understanding of commercial insurance products, markets, and underwriting considerations.

• Accurately track business development activities, pipeline performance, and client interactions.

• Contribute to the ongoing growth and success of the commercial insurance division.

## Qualifications & Experience:

The ideal candidate brings a combination of business development expertise, relationship-building skills, and commercial acumen.

## Experience & Education:

• 5+ years of experience in business development, commercial sales, commercial insurance, financial services, or a related client-facing environment.

• Demonstrated success generating new business opportunities and building long-term client relationships.

• Experience working within a relationship-based sales environment.

• Post-secondary education in Business, Commerce, Finance, Insurance, or a related discipline is considered an asset.

• Insurance industry experience or licensing is considered an asset; licensing support may be available for the right candidate.

## Skills & Competencies:

• Strong prospecting, networking, and relationship-building abilities.

• Excellent communication, presentation, and negotiation skills.

• Consultative and solutions-oriented approach to sales.

• Strong business acumen and commercial awareness.

• Ability to develop credibility and trust with business leaders and decision-makers.

• Highly organized with strong pipeline management capabilities.

• Self-motivated with the ability to work independently and collaboratively.

• Strong client focus and commitment to service excellence.

## Why Join MUNN Insurance?

• Join one of Atlantic Canada's most respected independent insurance brokerages.

• Play a key role in growing MUNN's commercial presence throughout Nova Scotia.

• Work alongside an experienced and collaborative commercial insurance team.

• Build meaningful relationships with business leaders across the province.

• Enjoy the support of a well-established organization with a strong reputation and growth mindset.

• Contribute to an organization committed to innovation, client service, and community involvement.

2235080.description:
Human Resources Generalist

Designated office:

6080 Young Street

Halifax, NS

This position is

Working in the designated office five (5) days per week, Monday to Friday, 8:30am-5:00pm.

Are you an HR professional who loves working with people and finding ways to create a great employee experience? We're looking for a driven HR Generalist to join our People & Culture team! This is an exciting opportunity for someone looking to grow their HR career while gaining hands-on experience across employee wellness and benefits, employee relations, recruitment, internal communications and other HR programs.

Reporting to the Director, People & Culture, you'll work closely with leaders, employees, and your People & Culture peers to support a wide range of initiatives that help our people thrive. If you're someone who enjoys variety, takes ownership of your work, and isn't afraid to roll up your sleeves and jump in, you’ll be a great fit!

What You’ll Be Doing

No two days are the same in this role. You can expect to:

• Administer group benefits and pension programs while ensuring employees understand and can effectively access available resources.

• Coordinate disability management and employee leave processes, including medical, parental, compassionate care, and other leaves.

• Support employees and leaders throughout the leave lifecycle, including documentation, communication, accommodations, and return-to-work planning.

• Draft, proofread, and distribute employee communications, ensuring information is clear and accurate.

• Provide guidance on HR policies, employment standards, and workplace practices.

• Assist with investigations, progressive discipline processes, and related documentation.

• Support and coordinate employee experience and wellness initiatives.

• Co-chair the Employment Equity Committee and support compliance and reporting requirements.

• Maintain accurate employee records and HRIS data while ensuring confidentiality.

• Contribute to the development and continuous improvement of HR policies, programs, and processes.

• Assist with recruitment activities and help create a positive candidate experience.

• Collaborate on People & Culture projects and initiatives that enhance the employee experience.

What You’ll Bring

We're focused on finding someone who is eager to learn, contribute, and grow. You'll be successful in this role if you have:

• Undergraduate degree in Commerce, Business Administration, or a related discipline with a concentration in Human Resources.

• 3+ years of progressive Human Resources experience.

• Experience administering employee benefits, disability management, accommodations, or leave programs.

• Knowledge of benefit plans, pension administration, and applicable employment legislation.

• Experience supporting wellness, employee engagement, or employee experience initiatives is considered an asset.

• Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.

• Excellent communication, relationship-building, and customer service skills.

• A high level of discretion and attention to detail when handling confidential information.

• A proactive mindset, strong follow-through, and a willingness to take initiative.

• A genuine passion for supporting employees and creating a positive workplace experience.

• CPHR designation, or progress toward obtaining a CPHR designation, is considered an asset.

About Eastlink

Eastlink is proudly family-owned and headquartered in Halifax, Nova Scotia. After more than 50 years, we’ve grown from a small-town startup into one of Canada’s Best Managed companies without losing our entrepreneurial edge. We move fast. We try new things. We care about doing right by our customers, and we’re not afraid to take a different approach to make that happen.

Why Work With Us

We could say we’re not your typical telecom, but what makes us different is how we operate day to day. At Eastlink, we’re a tight-knit team all working toward common goals. We’re big enough to do meaningful work, but small enough that you can actually make your mark. You won’t get stuck waiting for layers of approval or years of tenure to make an impact! We believe in getting involved, speaking up, and figuring things out together. We’re always listening, learning, and adapting because our customers (and our people) expect us to. And just like we invest in our network, we invest in you, with intention and for the long run.

We’re committed to building a workplace where everyone feels they belong. We embrace diversity, inclusion, equity, and accessibility throughout all levels of the organization and encourage members of equity groups to self-identify during the application process.

About Us
At Service Nova Scotia, we impact every citizen, business and municipality in Nova Scotia. Our mandate is to design and deliver programs and services to meet the needs of our clients and the public good through a culture of excellence.

Service Nova Scotia's vision is to be a recognized leader in service and public protection that delivers trusted, accessible, modern programs, and contributes to Nova Scotia as a safe and desirable place to live, work and do business.

About Our Opportunity
As a Land Registration Officer, you are accountable for ensuring that all documents submitted to the Land Registration Office are in proper legal form and meet all requirements of the Land Registration Act and the Registry Act and other statutes.

Primary Accountabilities
• Receiving payments for document submissions, products, services, and deed transfer tax and property accounts for monies received;

• Ensuring that applications and documents are accurately prepared, approved, registered and indexed for future access in accordance with established policies and procedures;

• Approving or rejecting draft applications for registration of parcels into the land registration system and for maintaining ownership and other interests in land parcel registers;

Qualifications and Experience

2240846.title: Senior Manager, Development & Communications
2240846.description:
Reports to: Executive Director
Salary: $70,000 - $90,000. Commensurate with experience
Hours: Full-time, 37.5 hours/week; flexible work arrangements may be considered
Location: Dartmouth, NS | Hybrid & flexible work environment; regular in-person presence required for team, donor and community engagement
Direct Report: Manager, Marketing & Communications (1)
Deadline: October 5, 2026

## Why You'll Love Working at PREP

At The PREP Academy, we believe our people are our greatest strength. We are committed to creating a workplace where employees feel supported, valued, and empowered to make a meaningful impact. Our total compensation package includes:

• Comprehensive health, dental & life insurance (cost-shared)

• Employee Assistance Program

• 3 weeks vacation, increasing to 4 weeks after your third year

• Paid December office closure (typically 3 weeks)

• Paid birthday off

• Summer Hours

• Annual $500 Professional Development Fund

• Annual $500 Education Scholarship

• Company laptop & mobile phone

Most importantly, you'll join a passionate, mission-driven team transforming educational outcomes for African Nova Scotian youth across Nova Scotia.

## About The PREP Academy

The PREP Academy is a community based registered charity that inspires and prepares African Nova Scotian students for postsecondary education. Our culturally informed programs guide students as they plan, prepare and pursue college, university and apprenticeship pathways directly after high school. Our programs are growing, our impact is being demonstrated, our relationships are expanding, and we are building the organizational capacity required to strengthen and expand our impact serving African Nova Scotian youth and families across the province.

## Position Summary

The Senior Manager, Development & Communications provides strategic leadership for The PREP Academy's fundraising, donor engagement and communications efforts. As a key member of the senior leadership team and trusted thought partner to the Executive Director, the Senior Manager is accountable for growing and diversifying revenue, strengthening donor relationships, and building the strategies, systems and team capacity that support PREP's long-term sustainability.

The Senior Manager will lead PREP's organizational fundraising strategies across individual, corporate and foundation giving, grants, annual giving, major gifts, events and emerging opportunities created by PREP's charitable status. They will lead and manage PREP's donor, funder and prospect portfolio while developing thoughtful strategies to identify, qualify, cultivate, solicit, steward, renew and grow relationships.

For the first time, PREP is bringing Development and Communications together under one leader. This is a fundraising leadership role first: the Senior Manager will provide strategic direction to our Communications team, rather than lead the day-to-day execution of communications. They will help mobilize the team around a more integrated approach to donor storytelling, impact communications and organizational priorities, ensuring how we communicate PREP's work strengthens relationships, demonstrates impact and inspires people to invest in our mission.

This is a hands-on leadership role with creative freedom to bring PREP's relationship-based fundraising philosophy to life and build on the momentum of a growing organization. We're looking for an experienced fundraiser and storyteller who can set the strategy and execute it, someone who can write a compelling proposal, sit across the table from a prospective donor and make the ask, pick up the phone to build a new relationship, steward a long-standing supporter, and lead and empower a team to bring PREP's impact stories to life.

As PREP grows, this person will have the opportunity to build and shape the Development & Communications function, strengthen the team around them, and grow their leadership within the organization.

## Key Responsibilities

• As a member of PREP's senior leadership team, contribute to organizational strategy, annual planning, decision-making and future planning, bringing a Development, Communications and external-relations perspective to PREP's leadership.

• Build and actively manage PREP's donor, funder and prospect portfolio, continually identifying and qualifying new opportunities and developing tailored strategies to cultivate, solicit, steward, renew and grow relationships.

• Personally lead frontline fundraising and relationship development, including prospect outreach, donor and funder meetings, presentations, direct funding asks and follow-ups, partnering with the Executive Director where executive involvement can strengthen key relationships and opportunities.

• Lead PREP's grant development and management, identifying aligned opportunities, writing and submitting compelling proposals, and collaborating across Student Services and Finance to develop strong narratives, budgets, impact measures and timely funder reports.

• Develop and lead PREP's organization-wide approach to donor stewardship and engagement, creating thoughtful and personalized opportunities that deepen relationships, demonstrate impact and support donor recognition, renewal and increased giving.

• Grow PREP's network and presence within Nova Scotia's business, philanthropic and community landscape, proactively developing new relationships, identifying emerging opportunities and representing PREP at donor meetings, community and business events, conferences and other external engagements.

• Provide strategic direction to PREP's Communications team, establishing shared priorities and mobilizing the team to ensure donor storytelling, impact communications, campaigns and external communications strengthen relationships, build awareness and support PREP's fundraising and organizational priorities.

• Provide thoughtful and intentional people leadership, including clear expectations, delegation, regular coaching and feedback, performance management and reviews, professional development, and opportunities for team members to grow their skills, confidence and leadership.

• Prepare meaningful reports, monitor and analyze fundraising performance, including revenue, pipeline health, donor engagement, renewals, forecasts and progress toward goals, and ensure the donor database is effectively managed and maintained.

• Perform other duties as assigned to support PREP's development goals.

## Education and Experience

• Degree or diploma in a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and professional experience.

• 5+ years of progressive fundraising experience, with demonstrated success generating revenue and building donor relationships.

• Demonstrated experience cultivating, soliciting and stewarding donors, including making direct funding asks.

• Strong grant writing and proposal development experience, with a track record of securing funding and completing funder reporting.

• Experience implementing fundraising strategies, managing donor pipelines and working toward revenue goals and targets.

• People leadership experience, including coaching, performance management and supporting the growth and development of staff.

## What You'll Bring

• An exceptional relationship-builder who approaches fundraising with warmth, curiosity, integrity and a genuine interest in people.

• A strong writer and storyteller who can translate complex information and impact into compelling donor communications.

• Strong strategic thinking and judgment, with the ability to recognize opportunities, assess alignment and make thoughtful recommendations.

• Excellent organization, attention to detail and follow-through, with the ability to independently manage multiple relationships, deadlines and priorities without losing sight of the bigger picture.

• A confident and thoughtful people leader who creates clarity and accountability, empowers others to lead, and invests in the growth and development of their team.

• Comfort building something that is still growing, rather than requiring established systems or a large Development team to be successful.

• Knowledge of or relationships within Nova Scotia's business, philanthropic, nonprofit and community landscape is a strong asset.

Statement of Intention: We are dedicated to empowering and uplifting Black youth in education through our programs, initiatives, and advocacy. While our mission focuses on serving Black students and addressing systemic inequities in education, our team reflects a commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion across all identities. We welcome and encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds. Candidates do not need to identify as Black but must demonstrate a deep understanding of and respect for the lived experiences, cultural backgrounds, and unique challenges faced by the students and communities we serve.

## How to Apply

Please merge your cover letter and resume into one PDF and:

• send to: hr@theprepacademy.ca

• use the subject header: Senior Manager, Development & Communications

Candidates selected for an interview may be asked to participate in a two part interview process.

2239105.title: Fractional CFO
2239105.description:
## About Tidal CFO

Tidal CFO is a remote-first, CPA-led fractional finance firm based in Atlantic Canada. We work with Canadian businesses - startups, nonprofits, and growing SMEs - to bring clarity, structure, and confidence to their finances.

We're not a traditional accounting firm. No timesheets, no billable-hour culture, no scramble to hit utilization targets. We run on a subscription model, which means you're measured by the quality of the work you produce and the outcomes your clients get - not the hours you clock.

Advisory is the product here. Clean books are the foundation everything sits on, and we have a team that produces them - but what our clients actually pay for is someone who reads the numbers before the meeting and tells them what to do about it. That's the seat we're hiring for.

## The Role

We're hiring a Fractional CFO to carry a portfolio of four to five clients as their finance leader. You'll own the financial picture end to end: understanding what the numbers are saying, building the forecasts, running the meeting, and being the go to person the owner or the board calls when a decision is needed.

This is not a review-and-sign-off seat. You'll have a delivery team producing clean books underneath you and a Manager coordinating the close - but the analysis, the modelling, and the judgment are yours. The portfolio is deliberately small because the work goes deep. You are expected to know these businesses well enough to see what is coming before it arrives.

## What You'll Do

• Own the financial picture
• Review monthly results across your portfolio and form a view on what changed, why, and what it means

• Work with the delivery team to resolve close issues affecting your clients

• Look forward, not just back
• Build and maintain 13-week cash flow forecasts and rolling financial models

• Prepare budgets, three-statement pro formas, and scenario analysis as engagements require

• Flag pressure points early - runway, covenant risk, working capital, hiring capacity

• Lead the client relationship
• Run monthly client meetings and drive the actions that come out of them

• Advise between meetings on lender discussions, pricing, hiring, and funding decisions

• Prepare board and investor reporting where the engagement calls for it

• Maintain your professional network and refer opportunities internally - pipeline and pricing are owned elsewhere

## What We're Looking For

## Required

• 6+ years post-designation as a CPA in good standing, including at least two years in a Controller, Director of Finance, or CFO seat with genuine ownership of the numbers.

• A multi-client rhythm - either at a fractional CFO, CAS, or advisory firm, or in public accounting with real industry exposure. You know how to hold several businesses in your head at once and switch between them cleanly.

• At least one year owning month-end close on a deadline, together with substantive FP&A experience. We need both - one without the other does not work in this seat.

• Models you have built from a blank sheet - 13-week cash flow forecasts, three-statement pro formas, and rolling forecasts. Not inherited and updated.

• Strong Excel modelling. Driver-based, formula-driven, no black boxes.

• Credibility with owners, executives, and boards - you can influence a decision maker, and people take your view seriously because you have earned it.

• Comfort with tough conversations and judgment calls. You will need to tell an owner something they do not want to hear, and take a position when the answer is not clean.

## Strong assets

• Professional relationships that outlast the engagement - clients, bankers, lawyers, and other advisors who would take your call three years later

• Industry depth in one or more of: nonprofit, construction and trades, property, or venture-funded startups

• Fluency in QuickBooks Online and Xero - you'll pull your own data

• Bilingual (English / French) is a strong asset - not required

## What This Isn't

This isn't a compliance seat. If your background is audit and tax with no time spent inside a business owning the numbers, this will not be a fit - the work here is forward-looking.

It's also not a sales seat. No quota, no pipeline targets, no prospecting. If your network brings something to the door we will happily take it, but nobody is measuring you on it.

And it isn't a seat where you delegate the work. You have a team producing the books, but you build the model and write the analysis yourself.

## What We Offer

• Competitive compensation aligned with experience, plus a portfolio performance bonus tied to the profitability of the clients you manage

• Comprehensive health benefits and paid vacation

• Fully remote - work from wherever you do your best work

• A small, high-trust team where your work is visible and genuinely valued

• Real influence over how the CFO practice gets built as the firm scales

## To Apply

Send us your resume and a few lines on a decision you helped an owner or a board make, and what the numbers had to do with it - we read those.

2237826.title: Mine Engineer
2237826.description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is transforming the future?

## Who We Are

We are Vale Base Metals – a global supplier of the critical minerals transforming the future.

With industry-leading reserves of copper and nickel in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia, and state-of-the-art infrastructure in the U.K., Canada, and Japan, VBM delivers a secure and responsible supply of high-quality products to customers across Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

Global demand for critical minerals is growing exponentially. From energy to aerospace, batteries to magnets, robotics to artificial intelligence, a secure and responsible supply of critical minerals is fundamental to power modern technologies. And at Vale Base Metals, we are transforming our business to provide a secure and responsible supply of these minerals.

Join our diverse team of 13,000 talented individuals committed to providing mineral security to a world in transition. We invite you to put your skills to work, driving meaningful and enduring change while enjoying a rewarding career.

The Opportunity
We are currently seeking a Mine Engineer to join our Mines Technical Services (MTS) team in Voisey's Bay, Labrador, a fly-in fly-out operation.

The role is a permanent on-site position, working a 2 week on/2 week off schedule.

As a Mine Engineer, you will be responsible for designing, planning, scheduling, and budgeting mine operations. You are responsible to consult with other technical staff such as geologists and metallurgical engineers to determine best mining practices and to set goals for the operations department. The MTS Team works collaboratively with peers and cross functionally with all other areas of the mine to complete tasks in their area of accountability.

Additionally, in this position you will:

Mid Range Planning:
• Prepare mid-range rolling monthly and quarterly mine plans which will provide the basis for short range 1-week planning process.

• Provide guidance to the Mine Operations team on monthly targets for production, development and backfilling activities.

• Ensure plan compliance through frequent field visits and observations.

• Coordinate preparation of plans with all stakeholders including mine operations, mobile and fixed plan maintenance teams, and MTS Mine Planning team.

• Proactively work with the Capital Construction team to ensure mine infrastructure design and execution is completed to support the mine plan.

• Provide support for the mine budget targets.

Mine Design:
• Collect, document, and assess engineering data within the mine to improve efficiency.

• Produce underground mid range mine designs using the ore body block models, decide what methods and equipment will be used for accessing and extracting ore and waste material and provide a schedule for the removal of this material.

• Consult with geologists and engineers about the design, selection, and provision of machines, facilities, and systems for mining, and infrastructure such as access roads, water and power supplies.

General:
• Provide engineering support to our team of geologists, mining engineers, and technologists.

• Coordinate with operations to ensure there is proper implementation of the plans.

• Record mine engineering related information to generate monthly production reports.

• Ensure mining regulations are followed, including the proper use and care of explosives, and the correct ventilation to allow the removal of dust and gases.

• Monitor development and production progress.

• Update and maintain water management designs.

• Establish effective communication channels with both remote and on-site teams.

• Maintain a focus on safety for the work being implemented in conjunction with MTS Safety Plan.

What We Offer You
• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, flex health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare online

• Online training and career development opportunities

• Chartered flights within Newfoundland & Labrador

• 24/7 access to a fully stocked cafeteria with balanced meals prepared by our culinary team

• Access to recreational facilities and social activities (cardio/weight room, gymnasium, music room, movie theatre, etc.)

• Accommodations are equipped with cable TV, internet, and unlimited long-distance calling

• All Personal Protective Equipment is provided upon hire. Employees are given a safety boot allowance and receive a 100% reimbursement for prescription safety glasses

About You

## Education:

• An Undergraduate Degree in Mining Engineering is required.

• P. Eng. designation is required.

## Experience:

• A minimum of 4 years' experience in a similar role within an underground mining environment.

## Skills:

• Ability to design blast patterns, stockpiles, and dumps and provide innovative solutions to mine related problems, knowledge of engineering planning software.

• Knowledge of the Occupational Health and Safety Act.

• Ability to be flexible and adaptable – quickly understand the context of change and proactively adjust.

• Practice teamwork and collaboration within and between areas.

• Aid operating, geological, and technologist staff in mine planning, indicating blast designs, mine schedules, and production plans.

Why Newfoundland and Labrador
Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada's easternmost province, is known for its rugged coastline, rich cultural heritage, and significant natural resources. The province's economy is bolstered by a robust mining sector, where Vale Base Metals' integrated operations play a crucial role.

At Long Harbour, we operate a state-of-the-art processing plant, which refines nickel concentrate from Vale Base Metals' Voisey's Bay mine, located in Labrador, into nickel, copper, and cobalt products. This plant is a cornerstone of our commitment to value-added processing in Canada. Meanwhile, the Voisey's Bay mine is one of the world's most substantial nickel deposits. It provides high-quality nickel, copper, and cobalt, essential for the 21st century economy.

Include to Transform
At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people can act like owners, being their authentic selves and empowering them to deliver results. Vale Base Metals encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

Application
Vale recognizes the Impacts and Benefits Agreements with the Innu Nation and the Nunatsiavut Government in which Innu and Inuit workers have first preference for employment at the Voisey's Bay Mine Site. This is guided by an adjacency principle that first gives preference to those who live on the coast of Labrador, followed by those residing in the rest of Labrador, those residing on the island of the province, followed by the rest of Canada.

Next, priority will be given to Newfoundland and Labrador residents. We also welcome those who are willing to relocate back home and those looking to make NL their permanent home.

Accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Innu Nation members and Nunatsiavut beneficiaries can submit their application to their Vale Indigenous Employment Coordinator.

Employees engaged by the Company must be lawfully able to work for the Company in the country where the role is located. The Company does not provide immigration, work permit, or permanent residence sponsorship or assistance.

2241002.description:
## Professional Support

## Student Accessibility Specialist (PS4)

Education

Burridge Campus

The position is located at Burridge Campus while also supporting the Shelburne Campus and Digby Learning Centre.

Yarmouth, Nova Scotia

## Student Supports

Term, Full-time Position: Commencing approximately October 15, 2026 and ending approximately January 21, 2028
Application deadline is 11:59PM, September 29, 2026

Competition No. 2627-188

The salary scale for Professional Support 4 is based on steps that range from $80,335.45 - $100,491.74. New Professional Support may receive up to a maximum of seven steps for relevant occupational experience which is $88,020.79 annually.

Qualifications

## Qualifications and Occupational Experience:

• The minimum educational qualification for this position is a Bachelor's degree with a focus on adult education, neuroeducation, special education, psychology, social work, or other related field. Certificate in Applied Disability Studies is considered an asset.

• You have a minimum of three years of recent and relevant occupational experience developing and supporting academic accommodation plans for students with disabilities in a post-secondary environment.

• You have strong demonstrated experience using computer applications such as the Microsoft Office Suite, E-mail, Microsoft Teams, and have relevant experience with case file management, assistive technologies, and learning management systems.

• You have specific knowledge and understanding of using online environments to support students.

• You are comfortable working in a digital environment; you take responsibility for acquiring knowledge about advancing technology; and you are committed to using technology to create an exceptional student experience.

• You have demonstrated knowledge of adult learning and student development principles, disabilities, and learning support intervention.

• You have experience in workshop preparation, delivery, and facilitation.

• You have experience supporting/providing service to students and prospective students.

## Relevant Skills and Knowledge

• You demonstrate a commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, accessibility and anti-racism.

• You demonstrate a high level of problem solving, critical thinking and professional judgement while acting independently to serve students holistically and equitably under parameters of policy and external agreements.

• You possess excellent interpersonal skills that enable you to interact with a diversity of people and support resolution of issues.

• You demonstrate understanding of and skill in interviewing techniques and professional boundaries, including privacy and confidentiality.

• You are known for your superior customer service skills and are able to create a relationship of trust beyond the immediate interaction.

• Your superb team working skills enable you to contribute positively to a team environment

• You have specific technical occupational knowledge and skill in assistive technology and developing accommodation plans.

• You have specific knowledge and understanding of diverse populations including Indigenous populations.

• You understand universal design principles to model and promote accessibility among students, colleagues, and educational partners

• You possess excellent coordination skills specifically related to organizing supports and accommodations for students.

• You have proven records management skills and abilities in keeping confidential case notes, creating and maintaining electronic student files, data logging and tracking.

• Excellent communication skills while working with colleagues and serving students in both physical and virtual environments.

Responsibilities

## What you will be doing…

Reporting to the Manager, Student Supports, and under the functional guidance of the Manager, Student Accessibility Services, you are accountable for leading accommodation planning and approval for students with disabilities. This includes but is not limited to supporting student accommodation requests, collecting student documentation, evaluating student requests in relation to their documentation and the nature of programming, applying professional judgement and expertise related to the impact of disability in the NSCC environment and consulting with qualified assessing professionals as needed.

For example, you will:

• Provide learning strategies to complement student accommodation plans including, but not limited to, improving learning skills, integrating technology, accessing learning resources and tools and developing communication plans with faculty.

• Organize services, refer students to appropriate learning supports, assess eligibility for funding programs, facilitate government mandated funding applications, and comply with external government partners' processes and legislation.

• Further the College's vision of equity in relation to our legal duty to accommodate in accordance with the Human Rights Commission, liaise with the Centre for Teaching and Learning and collaborate with faculty members on the implementation of accommodation plans and supports.

• Contribute to and participate in campus initiatives and signature events.

As part of the Student Supports team, you will participate in, or at times lead, the organization of campus events, activities, or committees that contribute to the distinctive student experience, such as Orientation, Wellness Week, and Convocation. You are passionate about supporting students and providing excellent customer service.

As a condition of employment, Professional Support employees at NSCC must complete a part-time adult education program delivered by NSCC. This adult education program is a significant investment on the part of NSCC in the learning and development of new employees. To achieve regular status; all probationary, full or part-time Professional Support employees of the College must successfully complete the program within their probationary period. Term full-time Professional Support employees whose term appointment is twelve or more months are also required to participate in this program.

Candidates selected for interviews will be expected to provide at least three recent occupational references. The successful candidate will be expected to provide official transcripts to show proof of academic achievements.

NSCC is committed to the full inclusion of all applicants. As part of this commitment, NSCC will ensure that applicants are provided reasonable accommodations, as required. If accommodation is needed to participate in the job application process, please contact David Meister, HR & Talent Consultant, at david.meister@nscc.ca. Our Employee Workplace Accommodation Policy can be found here.

Unfortunately, we can not accept late or paper applications.

Competition # : 50019

Department: Emergency Management

Location: DARTMOUTH

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: Exclusion - Non Union - NSPG

Closing Date: 08-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
The Department of Emergency Management is responsible for leading disaster and emergency planning, preparedness, response and recovery activities on behalf of the Province of Nova Scotia. The objective of the Department is to ensure that Nova Scotians are safe, prepared and resilient in the face of disasters and emergencies. The Department leads the coordination and co-operation of partners and resources during provincial-level critical incidents, supports municipal and other partners in regional-level and local events, administers the province's 911 service, maintains critical communications infrastructure and supports operations of our regional emergency management centres. The Department also works to ensure critical government services continue to function during and after critical events.
The Planning and Preparedness Branch enhances preparedness, reduces vulnerabilities, and ensures a coordinated response to critical incidents and emergencies by:

• Standing up and deploying the Nova Scotia Guard

• Reviewing comprehensive emergency management programs by the province and municipalities and ensuring they are robust

• Conducting thorough risk assessments and advising on mitigation strategies

• Administering the Disaster Financial Assistance program to ensure recovery takes place as quickly as possible

• Leading strategic policy, including the management of federal and regional agreements and management of legislation, regulations, policies, establishing standards and preparedness initiatives

• Supporting effective risk management and business continuity for the Province, municipalities, and critical infrastructure partners

• Managing the resiliency office

About Our Opportunity
As the Program Lead, Emergency Financial Assistance Programs, you will lead the administration and continuous improvement of the Emergency Services Provider Fund and Disaster Financial Assistance. You may also support the design and delivery of other emergency-related funding and assistance programs.
Working closely with the Manager, you will provide program, financial and operational leadership. You will help establish clear and consistent program practices, strengthen financial controls, and ensure files and decisions are well documented and audit-ready.
A significant part of this role involves turning program requirements into practical tools and processes. You will develop standard operating procedures, templates, guidance materials, decision documents, reporting tools and other resources that support consistent service delivery. You will also recommend ways to improve programs when policies, community needs or emergency conditions change.

Primary Accountabilities
In this role, you will:

• Lead the planning, administration, monitoring and continuous improvement of the Emergency Services Provider Fund and Disaster Financial Assistance.

• Support the design and implementation of emergency funding and assistance programs, including programs that may need to be established within short operational timelines.

• Develop and maintain standard operating procedures, program guidelines, templates, forms, workflows, decision records and other program documentation.

• Establish clear controls and record-keeping practices so that program decisions, expenditures and files are complete, consistent and audit-ready.

• Manage program budgets, forecasts and financial reporting, and identify emerging pressures, risks and opportunities.

• Provide financial analysis, advice and recommendations to the Manager, senior leaders and program colleagues.

• Prepare briefing notes, presentation materials, correspondence, reports, recommendations and decision documents for senior leaders and, where required, the Minister.

• Build collaborative relationships with municipalities, communities, emergency service providers and partners within and outside government.

• Interpret and apply government legislation, policies, financial controls, procurement requirements and administrative processes.

• Support cross-departmental planning and collaboration.

• Act for the Manager during absences, as assigned.

Qualifications and Experience
To be successful in this role, you have completed post-secondary education in public administration, business administration, finance, accounting, commerce or another relevant discipline, plus several years of related experience managing or administering a program. An acceptable combination of education, training and experience will also be considered.

In addition, you have experience

• Managing a budget and financial reporting.

• Developing program documentation, such as standard operating procedures, guidelines, templates, and process maps

• Preparing briefing notes, recommendations, reports, presentations or other decision-support materials.

• Advising senior leaders on complex program, operational, policy or financial matters.

You also demonstrate strong written communication, as well as presentation skills. You think creatively and strategically while maintaining consistent, fair and accountable program delivery. The ability to manage multiple priorities and adapt plans when operational needs or emergency conditions change is essential to your success.

The following are considered assets including:

• Experience with emergency management, disaster recovery, disaster financial assistance or emergency-services funding programs.

• Knowledge of government decision-making, financial administration, or procurement processes.

• Experience supervising and mentoring staff.

• Proficiency in both English and French.

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
We recognize equivalent combinations of training, education, and experience, providing opportunities for individuals with diverse backgrounds to contribute their skills and expertise. Equivalencies include, but are not limited to:

• A related master's degree combined with relevant program, policy or financial experience.

• A related diploma combined with substantial relevant experience.

• Significant experience leading programs, managing budgets, developing operational processes and advising senior leaders.

Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
Your typical work week is 35 hours with 7-hour days. Most work is completed in an office and will have competing priorities, deadlines and interruptions, particularly when emergency programs are activated. Occasional travel to site or community visits may be required from time to time. Some travel or work may occur outside regular business hours.
You must be available to participate in the on-call Duty Officer stand-by rotation and available to support the response and recovery of emergency events as required in the Provincial Coordination Centre.

What We Offer
• Career Development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career

• Engaging workplace: our Employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in, we have forward-thinking policies and strategies

• Countless career paths

Requisition ID: 1704

Why Choose IMP Aerospace & Defence:
IMP Aerospace & Defence is not only one of the leading companies in the Aerospace field, but we are also one of the most engaging and equality advocating companies to work for. We believe that regardless of where you work at IMP Aerospace & Defence, you are a part of our ever-growing team. IMP is able to achieve success through this teamwork mindset. That is why at IMP, you are not defined by your role.

Position Overview:
Responsible for installing, repairing, inspecting and/or maintaining all electrical and/or electronic equipment within the facility, while following the Canadian Electrical Code, local building codes and regulations and/or established processes and procedures.
This is a journey-level position. Working conditions include restricted movement, hazardous materials, lifting and carrying heavy objects.

What You Will Do:
• Read and interpret drawings, blueprints, schematics, and electrical code specifications to determine layout of industrial electrical equipment and/or installations.

• Work from elevated heights/positions with the aid of aerial man lifts, scaffolding and/or ladders while utilizing fall protection training and equipment.

• Adhere to workplace safety policies, regulations and the use of safety equipment will be the highest priority for you and your co-workers.

• Perform 'general' maintenance tasks including basic mechanical work as required and assisting with emergency maintenance situations.

• Follow the Canadian Electrical Code, local building codes/regulations and Company policy or procedures and interpret electrical code specifications.

• Read, review, amend and/or develop technical wiring diagrams, schematics, blueprints and instructions to cover the scheduled and emergency repairs.

• Conduct a detailed risk assessment of the work sequence to identify the materials and quantities needed for new and/or repair electrical/electronic projects.

• Perform general electrical maintenance (i.e. install, maintain and repair electrical controls, panel boxes, wiring and lighting systems) and programming of equipment (i.e. heating system, ID machines and/or other equipment as required) while operating with safety as a primary concern for self and customer.

• Maintain, repair, test and install electrical motors, generator, alternators, industrial storage batteries and hydraulic and pneumatic electrical control systems.

• Relocate or Install surface mount and/or overhead cables.

• Troubleshoot electrical equipment issues using the appropriate testing devices to determine the condition of electrical equipment such as test and measure voltage, loads, ground faults integrity of circuits.

• Repairs and maintains high voltage systems

• Troubleshoot malfunctions and repair or replace equipment, electrical wiring or fixtures.

• Inspect transformers, circuit breakers and other electrical components for corrective maintenance.

• Conduct preventative maintenance programs and keep maintenance records.

What You Will Bring:
• Completion of High School (Grade 12) or equivalent experience and/or training;

• The candidate will have a red seal industrial electrician certification and minimum of 5 years industry experience with equipment controls.

• Knowledge of the tools, equipment, and materials common to the electrical trade

• Knowledge of applicable electrical codes, standards, and regulations

• Knowledge of electrical application for high and low voltage electric system.

• Must be able to work at heights and in confined spaces;

• Demonstrate a personal commitment to IMP Occupational Health, Safety and Environment policies.

• Participate in Continuous Improvement activities in your area.

• Must be eligible to meet requirements for Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP), U.S. International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and Canadian Government Security Clearances.

The Department of Public Works supports Nova Scotia's 23,000 kilometers of roads and highways and 4,100 bridges. Our Highway Programs Division is growing, and we have a challenging and exciting opportunity available for an Engineering Aide.

This is an exciting opportunity to work alongside our professional team of Engineers who manage all phases of contract work for bridge and highway construction and rehabilitation.

You will calculate, compile and enter data in our Contract Payment System and SAP. With this data, you will produce reports for payment to contractors and perform invoicing and accounts receivable functions with respect to highway and bridge contract work. ## Job Title: Fisheries Engineer
Location: Halifax, NS
TP - KLA - 7986

Meridia Recruitment Solutions is proud to partner with Kleinschmidt, one of North America's premier employee-owned consulting firms specializing in hydropower. Together, we are recruiting for a Fisheries Engineer to join Kleinschmidt's growing team in Canada.

Founded in 1966, Kleinschmidt is a growing company, with an established presence in both Canada and the United States. The people of Kleinschmidt combine engineering expertise, regulatory know-how, and scientific skills to tackle the most challenging projects in renewable energy, water resources, and the natural environment. As an organization, Kleinschmidt brings unparalleled value to clients by developing engineering, regulatory, and environmental solutions that lower cost, shorten schedules, and improve regulatory relationships.

By joining Kleinschmidt, you'll find a vibrant community of professionals eager to share knowledge and help you achieve your career goals. You'll work on a variety of projects across North America, which will give you the opportunity to make a positive impact on local communities and the environment. Best of all, you'll have access to incredible professional development programs. At Kleinschmidt, you're in control of your own destiny!

Role Description:
As the Fisheries Engineer, you will serve a foundational role on multi-disciplinary teams of engineers and scientists in the delivery of fish passage projects. General tasks will include performing and/or managing structural, civil, and hydraulic design tasks in support of fisheries engineering projects.
Responsibilities include:

• Leading the design and implementation of fisheries engineering projects, including fish passage facilities, hatcheries, culvert retrofits, and river or stream restoration efforts.

• Applying expertise in structural, civil, or hydraulic engineering to support fish-friendly infrastructure projects from concept through construction.

• Serving as a project manager on multi-disciplinary projects, overseeing budgets, schedules, deliverables, and coordination with internal teams and external stakeholders.

• Engaging with clients, regulatory agencies, and contractors during all project phases-ensuring compliance with applicable standards, codes, and permitting requirements.

• Mentoring junior engineers and technical staff, fostering professional growth and promoting a collaborative, team-oriented environment.

• Contributing to business development efforts by building and maintaining long-term relationships with clients, preparing proposals, and identifying new project opportunities.

• Participating in field investigations, construction oversight, and technical report development to support fisheries-related infrastructure and habitat restoration work.

## Required Qualifications:

• Bachelor's degree (BS, BSc, or BEng) in Civil, Structural, Hydraulic, or a closely related engineering discipline.

• Licensed Professional Engineer (P.Eng.).

• Minimum of 10 years of professional engineering experience, ideally with a focus in fisheries, water resources, or ecological infrastructure.

• Knowledge of relevant design standards, codes, and best practices in fisheries engineering.

• Proven ability to work directly with clients, regulatory agencies, and contractors throughout all phases of project development and execution.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with experience preparing technical reports, permit documents, and client presentations.

## Preferred Qualifications:

• Experience with fish passage systems, hatchery design, stream restoration, or related fisheries infrastructure projects.

• Familiarity with permitting and regulatory processes in both Canadian and U.S. jurisdictions.

• Demonstrated experience managing multi-disciplinary project teams and overseeing multiple projects concurrently.

• Passion for mentoring junior staff and contributing to a collaborative, high-performing engineering team.

## Additional Requirements:

• Must possess authorization to work in Canada and be able to acquire authorization to work in the United States.

• Must be willing to travel periodically and possess a valid driver's license.

• Preference will be given to candidates in Nova Scotia, but candidates from other provinces will also be considered.

• Strong analytical skills and the ability to work independently.

• Strong skills in MS Office Suite of applications particularly Excel & Access

• Experience with ERP systems (e.g. JD Edwards, SAP, PeopleSoft etc).

• Strong verbal and written communications skills.

• Ability to meet objectives working with colleagues.

2239179.description:
## Job Title: Procurement Specialist
Location: Halifax, NS
TP - AML - 10091

Ace Mechanical Ltd. (Ace) is a well-established mechanical contractor specializing in plumbing, heating, ventilation, and control systems for institutional, commercial, and multi-unit residential projects. Founded in the late 1970s and operating under current ownership since 2014, Ace has built a strong reputation for reliability, quality workmanship, and delivering value to clients across the Halifax Regional Municipality.

Working closely with developers, general contractors, suppliers, and industry partners, Ace Mechanical is known for its collaborative approach and commitment to operational excellence. The company has cultivated a hands-on, team-oriented culture where accountability, professionalism, and strong working relationships contribute to its continued success.
Meridia Recruitment is pleased to partner with Ace Mechanical Ltd. to recruit a Procurement Specialist to join their team in Halifax, Nova Scotia.

Role Description
The Procurement Specialist will play a key role in managing procurement activities across the organization. Working closely with the Director of Operations, this position will support projects from the bidding stage through project execution by managing supplier relationships, material procurement, purchasing activities, and delivery coordination. As the company continues to grow, this role offers the opportunity to become the organization's dedicated procurement subject matter expert and trusted resource for all procurement-related activities.

## Your responsibilities will include:

• Prepare and process purchase orders, review order details for accuracy, and coordinate with internal teams to ensure timely delivery of products.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with suppliers, vendors, and wholesalers.

• Obtain and track supplier quotations, pricing, and delivery commitments.

• Participate in the bidding process by obtaining supplier pricing and supporting quotation requests.

• Support the transition of awarded bids into active projects from a procurement perspective.

• Coordinate material and equipment orders to support operational and project requirements.

• Monitor order status and follow up on outstanding deliveries.

• Track material orders from issuance through delivery.

• Identify and communicate price increases, supply shortages, delays, and discrepancies.

• Assisting in analyzing procurement data to identify cost-saving opportunities and improve overall procurement processes.

• Manage packing slips, material return slips, material transfer slips, and receiving documentation.

• Maintain records of material receipts, returns, credits, and warranty documentation.

• Coordinate supplier returns and warranty claims as required.

• Review supplier invoices against purchase orders and receiving documentation.

• Assist with invoice coding, routing, approval processes, and vendor reconciliations.

• Support Accounting with procurement-related recordkeeping.

• Work closely with project teams to support project delivery requirements.

• Assist with the implementation and ongoing use of ERP software and procurement systems.

• Perform general administrative duties, including obtaining office supplies and supporting internal administration as required.

• Ensure purchasing records and vendor documentation remain accurate, organized, and complete.

Your Qualifications
As the ideal candidate, you are a detail-oriented and dependable procurement professional who thrives in a fast-paced environment and enjoys taking ownership of your work. You excel at building strong supplier relationships, managing multiple priorities, and maintaining accurate records while supporting operational efficiency. You are proactive, adaptable, and comfortable working independently, with a desire to contribute to a growing organization where your impact will be highly visible.

## Your qualifications include:

• 1-3 years of experience in procurement, purchasing, or a related role, ideally within a construction, mechanical contracting, industrial, manufacturing, or other project-based environment.

• Diploma in Engineering Technology, Business Administration, Construction Administration, Supply Chain Management, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Strong understanding of project procurement activities and the construction project lifecycle, including bidding, purchasing, delivery coordination, and project execution.

• Strong organizational, administrative, time-management, and prioritization skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment.

• Excellent attention to detail, accuracy, recordkeeping, and follow-through.

• Effective verbal and written communication skills, with professional customer service and vendor relationship management abilities.

• Self-motivated, dependable, adaptable, and solution-oriented, with the ability to work independently while collaborating across departments.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office 365, particularly Excel, Outlook, and Word.

• Experience with accounting or ERP software is considered an asset.

## Why Join Ace Mechanical Ltd.?

• Competitive salary commensurate with experience.

• Vacation and paid time off.

• Comprehensive health and dental benefits.

• Defined contribution pension plan with employer contributions.

• Opportunity to work with a growing local team supporting mechanical construction operations in our region.

As the system grows and evolves, our work is fast-paced and increasingly connected across programs, services and digital tools, creating new opportunities to improve how families, early childhood educators, service providers and communities are supported across the province.

Primary Accountabilities
The Mechanic uses specialized tools and equipment located in government facilities designed and equipped for mechanical work and assists with field repairs as required. The Mechanic may do any one or a combination of the following or other related duties as required to complete vehicle repairs, modifications and/or preventative maintenance. Some duties will consist of Mechanical Repairs, Internal Combustion / Diesel Engines, Fuel Systems, Engine Management Systems, Electrical, Electronic and Vacuum Control Systems, Power Train Systems, Anti-lock Braking Systems, Steering and Suspension Systems and Heating and Cooling Systems.
