Job Title: System Safety Engineer
Location: Dartmouth, Nova Scotia
TP - PPL- 10087

Meridia Recruitment Solutions has partnered with GeoSpectrum Technologies in search of a System Safety Engineer to join their growing team based in Dartmouth, Nova Scotia.

Founded in 1994, GeoSpectrum Technologies has built a strong reputation for designing and manufacturing advanced underwater acoustic systems and components used in the maritime surveillance, ocean science, defence, and energy sectors. Known for their innovation and collaborative culture, GeoSpectrum delivers highly customized, reliable technology solutions while fostering a workplace built on technical excellence, employee engagement, and continuous growth.

Role Description:
The System Safety Engineer serves as a key member of GeoSpectrum's Integrated Program Teams, acting as the focal point for system safety across complex development programs. This role leads and facilitates system safety activities to ensure risks are systematically identified, assessed, mitigated, and managed throughout the program lifecycle, from concept and design through testing, trials, and final delivery.

Working closely with multidisciplinary teams and subject matter experts, the System Safety Engineer leads System Safety Working Groups (SSWG), facilitates hazard analysis activities, and develops safety documentation in support of internal processes and customer requirements. The successful candidate will play a key role in shaping safety cases, supporting safe system design, and driving the continuous improvement of GeoSpectrum's system safety practices.

## Your responsibilities will include:

• Act as Program Safety Manager within Integrated Program Teams, leading safety activities across the full program lifecycle.

• Facilitate System Safety Working Groups (SSWG) and collaborate with technical subject matter experts to identify, assess, and mitigate hazards.

• Lead and support Preliminary Hazard Analyses (PHA), Functional Hazard Analyses (FHA), Sub-System Hazard Analyses (SSHA), and other safety assessments.

• Develop and maintain safety documentation in accordance with internal processes, customer requirements, and applicable industry standards.

• Partner with Systems Engineers and product teams to define safety requirements and support verification and validation activities.

• Track hazards, mitigations, residual risks, and safety requirement verification activities throughout program execution.

• Support testing, field trials, and operational activities through hazard identification, risk assessment, and safety planning.

• Develop safety cases and supporting documentation for unique testing and operational scenarios.

• Contribute to the continuous improvement of GeoSpectrum's system safety processes, procedures, tools, and methodologies.

• Champion safety best practices and support the evolution of the organization's approach to System Safety Engineering.

Your Qualifications:
The ideal candidate is a collaborative and analytical engineering professional with experience identifying, assessing, and mitigating hazards within complex systems, processes, or operational environments. You are comfortable facilitating technical discussions, working with subject matter experts, and guiding cross-functional teams through safety and risk assessments.

## Key qualifications include:

• Post-secondary education in Engineering (Mechanical, Electrical, Systems, Chemical, or a related discipline) or equivalent career experience.

• Experience conducting hazard analyses, risk assessments, or safety engineering activities within complex technical environments.

• Experience working with complex integrated systems across electrical, mechanical, software, and controls domains.

• Strong understanding of system safety principles, hazard analysis methodologies, and safety management frameworks.

• Demonstrated ability to facilitate technical discussions and collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams and subject matter experts.

• Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving abilities.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively in both technical and non-technical environments.

## Assets include:

• Experience with MIL-STD-882 and related system safety processes.

• Experience leading System Safety Working Groups (SSWG), safety reviews, or hazard analysis sessions.

• Experience as a Program Safety Manager or in a similar system safety role.

• Experience developing safety cases and supporting test or trial activities.

• Experience within defence, aerospace, marine, industrial, energy, or other highly regulated environments.

• Background in process safety, reliability engineering, or related disciplines.

With industry-leading reserves of copper and nickel in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia, and state-of-the-art infrastructure in the U.K., Canada, and Japan, VBM delivers a secure and responsible supply of high-quality products to customers across Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

Global demand for critical minerals is growing exponentially. From energy to aerospace, batteries to magnets, robotics to artificial intelligence, a secure and responsible supply of critical minerals is fundamental to power modern technologies. And at Vale Base Metals, we are transforming our business to provide a secure and responsible supply of these minerals.

Join our diverse team of 13,000 talented individuals committed to providing mineral security to a world in transition. We invite you to put your skills to work, driving meaningful and enduring change while enjoying a rewarding career.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking Underground Mine Trainers to join our People & Community Department in Voisey's Bay, Labrador, a fly-in fly-out operation. Relocation will be required for this role.

This permanent position will be on a 2 week on/2 week off rotation working at the mine site.

As an Underground Mine Trainer, your primary responsibility will be to ensure that employees receive the knowledge and practical training to work safely and productively in an Underground Mine environment. You will also support the development of workers in other related fields as per business need. Your experience and skills will allow you to administer and assist in the development, coordinator, and delivery of all facets of Underground Miner training. You will be required to perform regulatory training, equipment training, assess competencies/qualifications, and execute Vale related training initiatives.

Additionally, in this position you will:

• Provide instruction and functional training on mining equipment and processes to a level of competency required by the company.

• Organize and deliver safe and effective classroom, practical and follow-up training in a timely manner.

• Develop Equipment, OHS, Site and Company related training programs.

• Mentor and coach employees in the safe, effective and productive operation of Underground work.

• Deliver orientation training to all employees, contractors, and visitors to site as scheduled.

• Deliver specialized certification training to the entire site as required. (examples include Fall Protection, LOTO and First Aid).

• Develop, coordinate and provide field instruction and competency evaluations to support applicable maintenance and other training programs.

## What We Offer You

• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, flex health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare online

• Online training and career development opportunities

• Relocation Assistance

• Chartered flights within Newfoundland & Labrador

• 24/7 access to a fully stocked cafeteria with balanced meals prepared by our culinary team

• Access to recreational facilities and social activities (cardio/weight room, gymnasium, music room, movie theatre, etc.)

• Accommodations are equipped with cable TV, internet, and unlimited long-distance calling

• All Personal Protective Equipment is provided upon hire. Employees are given a safety boot allowance and receive a 100% reimbursement for prescription safety glasses

## About You

## Education:

• A minimum of Secondary School or equivalent is required.

• Completion of a program of study related to adult education and administration of workplace learning and training is preferred.

• Underground Hard Rock Miner Common Core with Specialty Modules or equivalent (Please provide transcript with application).

• Additional Trainer Certifications (Workplace NL Trainer, St John Ambulance Trainer, etc.) are considered an asset.

• Minimum Class 5 provincial Driver License.

## Experience:

• A minimum of 8 years' underground mining experience with a proven ability to operate a variety of underground equipment and processes across production and development as well as construction aspects of mining (Scoop Tram, Haulage Truck, Mechanized Rock Bolter, Jumbo, In-The-Hole drill (ITH), Scaler, Scissor Deck, UG Construction, muck circuit- crusher/conveyor, boom truck, forklift, pastefill etc.) is required. A combination of operating and maintenance experience with underground equipment will also be considered.

• Experience with Maclean, CAT, Sandvik and Epiroc equipment preferred.

• Experience with Mining Equipment Simulator Operation preferred. Experience with computer- or console- based video games may be considered as transferable skills.

• Experience working with a Learning Management System preferred.

• Underground Mine Rescue experience is considered an asset.

## Skills:

• Ability to promote and demonstrate Risk Management and Health & Safety in training.

• Strong communication and presentation skills – both oral and written.

• Solid working knowledge of NL OH&S and Mines Safety Acts and Regulations.

• Experience working in a diverse culture and the ability to facilitate effectively.

• Self-motivated, and be an active team member to ensure team goals are achieved.

• Proficient use of Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, etc.).

## Why Newfoundland and Labrador

Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada's easternmost province, is known for its rugged coastline, rich cultural heritage, and significant natural resources. The province's economy is bolstered by a robust mining sector, where Vale Base Metals' integrated operations play a crucial role.

At Long Harbour, we operate a state-of-the-art processing plant, which refines nickel concentrate from Vale Base Metals' Voisey's Bay mine, located in Labrador, into nickel, copper, and cobalt products. This plant is a cornerstone of our commitment to value-added processing in Canada. Meanwhile, the Voisey's Bay mine is one of the world's most substantial nickel deposits. It provides high-quality nickel, copper, and cobalt, essential for the 21st century economy.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people can act like owners, being their authentic selves and empowering them to deliver results. Vale Base Metals encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

Vale recognizes the Impacts and Benefits Agreements with the Innu Nation and the Nunatsiavut Government in which Innu and Inuit workers have first preference for employment at the Voisey's Bay Mine Site. This is guided by an adjacency principle that first gives preference to those who live on the coast of Labrador, followed by those residing in the rest of Labrador, those residing on the island of the province, followed by the rest of Canada.

Next, priority will be given to Newfoundland and Labrador residents. We also welcome those who are willing to relocate back home and those looking to make NL their permanent home.

Accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Innu Nation members and Nunatsiavut beneficiaries can submit their application to their Vale Indigenous Employment Coordinator.

Employees engaged by the Company must be lawfully able to work for the Company in the country where the role is located. The Company does not provide immigration, work permit, or permanent residence sponsorship or assistance.

Pay Grade: G01

Apply by: Sunday, October 4th, 2026

## #ValeBaseMetals

Interested applicants must submit their application online at https://vale.eightfold.ai/careers.

If you're looking for a fulfilling career that can make a real difference in your life, and the lives of others, you've come to the right place.

2240070.description:
Competition # : 49843

Department: Education & Early Childhood Development

Location: HALIFAX

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: Exclusion - Non Union - NSPG

Closing Date: 28-Sep-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us The Department of Education and Early Childhood Development (EECD) is leading the transformation of the early years and public education system in Nova Scotia. We are doing this by designing an innovative curriculum, facilitating excellence in teaching and learning, ensuring an inclusive education experience, and working closely with our partners in early learning and education. This will provide children, students, and families with a strong foundation for success. This department is a perfect fit for those that want to be part of the future of early learning and public education in the province by supporting student learning in a progressive and responsive policy environment. The Early Learning and Child Care (ELCC) branch regulates, funds, and supports early learning and child care providers and sector partners across Nova Scotia. As the sector continues to evolve within a publicly funded early learning and child care system, the department is strengthening how it works with operators to support sustainability, monitor public investment, and help funded organizations meet evolving expectations.About Our Opportunity The Early Learning and Child Care (ELCC) sector is continuing to grow and mature as part of Nova Scotia's publicly funded child care system. This transformation has increased the scale, complexity, and visibility of educator-facing services, including educator classification, professional development validation, bursary administration, workforce supports, and digital service delivery. As Manager, Educator Services, you will provide operational leadership for a portfolio of services that support early childhood educators and strengthen the ELCC workforce. You will oversee educator classification processes, professional learning validation, bursary administration, educator-facing digital services, and high-volume educator inquiries and service requests. This work requires strong operational judgement, service delivery experience, and the ability to lead in a changing environment where programs, systems, and expectations continue to evolve. You will work closely with the Director, Educator and Family Services, ELCC program areas, digital delivery partners, sector stakeholders, and post-secondary or training partners to support clear, consistent, and responsive educator services. Your work will help strengthen accountability, improve service quality, support workforce development, and ensure educator-facing services are aligned with the needs of the child care system.Primary Accountabilities
As the Manager, Educator Services, you will:

• Provide operational leadership for educator-facing services, including educator classification, professional development validation, bursary administration, workforce supports, and related service channels.

• Lead and manage day-to-day service delivery to support timely, consistent, and accurate responses to educator inquiries, applications, and service requests.

• Oversee processes related to educator classification, including application review, service standards, quality assurance, reporting, and continuous improvement.

• Support the validation of professional learning and training activities required for educator classification, professional development, or workforce-related initiatives.

• Provide oversight for bursary administration and related supports that help strengthen the early childhood education workforce.

• Support educator-facing digital services, including service readiness, user support, process improvement, data quality, and operational feedback for system enhancements.

• Monitor service volumes, trends, risks, backlogs, and operational issues, and recommend practical actions to improve service delivery and accountability.

• Develop and maintain policies, procedures, tools, templates, and service standards to support consistent and transparent educator services.

• Work with internal partners, external stakeholders, and service providers to clarify requirements, resolve complex issues, and support coordinated service delivery.

• Provide leadership to staff through coaching, workload management, performance support, and clear communication of priorities and expectations.

• Prepare briefing materials, reports, analysis, and recommendations for the Director, senior leaders, and other decision-makers.

• Support workforce development initiatives by contributing operational advice, service data, and practical insight into educator needs, training pathways, and system pressures.

• Promote a respectful, service-oriented, and accountable work environment that supports educators, strengthens public trust, and contributes to a sustainable early learning and child care system.

Qualifications and Experience
To be successful in this role, you have a bachelor's degree in public administration, business administration, or a related field, in addition to a minimum of six years of related experience. An equivalent combination of training and experience may be considered.

You bring experience leading programs, services, or operational teams in a public sector, education, early learning and child care, human services, workforce development, regulatory, or client-service environment. You understand how to manage service delivery in a complex and changing system, and you are comfortable balancing policy requirements, operational realities, client service, and accountability.

You have experience leading people, setting priorities, managing workloads, supporting staff performance, and improving processes. You can work through ambiguity, identify service risks or gaps, and develop practical solutions that improve consistency, timeliness, accuracy, and user experience.

You also have experience:

• Managing programs or services that involve application review, assessment, eligibility, classification, certification, validation, or other structured decision-making processes.

• Interpreting and applying legislation, regulations, policies, procedures, program criteria, or service standards.

• Supporting service delivery improvements, including process mapping, workflow redesign, quality assurance, performance monitoring, or digital service implementation.

• Working with internal and external partners to resolve complex issues and support consistent program or service delivery.

• Using information, data, and service trends to identify risks, monitor performance, and make recommendations.

• Preparing briefing materials, reports, correspondence, procedures, and recommendations for management or senior leaders.

• Communicating clearly with staff, partners, stakeholders, and service users, including when issues are sensitive, urgent, or complex.

• Managing confidential and sensitive information with sound judgement and discretion.

You are a collaborative leader, strong communicator, and practical problem solver. You bring good judgement, professionalism, and a service-oriented approach to your work, and you can support accountability while building positive relationships across a complex service system.

Assets
• Knowledge of Nova Scotia's early learning and child care sector, including educator classification, professional learning, workforce development, and sector sustainability.

• Experience with educator certification, classification, credential assessment, registration, licensing, or similar assessment-based services.

• Experience administering bursaries, grants, training supports, workforce development programs, or related funding initiatives.

• Experience supporting digital service delivery, online applications, registries, case management systems, or client portals.

• Experience developing or monitoring service standards, performance indicators, dashboards, or operational reports.

• Experience working with post-secondary institutions, training providers, professional learning organizations, sector partners, or regulated service providers.

• Experience leading staff in a high-volume, client-service, operational, or public-facing program environment.

• Bilingualism in English and French.

Equivalency We welcome candidates with diverse and transferable experience. Applicants who do not meet the exact education requirement may still be considered if they clearly demonstrate an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience. Equivalent experience should show substantial depth in financial analysis, accounting, funding administration, compliance monitoring, internal controls, or a closely related area. Applicants relying on equivalency must clearly explain in their application how their background gives them the financial judgement, analytical skills, and accountability experience needed for this role.Benefits Based on the employment status, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined BenefitDefined Benefit Pension Plan Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government eBenefits for government employeesmployees.What We Offer

• Engaging workplace: our employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in, we have forward-thinking policies and strategies

• Countless career paths

2238148.title: Dietary Aide - WEEKENDS ONLY
2238148.description:
## RISK MANAGEMENT

Department: Food Services

Location: Berwick, Nova Scotia

Union: Unionized

Responsible to: Director of Food Services

## Position Summary

The Dietary Aide supports the delivery of high-quality food services to residents, tenants, visitors, and staff by assisting with food preparation, tray assembly, meal service, dishwashing, sanitation, and kitchen operations. The Dietary Aide contributes to a positive dining experience by ensuring meals are prepared, delivered, and served in a safe, efficient, and resident-centered manner. The position plays an important role in maintaining food safety standards, supporting therapeutic diets, promoting cleanliness throughout the Food Services Department, and working collaboratively with team members to provide exceptional service.

## Key Accountabilities

## Meal Preparation and Service

• Participate in all aspects of tray preparation, assembly, and meal service.

• Prepare and serve food and beverages according to established menus, recipes, portion standards, and therapeutic diet requirements.

• Assist with the preparation of special diets and texture-modified foods as directed.

• Assist with the preparation of vegetables, sandwiches, salads, desserts, nourishments, and other food items as assigned.

• Ensure food items are presented in an appealing and appetizing manner.

• Support resident-centered dining practices and respond respectfully to resident needs and preferences, while promoting dignity and choice.

• Check internal temperatures and adhere to all local and provincial health and safety regulations.

## Food Delivery and Dining Support

• Deliver food carts, meal trays, and supplies to designated areas throughout the facility.

• Collect food carts, trays, dishes, and utensils following meal service.

• Strip and clean trays and dining room tables.

• Assist in maintaining a pleasant, clean, and organized dining environment.

• Support positive interactions with residents, families, visitors, and team members during meal service.

• Supervise and support residents during meals in shared dining spaces, ensuring a safe, comfortable, and positive dining experience.

• Observe any reported changes in residents' appetite, eating patterns, swallowing difficulties, or concerns to nursing staff.

## Cleaning and Sanitation

• Operate dishwashing equipment according to established procedures.

• Clean and sanitize dishes, utensils, equipment, work surfaces, and food preparation areas.

• Participate in departmental cleaning schedules and sanitation programs.

• Ensure compliance with food safety, infection prevention, and workplace safety standards.

• Maintain cleanliness and organization of storage areas, workstations, and service areas.

• Dispose of waste and recycling according to organizational procedures.

• Record daily temperatures of all dishwashers; wash and rinse cycles.

• Maintain monthly cleaning and kitchen duties schedules; sign off when completed.

## Inventory and Supply Support

• Stock shelves, refrigerators, and storage areas as required.

• Assist with receiving, storing, rotating, and organizing food and supplies.

• Report shortages, damaged products, or equipment concerns to the appropriate supervisor.

• Support efforts to minimize waste and ensure proper food handling practices.

• Ensure correct labeling of food items and leftovers.

• Follow the first-in-first-out rule to ensure correct rotation of food items.

• Document spoiled foods and wastage to monitor inventory.

## Teamwork and Collaboration

• Work collaboratively with Food Services Department team members and other departments.

• Follow oral and written instructions accurately and efficiently.

• Demonstrate flexibility in performing assigned duties and learning new tasks.

• Participate in orientation, training, and educational opportunities as required.

• Report equipment concerns, food shortages, safety hazards, and incidents promptly.

• Be respectful of your fellow workers.

• Take part in department quality control audits and procedures.

• Assist in the training of department staff and students.

• Perform other related duties as assigned.

## Qualifications

## Education

## Required:

• Grade 12 education or equivalent.

• First aid in choking (obtained internally within organizational timelines).

## Preferred:

• Recent Food Safety Training or equivalent food safety certification.

• Additional food service, hospitality, or dietary training.

## Experience

## Preferred:

• Previous experience in institutional, healthcare, long-term care, hospitality, or commercial food service environments.

## Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

• Ability to read, write, and follow oral and written instructions.

• Ability to complete routine written documentation and records.

• Strong communication and interpersonal skills.

• Commitment to excellent customer service and resident satisfaction.

• Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.

• Willingness to learn new skills and tasks.

• Ability to maintain confidentiality regarding residents and organizational information.

• Knowledge of safe food handling and sanitation practices is considered an asset.

• Knowledge of dementia care principles and the ability to use respectful, person-centred approaches when communicating and supporting residents during meal service.

## Working Conditions

## Physical Demands

• Shift work, including days, evenings, weekends, and holidays.

• Frequent standing and walking throughout the shift.

• Ability to safely handle and transport food service supplies, meal trays, and equipment using appropriate lifting techniques and assistive devices as required.

• Frequent reaching, bending, stooping, pushing, pulling, and repetitive movements.

• Ability to work safely while handling food service equipment and supplies.

## Mental Demands

• Ability to maintain attention to detail while working in a fast-paced environment.

• Ability to prioritize tasks and complete work within established timelines.

• Ability to follow detailed instructions and maintain accuracy.

• Ability to adapt to changing priorities and operational needs.

• Frequent interaction with older adults, including those living with dementia and other cognitive impairments.

## Environmental Conditions

• Exposure to kitchen environments including varying temperatures.

• Exposure to cleaning and sanitation products.

• Exposure to dishwashing equipment, food service equipment, and hot surfaces.

• Work performed throughout the Food Services Department and various service areas within the facility.

## Interpersonal Relationships

The Dietary Aide maintains positive and professional working relationships with:

• Residents and families.

• Food Services Department team members.

• Nursing and clinical staff.

• Environmental Services staff.

• Leadership team members.

• Volunteers, visitors, and community partners.

Teamwork, communication, and mutual respect are essential to providing exceptional resident care and service.

## Core Competencies

• Resident-Centered Service.

• Teamwork and Collaboration.

• Food Safety and Sanitation.

• Accountability.

• Communication.

• Attention to Detail.

• Adaptability.

• Professionalism.

• Time Management.

• Continuous Learning.

2238730.title: Senior Product Marketing Specialist
2238730.description:
## Senior Product Marketing Specialist
Halifax, Nova Scotia
Reference # JL-PAL-10033

For more than 50 years, PAL Aerospace has been delivering airborne special mission solutions that help customers address complex security, safety, environmental, and economic challenges around the world. Operating in more than 40 countries, PAL Aerospace provides a full spectrum of capabilities spanning special mission aircraft, mission system software, engineering and design services, contracted ISR operations, aircrew training, and in-service support. Today, the organization serves customers across defence, public safety, law enforcement, border security, maritime surveillance, environmental monitoring, and civil operations.

As PAL Aerospace continues to grow, they are seeking a Senior Product Marketing Specialist to join their Halifax-based marketing team.

## The Role

Reporting to Trevor, Director of Marketing, the Senior Product Marketing Specialist will lead product marketing efforts across PAL Aerospace's growing portfolio of special mission solutions, including the PAL Aerospace Mission System and CarteNav's AIMS-ISR and AIMS-C4 platforms. Working closely with engineering, operations, software development, business development, and customers worldwide, you will transform complex technical capabilities into compelling stories that resonate with operators, agencies, partners, OEMs, and government stakeholders.

This is an opportunity for a product marketer who wants to move beyond traditional SaaS marketing and help shape the future of products that support public safety, defence, surveillance, environmental monitoring, and mission-critical operations around the world.

The ideal candidate is not a marketing generalist, but rather someone who is passionate about product marketing, has strong opinions on positioning, messaging, and competitive differentiation, and enjoys working closely with technical subject matter experts to bring products to market.

## Duties & Responsibilities:

• Drive product positioning, messaging, and value proposition development across mission system software, special mission aircraft solutions, contracted ISR operations, and engineering services.

• Lead go-to-market planning and execution for new product launches and major product enhancements.

• Conduct customer interviews, competitive analysis, win-loss reviews, and market research to identify and validate differentiators and market opportunities.

• Work closely with Business Development, Sales, Engineering, Operations, and Product teams to ensure organizational alignment and go-to-market readiness.

• Develop sales enablement content, including presentations, product briefs, one-pagers, competitive positioning materials, thought leadership content, case studies, and campaign assets.

• Own and facilitate customer and partner-facing broadcasts, webinars, and thought leadership initiatives from concept development through execution and content repurposing.

• Serve as a product expert and trusted marketing partner to internal stakeholders and external partners.

2240148.title: Treasury & Corporate Finance Co-op Student
2240148.description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is growing?

## Who We Are

We are Vale Base Metals – a global supplier of the critical minerals transforming the future.

With industry-leading reserves of copper and nickel in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia, and state-of-the-art infrastructure in the U.K., Canada, and Japan, VBM delivers a secure and responsible supply of high-quality products to customers across Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

Global demand for critical minerals is growing exponentially. From energy to aerospace, batteries to magnets, robotics to artificial intelligence, a secure and responsible supply of critical minerals is fundamental to power modern technologies. And at Vale Base Metals, we are transforming our business to provide a secure and responsible supply of these minerals.

Join our diverse team of 15,000 talented individuals committed to providing mineral security to a world in transition. We invite you to put your skills to work, driving meaningful and enduring change while enjoying a rewarding career.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking a Treasury & Corporate Finance co-op student to join our Treasury team in Toronto.

The role is hybrid and an 8, 12, or 18 months fixed term position starting in January 2027. This posting is for an existing position vacancy.

As a Treasury & Corporate Finance student, you'll gain hands-on exposure to treasury operations, financial analysis, cash and liquidity management, corporate finance, and financial risk management within a global organization.

Additionally, in this position you will:

• Support the preparation of recurring treasury and financial reports; analyze data to identify trends, variances, and potential issues; and assist with presentation materials for internal stakeholders.

• Help monitor daily cash positions, update short-term cash flow forecasts, support payment and receipt processes, and assist with bank account reconciliations and investigation of outstanding items.

• Support analyses of debt, liquidity, capital structure, funding alternatives, interest costs, and other corporate finance topics.

• Assist with data collection, reporting, and analysis related to foreign exchange, interest rate, counterparty credit, and liquidity risks, in accordance with established policies and controls.

• Help improve reports, controls, dashboards, and workflows using Excel, Microsoft Copilot, artificial intelligence, and other data-analysis or automation tools.

• Maintain accurate records and supporting documentation, follow internal policies and procedures, and assist with audit or compliance requests.

• Contribute to treasury projects and cross-functional initiatives, prepare meeting materials, track agreed actions, and perform other relevant assignments.

## What We Offer You

• Competitive compensation

• Flexible work arrangements

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Online training and career development opportunities

• Opportunities to build your network and lots of fun!

## About You

## Education:

• Currently enrolled in your second year of a bachelor's degree program in Finance, Economics, Business Administration, Accounting, Engineering, Data Analytics, or a related field.

## Skills:

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy.

• Clear written and verbal communication skills.

• Ability to organize priorities, meet deadlines, work collaboratively, and handle confidential information responsibly.

• Proactive attitude, curiosity, sound judgment, and willingness to learn.

• Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint; familiarity with Microsoft Copilot, artificial intelligence, data visualization, automation tools, or enterprise systems is an asset.

## Why Toronto

Vale Base Metals' Toronto office serves as a pivotal hub for the company's operations. This office is central to Vale Base Metals' finance, strategic planning, commercial (marketing and sales), and sustainability teams, driving key initiatives that support the company's global mission. Toronto's vibrant, diverse, and dynamic environment enhances Vale Base Metals' ability to innovate and excel in these critical areas, reflecting the city's status as a leading international business center.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people can act like owners, being their authentic selves and empowering them to deliver results. Vale Base Metals encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry. In accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Employees engaged by the company must be lawfully able to work for the company in the country where the role is located. The company does not provide immigration, work permit, or permanent residence sponsorship or assistance.

## Director, Contractor Network
Dartmouth, Nova Scotia
Reference # JL-CAA-9930

CAA Atlantic is one of Canada's most trusted and respected membership organizations, proudly serving more than 330,000 members across Atlantic Canada. As part of the Canadian Automobile Association federation, with nearly 7 million members nationally, we help Atlantic Canadians move through life with greater safety, confidence, and peace of mind-whether they are on the road close to home or planning travel around the world. Recognized as one of Canada's Most Admired Corporate Cultures, CAA Atlantic offers a workplace where purpose, service, and people come together. We are committed to supporting employee growth through ongoing learning, meaningful development opportunities, competitive benefits, a generous vacation allowance, and an annual incentive program. For leaders who are passionate about service excellence, operational performance, and member value, this is an opportunity to contribute to a trusted Atlantic Canadian brand with national reach.

• Careers CAA Atlantic - Employee Benefits

• Careers CAA Atlantic- Team Member Stories

## The Role

CAA Atlantic is seeking a Director, Contractor Network to play a critical leadership role in shaping the quality, reliability, and future evolution of our roadside and repair partner network. Working closely with the Vice President, Operations and the roadside team, this role will lead the strategy, performance, engagement, and continuous improvement of a regional network that directly supports member safety, service excellence, and trust across Atlantic Canada. The Director oversees a network of more than 150 mobile service providers and more than 50 Approved Auto Repair Service facilities. This is a hands-on strategic leadership role focused on strengthening partner relationships, elevating service quality, advancing safe and consistent operations, improving network performance, and ensuring members receive trusted support when they need it most.

## Duties & Responsibilities:

• Partner with the Vice President, Operations to develop and execute a multi-year strategy for the evolution, performance, and management of the Contractor Network.

• Lead network strategies in collaboration with internal teams, service providers, vendors, and external partners, ensuring alignment with CAA Atlantic's strategic objectives, values, and member promise.

• Ensure reliable, high-quality service delivery to CAA members through clear operating standards, strong partner engagement, and disciplined performance management.

• Use contracts, service standards, KPIs, dashboards, and partner scorecards to establish expectations, monitor performance, identify root causes, and drive continuous improvement.

• Lead the implementation and operationalization of digital tools and solutions that enhance contractor performance, member experience, safety, and operational efficiency.

• Strengthen service provider engagement through communication, training, coaching, feedback, and incentive programs aligned with organizational priorities.

• Negotiate and manage contracts, support cost containment initiatives, and contribute to annual budget planning, expenditure tracking, and cost reviews.

• Develop and manage plans to strengthen collaboration with Approved Auto Repair Service partners, enhance the AARS program, and identify strategic opportunities for growth.

• Collaborate across CAA Atlantic and with other CAA Clubs to identify best practices, streamline operations, improve efficiencies, and support consistent service excellence.

• Support employee and partner development through training, coaching, mentorship, open communication, and a commitment to safe, member-focused service delivery.

## Qualifications & Experience:

• Post-secondary education in Business Administration or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Minimum 10 years of progressive leadership experience in a medium or large-scale organization, ideally in operations, vendor or partner management, network operations, automotive, towing, service, heavy equipment, transportation, or a related industry.

• Demonstrated experience developing strategy, managing contracts, negotiating agreements, evaluating vendor performance, and leading external partner relationships.

• Strong understanding of towing operations, service delivery networks, small business owner/operator dynamics, and industry trends or best practices.

• Experience using KPIs, dashboards, financial information, and operational data to drive performance improvement, budget discipline, and service quality.

• Proven ability to provide feedback and coaching, manage escalations, resolve disputes, and maintain strong partner relationships.

• Excellent communication, presentation, problem-solving, influencing, and leadership capabilities, with the ability to build credibility across all levels of an organization.

• Familiarity with safety standards and compliance requirements within service delivery networks is considered an asset.

• Willingness to travel throughout Atlantic Canada.

• Bilingual proficiency in English and French, written and verbal, is considered an asset.

## ABOUT ALDERWOOD:

Alderwood cares for 70 residents across Nursing Home and Residential Care. Our home is divided into six distinct home areas; five Nursing Home (11-12 residents each) and one Residential Care (11 residents). All residents have private rooms and bathrooms to ensure their comfort and dignity, and Alderwood Home Areas are designed to create a genuine sense of belonging for our residents.

We are dedicated to enhancing the quality of life for our residents supporting their mental, physical, spiritual, emotional, and social well-being through compassionate, person-centered care. Our team of skilled, caring staff work together to create a safe, comfortable, and nurturing environment where residents feel valued and supported every day.

## ABOUT THE ROLE:

Alderwood is seeking a dedicated, long-term leader who is committed to growing with our organization and making a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents. This person will provide thoughtful, and strategic direction, as part of the Senior Leadership Team.

The Director of Care (DOC) plays a key leadership role in supporting resident-centered care and the overall operations of the home. Working closely with the Clinical Nursing Manager, the DOC ensures clinical excellence, operational efficiency, and continuous quality improvement. Together, these roles compassion, professionalism, and accountability.

This role holds primary responsibility for the operation and leadership of the Nursing Department, ensuring provision of comprehensive nursing and Allied health services to all residents which meet the Mission, Vision, and Values of Alderwood.

This role is ideal for a leader who is motivated by optimizing operations while maintaining a warm, home-like environment for residents and staff. You will have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on daily care delivery and the overall success of the home.

## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Provide leadership, direction, and oversight for all clinical and care operations

• Collaborate with other senior leaders to optimize operational efficiency and resident outcomes

• Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, licensing standards, and quality initiatives

• Lead, mentor, and develop direct reports and frontline staff

• Oversee staffing and workforce planning to meet resident care needs

• Allocation and monitoring of both fiscal and personnel resources

• Implement and monitor policies, procedures, and best practices

• Foster a culture of teamwork, respect, and continuous improvement

• Support strategic initiatives to enhance resident experience and organizational performance

## REQUIREMENTS:

• Current License with NSCN

• Demonstrated leadership experience and ability to co-ordinate, supervise and oversee a comprehensive nursing care program

• Show a proven track record of leadership in a team setting

• Clinical experience in a long-term care setting an asset

• Minimum 5 years nursing experience

• Effective written, oral and interpersonal communication skills

• Demonstrated experience with use of technology as part of operations, with a working knowledge of computers (ie. Microsoft Office applications, healthcare management software, scheduling programs)

• Adheres to the Director of Care roles and responsibilities in the Job Position Outline

• Skilled in problem solving, flexible, strong organizational skills and adherence to timelines

• History of satisfactory attendance and capable to meet the demands of the job

## BENEFITS:

We value our leaders and are committed to supporting their professional growth, wellbeing, and work-life balance. As part of our team, you will enjoy a comprehensive benefits package, including:

• Competitive salary

• Health and Dental Coverage

• Life Insurance

2240244.description:
Competition # : 49880

Department: Public Prosecution Service

Location: PORT HAWKESBURY

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: NSCAA

Closing Date: 29-Sep-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
The Public Prosecution Service (PPS) offers a unique and meaningful opportunity to contribute to justice and public safety. Established in 1990 as the first statutorily based independent prosecution service in Canada, the mandate of the PPS is rooted in its commitment to ensuring fair and equal treatment in the prosecution of criminal and provincial offences.
We are looking for the brightest legal minds, who also reflect the rich diversity of our province! We don't just accept difference – we celebrate a supportive culture of diversity and belonging. We strive to create an environment where different perspectives and experiences are welcomed and valued. We encourage applications from those that equally value and champion equity, diversity, inclusion, and accessibility (EDIA).

Why Choose Us?
A career with the Public Prosecution Service in Nova Scotia provides a unique opportunity to contribute to justice, public safety, and the overall well-being of the community while working in a professional, inclusive, and ethical environment.
We are a dedicated and passionate team with a determination to make a difference in the society we serve, utilizing our expertise and recognizing and applying an equity and inclusion lens to our work, in our training and development, workplace culture, communications, partnering and engagement to ensure we protect and reflect the communities we live in and serve.

What We Offer
1. Commitment to Justice and Public Interest:
This is achieved by performing prosecution duties with fairness, professionalism, and integrity. Employees actively contribute to upholding the principles of justice in Nova Scotia.
2. Mission and Goals:
Aligning with the Government of Nova Scotia's priority of fulfilling social responsibility for public safety, the PPS' mission and goals include providing excellence in public service, identifying, and managing resources effectively, applying best business practices, and fostering an environment for independent prosecutorial discretion that recognizes the importance of diversity and inclusion in ensuring representation reflective of the community.
3. Core Business Functions:
Employees at the PPS engage in core business functions that play a crucial role in the legal landscape of Nova Scotia. These functions include representing the Crown in criminal and quasi-criminal matters at all levels of court, handling appeals, providing legal advice and assistance to law enforcement, and actively participating in the development of criminal law and prosecutions policy.
4. Professional Development and High Ethical Standards:
The PPS is committed to maintaining a diverse team that reflects excellence, dedication to public service, and high ethical standards. Employees have the opportunity for professional development in a welcoming environment that values continuous improvement and recognizes diversity and inclusion contributes to a healthy and thriving workplace culture that allows team members to be their full selves at work, while upholding the highest ethical principles.
5. Community Engagement:
The PPS is focused on providing a service that is reflective of the community it serves. By fostering diversity and inclusivity, employees contribute to building a legal system that understands and respects the needs and perspectives of the broader community.
6. Impactful Contribution to Society:
Working for the PPS allows individuals to make a direct and meaningful impact on society by upholding the rule of law, protecting the safety and well-being of the community, and ensuring the fair treatment of those accused of prohibited conduct.
For more information on the Public Prosecution Service please visit the following link: https://novascotia.ca/pps/

About Our Opportunity
This position is based in Cape Breton Region will report to the Chief Crown Attorney, Cape Breton Region, to whom the incumbent is accountable for the provision of competent prosecution services. The Crown Attorney will advise law enforcement agencies when requested. Other key responsibilities include conducting the prosecution of charges resulting from matters within the Public Prosecution Service mandate that result from law enforcement agency investigations and other prosecutions and duties as directed by the Chief Crown Attorney, Cape Breton.

Qualifications and Experience
You are a practicing member of the Nova Scotia Barristers' Society (or eligible to become so) and have a thorough understanding of the prosecution process, and competence in the areas of criminal procedures, evidence, and substantive criminal law. You must have at least one year of criminal prosecutions or other criminal law experience
You may be required to travel throughout the province to prosecute cases and may be required to do so for extended periods of time.
Successful applicants may be required to provide a current Certificate of Standing from their law society, including all jurisdictions of which they are members, whether non-practicing or practicing.
The above qualifications will be assessed using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Additional Information
This is a permanent employment opportunity, located in Port Hawkesbury, NS.
Must have access to reliable transportation as travel throughout the region and across the province is required.

Pay Grade: CA - CA

Salary Range: $3,639.93 - $7,697.97 Bi-Weekly

2238017.title: General Manager
2238017.description:
## General Manager
Halifax or Annapolis Valley, Nova Scotia
Reference # JL-PGD-10043

Parsons Green Developments (PGD) is one of Nova Scotia's most active privately owned real estate development and property management companies. Since developing its first apartment building in 2008, PGD has grown from a single 22-unit property into a portfolio of nearly 400 residential units spanning multiple communities throughout the Annapolis Valley and beyond. With additional communities under construction, including over 100 units opening in the next year, and a substantial pipeline of future projects, the portfolio is expected to continue growing significantly over the coming years.

Known for delivering high-quality rental communities, strong tenant experiences, and long-term investment performance, PGD has established itself as a market leader in creating Class A rental housing throughout the Valley. The company prides itself on integrity, entrepreneurial thinking, operational excellence, and a commitment to building communities that residents are proud to call home.

As the organization continues its rapid growth, PGD is seeking a General Manager to serve as a key strategic and operational partner to the President. This is a unique opportunity for a business leader who thrives in a fast-moving entrepreneurial environment and wants to play a critical role in shaping the future of a growing real estate organization.

## The Role

Reporting directly to the President, the General Manager will be the senior operational leader of the business and the highest-ranking position within the organization outside of the President. The successful candidate will provide leadership across property management, administration, financial oversight, organizational development, and operational excellence while supporting the continued growth of the company's real estate portfolio.

The General Manager will bring structure, accountability, and forward-thinking leadership to the organization while ensuring the right people, systems, and processes are in place to support the next phase of growth. Acting as a trusted advisor and extension of the President, the General Manager will lead day-to-day business operations, oversee key managers and external partners, and drive initiatives that improve efficiency, profitability, and scalability across the company.

## Key Responsibilities

## Leadership & Organizational Development

• Provide overall leadership and day-to-day operational management of the business.

• Lead, coach, mentor, and develop managers and staff across multiple functional areas.

• Establish performance expectations, accountability measures, and operational priorities.

• Evaluate organizational structure and recommend improvements to support future growth.

• Partner with the President on succession planning, workforce planning, and talent development.

• Foster a culture of responsiveness, professionalism, accountability, and continuous improvement.

## Property Management Oversight

• Provide leadership and oversight to the Property Management function, including lease-up activities, tenant experience, operational performance, and portfolio growth.

• Work closely with the Director of Property Management to establish goals, improve processes, and ensure timely execution of priorities.

• Monitor occupancy, leasing performance, rental strategies, and operational metrics.

• Support the implementation of scalable processes to accommodate significant portfolio growth over the coming years.

• Ensure property operations continue to reflect the company's reputation for quality and service excellence.

• Leverage operational insights, tenant feedback, leasing trends, and portfolio performance data to inform future development decisions and ensure lessons learned from existing communities are incorporated into new projects.

## Financial & Business Management

• Oversee financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, cash flow management, and operational performance measurement.

• Work closely with the company's bookkeeping and external accounting partners to ensure accurate and timely reporting.

• Review financial analyses, lender requests, and business performance metrics to support informed decision-making.

• Assist in the preparation of financing materials and reporting requirements for financial institutions.

• Monitor operating results across the portfolio and identify opportunities to improve profitability and efficiency.

• Translate financial information into actionable business recommendations for the President.

## Operational Excellence

• Develop and implement systems, policies, and operating procedures that support a growing organization.

• Lead initiatives to improve document management, information accessibility, reporting processes, and workflow effectiveness.

• Identify operational bottlenecks and implement solutions that improve responsiveness and execution.

• Coordinate internal resources and third-party partners to ensure business objectives are achieved efficiently and effectively.

• Take ownership of special projects and organizational initiatives as required.

## Strategic Partnership

• Act as a trusted business partner to the President by providing sound judgment, recommendations, and decision support.

• Participate in strategic planning and help translate organizational objectives into actionable plans.

• Support investor, lender, municipal, and professional stakeholder relationships as required.

• Contribute to future development initiatives by providing operational, financial, and organizational insight.

• Act as a critical liaison between Operations and Development, ensuring information, market intelligence, tenant insights, and operational performance data are utilized to enhance future development planning and investment decisions.

• Create the leadership capacity necessary for the President to focus on development opportunities, strategic growth, and long-term value creation.

## The Ideal Candidate

As the ideal candidate, you are an experienced operational leader who combines strong business acumen with a practical, hands-on approach. You are comfortable navigating complexity, managing competing priorities, and leading growing teams within entrepreneurial environments. You bring a sense of urgency, strong financial understanding, and the ability to anticipate issues before they arise. Your qualifications include:

• Bachelor's degree in business administration, Commerce, Finance, Accounting, Real Estate, or a related discipline.

• Progressive leadership experience within property management, real estate development, construction, professional services, or a comparable entrepreneurial business environment.

• Demonstrated experience leading teams and managing managers.

• Strong financial literacy with experience interpreting financial statements, budgets, forecasts, and business performance metrics.

• Proven ability to establish systems, processes, and organizational structure to support growth.

• Experience working with external stakeholders, including lenders, professional advisors, and service providers.

• Exceptional organizational, communication, and relationship-building skills.

• Sound judgment, strong problem-solving abilities, and a proactive leadership style.

• A collaborative approach balanced with the confidence to make decisions and drive accountability.

• Experience within real estate development, property management, or construction-related industries will be considered a strong asset.

## Why Join Parsons Green Developments?

This is an opportunity to join a respected and growing Nova Scotia organization at an exciting point in its evolution. The General Manager will have the opportunity to influence strategy, shape organizational growth, mentor talented employees, and contribute directly to the expansion of one of the province's most active residential development companies. As PGD continues to scale its portfolio and operations, this role offers significant opportunity for long-term growth and increased leadership responsibility.

## To express interest in this opportunity please apply online directly here.

If you have any questions, please contact Kate Spares, Recruitment Specialist, at kspares@kbrs.ca or Jeff Lanthier, Partner, at jlanthier@kbrs.ca. If you require accommodation to participate in the recruitment process, please let us know.

2239833.description:
Job Title: Department Supervisor, Quality Assurance
Location: Dartmouth, Nova Scotia
TP - xxx - 10111

Atlantic Hardchrome is a specialized manufacturing and repair company based in Dartmouth, Nova Scotia, providing hard chrome plating, CNC machining and manufacturing, conventional machining and grinding, equipment servicing, assembly, testing, and component restoration services. Since 1971, the company has built a reputation for quality, technical expertise, and delivering cost-effective solutions that help customers repair, rebuild, and restore critical equipment and components.

Serving customers across Canada, the United States, Europe, and beyond, Atlantic Hardchrome is supported by certifications including AS9100D/ISO 9001:2015, Controlled Goods, CWB, and Joint Certification Program (JCP).

Meridia Recruitment Solutions is excited to be partnered with Atlantic Hardchrome to recruit a Department Supervisor, Quality Assurance to join their team located in Dartmouth, Nova Scotia.

Role Description:
Reporting to the Vice President of Operations, the Department Supervisor, Quality Assurance is responsible for leading Atlantic Hardchrome's quality assurance function and overseeing a team of Quality Inspectors. This role provides leadership across quality assurance activities, special project oversight, customer communication, auditing, compliance, and technical support.
In this role, you will support the organization's quality management systems through audit activities, root cause investigations, compliance oversight, and ongoing interaction with customers and internal teams.

## Your responsibilities will include:

• Overseeing the team responsible for final QA inspection of manufactured and repaired parts.

• Managing the scheduling and daily activities of the Quality Inspectors.

• Reviewing daily non-conformance reports (NCRs) and determining appropriate follow-up actions.

• Conducting root cause investigations for significant quality issues and documenting findings.

• Monitoring NCR data to identify trends and support efforts to reduce recurring issues.

• Planning, scheduling, and monitoring special projects.

• Scheduling progress meetings with management and customers to ensure continued communication and customer support.

• Planning and completing internal and external audits.

• Overseeing company compliance with ISO 9001, AS9100, CWB, Controlled Goods, and Environmental requirements.

• Monitoring QA documentation to ensure compliance with applicable customer standards, industry codes and practices, and company quality systems.

• Operating inspection equipment, including CMMs, profilometers, micrometers, and other measuring devices.

• Providing technical support to operations with a focus on chemistry for plating.

• Developing standard operating procedures to standardize and control internal and external processes.

• Continually interacting with customers to interpret their needs and requirements.

• Performing other duties as assigned by the Vice President of Operations.

Your Qualifications
As the ideal candidate, you bring quality assurance leadership experience within a manufacturing or industrial environment and a strong technical foundation. You are comfortable leading investigations, supporting audits, overseeing quality processes, and working directly with customers and internal stakeholders.

## Key qualifications include:

• Degree, diploma, or educational background in Engineering, Chemistry, or a related technical discipline is preferred.

• 5+ years of QA supervisory experience in a machining, manufacturing, or related industrial environment.

• Lead Auditor training is preferred.

• Experience planning and completing internal and external audits.

• Experience overseeing quality assurance activities within a manufacturing environment.

• Experience conducting root cause investigations and managing non-conformance reports (NCRs).

• Experience supervising quality personnel.

• Strong communication and organizational skills.

## Assets include:

• Experience supporting plating operations or chemistry-related manufacturing processes.

• Experience with ISO 9001 quality management systems.

• Experience with AS9100 quality management systems is an asset.

• Experience operating CMMs, profilometers, micrometers, and other inspection equipment.

• Experience within machining, manufacturing, marine, defense, metal finishing, or electronics manufacturing environments.

## Why Join Atlantic Hardchrome?

• Competitive salary based on experience.

• Extended health and dental benefits.

• RRSP matching program of up to 4%.

• Paid vacation entitlement that increases with service.

MUNN Insurance has been protecting Atlantic Canadians for more than 100 years and is one of the region's leading independent insurance brokerages. With offices across Newfoundland and Labrador and Nova Scotia, MUNN is committed to delivering exceptional insurance solutions and personalized service to individuals, families, and businesses.

Built on a foundation of trust, expertise, and client advocacy, MUNN partners with leading insurance providers to deliver competitive coverage and peace of mind. MUNN's culture is rooted in collaboration, innovation, accountability, and a commitment to providing exceptional experiences for both clients and employees.

Reporting to the Commercial Sales leadership team, the Commercial Digital Sales Advisor is responsible for converting inbound, referral, and digitally generated opportunities into long-term commercial insurance clients while managing and growing an assigned portfolio.

This role combines consultative selling, insurance expertise, and relationship management to help businesses make informed insurance decisions. As the primary advisor throughout the client lifecycle, you will manage opportunities from initial consultation through binding and renewal, while developing long-term client relationships that contribute to portfolio growth and retention.

This opportunity is ideal for an insurance professional who enjoys building relationships, providing trusted advice, and taking ownership of both business development and client success.

Digital Sales & New Business Development

• Respond to inbound, referral, and digitally generated commercial insurance opportunities.

• Conduct discovery conversations to understand client operations, risks, and insurance needs.

• Develop insurance strategies and recommend coverage solutions tailored to each client's business.

• Prepare and present proposals through telephone, video conferencing, email, and other digital channels.

Client Relationship Management & Retention

• Develop a comprehensive understanding of clients' businesses and changing insurance requirements.

• Conduct regular account reviews and proactive client outreach activities.

Portfolio Growth & Insurance Advisory

Administration & Collaboration

• Strong understanding of commercial insurance products, coverages, and risk exposures.

Title: Senior Data Specialist

Employee Working Location: Partially Virtual / Hybrid (Canada)

Employment Status: Permanent Full-time

The Canadian Red Cross (Red Cross) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

The Senior Data Specialist reporting the Lead, Data and Analytics, in Humanitarian Services, designs and maintains scalable data systems and standards that enable high-quality analytics and informed decision-making. This role supports organizational priorities by developing sustainable data structures, promoting data governance, and translating complex data into actionable insights. Through collaboration, mentorship, and continuous improvement, the Senior Data Specialist strengthens data capabilities and fosters a culture of responsible data use.

## In this role, you will:

• Collaborate with leaders to understand priorities and identify opportunities where data management and analytics can support long-term improvements in services and knowledge sharing.

• Lead the design and implementation of sustainable data solutions, including data models, pipelines, and repositories that support scalable analytics and reporting in partnership with Technology Group.

• Conduct in-depth analyses to uncover trends and insights that inform strategic planning and operational improvements.

• Develop and maintain data management frameworks and standards to ensure consistency, quality, and reusability across systems and teams.

• Translate complex data findings into clear narratives and visualizations that support evidence-based decision-making.

• Partner with cross-functional teams to align data capabilities with organizational goals and long-term planning.

• Contribute to the implementation of data governance practices, promoting data quality, integrity, and responsible use.

• Recommend and implement improvements to data tools, processes, and methodologies that enhance long-term data utility.

• Mentor colleagues in data stewardship, governance, and the application of data standards to promote sustainable data practices.

• Participate in internal data forums and contribute to the implementation of organizational data strategies and standards.

• Stay informed on developments in data analytics, tools, and relevant policies to ensure best practices are applied.

• Ensure data security and integrity in all analytics activities and assist in identifying and mitigating data-related risks.

## What we are looking for :

• Qualifications include a minimum of 6-9 years experience and a 3-year college diploma or university degree in Data Science, Information Management, Computer Science, Statistics or a related field and/or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Expertise in data management and analytics, along with an understanding of how data supports operational and strategic decision making

• Strong understanding of data architecture, data modeling, and metadata management.

• Proficiency in data analytics, statistical methods, and data visualization tools and software (e.g., Power BI, Tableau, R, Python, SQL).

• Knowledge of cloud-based platforms (e.g., Azure, AWS, GCP).

• Experience using Python or R for data manipulation, automation, and statistical analysis.

• Ability to create compelling data narratives and visualizations that support decision-making.

• Ability to document and maintain data standards and technical specifications.

• Familiarity with data governance principles, data quality standards, and privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA).

• Experience with and understanding of best practices around data management concepts, including data quality, data cleansing, standardization, metadata management, privacy, and security governance

• Ability to identify complex problems, analyze interrelated factors, assess and mitigate risks, and develop solutions using specialized skills.

• Communication and influence skills to gather perspectives, understand needs, and present information to reach consensus, often in somewhat sensitive situations.

• Ability to guide and coordinate the work of others to ensure work is completed to meet business needs and in compliance with applicable data and privacy policy and legislation

• Ability to demonstrate a high level of discretion and integrity to handle sensitive workforce and organizational information.
* Lived and/or professional experience with First Nations, Inuit and/or Métis Nations or communities is an asset.

## Working Conditions :

• Requires significant attention to detail and concentration and ability to mentally process large amounts of information.

• The work pace is often unpredictable with significant time pressures.

• Ability to adapt to frequent and often urgent changes in priorities, and make decisions under pressure, work at an
unpredictable pace.

• Work will be conducted in an office-like setting.

• May require travel to safe locations; limited exposure to adverse conditions.

• Work requires the ability to work to deadlines.

• Work requires interactions with dissatisfied clients and the resolution of complex client issues.

• In a large-scale emergency, where staff numbers are compromised or additional resources are required provide disaster relief and/or emergency field operational support.

Permanent

As a national health solutions partner, we put people first in everything we do - and that begins with our team of 8,000+ professionals who bring a cross-section of diverse life experiences and career expertise to Medavie. By collaborating and innovating together, our employees are creating industry-leading solutions in insurance, primary care and emergency medical services that impact millions of lives in Canada each year.

Our mission is to improve the wellbeing of Canadians so that every life can be lived to the fullest - and it's reflected in our award-winning culture.
