Medavie is seeking an enterprise-minded leader to shape and advance our Data, Analytics and Artificial Intelligence (DAA) agenda. Reporting to the EVP of the Enterprise Transformation Office, you will set strategic direction, establish the governance model for enterprise DAA decisions, and help ensure investments translate into measurable business outcomes.

In this leadership role, you will work across Business Lines, Technology, Risk, Privacy, Legal and executive leadership to create a consistent approach for identifying, prioritizing, governing and measuring DAA opportunities. You will bring clarity to decision rights, forums, escalation pathways, prioritization criteria and strategic guardrails, while building alignment around a practical, scalable and responsible enterprise direction.

Success in this role requires strategic thinking, sound judgment and the ability to influence across a complex organization. You will connect enterprise ambition to execution, strengthen value-based decision-making and foster a culture of responsible innovation, transparency and accountability.

## What You Will Do

• Define, maintain and execute Medavie's enterprise DAA strategy and multi-year roadmap in collaboration with IT, translating strategic objectives into clear priorities, target outcomes, capability requirements and sequencing considerations.

• Assess emerging technologies, vendor developments, regulatory changes and external practices, and translate them into strategic opportunities or roadmap implications.

• Establish strategic guardrails to assess DAA opportunities based on enterprise alignment, business value and organizational readiness.

• Align the DAA portfolio and foundational investments to enterprise ambition, partnering with portfolio intake and key stakeholders to prioritize initiatives.

• Establish and maintain the enterprise DAA program governance operating model, including decision rights, governance forums, executive decision-making cadences and escalation pathways.

• Facilitate enterprise governance forums that review DAA priorities, investment choices, strategic risks, dependencies and trade-offs.

• Embed applicable data and AI requirements into governance processes so initiatives are assessed consistently before investment and prioritization decisions are made.

• Define governance reporting that provides decision-makers with visibility into strategic alignment, portfolio direction, material risks, key dependencies and value realization.

• Build strong relationships with executives, business leaders, IT teams and support functions to drive alignment around DAA strategy and governance expectations.

• Act as a trusted advisor and enterprise subject matter expert on DAA strategy, governance model design, value realization and operating model practices.

• Drive adoption of governance, portfolio management disciplines and value-based decision-making across the organization.

• Establish meaningful metrics and key performance indicators to monitor strategy execution, portfolio alignment and governance effectiveness, using insights to continuously improve enterprise practices.

## What You Need to Succeed

Education: Bachelor's degree in Information Management, Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Administration or a related field. An equivalent combination of education and relevant experience will also be considered.

## Qualifications

• 10+ years of experience in strategy, enterprise transformation or a related field.

• Experience establishing operating models, governance models and strategic planning cadences within data, analytics, AI or technology environments.

• Demonstrated experience leading enterprise-wide strategic initiatives across multiple business functions.

• Demonstrated ability to work effectively with executive and board-level stakeholders, influence decisions and build alignment across senior leadership.

• Strong strategic thinking and synthesis skills, with the ability to translate complex concepts into clear, actionable insights and executive-ready communications.

• Experience developing and implementing enterprise AI and data literacy programs or capability-building strategies that increase adoption of data-driven and AI-enabled practices.

• Strong understanding of AI literacy requirements, responsible AI principles and approaches for building organizational awareness and competency across diverse stakeholder groups.

• Deep understanding of DAA program governance principles, operating model design and leading practices within data, analytics and AI environments.

• Ability to lead through influence and build alignment across functions.

• Strong knowledge of data privacy regulations and AI governance and model risk considerations.

• Comfort working in a fast-paced environment with evolving priorities, competing demands and a high degree of ambiguity.

Language Requirement: Bilingualism (EN/FR) is considered an asset. English is requirement, written and verbal, to provide services to our customers and communicate with internal stakeholders

Security Clearance Requirement: This position requires Reliability Status Clearance (Enhanced Level B), including fingerprinting, a criminal record check and a credit check. Candidates must have resided in Canada for at least five years and hold Canadian citizenship or permanent resident status.

2241001.description:
## Office Operations Manager
Halifax, NS
HL-NSSA-10176

The Nova Scotia Association of Architects (NSAA) is the self-governing professional association that is responsible for licensing and regulating the practice of architecture in Nova Scotia. Established in 1932 and mandated under The Architects Act, the NSAA protects the public interest through the regulation of architects and architectural firms across the province. The Association oversees licensure, professional standards, continuing professional development requirements, and regulatory compliance to protect the public and advance the professional practice of architecture.

We are pleased to be partnered with them to bring an Office Operations Manager to their team in Halifax, NS. Reporting to the Executive Director, the Office Operations Manager is responsible for the seamless administration and operation of the organization. This position provides executive support to the Executive Director while overseeing administrative systems, volunteer and committee support, member service administration, communications, records management, and special events.

The successful candidate will be a key operational resource, ensuring organizational effectiveness through strong planning, process improvement, support for partners and third-party collaborators of the organization, and demonstrating strong attention to detail. Working in a fast-paced environment, this role requires exceptional judgment, discretion, initiative, and the ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining a high standard of professionalism and confidentiality.

## Responsibilities in this role will include:

## Executive and Organizational Support

• Provide executive support to the Executive Director, including managing schedules, priorities, meetings, correspondence, and confidential matters.

• Coordinate administrative activities to ensure smooth day-to-day operations including responding to inquiries, triaging communications, replenishing all office supplies.

• Identify opportunities to improve office systems, processes, and administrative procedures to increase efficiency and service delivery.

• Prepare reports, briefing materials, presentations, and correspondence.

• Maintain organizational calendars and coordinate meeting schedules and quorum requirements.

## Committee Administration

• Coordinate all aspects of committee meetings, including scheduling, agendas, meeting materials, and follow-up activities.

• Prepare, distribute, and maintain meeting packages and supporting documentation.

• Compile and distribute meeting minutes and action items.

• Maintain online archives and records.

• Coordinate all meeting logistics, including venue setup, catering, virtual meeting platforms, and related arrangements.

## Financial Administration

• Coordinate monthly financial documentation.

• Distribute financial packages to external bookkeeper for reporting purposes.

• Manage cheque issuances.

• Maintain organized financial records and supporting documentation.

## Membership and Program Administration

• Maintain and update member records within the organization's database.

• Complete data entry, reporting, and member information management.

• Support annual reporting and membership renewal processes.

• Administer continuing education records, certifications, and compliance tracking.

• Coordinate logistics associated with educational courses and professional development.

## Communications and Engagement

• Develop, edit, and distribute member communications, newsletters, reports, and organizational announcements.

• Maintain website content, including member updates, events, resources, and organizational information.

• Support social media activities and communication initiatives.

• Preparing and distributing bi-monthly bulletin.

## Special Events

• Lead the planning and execution of organizational events, including Annual General Meetings (AGM) and Holiday Social.

• Liaise with venues, suppliers, speakers, and interested parties to ensure successful event delivery.

• Manage event logistics, registrations, materials, communications, and on-site coordination.

• Organize and preparing the First-Licensure recognition component of the AGM including the preparation certificates and candidate backgrounds.

## Records Management and Compliance

• Develop, implement, and maintain records management policies and procedures.

• Ensure accurate and secure management of member and corporate records.

• In consultation with the team develop, implement and maintain an NSAA membership archive, and maintain a records management policy for member files and corporate permit files (paper files).

• Promote best practices in information management and document control.

## The ideal candidate will posses:

• Post-secondary education plus a minimum of five years of relevant administrative experience (or equivalent combination of education and experience).

• Experience in progressively senior administrative, operations, or executive support positions.

• Exceptional organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.

• Demonstrated understanding of administrative controls, records management, policy compliance, and confidentiality requirements.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite including PowerPoint, Adobe In-Design Suite. Experience with MailChimp and WordPress is an asset.

• Exceptional organizational, analytical, and communications skills with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities within a confidential environment.

• Demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgment, think critically, and respond appropriately in complex situations.

• Thrives in a small team environment.

• Experience in special events/meeting coordination, records management, policy and compliance activities.

• Ability to communicate step-by-step processes with ease.

• Outstanding client service skills.

2238718.title: Cloud Accountant
2238718.description:
Cloud Accountant
Tidal CFO Services Inc. - Remote (Atlantic Canada preferred)
$50,000 - $60,000 annually, plus health benefits

About Tidal CFO
Tidal CFO is a remote-first, CPA-led fractional finance firm based in Atlantic Canada. We work with Canadian businesses - startups, nonprofits, and growing SMEs - to bring clarity, structure, and confidence to their finances.

We're not a traditional accounting firm. No timesheets, no billable-hour culture, no scramble to hit utilization targets. We run on a retainer model, which means you're measured by the quality and reliability of the books you produce - not the hours you clock. And here, bookkeeping isn't the bottom of the pile. Clean, accurate books are the foundation everything else is built on - our entire advisory and CFO practice is only as good as the numbers underneath it. We take that work seriously, and we're looking for someone who does too.

The Role
We're hiring a Cloud Accountant to take on a portfolio of client books in a modern, cloud-based environment - coding, reconciling, and closing each month to a standard you'd be proud to put your name on.

This is the seat for someone who has the fundamentals down and is ready to own real client files. You've done full-cycle bookkeeping before. You know your way around QuickBooks Online or Xero, and you're ready to get fast in both. You can work a file end to end, and you know when a question is above your line.

You won't be doing it alone. Your work is reviewed by a Senior Cloud Accountant, and you have a Manager and a CPA-led team behind you for the complex calls. But the day-to-day file is yours to run - and as you build depth, so does the complexity of the portfolio you carry.

Because we're remote-first, you'll need to work independently, communicate proactively, and engage directly with clients - including picking up the phone when that's the fastest way to get an answer and keep work moving.

## What You'll Do

• Own the books
• Take ownership of full-cycle bookkeeping for your assigned clients in QBO or Xero

• Code transactions with judgment - prepaids, fixed assets, owner items, and non-business expenses handled correctly and consistently, with a Senior reviewing before delivery

• Keep workflows current so nothing sits idle without explanation, and flag anything that doesn't look right

• Reconcile with rigour
• Complete monthly bank and credit card reconciliations with minimal unexplained items at month-end

• Investigate discrepancies using logic, history, and independent research before escalating- and bring the steps you've already tried when you do

• Make the most of the tools
• Use Dext to manage receipts and source documents, keeping inboxes clear and organized

• Build and maintain supplier and bank rules to cut repetitive work - applying automation thoughtfully, with healthy professional skepticism

• Get the month closed
• Ensure reconciliations and supporting schedules are complete, documented, and audit-ready ahead of review

• Run a first-pass review of the P&L and Balance Sheet to catch obvious errors and anomalies before the file reaches your Senior

• Keep work moving and clients informed
• Manage your tasks in our practice management system and keep statuses current - stale statuses aren't a thing here

• Communicate directly with clients to request information, clarify transactions, and resolve open items - by phone or email, whatever gets it done

## What We're Looking For

• 2+ years of full-cycle bookkeeping. Firm-side cloud experience is ideal, but strong in-house experience across multiple entities counts too.

• Hands-on experience with QuickBooks Online or Xero - and the appetite to get fully fluent in both. We'll invest in getting you there.

• Dext experience managing receipts and document workflows, or comparable document-capture tooling.

• Someone who likes the craft of clean books - you find satisfaction in a tidy reconciliation, not just in getting it off your plate.

• A remote self-starter who manages multiple clients and priorities and asks good questions early rather than late.

• A confident communicator who's comfortable engaging clients directly and picking up the phone when needed.

• Bilingual (English / French) is a strong asset - not required.

• Comfortable in a fast-paced environment with at times conflicting priorities.

## What This Isn't

• This isn't a data-entry seat. You own the file and exercise judgment - we're not handing you a coding sheet to follow.

• It's also not a CFO or advisory role. You'll see how clean books feed the advisory work we do, and there's a defined path toward it - but this seat is about learning to do the bookkeeping exceptionally well.

• And it isn't unsupported. You'll work inside a structured system with documented processes, modern tools, review layers built into the workflow, and a team to escalate to when a call is above your line.

Where This Goes
We promote from this seat. Our Senior Cloud Accountants own larger, more complex portfolios and review the work of others - and that's the natural next step here for someone who earns it. We'll be clear with you from day one about what "ready" looks like, and we'll review it with you rather than leaving you to guess.

## What We Offer

• Base salary of $52,000 - $62,000, depending on experience

• Comprehensive health and dental benefits

• Fully remote - work from wherever you do your best work

• 3 weeks paid time off

• A modern, best-in-class cloud stack and documented processes - no chasing down information

• A small, high-trust team where your work is visible and genuinely valued

• Room to grow as the firm scales

2239992.title: Trainer, Process Operations
2239992.description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is transforming the future?

## Who We Are

We are Vale Base Metals – a global supplier of the critical minerals transforming the future.

With industry-leading reserves of copper and nickel in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia, and state-of-the-art infrastructure in the U.K., Canada, and Japan, VBM delivers a secure and responsible supply of high-quality products to customers across Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

Global demand for critical minerals is growing exponentially. From energy to aerospace, batteries to magnets, robotics to artificial intelligence, a secure and responsible supply of critical minerals is fundamental to power modern technologies. And at Vale Base Metals, we are transforming our business to provide a secure and responsible supply of these minerals.

Join our diverse team of 13,000 talented individuals committed to providing mineral security to a world in transition. We invite you to put your skills to work, driving meaningful and enduring change while enjoying a rewarding career.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking a Process Operations Trainer to join our People & Community Department in Long Harbour, NL.

This permanent position will be on a 4x10s schedule (Monday to Thursday OR Tuesday to Friday) working at the Long Harbour Operations site in Long Harbour, NL.

The Process Operations Trainer must ensure that Process Operations employees receive the knowledge and practical training required to become safe and productive processing plant technicians and/or other hydrometallurgical refining-related roles. Additionally, the Process Operations Trainer is responsible for training Process Maintenance employees in the safe operation of any Process Operations mobile or fixed equipment they are required to operate.

The Process Operations Trainer must ensure all training complies with legislative requirements (i.e., OH&S Regulations, WHMIS Act, Radiation Act, etc.) and conforms to company policies (i.e., Safe Production, HSER, etc.). To build and maintain a safe, cost-effective, and productive operation, the Process Operations Trainer must establish and maintain communication with all operational stakeholders (workers, supervisors, department heads, etc.) to ensure identified training needs are addressed in a timely manner and that risks associated with the business are reduced to "as low as reasonably achievable".

Additionally, in this position, you will:

• Identify training needs for Process Operations employees and, where applicable, other employees at the Long Harbour Operation (LHO).

• Prepare prior learning assessments and lesson plans for employees.

• Contribute to the research and development of training materials, ensuring content is relevant and supports both the course objectives and overall training program.
Schedule and deliver safe and effective training in a timely manner.

• Train, mentor, and coach employees in the safe, effective, and productive operation of support mobile equipment and hydrometallurgical refining processes; required safety systems and programs; hazard identification; risk assessment; and reducing risk to "as low as reasonably achievable."

• Evaluate employee performance and communicate findings to both the Process Operations Department and the employee.

• Ensure all training complies with legislative requirements and company policies.
In collaboration with frontline leadership, develop and monitor individual employee training plans to ensure conformance.

• Maintain employee training records, both electronic and hard copy.

• Participate in committee and team meetings related to the development and enhancement of employee skills.

## What We Offer You

• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Flexible work arrangements

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare online

• Online training and career development opportunities

• A Bus Service departing from the St. John's vicinity.

## About You

## Education:

• A minimum of Grade 12 education is required.

• Post-secondary education in adult education or a relevant field is preferred.

• Adult Education training, WorkplaceNL Certified Trainer, Train the Trainer program(s), or Heavy Equipment Operation Certification all considered an asset.

## Experience:

• A minimum of 5 years' experience is required.

• Previous experience with Process Operation preferred.

• Considered an asset:
• Training in the classroom and/or hands on training.

• Experience mentoring others.

• Instructional design experience.

• Zero-Energy/LOTO/P2W experience.

## Skills:

• Strong obsession with safety and risk management

• Strong presentation, oral and written communication skills.

• Good interpersonal, time management and organizational skills.

• Sense of ownership and ability to work with minimal supervision.

• Ability to solve problems and think proactively and engage with others.

• Strong computer skills, and proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite.

• Demonstrates leadership and commitment towards diversity, equity, and inclusion.

## Why Newfoundland and Labrador

Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada's easternmost province, is known for its rugged coastline, rich cultural heritage, and significant natural resources. The province's economy is bolstered by a robust mining sector, where Vale Base Metals' integrated operations play a crucial role.

At Long Harbour, we operate a state-of-the-art processing plant, which refines nickel concentrate from Vale Base Metals' Voisey's Bay mine, located in Labrador, into nickel, copper, and cobalt products. This plant is a cornerstone of our commitment to value-added processing in Canada. Meanwhile, the Voisey's Bay mine is one of the world's most substantial nickel deposits. It provides high-quality nickel, copper, and cobalt, essential for the 21st century economy.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people can act like owners, being their authentic selves and empowering them to deliver results. Vale Base Metals encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

Accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Employees engaged by the Company must be lawfully able to work for the Company in the country where the role is located. The Company does not provide immigration, work permit, or permanent residence sponsorship or assistance.

## Pay Grade: G01

## Apply by: Sunday, September 27th, 2026

## #ValeBaseMetals

2234960.title: Senior Risk & Compliance Advisor
2234960.employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
2234960.description:

Department: Finance and Treasury Board

Location: HALIFAX

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: Exclusion - Non Union - NSPG

About Us
At the Nova Scotia Department of Finance and Treasury Board, we strive to provide financial leadership, analysis, and policies that strengthen Nova Scotia. As stewards of the province's financial affairs, we deliver a wide range of corporate fiscal and management services.
Our eight Financial Advisory Services (FAS) units work directly with departments, crown corporations, and other public service entities, providing valuable support in budgeting, forecasting, and offering a range of program-related financial advice. We are continuously seeking new and innovative ways to improve how we plan, manage,budget, and invest.

About Our Opportunity
Reporting to the Director, Financial Advisory Services, the Senior Risk & Compliance Advisor provides expert advice and leadership in financial compliance, internal controls, and risk management for federally funded programs and departmental operations.

The role focuses on establishing and maintaining financial compliance frameworks and internal control standards, including internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR), and ensuring alignment with government policies, legislation, and funding agreements. The Advisor plays a key role in strengthening financial oversight, internal control consistency, and accountability across program areas.

The Advisor is focused on shaping how compliance, risk, and internal control practices are designed, implemented, and sustained across a complex operational environment. This includes leading the development of risk-based monitoring approaches and ensuring financial and compliance risks are identified and managed effectively.

Working closely with program leadership, the Advisor applies a risk-based, proportionate approach to compliance and oversight in a high-volume environment. The role emphasizes influencing decision-making and building capability within program areas, while implementing practical and sustainable approaches that support both accountability and effective service delivery.

Primary Accountabilities
• Establish and maintain financial compliance and internal control standards, providing expert advice on their application across program areas.

• Lead the development, implementation, and ongoing assessment of internal control frameworks (ICFR), including documentation and evaluation of control effectiveness.

• Design and operate a risk-based financial compliance and internal control monitoring program, including risk assessment approaches and prioritization of review and monitoring activities based on risk and materiality.

• Provide risk and compliance oversight of funding agreements, including advising on reporting requirements, eligibility criteria, audit provisions, and enforcement mechanisms.

• Identify and assess financial and compliance risks and control deficiencies and provide evidence-based recommendations and mitigation strategies.

• Implement compliance standards and supporting tools and guidance to promote consistent financial practices and strengthen accountability.

• Support the development of financial capability within program areas through guidance, training, and ongoing advisory support.

• Support audit readiness and act as a key liaison with internal and external auditors.

• Influence program decision-making through clear, structured advice and strong working relationships that support improved compliance and accountability.

Qualifications and Experience
This role is an opportunity for a Canadian Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) with a minimum of five years progressive experience in financial compliance, internal controls, or risk management within complex environments, including advising senior leadership and addressing system-level financial risks. The ideal candidate brings:

• Strong knowledge of internal control frameworks (e.g., ICFR, COSO), government financial policies, and funding agreements.

• Demonstrated experience leading or advising on financial compliance, internal control, or risk management practices in complex, high-volume environments.

• Demonstrated experience designing and evaluating internal control frameworks, including assessing control effectiveness and supporting remediation of deficiencies.

• Experience developing or applying risk-based approaches to monitoring or oversight, including prioritizing work based on risk and materiality.

• Experience reviewing or advising on funding agreements or contracts, including assessing compliance risks related to reporting, eligibility, and enforcement.

• Strong analytical, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills.

• Demonstrated ability to advise and influence senior leaders and non-financial audiences.

• Experience building or improving structures, including processes or documentation, in evolving or developing environments.

• Experience supporting financial capability development within program or operational teams.

Equivalency
Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
Work is performed in an office environment with competing priorities and deadlines. The role operates in a fast-paced setting with a strong focus on program delivery, requiring sound judgment to balance compliance requirements with operational needs.

What We Offer
• Career development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career

• Engaging workplace: our employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in, we have forward-thinking policies and strategies

• Countless career paths

• A Dynamic, client-focused office environment where service excellence and teamwork are our focus.

Pay Grade: EC 12

Salary Range: $3,929.22 - $4,911.52 Bi-Weekly

Employment Equity Statement: Our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative, at all job levels, of the citizens we serve. About Us

At CBCL our purpose is to create a positive and lasting impact on people and our planet. As an employee-owned firm, at CBCL, our people are everything. We are committed to promoting inclusivity and diversity for a workplace where everyone can thrive, and we build long-term relationships with our clients while providing them with innovative solutions.

We have earned recognition as one of Canada's Top 100 Employers and one of Canada's Best Managed Companies. Our multitalented group of professionals offer consulting in the Infrastructure, Water and Wastewater, Buildings, Industrial, and Earth and Environment sectors. We value our people, our communities, and our history and look forward to continuing our steady growth.

Along with our commitment to reducing our carbon footprint corporately, CBCL develops and implements sustainable engineering solutions that respect the current social and environmental impacts, as well as future implications of our designs.

CBCL operates from its offices in Halifax and Sydney, NS; Charlottetown, PE; Saint John, Fredericton and Moncton, NB; St. John's, NL, and Ottawa, ON.

2241232.title: Innu Employment Coordinator
2241232.description:
Who We Are
We are Vale Base Metals – a global supplier of the critical minerals transforming the future.

With industry-leading reserves of copper and nickel in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia, and state-of-the-art infrastructure in the U.K., Canada, and Japan, VBM delivers a secure and responsible supply of high-quality products to customers across Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

Global demand for critical minerals is growing exponentially. From energy to aerospace, batteries to magnets, robotics to artificial intelligence, a secure and responsible supply of critical minerals is fundamental to power modern technologies. And at Vale Base Metals, we are transforming our business to provide a secure and responsible supply of these minerals.

Join our diverse team of 13,000 talented individuals committed to providing mineral security to a world in transition. We invite you to put your skills to work, driving meaningful and enduring change while enjoying a rewarding career.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking an Innu Employment Coordinator to join our People and Community team in Voisey's Bay, Labrador, a fly-in fly-out operation.

This is a permanent position, working a Monday to Friday schedule with regular travel to the Voisey's Bay Mine Site and Innu communities within Labrador.

As an Innu Employment Coordinator, you will play an integral part in supporting the hiring and training preferences for Innu Nation Members. The primary objective of the role is to ensure that qualified Indigenous candidates are given first consideration for all employment and training opportunities at the Voisey's Bay Mine Site as it relates to the Impacts and Benefits Agreement (IBA) with Innu Nation.

Additionally, in this position you will:

• Assist with recruitment efforts to hire Innu Nation members for job openings and training opportunities at the Voisey's Bay Mine Site.

• Assist the Talent Acquisition team and site Contractors in identifying qualified Indigenous employees.

• Attend all Innu candidate's interviews to ensure comfort, accuracy and consistency in the recruitment and selection process; and provide translation in Innu Amun to candidates where necessary.

• Assist in coordinating and facilitating events onsite in Voisey's Bay and Innu communities.

• Network with Innu Nation in the Innu communities to source interested candidates.

• Identify barriers for Innu employees and use that information to maintain and improve the Innu Employee retention rate.

• Travel to Innu communities to visit schools, hold public meetings regarding work, environmental issues, winter shipping, and any other topics the community would like to discuss regarding the Voisey's Bay Mine Site.

## What We Offer You

• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, flex health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare online

• Online training and career development opportunities

• Chartered flights within Newfoundland & Labrador

• 24/7 access to a fully stocked cafeteria with balanced meals prepared by our culinary team

• Access to recreational facilities and social activities (cardio/weight room, gymnasium, music room, movie theatre, etc.)

• Accommodations are equipped with cable TV, internet, and unlimited long-distance calling

• All Personal Protective Equipment is provided upon hire. Employees are given a safety boot allowance and receive a 100% reimbursement for prescription safety glasses

## About You

## Must be an Innu Nation member.

## Education:

• University related to community studies, business management, or a related field of study.

## Experience:

• 3 years' experience in a related position, preferably within community studies.

• Experience working in an industrial workplace is considered an asset.

• Previous experience in a fly in/fly out environment is considered an asset.

## Skills:

• Must have a good working relationship with the Innu community.

• Must be fluent in English.

• High degree of sensitivity to cultural diversity in the workforce.

• Committed to the employment and educational development of Innu Nation members.

• Must be able to maintain a high level of confidentiality.

• Self-motivated and able to work independently and unsupervised as required.

• Strong communication and report writing skills.

• Knowledge of the Impacts and Benefits Agreement and process would be an asset.

• Good computer skills are required (Word, Excel and Power Point).

• Ability to work in remote sites, travel to remote communities, and work extended hours.

## Why Newfoundland and Labrador

Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada's easternmost province, is known for its rugged coastline, rich cultural heritage, and significant natural resources. The province's economy is bolstered by a robust mining sector, where Vale Base Metals' integrated operations play a crucial role.

At Long Harbour, we operate a state-of-the-art processing plant, which refines nickel concentrate from Vale Base Metals' Voisey's Bay mine, located in Labrador, into nickel, copper, and cobalt products. This plant is a cornerstone of our commitment to value-added processing in Canada. Meanwhile, the Voisey's Bay mine is one of the world's most substantial nickel deposits. It provides high-quality nickel, copper, and cobalt, essential for the 21st century economy.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people can act like owners, being their authentic selves and empowering them to deliver results. Vale Base Metals encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

Vale recognizes the Impacts and Benefits Agreements with the Innu Nation and the Nunatsiavut Government in which Innu and Inuit workers have first preference for employment at the Voisey's Bay Mine Site. This is guided by an adjacency principle that first gives preference to those who live on the coast of Labrador, followed by those residing in the rest of Labrador, those residing on the island of the province, followed by the rest of Canada.

Next, priority will be given to Newfoundland and Labrador residents. We also welcome those who are willing to relocate back home and those looking to make NL their permanent home.

Accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Innu Nation members and Nunatsiavut beneficiaries can submit their application to their Vale Indigenous Employment Coordinator.

Employees engaged by the Company must be lawfully able to work for the Company in the country where the role is located. The Company does not provide immigration, work permit, or permanent residence sponsorship or assistance.

Pay Grade: F6T

Apply by: Sunday, October 11th 2026.

## #ValeBaseMetals

Interested applicants must submit their application online at https://vale.eightfold.ai/careers.

About Us
The Nova Scotia Public Prosecution Service (PPS) was established in 1990 as the first statutorily based independent prosecution service in Canada. The Public Prosecution Service is responsible for all prosecutions and appeals within the jurisdiction of the Attorney General.
With the guiding mission of providing fair and equal treatment in the prosecution of offences, the PPS prosecutes charges laid under the Criminal Code and under Nova Scotia statutes such as the Occupational Health and Safety Act. The Head Office is in Halifax and there are regional offices located throughout the province.
The core functions of the Nova Scotia Public Prosecution Service are to:

• Represent the Crown in the conduct of criminal trials and quasi-criminal appeals before all levels of courts

• Participate in the development of criminal law and criminal prosecutions policy

• Provide advice to police in respect of prosecutions generally or in respect of specific investigations

For more information on the Public Prosecution Service please visit https://novascotia.ca/pps/

About Our Opportunity
Under the direction of the Supervisor, Support Services the Legal Services Technician 3 (Paralegal) is responsible for triaging files, determining relevant documents, legal research, preparation of legal documents and correspondence, file management and organization, and other administrative functions and duties as assigned.

Primary Accountabilities
The Legal Services Technician is responsible for providing Crown Attorneys with legal research and a variety of case management services, as well as the preparation and processing of legal documents and correspondence. The Legal Services Technician utilizes law libraries and online legal research tools such as QuickLaw, Westlaw and CanLii. The Legal Services Technician prepares comprehensive legal memoranda for the benefit of Crown Attorneys at the pre-trial, trial and appellate stages of proceedings. The Legal Services Technician is responsible for case management of large files and file management of ongoing advice and prosecution files. The Legal Services Technician works collaboratively as part of the support team to assist with other administrative functions and duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Experience
Successful completion of a two-year Legal Services Technician course or Paralegal technology course from a recognized institution with 6 years' verifiable experience, some of which has been in the areas of regulatory and criminal law. An acceptable equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered.
A thorough knowledge of the Criminal Code, Provincial statutes and regulations relating to the environment, public health, animal welfare, food safety, aquaculture and wildlife, Summary Proceedings Act, and the Crown Lands Act, as well as having the ability to research legislative history is required.
You possess working knowledge of the criminal court process, in particular prosecutions procedures, including working with legal documents and forms, court proceedings and legal terminology as required. You demonstrate an understanding of law libraries with the capability to use online legal research databases and library protocols as required. You have excellent oral and written communications skills, a high degree of initiative, substantial problem-solving capability and the ability to work independently and as part of a team. You have the ability to work accurately in a highly time sensitive environment utilizing sound judgement, strong organizational and prioritization skills.
We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency

## Job Title: Service Advisor
Location: Dartmouth, NS
TP - DIE - 9308

Meridia Recruitment Solutions is pleased to partner with DAC Industrial Engines in the search for a Service Advisor based in Dartmouth, NS. Founded in 2005, DAC is a privately held engine company serving a wide variety of markets across Atlantic Canada, including agriculture, construction machinery, welding, compressors, material handling, marine, pumps and irrigation, forestry, ground support, and mining.
As authorized representatives of leading global manufacturers, DAC goes beyond standard supply by tailoring engines and solutions to meet each customer's specific needs. Known for quick turnaround times, technical expertise, and relationship?driven service, DAC has become a trusted partner and lead vendor for many clients across the region.

Role Description
Reporting to the Service Manager, you will play a critical customer-facing role and would be responsible for coordinating service requests, supporting the service team, and ensuring customers receive exceptional communication throughout the repair and maintenance process. Acting as the primary link between customers and technicians, you will contribute to efficient workflow, accurate documentation, and a seamless service experience.
Your responsibilities will include:

## Customer Service

• Greet customers, listen to their needs, and help identify equipment concerns.

• Serve as the primary point of contact for walk-ins and incoming service calls.

• Clearly explain repair work, timelines, and options to customers.

• Communicate progress updates and ensure a professional, customer-focused experience.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with repeat customers and contract clients.

## Service Coordination & Administration

• Create, assign, and accurately maintain work orders.

• Prepare quotes, process invoices, create warranty claims, and handle payments.

• Coordinate with the Service Manager and technicians to schedule and prioritize work.

• Ensure work orders contain complete and accurate information before submission to the Service Administrator.

• Assist with identifying, sourcing, and providing technicians with commonly used or fast-moving parts.

## Operational Support

• Help ensure the service department operates efficiently and maintains a positive customer experience.

• Support shop workflow by coordinating time, parts, and technician resources.

• Manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment while maintaining attention to detail.

• Contribute to a collaborative, team-oriented work culture.

## Qualifications

• 3+ years of experience as a Service Advisor, Service Coordinator, or similar role (equipment/industrial environment preferred).

• Strong customer service and communication skills.

• Solid understanding of mechanical concepts (engine and equipment knowledge an asset; technician background not required).

• Excellent organizational skills with the ability to multitask and manage competing priorities.

• Strong computer skills (Microsoft Office, email, and service software experience).

• Positive attitude, team-oriented mindset, and the ability to build strong internal and external relationships.

## Why Join DAC?

• Small, supportive, family oriented culture where people genuinely enjoy working together and new team members are welcomed into a close knit environment.

• Work with great customers, primarily repeat contract clients, allowing you to build long term relationships without the individual consumer pressures found in other industries.

• Room to grow in a company that actively promotes from within and offers opportunities across multiple locations as the business expands.

• A role built for balance, where you focus on customers and technicians while administrative heavy lifting is supported by a dedicated Service Administrator.

• Competitive compensation and benefits, including hourly pay with commission opportunities, medical coverage, team lunches, BBQs, paid vacation and a comprehensive benefits package.

Competition # : 49927

Location: HALIFAX

Type of Employment: Temporary

About Us
The Department of Health and Wellness offers opportunities to grow and advance in a dynamic sector that touches the lives of all Nova Scotians. Along with our partners, including the Nova Scotia Health Authority and the IWK Health Centre, we are committed to continually improving our health care system. With a focus on continual improvements within the health system, the department is thinking differently about how to plan, fund, legislate and monitor to improve access and service delivery. To do this, we need leaders at all levels of the organization who embrace a challenge and believe in their ability to make a difference.

About Our Opportunity
Reporting to the Data Scientist, you will be responsible for providing analytical and technical support on health economic policy issues relevant to the Nova Scotia health sector. This position will research economic studies and economic strategies for a range of program options to support the ongoing sustainability of the Nova Scotia health sector, and further will be responsible for developing quantitative methodologies applicable to the health sector.

In this position you will also lead other health-related advanced analytical projects and model complex business problems, discovering business insights and identifying opportunities using statistical, algorithmic, mining and visualization techniques. You will employ innovative techniques and methodologies to reveal insights held within strategic data assets. In addition, the incumbent is responsible for integrating and preparing large, varied datasets, architecting specialized databases, and communicating results to a broad group of stakeholders.

Primary Accountabilities
More specifically, in this role you will:

• Use your knowledge and expertise in methods of producing statistical inference to create strategic insights for improving the value for money spent on healthcare in Nova Scotia.

• Conceptualize and implement complex economic studies using cost-benefit, cost-effectiveness, budget impact assessments, or other methods of statistical inference to produce analytical research findings relevant to DHW's strategic objectives.

• Engage in knowledge translation and communication of results of complex financial and health economic analysis into practical use through reports, briefing notes, fact sheets, slide decks, and oral presentations to a largely non-financial client population and disseminate information to managers/stakeholders/users

• Produce health economic forecasts for strategic investment planning and senior management briefings, public forecast updates, and long-term program planning.

• Initiate proactive analysis of data to uncover insights hidden in existing and new data sources.

• Maintain cutting-edge competency in the highly strategic and complex field of health economic analysis to ensure evidence-informed advice provided to executive leadership is accurate.

• Develop and maintain productive relationships across government, the health system, and various external partners, such as academia.

Qualifications and Experience
This role requires the incumbent to hold a Bachelor's degree in a related field (e.g. statistics, economics, health economics, or econometrics) and 5 years of related experience; or a Master's degree in a related field (e.g. statistics, economics, health economics, or econometrics) and 2 years of related experience. Recent experience must include projects with a quantitative statistical emphasis.

As the successful candidate, you possess strong interpersonal skills, enjoy working in a fast-paced, agile environment, and can demonstrate the following:

• Excellent communication (verbal and written), presentation and consultation skills, and the ability to articulate information in a way that many users readily understand.

• Strong interpersonal and negotiation abilities which enable you to effectively support diverse clients and manage difficult conversations.

• Extensive knowledge undertaking appropriate economic analysis and using analytical tools.

• Demonstrated recent experience in analyzing, interpreting, and reporting data and information from large health-related administrative databases to support the planning and management of the health care system or other health initiatives.

• Demonstrated proficiency in methodological design, querying, and analyzing data, using the integration of multiple datasets to produce informative reports, dashboards, graphs, and statistical outputs.

• Proven capabilities using Microsoft Structured Query Language (SQL), Microsoft Excel, and experience using statistical analysis software capable of handling large datasets and complex analyses (R, Python, Stata, etc.)

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency

Title: Senior Emergency Management Coordinator

Employee Working Location: Partially Virtual / Hybrid (Vancouver, British Columbia)

Employment Status: Temporary Full-time (12 months)

The Canadian Red Cross (CRC) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

## In this role, you will:

## Volunteer Management:

• Oversee the recruitment, onboarding, and local roster management of volunteers across service lines.

• Contribute to workforce planning by identifying local operational needs, volunteer gaps, and internal promotion opportunities.

• Implement and lead volunteer connection strategies through regular communication, activities, and informal recognition.

• Supervise volunteers deployed for PDA services , providing guidance, mentorship, and performance feedback to ensure readiness and compliance with service protocols

## Personal Disaster Assistance (PDA) Service Execution:

• Lead the local execution of the PDA service line, ensuring effective service delivery in alignment with established standards.

• Maintain a state of readiness for local PDA activations and ensure adherence to PDA agreements.

• Oversee and complete all PDA-related processes and systems to support timely and effective response.

• Ensure proper management of requisite PDA supplies and assets as per the service delivery plan.

• Build partnerships with local governments, community leaders, and response organizations to enhance response capacity.

## Response Readiness & Emergency Preparedness:

• Participate in and support emergency preparedness and community risk reduction activities, including annual campaigns.

• Coordinate and support the implementation of local emergency response plans in accordance with program standards.

• Support or lead the setup and operation of relief efforts during emergency responses.

• Deploy as needed in response roles and contribute to operational workforce planning.

• Engage in response debriefs and after-action reviews to enhance service quality and continuous improvement.

## What we are looking for:

• A minimum of 3 years of relevant experience and relevant qualifications in volunteer management, community development, emergency management, planning and evaluation or a related field and/or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Ability to adapt knowledge and practices to varying situations or equipment

• Experience in volunteer management, including recruitment, engagement, supervision, and training.

• Experience in developing and implementing emergency response plans and conducting preparedness initiatives.

• Strong understanding of emergency management principles, disaster response protocols, and community preparedness strategies.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, databases, and volunteer management systems.

• Valid driver's license and clean driver's abstract.

• Skills to investigate problems and propose solutions, including interpreting information in unfamiliar areas, consulting with others, and innovating on standard procedures.

• Communication skills, diplomacy and empathy to interpret information and deliver advice, clarify stakeholder needs, offer solutions, and resolve escalations in new or sensitive situations

• Fluency in English is required; French is an asset.

• Ability to work flexible hours, including evenings and weekends, as required during emergency responses.

## Working Conditions:

• Role will be working primarily in an office environment when not deployed to an emergency response operation.

• Some domestic travel in generally safe environments

• Some travel by vehicle may be required.A valid provincial driver's license is required.

• All roles within the Humanitarian Services (HS) team contribute to emergency response efforts directly or indirectly.

• All CRC roles are required to adapt work and priorities to support emergency response efforts, be present in person as required to support service delivery and deploy to emergency responses when appropriate and/or required (personnel availability and request for exceptions will be discussed with line management).

• For CRC roles that are assigned a function in the Emergency Relief operational structure (in field and virtual), personnel may be required to be part of an on-call roster and be available for scheduled on-call work

• As we work with and support people (managers, colleagues, beneficiaries/customers, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.

• Eligibility to work in Canada. At this time, we welcome applications from candidates eligible to work in Canada. If you are not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada, we encourage you to carefully review your visa to find out whether you are eligible to work in the job you are considering applying for. Refer to our FAQ for more information.

• If you are selected for this role, you will be required to complete a successful pre-employment screening process which includes a satisfactory Enhanced Police Information Check (E-PIC).

## Details:

The Halifax Regional Centre for Education (HRCE) is the largest Centre for Education in Atlantic Canada with over 10,000 full-time, part-time and casual employees. Serving more than 58,000 students in 137 schools, our geographic region spans a 350 km radius. Add yourself to a world of learning today!

## HRCE offers:

• Attractive schedules offering work/life balance

• Competitive compensation and time off

• Comprehensive health and dental benefits cost-shared with the employer

• Defined benefit pension plan with contributions matched by the employer

• Access to generous sick time benefits

• Excellent career opportunities and potential for professional growth and development

• Employee and Family Assistance Program

Community Outreach Workers (COWs) are members of the Canadian Union of Public Employees, Local 5047 (CUPE). The CUPE collective agreement can be accessed by clicking HERE

Due to the nature of the position a car is required as travel will include all schools within HRCE (mileage is reimbursed).

The Community Outreach Worker is responsible for developing a proactive approach to connecting families and community groups in order to facilitate support and services to students. Working with an assigned group of schools, the Community Outreach Worker will establish an active network of community groups representing the diverse nature of the community and build bridges to connect families and schools with the ultimate goal of improving student success. Consistent with the Department of Education and Early Childhood Development and the Halifax Regional Centre for Education policies, the Community Outreach Worker will work within an established accountability framework to ensure effective connections and communication exist between the school, the families and other appropriate community agencies. Working collaboratively with Principals and other staff, the Community Outreach Worker reports directly to a designated SchoolsPlus Facilitator.

## Qualifications:

• Undergraduate degree in Social Sciences (i.e. Sociology, Psychology, Community Studies, Family Studies) or equivalent through a combination of experience and a relevant Diploma/Certificate from a recognized community college;

• Minimum three (3) years successful experience working with students and their families;

• Direct knowledge and experience of communities served considered an asset;

• Experience with collaborative practices and involvement in community development initiatives, community boards and/or hubs considered an asset;

• Valid Nova Scotia driver's license and reliable vehicle.

## Rate of Pay:

This is a 12-month per year CUPE position with a starting annual salary of $54,818.24 paid every two weeks. Salary is based on a six (6) step scale with step increases occurring annually in accordance with the Collective Agreement as shown below.

The annual salary for term positions less than one year is pro-rated over the length of the term.

## Hours of Work:

Seven (7) hours per day (excluding lunch) totalling 35 hours per week, Monday through Friday.

## Vacation:

Community Outreach Workers initially receive three (3) weeks vacation per year (15 days) for the quota period September 1 st to August 31 st . COWs employed less than one year receive 10 vacation days for the first year pro-rated based on start date. Term COWs receive 4% vacation pay on each pay.

## Please refer to job description for further details.

Current employees - please update your employee ID on the Job Posting page before applying to positions to ensure your contract/employment status shows correctly.

Nova Scotia's Regional Centres for Education and the Conseil scolaire acadien provincial (CSAP) are committed to an inclusive education system that supports the well-being and achievement of every student and is high-quality, culturally and linguistically responsive.

The Halifax Regional Centre for Education (HRCE) is actively working to hire individuals from under-represented groups, particularly people of African Nova Scotian, African Canadian and African ancestry and Mi'kmaw/Indigenous ancestry, to work toward equitable representation within all employee groups. Equitable hiring strengthens the knowledge and expertise in our schools, and supports our public education system in establishing schools as safe, caring, and accessible learning spaces that support all students. This will provide opportunities for students to see themselves reflected throughout their schools, learning resources, and within their learning experiences.

2241312.title: Project Manager-Engineering
2241312.description:
The Opportunity

Company, Department: NS Power, Energy Delivery Capital Execution

Position Title: Project Manager-Engineering

Location: Halifax, NS

Closing Date: October 9, 2026

As Project Manager, Engineering, you will lead capital projects that support the reliability of Nova Scotia's electrical substation infrastructure. From early project development and business case planning through engineering, construction, commissioning, and closeout, you will have the opportunity to guide complex projects through their full lifecycle and see the tangible results of your work.
Working with high and medium voltage substation infrastructure, you will bring together technical expertise, project leadership, and strong stakeholder collaboration to deliver projects safely, efficiently, on schedule, and within budget. You will partner with teams across Engineering, Field Operations, Control Center Operations, Asset Management, System Planning, Environmental Services, and Safety, while also coordinating with contractors and external stakeholders.

This is an opportunity for an experienced engineering and project management professional who enjoys taking ownership, solving complex challenges, and working collaboratively across disciplines. You will contribute directly to the successful delivery of reliability-focused capital investments while continuing to build your experience in a complex, regulated utility environment.

Key elements of this role include:

• Lead Substation Reliability Capital Projects involving high and medium voltage infrastructure, including transformers, switches, circuit breakers, reclosers, buswork, and related equipment.

• Manage projects from development and planning through engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, and closeout, maintaining accountability throughout the full lifecycle.

• Develop project scopes, evaluate alternatives, and support economic and business case justification to help advance well-informed investment decisions.

• Drive successful project delivery by actively managing scope, schedules, budgets, costs, risks, and competing priorities.

• Provide financial oversight through effective budgeting, monitoring, forecasting, and cost control throughout project execution.

• Navigate regulatory governance requirements and ensure project scope and justification align with applicable regulatory and organizational standards.

• Bring together cross-functional teams and contractors to establish alignment, coordinate activities, resolve challenges, and keep projects moving forward.

• Build effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including customers, to support successful project development and implementation.

• Champion a strong safety culture, with accountability for the safety of yourself, colleagues, and contractors working under your direction.

• Support responsible project delivery by ensuring environmental performance aligns with established environmental management processes and initiatives.

These skills will make you successful:

You combine strong engineering knowledge with practical project leadership and an ability to bring people together around shared outcomes. Your experience enables you to navigate complex projects while balancing technical, financial, regulatory, safety, and stakeholder considerations.

• A Bachelor's degree in Engineering, combined with full membership or eligibility for membership in Engineers Nova Scotia. An equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant experience may also be considered.

• At least six years of demonstrated experience managing projects through planning and execution, with a strong understanding of the full project lifecycle.

• Strong project management capabilities and knowledge of formal project management methodologies.

• A demonstrated ability to keep projects on schedule, within scope, and within budget, while successfully managing multiple priorities.

• Sound financial management skills, including budgeting and project cost control.

• Strong communication, collaboration, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work effectively across technical teams, operational groups, contractors, customers, and other stakeholders.

• The ability to coordinate work and make progress in a complex, cross-functional environment.

• A valid driver's license and willingness to travel within Nova Scotia as required to support projects.

Experience with high or medium voltage electrical infrastructure and familiarity with a regulated utility environment would be valuable assets. PMP certification is also considered an asset.

We understand that experience comes in many forms, and we're dedicated to adding new perspectives to the team. So, if your experience is close to what we've listed above, please consider applying.

Learn more about our culture and values

At the Emera Group of Companies, you'll be part of an inclusive, respectful workplace where everyone is welcomed and supported. Come build a career as unique as you are: making an impact from Atlantic Canada to the world. Your experience and perspective will help us to safely deliver cleaner, more reliable energy to our customers.

If working in an innovative environment, challenging yourself, and shaping a cleaner energy future inspires you, we want to hear from you. Apply by October 9, 2026 and let us know why this role is right for you.

The perks of joining our team? We offer:

• Flexibility: One flexible remote workday.

• Health & Wellbeing: A comprehensive benefits plan, 24/7 access to virtual health care services for you and your family through Dialogue, access to a free on-site fitness centre, Employee and Family Assistance Program, parental leave top-up plan and wellness benefits.

• Grow Your Career: Opportunities to advance within and between our affiliate companies, a focus on employee development and available sponsored education programs.

• Community Engagement & Care: Corporate investments in the places where our people live and work, mentoring opportunities, fundraising-matching, volunteer programs, various committees and employee resource groups, and scholarships for children of employees.

• Competitive Compensation: Short-term incentive plan and a Defined Contribution Pension Plan.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion at Emera

As one of Atlantic Canada's largest publicly traded companies, we are ranked one of Canada's Top 100 Employers, Top Employers for Young People and Top Diversity Employers. We know our success is driven by our dedicated teams and we strongly encourage applications from all qualified candidates, including persons who identify as racially visible, Indigenous, persons with disabilities, women in underrepresented roles and members of the 2SLGBTQ+ community.
Applicants from these equity groups may self-identify through the online application process. We support candidates and employees with access and accommodation needs and encourage you to let us know when you require accommodation.

Recruitment & Promotion Policy

The success of the Emera Company is driven by its people: a strong team with a shared commitment to support the Emera Company mission and values. The purpose of our recruitment policy is to provide a consistent framework to support fair and equitable attraction, hiring, and retention of the best talent for vacant positions. We are dedicated to maintaining a fair hiring process that provides equitable opportunities to all our applicants and is guided by our company values.

If you have any questions about this opportunity or if you are experiencing any technical difficulty with the application process, please email careers@nspower.ca

The Opportunity

Company, Department: Nova Scotia Power Inc. Major Projects

Location: Halifax, NS

Type of Employment: Full-time, Regular

Closing Date: October 9th, 2026

We are looking for a Cost Specialist to join our Major Projects team. Reporting to the Manager, Project Controls, you will support project estimating, forecasting, cost analysis, and reporting activities across major capital projects.
Key elements of this role include:

The Cost Specialist will collaborate extensively with internal project stakeholders, consultants, and contractors to ensure consistency in cost methodologies, forecasting practices, and reporting outputs that align with Nova Scotia Power's standards and requirements.

• Degree or Diploma in Business Administration.

• Demonstrated experience in project budgeting, forecasting, reporting.

• Solid understanding of, and experience with project estimating, forecasting and cost control methodologies.

• Strong analytical and quantitative skills, attentive to detail.

Oxford Frozen Foods, a member of the Bragg Group of Companies, is a family-owned international business that has over 1,200 employees, eight manufacturing facilities and two large farming operations within Atlantic Canada and the United States. Oxford Frozen Foods is the world's largest provider of Wild Blueberries, one of North America's largest producers of premium frozen carrots and one of Canada's premier manufacturers of onion rings and battered appetizers.
