Competition # : 49930

Department: Emergency Management

Location: Flexible

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: Exclusion - Non Union - NSPG

Closing Date: 02-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
The Department of Emergency Management is responsible for leading disaster and emergency planning, preparedness, response and recovery activities on behalf of the Province of Nova Scotia. The objective of the Department is to ensure that Nova Scotians are safe, prepared and resilient in the face of disasters and emergencies. The Department leads the coordination and co-operation of partners and resources during provincial-level critical incidents, supports municipal and other partners in regional-level and local events, administers the province's 911 service, maintains critical communications infrastructure and supports operations of our regional emergency management centres. The Department also works to ensure critical government services continue to function during and after critical events.

The Regional Operations and Infrastructure Branch enhances the safety and resilience of our Province by:

• Establishing and maintaining Regional Emergency Operations Centres (REOCs) in 6 regions in Nova Scotia. The REOCs provide leadership in building regional emergency operations networks; ensuring collaborative efforts around emergency planning, training and exercising and developing regional plans for equipment and stores to support emergency response

• Coordinating response to regional emergencies

• Strengthening local and regional emergency preparedness through outreach and education to Nova Scotians at community events, schools, organizations, and through information sessions

• Setting standards in the provincial emergency management program for training and exercising

• Fostering strong collaboration, communication, and emergency management planning with regional partners, including the development and coordination of regional Nova Scotia Guard networks

• Providing information to the Provincial Coordination Centre and the 24/7 Watch Desk staff to ensure real-time situational awareness, coordination, and support during emergencies and actioning critical information received from the Provincial Coordination Centre in the regions

About Our Opportunity
The Program Manager, Evaluation and Accountability develops, administers, and maintains evaluation, accountability, and performance-measurement frameworks for departmental training, exercising, learning, and preparedness programs.

In this role, you establish program standards, reporting requirements, performance indicators, evaluation methods, accountability tools, and evidence-based measures. Your work helps assess program effectiveness, relevance, accessibility, outcomes, and impact. You also provide advice and recommendations to senior leadership on program direction, policy development, reporting, governance, risk mitigation, and continuous improvement.

Primary Accountabilities
As the Program Manager, Evaluation and Accountability, you:

• Develop, administer, and maintain evaluation, accountability, and performance-measurement frameworks for training, exercising, learning, and preparedness programs.

• Establish program standards, reporting requirements, performance indicators, evaluation methods, accountability tools, and evidence-based measures.

• Assess program effectiveness, relevance, accessibility, outcomes, impact, risks, gaps, and compliance considerations.

• Conduct post-delivery evaluations, preparedness reviews, after-action reviews, and lessons-learned processes.

• Assess program objectives, document findings, identify improvements, and support organizational learning.

• Analyze evaluation findings, participation data, completion records, delivery history, learning-management-system reports, feedback, and performance results.

• Use evidence to inform program decisions, reporting products, governance processes, and future planning.

• Identify capability gaps, emerging issues, systemic factors, risks, compliance concerns, and accountability considerations that affect emergency-management readiness outcomes.

• Provide advice and recommendations to senior leadership on program direction, policy development, reporting, governance, performance improvement, risk mitigation, and continuous-improvement priorities.

• Track corrective measures, improvement actions, assigned responsibilities, and implementation progress.

• Monitor delivery quality, adherence to approved curriculum, use of established training and exercising standards, and implementation of evaluation requirements.

• Support consistent, effective, and accountable program delivery across DEM programs.

• Identify and report system-level, incident-related, and individual learning or performance issues that may affect preparedness, response capacity, program effectiveness, governance, or organizational accountability.

Qualifications and Experience
To be successful in this role, you have demonstrated experience in program evaluation, program management, policy, or a related area. Your experience includes developing or applying evaluation frameworks, performance indicators, reporting requirements, standards, and evidence-based measures.

You also have experience:

• Analysing qualitative and quantitative information from multiple sources to identify trends, risks, gaps, outcomes, and opportunities for improvement.

• Evaluating programs, services, training, exercises, preparedness activities, or other organizational initiatives.

• Preparing clear reports, recommendations, briefing materials, or decision-support products for senior leaders.

• Managing competing priorities and delivering work within established timelines.

• Building effective working relationships with internal and external partners.

The following would be considered assets:

• Experience in emergency management, preparedness, organizational readiness, or business continuity.

• Experience evaluating training, learning, or exercise programs.

• Experience using learning-management-system information, participation records, completion data, feedback, or other program data for analysis and reporting.

• Experience working in a government, public-sector, or other complex multi-stakeholder environment.

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
We recognize equivalent combinations of training, education, and experience, providing opportunities for individuals with diverse backgrounds to contribute their skills and expertise. Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
Your normal work week is 35 hours/week, 7 hours/day. Most work is completed in an office or classroom environment and involves extended periods of concentration, computer use, meetings, planning, writing, and reviewing detailed materials.

The work includes facilitating or supporting training, workshops, planning sessions, and exercises in different settings. These activities may require standing for periods of time, transporting or arranging learning materials, and working in spaces with varying noise levels.

You must be able to travel periodically within Nova Scotia and, on occasion, outside the province. Travel may involve locations not readily served by public transport and may occasionally affect regular working hours.

Additional Information
The worksite location is flexible and may be located in any of the Emergency Management offices. Your worksite location will be determined at the offer negotiation stage.

What We Offer
• Career Development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career

• Engaging workplace: our Employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in, we have forward-thinking policies and strategies

• Countless career paths

Pay Grade: EC 11

Salary Range: $3,571.99 - $4,465.03 Bi-Weekly

Employment Equity Statement: Our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative, at all job levels, of the citizens we serve. The Government of Nova Scotia has an Employment Equity Policy, and we welcome applications from Indigenous People, African Nova Scotians, Persons of African Descent, Racialized Persons, Persons with Disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+ Persons and Women in occupations or positions where they are under-represented. If you are a member of one of these equity groups, you are encouraged to self-identify on your electronic application.

The Opportunity

Company, Department: Smart Meter Operations Centre

Location: Halifax, Nova Scotia

Type of Employment: Permanent, Full-Time

Closing Date: October 8, 2026

At Nova Scotia Power, our Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) program plays a critical role in delivering reliable service, enhancing the customer experience, supporting grid operations, and enabling data-driven decision-making across the organization.

We are seeking an AMI Solutions Specialist to help maximize the value of our smart meter ecosystem through data analysis, technical problem solving, stakeholder collaboration, and continuous improvement. In this role, you will work at the intersection of technology, operations, and business, helping ensure our AMI systems and processes continue to support critical business functions while identifying opportunities for innovation and optimization.

This role combines technical problem-solving, data analysis, project delivery, and stakeholder engagement to support the ongoing evolution of Nova Scotia Power's smart grid technologies.

This role is ideal for a systems thinker who enjoys solving complex business and technical challenges, working with data to uncover insights, leading cross-functional initiatives, and driving meaningful operational improvements. Acting as a bridge between technology, operations, and business teams, you will play a key role in ensuring our AMI systems, processes, and data continue to deliver reliable business outcomes while supporting innovation across the organization.

Key elements of this role include:

As the AMI Solutions Specialist, you will be responsible for supporting and enhancing our AMI ecosystem while driving initiatives that improve system performance, operational efficiency, and business value. You will:

• Analyze smart meter and operational data to identify trends, investigate issues, perform root cause analysis, and develop both immediate and long-term solutions.

• Lead and support investigations into complex business and technical challenges, assessing impacts, risks, and dependencies while developing practical and sustainable recommendations.

• Troubleshoot and resolve complex techno-functional issues affecting AMI systems, business processes, data quality, and customer outcomes.

• Partner with business and technical stakeholders to gather requirements, evaluate solution options, support testing and validation activities, and coordinate successful implementation of system and process enhancements.

• Develop and implement process improvements that increase efficiency, strengthen data integrity, improve system performance, and enhance team effectiveness.

• Serve as a subject matter expert on AMI systems and processes, providing guidance and recommendations related to system functionality, data quality, and operational performance.

• Collaborate closely with Customer Care, Billing Services, Meter Field Services, IT teams, vendors, and external partners to support the reliable operation of critical business functions.

• Work with large data sets to support troubleshooting, analysis, and decision-making.

• Develop reporting, dashboards, and performance insights that support operational excellence and informed decision-making.

• Monitor system performance, identify opportunities for optimization, and champion continuous improvement initiatives across the AMI ecosystem.

• Stay current on industry trends, emerging technologies, and smart grid innovations to help identify new opportunities to create value for the business.

These skills will make you successful:

To thrive in this role, you recognize yourself in many of the following qualifications and competencies:

• Degree in Industrial Engineering, Systems Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Analytics, Business Technology Management, or a related technical discipline.

• Around 3 years of experience in a technical solutions, systems analysis, business analysis, project delivery, operations improvement, continuous improvement, or data analytics role.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including experience working with large and complex datasets and using SQL or similar tools to investigate issues and support decision-making.

• Experience gathering business requirements, documenting processes, supporting testing activities, implementing technology solutions, and driving change initiatives.

• Demonstrated ability to investigate complex business or technical problems, perform root cause analysis, assess risks, and develop practical recommendations.

• Experience leading or supporting cross-functional initiatives involving multiple stakeholders, competing priorities, and evolving business requirements.

• Strong communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to translate technical concepts into clear, actionable recommendations for both technical and non-technical audiences.

• Proven ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining a high degree of accuracy, organization, and attention to detail.

• Curiosity, adaptability, critical thinking, and a passion for solving complex problems and driving continuous improvement.

• Experience with utility operations, Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI), Oracle Meter Data Management, Itron technologies, smart grid systems, Tableau, Power BI, or other data visualization tools is considered an asset.

We understand that experience comes in many forms, and we're dedicated to adding new perspectives to the team. So, if your experience is close to what we've listed above, we encourage you to apply.

At the Emera Group of Companies, you'll be part of an inclusive, respectful workplace where everyone is welcomed and supported. Come build a career as unique as you are: making an impact from Atlantic Canada to the world. Your experience and perspective will help us to safely deliver cleaner, more reliable energy to our customers.

• 2–4 years of experience in industrial process specifically in Pulp and Paper processes.

• Collaboration between multiple disciplines and levels of expertise.

• Mentoring opportunities to foster your personal and professional development.

• Accessible and central offices in Atlantic Canada and Ottawa.

• Access to training opportunities in areas ranging from technical development to leadership skills.

About Us

At CBCL our purpose is to create a positive and lasting impact on people and planet. As an employee-owned firm, at CBCL, our people are everything. Job Title: Senior Electrical Engineer
Location: Halifax, NS | Sydney, NS | St. John's, NL, | Stephenville, NL
TP - EFL - 8941

Meridia Recruitment Solutions is proud to partner with Emera Newfoundland & Labrador (Emera NL) in the search for a Senior Electrical Engineer to join their team. Emera NL is the owner and operator of the Maritime Link, one of Atlantic Canada's most complex and sophisticated electricity assets, enabling the interconnection between Newfoundland & Labrador and Nova Scotia through a high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission system.

As a small, technically driven organization within the Emera family, Emera NL operates with a strong owner mindset. The team is lean, collaborative, and deeply invested in the long-term performance of its assets. This role offers a unique opportunity for an experienced electrical engineer to play a hands-on technical leadership role, gain deep exposure to HVDC systems, and help shape the future asset strategy of a nationally significant transmission link.

## Role Description:

As Senior Electrical Engineer, you will serve as the technical authority for Emera NL's HVDC transmission asset. Reporting to the Director of Engineering, you will provide electrical engineering leadership across operations, asset management, inspections, maintenance planning, and continuous improvement initiatives. The role goes well beyond traditional design work, as you will be relied upon to troubleshoot complex issues, work directly with operations and site teams, and help ensure the system continues to operate safely, efficiently, and reliably for decades to come.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Serving as the internal technical expert for the Maritime Link HVDC system, including transmission assets, converter stations, and control systems.

• Reviewing and interpreting vendor documentation, technical studies, reports, and operating procedures.

• Leading inspection strategies, condition assessments, and long-term maintenance planning as OEM support contracts wind down.

• Developing and maintaining risk-based asset management plans to ensure long-term reliability and performance.

• Supporting outage planning and execution, including participation in the annual planned outage and post-outage analysis.

• Working closely with operations teams to diagnose and resolve complex technical issues, providing sound judgement during abnormal or emergency conditions.

• Supporting protection, control, and automation activities in a controls-intensive operating environment.

• Collaborating with internal stakeholders, external contractors, OEMs, and consultants on ongoing operations and future initiatives.

• Contributing engineering input to capital planning, reliability improvements, and potential new infrastructure opportunities.

• Maintaining and enhancing engineering standards, documentation, and technical processes.

• Building internal technical capability and act as a trusted advisor within a lean, ownership-driven team.

• Participating in specialized training and industry forums, including international HVDC user conferences.

## Ideal Qualifications:

• Degree in Electrical Engineering with P.Eng. designation or eligibility for registration in Newfoundland & Labrador.

• Strong background in electrical power systems, ideally within utility operations, transmission, protection & controls, automation, or other complex industrial environments.

• Experience supporting operating assets, with a practical understanding of how systems perform in real-world, operational conditions.

• Comfortable working across disciplines, including controls, protection, automation, and systems integration.

• Exposure to HVDC systems is considered an asset; however, a strong electrical foundation is more important, and training will be provided for the right individual.

• Practical, solutions-oriented engineer with an ownership mindset and the ability to remain calm under pressure.

• Strong communicator who works effectively within a small, highly collaborative team.

• Motivated to build long-term technical depth in a unique and highly specialized power system environment.

## Why This Role Stands Out:

• Run a truly unique, complex asset that plays a vital role in Atlantic Canada's power system.

• Become a recognized HVDC expert through hands-on experience and global training opportunities.

• Work in a lean team where engineering judgement matters and your contributions are visible.

• Enjoy meaningful technical autonomy while being supported by experienced leaders and partners.

For more information contact Thomas Pugh, Partner, at 902-818-4506 and tpugh@kbrs.ca or Rick Neima, Consultant at 902-488-2534 and rneima@kbrs.ca, or please apply online by clicking the "Apply Now" button below. Company, Department: Nova Scotia Power, ERP Product Support
Location: Halifax, Nova Scotia

• Support user access provisioning and administration activities for enterprise systems and applications.

• Assist with role management, access governance, and security-related processes.

• Coordinate and support ServiceNow requests, incidents, and operational activities.

• Participate in user access reviews and compliance-related initiatives.

• Create and maintain process documentation, knowledge articles, and operational procedures.

• Support day-to-day application operations and technology support activities.

• Assist with reporting, metrics tracking, and data analysis to support decision-making and operational effectiveness.

• Collaborate with technology, security, and business teams to support project and operational objectives.

• Identify opportunities for process improvements and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives.

• Participate in technology projects and gain exposure to enterprise application management practices.

## Who you are:

We're looking for a motivated student who enjoys problem-solving, learning new technologies, and supporting systems that enable business success. You will be a strong candidate if you:

• Are currently enrolled in a post-secondary program in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, Business, Engineering, Cybersecurity, or a related field.

• Have an interest in technology operations, enterprise applications, cybersecurity, access management, or business systems.

• Possess strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

• Have excellent attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy.

• Are comfortable using Microsoft 365 applications, particularly Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.

• Communicate effectively and can work with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Learn new technologies, systems, and business processes quickly.

• Are organized and able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

• Work well independently while also contributing positively to a collaborative team.

• Have previous co-op, internship, academic project, volunteer, or work experience related to technology, business systems, data analysis, or process improvement (considered an asset).

## What we offer:

• Networking & Growth: Join a network of current and former co-op students and build connections through biweekly events such as keynote speaker series, coffee chats, volunteer opportunities, and social activities.

• Comprehensive Onboarding: Start your term with confidence through our engaging onboarding program, which includes facilitated group orientation sessions, a Student Handbook, and a Technology Guide designed to set you up for success from day one.

• Community Engagement & Giving Back: Get involved through mentoring opportunities, employee resource groups, volunteer programs, fundraising-matching initiatives, and various committees that support the communities where we live and work.

• Meaningful Project Experience: Support technology initiatives that help strengthen enterprise systems, improve operational processes, and enable secure access to critical business applications used across Nova Scotia Power.

• Hands-On Learning & Development: Gain practical experience in access management, technology operations, enterprise applications, reporting, process documentation, and technology governance.

• Exposure to Industry-Leading Platforms: Build experience working with enterprise technologies such as Oracle Fusion and ServiceNow while learning how large organizations manage application access, compliance, and operational excellence.

2239731.title: Manager- Relief
2239731.description:
Title: Manager- Relief

Employee Working Location: Alberta/ Northwest Territories

Employment Status: Permanent full-time

The Canadian Red Cross (Red Cross) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

The Manager, Relief ensures exceptional client and stakeholder service while maintaining team efficiency in a collaborative
environment. They oversee daily operations, manage resources, and address escalations to meet service goals and short-term emergency goals.
objectives. They work with stakeholders to align operational needs with organizational priorities and support team members in
coordinating services for clients affected by emergencies, tailored to the event's scope and impact.

## In this role you will:

• Coordinate with various agencies, organizations, and community stakeholders to ensure a unified and effective response/s.

• Build and maintain relationships with government, community/local groups, different non-profits and various funders.

• Understand the scope, reporting requirements, and budget as the main point of contact for executing our contract/s or service agreement/s.

• Lead, organize and participate in emergency response exercises, workshops and learning sessions to evaluate and improve readiness internally and externally.

• Lead and coordinate emergency relief efforts during response operations.

• Ensure the availability and functionality of emergency response resources.

• Develop and implement strategies to mitigate risks and enhance community resilience.

• Stay informed about changes in policies and regulations related to emergency management.

• Conduct and participate in reviews of emergency responses to identify strengths, lessons learned, and areas for improvement.

• Implement changes to plans and procedures based on post-incident analyses.

• Engage with communities and partner organizations to build awareness and strengthen emergency preparedness and resilience.

## What we are looking for:

• A minimum of 4-7 years' experience and a 3-year college diploma or university degree in emergency
management, social services, health services, logistics, project management and/or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Supervisory or management experience with leadership and team management skills and the ability to manage performance, resolve conflicts, and engage employees.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint), SharePoint, database platforms and interactive data visualization software is required.

• Ability to plan, adjust and operationalize the service agreements by understanding the needs and impact of the service and
choosing the best method of delivery based on these needs.

• Ability to identify complex problems, analyze interrelated factors, mitigate risks, and develop solutions using specialized skills.

• Communication and influencing skills to synthesize diverse and sometimes conflicting perspectives and find mutually beneficial solutions, often in sensitive or complex situations.

• Fluency in English is required; French is an asset.

## Working Conditions:

• The role includes fieldwork, deployment to emergency operations regionally and across Canada, and office-based work during non-deployment periods.

• Domestic travel to generally safe, but high-stress environments; exposure to major adverse conditions requiring personal safety management.

• Work requires the ability to work to multiple, business critical, and conflicting deadlines.

• Work requires interactions in difficult, emotionally charged situations.

• Work requires interactions and support to clients who are experiencing traumatic situations.

• In a large scale emergency where staff numbers are compromised or additional resources are required, provide disaster relief and/or emergency field operational support.

• Potential for responding to disaster areas, as well as difficult and unstable conditions (environmental, physical, social, etc.) and uncomfortable conditions (noise, odors, smoke, humidity, vulnerable beneficiaries). These stressful rapidly changing
environments with limited information to make decisions have the potential to affect the physical and psychological state of the responders on site.

• Will be required to work extended hours during peak periods on short notice.

• As we work with and support people (managers, colleagues, beneficiaries/customers, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.

• Eligibility to work in Canada: At this time, we welcome applications from candidates eligible to work in Canada. If you are not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada, we encourage you to carefully review your visa to find out whether you are eligible to work in the job you are considering applying for. Refer to our FAQ for more information.

• If you are selected for this role, you will be required to complete a successful pre-employment screening process which includes a satisfactory Enhanced Police Information Check (E-PIC).

2240626.title: Quality Assurance Technician
2240626.description:
Located in Oxford, NS
Application Deadline: October 1, 2026
Estimated Start Date: Immediate Need

This position will include Shift Work.

Oxford Frozen Foods Ltd, a member of the Bragg Group of Companies, is a family-owned international business that has over 1,200 employees, eight manufacturing facilities and two large farming operations within Atlantic Canada and the United States. Oxford Frozen Foods is the world's largest provider of Wild Blueberries, one of North America's largest producers of premium frozen carrots and one of Canada's premier manufacturers of onion rings and battered appetizers.

## Benefits of being an Oxford Frozen Foods Employee:

• Comprehensive benefit package including a matching contribution pension plan.

• Employee Housing Loan program provides a forgivable loan up to $40,000, interest free.

• Vacation PLUS we offer a vacation purchase plan allowing for additional time off.

• Employee Discount Program offering great discounts across Atlantic Canada.

• Employee pricing on products we produce.

## Position Scope:

As a Quality Assurance Technician, you are responsible for ensuring that all processed products meet strict quality standards and specifications. Operating both independently and collaboratively as part of a team, you will utilize your strong organizational, multitasking, and time management skills to monitor scales, metal detectors, and coders hourly, ensuring proper coding for all products on shift. Your clear communication and interpersonal abilities will be essential as you perform pre-operational line inspections, certify quality standards, and provide constructive feedback to drive ongoing improvements—taking decisive action to make real-time changes when necessary. You will be expected to follow all safety policies and procedures closely, adapt to other duties as required, and safely handle various ingredients, including onions and wheat products.

## Work Environment & Physical Requirements:

• Production environment.

• Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) as required.

• Ability to lift 50lbs.

## Qualifications:

• Grade Twelve Diploma or equivalent GED Certificate is a requirement

• Post-secondary education within a science specialty would be considered an asset

• Experience working within Quality or as a Grader would be considered an asset

Oxford Frozen Foods is committed to providing a safe, respectful, inclusive workplace free from discrimination, harassment, and workplace violence and welcome applications from all qualified individuals.

Applications can be made by visiting www.oxfordfrozenfoods.com/opportunity and applying through our career center.

2239994.title: Safety Trainer
2239994.description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is transforming the future?

## Who We Are

We are Vale Base Metals – a global supplier of the critical minerals transforming the future.

With industry-leading reserves of copper and nickel in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia, and state-of-the-art infrastructure in the U.K., Canada, and Japan, VBM delivers a secure and responsible supply of high-quality products to customers across Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

Global demand for critical minerals is growing exponentially. From energy to aerospace, batteries to magnets, robotics to artificial intelligence, a secure and responsible supply of critical minerals is fundamental to power modern technologies. And at Vale Base Metals, we are transforming our business to provide a secure and responsible supply of these minerals.

Join our diverse team of 13,000 talented individuals committed to providing mineral security to a world in transition. We invite you to put your skills to work, driving meaningful and enduring change while enjoying a rewarding career.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking a Safety Trainer to join our People & Community Department in Voisey's Bay, Labrador, a fly-in fly-out operation.

This permanent position will be on a 2 week on/2 week off rotation working at the mine site.

The Safety Trainer will lead the delivery of all safety training for the business, based on site specific requirements, and the expectations of the Vale Base Metals Health and Safety business unit, and provincial/federal legislation. By ensuring effective delivery of safety training programs for the operation, the Safety Trainer is integral in supporting the development of employee knowledge and skills which are vital to sound risk management in daily work activities. The Safety Trainer will also support in field training for various HEO equipment, maintenance training, and support the various training plans for the surface operations.

Additionally, in this position you will:

• Deliver safety training to all site personnel, including applicable orientation programs, company specific training and regulatory training.

• Assist in the development, review and revision of safety training programs.

• Provide field instruction and competency evaluations as necessary to support applicable training programs.

• Liaise with operational departments to optimize delivery of training, maximizing values of time and resources.

• Maintain required trainer certifications necessary to deliver safety training programs.

• Keep current with legislation and industry best practice in support of safety training program continuous improvement.

• Provide feedback as necessary, to respective departments, on individual performance noted during the delivery of safety training programs.

• Provide advice and support in the field as necessary to support the implementation of safety, maintenance, and heavy equipment training programs where practical instruction is necessary to support classroom theory.

## What We Offer You

• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, flex health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare online

• Online training and career development opportunities

• Chartered flights within Newfoundland & Labrador

• 24/7 access to a fully stocked cafeteria with balanced meals prepared by our culinary team

• Access to recreational facilities and social activities (cardio/weight room, gymnasium, music room, movie theatre, etc.)

• Accommodations are equipped with cable TV, internet, and unlimited long-distance calling

• All Personal Protective Equipment is provided upon hire. Employees are given a safety boot allowance and receive a 100% reimbursement for prescription safety glasses

## About You

## Education:

• A minimum of post-secondary education within Health & Safety or a related journeyperson trades program is required.

• Preferred certifications in the following: WorkplaceNL certified in Fall Protection, Confined Space, Power Line Hazards, Supervisor Health & Safety, Occupational Health and Safety Committee, and St. John's Ambulance First Aid.

## Experience:

• A minimum of 3 years experience in a similar role.

## Skills:

• Demonstrate leadership skills and abilities.

• Strong presentation, oral, and written communication skills.

• Familiar with provincial regulations.

• Extensive knowledge of heavy equipment/maintenance training within the mining industry.

• Excellent problem solving and computer skills (Word, Excel, Power Point, etc.).

• Safety oriented and respect for all cultural diversity.

• Work with minimum supervision.

## Why Newfoundland and Labrador

Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada's easternmost province, is known for its rugged coastline, rich cultural heritage, and significant natural resources. The province's economy is bolstered by a robust mining sector, where Vale Base Metals' integrated operations play a crucial role.

At Long Harbour, we operate a state-of-the-art processing plant, which refines nickel concentrate from Vale Base Metals' Voisey's Bay mine, located in Labrador, into nickel, copper, and cobalt products. This plant is a cornerstone of our commitment to value-added processing in Canada. Meanwhile, the Voisey's Bay mine is one of the world's most substantial nickel

deposits. It provides high-quality nickel, copper, and cobalt, essential for the 21st century economy.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people can act like owners, being their authentic selves and empowering them to deliver results. Vale Base Metals encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

Vale recognizes the Impacts and Benefits Agreements with the Innu Nation and the Nunatsiavut Government in which Innu and Inuit workers have first preference for employment at the Voisey's Bay Mine Site. This is guided by an adjacency principle that first gives preference to those who live on the coast of Labrador, followed by those residing in the rest of Labrador, those residing on the island of the province, followed by the rest of Canada.

Next, priority will be given to Newfoundland and Labrador residents. We also welcome those who are willing to relocate back home and those looking to make NL their permanent home.

Accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Innu Nation members and Nunatsiavut beneficiaries can submit their application to their Vale Indigenous Employment Coordinator.

Employees engaged by the Company must be lawfully able to work for the Company in the country where the role is located. The Company does not provide immigration, work permit, or permanent residence sponsorship or assistance.

## Pay Grade: G01

## Apply by: Sunday, September 27th, 2026

## #ValeBaseMetals

Interested applicants must submit their application online at https://vale.eightfold.ai/careers.

2240172.title: Sr Program Advisor, Humanitarian Foresights
2240172.description:
Title: Sr Program Advisor, Humanitarian Foresights

Employee Working Location: Partially Virtual / Hybrid (Canada)

Employment Status: Permanent Full-time

The Canadian Red Cross (Red Cross) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

The Canadian Red Cross is looking for an analytical Senior Program Advisor who can turn research and emerging insights into useful guidance and concrete products. This role will help us understand what is changing, what it may mean, and where future risks and opportunities may emerge by bringing together data, operational insight, and diverse perspectives to support evidence-informed decisions, innovation, and organizational readiness.
The successful candidate will be comfortable working with ambiguity, exploring complex problems, testing assumptions, and translating a wide range of information into clear and useful insights. They will work collaboratively across teams and with external partners to identify emerging issues, strengthen analysis, and support the development of practical responses and new opportunities.

## In this role, you will :

• Implement and continuously improve a humanitarian foresight cycle, including the development of annual risk-based scenarios, to support operational and longer-term planning with evidence-based assumptions.

• Conduct research, environmental scanning, and analysis using internal and external sources to identify emerging humanitarian trends, risks, opportunities, and planning implications.

• Develop clear foresight products, scenarios, briefings, presentations, and recommendations that translate complex information into useful insights for planning and decision-making.

• Apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills to frame complex challenges, test assumptions, and identify practical options.

• Support the identification and assessment of innovative approaches, service improvements, partnerships, and future opportunities.

• Develop risk-based scenarios and assess potential humanitarian impacts, readiness, and capacity or capability needs to support strategic planning, program or service design, and organizational improvement.

• Build and maintain internal and external partnerships across public, private, academic, and humanitarian sectors to gather and validate insights, strengthen analysis, share relevant risk information and lessons learned, and support senior leaders' engagement in foresight and emergency-planning forums.

• Contribute subject matter expertise and advice to projects and initiatives that strengthen organizational readiness, effectiveness, and impact.

• Contribute effectively within project and matrix teams; support planning and reporting; maintain organized team documentation and records, including SharePoint filing; manage relevant subscriptions and information resources; and continuously improve foresight methods, tools, and products through research, learning, and collaboration.

## What we are looking for:

• A minimum of six to nine years of job-related experience and a three-year college diploma or university degree in social sciences, community development, Indigenous studies, public administration, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. A graduate diploma or degree, professional degree, certification, or designation in a related field may be required.

• Experience in research, strategic analysis, policy, program or service design, foresight, risk analysis, innovation, planning, emergency management, or a related field.

• Strong analytical skills and the ability to gather, integrate, interpret, and assess complex information.

• The ability to identify patterns, trends, risks, opportunities, and connections across different issues and sources.

• Demonstrated problem-solving skills and comfort working on complex issues where the way forward may not be immediately apparent.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex information into concise and accessible insights.

• Experience preparing briefings, reports, presentations, recommendations, or other products for decision-makers and diverse audiences.

• Strong collaboration, facilitation, and stakeholder-engagement skills.

• Curiosity, sound judgment, initiative, and a willingness to explore new ideas and approaches.

• The ability to work independently under broad direction while contributing effectively within cross-functional or matrix teams.

• Experience with horizon scanning, forecasting, scenario planning, systems thinking, futures methods, or innovation methods would be an asset.

• English proficiency required, French is a strong asset.

## Working conditions:

• The work is primarily performed in an office or remote-work environment and requires sustained concentration and the ability to process significant amounts of information.

• The role may require occasional travel and flexibility during periods of heightened operational activity.

• Participation in emergency planning, preparedness, or response activities may be required.

• As we work with and support people (managers, colleagues, beneficiaries/customers, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.

• Eligibility to work in Canada: At this time, we welcome applications from candidates eligible to work in Canada. If you are not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada, we encourage you to carefully review your visa to find out whether you are eligible to work in the job you are considering applying for. Refer to our FAQ for more information.

• If you are selected for this role, you will be required to complete a successful pre-employment screening process which includes a satisfactory Enhanced Police Information Check (E-PIC).

2240016.title: Senior Accountant, New Operations
2240016.description:
## Senior Accountant, New Operations
Halifax, NS
Reference # HL-SHX-10106

We are pleased to be partnered with Shannex in bringing a Senior Accountant, New Operations to their talented team in Halifax, NS. Founded in 1988, Shannex has grown from one nursing home into a full continuum of services across Nova Scotia, New Brunswick and Ontario, including home care, retirement living, assisted living, memory care, long-term care and hospitality. Its mission is to Lead the Way to Better Living for individuals and communities by providing the best care and service excellence to people as they age. This is an exciting opportunity to join Shannex and be part of innovative and growing organization.

The Senior Accountant, New Operations will provide in-depth financial statement review, analysis, account reconciliations and support across finance divisions, with an opportunity to contribute to business growth and continuous improvement across new business sectors.

## Key Responsibilities:

• Assist with the timely preparation of monthly, quarterly and annual financial statements

• Reconcile corporate general ledger accounts, investigate reconciling items and work cross-functionally to ensure appropriate accounting under ASPE.

• Review financial reports and prepare detailed variance explanations that support decision-making.

• Partner with accounting, treasury, financial planning and analysis, operations and other finance departments to streamline processes, improve efficiency and strengthen performance.

• Build and use financial analysis tools to manage and report on new operation results.

• Document accounting processes and policies to guide the financial reporting team.

• Assist with annual audited financial statements and liaise with auditors to address queries.

• Support budgeting, forecasting and variance analysis.

• Prepare financial reports, charts, tables, PowerPoint presentations and other exhibits; respond to ad hoc projects related to business growth.

## The ideal candidate will have:

• CPA designation or near completion of the CPA program coupled with a bachelor's degree in accounting or finance.

• Accounting experience in public practice or a comparable corporate role is a strong asset.

• Strong computer literacy and advanced working knowledge of Microsoft Office, including Excel, PowerPoint and Word.

• Thorough technical knowledge of Accounting Standards.

• Strong organizational skills and exceptional attention to detail.

• Excellent communication skills.

• Experience with Yardi software is considered an asset.

• Passion for the healthcare sector and/or ensuring seniors have access to quality accommodations, services and care.

As Shannex continues to expand and innovate, you will have the chance to make a meaningful contribution while developing your career within a collaborative, purpose-driven and innovative environment. This isn't an opportunity to miss out on.

To express interest in this opportunity please apply online at: https://meridiarecruitment.ca/Career/17888860926110000008bdc

For more information about this exciting opportunity please contact Heather Labucki, Partner, or Sara Morey, Senior Consultant, at smorey@kbrs.ca. If you require accommodation to participate in the recruitment process, please let Sara Morey know.

Meridia Recruitment Solutions connects leading organizations with top talent by building strong relationships and creating ideal matches with candidates because we are only successful when you are. We appreciate your interest in this opportunity.

To learn more about Meridia Recruitment Solutions, our job opportunities, and career advice we invite you to explore our site and subscribe for career alerts.

2240243.title: Business Services Clerk (Clerk 4)
2240243.employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
2240243.description:
Competition # : 49886

Department: Public Works

Location: HALIFAX

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: NSGEU - NSPG

Closing Date: 29-Sep-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About UsMaintaining and building our Provincial infrastructure is no small job. The Real Estate and Infrastructure Management Division at the Department of Public Works supports Nova Scotia's 2,400 buildings and infrastructure assets across a wide range of clients. We maintain and support various government buildings and other built assets, including museums, core buildings and office buildings supporting the work of government, correctional centres, and justice centres.About Our Opportunity
Reporting to the Manager of Business Services, the Business Services Clerk plays a vital role in supporting the operational and procurement functions of the Real Estate and Infrastructure Management Division within the Department of Public Works.

Primary Accountabilities
You provide critical procurement support to the Real Estate and Infrastructure Management Branch, ensuring accuracy, compliance, and efficiency across all purchasing activities. You collaborate with internal stakeholders to validate procurement requests, secure senior management approvals, and prepare front-end tender documents in Ariba and SAP S4 purchase orders. You also manage standing offer purchases in accordance with government directives, verify offer details, and support agreement administration.

You will also be responsible for processing accounts payable transactions, including AP and MIRO invoices, ensuring appropriate approvals, accurate coding, and compliance with financial controls and departmental procedures. You are also responsible for verifying work order information and entering time confirmations within SAP S4 to support labour cost recovery, project billing, and accurate financial reporting.

Qualifications and ExperienceYou have five (5) years of related experience. An equivalent combination of education, training and experience will be considered. You have experience in government procurement policies, S4, Ariba, Microsoft Office Suite and reporting.
Proficiency in data entry and extensive knowledge in spreadsheet software and creation, word processing, and email applications is essential.

You must demonstrate excellent coordination and organization skills along with experience in maintaining records in both manual and computerized environments.

The following qualifications are considered assets:

• Completed course work in bookkeeping and accounting;

• Familiarity with STAR/STOR;

• Experience with preparation of building construction quantity documents; and

• Experience with S4 (or equivalent).

As the ideal candidate, you have exceptional planning and organizational skills to assist with the efficient operation of our office. You are an analytical thinker who presents information in a clear, concise manner. You are also a self-motivated individual who works both independently with minimal supervision and participates fully as an effective team player.

You maintain a professional and courteous disposition and hold a high standard for client and customer service.

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
An equivalent combination of relevant training and experience will be considered. Related equivalencies include, but are not limited to:

• A completed related bachelor's degree and one (1) year of experience

• A completed related diploma and three (3) years of experience

Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
• Normal work week is 35 hours/week, 7 hours/day.

• May be required to work overtime on occasion.

• Typically located in a comfortable office environment.

• Much of the time is spent in a comfortable position with frequent opportunity to move about.

• Regularly reads and interprets multiple sources of information, regular requirement to type, read and work on a computer.

• May experience pressure with deadlines and need for accuracy.

What We Offer
• Career development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career

• Engaging workplace: our employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in, we have forward-thinking policies and strategies

• Countless career paths

Pay Grade: CL 22

Salary Range: $2,123.03 - $2,348.18 Bi-Weekly

Employment Equity Statement: Our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative, at all job levels, of the citizens we serve. The Government of Nova Scotia has an Employment Equity Policy, and we welcome applications from Indigenous People, African Nova Scotians, Persons of African Descent, Racialized Persons, Persons with Disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+ Persons and Women in occupations or positions where they are under-represented. If you are a member of one of these equity groups, you are encouraged to self-identify on your electronic application.

Accommodation Statement: We are committed to providing an inclusive and accessible recruitment process. Candidates may request accommodations based on any grounds protected by the Human Rights Act. If you require an accommodation throughout the recruitment process, please contact us at competitions@novascotia.ca.

2241269.title: Senior Clinical Specialist
2241269.description:
Title : Senior Clinical Specialist

Employee Working Location : Partially Virtual / Hybrid (Canada)

Employment Status : Permanent, Full-time

The Canadian Red Cross (CRC) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

The Senior Clinical Specialist is responsible to deploy to emergency health settings to provide immediate health care support and/or provide direct clinical care to patients. In between deployments, they will engage in relevant learning and contribute to clinical services as a Subject Matter Expert (SME). They are responsible for leading health assessments, supporting the design and implementation of clinical services, and training health personnel. They coordinate with on-site clinical team leads to address issues raised by deployed personnel, ensure consistency with clinical trends and guidelines, support new procedures, and observe health protocols.

## In this role, you will:

While deployed to emergency operations and programs:

• Provision of clinical and health care to patients and clients. Lead clinical assessments, implement clinical and health services, and supervise and train clinical, non-clinical and auxiliary personnel as relevant.

• Liaise with partner agencies on clinical issues, act as a resource between clinicians and roster managers, and stay current on regulatory changes.

• Coordinate with on-site clinical team leads to address issues that impact operations.

• Ensure consistency with clinical trends and guidelines, support the implementation of new procedures, and observe health authority and CRC protocols.

• Teach, mentor, and train appropriate auxiliary personnel.

• Manage medical supplies ensuring they are stored, monitored, and replenished according to best practice and following health authority and CRC guidelines.

• Ensure appropriate patient monitoring following medical procedures.

While not deployed:

• Provide input on clinical operations and support operational leads with planning and design.

• Contribute as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) by drafting, updating, and maintaining clinical SOPs in line with guidelines.

• Maintain communication with HiE Roster Manager and help monitor readiness for clinical deployments.

• Stay updated on licensing requirements for healthcare professionals and review clinical learning paths for compliance.

• Support international clinical readiness and deployment as directed by the team lead.

## What we are looking for:

• Qualifications include a minimum of 6-9 years clinical experience and Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN), or Bachelor of Nursing (BN), or Diplome d'Études Collégiales (DEC) in Nursing, or BNI (DEC-BAC) or other bachelor's in clinical health care.

• Current Professional Registration in one province in Canada is required.

• Able to travel on short notice to other destinations within the province for periods of several weeks (2-6 weeks) is a
requirement.

• Proficiency in standard computer applications (Microsoft Office Suite).

• Experience in health needs assessment and the design of health programming.

• Ability to coordinate with authorities and foster effective working relationships with health stakeholders at various levels.

• Ability to identify complex problems, analyze interrelated factors, assess and mitigate risks, and develop solutions using specialized skills.

• Communication and influence skills to gather perspectives, understand needs, and present information to reach consensus, often in somewhat sensitive situations.

• Training, facilitation, coaching, and/or education skills.

• Able to travel to remote locations for 2-6 weeks as required.

• Fluency in English is required.

• Experience living or working in a cultural context other than their own, experience working in Indigenous Communities, and/or in remote and isolated communities.

• Ability to adapt to changing circumstances in a fast-paced environment.

## Working Conditions:

This role is a response and operational profile that requires scheduled travel, deployment, and in community in-person presence.

Physical Effort

• Occasional requirement to lift up to 5kg in order to perform the requirements of the role.

• Occasional requirement for prolonged sitting with infrequent breaks in order to perform the requirements of the role.

• Occasional requirement for prolonged standing with infrequent breaks in order to perform the requirements of the role.

Sensory & Mental Effort

• Requires significant attention to detail and concentration and ability to mentally process large amounts of information.

• The work pace is often unpredictable with significant time pressures.

• Ability to adapt to frequent and often urgent changes in priorities, and make decisions under pressure, work at an
unpredictable pace.

Work Environment

• The role includes fieldwork, deployment to emergency operations, and office-based work during non-deployment periods.

• Domestic or international travel to unsafe or high-stress environments; exposure to major adverse conditions requiring
personal safety management.

• Work requires the ability to work to multiple, business critical, and conflicting deadlines.

• Work requires interactions in difficult, emotionally charged situations.

• Work requires interactions and support to clients who are experiencing traumatic situations.

• Potential for responding to disaster areas, as well as difficult and unstable conditions (environmental, physical, social, etc.) and uncomfortable conditions (noise, odors, smoke, humidity, vulnerable beneficiaries). These stressful rapidly changing environments with limited information to make decisions have the potential to affect the physical and psychological state of the responders on site.

• Will be required to work extended hours during peak periods on short notice.

• If you are within the teams delivering services in the emergency management continuum you will be required to travel and deploy as directed by your line management to meet the demands of your role and this can include contexts of community engagement and long-term programming in operational response.

• As we work with and support people (managers, colleagues, beneficiaries/customers, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.

• Eligibility to work in Canada: At this time, we welcome applications from candidates eligible to work in Canada. If you are not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada, we encourage you to carefully review your visa to find out whether you are eligible to work in the job you are considering applying for. Refer to our FAQ for more information.

• If you are selected for this role, you will be required to complete a successful pre-employment screening process which includes a satisfactory Enhanced Police Information Check (E-PIC).

2241313.title: Sr Mgr, Substation Reliability
2241313.description:
The Opportunity

Company, Department: Nova Scotia Power, Reliability, Standards and Engagement

Position Title: Senior Manager, Substation Reliability

Reports To: Director, Reliability

Location: Halifax, Nova Scotia

Closing Date: October 9, 2026

At Nova Scotia Power, we are committed to providing safe, reliable electricity so that our customers and communities can thrive. The Senior Manager, Substation Reliability is responsible for the strategic development, governance, and execution oversight of Nova Scotia Power's Substation Capital Investment Program.

This position provides leadership to a team of engineers, project managers and technical specialists responsible for project execution, capital planning, engineering design, protection and control coordination, and reliability improvement initiatives associated with the transmission and distribution substation fleet.

The role is accountable for ensuring capital investments are aligned with long-term asset strategies, system planning requirements, asset condition assessments, regulatory commitments and corporate reliability objectives.

Key elements of this role include:

As Senior Manager, Substation Reliability, you will:

• Provide leadership, coaching, performance management and development for the Substation Reliability team.

• Develop plans to implement long-term asset management strategies for transmission and distribution substation assets.

• Work with the EAM team to understand asset health, risk and criticality assessments to identify investment needs and reliability risks.

• Lead the development and oversight of the Substation Capital Investment Program with the Substation Project Management and Substation Design Leads.

• Ensure projects are appropriately scoped, justified, estimated, approved and delivered in accordance with corporate capital governance requirements and ACE directives.

• Provide oversight of project execution activities including engineering design, project management, protection and control, commissioning and project close-out with the Substation Project Management and Substation Design Leads.

• Monitor program performance and implement actions to address schedule, scope, cost and execution risks.

• Ensure capital plans remain responsive to emergent equipment failures and changing system needs.

• Lead development of annual and multi-year capital investment plans, business cases, ACE filings, forecasting and reporting.

• Provide strategic oversight for procurement of major substation equipment and long-lead materials.

• Act as a liaison between Asset Management, Operations, Engineering, System Planning, Project Delivery and other stakeholders.

• Provide leadership and technical direction as required during major equipment failures, system disturbances and restoration events.

These skills will make you successful:

• Registered Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) with Engineers Nova Scotia or eligible for registration.

• Minimum 5 years of progressively responsible utility engineering, asset management, reliability, operations or capital program experience.

• Leadership experience managing technical or professional teams.

• Demonstrated experience with transmission and distribution substations, asset management and capital planning.

• Strong leadership, communication, stakeholder engagement, financial management and analytical skills.

SAFETY
• Responsible for personal safety and the safety of employees, contractors and others under their direction.

• Ensure compliance with all Occupational Health and Safety requirements and company procedures.

• Promote a culture of safety, risk awareness and continuous improvement.

## ENVIRONMENT

• Accountable for environmental performance in accordance with environmental management system requirements.

• Ensure environmental requirements are incorporated into planning and project execution activities.

We understand that experience comes in many forms, and we're dedicated to adding new perspectives to the team. So, if your experience is close to what we've listed above, please consider applying.

Learn more about our culture and values

At the Emera Group of Companies, you'll be part of an inclusive, respectful workplace where everyone is welcomed and supported. Come build a career as unique as you are: making an impact from Atlantic Canada to the world. Your experience and perspective will help us to safely deliver cleaner, more reliable energy to our customers.

If working in an innovative environment, challenging yourself, and shaping a cleaner energy future inspires you, we want to hear from you. Apply by October 9, 2026 and let us know why this role is right for you.

The perks of joining our team? We offer:

• Flexibility: One flexible remote workday.

• Health & Wellbeing: A comprehensive benefits plan, 24/7 access to virtual health care services for you and your family through Dialogue, access to a free on-site fitness centre, Employee and Family Assistance Program, parental leave top-up plan and wellness benefits.

• Grow Your Career: Opportunities to advance within and between our affiliate companies, a focus on employee development and available sponsored education programs.

• Community Engagement & Care: Corporate investments in the places where our people live and work, mentoring opportunities, fundraising-matching, volunteer programs, various committees and employee resource groups, and scholarships for children of employees.

• Competitive Compensation: Short-term incentive plan and a Defined Contribution Pension Plan.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion at Emera

As one of Atlantic Canada's largest publicly traded companies, we are ranked one of Canada's Top 100 Employers, Top Employers for Young People and Top Diversity Employers. We know our success is driven by our dedicated teams and we strongly encourage applications from all qualified candidates, including persons who identify as racially visible, Indigenous, persons with disabilities, women in underrepresented roles and members of the 2SLGBTQ+ community.
Applicants from these equity groups may self-identify through the online application process. We support candidates and employees with access and accommodation needs and encourage you to let us know when you require accommodation.

Recruitment & Promotion Policy

The success of the Emera Company is driven by its people: a strong team with a shared commitment to support the Emera Company mission and values. Reporting to the Team Leader and working in a team environment, the Administrative Assistant (15 Month Term) will be responsible for providing a variety of duties from multiple programs with varying degrees of eligibility and policy requirements. Specifically, the Administrative Assistant will provide administrative support to the Provincial Program Team, supporting the accurate and timely processing, tracking and communication of program files in accordance with program policies and direction.

## Key Responsibilities

## Program Administration

• Coordinate pre-approval files and provide administrative support to the Medicare team, Medical Services Insurance (MSI) Medical Consultants and clients throughout program reviews.

• Prepare correspondence related to program approvals, denials, appeals and pre-approval decisions, ensuring current versions and supporting documentation are maintained accurately.

• Maintain tracking tools and reports for application status, decisions, outstanding actions and escalations.

• Coordinate the secure transmission and management of case documentation in accordance with privacy, confidentiality and record-management requirements.

• Support case-file review meetings through agenda and package preparation, minute taking, action-item tracking and follow-up with internal teams and the Department of Health and Wellness (DHW).

## Communication and Stakeholder Support

• Prepare clear and accurate program and provider correspondence in accordance with approved policies, procedures and operational direction.

• Respond to or route provider and Nova Scotia resident inquiries, ensure telephone messages are returned within appropriate timeframes, and escalate non-standard or sensitive matters as required.

• Establish and maintain effective working relationships with internal operational areas, program partners and external stakeholders.

## General Departmental Support

• Support the accurate and timely production and distribution of customer publications and website documents.

• Support updates to departmental procedures, business tools and administrative processes.

• Maintain general departmental files and records accurately and efficiently.

## Post Payment Administrative Support

• Compile monthly, semi-annual and annual audit and contract activity reports and maintain related Excel tracking spreadsheets.

• Maintain medical and audit records accurately and securely.

• Support audit-related system updates and the MSI service verification process associated with the Medicare Audit Plan.

## Qualifications

Experience: Minimum of three years relevant work experience. Knowledge of Medical and Pharmaceutical Terminology is an asset. Work in an office environment would be considered an asset.

## Knowledge and Skills

• Highly effective listening skills to ascertain customer's needs and determine appropriate action required for solution.

• Communicates clearly and confidently verbally and in writing to a variety of audiences.

• Demonstrates the ability to tailor information and delivery to suit the nature of the material, audience and situation. It requires excellent verbal skills to explain complex issues to customers.

## Computer Skills

• Experience working with multiple software applications (Word & Excel) including experience navigating between applications and the internet. Strong keyboarding skills and the ability to enter data with speed and precision.

## Knowledge

• Demonstrate knowledge of customer needs and various processes and procedures in own work areas as well as general understanding of processes in related work areas. Has a broad understanding of NS Provincial Programs.

## Teamwork

• Demonstrate an understanding of how the job contributes to the overall work unit and is proactive to help others.

## Program Administration

• Ability to interpret and apply documented policies, procedures and operational direction when providing OOP/OOC administrative support.

## Language Skills

• English required, bilingualism (English/French) would be considered an asset.

## What's in it for you?

What makes us a different kind of employer? Our award-winning culture, a team who really cares, unmatched training and support are all dedicated to ensuring you are set up for success.
