2241067.description:
Competition # : 49996

Department: Opportunities and Social Development

Location: HALIFAX

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: NSGEU - NSPG

Closing Date: 08-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
At the Department of Opportunities and Social Development (OSD), we are a large and diverse department providing a broad portfolio of programs and services including Child and Family Wellbeing (CFW), Employment Support Services(ESS), Income Assistance (IA), Homelessness and Supportive Housing, and Disability Support Program(DSP).

Through our services, we advocate and help vulnerable Nova Scotians be independent, self-reliant, and secure. We work collaboratively across the province with a strong dedicated network of supports and staff, to achieve desired and shared outcomes for all.

About Our Opportunity
The Central Registry Clerk provides administrative and clerical records services that support the Department's Central Registry daily operations under the direction of the Records Analyst 2. The role helps maintain integrity, accessibility, security, and accurate tracking of physical and electronic records while delivering responsive service to departmental clients.

Working within established legislation, policies, procedures, and records schedules, the Clerk creates, retrieves, returns, files, inventories, scans, and tracks records; supports storage, reactivation, disposition, litigation and information-access searches; and contributes operational knowledge and supports records digitization projects and FileNet initiatives.

Primary Accountabilities
• Monitor the Central Registry shared email account and respond to routine records enquiries and service requests from Head Office and regional offices.

• Create new physical record folders and update record categories, metadata, descriptions, locations, status, and other authorized information in FileNet or related tracking tools.

• Process file retrieval, search, charge-out, return, check-in, filing, and reactivation requests, maintaining accurate tracking information at each stage.

• Conduct assigned records searches, prepare search reports, and retrieve records in support of FOIPOP, litigation, discovery, Adoption Disclosure, and other authorized business requests.

• Prepare records for off-site storage by assigning box numbers, reviewing inventory information, supporting transmittal documentation, and updating databases and box lists.

• Assist with records disposition activities by identifying eligible files, pulling records, checking inventories, and preparing supporting administrative documentation for Records Analyst review.

• Inventory physical records, enter folder descriptions, replace damaged folders, complete shelf checks, reorganize files, and help maintain orderly and accessible storage areas.

• Scan and transcribe historical, fragile, or requested records; perform quality checks; apply approved naming practices; and maintain security during digitization work.

• Maintain routine access lists, program contacts, supply stocks, and other operational records used to deliver Central Registry services.

• Participate in cross-training, procedure updates, FileNet or electronic records management projects, and other assigned Central Registry initiatives.

• Provide backup support to other Records Clerks and perform related duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Experience
To be successful in this role, the applicant will have at least three years of related administrative, clerical, records, registry, filing, or information-management experience. An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience may be considered.

You also have:

- Experience working with physical and electronic records management systems such as FileNet.

- Experience in applying records classification and retention schedules, such as STAR/STOR.

- Experience maintaining records inventories, databases, and spreadsheets using records management tracking tools.

- Experience using office scanning equipment.

- Proficiency using Microsoft Office Suite applications and other Records Management tools, such as MS Access, Excel, Word, Outlook, SharePoint; and Adobe Acrobat.

- Strong attention to detail and the ability to enter, verify, organize, and retrieve information accurately using records management principles and best practices.

- Knowledge of records management principles and of records management lifecycles.

- Good judgement and understanding of the need to protect confidential, sensitive, and historical information.

- Exceptional customer service and communication skills for supporting staff across Head Office and regional locations.

- Organizational and time-management skills, including the ability to manage frequent interruptions and changing priorities.

- The ability to follow legislation, policies, schedules, procedures, and established work processes while identifying discrepancies for supervisor review.

- The ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment.

- The ability to regularly work with boxes weighing 40-45 pounds.

Assets include:

- Familiarity with the Government Records Act, FOIPOP Act, Public Archives Act, or related privacy and information-management requirements.

- Applying records digitization workflows.

- Experience performing records searches, records storage transfers, reactivations, dispositions, litigation holds and discovery support.

- Experience handling historical, archival, fragile, personal, confidential, or sensitive records.

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
We recognize equivalent combinations of training, education, and experience, providing opportunities for individuals with diverse backgrounds to contribute their skills and expertise. Equivalencies include, but are not limited to:

• Completion of a related 2-year diploma and 1 year of related experience

• Completion of a related 1-year diploma and 2 years of related experience

• Completion of a related Bachelor's degree

Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
• Normal work week is 35 hours/week, 7 hours/day.

• Work is primarily in the Central Registry.

• Ability to review documents or files for hours is required.

• Must be able to lift and carry boxes weighing up to 40-45 pounds and climb step ladders.

• Requires working in file rooms with records that may be dusty.

• Occasional travel to regional offices or off-site storage as required, as such a Driver's license is an asset.

What We Offer
• Career Development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career.

• Engaging workplace. Our Employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in. We have forward-thinking policies and strategies.

• Countless Career Paths.

Pay Grade: CL 13

Salary Range: $1,647.65 - $1,793.47 Bi-Weekly

Employment Equity Statement: Our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative, at all job levels, of the citizens we serve. The Government of Nova Scotia has an Employment Equity Policy, and we welcome applications from Indigenous People, African Nova Scotians, Persons of African Descent, Racialized Persons, Persons with Disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+ Persons and Women in occupations or positions where they are under-represented. If you are a member of one of these equity groups, you are encouraged to self-identify on your electronic application.

Accommodation Statement: We are committed to providing an inclusive and accessible recruitment process. Candidates may request accommodations based on any grounds protected by the Human Rights Act. If you require an accommodation throughout the recruitment process, please contact us at competitions@novascotia.ca.

Eastlink is seeking a Retail Sales Representative to join our team within our store at Halifax Shopping Centre. We are looking for a passionate individual who will help deliver great customer service and sales.

## What does the day-to-day look like?

• Everyday there are opportunities to learn more about our products, services and promotions allowing you to excel in technical expertise

• In addition, every customer interaction is an opportunity to build customer loyalty by using your expertise and product knowledge

• Our teams thrive on the chance to drive in-store sales! Hitting personal targets is fun and we will help you get there!

• Our teams are brand ambassadors, knowledge leaders and our customers trust us to help them choose the best solution for their needs

## What will you bring?

• A positive attitude and a passion for providing the best-in-class service in the telecommunications industry

• A true team player, you support your colleagues on your team or in other retail locations if needed

• You are tech savvy and have an interest in staying up to date with the newest technology

• You use your skills and personality to provide exceptional customer service, finding the right solution to each individual need

## What we offer?

Your earning potential (salary plus commission, incentive & growth share) could be $36,000 to $45,000 per year*! Or even more!

• A fun, competitive work environment where you will earn $18.15/hour plus uncapped commissions on sales

• Flexible work schedule – great for students!

• A comprehensive benefits plan that offers coverage for many different services along with an employer matched pension plan

• Opportunities to participate in frequent contests and internal promotions that recognize and promote high-performance

• Employee referral bonus when your referral is successfully hired

• The opportunity to work with leading edge technology in a progressive business, and participate in training to stay abreast with current technology

• Potential to grow your career in a multi-functional company

• A chance to work with a locally owned and operated company that is constantly evolving and will provide the support for someone who is passionate about developing their career with Eastlink

About Eastlink

Eastlink is proudly family-owned and headquartered in Halifax, Nova Scotia. After more than 50 years, we’ve grown from a small-town startup into one of Canada’s Best Managed companies without losing our entrepreneurial edge. We move fast. We try new things. We care about doing right by our customers, and we’re not afraid to take a different approach to make that happen.

Why Work With Us

We could say we’re not your typical telecom, but what makes us different is how we operate day to day. At Eastlink, we’re a tight-knit team all working toward common goals. We’re big enough to do meaningful work, but small enough that you can actually make your mark. You won’t get stuck waiting for layers of approval or years of tenure to make an impact! We believe in getting involved, speaking up, and figuring things out together. We’re always listening, learning, and adapting because our customers (and our people) expect us to. And just like we invest in our network, we invest in you, with intention and for the long run.

2239202.title: Architectural Technologist
2239202.description:
Job Title: Architectural Technologist
Location: Halifax, Nova Scotia
TP - SBG - 10098

For over 50 years, Sealand Building Group has been more than a construction company. They are dedicated partners in progress, creating controlled environments that help shape a better future for their customers, employees, and communities. Specializing in food processing, cold storage, agribusiness, distribution, and advanced manufacturing facilities, Sealand designs and builds reliable, high-performance environments that support some of Canada's most essential industries.

Sealand approaches every project with a foundation of strong values: humility in their work, honesty in their partnerships, a focus on results, kindness in their actions, and honor in their commitments. This philosophy enables them to deliver not only technically sound facilities, but also lasting relationships built on trust and shared success.

Meridia Recruitment Solutions is pleased to partner with Sealand Building Group in the recruitment of an Architectural Technologist to join their team located in Halifax, Nova Scotia.

Role Description
As an Architectural Technologist, you will play an integral role in the design and technical development of industrial and commercial construction projects. Working closely with Project Managers, consultants, engineers, trade partners, and clients, you will transform concepts into detailed construction documents while helping ensure projects are coordinated, code-compliant, and ready for successful execution.

This is an excellent opportunity for a motivated design professional who enjoys balancing technical drafting, design coordination, and project support. You will contribute throughout the project lifecycle, from preliminary planning and design development through construction and project closeout, while gaining exposure to some of Atlantic Canada's most specialized construction projects.

## Your responsibilities will include:

• Prepare conceptual layouts, design-development drawings, permit packages, and construction documents.

• Develop floor plans, elevations, sections, details, schedules, and building-envelope assemblies.

• Produce accurate as-built drawings and updated drawings at project completion.

• Work closely with design, project and site teams to support the successful transition from design into construction.

• Participate in site visits to gather field measurements, verify construction progress, help address design-related issues and support ongoing project requirements.

• Support permit submissions, regulatory approvals, and project closeout activities.

• Research and understand building codes, bylaws, space requirements, site requirements, and technical standards to support compliant and effective design solutions.

• Assist project teams with design development and related project administration activities, including support with contract and bidding documentation as required.

• Review drawings from various disciplines to identify conflicts and support effective project coordination.

• Assist with project documentation, tender packages, contract-related information, and other project support activities.

• Maintain accurate drawing logs, shop drawing records, and project documentation.

• Update and assemble as-built drawings and project closeout documentation.

• Participate in project meetings and collaborate with clients, consultants, and internal project teams.

• Support continuous improvement initiatives aimed at enhancing design and project delivery processes.

Your Qualifications
The ideal candidate is a detail-oriented Architectural Technologist who enjoys collaborating with multidisciplinary teams and contributing to projects from concept through construction. You possess strong technical drafting capabilities, sound knowledge of building construction, and a proactive approach to problem-solving.
Your qualifications include:

• Diploma or degree in Architectural Technology or a related discipline.

• Minimum of 2 years of experience in Architectural Technology, commercial construction design, or a related environment.

• Proficiency with AutoCAD and Revit.

• Knowledge of the National Building Code of Canada and applicable construction standards.

• Experience preparing construction drawings, technical documentation, and related design deliverables.

• Strong attention to detail and commitment to producing accurate, high-quality work.

• Strong communication and collaboration skills with the ability to work effectively across multidisciplinary project teams.

• Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

• Ability to proactively identify and resolve technical and design challenges in a practical and cost-effective manner.

## Assets Include:

• Experience working on industrial, food processing, cold storage, manufacturing, distribution, or specialized commercial construction projects.

• Experience in a design-build construction environment.

• Site experience and exposure to active construction environments.

## Why Join Sealand Building Group?

• Professional development, education, and training opportunities.

• A collaborative and supportive team environment.

• The opportunity to work on specialized projects that help build Canada's food industry.

• Competitive compensation and benefits.

• Quality vehicles, accommodations, and technology resources.

• Travel per diem, where applicable.

2240920.description:
Title: Senior PGIE Advisor

Employee Working Location: Partially Virtual / Hybrid (Canada)

Employment Status: Temporary Full-time (12 Months)

The Canadian Red Cross (Red Cross) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

The Senior PGIE (Protection, Gender, Inclusion and Engagement) Advisor - Enablement provides subject matter expertise and technical advisory support to strengthen the effectiveness of PGIE and Safeguarding elements within Humanitarian Services. They support all Humanitarian service lines by offering technical guidance, capacity building, training, and by developing PGIE and Safeguarding tools and standards. The role helps assess program and service needs, recommends operational improvements, and ensures alignment with organizational priorities and community needs. It also monitors performance, supports compliance, and facilitates collaboration across stakeholders to drive continuous improvement and impact.

## In this role, you will :

• Provide subject matter expertise and strategic and technical guidance to strengthen program/service effectiveness, ensuring alignment with best practices, organizational priorities, and national society needs.

• Assess program/service gaps, analyze trends, and provide recommendations for operational enhancements to improve service delivery, accessibility, and impact.

• Serve as a key advisor to internal teams at national and provincial levels, fostering collaboration and knowledge-sharing.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with government agencies, nonprofits, national societies, Indigenous organizations, and other key stakeholders to support service delivery.

• Provide technical expertise, training, and mentorship to internal teams and external partners to enhance their capacity in program delivery.

• Contribute to financial reporting and compliance with funding requirements, while ensuring transparency and accountability to partners.

• Develop and implement training materials, toolkits, and resources to support program effectiveness and knowledge transfer.

• Advise on culturally safe and inclusive approaches to ensure equitable program/service access for diverse communities.

• Lead program/service evaluation efforts by analyzing performance metrics, community feedback, and impact assessments to inform decision-making.

• Ensure compliance with funding agreements, regulatory requirements, and organizational policies, providing advisory support to mitigate risks and improve accountability.

• Contribute to the development of performance reports, dashboards, and impact narratives for leadership and external stakeholders.

• Guide the development and execution of relevant strategies that foster meaningful participation, co-design, and inclusive decision-making.

• Work with communities to identify evolving needs, emerging challenges, and opportunities for program/service enhancement.

• Advocate for community-driven solutions, ensuring program strategies reflect cultural, social, and economic considerations.

## What we are looking for :

• Qualifications include a 3-year college diploma or university degree in social sciences, community development, Indigenous studies, Gender and Social Justice, Feminist studies or a related field. An equivalent combination of education and experience related to protection, diversity and inclusion, child protection, gender equality, anti-racism and decolonial approaches, and/or SGBV programming would be an asset.

• A minimum of 6-9 years' experience in humanitarian assistance, international or community development, public administration or other related field.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint) and SharePoint.

• Ability to identify complex problems, analyze interrelated factors, assess and mitigate risks, and develop solutions using specialized skills.

• Communication and influence skills to gather perspectives, understand needs, and present information to reach consensus, often in somewhat sensitive situations.

• Knowledge of community engagement principles, participatory approaches, and capacity-building techniques.

• Experience working with diverse communities, including Indigenous, rural, and underserved populations.

• Fluency in English is required; Fluency in French and or Spanish is considered a strong asset. Additional languages relevant to the communities and regions served by the organization are considered an asset.

## Working Conditions :

• The majority of the work is conducted virtually, with possibility of deployment and on-site meetings.

• As we work with and support people (managers, colleagues, beneficiaries/customers, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.

• Eligibility to work in Canada: At this time, we welcome applications from candidates eligible to work in Canada. If you are not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada, we encourage you to carefully review your visa to find out whether you are eligible to work in the job you are considering applying for. Refer to our FAQ for more information.

• If you are selected for this role, you will be required to complete a successful pre-employment screening process which includes a satisfactory Enhanced Police Information Check (E-PIC).

About Us
We are currently hiring for Spare Winter Equipment Operators in Richmond County and Inverness South at the following bases: St. Peters and Martinique (Zone 5) and Inverness South, Port Hawkesbury, Ashfield, Judique (Zone 6). Work may be available at any of these locations. Please quote the competition number and the Zone(s) you are applying for as noted above on your application.

About Our OpportunitySuccessful candidates will begin with two weeks of paid training designed to build the knowledge and skills required for effective snow and ice control operations. Following training, you will complete 45 hours of paid plowing experience under the guidance of an experienced Operator. Candidates must also successfully complete a driving assessment using a one-person-truck-plow equipped with a front plow, wing, and salt controls. This is a spare position, and hours of work are not guaranteed. Employees are called in as operational needs require. There may be an opportunity to participate in the Winter Wage Guarantee, which provides guaranteed work for a minimum of two weeks and may continue for the duration of the winter season. If placed on the Winter Wage Guarantee, the following will apply:
• Guaranteed 90 hours of pay every two weeks

• $0.95/per hour premium

• Opportunities for overtime

• Scheduled days off (2 days bi-weekly)

You are responsible for operating snow removal equipment such as snowplows, graders, and loaders. This includes general maintenance of the equipment, pre-and-post trip inspections, and daily logs. You may also be required to perform other work, such as maintaining signs, road surface repairs and traffic control.

Qualifications and Experience
Two years of experience or an acceptable equivalent of education, training, and relevant experience.

Minimum of Class III license with air brake endorsement.

Reading and writing skills are required to understand department documentation and to complete daily logs, inspection reports, etc.

The following is not required but considered helpful:

• A professional driving course from a recognized truck driving training facility

• Knowledge of hydraulic systems and mechanical skills

• Training completed at any accredited heavy/commercial equipment training institute

• Previous experience driving a manual transmission, operating trucks with salt and plow equipment, and/or knowledge of salt spreading systems

You are flexible, self-motivated, and comfortable working in all weather conditions. You are respectful and understand the value of good customer service. You will be working around environmental hazards, various traffic conditions and occasional work performed in a mechanical environment.

Additional Information
Applicants who are unable to apply online are invited to stop by the local Area Office located at 1420 Highway 4, Port Hawkesbury to complete a paper application. Staff will be on site between 8:30 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. Monday to Friday to assist you. Please bring a current copy of your Drivers Abstract.

Candidates selected for a road test, interview and a physical must be available to complete these in the local area at determined dates and times. Testing will be done on an automatic or manual transmission truck dependent on area requirements.

Work may be available at any of these locations. Please quote the competition number and the Zone(s) you are applying for as noted above on your application.

About Our OpportunitySuccessful candidates will begin with two weeks of paid training designed to build the knowledge and skills required for effective snow and ice control operations. Following training, you will complete 45 hours of paid plowing experience under the guidance of an experienced Operator. Candidates must also successfully complete a driving assessment using a one-person-truck-plow equipped with a front plow, wing, and salt controls. This is a spare position, and hours of work are not guaranteed. Employees are called in as operational needs require. There may be an opportunity to participate in the Winter Wage Guarantee, which provides guaranteed work for a minimum of two weeks and may continue for the duration of the winter season. If placed on the Winter Wage Guarantee, the following will apply:
• Guaranteed 90 hours of pay every two weeks

• $0.95/per hour premium

• Opportunities for overtime

• Scheduled days off (2 days bi-weekly)

You are responsible for operating snow removal equipment such as snowplows, graders, and loaders. This includes general maintenance of the equipment, pre-and-post trip inspections, and daily logs. You may also be required to perform other work, such as maintaining signs, road surface repairs and traffic control.

Qualifications and Experience
Two years of experience or an acceptable equivalent of education, training, and relevant experience.

Minimum of Class III license with air brake endorsement.

Reading and writing skills are required to understand department documentation and to complete daily logs, inspection reports, etc.

The following is not required but considered helpful:

• A professional driving course from a recognized truck driving training facility

• Knowledge of hydraulic systems and mechanical skills

• Training completed at any accredited heavy/commercial equipment training institute

• Previous experience driving a manual transmission, operating trucks with salt and plow equipment, and/or knowledge of salt spreading systems

You are flexible, self-motivated, and comfortable working in all weather conditions. You are respectful and understand the value of good customer service. You will be working around environmental hazards, various traffic conditions and occasional work performed in a mechanical environment.

Additional Information
Applicants who are unable to apply online are invited to stop by the local Area Office located at 151 Keltic Drive, Sydney River to complete a paper application. Staff will be on site between 8:30 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. Monday to Friday to assist you. Please bring a current copy of your Drivers Abstract.

Candidates selected for a road test, interview and a physical must be available to complete these in the local area at determined dates and times. Testing will be done on an automatic or manual transmission truck dependent on area requirements.

Pay Grade: EQP OPER

Salary Range: $29.12 Hourly

2241198.title: Planning Coordinator
2241198.description:
The Opportunity

Company, Department: Nova Scotia Power, Distribution Planning

Location: Sackville, Nova Scotia

Type of Employment: Full time, Permanent

Salary: $30.48 per hour as per IBEW Collective Agreement Local 1928

Closing Date: October 9th, 2026

Reference: 2026-5914

We are looking for a Planning Coordinator to join our team. Reporting to the Planning Coordinator Supervisor, you will a team of professionals at our Sackville location.

Key elements of this role include:

As Planning Coordinator you will:

• Submit and monitor HRM/DOT permit requests, locates for water, sewer, gas, Aliant, Rogers, 360 Network, Environmental permits, engineering approval, issuing of joint use Aliant and CATV forms, creation of work orders when required, and release/booking for final staking when to-dos are completed.

• Check and update customer easements through Property Online, follow the planned outage process, and ensure account, project and task numbers are accurate for the work being performed.

• Manage underground locate requirements, such as updating work orders with diagrams, returning completed forms to customers, and submitting internal & external cable locates when required.

• Request quotes from external contractors for services such as tree trimming & Grade 1 Assessments when required, quoting these services, and releasing the work at various stages in the work order cycle.

• Be responsible for Make Ready and the Aliant work processes and month end invoicing to Aliant and CATV Companies.

• Also, process and calculate attachment fees related to contributed lines, credit in lieu of overhead, and developer rebates.

• You will need to manage the quoting process of work orders.

• You will be responsible for your personal safety and that of your co-workers by observing and ensuring compliance with all Occupational Health and Safety Rules and Regulations.

• You must be flexible and be available for overtime during peak seasons and after hour emergency service restoration.

These skills will make you successful:

• Grade XII education and/or a certificate, degree in business from a post-secondary institution and have a minimum five years' experience working in a customer service and operational environment with experience coordinating internal and external resources to meet productivity standards.

• Strong mathematical and analytical skills with great attention to detail as well as proven organizational skills are required.

• You have a proven track record of providing exceptional service to customers.

• The ideal candidate is able to demonstrate expertise in using NS Power's work management system (Maximo), Orcom CIS, Infoview, SharePoint, ViryaNet, Smartsheet, Oracle, Adobe suite, Property Online, Info-Excavation or equivalent work management experience.

• A high level of proficiency with MS Office, particularly MS Excel would be required.

• You have experience communicating complex information to customers in writing, phone and in person while maintaining a positive customer experience.

• The successful candidate must have knowledge of the Aliant Work Request and Joint Use process, Make Ready process, job pricing/estimation and financial calculations for contributed line rebates or equivalent experience would be considered.

• Experience with as well as familiarity with NS Power's processes for distribution line work management, make ready third-party attachment, and contributed line rebates would be considered an asset.

We understand that experience comes in many forms, and we're dedicated to adding new perspectives to the team. So, if your experience is close to what we've listed above, please consider applying.

Please Note: This is a bargaining unit position. External applicants will only be considered if there are no qualified bargaining unit candidates.

Learn more about our culture and values

At the Emera Group of Companies, you'll be part of an inclusive, respectful workplace where everyone is welcomed and supported. Come build a career as unique as you are: making an impact from Atlantic Canada to the world. Your experience and perspective will help us to safely deliver cleaner, more reliable energy to our customers. If working in an innovative environment, challenging yourself, and shaping a cleaner energy future inspires you, we want to hear from you. Apply by October 9th, 2026 and let us know why this role is right for you.

The perks of joining our team? We offer:

• Health & Wellbeing: A comprehensive benefits plan, 24/7 access to virtual health care services for you and your family through Dialogue, access to a free on-site fitness centre, Employee and Family Assistance Program, parental leave top-up plan and wellness benefits.

• Grow Your Career: Opportunities to advance within and between our affiliate companies, a focus on employee development and available sponsored education programs.

• Community Engagement & Care: Corporate investments in the places where our people live and work, mentoring opportunities, fundraising-matching & volunteer programs, various committees and employee resource groups, and scholarships for children of employees.

• Competitive Compensation: A comprehensive benefits plan and a Defined Contribution Pension Plan.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion at Emera

As one of Atlantic Canada's largest publicly traded companies, we are ranked one of Canada's Top 100 Employers, Top Employers for Young People and Top Diversity Employers. We know our success is driven by our dedicated teams and we strongly encourage applications from all qualified candidates, including persons who identify as racially visible, Indigenous, persons with disabilities, women in underrepresented roles and members of the 2SLGBTQ+ community.
Applicants from these equity groups may self-identify through the online application process. We support candidates and employees with access and accommodation needs and encourage you to let us know when you require accommodation.

Recruitment & Promotion Policy

The success of the Emera Company is driven by its people: a strong team with a shared commitment to support the Emera Company mission and values. The purpose of our recruitment policy is to provide a consistent framework to support fair and equitable attraction, hiring, and retention of the best talent for vacant positions. We are dedicated to maintaining a fair hiring process that provides equitable opportunities to all our applicants and is guided by our company values.

If you have any questions about this opportunity or if you are experiencing any technical difficulty with the application process, please email careers@nspower.ca

2240103.title: Manager, Business Development & Pricing
2240103.description:
Manager, Business Development & Pricing
Halifax, Nova Scotia
Reference # JL-STE-10102

As Atlantic Canada's largest regional law firm, Stewart McKelvey is committed to delivering exceptional legal services and innovative solutions to clients across Canada and beyond. With six offices and a growing national reach, the firm continues to evolve its approach to business development, client service, and commercial operations to support long-term growth.

On behalf of our client, we are seeking a Manager, Business Development & Pricing to join Stewart McKelvey's Commercial Operations team. Think of this role less as closing deals and more as building the engine behind growth: you won't be pitching clients yourself, but you will be the person equipping the firm's lawyers with the strategy, tools, and structure they need to win and grow business. A solid grounding in business development and marketing principles is essential, but it will be applied through strategy, systems, and enablement rather than direct client-facing sales.

Reporting to the Director, Commercial Operations, this role will serve as a key partner to firm leadership, supporting business development strategy execution, pricing initiatives, proposal management, CRM optimization, and commercial operations across the firm. This is an exciting opportunity for a collaborative professional who enjoys bringing structure to complex initiatives, leading through change, and helping professionals achieve growth objectives.

## The Opportunity

As Manager, Business Development & Pricing, you will play a pivotal role in supporting the firm's strategic growth initiatives. Acting as a trusted advisor to lawyers, practice groups, and internal stakeholders, you will help translate strategy into action by driving business development programs, managing pricing workflows, supporting proposal development, and contributing to a high-performing team. This role is highly collaborative in nature and requires an individual who can move comfortably between practice areas, communicate clearly, anticipate needs, manage competing priorities, and provide thoughtful solutions in a fast-paced professional services environment. You will provide leadership to a team of professionals while working closely with departments across the firm's offices.

## Key Responsibilities:

• Support the implementation of firm-wide business development strategies and growth initiatives.

• Partner with lawyers and practice groups to enhance client development activities and identify opportunities for growth.

• Coordinate and manage pricing activities, including annual rate reviews, client pricing arrangements, alternative fee arrangements (AFAs), and RFP pricing submissions.

• Collaborate with Finance and firm leadership to develop pricing recommendations and support informed decision-making.

• Lead and support proposal and RFP development, ensuring high-quality submissions that align with client objectives.

• Oversee the firm's CRM strategy and adoption efforts, leveraging data to support business development planning and decision-making.

• Drive process improvements and operational efficiencies across business development and pricing functions.

• Support change management initiatives related to emerging technologies, evolving client expectations, and business development best practices.

• Prepare reports, presentations, and recommendations for senior leadership and internal stakeholders.

• Serve as a key resource for lawyers and internal clients, responding to requests with professionalism, urgency, and sound judgment.

• Coach, mentor, and develop team members while fostering a collaborative and service-focused culture.

## The Ideal Candidate

You are a planner and implementer who enjoys bringing people, processes, and priorities together. You are service-oriented, highly organized, and naturally collaborative, with the ability to build credibility and influence across diverse stakeholder groups. You thrive in environments where responsiveness, professionalism, and quality matter. You are comfortable leading teams through change, and balancing strategic objectives with day-to-day operational demands.

Most importantly, you are someone who anticipates needs, approaches challenges with solutions, and can be relied upon to deliver results.

## Qualifications

• Post-secondary education in Business, Marketing, Commerce, Communications, Finance, or a related discipline.

• Experience in business development, commercial operations, client service, project management, pricing, account management, marketing, or a related function.

• Experience working within a professional services environment is considered a strong asset.

• Previous people leadership experience, including coaching, mentoring, or managing direct reports.

• Strong project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.

• Excellent written communication and proposal-writing abilities.

• Demonstrated ability to influence and collaborate effectively across multiple stakeholder groups.

• Strong business acumen and comfort working with financial and operational information.

• Experience implementing CRM or similar systems would be considered an asset.

• Proven ability to lead teams through organizational change and continuous improvement initiatives.

• Exceptional organizational skills, attention to detail, and problem-solving abilities.

## Why Join Stewart McKelvey?

This is an opportunity to join one of Atlantic Canada's most respected professional services organizations at a time of significant growth and evolution. You will have the opportunity to lead firm-wide business development and pricing initiatives while working alongside a collaborative leadership team committed to innovation, continuous improvement, and exceptional client service.

Stewart McKelvey offers a competitive compensation and benefits package, including:

• Comprehensive health and dental benefits

• RRSP or pension matching program

• Professional development opportunities

• Collaborative and supportive team environment

• Flexible approach to in-office work across the firm's office network

If you are a commercially minded leader who enjoys bringing strategy to life, supporting teams through change, and helping professionals achieve meaningful growth, we would welcome the opportunity to connect with you.

## To express interest in this opportunity please apply online directly here.

If you have any questions, please contact Kate Spares, Recruitment Specialist, at kspares@kbrs.ca or Jeff Lanthier, Partner, at jlanthier@kbrs.ca. If you require accommodation to participate in the recruitment process, please let us know.

To learn more about Meridia Recruitment Solutions, our job opportunities, and career advice we invite you to explore our site and subscribe for career alerts.

2234383.title: Technical Drafting Manager
2234383.description:
Job Title: Technical Drafting Manager
Location: Dartmouth, Nova Scotia
TP - FPS - 9859

Meridia Recruitment Solutions is pleased to partner with Babcock & Wilcox FPS inc. in the search for a Technical Drafting Manager to join their team in Dartmouth, Nova Scotia.

FPS is a Canadian-based company that has supplied system hardware, software, and services to international customers for more than 40 years. As a wholly owned subsidiary of Babcock & Wilcox Enterprises Inc., FPS is recognized as a world-class provider of control solutions and instrumentation serving electrical utilities, pulp and paper facilities, and petrochemical operations around the globe.

## Role Description

Babcock & Wilcox FPS is seeking an individual who can assume leadership of a well-established drafting department as part of a planned succession for the current Technical Drafting Manager. To support a successful transition, the successful candidate will benefit from a structured onboarding and knowledge-transfer period with the retiring manager, ensuring continuity of team leadership, processes, standards, and institutional knowledge.

Reporting to the Vice President, Product Engineering, and supported from a technical perspective by the Mechanical Drafting Lead, you will provide overall leadership for a multidisciplinary drafting team while serving as the critical link between the Engineering and Drafting departments. You will oversee all drafting operations, ensuring quality, consistency, efficiency, and alignment with project objectives.

## Key Responsibilities

• Manage and prioritize all drafting workload, ensuring alignment with project schedules and engineering deliverables.

• Assign and coordinate drafting tasks across a team of CAD technicians.

• Lead a drafting group of approximately seven personnel.

• Interface with engineers to review markups, clarify requirements, and resolve drawing-related issues.

• Review electrical, cabinet layout, and Boolean logic drawings for clarity, accuracy, and compliance with FPS standards.

• Ensure adherence to company drafting standards, naming conventions, and revision control practices.

• Oversee drawing quality prior to acceptance and release.

• Coordinate cross-disciplinary drafting activities between electrical and mechanical teams.

• Conduct employee performance reviews and support team development.

• Review and approve vacation requests and manage team availability.

• Support onboarding and training of drafting personnel, including participation in a structured transition from the current Drafting Manager.

## Ideal Qualifications

• Electrical Engineering Technology diploma or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Demonstrated experience with electrical and control system drawings, including PLC cabinet layouts and wiring diagrams.

• Understanding of electrical principles, industrial control systems, PLCs, and Boolean logic.

• Experience reviewing engineering markups and technical documentation.

• Strong organizational, communication, and workload management skills.

• Previous supervisory, team lead, mentoring, or coordination experience within a drafting or technical environment is preferred.

## Preferred Qualifications

• Drafting experience in AutoCAD (2D).

• Experience within industrial control systems, power generation, process industries, or related sectors.

• Familiarity with drafting standards, QA/QC processes, and document control systems.

## Why Join Babcock & Wilcox FPS?

• Leadership Opportunity: Lead an established technical team that plays a critical role in delivering projects to customers around the world.

• Career Impact: Influence drafting standards, workflows, and continuous improvement initiatives across the organization.

• Stable, Global Business: Join a respected company with more than four decades of success and the backing of Babcock & Wilcox Enterprises.

• Collaborative Environment: Work closely with engineering, manufacturing, and project teams while mentoring future drafting talent.

• Knowledge Transfer & Mentorship: Gain firsthand insight into established practices, processes, and team leadership through a structured transition period with the incumbent manager.

• Comprehensive Benefits: RRSP Co-Contribution Program, Health Spending Account, Comprehensive Medical and Dental Coverage, Post-Secondary Education Assistance for Children, and Gym Membership Support.

To express interest in this opportunity please apply online by clicking "Apply Now" below.

For more information contact Thomas Pugh, Partner, at 902-818-4506 and tpugh@kbrs.ca or Rick Neima, Senior Consultant at 902-488-2534 and rneima@kbrs.ca, or please apply online by clicking the "Apply Now" button below. If you require accommodation to participate in the recruitment process, please let us know.

2240875.title: Quality Assurance Specialist (Program Admin Officer 3)
2240875.employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
2240875.description:
Competition # : 49945

Department: Education & Early Childhood Development

Location: HALIFAX

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: NSGEU - NSPG

Closing Date: 06-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
The Department of Education and Early Childhood Development is leading the transformation of the early years and public education system in Nova Scotia. We are doing this by working closely with our partners in education to design innovative curriculum and facilitate excellence in teaching and learning to ensure an inclusive education experience.

About Our Opportunity
The Quality Assurance Specialist plays a critical role in supporting the delivery of high-quality, safe, and inclusive early learning and childcare services across Nova Scotia. Responsible for monitoring compliance with licensing and safety standards, auditing programs and policies for alignment with departmental expectations, and responding to complaints or concerns raised by families, service providers, or the public. Contributes to the ongoing education and capacity building of providers by promoting awareness and understanding of standards, policies, and best practices.

Through inspections, program reviews, and policy oversight, ensures that early learning environments foster positive outcomes for children and meet the expectations set by the Department of Education and Early Childhood Development.

Primary Accountabilities

## Partner Engagement and Support:

• Provide guidance, consultation, and training to childcare providers and early years centers to enhance understanding of licensing requirements and support quality improvement.

• Offer expert advice on policy development, inclusive practices, and service enhancements to help programs meet the developmental needs of all children.

• Facilitate education and outreach efforts through presentations, training sessions, and direct support to ensure providers remain informed and compliant.

## Licensing and Compliance:

• Coordinate and conduct inspections of early learning and childcare facilities, including new sites, renovations and expansions, to assess compliance with provincial legislation, licensing, health, and safety standards.

• Review and evaluate proposals, architectural plans, and physical environments to determine readiness for licensing and adherence to departmental policy.

• Uses a risk-based licensing approach that prioritizes areas of greatest impact on the health and safety of children

• Prepare inspection reports, assess risk to child safety, and issue compliance requirements; follow up to support corrective actions and continuous improvement.

• Monitor facilities for license issuance or renewal, investigate deficiencies, and make recommendations for enforcement as needed.

• Support childcare centres in achieving voluntary compliance; educate centre Directors and Staff on Regulations and compliance standards.

Primary accountabilities (cont'd)

## Program Monitoring and Improvement:

• Conduct audits of licensed childcare programs to assess service quality, policy alignment, and compliance with departmental standards and federal/provincial funding requirements.

• Identify areas of non-compliance, evaluate associated risks, and issue requirements to mitigate risk and ensure corrective action.

• Monitor and evaluate program effectiveness in supporting children's development and meeting diverse family needs; recommend improvements based on findings.

• Support development and implementation of tools, resources, and protocols to promote consistent quality assurance across programs.

• Assist in the rollout and monitoring of departmental initiatives and early childhood development

## Complaint Resolution and Investigations:

• Receive, document, and investigate complaints from families, community members, or partners regarding licensed programs or potential non-compliance.

• Analyze reports from providers, determine the level of risk, and evaluate facility response plans to ensure issues are resolved and risks mitigated.

• Collaborate with other departmental staff to determine appropriate responses and follow-up actions and ensure transparent, fair, and timely resolution processes that center the well-being of children.

Qualifications and Experience
To be considered for this opportunity, you have a bachelor's degree in a related field (e.g. Education) and a minimum of 5 years experience in an early learning and child-care setting, or a work environment with a focus on policy and regulations. An equivalent combination of education and/or experience may be considered.

In addition, you possess the following:

• Excellent communication skills, interpersonal, verbal, and written, including the ability to write effectively.

• Strong collaboration and facilitation skills, including developing and maintaining collaborative working relationships with stakeholders and staff.

• Effective time management skills in relation to managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment demonstrating sound judgement, attention to detail and initiative.

• Ability to analyze procedural and/or program problems, develop, recommend, and implement solutions as needed.

• Excellent initiative with a focus on continuous improvement.

• Ability to work effectively independently and within a team environment, and promote equity, diversity, and inclusion in the workplace.

• This position requires access to a reliable motor vehicle and a valid driver's license. Offer of employment is contingent on an appropriate background such as criminal records check and child abuse register.

## Assets considered for a Program Admin Officer 3 role include:

• Working knowledge of programs and services offered by various branches within the Department of Education and Early Childhood Development.

• Prior experience working with current legislation, regulations, and policies with knowledge of government operations, programming, and educational frameworks.

• Bilingualism (English and French)

We may assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
• Standard office environment with regular computer and phone use.

• Occasional tight deadlines or competing priorities.

• May involve handling inquiries of a sensitive or confidential nature.

Additional Information
This competition is being leveraged to fill a full-time permanent position In Halifax, Nova Scotia. Regular travel will be needed across the province.

What We Offer
• Career development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career

• Engaging workplace: our employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in, we have forward-thinking policies and strategies

• Countless career paths

• Department specific flexible working schedules

Pay Grade: PR 13

Salary Range: $2,805.63 - $3,410.48 Bi-Weekly

Employment Equity Statement: Our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative, at all job levels, of the citizens we serve. The Government of Nova Scotia has an Employment Equity Policy, and we welcome applications from Indigenous People, African Nova Scotians, Persons of African Descent, Racialized Persons, Persons with Disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+ Persons and Women in occupations or positions where they are under-represented. If you are a member of one of these equity groups, you are encouraged to self-identify on your electronic application.

Accommodation Statement: We are committed to providing an inclusive and accessible recruitment process. Candidates may request accommodations based on any grounds protected by the Human Rights Act. If you require an accommodation throughout the recruitment process, please contact us at competitions@novascotia.ca.

2240992.title: Manager HR Information Management
2240992.employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
2240992.description:
Competition # : 49861

Department: Public Service Commission

Location: HALIFAX

Type of Employment: Term

Union Status: Exclusion - Non Union - NSPG

Closing Date: 07-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
The Public Service Commission (PSC) is government's human resources organization supporting departments, agencies, and employees to deliver programs and services to Nova Scotians. We are committed to building a collaborative and inclusive public service grounded in respect, integrity, diversity, accountability, and the public good.

The PSC establishes human resource policies, programs, standards, and procedures, and provides direction, advice, and support to departments to ensure consistent, effective application across government.

We are focused on the current and future needs of the provincial workforce to ensure the public service is equipped to meet the demands of a growing and changing province.

For more information on the Public Service Commission, please visit the following link: https://beta.novascotia.ca/government/public-service-commission

About Our Opportunity
As the Manager, HR Information Management, you will lead the governance, security, quality, and appropriate use of strategic human resources information assets across the Public Service Commission.

Reporting to the Director, Workforce Intelligence and Systems, you will lead a professional team responsible for HR information systems, information governance, data quality, records management, and related information services. You will oversee system improvements and information management practices that support HR service delivery, workforce planning, policy development, reporting, analysis, and informed decision-making.

Working with senior leaders, departments, technology teams, corporate partners, and service providers, you will establish priorities, manage risks, and ensure HR information and systems are reliable, secure, and managed in accordance with legislation, policy, and privacy requirements.

You will also support continuous improvement by maintaining an understanding of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and automation, and exploring how they can responsibly streamline processes and improve services.

Primary Accountabilities
• Strategic Leadership and Service Direction: Sets priorities and provides strategic direction for HR information systems, information governance, records management, and related services. Aligns team plans and resources with organizational and government priorities.

• Information Governance and Data Quality: Leads frameworks, standards, and processes that support the accuracy, reliability, consistency, security, and appropriate use of workforce information.

• HR Information Systems Management: Oversees system enhancements, upgrades, integrations, support models, and service improvements to ensure HR technologies meet organizational and user needs.

• Privacy, Security and Risk Management: Leads security frameworks and controls for HR information. Ensures practices align with legislation, policy, privacy requirements, and the Public Service Commission's security and risk profile.

• Records and Information Management: Oversees the Commission's records management program and ensures information is collected, used, retained, protected, and disposed of in accordance with legislative and policy requirements.

• Technology, Innovation and Continuous Improvement: Provides leadership for the continuous improvement of HR information systems and information management services. Maintains an understanding of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and automation, and supports the responsible exploration of opportunities to streamline existing processes, reduce manual effort, and improve service delivery while considering privacy, security, information governance, and operational risk.

• Partnerships, Advice and Organizational Enablement: Builds relationships with senior leaders, departments, corporate partners, service providers, and vendors. Provides advice on complex information management and technology matters and leads communication, consultation, training, and education activities.

Title: Senior Coordinator, Business Support and Program Management

Employee Working Location: Partially Virtual / Hybrid (Canada)

Employment Status: Permanent Full-time

The Canadian Red Cross (CRC) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

## In this role, you will:

• Support the Manager, Training in the planning, implementation, coordination, and continuous improvement of RR&R learning, training, and capacity-building initiatives. This role is responsible for maintaining the systems, processes, standards, and infrastructure that support training delivery across RR&R teams, including Indigenous Programs, Youth Engagement, Disaster Risk Reduction-Climate Change Adaptation, and Psychological First Aid programming.

• The role serves as a central coordination point for education and training operations, including learning pathways, scheduling systems, quality standards, data collection, reporting, and continuous improvement initiatives.

• Support the planning, execution, and monitoring of programs/services, ensuring adherence to timelines, budgets, and quality standards.

• Assist with logistics, procurement, and administrative needs to facilitate smooth operations.

• Organize and facilitate meetings, workshops, and key activities, ensuring proper documentation and follow-up.

• Develop and maintain systems and documentation to ensure consistency across program/service line processes and procedures.

• Maintain team calendars, coordinate meetings, prepare agendas, issue minutes, and distribute materials.

• Support the development and implementation of virtual and in-person training for staff and volunteers involved in program/service delivery, and public-facing webinars.

• Collect, analyze, and report on key program/service indicators to support decision-making and continuous improvement.

• Assist in resource management, including tracking budgets, procurement needs, and reporting requirements.

• Prepare regular program reports and assist with data collection for assessments and program/service evaluations.

• Identify areas for process improvement within the program and service delivery framework and recommend changes.

## What we are looking for:

• Qualifications include a minimum of 4-5 years' experience and a 1-2 year post-secondary certification/diploma and/or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Experience in program or service coordination, including the development and implementation of program or service plans, budgets, and evaluation activities.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint) and SharePoint is required.

• Ability to manage program schedules and timelines; prioritize tasks, track progress, and meet deadlines.

• Skills to identify and resolve issues, by applying standard procedures and functional or organizational knowledge.

• Communication skills, diplomacy and empathy to interpret information and deliver advice, clarify clients or stakeholder needs, offer solutions, and resolve escalations in new or somewhat sensitive situations

• Ability to demonstrate compassion, empathy and understanding for individuals with differing cognitive and physical abilities.

• Ability to understand data analytics to assess performance metrics and generate reports for management.

• Fluency in English is required; French is an asset.

## Working Conditions:

• Travel may be required.

• All teams contribute to emergency response efforts directly or indirectly.

• All CRC roles are required to adapt work and priorities to support emergency response efforts, be present in person as required to support service delivery and deploy to emergency responses when appropriate and/or required (personnel availability and request for exceptions will be discussed with line management).

• For CRC roles that are assigned a function in the Emergency Relief operational structure (in field and virtual), personnel may be required to be part of an on-call roster and be available for scheduled on-call work.

• As we work with and support people (managers, colleagues, beneficiaries/customers, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.

• Eligibility to work in Canada. At this time, we welcome applications from candidates eligible to work in Canada. If you are not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada, we encourage you to carefully review your visa to find out whether you are eligible to work in the job you are considering applying for. Refer to our FAQ for more information.

• If you are selected for this role, you will be required to complete a successful pre-employment screening process which includes a satisfactory Enhanced Police Information Check (E-PIC).

2235318.title: Marketing Specialist, Digital Media
2235318.description:
## Marketing Specialist, Digital Media
Burnside, Nova Scotia
Reference #JL-CSP-9883

Cleve's Source for Sports is a locally owned, Atlantic Canadian sporting goods retailer that's been outfitting Maritimers since opening its first store in downtown Halifax in 1947. With locations across Nova Scotia and New Brunswick, we combine hometown roots and expert service with the buying power of Canada's largest sporting goods buying group. We're now investing seriously in our digital presence, and we're looking for the person to own it.

## The Role

Reporting to the Director of Strategic Development, the Marketing Specialist, Digital Media will lead the creation and execution of engaging digital content that strengthens Cleve's online presence and connects with communities across Atlantic Canada.

This is a hands-on, creative, high-visibility role. You will touch everything Cleve's does online - the content on TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook, our Google presence across all 16 stores, and the voice of the brand in every comment and review. You'll personally shoot and edit short-form video every week, and you'll spend real time on the road: monthly visits to our Halifax-area stores, quarterly visits across Nova Scotia, and twice-yearly trips to Yarmouth and New Brunswick stores, batch-filming content with our retail staff. Between visits, you'll coach staff across the chain to capture raw footage and turn their clips into publishable content. This is not a desk-only strategy job - you are the creator, editor, publisher, and community manager, with the mandate and support of ownership behind you.

## Duties & Responsibilities:

• Own the content strategy, creation, and publishing process across TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook.

• Develop, film, edit, and publish engaging short-form video content on an ongoing basis.

• Stay informed on emerging social media trends and identify opportunities to increase audience engagement.

• Travel regularly to Cleve's retail locations to capture content including staff profiles, product education, community partnerships, store highlights, and event coverage.

• Partner with store teams to capture user-generated content and transform raw footage into polished, brand-aligned social media assets.

• Ensure a strong local presence across all content through geotagging, community partnerships, and sport-specific engagement strategies.

• Manage and maintain Google Business Profiles for all store locations, including monitoring and responding to customer reviews.

• Collaborate with the Marketing team to support major retail campaigns, seasonal promotions, and special events.

• Monitor social media and digital performance metrics, providing ongoing insights and monthly reporting to leadership.

• Maintain a consistent and authentic brand voice across all digital channels.

## Qualifications & Experience:

The ideal candidate is a creative storyteller with strong technical skills and a passion for connecting brands with communities.

You bring:

• 1-3 years of experience managing business social media accounts, including TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook.

• Demonstrated experience creating engaging digital content for brands, organizations, or businesses.

• Strong photography, videography, and video editing skills, with a portfolio showcasing your work.

• Confidence appearing on camera and creating authentic, audience-focused content.

• Excellent written communication and copywriting skills.

• Strong understanding of social media analytics, engagement strategies, and content performance metrics.

• A proactive, entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.

• A valid driver's license and willingness to travel regularly throughout Nova Scotia and New Brunswick.

• Post-secondary education in Marketing, Communications, Digital Media, or a related field is considered an asset.

• A passion for sports, recreation, and community engagement is highly desirable.

## Why Join Cleve's?

Joining Cleve's means becoming part of a respected Atlantic Canadian brand with deep community roots and exciting growth plans.

In addition to a competitive compensation package, employees enjoy:

• Comprehensive health and dental benefits.

• Employee discounts across all Cleve's locations.

• Mileage reimbursement and travel expense coverage, where applicable.

• The opportunity to work directly with leadership and influence the evolution of the company's digital presence.

• Creative ownership and autonomy in a highly visible role.

• Professional growth opportunities as the digital marketing function continues to expand.

## To express interest in this opportunity please apply online directly here.

If you have any questions, please contact Kate Spares, Recruitment Specialist, at kspares@kbrs.ca or Jeff Lanthier, Partner, at jlanthier@kbrs.ca. If you require accommodation to participate in the recruitment process, please let us know.

Meridia Recruitment Solutions connects leading organizations with top talent by building strong relationships and creating ideal matches with candidates because we are only successful when you are. We appreciate your interest in this opportunity.

To learn more about Meridia Recruitment Solutions, our job opportunities, and career advice we invite you to explore our site and subscribe for career alerts.

2240981.description:
Requisition ID: 2631

Why Choose IMP Aerospace & Defence:
IMP Aerospace & Defence is not only one of the leading companies in the Aerospace field, but we are also one of the most engaging and equality advocating companies to work for. We believe that regardless of where you work at IMP Aerospace & Defence, you are a part of our ever-growing team. IMP is able to achieve success through this teamwork mindset. That is why at IMP, you are not defined by your role.

Position Overview:
The Apprentice Technician (AVN) will attend the Transport Canada accredited IMP Academy AME-M Training Program and participate in the required on the job training. They will work alongside qualified technicians to gain the required experience needed to complete the program and may work on multiple aircraft platforms. Duties for the apprentice include but are not limited to attending all training, participating in On-the-Job Experience (OJE) and On-the-Job Training (OJT) for servicing tasks, elementary tasks, and maintenance, including aircraft documentation, inspection, removal, cleaning, repair, Installation, adjustments, and testing of aircraft mechanical, and structural components. Upon successful completion of the IMP Academy program, apprentices will be moved into the Airframe Mechanic classification.

What You Will Do:
• You will be responsible for ensuring you are ready and available for all training modules and OJT experiences.

• Receive on-the-job training from other employees to progress through apprenticeship to certified Aircraft Maintenance Technician.

• Providing support to Airframe Mechanics for both on and off aircraft work.

• The safe operation of support equipment and hand/power tools while adhering to tool and Foreign Object Debris (FOD) control procedures.

• Maintain a clean and safe work area utilizing safe work practices and appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).

• Performance of on and off aircraft servicing, elementary work, modification, maintenance, and specialized maintenance under the supervision of a qualified technician.

• Perform other tasks as may be required from time to time.

• Adhere to policies, procedures and directives as established by the company.

• Upon completion of the apprenticeship program, you will then be required to assume the role and all responsibilities of the Airframe Mechanic.

What You Will Bring:
• A high school diploma or equivalent upon approval.

• Completion of the IMP Academy Introduction to Aerospace Program.

• Ability to use standard computer programs and such specialized ones as may be necessary in the performance of the duties.

• A strong willingness and the capability to learn the content and computer programs as required, follow procedures, and become familiar with technical terms and references.

• The capability to succeed in a fast-paced environment, working well under pressure while maintaining precision when faced with deadlines.

• Strong organizational, time management and critical thinking skills

• A self-directed work ethic where high attention to detail is the minimum standard

• A collaborative and cooperative attitude and a strong desire to see your program succeed.

• Demonstrate a personal commitment to IMP Occupational Health, Safety and Environment policies.

• Must be eligible to meet requirements for Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP), U.S. International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and Canadian government security clearances

What We Will Do For You:
• All of IMP's benefits become effective on your first day of work, regardless of your position.

• We offer a comprehensive Benefits Package, including RSP Program, Tuition Reimbursement Program, Long Service Awards, Volunteer Grant Program, Scholarship Program, and more!

References
Please include 2 professional references and their contact information (phone number and email) with your application.

IMP is committed to Employment Equity and our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative at all job levels. We welcome applicants from Indigenous People, Visible Minority Groups, Persons with Disabilities and Women in occupations or positions where they are under-represented. If you are a member of one of these equity groups, you are encouraged to self identify on either your cover letter or resume.
