2239985.title: Controller
2239985.description:
## Job Posting: Controller

Company: Prime Material Handling
Reports To: Director of Finance
Location: Dartmouth, NS
Position Type: Full-time, Permanent

## Job Summary

The Controller contributes to the overall success of Prime Material Handling by effectively managing our financial tasks, corporate budgets, and accounting operations. Reporting directly to the Director of Finance, you will maximize return on financial assets by maintaining a strong control environment that ensures compliance with company and legislative policies.

As a growing company, we need a hands-on leader who will manage and mentor an experienced team of three accounting professionals, with a heavy, direct focus on overseeing Accounts Receivable (AR), billing, and cash collections. Beyond team management, you will take ownership of reconciliations, cash flow projections, and budgeting, while partnering with the Director of Finance to provide strategic direction and guidance on key business decisions. This role is a true "player-coach" position-requiring someone who is equally comfortable shaping strategy and rolling up their sleeves to support frontline daily tasks.

## Key Duties and Responsibilities

## Strategic Financial Management & Controller Functions

· Strategy & Guidance: Provide the Management Team with accurate, timely financial data and recommendations to support growth and business decisions.

· Financial Reporting: Develop and maintain timely, accurate monthly financial statements and reports in accordance with GAAP.

· Budgeting & Variance Analysis: Partner with the Director of Finance and department heads (including Parts and Service) to establish annual budgets; deliver clear analysis of actual results vs. budgets.

· Cash Flow Optimization: Develop, manage, and monitor rigorous daily and weekly cash flow forecasting models.

· Compliance & Audits: Ensure all statutory requirements are met; prepare all supporting information for the annual accounting review, CRA, and Workers' Compensation Board.

· Continuous Improvement: Continually leverage available resources to improve operational efficiency across financial, customer, and internal processes.

## Team Leadership & Operational Focus

· Team Management: Supervise and mentor an experienced 3-person accounting team handling day-to-day transaction processing (AR and AP).

· Frontline Support: Demonstrate a genuine willingness to roll up your sleeves and assist the team with daily data entry, customer questions, and high-volume operations depending on the day's needs.

· Payroll Administration: Manage corporate payroll functions to ensure accurate and timely compensation.

## Skills and Qualifications

· Education: Post-Secondary degree in Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field.

· Designation: A CPA professional designation is highly valued.

· Technical Skills: Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel is strictly required for data manipulation, modeling, and financial analysis.

· Systems Adaptability: Strong technical aptitude with the ability to quickly master and navigate our industry-specific ERP system.

· Experience: 5+ years of progressive corporate accounting experience, including team management and direct exposure to budgeting/forecasting.

· Leadership Style: A flexible, collaborative leader who empowers others, listens to varied perspectives, and stays close to the frontline work rather than focusing solely on high-level delegation.

· Problem Solving: Ability to use complex reasoning, brainstorm creative solutions to immediate operational issues, and translate organizational strategies into actionable plans.

## Working Conditions

• Working in a climate-controlled office environment in Dartmouth, NS.

• Working in a fast-paced, growing business environment.

• Working overtime on occasion to meet month-end or budget deadlines.

• Sitting for extended periods of time.

• Travel between the head office and branches on occasion.

Prime Material Handling Equipment Limited offers a competitive salary, medical and dental plan, RSP and other benefits in a family-oriented, safe and respectful work environment that continually encourages its greatest assets to learn and develop!

Develop your career with us by submitting your resume via email.

No Phone Calls

We are currently seeking a Lead Geotechnical Engineer to join our Geotechnical - Dams team in Sudbury. The role is a permanent on-site position.

The Lead Geotechnical Engineer provides technical leadership for the safe design, operation, monitoring, and closure of tailings storage facilities, dams, and related water management infrastructure. The role evaluates geotechnical performance through inspections, monitoring data analysis, and risk assessments to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, industry standards, and design objectives. Working closely with internal and external stakeholders, the incumbent develops risk mitigation strategies, supports dam safety and governance programs, and delivers engineering solutions that protect people, the environment, and the business.

• Conduct inspections and assess facility conditions, performance, and risks.

• Review monitoring data and perform geotechnical analyses to evaluate stability, seepage, deformation, and overall performance.

• Develop and implement risk mitigation measures and operational improvements.

• Collaborate with operations, environmental, project, and engineering teams to support tailings and dam safety objectives.

• Ensure compliance through technical documentation, reporting, and participation in audits and reviews.

• Manage and review consultant and contractor deliverables.

• Support incident investigations, dam safety reviews, emergency preparedness, and change management processes.

• Drive continuous improvement in geotechnical practices, monitoring programs, and tailings governance.

• Communicate technical findings and recommendations to stakeholders.

• Undergraduate degree in Engineering in appropriate discipline.

• Professional engineering designation (P.Eng) required.

## Experience:

• 8-10 years of relevant experience preferred.

• Experience managing FEL studies, as well as supporting or leading pre-feasibility, feasibility, and large-scale project execution within mining, extractive, or infrastructure industries.

• Operational and site-based experience in mining environments, including underground operations, with technical exposure to open pits, stockpiles, and dams.

• Experience working on brownfield projects, operations, or maintenance activities, with knowledge of project delivery systems and associated deliverables.

• Broad industry experience and networks across mining and geotechnical disciplines, with exposure to multiple commodities considered an asset.

## Skills:

• Strong commitment to safety, technical excellence, and delivering results.

• Excellent communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to convey complex technical concepts and work effectively within multidisciplinary teams.

• Proven ability to analyze alternatives, assess risks and opportunities, and recommend practical solutions.

## Why Sudbury

Greater Sudbury is a vibrant city in northeastern Ontario, renowned for its rich mining history and significant role in Canada's mineral production. The city sits atop one of the world's largest and oldest meteorite impact sites, the Sudbury Basin, which is exceptionally rich in nickel, copper, and other critical minerals that are required for modern technologies such as AI and defence. The mining sector is a cornerstone of Sudbury's economy, driving both employment and economic growth, and Vale Base Metals plays a pivotal role in this regard. Our commitment to the community is as deep as our mines.

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people can act like owners, being their authentic selves and empowering them to deliver results. Vale Base Metals encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

In accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Employees engaged by the Company must be lawfully able to work for the Company in the country where the role is located. The Company does not provide immigration, work permit, or permanent residence sponsorship or assistance.

Dartmouth, NS
Reference # HL-MOT-9953

Our client, MetOcean Telematics Limited (MetOcean), contributes to the worldwide effort to better understand, assess, monitor, and connect our planet. Their mission is to connect the world without limits. They ensure critical data is transmitted, received, and processed in the fastest and most reliable manner possible anywhere in the world. They value collaboration, innovation, achievement, and connection.

We are pleased to be partnering with MetOcean in the recruitment of an Accounting Technician to join their organization in their Dartmouth, NS office.

Reporting to the Controller, the Accounting Technician will support the accounting team in maintaining accurate financial records and ensuring the timely preparation of internal financial statements. This role plays a key part in month-end and year-end processes, reconciliations, reporting activities, and ongoing financial operations, helping provide management with reliable information for effective decision-making.

## Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

• Prepare and review general ledger account entries, reconciliations, and supporting schedules

• Support month-end and year-end close activities, ensuring accurate and timely financial reporting

• Prepare monthly financial statements and related management reports, including consolidated monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements

• Compile monthly working paper files

• Assist with external reviews by providing requested documentation and supporting explanations

• Provide backup support for Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable functions

• Prepare operating expense analyses and provide insight to management

• Support and maintain adherence to third-party reporting requirements

• Identify opportunities to improve efficiency and effectiveness within routine accounting processes

• Perform ad hoc analysis and reporting, including the enhancement of existing reports

• Other duties, as assigned

## The ideal candidate will have:

• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Business, Commerce, Accounting, or a related discipline

• Minimum 2 years of progressive accounting or finance experience, including financial reporting and month-end close responsibilities

• Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel and the Office 365 suite of applications

• Experience with Microsoft Dynamics GP or other ERP systems considered an asset

• Experience with Microsoft Power BI considered an asset

• CPA student or newly designated CPA considered an asset

• Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate and implement effective solutions

• Excellent organization and time management skills

• Strong attention to detail and ability to adapt in a dynamic environment

• Ability to interpret and integrate information from multiple sources of varying complexity

• Strong written and verbal communication skills

• Proven ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a team environment

MetOcean Telematics is one of Nova Scotia's and Atlantic Canada's Small & Medium Top Employers. They are leaders in Satellite IoT-enabled solutions and design and manufacture their products right in Dartmouth, NS. As a global provider of innovative telemetry products, options, and solutions, they serve environmental, marine, defence, and security clients around the world. This is an exciting opportunity to join a growing organization that is making a meaningful impact on a global scale.

MetOcean Telematics is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or disability status.

We are currently hiring for Spare Winter Equipment Operators in Colchester County at the following bases: Zone 14 (Bible Hill, Brookfield), Zone 15 (Wallace, Tatamagouche, Welsford) and Zone 16 (Londonderry). About Our OpportunitySuccessful candidates will begin with two weeks of paid training designed to build the knowledge and skills required for effective snow and ice control operations. Candidates must also successfully complete a driving assessment using a one-person-truck-plow equipped with a front plow, wing, and salt controls. You are flexible, self-motivated, and comfortable working in all weather conditions. You are respectful and understand the value of good customer service. You will be working around environmental hazards, various traffic conditions and occasional work performed in a mechanical environment.

2134562.description:
Title : Technologist, Medical Radiation (MRT)

Employee Working Location : In-person (Canada)

Employment status : Deployed 3-4 weeks working full-time hours when deployed

Salary band : $41.23 / hour (eligible for pier diems, travel and accommodation covered by CRC)

The Canadian Red Cross (CRC) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2024, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

## In this role, you will :

• Perform, monitor, and report radiographic investigations and services as per medical orders, delivering safe, high-quality care in accordance with professional standards, clinical guidelines, and medical directives.

• Ensure the quality and safety of all radiographic services by operating equipment correctly and maintaining compliance with national standards, regulations, and health authority requirements throughout deployment.

• Conduct and contribute to clinical assessments of radiographic services, monitor patient outcomes, and support the continuous improvement of imaging protocols and operational practices.

• Collaborate with the multidisciplinary team, on-site clinical leads, local health authorities, and partner agencies to promote efficient patient care and maintain effective communication channels during deployment.

• Manage, monitor, and ensure the safe, correct use and function of radiography equipment and associated medical supplies in line with operational and partner requirements.

• Maintain accurate documentation, data collection, and reporting that meets local legal requirements, regulatory standards, and organizational obligations.

• Support planning and delivery of radiography services as requested by the partner, including active participation in service monitoring and the implementation of new procedures or protocols.

• Mentor and build the capacity of clinical, non-clinical, and auxiliary personnel in radiographic practices as appropriate.

• Adhere to all deployment requirements, including flexibility across assigned shifts, completion of the CRC Learning Pathway and site-specific training, currency of certifications and licensures, maintenance of professional indemnity coverage, and compliance with medical, safety, and infection prevention protocols.

• Work independently and responsibly in mobile or dynamic settings, upholding organizational and partner standards at all times.

## What we are looking for :

• Academic qualification in Medical Radiation Technology (minimum 3-year college diploma or university degree) or equivalent combination of education and experience.

• CAMRT certificate required and collected as a part of the process..

• Current Professional Registration in good standing in at least one province in Canada.

• Professional certification or post-graduate qualification in trauma/emergency radiation technology, humanitarian affairs, or a related field is an asset.

• Minimum 4-7 years of professional experience in medical radiation technology.

• Experience in a radiology department using hard copy films and analogue equipment.

• Experience operating portable X-ray machines and other radiographic equipment in clinical or field settings.

• Experience monitoring equipment performance and conducting basic verification and quality control checks.

• Experience working in emergency, humanitarian, or resource-limited contexts.

• Experience living or working in a cultural context other than their own, including Indigenous, remote, or isolated communities, is an asset.

• Ability to identify, investigate, and analyze equipment or service problems, determine root causes and risks, and apply technical knowledge to develop practical solutions.

• Proficiency in standard computer applications (Microsoft Office Suite).

• Experience in health needs assessment and the design or adaptation of radiographic service protocols in dynamic or non-standard settings.

• Training, facilitation, coaching, and capacity-building skills applicable to clinical, non-clinical, and auxiliary personnel.

• Ability to coordinate with health authorities and foster effective working relationships with multidisciplinary teams and partner stakeholders at various levels.

• Strong communication skills, diplomacy, and empathy to interpret and deliver clinical information, clarify stakeholder needs, and resolve issues in sensitive or complex situations.

• Ability to adapt to changing circumstances and work independently in fast-paced, mobile, or dynamic environments.

• Flexibility to travel on short notice to various destinations for periods of several weeks as required.

• Fluency in English is required; French is an asset.

• Maintenance of current professional indemnity coverage and compliance with all medical, safety, and certification prerequisites for deployment.

## Working conditions :

• Difficult and demanding -both physically and psychologically-working conditions are expected.

• Due to dynamic nature of an emergency and proximity to epidemic/ pandemic affected area, issues with access and mobility and strict protocols and procedures.

• Possible long hours of work in demanding context with limited resources

• Potential for exposure to communicable disease (TB, Covid, etc.), bodily fluid, and hazardous materials that can result in potential health risks to the incumbent.

• Living conditions vary by deployment. When deployed to remote, northern nursing stations, the following can be expected: very basic living conditions including group living and shared accommodations ,potential for placement in community with non-potable water, potential for placement in community with water shortages and/or frozen plumbing for days at a time.

• If requested by CRC clinical support team, must complete any pre or post deployment screening ( i.e.. TB screening, Covid testing)

• Must ensure all prescription medications are up to date and supply will be sufficient for duration of deployment.

• A valid provincial driver's licenceis an asset

• As a health care provider, you may be required to provide a health attestation regarding vaccination history depending on deployment/partner requests.

• As we work with and support people (managers, colleagues, beneficiaries/customers, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.

• Eligibility to work in Canada: At this time, we welcome applications from candidates eligible to work in Canada. If you are not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada, we encourage you to carefully review your visa to find out whether you are eligible to work in the job you are considering applying for. Refer to our FAQ for more information.

• If you are selected for this role, you will be required to complete a successful pre-employment screening process which includes a satisfactory Enhanced Police Information Check (E-PIC).

• Full vaccination against COVID-19 is mandatory for this position and operation.

Before you apply, please watch this video to learn more about a casual position with the Canadian Red Cross.

The Halifax Regional Centre for Education (HRCE) is the largest Centre for Education in Atlantic Canada with over 11,000 full-time, part-time and casual employees. 2240350.title: Family Support Worker (Counsellor 2AB)
2240350.employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
2240350.description:
Competition # : 49918

Department: Opportunities and Social Development

Location: HALIFAX

Type of Employment: Term

Union Status: NSGEU - NSPG

Closing Date: 30-Sep-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
At the Department of Opportunities and Social Development (OSD), we are a large and diverse department providing a broad portfolio of programs and services including Child and Family Wellbeing (CFW), Employment Support Services(ESS), Income Assistance (IA), Homelessness and Supportive Housing, and Disability Support Program(DSP).

Through our services, we advocate and help vulnerable Nova Scotians be independent, self-reliant, and secure. We work collaboratively across the province with a strong dedicated network of supports and staff, to achieve desired and shared outcomes for all.

About Our Opportunity
As a Family Support Worker, you will provide support to the children, youth and families connected to the Child and Family Wellbeing program. You will have an in-depth involvement and will play an active role in working with children, youth and families to build resilience and inspire change. While working collaboratively with the social worker, you will develop and deliver a plan to provide service, education, support and advocacy to the families, children & youth in care.

If you are looking for an opportunity to make positive impacts on the lives of children and families, establish positive connections and build everlasting relationships within your community, we welcome you to apply!

Primary Accountabilities
As an integral part of the Child and Family Wellbeing program, some of your key responsibilities include:

• Developing strategies and providing knowledge, tools and guidance to families and youth to support independent living and meeting their physical/emotional, social and learning needs.

• Building positive relationships with diverse clients (families, children & youth), ensuring respect, empathy and an understanding of the impact of their trauma.

• Advocating for clients and helping them connect to community supports and resources.

• Assisting with income and social supports, affordable housing and life skills.

• Making independent visits to clients in their homes/communities and attending court sessions.

• Comprehensive and timely evaluation of ongoing services to clients with an intent to find solutions and improve services.

Qualifications and Experience
You have an approved Child & Youth Care Worker diploma from a provincially approved post-secondary institution. An undergraduate degree in Social Sciences is considered an asset.

You are compassionate, empathetic and resilient with a focus on inclusivity and understanding the needs of diverse clients. You must demonstrate:

• Knowledge of child development, family dynamics and community resources along with an understanding of physical, psychological, and emotional needs of children and youth in a family setting as well as in care.

• Knowledge of financial management and healthy child development & life skills

• Understanding and experience with working towards the objectives of the established case plans.

• Ability to work independently and in a team environment, to strengthen and improve the support provided to children and families.

• Ability to work collaboratively and build relationships & networks with diverse individuals, groups and communities.

• Effective interactive communication skills (written and verbal) to engage collaborations and navigate diverse client environments with tact and empathy.

• Ability to adapt to the changing/unpredictable client circumstances, exercise timely judgement and make decisions to provide a culturally responsive service to clients.

• Knowledge of various software packages, such as Microsoft Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams).

Following are the assets for this role:

• previous experience in child welfare or other social services,

• experience with the department case management systems (ICM/CCM)

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies, using one or more of the following tools: standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and background & reference checks.

Equivalency
We recognize equivalent combinations of training, education, and experience, providing opportunities for individuals with diverse backgrounds to contribute their skills and expertise. Equivalencies include, but are not limited to:

• A related bachelor's in social science (such as Psychology, Sociology, Social Work, or Community Studies)

• A completed diploma in Disability Supports or Social Services

Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
Most of your work involves independently meeting with clients conducting their sessions predominately in isolation from other staff in various locations (i.e. offices, homes (hazards may be present within homes), community agencies/organizations) in both rural and urban settings; this can be outside regular working hours. This necessitates considerable driving time, sometimes with unpredictable and adverse travel/weather conditions.

While present in the office, your time is spent a comfortable office environment.

Your personal resiliency is essential to meet the physical and emotional demands of this position. You will be immersed in high stress and crisis situations, exposed to various living conditions and aggressive behaviour. You must be able to work under pressure and with clients who may be resistant to service and should be personally and professionally committed to inclusively working with culturally diverse individuals.

Additional Information
This is a Term opportunity with an anticipated end date of Sept 14, 2027. The appointment status ('term', 'temporary' or 'casual') is dependent on the start date of the successful candidate.

A valid driver's license, and the ability to travel and access to a reliable vehicle are required. You will use your personal vehicle, and your vehicle must be properly equipped for the transportation of infants and children.

What We Offer
• Career Possibilities: you will have access to multiple career paths, career guidance, and ongoing training for every stage of your career.

• Rewarding and versatile work; daily, you will get to see the impact you have in and around your community.

You will play an important role in a dynamic and passionate team, collaborating on a variety of projects of all sizes and scopes in the environment, renewable energies, hydroelectricity, transportation, materials, buildings and climate change markets. At Englobe, our rigor is matched by sincere care for our colleagues, our customers, our communities , and the environment. We are committed to making a real difference, one project at a time, and to having a positive, lasting impact. We approach our work with fresh perspectives, relying on collaboration and a diversity of voices. With an entrepreneurial spirit, we empower our customers and communities with boldness and optimism. We are determined to leave a lasting legacy for generations to come.

As a Senior Hazmat Environmental Consultant, you will play a key role in leading field investigations, mentoring junior staff, and supporting the continued growth of our environmental services team. • Collaborate with project managers and technical specialists to plan and execute environmental investigation programs.

• Prepare and contribute to proposals, scopes of work, and cost estimates for environmental investigation and hazardous materials assessment projects.

• Review field notes, data collection records, and technical documentation to ensure accuracy, completeness, and regulatory compliance.

• Communicate effectively with clients, contractors, and project teams to coordinate field programs and communicate technical findings.

• Contribute to building and maintaining strong client relationships.

• Support the continued development and growth of Englobe's environmental field team through knowledge sharing and mentorship.

• Apply and promote Englobe's strong health and safety culture during all field and office activities.

## What makes you unique

• Diploma or degree in Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Geology, or related discipline.

• 10 years of consulting experience in hazardous materials investigations.

• Experience conducting Phase I and Phase II Environmental Site Assessments.

• Strong technical report writing and data interpretation skills.

• Demonstrated ability to prepare clear, well-structured technical reports and proposals.

• Real flexibility;

About Us
The Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration is a dynamic and innovative department focused on strategies, policies and programs that help people live, learn and work to their highest potential in vibrant businesses and organizations throughout Nova Scotia.
The Corporate Policy and Services Branch is the department's primary link with broader government. It helps ensure the department aligns with government policies, priorities and processes, and supports informed departmental and government decision-making. The branch leads and coordinates functions including corporate policy and planning, accountability and performance reporting, strategic initiatives, research, intergovernmental affairs, access and privacy, records and information management, facilities, and legislative and executive coordination.

About Our Opportunity
As Director, Data Strategy, Performance and Analytics, you will establish and lead a coordinated departmental function that strengthens how Labour, Skills and Immigration governs, prioritizes, analyzes and uses data. Reporting to the Senior Executive Director, Corporate Policy and Services, you will provide strategic leadership for departmental data strategy, performance measurement, reporting standards, analytics priorities and related governance practices.
You will lead a team and work across branches to bring greater consistency to analytics, accountability and performance reporting. Your work will support evidence-based policy and program design, operational planning, resource allocation, accountability reporting and executive decision-making. You will exercise considerable judgment in setting priorities, developing standards and workplans, and providing advice on complex and sensitive issues.

Primary Accountabilities
In this role, you will:

• Lead the development, implementation and ongoing administration of a departmental data strategy, including priorities, governance, standards and accountabilities.

• Develop common approaches to performance measurement, outcomes reporting and executive-level monitoring across the department.

• Identify and oversee departmental analytics priorities, products and workplans, including executive dashboards and decision-support products.

• Provide strategic advice to senior leadership on program performance, operational pressures, emerging trends, risks and opportunities.

• Guide the coordination and transition of analytics, reporting and performance-related work into a more integrated departmental function.

• Establish data governance practices that support appropriate, consistent and effective use of departmental information.

• Support program evaluation and the use of evidence to improve policy, program design, service delivery and accountability.

• Build strong working relationships across the department and with central agencies, other government departments and external partners.

• Lead, develop and support a high-performing team by setting priorities, assigning work, managing performance and supporting employee development.

• Contribute to workforce planning, organizational design, resource allocation and other confidential management discussions and decisions.

Qualifications and Experience
You are a strategic, collaborative leader with strong expertise in data strategy, performance measurement and analytics. You can translate complex evidence into clear advice and practical tools for executives and program leaders. You are comfortable working across organizational boundaries, building shared approaches and leading change in an environment with multiple priorities.
You have a related post-secondary degree, such as public administration, business administration, economics, statistics, data science, social sciences or another relevant discipline, along with several years of progressively responsible experience leading data, analytics, performance, evaluation or strategic planning functions. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
Your application must clearly demonstrate:

• Progressive leadership experience, including leading and developing a team and managing competing priorities.

• Experience developing or implementing organizational data strategies, data governance frameworks or enterprise analytics approaches.

• Experience with performance measurement, outcomes reporting, program evaluation and executive dashboards or similar decision-support products.

• Experience using evidence and analysis to support policy, program, operational or resource-allocation decisions.

• Strong strategic thinking, judgment and problem-solving skills, including experience advising senior leaders on complex or sensitive matters.

• Experience leading organizational change and building collaborative relationships across diverse programs, professions and stakeholder groups.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical information in clear, practical language.

• A demonstrated commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion and accessibility in leadership and decision-making.

The following are considered assets:
• Experience working in the public sector or in a large, complex organization.

• Experience with economics, labour market information, labour market analysis or related forecasting and research.

• Experience with advanced analytics, business intelligence platforms, data visualization tools or modern data environments.

• Formal training or demonstrated experience in change management.

• Experience establishing new teams, functions or centres of expertise.

Please submit a cover letter and resume that clearly demonstrate how you meet the qualifications and experience for this position.

LEADS
The Government of Nova Scotia has adopted the LEADS Leadership Framework. During the interview, candidates will be expected to describe how they have demonstrated the behaviours and capabilities required to lead effectively in a caring and inclusive environment. The LEADS domains are Leads Self, Engage Others, Achieve Results, Develop Coalitions and Systems Transformation.
We will assess the qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, oral presentation, interview and reference checks.

• Engaging workplace: our employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in, we have forward-thinking policies and strategies

• Countless career paths

With VON you get to hit the open road, where the scenery and work are different every day. We offer a workplace free from the repetitive and boring, where you know you've helped someone remain independent, and meet some great people along the way. Our CCAs provide care in client homes and other settings in communities across Nova Scotia.

## Come for the job, stay for the chance to make a real difference.

## What we can offer you:

• Competitive salaries and vacation time

• Tiered Benefits (health, dental, LTD) & an Employee Assistance Program

• Defined Benefit Pension Plan with company contribution

• Travel compensation

• Comprehensive orientation program

• Opportunity to use your skills and expand your knowledge

• Work with clients in their homes to provide personal care

• Assist with daily living activities, such as grooming, dressing and bathing

• Provide respite care

• Plan and prepare meals and light household duties

• Help with mobility and transfers

• Monitor and maintain household safety

• …and much more!

## What we need from you:

• Continuing Care Assistant Certification (CCA)

• PSW, HSW, etc. certification from another province or other relevant certification or work experience (who are enrolled in or are eligible to enroll in the Nova Scotia CCA Recognizing Prior Learning (RPL) Program)

• Students in nursing, CCA programs and internationally educated nurses will also be considered

• A current and original copy of a satisfactory Criminal Records Check and Child Abuse Registry Check are required, a Vulnerable Sector Search may also be required

Are you working in healthcare or a related field and interested in starting a career as a Continuing Care Assistant? Work with us while you are completing the RPL Program!

Funding is available through the Department of Health and Wellness for the Recognized Prior Learning (RPL) Program.

## What is the RPL Program?

The CCA-RPL program recognizes knowledge, skills, and attitudes gained through on-the-job training, formal education, and life experiences to be assessed for credit awarded towards CCA program education. For more information about the program and available funding, please contact:

CCA Recognizing Prior Learning (RPL) Program
E: CCARPL@healthassociation.ns.ca

## Funding for CCA Programs at community colleges

Funding is also available for the Continuing Care Assistant Program at community colleges across Nova Scotia. The Nova Scotia Government covers tuition and most program costs for eligible applicants. Please contact your local college for more details.

2240566.employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
2240566.description:
Competition # : 49935

Department: Emergency Management

Location: Flexible

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: Exclusion - Non Union - NSPG

Closing Date: 02-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
The Department of Emergency Management is responsible for leading disaster and emergency planning, preparedness, response and recovery activities on behalf of the Province of Nova Scotia. The objective of the Department is to ensure that Nova Scotians are safe, prepared and resilient in the face of disasters and emergencies. The Department leads the coordination and co-operation of partners and resources during provincial level critical incidents, administers the province's 911 service, maintains critical communications infrastructure and supports operations of our regional emergency management centres. The Department also works to ensure critical government services continue to function.

The Regional Operations and Infrastructure Branch enhances the safety and resilience of our Province by:

• Establishing and maintaining Regional Emergency Operations Centres (REOCs) in 6 regions in Nova Scotia. The REOCs provide leadership in building regional emergency operations networks; ensuring collaborative efforts around emergency planning, training and exercising and developing regional plans for equipment and stores to support emergency response

• Coordinating response to regional emergencies

• Strengthening local and regional emergency preparedness through outreach and education to Nova Scotians at community events, schools, organizations, and through information sessions

• Setting standards in the provincial emergency management program for training and exercising

• Fostering strong collaboration, communication, and emergency management planning with regional partners, including the development and coordination of regional Nova Scotia Guard networks

• Providing information to the Provincial Coordination Centre and the 24/7 Watch Desk staff to ensure real-time situational awareness, coordination, and support during emergencies and actioning critical information received from the Provincial Coordination Centre in the regions

About Our Opportunity
As the Manager, Development and Delivery, you will lead the design, development, delivery , and continuous improvement of the Department's emergency management training and exercise programs.

You will transform complex and important emergency management education and information into accessible, practical learning experiences for varied audiences. Your work will include assessing learning needs, establishing education pathways and curriculum standards, developing courses and exercises, selecting effective delivery models, and creating resources for learners, instructors, and facilitators.

You will provide strategic and operational leadership to a team of professionals and work closely with government, communities, and partner organizations. You will have the opportunity to rethink traditional approaches, introduce modern and inclusive learning practices, and strengthen the consistency and operational relevance of emergency management education.

This position is well suited to an education or learning-development leader who wants their work to contribute directly to community readiness and public safety.

Primary Accountabilities
• Lead a professional team responsible for developing and supporting emergency management training, education, and exercise programs.

• Conduct needs assessments to identify capability gaps, emerging requirements, priority audiences, and opportunities for program development.

• Develop annual and multi-year training and exercise plans that define priorities, learning outcomes, audiences, sequencing, delivery models, resource requirements, and implementation standards.

• Create and maintain training and exercise catalogues, role-based education pathways, and certification or qualification frameworks that support progressive learning and capability development.

• Establish standards for curriculum, courses, exercises, learning resources, and delivery practices, ensuring that content reflects legislation, policy, recognised practices, accessibility requirements, and operational needs.

• Develop and maintain courses, facilitator guides, participant materials, manuals, job aids, templates, checklists, infographics, and other practical learning resources.

• Select fit-for-purpose learning and delivery methods based on the audience, subject matter, required level of complexity, available resources, accessibility needs, and intended outcomes.

• Develop facilitation models, workshop formats, train-the-trainer programming, and instructor supports that enable consistent delivery across regions, programs, and partner organizations.

• Research emerging educational practices, technologies, standards, and tools, including responsible uses of artificial intelligence, and assess how they may improve program quality, accessibility, and administration.

• Apply an equity, diversity, inclusion, and accessibility lens throughout program design, resource development, facilitation, and evaluation.

• Build collaborative relationships with internal and external partners and represent the Department on relevant committees and working groups.

• Manage human and financial resources, establish team priorities, support employee development, monitor expenditures, and contribute to a respectful, healthy, and inclusive workplace.

• Provide advice to senior leaders on program priorities, implementation needs, risks, resources, and opportunities for continuous improvement.

Qualifications and Experience
You are an experienced education, curriculum, learning and development, or instructional-design professional who can connect long-term strategy with practical implementation.

You have a university degree in education, adult education, instructional design, curriculum studies or another related field, plus significant related experience; an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience will also be considered. You must also demonstrate:

- experience applying adult learning principles to the design, development, delivery, and evaluation of education or training programs.
- experience developing courses, learning pathways, facilitator resources, and practical tools for varied audiences.
- leading complex program or curriculum-development work from needs assessment and planning through delivery and evaluation.
- leadership experience that may include managing employees, leading multidisciplinary teams, coaching colleagues, or directing significant programs or projects.
- strong facilitation and presentation skills, with the ability to explain complex subjects in clear and audience-appropriate language.
- strong written communication skills and experience producing structured, accessible learning products and guidance.
- experience incorporating equity, diversity, inclusion, and accessibility considerations into learning design and delivery.

The following would be considered assets:

- a completed related graduate degree
- knowledge of emergency management, public safety, or experience designing emergency exercises, simulations, tabletop exercises, or scenario-based learning.
- experience implementing or administering a learning management system.
- experience with curriculum-development
- experience assessing and applying emerging and modern technologies, including artificial intelligence, in a responsible, secure, and accessible manner.

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
We recognize equivalent combinations of training, education, and experience, providing opportunities for individuals with diverse backgrounds to contribute their skills and expertise. Equivalencies include:

• A related diploma with substantial experience in adult education, curriculum development, instructional design, or learning-program leadership.

• Significant experience leading the design and implementation of complex education or training programs, supported by relevant professional learning or certification.

Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
Your normal work week is 35 hours/week, 7 hours/day. Most work is completed in an office or classroom environment and involves extended periods of concentration, computer use, meetings, planning, writing, and reviewing detailed materials.

The work includes facilitating or supporting training, workshops, planning sessions, and exercises in different settings. These activities may require standing for periods of time, transporting or arranging learning materials, working in spaces with varying noise levels.

You must be able to travel periodically within Nova Scotia and, on occasion, outside the province. Travel may involve locations not readily served by public transport and may occasionally affect regular working hours.

Additional Information
The worksite location is flexible and may be located in any of the Emergency Management offices. Your worksite location will be determined at the offer negotiation stage.

What We Offer
• Career development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career

• Engaging workplace: our employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in, we have forward-thinking policies and strategies

2237324.description:
Title: Coordinator - HiE

Employee Working Location: Partially Virtual / Hybrid (Canada)

Employment Status: Permanent Full-time

The Canadian Red Cross (Red Cross) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

Program/Service Coordinator (Internal Support) supports the effective delivery of Health in Emergencies (HIE) programs and services through administrative, operational, project coordination, and systems support. The coordinator plays a key role in strengthening departmental processes, information management, and digital systems to improve efficiency, collaboration, and service delivery.
The role provides administrative, logistical, and technical support to HIE initiatives, including emergency preparedness and response activities. The coordinator contributes to the development and maintenance of operational systems, supports data collection and reporting, coordinates team activities, and assists with continuous improvement initiatives. The successful candidate is highly organized, technologically savvy, and fully bilingual in English and French, with the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced and evolving environment.

## In this role, you will:

• Assist with the development and implementation of program and service delivery plans to support HIE operational objectives.

• Coordinate and manage day-to-day administrative and operational activities for assigned programs, projects, and initiatives.

• Support implementation, monitoring, and reporting of program and service delivery activities.

• Coordinate meetings, workshops, training sessions, and special events, including logistics, documentation, and follow-up actions.

• Assist with the deployment and coordination of staff, volunteers, equipment, and resources during emergency preparedness and response activities.

• Support the development, implementation, and maintenance of departmental administrative systems, digital workflows, and information management processes.

• Serve as a departmental resource for Microsoft 365 applications, including SharePoint, Teams, Planner, Forms, and other digital collaboration tools.

• Maintain and improve electronic filing systems, document repositories, trackers, dashboards, and reporting tools.

• Identify opportunities to streamline processes, automate routine tasks, and improve operational efficiency.

• Collect, track, and maintain program and operational data, statistics, and performance indicators.

• Prepare regular reports, presentations, briefing materials, and communications in support of departmental activities.

• Assist in monitoring budgets, expenditures, procurement activities, and resource utilization.

• Support the preparation of evaluative reports, performance reports, and management updates.

• Ensure information and records are accurate, current, and maintained according to organizational standards.

• Work collaboratively with colleagues and internal stakeholders to support the implementation of HIE programs and activities.

• Build and maintain effective working relationships across departments to facilitate information sharing and coordination.

• Provide guidance and support to team members regarding processes, systems, and administrative procedures.

• Contribute to the development and implementation of training and onboarding materials for staff and volunteers.

• Identify areas for operational, administrative, and service delivery improvement.

• Recommend and support implementation of solutions that enhance effectiveness, efficiency, and user experience.

• Contribute to the development of innovative approaches, tools, and strategies that strengthen HIE operations and service delivery.

## What we are looking for:

• Minimum of 3 years of relevant experience in program coordination, operations, administration, project coordination, or a related field.

• 1-2 year post-secondary certification/diploma in Business Administration, Project Management, Public Administration,

• Information Management, or a related discipline, and/or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Fluency in English and French (spoken and written) is required.

• Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint).

• Strong proficiency with SharePoint and Microsoft 365 collaboration tools, including Teams, Forms, Planner, and related applications.

• Demonstrated ability to learn and leverage digital technologies to improve workflow efficiency and information management.

• Experience developing or maintaining tracking systems, databases, dashboards, or reporting tools is considered an asset.

• Familiarity with Power BI, Power Automate, or other business process automation tools is considered an asset.

• Strong organizational, project coordination, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and drive continuous improvement.

## Working conditions:

• All CRC roles are required to adapt work and priorities to support emergency response efforts, be present in person as required to support service delivery and deploy to emergency responses when appropriate and/or required (personnel availability and request for exceptions will be discussed with line management).

• As we work with and support people (managers, colleagues, beneficiaries/customers, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.

• Eligibility to work in Canada: At this time, we welcome applications from candidates eligible to work in Canada. If you are not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada, we encourage you to carefully review your visa to find out whether you are eligible to work in the job you are considering applying for. Refer to our FAQ for more information.

• If you are selected for this role, you will be required to complete a successful pre-employment screening process which includes a satisfactory Enhanced Police Information Check (E-PIC).

2239320.description:
Requisition ID: 2614

Why Choose IMP Aerospace & Defence:
IMP Aerospace & Defence is not only one of the leading companies in the Aerospace field, but we are also one of the most engaging and equality advocating companies to work for. We believe that regardless of where you work at IMP Aerospace & Defence, you are a part of our ever-growing team. IMP is able to achieve success through this teamwork mindset. That is why at IMP, you are not defined by your role.

Position Overview:
To carry out all required aspects of the procurement and supply function for the acquisition of common aerospace production goods and services, while ensuring value is maximized at all times. Make sure all goods and services are ordered in accordance with specifications as provided by requestor. Reporting to the CSH Material Supervisor, this position will liaise directly with strategic & non-strategic suppliers as well as internal stakeholders in Production Planners, LCMMs, Production Support (Paint/Process, Component Repair and Facilities), Inventory Management, Warehousing and Subcontractors as well as functional areas such as Contracts and Finance.

What You Will Do:

• Provide assistance in developing short- and long-term plans to meet procurement and contracting requirements.

• Advising employees and managers on policies related to procurement and contracting

• Identify effective cost savings solutions such as determination of economic order quantities, better value sources and procurement methods

• Prepares RFP/RFQ, submit to selected suppliers, prepare cost analysis, review quotes from suppliers, negotiate with suppliers, prepare recommendations, implement and set up new suppliers

• Expedites, maintains, updates edits and resolve supplier issues related to purchase orders & credit application and invoice reconciliation

• Prepare and release purchase orders to potential suppliers

• Monitor and report suppliers performance Review and approve or recommend policies and procedures

• Participate in Quality Assurance Materiel Review Boards as required

• Understand moderately complex technical drawings and specifications

• Provide oral and written reports and correspondence as required, internal and external

• Attend industry exhibitions as required and meet industry representatives on behalf of the company

• Supervise and train assigned junior and intermediate buyers to include monitoring performance and preparing evaluation reports

• Carry out special assignments as required Participate in departmental and program review meetings

• Other duties as assigned

What You Will Bring:
• Undergraduate degree or college diploma preferably in business administration or commerce and 5 to 7 years experience in the aerospace industry or relevant military supply management experience or experience working with Government Procurement

• The ideal candidate will have a strong background and comprehensive understanding of supply chain issues and deliverables and fundamental knowledge of purchasing processes and systems.

• Preference given to candidates pursuing the program of the Purchasing Management Association of Canada (PMAC).

• The candidate must have the ability to multi-task and shift priorities without jeopardizing timelines.

• Must have demonstrated experience with ERP systems and Inventory Management Control - JDE knowledge would be an asset

• Skill in using computers for spreadsheet analysis and communications;

• Experience identifying problems, assessing risks and identifying challenges within the procurement and contracting areas

• Respect for accuracy and detail Strong team player with a willingness and capability to lead others.

• Incumbents must be able to pass and maintain Public Works Government Services Canada (PWGSC) and Transport Canada security clearances

What We Will Do For You:

2228575.employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
2228575.description:
Competition # : 48849

Location: HALIFAX

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: Exclusion - Non Union - NSPG

Closing Date: 13-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
The Department of Seniors and Long-Term Care offers opportunities to grow and advance in a dynamic sector that touches the lives of many Nova Scotians. Along with our partners, including the Nova Scotia Health Authority, the Department of Health and Wellness, long-term care facilities, home care agencies, training institutions and other sector leaders, we're committed to continually improving the support system for seniors and others requiring home care, long-term care and other community-based supports.
In addition, the department supports the social and economic well-being of older adults ensuring policy formulation and effective decision-making as well as policy coherence across government departments as it relates to aging. The department is thinking differently about how to plan, fund, legislate and monitor to improve access and service delivery for Nova Scotia's senior population. To do this, we need leaders at all levels of the organization who embrace a challenge and believe in their ability to make a difference.

About Our Opportunity
Reporting to the Executive Director, Continuing Care, as the Director of Long Term Care (LTC), you will play a key leadership role in the Branch leadership team whose mandate is to lead, prioritize and drive Continuing Care initiatives that lead to better resident/client care outcomes, stronger system performance across the broader health system, and timely advice to senior leadership on sector priorities, risks, and emerging issues.
You will provide both operational and strategic leadership. Specifically, you are accountable for advancing program excellence and system change through strategic partnerships, and for overseeing programs, initiatives and projects that are governed by multiple pieces of provincial legislation, regulations, policies, and standards. You will maintain a strong connection to the sector, monitor performance and emerging pressures, identify and assess risks, and provide timely, evidence-informed advice to senior leadership on policy, investment, operational priorities, and mitigation strategies. You will also work collaboratively with multiple and diverse stakeholders to strengthen the continuing care system and improve access to quality care.

Primary Accountabilities
More specifically, in this role you will:

• Provide strategic and operational leadership for the Continuing Care sector, ensuring alignment with government priorities, departmental direction, and broader health system objectives.

• Maintain an ongoing understanding of sector pressures, performance, emerging issues, and system risks, and translate this intelligence into timely advice and action.

• Advise senior leadership on Continuing Care sector policy, investment considerations, operational pressures, and risk mitigation strategies.

• Identify, assess, and escalate emerging issues and risks, and lead or support coordinated responses as appropriate.

• Lead the implementation of programs, initiatives, and system improvement efforts within a complex legislative, regulatory, and policy environment.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with operators, service providers, health system partners, and other stakeholders to understand impacts, inform decisions, and support system performance.

• Support policy and program development by bringing operational insight, sector intelligence, and practical implementation considerations into decision-making.

• Influence and contribute to strategic planning, priority setting, and resource discussions related to Continuing Care services in Nova Scotia.

• Demonstrate sound fiscal oversight paired with an understanding of complex funding environments.

Will be required to support the broader continuing care/department programs as needed.

Qualifications and Experience
You have experience in complex, multi-faceted environments where understanding interdependencies across program areas, sectors, and systems is critical to success, and you apply this understanding in your everyday work.
You are strategic and adaptive, enjoy collaborative planning, and are able to meet the challenges inherent in a fast pace complex system. You are skilled at synthesizing information from multiple sources, assessing impacts, and recommending practical, timely courses of action.
You are resourceful and influential in your ability to secure buy-in through written materials and presentation, build capacity, optimize provincial resources and demonstrate public accountability. You have demonstrated experience identifying emerging operational, strategic, and reputational risks, and providing advice to senior leaders on policy, program, operational, and investment matters. You think outside the box, and you have the confidence and conviction to introduce innovative concepts and solutions founded on sound reason, judgment, experience, and expertise.
You are a leader who has extensive experience leading teams to achieve results in a fast-paced, changing environment. You bring strong judgment, professionalism, and the ability to navigate sensitive issues with discretion while building trusted relationships across government, the health system, and external partners.
You possess a Bachelor's Degree in a related field and several years of progressive leadership experience. The possession of a Master's Degree, a background in Nursing and/or leadership experience in Continuing Care are considered an asset. An equivalent combination of related training and experience may be acceptable.
Leadership competencies required at this level of work are Decisiveness; Strategic Orientation; Developing Others; Team Leadership; Self-Awareness & Personal Impact; Effective Interactive Communication; Partnering & Relationship Building; and Intercultural Diversity Proficiency.
We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
An equivalent combination of training, education and experience will be considered. Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
• Normal work week is 35 hours/week, 7 hours/day

• Will be required to work overtime on occasion

• Travel will be required

What We Offer
• Career development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career

• Engaging workplace: our employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in, we have forward-thinking policies and strategies

• Countless career paths

• A dynamic, client-focused office environment where service excellence and teamwork are our focus.

Location: HALIFAX

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: Exclusion - Non Union - NSPG

Closing Date: 06-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
The Office of the Auditor General serves the Nova Scotia House of Assembly and the people of Nova Scotia. Our vision is to be a relevant, valued and independent audit office serving the public interest as the House of Assembly's primary source of assurance on government performance. The Office accomplishes this through the conduct of financial and performance audits of government departments and agencies, as well as entities which receive funding from the government. With approximately 40 dedicated professionals, we pride ourselves on promoting excellence, integrity, and a supportive workplace. For more information, please visit www.oag-ns.ca.

About Our Opportunity
We're seeking an experienced, proactive Senior Administrative Coordinator to provide critical executive-level support to our Executive Leadership Team (ELT). In this trusted role, you'll help keep the Auditor General, Deputy Auditor General, and senior leaders operating at their best by coordinating complex schedules, managing the flow of confidential information, and serving as a key link between our Office and senior officials across government and beyond.

The work is steady and detail-driven. You'll manage calendars, coordinate meetings, keep correspondence and reports moving, and make sure the office runs smoothly day-to-day. Some periods are busier than others. This role suits someone who finds satisfaction in consistent, well-run processes and takes pride in getting the details right.

If you thrive in a professional environment where your judgment, discretion, and initiative are valued, this is your opportunity to make a meaningful impact behind the scenes.

What You'll Do:
• Provide high-level administrative support to the Auditor General, Deputy Auditor General, and senior leadership, including managing complex calendars, coordinating meetings, preparing agendas, taking minutes, and ensuring timely follow-up on action items.

• Act as a liaison with senior officials across government, legislative committees, and professional associations.

• Draft, proofread, and format confidential correspondence, reports, and official publications.

• Coordinate the design, layout, and production of Auditor General reports to the House of Assembly and Public Accounts Committee.

• Develop and maintain procedures, guides, and administrative workflows that keep the Office running smoothly.

• Anticipate information needs, manage sensitive records, and ensure secure handling of confidential materials.

• Coordinate select recurring items for the Human Resources Director: ergonomic assessment scheduling, new employee orientation scheduling, and years of service certificates production.

• Enter data across the employee life cycle in SAP: onboarding, position changes, offboarding, annual salary increases, time entry, and self-service account setup.

• Plan and coordinate office-wide activities and special projects, including staff days, training sessions organized by the Office, regional conferences and other Office-hosted events.

• Provide backup to the Administrative Assistant and coordinate office logistics as needed.

What You Bring:
• Proven experience providing senior-level administrative support, ideally in professional services, government, or public sector settings.

• Exceptional organizational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities and tight deadlines.

• Excellent judgment, discretion, and commitment to confidentiality and political neutrality.

• Strong writing, proofreading, and document production skills with a keen eye for detail.

• Proficiency with MS Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and the confidence to learn new technologies and tools.

• Comfort liaising with senior officials and representing the Office professionally.

• Initiative, flexibility, and confidence to solve problems independently.

• Proficiency with SAP is an asset.

• Experience creating data visualizations and infographics and an understanding of design principles and techniques is an asset.

What We Offer
• Career development – We are committed to your professional growth as a CPA. We fund your annual CPD requirements and support participation in CPA Atlantic events and national legislative audit networks. Because our team is small, you won't be siloed. You'll contribute to the full audit lifecycle from planning through to reporting, building depth and breadth that is hard to find in larger organizations. You'll also be mentored by senior CPAs who are invested in your success.

• Comprehensive benefits – Competitive salary, extended health and dental benefits, life insurance, and a defined benefit pension plan

• For more information visit our website: Career Information | Office of the Auditor General of Nova Scotia

About Us
We are currently hiring for Spare Winter Equipment Operators in Pictou County at the following bases: Salt Springs (Zone 11), Lyons Brook (Zone 11), MacLellan's Brook (Zone 10) and Kenzieville (Zone 10). Work may be available at any of these locations. Please quote the competition number and the Zone(s) you are applying for as noted above on your application.

Job Fair
If you would like to apply or are looking for additional information please attend our Career Fair on Saturday, September 19, 2026, from 9:00am to 12:00pm at the MacLellan's Brook Base located at 610 MacLellan's Brook Road.

About Our OpportunitySuccessful candidates will begin with two weeks of paid training designed to build the knowledge and skills required for effective snow and ice control operations. Following training, you will complete 45 hours of paid plowing experience under the guidance of an experienced Operator. Candidates must also successfully complete a driving assessment using a one-person-truck-plow equipped with a front plow, wing, and salt controls. This is a spare position, and hours of work are not guaranteed. Employees are called in as operational needs require. There may be an opportunity to participate in the Winter Wage Guarantee, which provides guaranteed work for a minimum of two weeks and may continue for the duration of the winter season. If placed on the Winter Wage Guarantee, the following will apply:
• Guaranteed 90 hours of pay every two weeks

• $0.95/per hour premium

• Opportunities for overtime

• Scheduled days off (2 days bi-weekly)

You are responsible for operating snow removal equipment such as snowplows, graders, and loaders. This includes general maintenance of the equipment, pre-and-post trip inspections, and daily logs. You may also be required to perform other work, such as maintaining signs, road surface repairs and traffic control.

Qualifications and Experience
Two years of experience or an acceptable equivalent of education, training, and relevant experience.

Minimum of Class III license with air brake endorsement.

Reading and writing skills are required to understand department documentation and to complete daily logs, inspection reports, etc.

The following is not required but considered helpful:

• A professional driving course from a recognized truck driving training facility

• Knowledge of hydraulic systems and mechanical skills

• Training completed at any accredited heavy/commercial equipment training institute

• Previous experience driving a manual transmission, operating trucks with salt and plow equipment, and/or knowledge of salt spreading systems

You are flexible, self-motivated, and comfortable working in all weather conditions. You are respectful and understand the value of good customer service. You will be working around environmental hazards, various traffic conditions and occasional work performed in a mechanical environment.

Applicants who are unable to apply online are invited to stop by the local Area Office located at 608 MacLellan's Brook Road, New Glasgow to complete a paper application. At CSDS, we prioritize people—both within our team and in the communities we serve. Our mission is to redefine how Nova Scotians engage with government by creating accessible, reliable digital solutions centered around user needs.
In today's tech-driven world, CSDS empowers government departments with essential digital solutions to meet Nova Scotians' expectations. As a trusted partner across government, we enable departments to fulfill their mandates with secure, user-friendly services. From healthcare and education to public safety, we collaborate to transform how services are designed and delivered.
We don't just implement technology; we modernize outdated systems and reimagine processes. Our agile, data-driven approach ensures that digital services are both efficient and adaptable to Nova Scotia's evolving needs.
Joining CSDS means contributing to work that makes a real difference. From providing vital tech support to healthcare professionals to strengthening cybersecurity and developing scalable digital platforms, you'll play a key role in building a more inclusive, responsive government for Nova Scotians.
Together, we're setting new standards for digital public service, delivering resilient solutions that meet today's needs—and anticipate tomorrow's challenges.

As the Manager, SaaS (Software-as-a-service) Solutions, you provide leadership and direction to a team of IT professionals; delivering corporate and line of business application services to multiple departments, agencies, boards and commissions. You play a lead role in ensuring the partner department's plans and objectives are effectively supported by translating their requirements into appropriate information technology plans and application solutions. Aligning appropriate methodologies, techniques and technologies to enable delivery of these solutions.
