2235866.title: Supply Chain Specialist
2235866.description:
Job Title: Supply Chain Specialist
Location: Dartmouth, Nova Scotia
TP - PPT - 9688

Meridia Recruitment Solutions has partnered with Pure Paint Laboratories to recruit a Supply Chain Specialist for their Operations team based in Dartmouth, Nova Scotia.

Pure Paint Laboratories (Pure Paint) is committed to creating healthy spaces for a healthier planet. The company produces North America's only fully developed petroleum-free, plant-based architectural paint, made entirely from renewable agricultural ingredients. Inspired by ancient, time-tested formulas, Pure Paint's products are non-toxic, fully biodegradable, and designed to support healthier indoor environments while contributing to a renewable future.

Through a manufacturing process that begins with cold-pressed oilseed crops and other natural ingredients, Pure Paint creates durable, high-quality paint products while maintaining a commitment to sustainability and healthier spaces for generations to come.

Role Description
Reporting to the Operations Director, the Supply Chain Specialist develops and maintains practical, resource-loaded schedules that support the safe, efficient, and timely execution of production planning. Working closely with Sales, Operations, Maintenance, Project Teams, Procurement, and Stores, you will coordinate resources, identify risks and constraints, and align weekly and daily schedules with business priorities.

## Your responsibilities will include:

• Building, maintaining, and communicating integrated schedules (daily, weekly, and rolling look-ahead) aligned to business priorities and available capacity.

• Converting approved work orders and scope into executable schedules by validating readiness requirements, including materials, tools, permits, access, labour skills, and durations.

• Facilitating weekly scheduling meetings with stakeholders and capturing decisions, constraints, and action items.

• Coordinating labour, equipment, and material planning while level-loading work to optimize utilization and reduce bottlenecks.

• Identifying critical path activities, dependencies, and schedule risks and proposing mitigation and scenario plans.

• Monitoring progress, updating schedules using actuals, and managing changes resulting from emergent work, outages, supply delays, or scope changes.

• Partnering with Procurement and Stores to confirm material availability, expedite shortages, and maintain a clear ready backlog.

• Maintaining scheduling standards, coding structures, and data quality within the ERP system.

• Producing routine schedule performance reports (planned vs. actual, compliance, backlog, resource loading) and presenting insights to leadership.

• Supporting shutdown and turnaround planning activities as required.

• Building long-range plans ranging from one to six months.

Your Qualifications
As the ideal candidate, you are highly organized and detail-oriented with strong planning, scheduling. analytical, and communication skills. You are capable of balancing competing priorities, facilitating stakeholder discussions, and adapting schedules as operational requirements change.

## Key qualifications include:

• Post-secondary education in Supply Chain, Business, Operations, Engineering or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• 2+ years of experience in scheduling, production planning, and/or sales and operations planning (S&OP) and procurement.

• Working knowledge of scheduling principles, including dependencies, constraints, critical path methodology, and capacity/resource planning.

• Experience with scheduling and/or work management systems such as Primavera P6, Microsoft Project, SAP, Maximo, Katana, or similar planning systems.

• Strong Microsoft Excel skills, including formulas, pivot tables, data analysis, and data cleaning.

• Strong planning, prioritization, and stakeholder management abilities.

• Excellent communication, analytical thinking, and problem-solving skills.

• A high level of attention to detail and commitment to schedule and data accuracy.

• Ability to adapt to changing priorities and re-plan effectively as constraints emerge.

• A continuous improvement mindset with the ability to identify root causes and recommend solutions.

• Strong understanding of the end-to-end supply chain, from raw material and packaging suppliers through to final delivery to the end customer.

To express interest in this opportunity please apply online by clicking "Apply Now" below.

For more information contact Thomas Pugh, Partner, at 902-818-4506 and tpugh@kbrs.ca or Rick Neima, Senior Consultant at 902-488-2534 and rneima@kbrs.ca, or please apply online by clicking the "Apply Now" button below. 2220359.title: Automation Engineer
2220359.description:
Automation Engineer

## Build a career that matters with one of the world's most respected employers!

## - - - - - - - - - - - -

## Automation Engineer

## Waterville, Nova Scotia

For 130 years, Michelin has innovated to improve the mobility of people and goods. Today, we are setting the benchmark across every tire and travel-related services market, while leading a global strategy to drive sustainable, profitable growth.

Michelin North America (Canada) Inc., which operates three tire manufacturing facilities in Nova Scotia, is seeking an Automation Engineer to join its team in Waterville, Nova Scotia.

The Automation Engineer will support the manufacturing process and equipment by designing, specifying, purchasing and constructing electrical automation systems and components. This position will include aspects of project management, technical specification, design, analysis, installation management, equipment start-up and manufacturing.

The successful candidate will be responsible for completing the automation portion of projects to enable the plant to meet its market, productivity, and quality goals. They will assist management with pre-studies of deployment and development projects in the electrical automation field. They will also complete design studies and follow procurement and fabrication of equipment and lead the installation, commissioning and start-up of the equipment in an industrial plant environment.

## Job responsibilities include:

• providing detailed electrical design and automation programming for assigned projects and plant technical assistance;

• providing estimates and technical schedules for all phases of process equipment addition, replacement or upgrade;

• providing backup support and training to plant maintenance teams on newly implemented automation systems;

• collaborating with internal company support groups to accomplish objectives, and provide contract engineering management and direction when needed; and,

• participating in assigned major capital projects and/or modifications from start to finish, including equipment reception, commissioning, and acceptance.

## Requirements for this position include:

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent in Electrical Engineering, or related field; and,

• minimum of 2-4 years of proven experience in electrical automation design.

## The following assets are preferred, but not required:

• experience with electrical design standards and the ability to complete controls systems designs using standard CAD design tools;

• experience in Project Team Leadership or Project Management;

• experience with PLC programming standards and programming software, including GRAFCET, Ladder Logic, and Structured Text (Rockwell and Siemens);

• experience with Variable Frequency drives and Motion Control technologies (Rockwell, Siemens and Control Techniques);

• experience with HMI configuration, programming and communication (Rockwell);

• experience with control systems network interfaces and various protocols for communications between devices including computer system databases;

• vision system configuration and interface for width measurement applications and defect detection applications (specific experience with Cognex, Keyence, Adept, Bytewise, Gocator is an asset); and,

• robotic experience, configuration or knowledge (Fanuc, ABB).

## Competencies:

• solid written and verbal communication skills;

• well-organized and able to manage multiple tasks simultaneously;

• ability to set and achieve goals with minimum supervision;

• demonstrated solid teamwork, interpersonal, leadership and planning skills; and,

• ability to maintain a high degree of confidentiality in dealings with outside contractors and equipment suppliers.

## How to apply:

Please merge your cover letter and resume into one Word or PDF document. Candidates must clearly indicate how they meet the requirements listed above. Deadline for applications is September 27, 2026.

Candidates selected to participate in the first round of interviews will be contacted via e-mail. All other candidates will be notified when the hiring process is complete.

## Why Michelin?

• Career Growth: Personalized development plans, mentorship, and cross-functional opportunities. Unique career paths and opportunities for advancement.

• Inclusive Culture: Thrive in a diverse, supportive environment where your competencies, contributions and behaviors are recognized. Option to join one of our Business Resource Groups and Inclusion Councils.

• Innovation-Driven: Work on projects that matter—from sustainable materials to digital transformation.

• Community Impact: Be part of a company that does what's right. We use sustainable business practices while balancing the needs of our customers and communities.

Michelin is an equal employment opportunity employer of visible minorities, women, Indigenous persons and people with disabilities. If you need accommodation for any part of the employment application process because of a disability, please contact us at accommodations@michelin.com.

## We build the future with people like you. Begin your career with Michelin today!

2215691.title: Director, Operational Policy & Market Operations
2215691.description:
## Director, Operational Policy & Market Operations
Halifax, NS
TP - IESO - 9311

Meridia Recruitment Solutions is pleased to partner with IESO Nova Scotia to recruit a Director, Operational Policy & Market Operations. This is a critical executive leadership role that will shape the rules, systems, and services required to run Nova Scotia's electricity market.

IESO Nova Scotia is an independent not-for-profit organization created by the Province of Nova Scotia to change the way Nova Scotia's electricity system is managed, by assuming responsibility for managing the province's power system in real-time, supporting Nova Scotia's clean energy goals under the province's Clean Power Plan and planning for the province's future energy needs. The organization is guided by operating principles and values that include credibility, transparency, collaboration, independence, innovation, respect, public service, safety and security and reliability for electricity customers.

Role Description
As a member of the Executive Team initially reporting to the CEO, the Director, Operational Policy & Market Operations will play a foundational role in designing and overseeing operational policy, market rules, market services, and settlement processes required for a fair, transparent, and reliable electricity market.

In this role, you will build, lead, and oversee the rulebook, services, and administrative systems that govern Nova Scotia's electricity market. This includes designing operational policies, creating and maintaining market rules and manuals, overseeing settlement and financial calculations, ensuring market transparency, and leading compliance and stakeholder engagement efforts.

This is a highly strategic role that blends policy design, technical expertise, regulatory understanding, and organizational leadership.

Your responsibilities will include:

## Operational Policy & Market Rule Development

• Lead the creation and continuous improvement of operational policies, market rules, and market manuals that support reliable, fair system operations.

• Establish structured processes for rule development, consultation, approvals, and ongoing change management.

• Ensure rules align with regulatory expectations, reliability standards, and the evolving needs of a more renewable grid.

## Market Arrangements & Market Services Design

• Design participant requirements, registration processes, and the administrative frameworks that enable market participation.

• Develop market services that support system reliability and future market evolution.

• Adapt market services and arrangements as Nova Scotia transitions to higher levels of renewable energy.

## Settlement & Market Administration Oversight

• Oversee settlement processes, including charge types, calculation methods, reconciliations, and dispute management.

• Ensure all settlement systems are accurate, auditable, timely, and supported by strong internal controls.

• Lead the development of participant facing administrative processes that ensure fairness and clarity.

## Market Data Transparency & Reporting

• Establish transparent data publication practices, including dashboards, operational reports, and public facing information.

• Ensure data governance frameworks support integrity, confidentiality, and public transparency.

## Compliance, Enforcement & Market Integrity

• Build and oversee compliance and enforcement frameworks related to market rules and operational policies.

• Support investigations, escalation processes, and remediation activities.

• Work closely with Legal and Regulatory Affairs to ensure clarity, enforceability, and alignment with regulatory expectations.

## Stakeholder Engagement & Consultation

• Lead engagement with government, regulators, utilities, market participants, and customers.

• Facilitate consultations, working groups, and technical forums.

• Represent IESO NS as a senior spokesperson on market design, policy, and operational matters.

## Enterprise Leadership & Team Development

• Recruit, build, and lead a new team responsible for policy, market services, and administration.

• Contribute to organizational strategy, operational readiness, and cultural development.

• Champion diversity, equity, inclusion, and Truth & Reconciliation.

## Qualifications

You bring a depth of experience in electricity markets, operational policy, system operations, settlements, or regulatory environments. You thrive in high scrutiny, multi stakeholder settings and have the judgment, communication skills, and collaborative mindset required to design complex policies and build institutional credibility.

The ideal candidate will have:

• Minimum 10 years of experience in electricity markets, system operations, operational policy, market governance, settlements, or related fields.

• Strong knowledge of market rule development, market operations, and policy frameworks, ideally within an ISO/IESO, utility, regulator, or similar environment.

• Experience designing or administering settlement processes and cost allocation methodologies.

• Demonstrated success in stakeholder engagement, consultation, and public facing communication.

• Strategic thinker with strong analytical and governance capabilities.

• Proven ability to lead teams, build new functions, and thrive in environments with evolving mandates.

To express interest in this opportunity please apply online by clicking "Apply Now" below.

For more information contact Thomas Pugh, Partner, at 902-818-4506 and tpugh@kbrs.ca or Rick Neima, Senior Consultant at 902-488-2534 and rneima@kbrs.ca, or please apply online by clicking the "Apply Now" button below. 2238250.title: Marketing Manager
2238250.description:
## Marketing Manager
Halifax, Nova Scotia
Reference #JL-GLX-10052

Galaxia was founded in 2020 with a bold vision: to advance Canada's presence in space through innovative satellite technologies. Since then, the company has grown into one of Canada's most exciting space technology firms, establishing itself as the only company of its kind in Atlantic Canada and one of only a handful across the country.

Headquartered in Halifax, Galaxia designs and builds satellite components, subsystems, and complete satellite solutions, serving both government and commercial customers. The company is currently delivering projects with the Department of National Defence and the Canadian Space Agency while expanding internationally through its newly established UK office. Galaxia is also working on next-generation satellite initiatives, including a 200kg-class satellite project alongside the European Space Agency.

As the company enters an exciting new stage of growth, Galaxia is looking to grow its team and further accelerate its expansion. With increasing visibility among government leaders, industry stakeholders, and the broader aerospace community, the company is seeking a Marketing Manager who can help tell its story, elevate its brand, and establish Galaxia as a defining name in Canada's modern space sector.

## The Role

Reporting to the VP Government Affairs and Public Relations, the Marketing Manager will be responsible for developing and executing Galaxia's overall marketing and communications strategy. This is a unique opportunity to join a rapidly growing space technology company at a pivotal moment in its evolution.

As the organization's first dedicated marketing leader, you will shape the company's public profile, strengthen its digital presence, increase media visibility, and build brand recognition across Canada and internationally. You will work closely with senior leadership, subject matter experts, external partners, and stakeholders to translate highly technical work into compelling stories that resonate with government, industry, academia, investors, and the public.

This is a highly hands-on role for an entrepreneurial marketer who thrives in growth-stage environments and enjoys both strategic planning and day-to-day execution.

## Duties & Responsibilities:

• Develop and execute a comprehensive marketing and brand strategy aligned with Galaxia's growth objectives.

• Position Galaxia as a leading voice in Canada's space and satellite industry.

• Create compelling narratives that communicate the company's mission, impact, innovation, and expertise.

• Lead content development across LinkedIn, company websites, thought leadership pieces, presentations, and other digital channels.

• Build and manage an editorial calendar and ensure a consistent flow of engaging content.

• Collaborate with technical teams to translate complex aerospace and defence concepts into accessible and engaging content.

• Monitor and enhance Galaxia's social media presence, with particular emphasis on LinkedIn and executive thought leadership.

• Measure and report on key marketing performance indicators, including audience growth, media coverage, engagement, and brand awareness.

• Manage relationships with external vendors, agencies, designers, and marketing partners.

• Support communications efforts related to corporate growth initiatives, strategic partnerships, and future fundraising activities.

• Contribute marketing support, where appropriate, to affiliated organizations including Psylogica and the Pulsar Institute.

• Maintain exceptional attention to detail and ensure all communications reflect the highest standards of quality, professionalism, and accuracy.

## Qualifications & Experience:

• Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, Public Relations, Business, or a related discipline.

• 5-8 years of progressive experience in marketing, communications, public relations, brand management, or related fields.

• Proven success building and growing brands, particularly within emerging, entrepreneurial, or high-growth organizations.

• Strong content creation, storytelling, and copywriting capabilities.

• Experience developing and executing social media strategies that drive engagement and visibility.

• Demonstrated ability to secure media coverage, thought leadership opportunities, and industry recognition.

• Strong understanding of digital marketing, brand development, and communications strategy.

• Ability to operate effectively with limited resources and identify creative, high-impact marketing opportunities.

• Excellent project management skills and the ability to balance multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

• Strong judgment, initiative, and a willingness to roll up your sleeves and execute.

• Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to producing polished, accurate work.

• Experience within aerospace, defence, technology, engineering, or other highly technical industries would be considered an asset.

• Experience with photography, videography, video editing, or multimedia content creation would be considered a strong asset.

## The Ideal Candidate

You are an ambitious, mid-career marketing professional who enjoys building something from the ground up. You are equal parts strategist and doer, capable of developing a long-term vision while also creating content, pursuing media opportunities, and driving execution.

You understand the realities of scaling organizations and are energized by the opportunity to make a meaningful impact. Most importantly, you are passionate about storytelling, curious about technology and innovation, and excited by the chance to help establish Galaxia as one of Canada's most recognized space companies.

If you have any questions, please contact Kate Spares, Recruitment Specialist, at kspares@kbrs.ca or Jeff Lanthier, Partner, at jlanthier@kbrs.ca. If you require accommodation to participate in the recruitment process, please let us know.

• Strong skills in business analytics tool, e.g., Microsoft Power BI

• Strong knowledge of MRP and Inventory Control practices.

• Strong communication skills, both written and spoken.

• Experience in aerospace industry is preferred.

Title: Senior Specialist - Indigenous Health

Employee Working Location: Partially Virtual / Hybrid (Canada)

Employment Status: Permanent Full-time

The Canadian Red Cross (Red Cross) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

The Senior Indigenous Health Specialist provides specialized Indigenous health and clinical expertise to support the planning, development and delivery of Health in Emergencies services within the Canadian Red Cross.
Working collaboratively with First Nations, Inuit and Métis Peoples, Indigenous Nations and communities, Indigenous leadership and organizations, health professionals, emergency management teams and partners, the Senior Specialist brings an Indigenous lens to public health, clinical services and emergency programming. The role supports culturally safe, respectful and responsive services that reflect Indigenous determinants of health, Indigenous knowledges, community priorities and relevant Indigenous rights frameworks.

The Senior Specialist also supports knowledge translation, health communication, relationship building, research and continuous improvement, helping teams apply clinical, public health and Indigenous health knowledge effectively across preparedness, response and recovery activities.

## In this role, you will:

• Provide Indigenous health and clinical subject-matter expertise to support the planning, development, implementation and evaluation of Health in Emergencies services.

• Contribute Indigenous health perspectives to preparedness, response, recovery and longer-term health programming, including clinical, public health and emergency management initiatives.

• Build and maintain respectful, reciprocal relationships with First Nations, Inuit and Métis Peoples, Indigenous Nations and communities, Indigenous leadership, health organizations and other partners.

• Engage with Indigenous communities and leadership to ensure programs and services reflect community-identified priorities, local context, Indigenous knowledges and culturally safe practices.

• Apply clinical and public health knowledge to support health assessments, service planning, continuity of care, health-needs analysis and appropriate referral/navigation pathways during emergencies.

• Develop and support knowledge translation and health communication approaches that make complex clinical, public health and emergency information accessible and relevant to diverse audiences.

• Facilitate reciprocal knowledge exchange between Indigenous communities, health professionals and emergency and humanitarian systems.

• Conduct research, environmental scans, assessments and analysis to inform program design, decision-making, monitoring and evaluation.

• Develop and contribute to learning resources, guidance, tools, briefings and other knowledge products that strengthen culturally safe practice across the Canadian Red Cross.

• Provide expert advice on Indigenous health, cultural safety, Indigenous rights, communication and community context to interdisciplinary teams, operational leaders and health professionals.

• Identify and support mitigation of cultural, communication, relational, clinical and operational risks that may affect program or service delivery.

• Represent Indigenous Health in internal and external working groups, partnerships and knowledge-sharing initiatives, and contribute to continuous improvement across Health in Emergencies.

## What we are looking for:

• Post-secondary education in a regulated health profession, health sciences, nursing, public health, medicine, dietetics, midwifery, occupational therapy, physiotherapy, pharmacy, paramedicine or another relevant clinical health profession is considered an asset.

• 6-9 years of relevant experience in Indigenous health, clinical services, public health, community health, health promotion or emergency health programming.

• Clinical experience in a healthcare, community health, public health or emergency health environment, with the ability to apply clinical knowledge to health service planning and delivery.

• Demonstrated experience working with First Nations, Inuit and/or Métis Peoples, Nations, communities, organizations or health systems in Canada.

• Strong understanding of Indigenous approaches to health and wellbeing, including the importance of community, culture, family, land, language and spirituality.

• Understanding of the impacts of colonization, systemic racism and jurisdictional barriers on Indigenous health and access to healthcare.

• Knowledge of cultural safety, cultural humility and Indigenous rights and health frameworks, including the Truth and Reconciliation Commission Calls to Action and the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples.

• Demonstrated ability to work respectfully across Indigenous and Western health knowledge systems.

• Strong relationship-building, facilitation, communication, clinical reasoning and interdisciplinary collaboration skills.

• Demonstrated ability to translate complex clinical, public health or emergency information for different audiences and contexts.

• Ability to work effectively in complex, rapidly changing and high-pressure environments.

• Proficiency with standard computer applications and the ability to support research, analysis, reporting and knowledge-management activities.

## Working Conditions:

About Us
The Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner (OIPC) (formerly known as the Freedom of Information & Protection of Privacy Review Office) provides impartial oversight of compliance with the governing access and privacy legislation. The OIPC delivers administrative justice to applicants by conducting investigations and mediations of complaints and reviews, issuing formal public reports, developing of educational materials and providing independent advice on access and privacy matters at the request of public bodies, municipalities and health information custodians.

About Our Opportunity
In handling all incoming contacts on behalf of the Information and Privacy Commissioner (Review Officer) (IPC), the Assessment & Awareness Officer conducts preliminary assessments when communicating with callers to determine if the complaint/inquiry/request is within the jurisdictional scope of the mandate of the IPC.

This position also promotes awareness, access and understanding of the role of the OIPC through the dissemination to information of stakeholders who contact the OIPC; by assisting in the logistics of presentations and training sessions and in some cases representing the OIPC at events; by preparing, proofing and disseminating Review Reports, Annual Reports, tools, press releases, correspondence, and notes drafted by the Commissioner and senior staff; by maintaining and monitoring website and social media accounts; and by developing and maintaining a network of collaborative working relationships with government organizations.

Working under the IPC, the Assessment & Awareness Officer provides senior level assistance and is responsible for the efficient and effective operation of the OIPC; works independently, providing confidential secretarial and office administrative support to the IPC, and other OIPC staff; acts as back-up to the Intake Manager; and acts as the Records Analyst.

Primary Accountabilities

• Complaint resolution and research;

• Promoting awareness of the Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner's role, function and responsibilities;

• Information and Privacy Commissioner support; and

• Office management and office administration.

Qualifications and Experience

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills with a high degree of professionalism, tact, and diplomacy.

The following would be considered an asset:

Title: Senior Program Coordinator, Social Emergencies

Employee Working Location: Partially Virtual / Hybrid

Employment Status: Permanent Full-time

The Canadian Red Cross (Red Cross) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2024, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

The Social Emergencies (SE) Program responds to an event or situation that exceeds the health and wellness resources and capacities of a community. The goal of the SE Program, in collaboration with the impacted community, is to provide stabilization, psychosocial support, resource mobilization, and support capacity building. The SE Program is guided by several complementary evidence-based frameworks, such as the CRC Indigenous Peoples and Community Engagement Pathway Frameworks and the Creating Safe Environments (CSE) Strategy, stewarded by Indigenous Programs. These frameworks align Risk Reduction and Resilience initiatives with principles for respectful engagement through all phases of a SE response to emphasize a community-driven, sustainable, and equitable recovery.

The Senior Program Coordinator, under the direction of the Senior Manager, will support the planning, coordination, and implementation of social emergency response initiatives. This role is responsible for ensuring rapid mobilization of resources through developing response protocols, supporting logistical coordination, and providing direct service delivery, including training and social emergency response. The Sr. Program Coordinator will play a key role in supporting program monitoring, evaluation, and continuous improvement, ensuring that activities are contextually relevant, evidence-informed, and aligned with organizational standards and community priorities.

## In this role, you will :

• Support the planning and implementation of the SE response strategy and ensure service delivery activities reflect cultural inclusion and safety.

• Support the planning and monitoring of the SE response structure, ensuring adherence to timelines, budgets, and quality standards.

• Assist with logistics, procurement, and administrative needs to facilitate successful SE responses.

• Coordinate technical support requests and ensure access to necessary resources.

• Organize and facilitate meetings, briefings, and key response activities, ensuring proper documentation and follow-up.

• Develop and maintain documentation to ensure consistency across SE processes and procedures

• Maintain and update SE response trackers, databases, and monitoring systems for real-time data tracking.

• Collect, analyze, and report on SE key program indicators to support decision-making and continuous improvement.

• Ensure proper documentation, storage, and accessibility of SE response data for compliance and future reference.

• Facilitate communication and collaboration with internal teams, external partners, and stakeholders to ensure alignment, support SE objectives, and enhance overall effectiveness.

## What we are looking for :

• Qualifications include a minimum of 4-5 years' experience and a 1-2 year post-secondary certification/diploma and/or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint) and SharePoint is required.

• Lived and/or has professional experience with First Nations, Inuit and/or Métis Nations or communities.

• Demonstrated experience working directly with Indigenous communities, organizations, or governments in a culturally safe, respectful, and reciprocal manner.

• Ability to identify, investigate and analyze problems, identify root causes and risks, and apply technical, functional and organizational knowledge to develop solutions.

• Ability to identify opportunities for process creation and/or improvement to enhance efficiency and effectiveness in service delivery.

• Ability to understand data analytics to assess performance metrics and generate reports for management.

• Communication skills, diplomacy and empathy to interpret information and deliver advice, clarify client or stakeholder needs, offer solutions, and resolve escalations in new or somewhat sensitive situations.

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

The New Brunswick Extra-Mural Program (EMP), often known as the "hospital without walls," has operated under the simple philosophy of helping New Brunswickers receive the care they need in the places where they are healthiest and happiest - their homes and communities. EMP makes a difference in the lives of those it serves by drastically reducing hospital admissions and greatly increasing patient satisfaction with its level of health care.

As part of EMP, your role is vital in our province's overall health. Join an integrated, multi-disciplinary team of health care professionals, dedicated to providing New Brunswickers with outstanding, highly coordinated primary health care.

## JOB SUMMARY

As a member of the interdisciplinary EMP team, the Licensed Practical Nurse is responsible for providing quality patient care within the scope of professional LPN practice to patients and families throughout their life span.

## REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND OTHER JOB REQUIREMENTS:

• Successful completion of an accredited school of Licensed Practical Nurses

• Active registration with ANBLPN;

• Minimum of three years recent medical/surgical, palliative care and wound care experience in an acute care setting;

## WHO WE ARE:

Mariner innovates always and everywhere, turning novel ideas into practical solutions. From products and services to venture creation, we build better futures powered by people. We partner with people embracing change, leveraging data, cybersecurity, cloud, and change management to drive successful business outcomes that matter to our customers.

Mariners build for change. Like SHIFT Energy, our energy management and decarbonization company. Or East Valley, created to scale social economic impact in our communities through investment and mentorship of emerging change-makers and their companies.

Mariner s purpose has always been to be a great, everlasting technology company and the core values that guide us every day are:

## OUR VALUES

• We care for our team.

• We care about the impact we have on our community.

• We serve by solving complex problems.

• We grow because growth fuels opportunities.

• We innovate always and everywhere.

• We build a business that lasts.

## OVERVIEW OF THE ROLE

We are looking for an experienced Procurement Manager to join a client-based project on a short-term engagement. This is a hands-on role focused on end-to-end procurement delivery, working closely with client stakeholders to support sourcing, supplier management, commercial negotiations, and procurement initiatives.

You will be expected to quickly understand the client environment, establish priorities, and provide practical procurement expertise throughout the engagement.

This is a full-time onsite engagement, with the successful candidate working in Saint John, New Brunswick.

## WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING IN THE ROLE

• Managing end-to-end procurement activities across assigned categories, projects, or supplier engagements.

• Working closely with client stakeholders to understand requirements, priorities, and commercial objectives.

• Leading sourcing activities, including market engagement, supplier evaluation, selection, and negotiation.

• Negotiating commercial terms and supporting contract development and execution.

• Managing supplier relationships and addressing commercial, performance, and delivery issues as required.

• Identifying opportunities to reduce costs, improve value, and increase procurement efficiency.

• Providing procurement guidance and recommendations to client stakeholders.

• Ensuring procurement activities align with client policies, governance requirements, and established processes.

• Managing procurement risks and escalating key issues where appropriate.

• Providing clear reporting and updates on procurement activities, outcomes, risks, and deliverables.

## WHAT SKILLS/QUALIFICATIONS YOU'LL NEED

• Proven experience in a Procurement Manager, Procurement Lead, Strategic Sourcing, Category Management, or similar procurement role.

• Strong experience managing end-to-end sourcing and procurement activities.

• Demonstrated commercial negotiation and supplier management experience.

• Strong understanding of procurement processes, contracting principles, and commercial risk.

• Experience working directly with senior stakeholders and translating business requirements into procurement strategies.

• Ability to quickly understand new organizations, priorities, and operating environments.

• Strong communication, negotiation, analytical, and stakeholder management skills.

• Ability to work independently and deliver effectively within a fast-paced, project-based environment.

• Previous consulting or client-facing project experience is considered an asset.

• Relevant procurement or supply chain qualifications or certifications are considered an asset.

• Hands-on experience developing and managing RFPs, RFQs, and competitive procurement processes is considered an asset.

## AND YOU ARE...

• Always improving your skills and knowledge: you want to be the best at what you do

• Curious and creative; comfortable taking on new problems and challenges

• A self-starter with the ability to recommend priorities to the project leader

• Comfortable working through problems and figuring things out with minimal supervision

• Great problem-solving skills: thorough and reliable

• Able to work in a team: share knowledge and assist other team members

• A good communicator: able to explain your ideas and recommendations

• Well organized and dependable under pressure: you manage your time effectively

• Energized by our company values!

## MARINER OFFERS YOU:

• A values-driven workplace where people really matter

• Flexible work location support for remote work/work from home. Some on-site work may be required.

• Competitive salary, retirement savings program, and rewards program

• Comprehensive health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance plans and access to e-health care

• Paid vacation, maternity/parental leave, paid sick leave and paid Mariner MyLife days

• Unlimited training

## WHY MARINER?

We believe in making a positive impact in the communities where we live and work! Not only are we passionate about nurturing a thriving technology sector here in Atlantic Canada, but we are also committed to solving technology challenges that will make an impact worldwide. Technology is everlasting, and we take pride in connecting world class talent to world class projects and business solutions.

If you are an IT Professional, Software Professional, or Management Consultant, that is passionate about career development, data, and problem solving, we want to hear from you! If this sounds like someone you know, share this with them so they do not miss the opportunity to experience Mariner!

To achieve this, we know we need to be all in on training and development of our team so we can continue to move the needle in the technology sector together. Of course, we offer competitive compensation and benefits packages to our team, but our competitive edge is the development and training that our team experiences every day.

Be part of our vibrant community that values diversity and embraces inclusion at every level. We are committed to fostering a culture where individuals from all backgrounds and walks of life feel empowered to contribute their unique perspectives. Our collaborative environment celebrates the richness of ideas and experiences, and we believe that by embracing diversity, we can achieve greater innovation and excellence together. Come and help us create a workplace that reflects the beautiful tapestry of our global community.

## Join our growing team!

2241261.description:
New Brunswick Housing Corporation
Regional Manager - Technical Services and Building Management
Pay Band 5
Open Competition
Northern Region & Moncton
Flexible Work Location Within the Assigned Region

Interested in making a difference in our province? We encourage you to Choose GNB!

The New Brunswick Housing Corporation is seeking an individual to join the Infrastructure Division as Regional Manager, Technical Services and Building Management, for the Northern Region.

The successful candidate may be based in one of the assigned regional offices, subject to operational requirements. The Northern Region includes Edmundston, Campbellton, Bathurst, the Acadian Peninsula, and Moncton.

## Who We Are

The New Brunswick Housing Corporation is responsible for developing and maintaining provincial housing facilities, programs, initiatives, strategies, and rental services for landlords and tenants. The Infrastructure Division supports the maintenance, renewal, and improvement of public housing assets and provides technical support for housing programs and related service delivery.

The Technical Services and Building Management Branch is responsible for supporting the safe, effective, and consistent management of existing public housing buildings and related housing assets. This includes technical inspections, building management, maintenance services, preventative maintenance, unit rehabilitation, contractor oversight, and support to housing programs and strategic housing initiatives.

## What You Will Do

Reporting to the Director of Technical Services and Building Management, the Regional Manager will provide regional leadership, coordination, and operational oversight for technical services, building management, and maintenance operations across the assigned region.

The successful candidate will directly supervise Technical Services Managers and provide indirect leadership to multidisciplinary regional teams involved in inspections, maintenance, trades, building operations, contractor coordination, and technical service delivery.

The Regional Manager will be responsible for:

• Leading the development and implementation of regional strategic and operational plans for technical services, building management, maintenance, inspections, unit rehabilitation, and asset renewal priorities

• Providing operational oversight and direction to Technical Services Managers to ensure consistent, safe, effective, and compliant service delivery across assigned regions

• Monitoring regional performance, service standards, maintenance priorities, inspection activity, vacancy turnaround, emergency response, contractor performance, and operational risks

• Reviewing and approving regional work plans, operational priorities, work order approvals, contract approvals, and budget-related decisions within delegated authority

• Supporting the development and implementation of preventative maintenance practices, inspection standards, reporting processes, and regional operating procedures

• Leading or supporting initiatives that improve service delivery, modernize maintenance and inspection practices, strengthen asset management, and support the transition from reactive to proactive building management

• Working with Program Delivery Managers, Housing Supervisors, Technical Services Managers, central office, contractors, and other partners to resolve complex regional issues and improve coordination between technical and program delivery functions

• Providing leadership during escalated or sensitive operational issues, including building safety concerns, fire or life safety issues, tenant displacement, urgent repairs, contractor performance concerns, and other high-impact regional matters

• Supporting financial and human resource management by monitoring regional budgets, identifying budget pressures, recommending mitigation strategies, supporting recruitment, managing performance, coaching staff, and addressing employee relations matters

• Overseeing regional and provincial service contracts related to building operations, maintenance, inspections, and other essential technical services in accordance with applicable legislation, procurement requirements, technical standards, and Housing NB policies

• Preparing reports, briefing material, recommendations, and operational updates to support branch-level decision-making and provincial service consistency

## Who You Are

You are an experienced operational leader with strong technical judgment, sound decision-making skills, and the ability to lead teams in a complex service-delivery environment. You are comfortable working with competing priorities, regional operational pressures, sensitive issues, and multiple stakeholders.

You can translate provincial direction into practical regional plans. You are able to support staff, resolve issues, improve processes, and maintain accountability for service standards, budget pressures, compliance, and results.

## Need to have:

• A bachelor's degree in engineering, engineering technology, building technology, or a related technical field and a minimum of five (5) years of related experience in infrastructure operations, facilities management, building management, maintenance management, construction, asset management, or engineering/technical services.

• or a technical diploma in building technology or a related field and a minimum of eight (8) years of related experience. Experience supervising or managing staff is required.

• An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience may be considered.

Candidates must be registered, or eligible for registration, as a Professional Engineer (P.Eng.), Professional Technologist (P.Tech.), or Certified Engineering Technologist (CET) in New Brunswick.

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

## Duties of Position:

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Primary Care Paramedics are based on the current National Occupational Competency Profile (NOCP) for Primary Care Paramedics,Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in paramedicine or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

Required Qualifications:

• You are entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizenship, permanent resident status or work permit)

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record

• Must have a high regard for confidentiality and patient safety

• Primary Care Paramedic program/course of over six months; If you do not have one and are interested in this career, here is a list of paramedic programs in Atlantic Canada, click here

• Must be registered, active Paramedic with the Paramedic Association of New Brunswick; If you are not currently registered in New Brunswick, please visit PANB at www.panb.ca

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 4 Driver's Licence (or equivalent)

Additional requirements for your application:

• Current Resume and Cover Letter

• A copy of your PCP diploma from an accredited institution

• Proof of current registration with Paramedic Association of New Brunswick

• Proof of completion of a Physical Abilities Test (PAT) specific to working as a paramedic within the last 12 months

• Proof of valid CPR level C certification issued in the last 12 months

• Photocopy of front and back of valid Class 4 driver's license (or equivalent) with minimum one year driving experience

• Driver's abstract; issued within the last 30 days

• Copy of any valid Driver's course certificate i.e. CEVO, VFIS or NS VSP or equivalent issued within the last three years

• Criminal Record with Vulnerable Sector Check; issued within the last 30 days

• Immunization Record (Tetanus Tdap) within the last 10 years, 2 MMR vaccines (Measles, Mumps and Rubella) or lab evidenced immunity, 2 Varicella vaccines (Chicken Pox) or lab evidenced immunity, 3 Hepatitis B doses and Lab evidenced immunity, TB Skin Test (2 step) and a 1-step in the last 12 months; if reactive a follow up chest x-ray). Please note, a meeting with our Employee Health and Wellness Consultant can be scheduled, to ensure that all vaccinations are up to date by the time an offer is made

• Valid Official Language Assessments (oral assessment only) in both French and English from the Department of Post-secondary Education, Training and Labour. You can contact them at LS-SL@gnb.ca. Please take into account the additional time to receive your language assessment

• Additional training and/or education is highly valued.

For any questions for our HR team, please contact us at jobs-emplois@ambulancenb.ca

If you are looking for a career that will change lives and have a direct impact on the health of our community, submit your application.

Ambulance NB is committed to the principle of equal opportunity in its employment practices and to providing an environment free from discrimination and harassment for all employees.

We would like to thank all candidates for expressing interest. Please note only those selected for interviews will be contacted.

2241258.description:
Probation and Parole Officer II Community and Youth Justice ServicesDepartment of Justice and Public SafetyCandidate InventoryOpen CompetitionVarious Locations (Campbellton or Bathurst)

Interested in making a difference in our province? We encourage you to Choose GNB!

## Who we are

The work we do has a positive impact on our communities and helps improve the everyday lives of New Brunswickers. Together, we are over 45,000 New Brunswickers who are passionate problem-solvers, who make a difference and are proud to call New Brunswick home.

The Department of Justice and Public Safety is dedicated to the rule of law, the promotion of the public interest, and the impartial administration of justice and works to improve the safety, security and resiliency of communities and citizens.

The department`s Community and Youth Justice Services Branch is seeking a Probation and Parole Officer in the Northern region. Probation and Parole Officers play a vital role in ensuring the safety of New Brunswickers through their work with clients in the criminal justice system, helping them follow their community service or conditional sentencing orders while encouraging a law-abiding mindset.

## What you will do

As a Probation and Parole Officer, your duties will include preparing pre-sentence reports and case plans; attending court; enforcing community service and conditional sentencing orders; reporting violations to law enforcement; and supervising and guiding clients on probation. You will be responsible for making community-based program referrals for your clients, which can include treatment for mental illness or addictions, or resources for education and career planning. You will work closely with departmental colleagues in Adult Custody Services, Victim Services, Court Services and other branches of Justice and Public Safety as clients move through the criminal justice system.

## Who you are

You are considered a change agent, encouraging positive behavioural attributes in the people you interact with. You are creative in problem solving and can react quickly when needed. You have excellent interpersonal and written communication skills. You treat people with politeness and professionalism, showing courtesy, empathy and kindness. You are committed to the well-being of your clients and in making your community a safer place to live.

Your attitude, skills and interests are just as important as your area of study. We are looking for diverse backgrounds that bring a combination of the following:

## Need to have

• Undergraduate degree in one of the related social sciences: psychology, sociology, criminology or social work

Written and spoken competence in English and French will be required. Please state your language capability.

Candidates must demonstrate on their application how they have acquired the education and experience for this position. Your resume should be in chronological order, specifying education and employment in months and years, including part-time and full-time employment. Screening for this competition is based on the resume you provide, so please ensure it is up to date when applying.

## Operational requirement

• Successful completion of a Canadian Police Information Centre (CPIC) vulnerable sector reference check

• Must have and maintain a valid minimum class 5 driver`s licence

## Nice to have

• Experience in a correctional environment or in counselling

Subject to the response to this competition, candidates may be required to demonstrate on their application one or more of the asset qualifications in addition to the essential qualifications in order to be given further consideration.

## Behavioural competencies

• Client service orientation;

• Analytical thinking;

• Teamwork and cooperation;

• Results orientation;

• Information seeking.

## Technical Skills

• Interviewing skills;

• Planning and organizational skills;

• Written communication;

• Ability to use Microsoft Office applications;

• Records and information management.

## Wage

$ 2,807 to $ 3,448 bi-weekly based on education and experience

## Work environment

• Office locations: Campbellton or Bathurst

• You may be required to travel to satellite offices.

• Hours of work: Monday to Friday, 8:15am - 4:30pm

• Your team will include other probation officers, victim services coordinators, a regional director and administrative support.

• We promote a scent-reduced environment.

• Is remote work possible: Remote or hybrid work arrangements are not available for this role.

## What can GNB offer you?

• Opportunities for career growth, professional development and training;

• Free access to Employee and Family Assistance Program (EFAP) and services;

• Comprehensive benefits package and the Public Service Shared Risk Pension Plan;

• Starting at 1.25 days/month of paid vacation;

• One paid volunteer day per year to give back to your community.

Providing a safe workplace for all. Your health & safety are important to us. GNB has implemented preventative measures across the organization to ensure your health & safety.

## How to apply

We encourage applicants to apply on-line at www.ere.gnb.ca, by mail at the following address or by email at HRcompetitions.concoursRH@gnb.ca by September 30, 2026 indicating competition number
R78-2026-0672.

This competition may be used to fill future vacancies at the same level.

Interested in making a difference in our province? We encourage you to Choose GNB!

The Department of Social Development is seeking qualified individuals to work as Social Workers in various zones across New Brunswick.

The Department is responsible for providing quality programs and services to all New Brunswickers including children, families, seniors, and persons with disabilities. The work may include a combination of the following functions: assessment, counselling, intervention, mediation, case management and report writing for a variety of services in areas such as front-line community, social, child welfare services and/or adult and senior services. Successful candidates will also be required to establish and maintain effective working relationships with clients, staff members, professionals, community and volunteer agencies, government departments and the public. Other related duties as assigned.

Your attitude, skills and interests are just as important as your area of study. We are looking for diverse backgrounds that bring a combination of the following:

## Need to have:

• Master's or Bachelor's degree in Social Work.

NOTICE TO PENDING SOCIAL WORK GRADUATES - Future graduates of a Master's / Bachelor's are encouraged to apply. Please ensure that your tentative date of convocation is indicated on your application.

Some positions require written and spoken competence in French and English. Others will require written and spoken competence in English or in French only. Please state your language capability.

Applicants must clearly demonstrate the essential qualifications to be given further consideration. Please ensure that preferred language for assessment is identified on your resume.

• Teamwork & Cooperation.

• Written Communication.

• Opportunities for career growth, professional development, and training.

• Free access to Employee and Family Assistance Program (EFAP) and services.

• South-East Zone (Moncton, Richibucto, Shediac, Sackville)

• South-West Zone (Saint John, Sussex, St. Stephen)

• Central Zone (Fredericton, Woodstock, Perth-Andover, Miramichi, Neguac)

2237834.description:
The Financial Controller is senior leadership position responsible for the overall financial stewardship, reporting, planning, and performance management of the Dobson Group.

This role combines the traditional responsibilities of corporate accounting with the forward-looking responsibilities of financial planning and analysis. The Controller will lead all accounting functions while serving on the Executive Leadership Team, providing insights, recommendations, and financial leadership that support profitable growth across the Dobson Group's Automotive, Recreational Vehicle, Outdoor Power Equipment, Property Management, Housing, and Land Development operations.

The successful candidate will be equally comfortable closing the books, presenting financial results, building budgets, evaluating capital investments, improving systems, and advising ownership on strategic opportunities.

Key Responsibilities

You will oversee, lead and develop the finance team, including Assistant Controllers, Payroll, AP, and AR.

Lead monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting and consolidations, ensuring accurate close processes, internal controls, and compliance with accounting standards.

Own the annual budgeting process, rolling forecasts, and long-range planning; deliver dashboards, KPIs, and performance insights across divisions.

Manage cash flow forecasting, banking relationships, credit facilities, and covenant/lender reporting.

Coordinate corporate tax planning, GST/HST and payroll remittances, and CRA compliance with external advisors.

Drive process improvement and automation (Microsoft 365, Power BI, AI tools) and support ERP/DMS/CRM optimization.

Serve as a trusted financial advisor to the founders and Executive Leadership Team; support strategic planning, capital evaluation, and enterprise risk decisions.

Leadership Competencies

The Financial Controller must demonstrate:

Financial acumen

Strategic thinking

Analytical problem-solving

Leadership and team development

Accountability and integrity

Communication and influence

Continuous improvement mindset

Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree Business Administration, or related field.

Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation.

10+ years of progressive accounting/finance experience, including 5+ years in a senior finance leadership role.

Experience leading multi-company or multi-division financial operations.

Strong financial acumen, strategic thinking, and team leadership skills; proficient in Microsoft 365 and modern accounting/BI tools.

EMP makes a difference in the lives of those it serves by drastically reducing hospital admissions and greatly increasing patient satisfaction with its level of health care.

As part of EMP, your role is vital in our province's overall health. Join an integrated, multi-disciplinary team of health care professionals, dedicated to providing New Brunswickers with outstanding, highly coordinated primary health care.

## PATIENT CARE ATTENDANTS to join our team!

Horizon Health Network (Horizon) is actively recruiting Patient Care Attendants interested in pursing their careers in New Brunswick.

Patient Care Attendants are primarily responsible for taking care of a patient's basic needs. They use strong communication skills, compassion, and patience to address any patient need that comes up. Patient Care Attendants work well with all members of the health care delivery team and are responsible for assisting with the delivery of care to patients.

Horizon is one of Atlantic Canada's Top Employers of Choice, and the second largest health authority in Atlantic Canada, servicing over a half a million people.

## Why you should work here

Working for Horizon gives you flexibility in your career, an east coast lifestyle and the chance to make a big difference in the lives of New Brunswickers.

Horizon is an equal opportunity employer that values and recognizes your contributions, is dedicated to patient safety and satisfaction, has competitive pay and benefits, and offers many opportunities for professional growth.

As a Horizon employee, you will benefit from engagement programs like Years of Service and our Bravo! recognition programs. You will also see a commitment to your well-being through our safe and respectful workplace programs that include safety initiatives, workplace violence prevention, and employee wellness services.

At Horizon, a rewarding opportunity is as close as the ocean!

New Brunswick is located on Canada's beautiful east coast. It is known for its welcoming people, billion-year-old coastlines, and rich heritage of Indigenous, Anglophone and Francophone communities which have been ranked among the best places in the world to live.

You have completed a patient care program/course. You have acute training and/or experience. You have written and spoken competence in English.

2200596.title: Fredericton Area Midwifery General Application
2200596.description:
## New Brunswick Midwifery is Expanding!

We're looking for passionate midwives to join the Horizon Health Network team in Fredericton, New Brunswick. Whether you're experienced or just starting your career, we have flexible opportunities available with full-time, part-time, and casual positions.

Our midwives provide comprehensive primary maternity care in a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment. We're committed to patient and family centered care, excellence in practice, and strong teamwork.

## The Fredericton Midwifery Centre

Since implementation in 2017, midwives have worked in a unionized employee model with Horizon Health Network, providing paid vacation and sick leave, pension, health benefits, overtime and on-call pay. The Fredericton Midwifery Centre is a stand-alone clinic on Fredericton's Northside with administrative, overhead and professional development funding provided by the employer. Caseload is 3 clients per month per full time midwife, drawn from a catchment area within 1 hour of the Dr Everett Chalmers Hospital. The Chalmers is a Level 3 hospital featuring an NICU and 24/7 ER and Obstetrical coverage. Caseload selection prioritises vulnerable populations as well as clients interested in homebirth. We support both in hospital and homebirths, with a homebirth rate of approximately 30%.

Midwives work in a flexible team with a focus on work-life balance for a midwife's individual needs. Our team places a strong emphasis on teamwork and communication, both within the midwifery group and the larger interprofessional team, and on a high standard of clinical care, ensuring our clients are receiving thorough informed choice discussions containing the most current clinical guidance. Midwifery is also still a young profession in New Brunswick and thus there are many opportunities to sit on Horizon-specific, local and provincial committees.

## About Fredericton

Home to two universities and the seat of New Brunswick's government, Fredericton is a bright and family friendly place to call home. With a robust outdoor activity network including kilometers of trail systems, countless green spaces surrounding city limits, a 400-acre old growth forest in the heart of the city and the Wolastoq River flowing through its downtown, you have only to choose your adventure.

If the arts are more your scene, Fredericton boasts many art galleries, the annual Harvest Jazz and Blues Festival, as well as the Fredericton Playhouse which hosts music and performance all year round. The food and craft beer community is also lively in Fredericton, featuring many independent local restaurants and breweries. Fredericton is not far from breathtaking beachcombing spots on the Atlantic Ocean, many camping opportunities in both provincial and national parks, and only a few hours away from Prince Edward Island and Nova Scotia. With much to offer, Fredericton looks forward to welcoming you to our beautiful city!

Join us in New Brunswick and enjoy work-life balance with a laid-back East Coast lifestyle, all while benefitting from opportunities for professional growth and development!

## Responsibilities

• Provide care, assessment, and monitoring of women during normal pregnancy, labour, and the postpartum period as well as their healthy newborns.

• Provide health care in clients' homes, communities and in hospital and clinic.

• Provide care consistent with the philosophy and ethics of midwifery care in Canada

• Respect community standards of care and NB code of ethics

• Support both hospital and home births, with a home birth rate of approx. 30%

• Work well within a team and maintain positive relationships with community providers

## Qualifications

• Must be a graduate of a Canadian university midwifery education program or an equivalent in accordance with the New Brunswick Midwifery Act and Regulations

• Must be eligible to register with the Midwifery Council of New Brunswick

• Must possess a valid driver's license and own a vehicle

• Ability to attend work on a regular basis

• Ability to perform the duties of the position

• Good work record

• Willingness to undergo a criminal record check and vulnerable sector record check as condition of employment

## Benefits

• Unionized employment

• Paid vacation and sick leave

• Pension and health benefits

• Overtime and on-call pay

• Admin, overhead, and professional development funding provided by the employer

• Opportunities to sit on local and provincial committees

Join us in shaping the future of midwifery care in New Brunswick!

## Interested? Apply Today?

Horizon Health Network (Horizon) only accepts on-line applications.

## About Horizon's Recruitment Process

We thank all applicant who apply; however, only those selected for further consideration will be contacted. All interested applicants are encouraged to apply as an equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered.

Horizon's recruitment screening process may include language proficiency testing, clerical testing and/or behavioral assessment. If you are selected for testing, you will be contacted via the email address provided on your application. The official results will be shared with the candidate, Human Resources and the requesting manager electronically and language results will be placed on the personnel file for Horizon's hiring purposes.

## Diversity Statement

Horizon is committed to enhancing our diverse and inclusive environment for our employees and patients. We believe in a healthcare system that equally supports all people regardless of race, ethnicity, national origin, social background, religion, gender identity or expression, age, disability, or sexual orientation. An environment based on a commitment to diversity and inclusion supports our goal of safe and quality patient care.

## Job Title: Project Coordinator
Location: Dieppe, NB
TP - APS - 10145

Approach Navigation Systems Inc. (ANS Inc.) is a respected Canadian corporation headquartered in Dieppe, New Brunswick. With a strong presence in the aviation, marine, and highway sectors, ANS Inc. specializes in supplying, installing, and maintaining navigation, weather, and communication systems. These innovative solutions contribute significantly to enhancing transportation safety and efficiency on a global scale. Partnered with Meridia, ANS Inc. is looking to add a dynamic and motivated Project Coordinator to their growing team.

Role Description
As the Project Coordinator, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring the seamless execution of projects by coordinating project teams, maintaining project documentation, and effectively communicating with stakeholders. Your adept coordination will be instrumental in driving project success and fostering collaborative excellence across the organization.

• Ensuring project teams adhere to provided timelines and deliverables

• Maintaining comprehensive project documentation throughout the project lifecycle

• Communicating project plans, actions, risks, and issues with key stakeholders

• Swiftly resolving any challenges that arise during the project

• Building and managing strong relationships with multiple teams

• Overseeing day-to-day activities for the Project Management team

• Analyzing project data and producing progress reports for evaluation

Your Qualifications
As an individual equipped with strong project coordination skills, you possess a solid foundation for excelling in this role. Your capacity for autonomous teamwork, impeccable time management, and adaptability further enhances your profile. Proficiency in software tools, meticulous attention to detail, and standout presentation skills underscore your technical proficiency. Your adept communication and interpersonal finesse enable seamless collaboration across diverse teams and stakeholders. In this dynamic and innovative environment, your ability to navigate intricate projects and ensure positive outcomes positions you as an asset to the team.

## Your qualifications include:

• Background in engineering, engineering technology or a related field. Equivalent experience will also be credited.

• 1-3 years of project management/coordinator experience within a similar industry

• Ability to work both independently and collaboratively as part of a team

• Excellent time management skills, effectively prioritizing tasks

• Adaptability to changing environments and timelines

• Keen attention to detail to ensure accuracy and quality

• Outstanding communication and organizational skills

• Strong interpersonal skills for effective team collaboration

• Capacity to organize priorities based on deadlines

• Familiarity with specific software packages related to project coordination

• Excellent presentation skills to convey information clearly

Joining ANS isn't just about finding a job; it's about embarking on a journey that combines innovation, collaboration, and personal growth. With the chance to impact global transportation through cutting-edge solutions, collaborate with industry experts, and experience a culture that celebrates your contributions, ANS Inc. offers a unique and fulfilling career path. Here, you won't simply be an employee; you'll be a valued member of a team dedicated to reshaping the future of transportation. If you're ready to make a difference, embrace challenges, and thrive in an environment that empowers you to excel, ANS Inc. welcomes you to be a driving force in our transformative mission.

The expected salary range for this position is $45,000 - $60,000, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in paramedicine or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Advanced Care Paramedic positions.
