Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

## Duties of Position:

Provide pre?hospital clinical care prior to the arrival of a transporting ambulance when required. This work involves assessment, triage and managing patient care independently and collaboratively with ambulance crews when required.

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Primary Care Paramedics are based on the current National Occupational Competency Profile (NOCP) for Primary Care Paramedics, Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Paramedics are also expected to maintain and operate ambulances or clinical support unit (CSU) and related equipment in accordance with patient needs and public safety. Assesses, triages, and manages patient care until the arrival of an ambulance. Assist and collaborate with ambulance personnel with the provision of medical treatment, when necessary.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in paramedicine or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

Required Qualifications:

• You are entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizenship, permanent resident status or work permit);

• Primary Care Paramedic program/course of over six months;

• Must meet all legislated requirements for Paramedics in New Brunswick;

• Must be registered, active Paramedic with the Paramedic Association of New Brunswick; If you are not currently registered in New Brunswick, please visit PANB at www.panb.ca

## Who we are

The work we do has a positive impact on our communities and helps improve the everyday lives of New Brunswickers. Together, we are over 45,000 New Brunswickers who are passionate problem-solvers, who make a difference and are proud to call New Brunswick home.

The Department of Transportation and Infrastructure has a broad mandate and is committed to maintaining and improving New Brunswick's public infrastructure. • performing normal maintenance and minor repairs on assigned equipment, preparing and maintaining work records on the operation of the assigned equipment;

Equipment Operator: $29.29 per hour, based on a 40- hour week.

Medavie Health Services New Brunswick (MHSNB) is the subsidiary of Medavie Health Services responsible for the optimal operation and management of EM/ANB, an integrated organization specializing in the delivery of primary health care services with the goal of facilitating access to quality care so that patients can achieve better health outcomes. MHSNB is fortunate to be able to count on the expertise of its employees who work passionately to build a healthier province.

Our company is currently looking for new team members to support its mission of providing excellence in emergency and community care within our various programs, namely Ambulance New Brunswick, the Extra-Mural Program and NB Health Link. Each advocates for a highly coordinated, quality service offering guided by a goal of continuous improvement across primary health care.

Medavie Health Services is part of Medavie, a health services organization. Together with Medavie Blue Cross, we are committed to providing innovative solutions that will improve the health of all Canadians.

As a not-for-profit organization, Medavie is proud to commit an annual social dividend to the Medavie Health Foundation to support programs and initiatives aimed at addressing some of our country's most pressing physical and mental health care challenges.

We are looking for a Quality & Risk Consultant. Reporting to the Director, Quality & Risk, the Quality & Risk Consultant will support risk management activities of home health services and pre-hospital care. Working with all areas of the organization, our patients and their families, as well as stakeholders, the Consultant will coordinate and process patient safety incidents, complaints and other risk related activities.

The Quality & Risk Consultant will focus on preventing adverse events and near misses which could impact patients, employees and our operations. The Consultant will also ensure all necessary information is collected regarding incidents and complaints by effectively communicating with patients, their families, other healthcare providers and stakeholders.

## As the ideal candidate for this position, you:

• Have a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) degree or diploma from a practical nursing program (LPN) awarded by an accredited educational institution;

• Have a minimum of three years working in the field of quality and risk management, or in a position where managing quality and risk is part of regular activities;

• Have an understanding of investigative processes and demonstrated experience in executing quality activities and investigations;

• Possess excellent analytical skills, including the ability to think outside existing management practices/models and demonstrate foresight about potential issues and opportunities;

• Have demonstrated ability to engage others in discussions and influence decisions through clear, concise, logical and compelling communication while providing the appropriate level of depth when communicating with a diverse group;

• Have an understanding of home care health and ambulance systems and inherent safety and risk management processes;

• Have exceptional communications skills both written and verbal, including the ability to engage various diverse groups in discussions;

• Are knowledgeable of applicable federal and provincial laws and regulations relating to privacy, patient safety and risk management as well as accreditation standards; and

• Have the ability to manage difficult emotional situations either in person or via telephone with the patient, family, external stakeholders and internal staff

• Bilingualism is mandatory for this position.

The Base Pay range may vary depending on the successful candidate or other relevant job-related factors such as knowledge, skills, qualifications, experience and education/training. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Medavie employees may participate in various performance-based incentive programs. Payments under these programs are discretionary and subject to both individual and organizational results.

While Medavie may use automated tools, including AI, to support application screening, candidates are expected to complete all recruitment interactions independently-without AI assistance-to ensure a fair and equitable process.

If you are interested in working with a dynamic team of professionals and possess the necessary qualifications, please apply now.

2240880.title: Community Coordinator
2240880.employer: The Canadian Mental Health Association of New Brunswick
2240880.description:
Acadie-Bathurst region

French language proficiency is a mandatory requirement for this position, in addition to English proficiency, as some individuals accessing CMHA of NB services communicate primarily in French. Therefore, candidates must possess the necessary French and English language skills to perform the role effectively.

## About CMHA of NB

The Canadian Mental Health Association of New Brunswick Inc. (CMHA of NB) is part of a nationwide, voluntary organization that that envisions a country where mental health is a universal human right. CMHA of NB work is guided by the mission of ensuring that all people in New Brunswick experience good mental health and well-being.

CMHA of NB is STEADFAST and has long fought to improve the state of mental health in New Brunswick, yet acknowledges that the work is ongoing and remains committed to this important task. CMHA of NB is INCLUSIVE and strives for all people in New Brunswick to see themselves represented and served by CMHA of NB. The organization values the voice of those who have experienced mental illness and recognize a diverse range of mental health approaches.

CMHA of NB is PROACTIVE, with leaders who value action over mere talk, and is committed to innovation and forward-thinking to continually address and improve mental health in New Brunswick. Furthermore, CMHA of NB is COMPASSIONATE, approaching its mission with empathy, care, love, and kindness.

CMHA of NB, being COLLABORATIVE, mobilizes and marshals resources, partners, and people to come together to realize necessary changes in our communities and in the mental health system in New Brunswick. CMHA of NB provides a wide range of services and supports to people who are experiencing mental illness, their families, friends, and the public. One of the core goals of these services is to help people with mental illness develop the personal tools to lead meaningful and productive lives.

## Position Description:

The Community Coordinator is the face of the Canadian Mental Health Association (CMHA) of New Brunswick in the communities they serve. This role is essential in promoting mental health awareness, reducing stigma, and connecting individuals to valuable mental health resources. The Community Coordinator will act as a primary connector of service providers in their health zone to ensure collaboration and connection, deliver informative presentations, advocate for mental health, and assist individuals in navigating available services. This position is community-based, involving frequent interaction with the public, local organizations, and community groups.

## Key Responsibilities:

Program and Service Delivery:

• Deliver CMHA-approved presentations on mental health, mental illness, and wellness to diverse community groups.

• Coordinate and manage logistics for community-based programs, including venue selection, registration, participant communication, and evaluation.

• Facilitate self-help/support groups or provide support for existing groups in the region.

• Serve as a regional resource navigator, assisting individuals with accessing services and resources such as mental health, addictions services, and community programs.

• Identify education opportunities and promote the services of CMHANB to individuals and organizations in the relevant health zone.

Program Development, Quality, and Monitoring:

• Ensure regional programs meet established standards, quality, safety, and confidentiality requirements, including adherence to PHIPPA regulations.

• Collaborate with the team to assess and improve existing programs and services.

• Administer and evaluate programs to measure their impact and outcomes, and report findings to the direct supervisor.

• Regularly review program effectiveness with the Manager and group facilitators, addressing any challenges and proposing solutions.

Public Awareness:

• Assist in raising awareness of CMHANB programs and services through methods and processes established by CMHA of NB.

• Networking and Partnerships:

• Represent CMHANB on community and provincial committees, promoting mental health initiatives and building partnerships with relevant organizations.

• Collaborate with community agencies to ensure CMHANB services are well-integrated and avoid duplication of efforts.

• Establish and maintain partnerships with public and private sector organizations to meet the specific needs of the local community.

Administration:

• Maintain accurate records and databases, ensuring confidentiality and adherence to data management policies.

• Submit mandatory reports, case updates, and other documentation on time using appropriate systems such as Teams and caseWORKS.

• Attend scheduled team meetings and contribute to collaborative decision-making.

## Qualifications:

• A diploma or degree in social work, psychology, health promotion, education, community development, or a related field.

• Minimum of 2-3 years of experience in a related field such as mental health support, community engagement, public health education, non-profit program delivery, or other related fields.

• A combination of related work experience and education may be considered.

• Proficiency in both English and French is mandatory.

• Excellent working knowledge and skills in MS Office 365 and digital database systems is required.

• Exceptional interpersonal, networking, and relationship-building abilities.

• Strong presentation and public speaking skills tailored to diverse audiences.

• A valid Work Permit is mandatory for temporary residents.

• Residency in New Brunswick (NB) or willingness to relocate is mandatory.

• A new Criminal Record and Vulnerable Sector Check is mandatory.

## Core Competencies:

• Interpersonal Relationship

• Networking

• Communication

• Service Orientation

• Self-Development

• Accountability

• Values, Ethics, Integrity

• Equity, Diversity, Inclusion, and Belonging (EDI)

If you're looking for a place where you can grow your healthcare career while building a healthy, well-rounded life, look no further.

New Brunswick communities offer affordable housing, a low cost of living, vibrant culture, and a rich east coast lifestyle that is never far from the city. Our people are the heart of our organization. We have more than 14,000 dedicated employees working with over 1,000 physicians, and play a major role in research, education, innovation and health and wellness.

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

## Duties of Position:

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Advanced Care Paramedics are based on the current National Occupational Competency Profile (NOCP) for Advanced Care Paramedics,Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in paramedicine or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Advanced Care Paramedic positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

Required Qualifications:

• You are entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizenship, permanent resident status or work permit)

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record

1862093.title: Saltwater Marine Site Manager
1862093.description:
Kelly Cove Salmon Ltd., a division of Cooke Aquaculture Inc., a dynamic and growing east coast family company, with Platinum Member status in Canada's Best Managed Companies Program, is offering a unique opportunity for a highly motivated individual to join the Company's team as Aquaculture Site Manager based on Grand Manan, NB. This position reports to the Saltwater Production Manager.

Cooke is a global seafood company with operations in North America, Europe, and South America. Our company's success is driven by our dynamic, highly-skilled and innovative management team, supported by dedicated employees who live in coastal communities and contribute to the local area's economy and sense of community.

The Role:
This position requires a degree of specialized expertise and skill in maintaining established standards of safety, quality and accuracy. The successful candidate will have the drive, determination and a self-disciplined approach to achieving results that meet the established criteria.

As a leader, you will be responsible and accountable for the performance and results of the aquaculture farm. Through successful leadership, you will motivate staff by creating a positive and safe work environment while having the ability to exercise the necessary authority to assure policies and procedures are followed and time frames are met.

The successful candidate will have proven experience in farming operations and strong supervisory and communication skills. Must possess strong abilities in fish husbandry, and have experience with monitoring and operating feed systems, mooring design and maintenance, and general maintenance on saltwater equipment, cages and vessels. Working flexible hours outside and on the water is a requirement for this position. Preference will be given to applicants with related post-secondary education, MED, small craft certification and experience operating saltwater fish farms.

The Opportunity:
The role description is just one part of the story. This is an opportunity to grow, to work within the parameters of the role but to reach your fullest potential. We are a team that is driven to succeed. We count performance, we reward contribution and we recognize talent.

It is about being at the center of a global leader in seafood and knowing you are part of that growth. The ability to bring your passion for learning, desire for growth and energy for moving your career forward is what we offer.

The Why:
Why Cooke? Simple - we are a company that rewards initiative, resourcefulness and work ethic. We will champion your growth and provide you with the platform to create your path, your career, and your future.

*As per company policy, a clear result of a pre-employment criminal background check.

*Salary commensurate with experience which includes a competitive health and dental benefits package.

NOTE: The recruiter is reviewing and interviewing eligible applicants for this position as they are received. If you are interested in this posting, you are encouraged to apply as soon as possible.

We thank all candidates for their interest, however, only those selected for interviews will be contacted.

2238714.title: Executive Director
2238714.description:
## Position Overview

The Chapman Group is helping its client, Saint John Newcomers Centre, hire its next Executive Director. Reporting to the Board of Directors through the Board Chair, the Executive Director provides strategic leadership, organizational direction, and full accountability for SJNC's mission, people, operations, and organizational performance. The Executive Director is responsible for the organization's financial sustainability, program quality, community trust, organizational culture, and effective governance. This is an ideal opportunity for a community-oriented leader with a strong record of organizational and people leadership, a demonstrated commitment to inclusion, and the ability to work effectively across government, employer, funder, and community relationships.

The successful candidate will be a strategic, people-focused, and culturally responsive leader who builds trust, strengthens relationships, supports employees, and advances SJNC's mission. They will understand the realities of nonprofit leadership and be able to lead effectively in a complex and evolving community environment.

Qualifications

## Education

• Post-secondary education in a relevant field such as community development, public administration, business, social work, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.

## Leadership & Professional Experience

• Significant progressive leadership experience in a nonprofit, community, public-sector, or similarly mission-driven organization, with demonstrated responsibility for people, organizational performance, and strategic priorities.

• Demonstrated success leading, motivating, and developing diverse teams and building a healthy, inclusive organizational culture.

• Understanding of nonprofit or community-based work, including the ability to balance organizational priorities, service demands, employee wellbeing, and available resources.

• Track record of significant budget and grant management experience.

• Experience building and maintaining effective partnerships across government, employer, funder, and community sectors.

• Experience working with diverse communities, including newcomer, low-income, racialized, and multicultural communities.

• Strong communication, presentation, and public representation skills, with the cultural awareness to work effectively across diverse communities and perspectives.

## Language & Multicultural Communication

• English-French bilingualism is considered an asset.

• Awareness of multilingual workplace and community dynamics and a commitment to accessible, inclusive communication are important.

• Additional language skills and experience working across languages and cultures are considered assets.

## Compensation

The compensation range is $85,000-$100,000 annually, commensurate with the candidate's knowledge, skills and experience.

## About Us

The Saint John Multicultural and Newcomers Resource Centre, commonly known as the Saint John Newcomers Centre (SJNC), is a community hub that supports and empowers newcomers and their families in the Saint John region. Our mission is to serve as that hub by providing coordinated and responsive supports that enable newcomers to build successful lives and contribute meaningfully to the community. We are guided by a vision of an inclusive region where everyone belongs and thrives.

SJNC works alongside community partners to strengthen both social and economic outcomes while contributing to a growing and vibrant region. Our work is grounded in respect, equity, and inclusion, ensuring every individual is valued and that diverse voices are welcomed, heard, and empowered. Through service excellence, innovation, collaboration, and integrity, we deliver accountable, evidence-informed solutions that respond to the evolving needs of our community.

## Application

Candidates are invited to submit a résumé and cover letter outlining their interest in the position and relevant experience, including one concrete example of their leadership experience

Responsibilities

## Strategic Leadership

• Identify and pursue opportunities to grow programs, partnerships, and community impact, ensuring the organization has a clear direction and is positioned for long-term success.

• Lead the development, implementation, and monitoring of strategic plans and organizational priorities.

• Anticipate emerging issues, opportunities, and external developments that may affect SJNC, its programs, or the communities it serves, and position the organization to respond appropriately.

• Ensure responsible stewardship of organizational resources and funders' investments.

• Provide the Board with timely, transparent, and meaningful reporting on organizational performance, finances, risks, strategic priorities, and emerging issues to support effective governance and informed decision-making.

## Community Leadership

• Provide a grassroots space for newcomer voices to be heard and represented in our communities and in civic and government institutions.

• Build and maintain strong relationships and partnerships with government, employers, funders, community partners, donors, sponsors, and philanthropic partners to advance SJNC's mandate and strategic priorities.

• Represent newcomer communities and organizational interests through advocacy, public visibility and relevant community, regional, and public forums.

• Maintain awareness of global events, conflicts, and emerging issues affecting newcomer communities locally, and support culturally sensitive, well-informed organizational responses and communication.

## Organizational and People Leadership

• Lead resource development efforts, including funding proposals, funder relationships, and diversification of revenue.

• Foster an inclusive, accountable, transparent, and psychologically safe workplace culture where employees feel respected, supported, connected to the mission, and able to sustain healthy workloads and professional growth.

• Lead and inspire a multicultural team with humility, curiosity, and adaptability, valuing diverse perspectives, listening actively, encouraging collaboration, and navigating organizational dynamics and change effectively.

• Oversee effective HR practices and organizational capacity, including recruitment, performance management, employee development, succession planning, and structures and resources that support strong service delivery.

• Ensure appropriate operational and financial oversight in partnership with the Board and leadership team

2224065.title: General Surgeon
2224065.description:
Horizon Health Network is seeking a General Surgeon to join our collegial and collaborative team in beautiful Upper River Valley, New Brunswick.

## Why you should work here

Horizon Health Network is the largest health authority in the region, employing dedicated professionals focused on delivering high-quality care. Our employees collaborate with community partners to provide accessible health programs and services to over half a million people through our 12 hospitals and more than 100 medical facilities and clinics.

Situated west-centrally in New Brunswick, the Upper River Valley area, including the Town of Woodstock and the Town of Hartland, Horizon's Upper River Valley Hospital serves a catchment population of 45,000. Many sites in this region are situated along the majestic St. John River valley and all sites are within driving distance of the province's historic capital, Fredericton.

The hospital provides services to the Town of Woodstock, Town of Hartland several villages and other surrounding communities. The community's economy is mainly based on natural resources and farming industries. The area has a diverse population distribution that is 60% rural and 40% urban.

The Upper River Valley Hospital is the newest hospital in New Brunswick. It has been designated as the first full-service hospital in Canada to be recognized as a leader in energy and environmental design.

## Incentives & Remuneration

Remuneration is via an alternative funding plan (AFP) arrangement.

Successful applicants may be eligible to receive the following:

• Rural recruitment incentive of $100,000.00 with a 4-year return of service.

• Moving expense reimbursement is also available.

## What you will do

• Perform both elective and emergency general surgical operations.

• Provide outpatient services for the assessment and management of patients including clinics and minor OR cases.

• Provide inpatient care including daily rounds on patients.

• Provide consultations to hospital-based patients as requested by medical or hospital staff.

• Maintain a private office for elective consultations and visits.

• Teaching responsibilities for residents, medical students, and others as appropriate.

• Collaborate with the interdisciplinary team to address staff and patient education needs.

• Participate in the use of departmental and corporate evidence-based rules of practice to ensure that expected standards of care are achieved.

• Participate in the on-call rota of the Division of General Surgery.

• Within the confines of this scope of practice and position description, provide other duties that may arise by circumstance and may be assigned by the Chief of the Department of Surgery, the Chief of Staff, Medical Director and/or Vice President of Medical Affairs.

## Who you are

• Must be eligible for license to practice medicine in the Province of New Brunswick.

• Must be eligible for membership with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of New Brunswick.

• Must be eligible for malpractice insurance from the Canadian Medical Protective Association (CMPA), or equivalent, appropriate to the category of practice.

• Excellent communication, interpersonal and team-building skills.

• Good attendance and work record.

## Interested? Apply Today!

If you have questions, please email physiciancareers@horizonnb.ca with the subject "Application for General Surgery, Upper River Valley".

COMPETITION NUMBER PC23024
CLASSIFICATION NAME Registered Nurse Class D
POSITION TITLE Nurse Practitioner - NB Health Link (NBHL)
CLASSIFICATION CODE RNCD
BARGAINING UNIT NBNU
UNIT LOCATION Various locations across the province
STATUS Casual
FULL TIME EQUIVALENT 0
HOURS OF WORK Starting 0800hr to 1600hr Monday-Friday. Subject to change due to operational requirements.
ANTICIPATED START DATE As soon as possible
ANTICIPATED END DATE Not applicable
SALARY RANGE As per collective agreement

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

NB Health Link (NBHL) leverages technological solutions and innovative clinical delivery models to provide access to care for New Brunswickers who don't have a family doctor or nurse practitioner. The program provides patients who are registered with the program access to a network of family doctors and nurse practitioners throughout the province - offering in-person, telephone and online appointments in both official languages.

As part of NBHL, your role is vital in our province's overall health. Join an integrated team of health care professionals, dedicated to providing New Brunswickers with outstanding, highly coordinated primary health care.

## JOB SUMMARY

The Nurse Practitioner (NP) is a generalist who offers quality and relevant care across the health continuum and throughout the patient's lifespan, including health promotion, disease and injury, prevention, curative, supportive, rehabilitative, and palliative care within an interdisciplinary team of health providers.

The service model is based on the principles of primary health care with the goal of supporting communities in meeting their health care needs.

As a key member of the NB Health Link team, the NP is responsible and accountable for their practice and professional conduct while working in collaboration with physicians to ensure quality and relevant care.

As an EM/ANB employee, the NPs are accountable to our patients and families and co-workers by participating in and supporting safety related initiatives as well as acting in a manner that fosters a culture of learning. Safety for patients, caregivers, and workplace are kept the priority.

## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Integrates a broad knowledge base and critical appraisal in determining and communicating the diagnosis and the patient's needs.

• Applies advanced assessment techniques, critical thinking and clinical decision-making skills when assessing patients.

• Systematically collects documents and critically analyzes health data by performing a holistic health assessment using multiple tools and sources of data.

• Completes a prescription accurately and completely according to relevant legislation, standards, and policies.

• Orders diagnostic imaging tests, laboratory and other tests when clinically indicated and in accordance with the Nurse Practitioner Schedules and program guidelines for Ordering.

• Promotes health and reduces the risk of complications, illness, and injury for patients.

• Ensures that diagnostic tests are interpreted, and results are acted upon in an appropriate and timely manner.

• Monitor the ongoing therapy of patients with chronic stable illnesses.

• Screen for the presence of chronic illnesses and works in collaboration with physicians who identified presence of chronic illness in patients.

• Monitors the effectiveness of interventions.

• Facilitates the patient's transition within and between health care settings, e.g., admitting,

• transferring, and discharging patients.

• Ability to work independently and as part of the interdisciplinary team including making appropriate referrals.

• Documents clinical data, assessment findings, diagnosis, plan of care, therapeutic intervention (including consent), patients' response and clinical rationale in a timely and accurate manner in the patient health record.

• Maintain a positive working relationship with the interdisciplinary team.

• Help build protocols and templates in prevention medicine for the program.

• Responsibilities to support the core provincial program will be the primary task.

• Other responsibilities may be assigned to support the program.

## REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND OTHER JOB REQUIREMENTS:

• Bachelor's Degree in Nursing and successful completion of a postgraduate Nurse Practitioner program in Primary Health Care.

• Registered as a Nurse Practitioner with the Nurses Association of New Brunswick

• Current Basic Life Saving certificate and maintain certification.

• At least 2 years' experience in primary health care setting in Community Health Centre or Collaborative Practice.;

• Excellent interpersonal, oral and written communication skills;

• Demonstrated organizational and leadership skills;

• Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with other members of a team toward common goals;

• Demonstrated ability to function independently in the role with recognized decision-making and problem-solving skills;

• Demonstrated ability to critically analyze theory and research literature and apply to practice;

• Demonstrated ability to integrate a determinants of health approach into care delivery;

• Actively participates as a team member to provide comprehensive care to all patients;

• Must be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record;

• Adherence to professional ethical principles.

• Skillful use of computer tools and Microsoft Office Programs.

All interested applicants are encouraged to apply as an equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered.

We would like to thank all candidates for expressing interest. Please note only those selected for interviews will be contacted.

NBHL is committed to the principle of equal opportunity in its employment practices and to providing an environment free from discrimination and harassment for all employees.

Working at Service New Brunswick is more than just a job — it's an opportunity to build a meaningful career. Guided by our vision of "Elevating Service Excellence", our teams provide high-quality, innovative public services for customers with a focus on value for all New Brunswickers.

Known for our people-oriented workplace culture, we foster an environment where innovation, inclusivity, and teamwork are celebrated. We are proud to be recognized as one of Atlantic Canada's Top Employers for 2026!

At SNB, our people are at the heart of everything we do. We are:

• Human-Centered: We prioritize well-being and flexibility for our employees.

• Driven by Growth: We invest in your professional development and career advancement.

• Celebrating Excellence: We recognize and reward outstanding contributions.

• United by Purpose: Every project you work on makes a real difference for New Brunswickers.

## SNB also offers a comprehensive employee benefits package.

Your responsibilities will include but are not limited to:

• Ensuring that customers are able to resume their work as quickly as possible following a disruption to an IT service, minimizing the adverse impact on business operation

• Receiving, prioritizing, documenting, and actively resolving end-user requests

Subject to the response, an equivalent combination of training and experience may be considered.

Written and spoken competence in English and French is required.

• ITIL certification

• Experience supporting basic computer hardware

• Experience supporting Windows, Android and IOS operating Systems

• Extensive application support experience

• Experience with a range of diagnostic utilities

• Experience with Microsoft Office 365

• Experience with anti-virus/anti-spyware tools

Applicants must clearly demonstrate the essential qualifications to be given further consideration. Resumes should be in chronological order specifying education and employment in months and years including relevant part-time and full-time employment.

BEHAVIOURAL COMPETENCIES: The successful candidate will possess the following behavioral competencies:

• Client Service Orientation

• Effective Interactive Communication

• Initiative

• Teamwork and Cooperation

• Analytcal Thinking and Judgement

TECHNICAL COMPETENCIES: The successful candidate will possess the following technical competencies:

• Specialized Subject Matter Expertise and Knowledge

• Ability to Use Office Technology, Software and Applications

• Written Communication

Resumes should be in chronological order specifying education and employment in months and years including part-time and full-time employment.

Salary : $49,244 - $68,744 annually – Pay Band 2 - Management and Non-Union Pay Plan

We encourage applicants to apply online by clicking here before September 15th 2026 indicating competition number R85-206/27-371. In the unlikely event that you experience technical difficulties or are unable to complete your application online, contact People and Culture.

We thank all those who apply however only those selected for further consideration will be contacted. This competition may be used to fill future vacancies at the same level within the same work location.

Candidates registered with the Equal Employment Opportunity Program and veterans, who demonstrate they are among the most qualified, shall be given preference at the time of appointment.

2238727.description:
Pay: CA$65-75.00 per hour (pay commensurate with experience and training)

Job description: Mental Health Therapist (MSW or LCT) in Fredericton, New Brunswick

About Us

Dr. Hilary Cartwright & Associates is a growing private practice providing individualized therapy and assessment services for children, adolescents, young adults, and their families. Our approach is grounded in research evidence and is designed to be both gender-affirming and inclusive of neurodiversity. We are committed to centering our clients' lived experiences without stigmatization or over-pathologizing, working from a strengths-informed perspective to create a safe, collaborative, and compassionate space for young people and their families.

About the Role

We are currently seeking a clinical therapist, registered as either an MSW or LCT, to provide individual therapy with children, adolescents, and young adults, and parent consultation services. In this position, the therapist will be remunerated on a per-session basis.

Our focus is on neuroaffirming therapy to support young people and their families with a range of concerns including developmental disabilities (including autism, attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), learning disorders, and intellectual disabilities), mood and anxiety disorders, obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), trauma, and gender identity. However, as our practice evolves, so do our specializations- so, if you have unique training in a particular area, we welcome you to apply!

This position will be based in-person at our new practice location here in Fredericton, NB with flexibility to work from home on occasion and offer virtual sessions.

· Excellent health care benefits package

· Competitive compensation

· Referrals from a waiting list

· Training in evidence-based therapeutic techniques such as ACT, DBT, CBT

2241073.title: Expression of Interest: Pay Band 4/5 - Federal-Provincial-Territorial Secretariat Opportunity
2241073.description:
NEW BRUNSWICK HOUSING CORPORATION

EXPRESSION OF INTEREST: Pay Band 4/5
Open Competition - Temporary Opportunity
Federal-Provincial-Territorial Secretariat Opportunity

Housing New Brunswick (HNB) is seeking expressions of interest from Pay Band 4 and 5 employees for roles in contributing to the development of an FPT Secretariat. Over the next few years, HNB will be preparing to assume a stronger leadership role in FPT housing collaboration, requiring strong coordination, policy analysis, strategic advice, and relationship management across many levels of government. This initiative aims to identify employees for temporary assignments, projects, development opportunities, or future roles within the evolving Secretariat.

## About the Opportunity:

The FPT Secretariat will help advance New Brunswick's housing priorities through effective intergovernmental coordination, clear advice to senior leaders, and timely support for national and regional housing discussions. The Secretariat will work closely with HNB teams, partners across the Government of New Brunswick, federal departments and other provinces and territories. This is an opportunity to gain exposure to high-priority intergovernmental work, strengthen briefing and policy skills, and contribute directly to Housing New Brunswick's readiness for future FPT leadership responsibilities while helping to shape a team that will become increasingly important to the organization over the coming years.

## Key Areas of Work:

• Support preparation for FPT, Provinces and Territories (PT), Assistant Deputy Minister (ADM), Deputy Minister and Minister-level meetings, including briefing notes, speaking notes, agendas, decision materials, and follow-up summaries.

• Leadership and collaboration on national working groups, including organizing facilitating and driving the agenda for multi-jurisdictional meetings to align strategic housing initiatives across regions.

• Development and delivery of high impact presentations for senior executives, intergovernmental partners, and stakeholder forums. Presentations must effectively communicate key insights, progress metrics, and strategic opportunities, and should reflect a high standard of analytical and visual clarity.

• Track federal, provincial and territorial housing developments, commitments, risks and opportunities relevant to New Brunswick.

• Coordinate input from HNB divisions and other departments to support clear and consistent provincial positions.

• Assist with federal agreement management, action plans, reporting, claims, performance tracking and related governance materials.

• Cross-jurisdictional analysis and reporting: includes performing in-depth jurisdictional analysis of housing policies, funding allocations, and performance outcomes and will involve synthesizing complex data sets to provide evidence-based insights and recommendations to senior leadership and working groups.

• Build and maintain strong working relationships with internal and external partners.

## Need to have:

• A bachelor's degree in business, sociology, or a related field and four (4) or five (5) years of related work experience. An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience may be considered.

• Written and spoken competence in English and French is required. Some positions only require English. Please state your language capability.

Applicants must clearly demonstrate the essential qualifications to be given further consideration. Please ensure that preferred language for assessment is identified on your resume.

## Behavioral Competencies:

The successful candidate will possess the following leadership competencies:

• Strategic Thinking

• Effective Interactive Communication

• Relationship / Network Building

• Analytical Thinking/Judgment

• Organizational Awareness

## Technical Competencies:

The successful candidate will possess the following technical competencies:

• Policy and Research Analysis

• Planning and Organizing Skills

• Written Communication

• Consulting Skills

• Project Management

## Who Should Apply

This opportunity may be a good fit for employees who are curious, organized, collaborative and interested in housing policy, federal funding programs and intergovernmental work, even if they do not have direct FPT experience. Candidates should be comfortable working in a fast-paced environment, managing competing deadlines, synthesizing information, and preparing clear written materials for senior decision-makers.

Ideal candidates will bring some combination of the following:

• Strong writing, research and analytical skills with good judgment, discretion and attention to detail.

• Experience preparing briefing notes, decision documents, meeting materials or policy advice.

• Ability to work across teams and build effective relationships.

• Intergovernmental relations or corporate coordination.

• Ability to organize information, track commitments and support follow-up on complex files.

• Comfort working with ambiguity and helping build new processes as the Secretariat develops.

Employees are encouraged to discuss their interest with their manager before applying.

Submitting an expression of interest does not ensure placement but may identify employees for future opportunities based on organizational needs and feasibility.

Interested employees are asked to submit a brief expression of interest outlining:

• Why you are interested in supporting the FPT Secretariat.

• Relevant experience, skills or strengths you would bring to the work.

• Any areas of development you are hoping to strengthen through this opportunity.

## Wage:

Pay Band 4 - $ 59, 644 - $ 83, 408 annually.
Pay Band 4 - $ 68, 276 - $ 95, 342 annually.

## How to apply:

We encourage applicants to apply online at www.ere.gnb.ca, by mail at the following address, or by email at HumanResources.sd@gnb.ca by October 9, 2026, indicating competition number R37-2026-27-20. This competition may be used to fill future vacancies at the same level.

2239995.description:
## GEOSPATIAL SPECIALIST

## OPEN COMPETITION

## DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH

## PERMANENT

## FREDERICTON

## (An alternate work location in New Brunswick may be considered)

The Department of Health is seeking an individual to join the Shared Analytics Branch as a Geospatial Specialist in Fredericton.

Reporting to the Manager of Analytics Response Management, the successful candidate will be responsible for designing, testing, and conducting geo-analysis of complex health system issues and identification of population health insights to assist in the planning of current and future Departmental projects. The successful candidate will also be responsible for communicating results and insights to various stakeholders and decision-makers as well as represent the Department on various federal/provincial/territorial, interdepartmental, intradepartmental and multi-stakeholder committees.

## As a Geospatial Specialist, you will be responsible for:

• Developing and conducting spatial health analysis using GIS/mapping software;

• Applying statistical, epidemiological, and algorithmic techniques to spatial analysis;

• Providing interpretation of complex data and results;

• Discovering patterns and trends through spatial mapping of data;

• Designing digital maps with geographic data and other data sources;

• Producing reports and presentations of geographic data utilizing data visualizations;

• Preparing large and varied administrative datasets for analysis;

• Manipulating data sets using various statistical and data management software;

• Developing and promoting the Geospatial program and GIS Governance within the health system;

• Participating on GIS working groups and work with data source stakeholders/partners.

## Who you are:

You are comfortable and effective working with executives, external stakeholders, clients and all levels of the organization. You are at your best when you are challenged and thrive on getting results. You are recognized for your attention to detail, organization skills, and ability to prioritize deliverables. You have well-developed writing skills to prepare material where interpretation, analysis, assessment and creativity, requiring the knowledgeable use of terminology and precise articulation of ideas or opinions, is necessary to effectively communicate.

## Essential Qualifications:

• Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Geography, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Computer Science or Engineering, or a related area;

• A minimum of five (5) years of related work experience to include two (2) years working with large administrative data sets;

• Experience with data manipulation software such as SPSS, SAS, Stata, R, and/or Python and experience with ESRI's GIS & Mapping tools;

• An equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered.

2214969.description:
Imagine a playground in Atlantic Canada surrounded by fresh waterways on one side and the ocean on the other. Come live and belong to a community where families can raise their children in a safe, close-knit environment with a reasonable cost of living.

Horizon Health Network is seeking Oncology Physicians to join our collaborative teams in beautiful New Brunswick, Canada!

## Why you should work here

Horizon Health Network is the largest health authority in the region, employing dedicated professionals focused on delivering high-quality care. Our employees collaborate with community partners to provide accessible health programs and services to over half a million people through our 12 hospitals and more than 100 medical facilities and clinics.

New Brunswick offers a safe, welcoming community and a relaxed lifestyle enriched by its Indigenous, Anglophone, and Francophone heritage. Whether by the ocean, a river, or a lake, you'll find an ideal place to call home—complete with short commutes, plenty of recreation, and space to enjoy with family and pets. At Horizon, you'll build a meaningful career that makes a difference while embracing the desirable East Coast lifestyle.

## Incentives & Remuneration

Successful applicants may be eligible to receive the following:

• Urban recruitment incentive of $50,000.00 with a return of service or Rural recruitment incentive of $100,000 with a return of service

• Moving expense reimbursement is also available.

Remuneration will be determined in accordance with the specific role and practice location. Additional details will be shared as the recruitment process progresses.

## What you will do

The Oncology Physician will join a well-established team of oncologists at one of our facilities. This full-time position offers an opportunity to provide high-quality, comprehensive medical care, with opportunities to participate in subspecialty activities catering to the applicant's interest. Opportunities and responsibilities may include:

• Provide high-quality care for patients with a range of oncological conditions across inpatient, outpatient, and emergency settings

• Collaborate closely with referring physicians and multidisciplinary care teams to ensure coordinated oncology care

• Participate in departmental quality improvement initiatives and service development

• Contribute to teaching, academic activities, and mentorship of medical learners

• Support the ongoing advancement of oncology services in New Brunswick.

## Who you are

• Medical degree from a recognized institution.

• Certification in Medical Oncology with the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada (FRCPC) or equivalent.

• Candidates must be eligible for licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of New Brunswick.

• Proficiency in English is required. Bilingual skills would be considered an asset.

• Interest in academic practice, teaching, or subspecialisation in oncology is considered an asset.

## Diversity Statement

Horizon is committed to enhancing our diverse and inclusive environment for our employees and patients. We believe in a healthcare system that equally supports all people regardless of race, ethnicity, national origin, social background, religion, gender identity or expression, age, disability, or sexual orientation. An environment based on a commitment to diversity and inclusion supports our goal of safe and quality patient care

## Interested? Apply Today!

If you have questions and/or to apply, please email physiciancareers@horizonnb.ca with the subject "Application for Oncology"

2240138.description:
The Financial and Consumer Services Commission (Commission) is a leader in integrated financial and consumer services regulation. The Commission's mandate is to protect consumers and enhance public confidence in the financial and consumer marketplace through the provision of regulatory and educational services. With offices in both Fredericton and Saint John, it is responsible for the administration and enforcement of provincial legislation regulating mortgage brokers, payday lenders, real estate, securities, insurance, pensions, credit unions, trust and loan companies, cooperatives, unclaimed property, and a wide range of consumer legislation. The Commission is a self funded Crown corporation responsible for the administration and enforcement of financial consumer services legislation.

We offer opportunities for dedicated professionals to play a vital role in carrying out our mandate.

## Investigator - Enforcement Division (Fredericton or Saint John Office)

We are seeking an experienced Investigator to join our Enforcement Division. Reporting to the Director of Enforcement, this position is responsible for investigating suspected breaches of New Brunswick Financial and Consumer Services legislation through the application of investigative, intelligence gathering, digital evidence analysis, and open-source intelligence (OSINT) techniques.

The successful candidate will assess complaints and referrals, develop investigative strategies, gather and analyze evidence, conduct interviews, support enforcement proceedings, and collaborate with regulatory and law enforcement partners. This role also contributes to identifying emerging risks and protecting New Brunswick consumers and investors.

## Your Focus:

• Assessing complaints, referrals, and intelligence, and developing investigative strategies;

• Conducting investigations into potential violations of financial and consumer services legislation;

• Gathering, analyzing, and preserving documentary, digital, and testimonial evidence;

• Conducting OSINT and digital investigations to identify evidence, intelligence, and emerging risks;

• Support enforcement proceedings through the preparation of reports, evidence, and testimony;

• Building relationships with regulators, law enforcement agencies, and other stakeholders to support investigations and intelligence sharing; and

• Monitoring emerging trends, technologies, and investigative practices to strengthen enforcement activities and regulatory outcomes.

## What you Bring

• Community College diploma and/or certificate in Criminology, Specialized training in Commerce, Accounting, Finance, Economics, Law, Data Analytics, or Intelligence Studies.

• Professional certification or specialized training in investigations, intelligence analysis, digital forensics, OSINT, fraud examination, compliance, or financial crime investigations is an asset.

• 3-5 years investigative experience in a regulatory, law enforcement, compliance, financial services or consumer protection environment.

• Good working knowledge of financial and consumer protection legislation.

• Experience conducting complex investigations, assessing evidence, and preparing investigative reports and recommendations.

• Demonstrated experience conducting investigative interviews and collecting, documenting and preserving evidence;

• Knowledge of internet and social media investigations, digital evidence handling, and; OSINT tools and techniques;

• Strong written and oral communication skills in both official languages are required.

## Additional Strengths

• Knowledge of AI-assisted research and investigative technologies, experience with cryptocurrency, blockchain analysis, digital asset or forensic investigations, and experience using case management systems is an asset.

The Financial and Consumer Services Commission offers a competitive salary and benefit package as well as excellent opportunities for personal growth and challenge. Salary will be commensurate with experience. If you are interested in being a key part of this team, please forward your résumé and covering letter.

Salary Range: $75,482 to $103,787 (annual compensation)

As a condition of employment, the successful candidate will be required to undergo a pre-employment background check in accordance with the Commission's Pre-Employment Background Checks Directive. This may include criminal record checks, credential verification, and reference checks.

For more information about this position please visit our website at www.fcnb.ca or call the Talent Acquisition Specialist at (506) 643-7790.

Please note that only candidates selected for further evaluation will be contacted.

2208989.title: Accounting Project Manager
2208989.description:
Cooke is a global seafood company with operations in North America, Europe, South America and Australia. Our company's success is driven by our dynamic, highly skilled, and innovative management team, supported by dedicated employees who live in coastal communities and contribute to the local area's economy and sense of community.

## The Role

We are hiring an Accounting Project Manager to join our team of dedicated accounting professionals. In this role, you will support multiple Cooke projects, ensuring that accounting requirements are met and that the project teams are supported.

This position offers the perfect blend of core accounting knowledge and hands-on project experience on a global scale, including system implementations and process improvement initiatives. You'll have the opportunity to work with international teams and gain insight into how accounting and systems operate across different regions.

This role can be based in either our Saint John, NB or Blacks Harbour, NB office.

## Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

• Representing the accounting team on multiple initiatives, including system rollouts and process improvement efforts.

• Facilitating working sessions with the accounting team to understand, document, and validate requirements.

• Understanding and communicating gaps between accounting needs and project scope and collaborating with cross-functional teams to drive resolution.

• Defining and managing detailed functional tasks to meet project deliverables. Ensuring resource requirements are communicated, and issues are escalated and solved in a timely manner.

• Completing project status updates on a weekly / as required basis.

• Managing testing phases, and ensuring that any issues are identified, communicated, and resolved.

• Creating training materials and delivering sessions to new users.

• Leading go-live activities and contributing to change management.

## To be successful in this role you will have:

• 5-8 years of accounting experience with a solid understanding of financial processes and reporting, ideally including involvement in system implementations and process improvement initiatives.

• University degree in Business, Finance, or a related field

• Professional Accounting Designation (CPA or equivalent) preferred.

• Advanced Microsoft Excel skills.

• Strong process improvement mindset.

• Excellent communication and problem-solving skills.

• Industry experience in manufacturing, aquaculture, or food processing is considered an asset.

• Ability to travel outside of Canada.

Join our team and enjoy the benefits of full-time year-round employment with competitive rates and a comprehensive benefits package tailored to support your well-being and career growth.

## Benefits Package:

• Health Benefits: Includes coverage for dental, vision, and extended medical care.

• Insurance: Life and disability insurance provided for financial security.

• Support Services: Access to an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

• Financial Planning: Opportunity for RRSP matching to support your retirement savings.

• Time Off: Paid vacation, holidays, and sick leave for work-life balance.

• Wellness: Wellness programs and access to on-site gym facilities (available in some locations).

• Career Development: Professional growth opportunities and avenues for advancement.

• Perks: Employee discounts on company products or services.

• Convenience: On-site parking or parking allowance.

If you're looking to join a supportive team environment with opportunities for personal and professional development, apply now and become part of our dynamic team.

## The Why

Why Cooke? Simple - because we are a company that rewards initiative, resourcefulness, and work ethic. We will champion your growth and provide you with the platform to create your path, your career, and your future.

NOTE: The recruiter is reviewing and interviewing eligible applicants for this position as they are received. If you are interested in this posting, you are encouraged to apply as soon as possible.

Responsibilities
The Student Life Officer is responsible for the planning, delivery, and evaluation of sporting, recreation, social, cultural, leisure, fundraising, wellness and volunteer student activities that enhance the quality of student life for NBCC students.

With direction provided by the Executive of the Local Campus Union and the NBCCSU General Manager, the Student Life Officer is responsible for the following key areas:

## Student Life:

• Assist in the planning, developing and implementation of the local campus annual business plan encompassing social, cultural and athletic events and cost estimates at the campus level.

• Develop and update a student events calendar in collaboration with the Executive and NBCC Staff.

• Liaise with community groups to support community events such as Run for the Cure, Dragonboat, and promote volunteerism at the campus.

• Manage extracurricular activities and events that complement NBCC's plans, i.e. Orientation of new students and Graduation.

• Ensure student committees and clubs are organized and advertised. Provide leadership to the committees/clubs, ensuring each has a terms of reference and adheres to NBCC policy. Provide budget oversight.

• Support and/or organize campus / community fundraising events.

• Organize leadership training for students through conferences, workshops and seminars.

• Coordinate with the NBCCSU and NBCC on matters related to student activities to ensure alignment with other scheduled events.

• Ensure adequate fitness activities and resources are available for students at their respective campus.

• Manage the Local NBCCSU Social Media accounts.

• Work virtually with the Student Life Officer Team to collaborate on events and ensure a similar student life experience at each campus.

## Supporting the Campus Union:

• Organize the annual student executive elections at the campus level.

• Ensure accounting policies are in place for managing the budget.

• Understand and provide guidance concerning the NBCCSU constitution, bylaws and guidelines, and assist the executive in adhering to these requirements.

• Provide guidance to the executive on its role with the students.

## Office Administration:

• Manage the flow of information from and to students, staff and community.

• Control the use of Student Union equipment, facilities and resources.

• Manage the financial aspects of the office, including events.

• Monitor the business plan, including the budget. Report any irregularities and recommend adjustments.

• Supervise any staff including practicum and summer students.

All applicants must be eligible to work in Canada at the time of application.

We promote an equal-opportunity work environment.

We welcome you to submit a detailed application and resume online by October 2, 2026. All applications will be acknowledged upon receipt.

2239491.title: Financial Controller
2239491.description:
## Financial Controller

Modern Construction, a subsidiary of the VINCI Group, was founded in 1945 and employs 160 people and operates across a range of activities, including construction and paving, asphalt production through a fixed plant, sale of aggregates with two operational quarries, trucking services and is an explosives distributor.

Modern Construction, located on the outskirts of Moncton, NB is currently looking for a financial controller. Reporting to the CFO, you will be tasked with preparing and reporting the financial data in compliance with the Group's fundamentals as well as accounting and management rules, all while meeting pre-determined deadlines.

Your main responsibilities will be as follows:

· Prepare monthly financial reports for management while analyzing and commenting on project and activity results in comparison to forecasts and operating budget.

· Prepare quarterly budgets for each center of operations with input from the management team.

· Ensure accurate and timely recording of revenues, expenses, accruals, and adjustments.

· Anticipate financial risks and proactively report budget overruns to decision-makers

· Ensure compliance with accounting standards and applicable tax and regulatory requirements.

· Prepare and coordinate year-end audit/review activities with external accountants and auditors.

· Oversee accounts receivable collections and monitor customer accounts.

· Oversee accounts payable to ensure invoices are properly approved, coded, and paid according to terms.

· Provide overall oversight of the payroll process, ensuring payroll is accurate and processed on time.

· Monitor cash position and forecast future cash requirements.

· Supervise and provide direction to the accounting staff.

· Support management with special projects and financial analysis as required.

· Assist with implementation and transition to new accounting systems (SAP).

Our ideal candidate is:

· An experienced professional with university studies in accounting (Bachelor's degree), finance or any other related field. A CPA designation would be considered an asset.

· 5+ years of similar experience in the accounting field.

· Bilingual (French and English).

· You must have a strong working knowledge of excel.

· Experience with SAP would be an advantage.

· Strong budgeting and forecasting skills, along with financial analysis.

· Have advisory skills and communication abilities that will enable you to support operational teams in achieving their budgetary objectives along with supporting your accounting team with their roles.

Most importantly, we're looking for someone who takes pride in their work, enjoys being part of a team, and is interested in building a long-term career with Modern Construction.

We offer a comprehensive compensation package, including competitive salary, performance-based bonuses, a benefits package that also includes a pension plan, health benefits, and an employee share purchase program.

If you are interested in applying for the position, please forward your resume to Lise Dupuis at lise.dupuis@moderngroup.ca

## Entity

VINCI Construction is one of the world's leading construction companies, specializing in transport infrastructure, buildings, networks, and urban development. VINCI Construction leverages a network of local businesses, specialist networks, and specific expertise in major infrastructure projects. Operating in over 100 countries, its 1,300 companies employ more than 119,000 people and generated revenue of €31.5 billion.

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

The New Brunswick Extra-Mural Program (EMP), often known as the "hospital without walls," has operated under the simple philosophy of helping New Brunswickers receive the care they need in the places where they are healthiest and happiest - their homes and communities. EMP makes a difference in the lives of those it serves by drastically reducing hospital admissions and greatly increasing patient satisfaction with its level of health care.

As part of EMP, your role is vital in our province's overall health. Join an integrated, multi-disciplinary team of health care professionals, dedicated to providing New Brunswickers with outstanding, highly coordinated primary health care.

2239964.title: AI Solutions Specialist
2239964.description:
We are looking for an AI Solutions Specialist to help Assumption Life turn AI ambitions into real business outcomes. This is a hands-on role for someone who is genuinely curious about AI, follows the space closely, and is excited to apply it in a company that serves Canadians.

Qualifications
• University degree or college diploma in Business Administration, Analytics, Information Systems, Data Science, Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

• 3+ years of professional experience working with technology in a delivery, integration, or business-improvement capacity, with a clear track record of turning ideas into working solutions.

• 1+ years of demonstrated experience building or integrating AI-enabled solutions, including agents, document automation, classification, retrieval-augmented generation, workflow automation, or API-based AI tools. Personal projects and self-directed work count.

• Strong hands-on experience with the Microsoft ecosystem, including Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Power Automate, Copilot Studio, Power Platform, Azure AI, and Microsoft Graph.

• Strong understanding of APIs, authentication, and secure integration patterns.

• Demonstrated curiosity about AI - you follow the space, experiment with new tools, and can speak to what you have explored and learned.

• Business acumen - the ability to identify where AI will create real value, and where it will not.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills in English. Some spoken French is an asset for collaboration with francophone colleagues.

Assets :

• Experience operating live solutions in production, including logging, monitoring, alerting, and incident response.

• Programming or scripting experience with tools such as Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, C#, SQL, or PowerShell.

• Experience in regulated environments, financial services, insurance, model monitoring, MLOps, or producing audit evidence.

• Familiarity with applicable Canadian regulatory guidelines for AI and model risk, responsible AI principles, or related compliance concepts.

Responsibilities
You will spend a portion of your time on research and development - exploring emerging tools, prototyping ideas, and running internal sessions to share what you learn with the broader team. The rest of your time goes into delivering solutions that work in production: AI agents, internal assistants, document automation, workflow improvements, and integrations with the systems our teams already use.

As our first dedicated AI hire, you will help shape how AI is delivered and supported at Assumption Life. You will not work alone - you will partner closely with IT Development, IT Operations, Enterprise Architecture, business teams, Information Security, Privacy, Legal and Compliance, and external vendors to make sure what we build is useful, secure, and sustainable.

Our technology environment is built on the Microsoft ecosystem - Microsoft 365, Azure, and Copilot - and this role will lean heavily on those tools while remaining open to approved third-party solutions where they bring stronger value.

• The chance to be part of a dynamic, high-performing team that adheres to the following ethical values: leadership, collaboration, trust and commitment;

• Training and development opportunities;

• A comprehensive benefits package including a competitive salary, bonus, pension and benefits;

• A dynamic location in downtown Moncton;

• A paid volunteer day;

• Time off to care for family members and pets.

2115202.description:
## Horizon Health Network is seeking full-time psychiatrists to join our team!

We have opportunities available throughout the beautiful province of New Brunswick and are looking for adult psychiatrists, child and youth psychiatrists, forensic psychiatrists, and geriatric psychiatrists.

## Why you should work here

Discover New Brunswick - a safe, welcoming province where work?life balance is truly possible. Our communities are shaped by rich Indigenous, Anglophone, and Francophone cultures, and offer your choice of ocean, river, or lakeside living. Enjoy short commutes, spacious yards, and endless outdoor activities, all while working with supportive teams who make a real difference in the lives of New Brunswickers. Horizon offers not just a career, but the east coast lifestyle so many people dream of.

Horizon Health Network is the second largest health-care organization in Atlantic Canada, operating 12 hospitals and more than 100 medical facilities, clinics and offices providing medical services ranging from acute care to community-based health services to New Brunswick, northern Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island. With 1,000 physicians, an annual budget exceeding $1 billion and approximately 13,000 employees, Horizon Health Network's strategic vision focuses on research, innovation and education.

For more information, visit the Horizon Health Network website at www.horizonnb.ca

## Incentives & Remuneration

Base salary range $305,091.15 – $370,295.10 plus fee for service billing opportunities, paid time off (vacation and education leave), health/travel insurance benefits, sick benefits, employer paid contributions to our pension plan.

Successful applicants may be eligible to receive the following:

• Recruitment incentives available:
• Urban Incentive: $50,000.00 with a 2-year return of service.

• Rural Incentive: $100,000.00 with a 4-year return of service.

• Moving expense reimbursement is available.

• Provided administrative support and office space.

## What you will do

Our ideal candidate will collaborate with other Physicians, Nursing and other Allied medical staff in the following areas:

• Community-based Addiction and Mental Health (AMH) team providing consultations and longitudinal care to patients via in-office, virtual and in-home/LTC visits

• Close collaboration with our outstanding Medicine colleagues including consultations to in-patient units

• ECT Service

All members of our department are expected to provide:

• After-hours and weekend on-call coverage for adults and children, providing care for inpatients and consultation to the emergency department (paid stipend and fee-for-service billing)

• ECT Service

• Clinical supervision of medical students and residents

(Note: These responsibilities are the basic and prime duties associated with this position; other related and allied duties may be assigned from time to time as may be necessary to the operation of Horizon Health Network.)

## Who you are

• You have a Medical Degree from a recognized medical school and postgraduate studies (residency) in the field of Psychiatry.

• You have experience in collaborative multidisciplinary Addiction and Mental Health care.

• You have Certification by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada, and a valid license through New Brunswick College of Physicians and Surgeons of New Brunswick (CPSNB) and become a member of the NB Medical Society.

• You practice medicine in a manner compatible with the Health Authority's mission, values, and strategic directions. https://horizonnb.ca/about-us/our-promise.

The physician must also meet continuing education requirements, adhere to departmental and health authority policies, comply with relevant legislation, and follow professional ethical standards set by regulatory bodies.

## Interested? Apply Today!

## Diversity Statement

Horizon is committed to enhancing our diverse and inclusive environment for our employees and patients. We believe in a healthcare system that equally supports all people regardless of race, ethnicity, national origin, social background, religion, gender identity or expression, age, disability, or sexual orientation. An environment based on a commitment to diversity and inclusion supports our goal of safe and quality patient care
