Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centers around the Maritimes and beyond.

## Duties of Position:

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Primary Care Paramedics are based on the current National Occupational Competency Profile (NOCP) for Primary Care Paramedics,Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in paramedicine or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

Required Qualifications:

• You are entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizenship, permanent resident status or work permit)

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record

• Must have a high regard for confidentiality and patient safety

• Primary Care Paramedic program/course of over six months; If you do not have one and are interested in this career, here is a list of paramedic programs in Atlantic Canada, click here

• Must be registered, active Paramedic with the Paramedic Association of New Brunswick; If you are not currently registered in New Brunswick, please visit PANB at www.panb.ca

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 4 Driver's License (or equivalent)

Additional requirements for your application:

• Current Resume and Cover Letter

• A copy of your PCP diploma from an accredited institution

• Proof of current registration with Paramedic Association of New Brunswick

• Proof of completion of a Physical Abilities Test (PAT) specific to working as a paramedic within the last 12 months

• Proof of valid CPR level C certification issued in the last 12 months

• Photocopy of front and back of valid Class 4 driver's license (or equivalent) with minimum one year driving experience

• Driver's abstract; issued within the last 30 days

• Copy of any valid Driver's course certificate i.e. CEVO, VFIS or NS VSP or equivalent issued within the last three years

• Criminal Record with Vulnerable Sector Check; issued within the last 30 days

• Immunization Record (Tetanus Tdap) within the last 10 years, 2 MMR vaccines (Measles, Mumps and Rubella) or lab evidenced immunity, 2 Varicella vaccines (Chicken Pox) or lab evidenced immunity, 3 Hepatitis B doses and Lab evidenced immunity, TB Skin Test (2 step) and a 1-step in the last 12 months; if reactive a follow up chest x-ray). Please note, a meeting with our Employee Health and Wellness Consultant can be scheduled, to ensure that all vaccinations are up to date by the time an offer is made

• Valid Official Language Assessments (oral assessment only) in both French and English from the Department of Post-secondary Education, Training and Labour. You can contact them at LS-SL@gnb.ca. Please take into account the additional time to receive your language assessment

NB Health Link (NBHL) leverages technological solutions and innovative clinical delivery models to provide access to care for New Brunswickers who don't have a family doctor or nurse practitioner. The program provides patients who are registered with the program access to a network of family doctors, physician assistants and nurse practitioners throughout the province - offering in-person, telephone and online appointments in both official languages.

As part of NBHL, your role is vital in our province's overall health. Join an integrated team of health care professionals, dedicated to providing New Brunswickers with outstanding, highly coordinated primary health care.

## JOB SUMMARY

The Nurse Practitioner (NP) is a generalist who offers quality and relevant care across the health continuum and throughout the patient's lifespan, including health promotion, disease and injury, prevention, curative, supportive, rehabilitative, and palliative care within an interdisciplinary team of health providers.

The service model is based on the principles of primary health care with the goal of supporting communities in meeting their health care needs.

As a key member of the NB Health Link team, the NP is responsible and accountable for their practice and professional conduct while working in collaboration with physicians to ensure quality and relevant care.

As an EM/ANB employee, the NPs are accountable to our patients and families and co-workers by participating in and supporting safety related initiatives as well as acting in a manner that fosters a culture of learning. Safety for patients, caregivers, and workplace are kept the priority.

## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Integrates a broad knowledge base and critical appraisal in determining and communicating the diagnosis and the patient's needs.

• Applies advanced assessment techniques, critical thinking and clinical decision-making skills when assessing patients.

• Systematically collects documents and critically analyzes health data by performing a holistic health assessment using multiple tools and sources of data.

• Completes a prescription accurately and completely according to relevant legislation, standards, and policies.

• Orders diagnostic imaging tests, laboratory and other tests when clinically indicated and in accordance with the Nurse Practitioner Schedules and program guidelines for Ordering.

• Promotes health and reduces the risk of complications, illness, and injury for patients.

• Ensures that diagnostic tests are interpreted, and results are acted upon in an appropriate and timely manner.

• Monitor the ongoing therapy of patients with chronic stable illnesses.

• Screen for the presence of chronic illnesses and works in collaboration with physicians who identified presence of chronic illness in patients.

• Monitors the effectiveness of interventions.

• Facilitates the patient's transition within and between health care settings, e.g., admitting,

• transferring, and discharging patients.

• Ability to work independently and as part of the interdisciplinary team including making appropriate referrals.

• Documents clinical data, assessment findings, diagnosis, plan of care, therapeutic intervention (including consent), patients' response and clinical rationale in a timely and accurate manner in the patient health record.

• Maintain a positive working relationship with the interdisciplinary team.

• Help build protocols and templates in prevention medicine for the program.

• Responsibilities to support the core provincial program will be the primary task.

• Other responsibilities may be assigned to support the program.

## REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND OTHER JOB REQUIREMENTS:

• Bachelor's Degree in Nursing and successful completion of a postgraduate Nurse Practitioner program in Primary Health Care.

• Registered as a Nurse Practitioner with the Nurses Association of New Brunswick

• Current Basic Life Saving certificate and maintain certification.

• At least 2 years' experience in primary health care setting in Community Health Centre or Collaborative Practice.;

• Excellent interpersonal, oral and written communication skills;

• Demonstrated organizational and leadership skills;

• Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with other members of a team toward common goals;

• Demonstrated ability to function independently in the role with recognized decision-making and problem-solving skills;

• Demonstrated ability to critically analyze theory and research literature and apply to practice;

• Demonstrated ability to integrate a determinants of health approach into care delivery;

• Actively participates as a team member to provide comprehensive care to all patients;

• Must be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record;

• Adherence to professional ethical principles.

• Skillful use of computer tools and Microsoft Office Programs.

All interested applicants are encouraged to apply as an equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered.

We would like to thank all candidates for expressing interest. Please note only those selected for interviews will be contacted.

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

## Duties of Position:

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Primary Care Paramedics are based on the current National Occupational Competency Profile (NOCP) for Primary Care Paramedics,Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in paramedicine or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

Required Qualifications:

• You are entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizenship, permanent resident status or work permit)

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record

• Must have a high regard for confidentiality and patient safety

• Primary Care Paramedic program/course of over six months; If you do not have one and are interested in this career, here is a list of paramedic programs in Atlantic Canada, click here

• Must be registered, active Paramedic with the Paramedic Association of New Brunswick; If you are not currently registered in New Brunswick, please visit PANB at www.panb.ca

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 4 Driver's Licence (or equivalent)

Additional requirements for your application:

• Current Resume and Cover Letter

• A copy of your PCP diploma from an accredited institution

• Proof of current registration with Paramedic Association of New Brunswick

• Proof of completion of a Physical Abilities Test (PAT) specific to working as a paramedic within the last 12 months

• Proof of valid CPR level C certification issued in the last 12 months

• Photocopy of front and back of valid Class 4 driver's license (or equivalent) with minimum one year driving experience

• Driver's abstract; issued within the last 30 days

• Copy of any valid Driver's course certificate i.e. CEVO, VFIS or NS VSP or equivalent issued within the last three years

• Criminal Record with Vulnerable Sector Check; issued within the last 30 days

• Immunization Record (Tetanus Tdap) within the last 10 years, 2 MMR vaccines (Measles, Mumps and Rubella) or lab evidenced immunity, 2 Varicella vaccines (Chicken Pox) or lab evidenced immunity, 3 Hepatitis B doses and Lab evidenced immunity, TB Skin Test (2 step) and a 1-step in the last 12 months; if reactive a follow up chest x-ray). Please note, a meeting with our Employee Health and Wellness Consultant can be scheduled, to ensure that all vaccinations are up to date by the time an offer is made

• Valid Official Language Assessments (oral assessment only) in both French and English from the Department of Post-secondary Education, Training and Labour. You can contact them at LS-SL@gnb.ca. Please take into account the additional time to receive your language assessment

• Additional training and/or education is highly valued.

1856193.title: Fish Processing Plant Worker - VA
1856193.description:
True North Salmon Limited Partnership, a division of Cooke Aquaculture Inc., a dynamic and growing east coast family company, with Platinum Member status in the Canada's Best Managed Companies Program has opportunities for highly motivated individuals to join the Company's Processing Team based out of our Fundy Bay Drive facility located in St. George, New Brunswick.

Cooke is a global seafood company with operations in North America, Europe, and South America. Our company's success is driven by our dynamic, highly skilled and innovative management team, supported by dedicated employees who live in coastal communities and contribute to the local area's economy and sense of community.

## The Role

As a result of our robust growth we are seeking Fish Processing Plant Workers to join our team.

## Primary duties of this role include, but are not limited to:

• Set up and operate machines to clean, cut, process, and package fresh fish products in accordance with operating procedures for safety and quality.

• Cut, clean, and trim whole fish for further processing.

• Scrape away scales, cut fish into fillets or portions, and remove scrap parts using a knife.

• Check fish fillets to determine the optimal number and size of fillet sections; cut sections according to specifications and place them in containers for weighing.

• Inspect products to ensure quality standards are met.

• Ice, weigh, and palletize products for transfer.

• Box or otherwise package fish for shipping.

• Check products and packaging for defects, ensure conformance to company standards, and perform corrective machine adjustments as required.

• Maintain a clean and organized work area.

*This position requires standing for long periods of time in a cold, wet environment and using hand tools including knives and pliers.

Available Shifts/Hours are as follows:

• Day Shift Monday to Friday : 7:00 a.m. - 3:30 p.m.

*Positions offer full-time year round employment and competitive rates.

## Benefits Package

• Health Benefits: Includes coverage for dental, vision, and extended medical care.

• Insurance: Life and disability insurance provided for financial security.

• SupportServices:Access to an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

• Financial Planning: Opportunity for RRSP matching to support your retirement savings.

• Wellness: Wellness programs.

• Career Development: Professional growth opportunities and avenues for advancement.

• Perks: Employee discounts on company products or services.

## The Opportunity

The role description is just one part of the story. This is an opportunity to grow, to work within the parameters of the role but to reach your fullest potential. We are a team that is driven to succeed. We count performance, we reward contribution and we recognize talent. It is about being at the center of a global leader in seafood and knowing you are part of that growth. The ability to bring your passion for learning, desire for growth and energy for moving your career forward is what we offer.

## The Why

Why Cooke? Simple - because we are a company that rewards initiative, resourcefulness and work ethic. We will champion your growth and provide you with the platform to create your path, your career, and your future.

NOTE: The recruiter is reviewing and interviewing eligible applicants for this position as they are received. If you are interested in this posting, you are encouraged to apply as soon as possible.

## *As per company policy, a criminal background check is required.

We appreciate all resumes; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

2240498.description:
Job Title: Forklift Operator

Location: Sackville, NB

Shift: Monday to Friday, 12pm-8pm

Wage: $20/hour

## Job Summary

The ideal candidate will operate and manage Johnston Stand up and counterbalance trucks to load and unload materials and deliveries, and move them to and from storage areas, machines, and loading docks. The cold warehouse temperatures range between 8 and 10 degrees.

## Responsibilities:

• Operate forklifts to move materials safely and efficiently.

• Load and unload trucks and shipping containers

• Case picking/re-palletizing product for customers

• Inspect incoming and outgoing shipments for damage and pallet stability.

• Complete damage reports and take photos when required.

• Perform pre-shift equipment inspections and report issues to the Operations Manager.

• Ensure loads are secure and properly balanced.

• Stack, organize, and relocate products and pallets.

• Maintain clean and organized work and storage areas.

• Identify and report damaged products, shortages, or quality concerns.

• Follow all company policies, safety procedures, and legal requirements.

• Complete daily equipment inspection and production records accurately

## Qualifications and Requirements:

• The ideal candidate is responsible and safety-focused

• Must be comfortable working in cold temperatures- not necessarily freezer

• Must have steel toe safety boots

• Must have a reliable means of transportation

• Previous forklift operating experience is required.

• Able to lift heavy loads and work long shifts.

• Pay close attention to detail and follow safety procedures.

• Operate a forklift safely in busy or tight spaces.

• Have good hand-eye coordination and manual dexterity.

• Ability to handle fragile and delicate materials with care.

• During downtime, complete tasks from the cleaning list at the shipper/receiver's desk.

• Initial each completed task on the cleaning sheet.

• Report directly to the Operations Manager.

2202457.description:
3 Positions (Lawyer 1 and Lawyer 2)
Office of the Attorney General
Department of Justice and Public Safety
Constitutional Law Group - Legal Services Branch
Fredericton, NB
Open Competition / Permanent

Interested in making a difference in our province? We encourage you to Choose GNB!

Who we are
The Attorney General is the law officer of the Executive Council and is responsible to see that the administration of public affairs is in accordance with the law and to ensure protection of the public interest. The Legal Services Branch provides civil and constitutional legal advice and representation to all provincial government departments and related agencies.
The Office of the Attorney General is seeking individuals to join the Legal Services Branch as Lawyers 1 and 2 within the Constitutional Law Group.

What you will do
The successful candidate will be assigned to the Constitutional Law Group and will work with other lawyers in a team setting and be responsible for conducting constitutional litigation and/or working with lawyers from the Litigation Group in constitutional litigation matters, appearing in all levels of courts and before administrative boards and tribunals throughout the province. The successful candidate will also be responsible for providing legal advice and opinions with respect to Memorandums to Executive Council, and other legal issues related to constitutional/Charter and indigenous law related matters.

## Work environment

• Location: Chancery Place, 675 King Street, Fredericton, NB

• Opportunity for hybrid work arrangement within New Brunswick, with prior approval from management

• Minimum 36.25 work hours per week

• We promote a scent-reduced environment

Who you are
As a team player, you will possess strong interpersonal and communication skills.
Your attitude, skills and interests are just as important as your area of study. We are looking for diverse backgrounds that bring a combination of the following:

Key Behavioral Traits: The successful candidates will possess the following behavioural competencies:

• Analytical thinking / judgment,

• Client service orientation,

• Effective interactive communication,

• Initiative, self-control/stamina,

• Commitment to learning, and

• Teamwork and cooperation.

## Need to have (essential skills and qualifications)

• Law Degree;

• Membership in good standing or eligibility for membership in good standing with the Law Society of New Brunswick;

• Minimum of 8 years at the bar for Lawyer 2 positions, and a minimum of 2 years at the bar for the Lawyer 1 position;

• Significant recent experience in litigation commensurate with the candidate's years at the Bar, including experience conducting hearings before any level of court, boards or tribunals;

• Significant recent experience in indigenous law commensurate with the candidate's years at the Bar.

## Please state your date of admission to a Canadian law society.

Written and spoken competence in English is required for the Lawyer 1 position and for one Lawyer 2 position. Written and spoken competence in French and English is required for one Lawyer 2 position. Please state your language capability.

Candidates must demonstrate on their applications how they have acquired the education and experience for this position. Your resume should be in chronological order specifying education and employment in months and years including part-time and full-time employment. Applicants must clearly demonstrate the essential qualifications to be given further consideration. Please indicate in your resume your language preference for an interview.

Nice to Have (asset qualifications)
Preference may be given to candidates who demonstrate, commensurate with years at the bar:

• Additional years of litigation experience

Subject to the response to this competition, candidates may be required to demonstrate on their application one or more of the asset qualifications in addition to the essential qualifications in order to be given further consideration.

## Operational requirements

• Travel;

• Possession of a valid driver's license; and

• Working outside of regular hours of work without prior notice.

Wage
Lawyer 1 - $88,291 to $139,958 annually, depending on education, experience, and/or years of admission to a Canadian law society

If applying by email or mail, please attach/include the writing sample. If applying online, please send the writing sample in a separate email to the address below.

• Comprehensive benefits package and the Public Service Shared Risk Pension Plan;

• Opportunities for career growth, professional development and training;

• Free access to Employee and Family Assistance Program (EFAP) and services;

• Additional benefits based on the collective agreement.

How to apply

by email at HRcompetitions.concoursRH@gnb.ca indicating the competition number/numbers for which you would like to apply:

2239988.title: Lead, Francophonie affairs
2239988.description:
## APPLICATION PROCESS

If this position aligns with your experience, skills and professional aspirations, we invite you to submit your application. In addition to your résumé, you must provide a cover letter.

Your cover letter must clearly demonstrate that you possess the experience, knowledge and abilities outlined below. Please include at least one specific example illustrating how you have applied this experience or knowledge in the context of a relevant initiative, partnership or project.

Your cover letter must demonstrate:

• relevant experience working, collaborating or representing organizations, institutions, networks or initiatives within Acadian and Francophone communities;

• practical knowledge of the realities, contemporary issues, institutions and networks regarding Francophonie affairs and Acadia in New Brunswick;

• the ability to apply this experience and knowledge to contribute effectively to the mandate of the City of Dieppe.

## SUMMARY

Reporting to the director responsible for Francophonie affairs, the incumbent provides strategic advice, represents the City at an institutional level, develops partnerships and coordinates municipal projects and initiatives. The incumbent contributes to integrating Francophonie affairs and Acadia priorities into the City's projects, programs and services, while promoting their visibility throughout the Dieppe community and among community partners.

The incumbent engages Acadian and Francophone communities, advises municipal departments and partners, and promotes the integration of Francophonie-related priorities into the City's projects, programs and services. The incumbent contributes to the profile and visibility of Francophonie affairs and Acadia through the development of strategic collaborations, municipal representation and the identification of opportunities that promote French-language vitality.

The scope of the position focuses on municipal directions, partnerships and strategic initiatives, rather than the direct delivery of services, individual intervention, teaching or client support.

## DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

## Advisory support and guidance

• Serve as a resource person for municipal departments on Francophonie, Acadia and linguistic vitality issues

• Advise and support departments in integrating practices that promote French-language vitality, active offer and bilingual services

• Contribute to the development of tools, resources and best practices in support of municipal priorities

## Partnerships and consultation

• Develop and maintain collaborative relationships with francophone and Acadian organizations, institutions and partners

• Coordinate consultation mechanisms related to municipal priorities concerning Francophonie affairs and the promotion of Acadia

• Represent the municipality in dealings with partners, networks and relevant bodies

## Promotion and development

• Coordinate activities, projects and initiatives that raise the profile of the Francophonie and Acadia

• Identify opportunities for collaboration, funding or development to support municipal objectives

• Help position the municipality as a dynamic, welcoming and inclusive francophone and Acadian community

## Coordination of initiatives and projects

• Coordinate the implementation of initiatives and actions arising from the municipal Francophonie and Acadia action plan

• Monitor timelines, deliverables and expected results

• Identify issues, risks and opportunities for improvement, and report them to management

## Analysis and reporting

• Monitor trends, issues, programs and opportunities related to Francophonie, Acadia, official languages and the development of Francophone communities

• Compile and analyze data relevant to the evaluation of initiatives

• Prepare reports, summaries, recommendations and other documents for management

## Other

• Carry out any other related duties related to their mandate

## MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

## Education

• Undergraduate degree (bachelor's) in public administration, communications, public relations, community development, political science, Francophone or Acadian studies, cultural management, sociology or an equivalent field of expertise

• An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered

## Experience

• Five (5) years of relevant experience in coordinating projects or initiatives, consultation, community development, government relations, partnerships, communications or public relations

• Demonstrated experience collaborating with organizations, institutions, networks or initiatives that support the promotion and vitality of New Brunswick's Francophone and Acadian communities

• Good understanding of the realities of francophone and Acadian communities, ideally in a minority context

• Experience in the francophone sector, public policy, the municipal sector, or community or quasi-public organizations (asset)

## Knowledge

2238371.description:
The Joint Economic Development Initiative (JEDI) is dedicated to supporting Indigenous peoples in reaching their full economic development potential through advocacy and networking. The JEDI team currently requires an Entrepreneur Development Officer.

Reporting to the Economic Development Manager, the Entrepreneur Development Officer will work closely with a wide range of stakeholders including Indigenous entrepreneurs and businesses, provincial and federal government departments, industry partners and JEDI staff participating in the business mentorship program to assist with finding new clients, markets and contracting opportunities.

## Primary responsibilities:

## Partnership development:

• Collaborate with key partners on strategies to support Indigenous peoples and businesses to achieve success, including:
• Working with the JEDI team and community Economic Development Officers on the information flow about economic development programs and initiatives within communities.

• Participating in key meetings and committees/working groups to report on project progress and to address any emerging issues.

• Assisting with preparation of reports and with day-to-day operational requirements of the program.

## Indigenous Entrepreneurship and Employment:

• Maintain a database of Indigenous businesses, keeping them informed of existing and emerging opportunities (such as funding, training, and contracts), and connecting them with key industry contacts and resources.

• Contribute to entrepreneurship program activities such as participant recruitment, day-to-day delivery as required, and supporting clients during program delivery, aftercare and beyond.

• Promote the procurement of goods or services from Indigenous businesses directly required in supply chains.

## Qualifications:

• A university degree in a related discipline (e.g. Business Administration, Public Relations, Communications) preferably with business development experience, or an equivalent combination of education, training and relevant experience.

• Understanding of First Nation communities, culture, and social concerns. Preference will be given to qualified candidates of Indigenous descent.

• Excellent interpersonal, relationship-building, networking and communication skills, both oral and written; strong organizational skills.

• Proficient in MS Office (Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Access). Experience using data management software is an asset.

• Experience/knowledge of the following would be considered strong assets, but are not requirements as they can be developed on the job:
• Budgeting, business analysis, market trend analysis, industry analysis, information systems, marketing and exporting

• Global supply chains, international marketing and supporting resources

• Valid driver's license and the ability to travel in the province.

• Satisfactory criminal background/vulnerable sector clearance and maintenance are required.

Candidates must clearly demonstrate on their application how they meet these qualifications.

Salary is based on $52,955 - $64,723 per annum.

For more information on our organization and team please visit: www.jedinb.ca

If you are interested in this position, please submit your confidential resume and cover letter saved as one document to janis.flemming@jedinb.ca stating Entrepreneur Development Officer in the subject line by 4:30 p.m. on September 26, 2026. As JEDI will begin reviewing applications and interviewing candidates during the recruitment period please submit your application as soon as possible.

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

The New Brunswick Extra-Mural Program (EMP), often known as the "hospital without walls," has operated under the simple philosophy of helping New Brunswickers receive the care they need in the places where they are healthiest and happiest - their homes and communities. EMP makes a difference in the lives of those it serves by drastically reducing hospital admissions and greatly increasing patient satisfaction with its level of health care.

As part of EMP, your role is vital in our province's overall health. Join an integrated, multi-disciplinary team of health care professionals, dedicated to providing New Brunswickers with outstanding, highly coordinated primary health care.

## JOB SUMMARY

Under the supervision of the manager, the Resource Nurse provides clinical guidance and support to EMP clinical staff in the planning and delivery of care to EMP patients and their families/support persons. They will act as a clinical leader, role model and change agent. The Resource Nurse will be responsible for clinical training and orientating of clinical staff at the local and regional levels.

They will collaborate in the development and updating of policies, procedures and protocols and the implementation of best practices and act as a resource person to clinical staff for managing clinical cases.

## Roles and Responsibilities

## Clinical Leadership and Patient Care

• Collaborates in the implementation of home care best practices.

• Maintains open lines of communication between members of the interdisciplinary team.

• Provides leadership and supports clinical staff with complex clinical situations in accordance with EMP Unit policies and procedures. Supports the team in the EMP Approval/Denial process where appropriate.

• Consults in developing and revising the policies, procedures, protocols and any other clinical documentation related to EMP.

• Promotes interdisciplinary patient centered care approach.

• Provides direct care to patients as needed based on unit requirements.

• Supports clinical staff to maintain ongoing collaborative relationship with the patient's primary provider (physician or Nurse Practitioner) and other healthcare professionals.

• Supports manager with Approval/Denial as requested.

• Communicates with Clinical manager and Clinical Nurse Specialist.

• Attends discipline specific meetings as appropriate

## Staff Orientation and Development

• Prepares, coordinates and delivers orientation and continuing education programs focused on skills specific to homecare practices and works in conjunction with other resource nurses across the EMP.

• Ensures the orientation material and training content are up to date.

• Promotes principals of home care practice with EMP clinical staff and supports nurses in developing skills needed to be competent.

• Acts as a mentor with new EMP clinical staff.

• Ongoing and monitoring professional competencies and certifications- conduct "skills lab"- linked to EMP Education manager and Clinical Nurse Specialist positions

• Assists the clinical manager with the monitoring and assessment of clinical activities and nursing competencies needed to meet home care standards.

• Assists the clinical manager with identification of educational needs, training needs and opportunities.

• Offers sessions to clinical staff in order to maintain required certifications (advanced skills, etc.).

• Trains the staff on using new pieces of equipment and techniques relevant to specific practice.

• Collaborates with the development of patient's educational tools and resources required for patients and families' teaching.

• Supports clinical staff in the acquisition of community problem solving / critical thinking skills in an effort to support informed decision-making.

• Participates in caseload review with the manager in an effort to support efficiency and consistency in caseload management as well as meeting home care best practice and EMP clinical practice leadership guidelines.

• Collaborates in the implementation of appropriate home care indicators and ensure that EMP staff is aware of the indicators and follow the provincial EMP Clinical Practice leadership Practice documents for home care.

• Supports EMP accountability framework to contribute to efficient performance

## Quality Improvement and Risk Management

• Collaborates in quality improvement initiatives as required.

• Responds to Wound Care consults generated through PIXalere (works in conjunction with EMP Skin & Wound Care Network)

## Research

• Assists in finding potential patients for researchers through the promotion of approved projects.

• Participates in research projects as required.

## REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND OTHER JOB REQUIREMENTS:

• Bachelor Degree in Nursing;

• Must be registered (active) or ability to register with the Nurses Association of New Brunswick;

• Minimum of five (5) years of experience with EMP acquired over the past eight (8) years;

• Demonstrated ability to provide education programs using exceptional interpersonal, leadership, and teaching skills;

• Demonstrated knowledge of current health trends, principles of home health care, community care, senior, acute, supportive and palliative care;

• Knowledge of the target population of EMP and available community resources;

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 5 Driver's License and good driving record (proof required);

• Submit a valid and clean criminal record check;

• Have a current CPR Level C certification that has been issued in the last 12 months;

• Demonstrated strong competency in Microsoft office (Word, Excel, Power Point) as well as confidence in computer use.

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and possess leadership and coaching skills, strong interpersonal skills, good judgment and decision making skills;

• Must demonstrate capacity to work independently

• Must have a good attendance record;

• Must have a high regard for confidentiality; and

• Must have excellent work habits and have a professional behaviours.

All interested applicants are encouraged to apply as an equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered.

Note: This position, due to the potential travel requirements, a valid Canadian passport or Nexus card will be required.

If you are interested in working with a dynamic team of professionals and possess the necessary qualifications, please click the 'Apply Now' button to submit your resume.

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Primary Care Paramedics are based on the current National Occupational Competency Profile (NOCP) for Primary Care Paramedics,Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

## Duties of Position:

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Primary Care Paramedics are based on the current National Occupational Competency Profile (NOCP) for Primary Care Paramedics,Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in paramedicine or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

Required Qualifications:

• You are entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizenship, permanent resident status or work permit)

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record

• Must have a high regard for confidentiality and patient safety

• Primary Care Paramedic program/course of over six months; If you do not have one and are interested in this career, here is a list of paramedic programs in Atlantic Canada, click here

• Must be registered, active Paramedic with the Paramedic Association of New Brunswick; If you are not currently registered in New Brunswick, please visit PANB at www.panb.ca

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 4 Driver's Licence (or equivalent)

Additional requirements for your application:

• Current Resume and Cover Letter

• A copy of your PCP diploma from an accredited institution

• Proof of current registration with Paramedic Association of New Brunswick

• Proof of completion of a Physical Abilities Test (PAT) specific to working as a paramedic within the last 12 months

• Proof of valid CPR level C certification issued in the last 12 months

• Photocopy of front and back of valid Class 4 driver's license (or equivalent) with minimum one year driving experience

• Driver's abstract; issued within the last 30 days

• Copy of any valid Driver's course certificate i.e. CEVO, VFIS or NS VSP or equivalent issued within the last three years

• Criminal Record with Vulnerable Sector Check; issued within the last 30 days

• Immunization Record (Tetanus Tdap) within the last 10 years, 2 MMR vaccines (Measles, Mumps and Rubella) or lab evidenced immunity, 2 Varicella vaccines (Chicken Pox) or lab evidenced immunity, 3 Hepatitis B doses and Lab evidenced immunity, TB Skin Test (2 step) and a 1-step in the last 12 months; if reactive a follow up chest x-ray). Please note, a meeting with our Employee Health and Wellness Consultant can be scheduled, to ensure that all vaccinations are up to date by the time an offer is made

• Valid Official Language Assessments (oral assessment only) in both French and English from the Department of Post-secondary Education, Training and Labour. You can contact them at LS-SL@gnb.ca. Please take into account the additional time to receive your language assessment

• Additional training and/or education is highly valued.

For any questions for our HR team, please contact us at jobs-emplois@ambulancenb.ca

If you are looking for a career that will change lives and have a direct impact on the health of our community, submit your application.

Ambulance NB is committed to the principle of equal opportunity in its employment practices and to providing an environment free from discrimination and harassment for all employees.

We would like to thank all candidates for expressing interest. Please note only those selected for interviews will be contacted.

2228459.title: Hematopathologist
2228459.description:
Horizon Health Network is seeking a Pathologist with Hematopathology training to join our collegial and collaborative team in beautiful Fredericton, New Brunswick.

This role will be part of the Department of Laboratory Medicine, which includes a team of 10 pathologists, 1 microbiologist, and 1 chemist. This role would have the successful candidate participating in a hemepath rotation (including peripheral blood, bone marrow and flow cytometry) with 2-3 other pathologists as well as general surgical pathology signoued. It would be an asset if the candidate had an interest in lab leadership, in particular within the hematology lab. Regional hematopathology support is available from our teams in Saint John and Moncton, both of which have established hematopathologists who can provide consultative and collaborative support when needed.

## Why you should work here

New Brunswick offers a safe and welcoming community with a relaxed lifestyle and a true work-life balance, enriched by its diverse Indigenous, Anglophone, and Francophone heritage.

Horizon Health Network is the largest health authority in the region, employing dedicated professionals focused on delivering high-quality care. Our employees collaborate with community partners to provide accessible health programs and services to over half a million people through our 12 hospitals and more than 100 medical facilities and clinics.

Located in the scenic St. John River Valley, Fredericton is New Brunswick's vibrant capital—perfect for individuals and families. As an officially bilingual city with a strong francophone community, it offers French-language education, cultural events, and healthcare at Le Centre communautaire Sainte-Anne. Residents enjoy a wide range of activities: water sports, golf, biking trails, skiing at Crabbe Mountain, live theatre, art galleries including the renowned Beaverbrook Art Gallery, and festivals like the Harvest Jazz and Blues Festival and Frostival. Attractions like the Boyce Farmer's Market and Science East make Fredericton a dynamic place to live.

## Incentives & Remuneration

Remuneration for the position is based on New Brunswick Medicare's Alternate Funding Plan (AFP), with a range of $378,000 - $416,000.

Successful applicants may be eligible to receive the following:

• Urban recruitment incentive of $50,000.00 with a 2-year return of service.

• Moving expense reimbursement is also available.

## What you will do

The physician will work collaboratively within an interdisciplinary team, adhere to evidence-based practices aligned with Horizon Health Network's mission. Protected research time is available for qualified candidates.

• Provide onsite medical reporting and consultation on peripheral blood morphology, bone marrow morphology, coagulation and flow cytometry and transfusion medicine.

• Clinical duties include medical oversight for technologists, regulatory issues, quality assurance, hemovigilance and occurrence management.

• Participate in the after-hours on-call rota.

• Practice in a collaborative fashion as a member of an interdisciplinary team and consult with members of other health professions as appropriate.

• Participate in the use of departmental and corporate evidence-based rules of practice to ensure that expected standards of care are achieved.

• Participate in the education of technologists, medical students, and residents.

(Note: These responsibilities are the basic and prime duties associated with this position; other related and allied duties may be assigned from time to time as may be necessary to the operation of Horizon Health Network.)

## Who you are

• Hematopathology certification by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada or acceptable equivalent. Alternatively, applicants may hold RCPSC certification in either General Pathology/Diagnostic and Clinical Pathology or Anatomical Pathology/Diagnostic and Molecular Pathology (or acceptable equivalent) with additional fellowship training in Hematopathology.

• Must hold a valid license to practice medicine in the Province of New Brunswick.

• Must be a member in good standing with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of New Brunswick.

• Must have current malpractice insurance from the Canadian Medical Protective Association (CMPA) appropriate to the category of practice or equivalent.

• Strong diagnostic and clinical skills with a commitment to high-quality patient care

• Ability to collaborate and communicate effectively within a multidisciplinary team and across regional sites

• Demonstrated interest in continuous improvement, quality assurance, and innovation in laboratory medicine

The physician must also meet continuing education requirements, adhere to departmental and health authority policies, comply with relevant legislation, and follow professional ethical standards set by regulatory bodies.

2241250.title: Integrated Pest Management Weed Specialist
2241250.employer: Department of Agriculture, Aquaculture and Fisheries
2241250.description:
Integrated Pest Management Weed SpecialistDepartment of Agriculture, Aquaculture and FisheriesAgrologist 3Open CompetitionFredericton

Interested in making a difference in our province? We encourage you to Choose GNB!

## Who we are:

The Department of Agriculture, Aquaculture and Fisheries is seeking an individual to join the Crop Sector Development Branch as an Integrated Pest Management (IPM) Weed Specialist, located in Fredericton.

The Department of Agriculture, Aquaculture and Fisheries is responsible for supporting growth, competitiveness and sustainability of these three sectors. We work collaboratively with industry, producers, researchers, indigenous communities, government partners and other stakeholders to support and advance opportunities in the primary and value-added agriculture, aquaculture and fishery sectors. As part of these initiatives, the Crop Sector Development Branch provides leadership, technical expertise, and advisory services to promote a sustainable, innovative, and competitive crop industry throughout the province.

## What you will do:

As a member of the Crop Sector Development team, reporting to the section manager, the selected candidate will be responsible for the following.

• Planning, developing, implementing, and evaluating pest management strategies.

• Evaluating and demonstrating new weed management technologies.

• Providing expert advisory services on weed management to producers, staff, and all crop sectors.

• Representing the department on various national, regional, and provincial committees and associations.

• Developing and delivering educational and reference materials on pest management and related topics, including presentations, newsletters, articles, fact sheets, selection guides, and website materials.

• Developing, implementing and monitoring pest management policies and management programs related to horticulture and field crops.

• Performing other related duties, as assigned.

Your attitude, skills and interests are just as important as your area of study. We are looking for diverse backgrounds that bring a combination of the following.

Essential Qualifications:

• A Master`s degree in Science with specialization in agriculture and focus on integrated pest management, particularly in weed management; and a minimum of eight (8) years of directly related work experience.

OR

• A Bachelor degree in Science with specialization in agriculture and focus on integrated pest management, particularly in weed management; and a minimum of ten (10) years of directly related work experience.

An equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered.

Written and spoken competence in English is required. Please state your language capability on your application.

Note: The successful candidate must be eligible for membership in the New Brunswick Institute of Agrologists and membership must be attained within six (6) months of appointment.

Applicants must clearly demonstrate the essential qualifications to be given further consideration. Please ensure that the preferred language for assessment is identified on your resume. Resumes should be in chronological order specifying education and employment in months and years including part-time and full-time employment.

## Asset Qualifications:

Preference may be given to candidates that demonstrate experience in one or more of the following: technology transfer; networking; field research trials for evaluation and demonstration; working with agricultural producers and producer groups. Subject to the response to this competition, candidates may be required to demonstrate on their application one or more of the asset qualifications in addition to the essential qualifications in order to be given further consideration

Behavioual Competencies: The successful candidate will possess the following behavioural competencies:

• Analytical Thinking/Judgment

• Client Service Orientation

• Effective Interactive Communication

• Information Seeking

• Initiative

• Relationship/Network Building

• Teamwork and Cooperation

Technical Competencies: The successful candidate will possess the following technical competencies:

• Specialized subject matter expertise and knowledge, including weed diagnostic skills and weed management knowledge;

• Knowledge of research methodologies, principles and practices;

• Written communication, including policies, analytical reports, proposals, and briefing materials;

• Presentation skills;

• Planning and organizing skills.

## Wage: Agrologist 3 - $75,898.16 to $103,884.56 annually

Note: In the event that this competition poses difficulties in recruiting a qualified candidate, a covering off appointment at a lower level may be made. In that case, candidates with less than the required related years of experience may also be considered.

## Operational Requirements:

Must be prepared to: travel within and outside of the province, including overnight stays, as required; work outside of the regular work hours, as required; work in agricultural environments which may include a variety of terrain and weather conditions; possess a valid class 5 driver licence as issued by the Province of New Brunswick, or equivalent; and possess or successfully complete Pesticide Applicator Certification within six (6) months of commencement.

## Work environment:

• Office location: Hugh John Flemming Forestry Centre, 1350 Regent Street, Fredericton, New Brunswick.

• Work hours: Monday to Friday / 8:15 to 4:30; 36.25 hours per week.

• We promote a scent-reduced environment.

Providing a safe workplace for all. Your health and safety are important to us. GNB has implemented preventative measures across the organization to ensure your health & safety. We promote a scent-reduced environment.

## How to apply:

We encourage applicants to apply online at www.ere.gnb.ca, by email at Brenda.Nicholson@gnb.ca, or by mail at the following address, by October 16, 2026, indicating competition number DAAF-26-07. This competition may be used to fill future vacancies at the same level.

Department of Agriculture, Aquaculture and FisheriesHuman Resource Services
Hugh John Flemming Forestry Centre
1350 Regent Street
Fredericton, NB E3C 2G6

We thank all those who apply, however, only those selected for further consideration will be contacted.

As per the?Civil Service Act, veterans who demonstrate they are among the most qualified, shall be given preference at the time of appointment.

We are an Equal Employment Opportunity Program (EEO) contributing to the creation of a more balanced workforce that reflects the diversity of the province by removing barriers to employment and providing individualized supports to designated equity group members.

2217406.title: Senior Contaminated Sites Professional
2217406.employer: GEMTEC Consulting Engineers and Scientists Limited
2217406.description:
Are you an experienced Contaminated Sites Professional looking to progress your career? We're looking for a Senior Contaminated Sites Professional to join our growing team in our Fredericton, NB office.

At GEMTEC, we offer something different. We're an employee-owned, 400-person multidisciplinary consulting firm—not too big, not too small. We're large enough to compete head-to-head with publicly traded engineering giants, but still small enough to maintain the culture and flexibility of a close-knit team.

Our size and hands-on management style let us move quickly, embrace new opportunities, and empower our people to shape their own careers—without getting lost in corporate bureaucracy.

You're a strong fit if you:

• Bring sharp attention to detail

• Tackle environmental challenges with practical, solutions-oriented thinking

• Take initiative and drive projects forward independently

• Approach each assignment with a sense of ownership and pride

• Adapt quickly when conditions or project needs change

A typical day on the job might look like:

• Providing consulting services as an Environmental Professional in contaminated sites management for government and private sector clients.

• Applying scientific and engineering principles to multi-disciplinary environmental projects.

• Managing and completing contaminated sites projects, including Phase I, II, and III Environmental Site Assessments, remediation programs, risk assessments, and environmental compliance monitoring.

• Preparing and reviewing proposals and technical reports.

• Collaborating with our Environmental Team and other GEMTEC service lines to design and deliver projects of varying sizes and complexities.

• Evaluating team needs and contributing to the growth and development of our Environmental Team.

The good stuff you get:

• Full-time (37.5 hours per week)

• Complete health & dental coverage including vision, paramedical services, Teladoc and Employee & Family Assistance Program when you need it

• Retirement planning made easier with a 5% employer match on your contributions

• Paid time off (vacation and sick days) and an office year-end closure (paid time off between Christmas and the New Year)

Your background and what you bring:

• A minimum of an undergraduate degree in a related field.

• A Registered Professional designation (e.g., P.Eng., P.Geo.) in Canada, with at least 12 years of experience in managing contaminated sites.

• A thorough understanding of provincial and federal regulations related to contaminated site management.

• Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple assignments effectively.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.

• Experience in preparing technical and cost proposals.

• Field program management, including resource and budget oversight.

• Ability to build business relationships with clients, regulators, and subcontractors.

• Experience with federal government clients is an asset.

• Technical experience in hydrogeology and/or environmental risk assessment is a plus.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office products, particularly Word and Excel.

Interested individuals, click here to apply: https://gemtec.bamboohr.com/careers/305

Thank you for taking the time to consider GEMTEC. Only candidates proceeding to the next phase of the application process will be contacted at this time. We encourage you to connect with us on LinkedIn, even if this opportunity isn't for you, the next one might be!

Should you be selected for an interview and require accommodation of any kind, please kindly help us understand how we can help.

2240214.description:
Req Id: 431777

Connection is everything. It drives us to innovate, explore, and stay close to what matters to us most. At Bell, we're building a more connected future through world-class networks, AI-powered solutions, and digital experiences that elevate how people live, work, and play every day.

We believe in empowering people. That's why we equip our teams with cutting-edge technology, AI tools, and a collaborative environment that supports creativity and growth. Want to be part of a diverse team where your work makes a real impact? If you're inspired by innovation that advances how people connect and transforms what's possible, you belong on #TeamBell.

Summary
We are seeking a highly motivated Cyber Security Analyst II to join Bell's Network team and play a key role in protecting and supporting our world-class broadband fibre and wireless networks. In this role, you will manage and support security operations, applications, processes, and technologies that enable the delivery of managed security services across secure operating environments. You will work closely with internal teams and customers to ensure operational excellence, meet contractual security requirements, respond to security incidents, and contribute to forensic investigations and restoration activities when needed.

This position requires a strong understanding of cybersecurity operations, customer-focused service delivery, and the ability to support a 24/7 security environment through on-call participation.

Key Responsibilities
• Manage the daily customer requests for changes to their security infrastructure.

• Prepare changes for security devices such as firewalls, intrusion detection and prevention systems, identity access management etc.

• Participate in new customer integration projects and services and prepare implementations.

• Reviews and interprets security alerts and provide diagnostics in the management of incidents to support clients.

• Depending on the nature of the security threat, assess and develop mitigation measures to ensure that appropriate treatment is applied, and ensure that customers are informed.

• Take proactive measures to manage all perimeter security equipment or associated components which may be interrupted or affected as a result of threats or vulnerabilities.

• Configure, install, manage and maintain security devices and provide general information and recommendations on security best practices.

• Develop documentation associated with maintenance releases and keep them updated.

• Observe security management best practices.

Critical Qualifications
• Completion of University or College program in Computer Science; or 5 years of equivalent industry experience in the information systems field.

• Demonstrated experience designing, implementing, and troubleshooting security solutions including authentication, authorization, encryption and audit capabilities as part of an overall system design.

• Practical experience recognized in the implementation, daily management and troubleshooting firewalls from multiple vendors.

• Proven experience in the daily management and troubleshooting of intrusion detection and prevention systems (IPS).

• Experience in troubleshooting security solutions including authentication capabilities, authorization, and encryption as well as securing devices access.

• Experience translating complex and ambiguous problems into actionable components.

• Ability to work on multiple clients and multiple technologies.

• Be able to work under pressure (required during incidents).

• Good communication skills, writing and presentations. Self starter with excellent organization and interpersonal skills.

• Excellent communication skills in both English and French (written and spoken).

Preferred Qualifications
• Hands-on security certifications from major vendors.

• Experience working with the following security management consoles of Checkpoint, Juniper, Cisco, Tufin, Fortinet, Mc Afee, Arcsight etc.

• Knowledge of offensive and defensive security operational tactics.

• Understanding of NIST, ISO 27001, ITIL, SAS70 (or 5970) and/or other compliance frameworks.

• Knowledge of security information events management (SIEM).

Adequate knowledge of French is required for positions in Quebec.

## Additional Information:

Position Type: Management Job Status: Regular - Full Time Job Location: Canada : Ontario : Toronto || Canada : New Brunswick : Fredericton || Canada : New Brunswick : Saint John || Canada : Nova Scotia : Halifax || Canada : Ontario : Ottawa
Work Arrangement: Hybrid

For work arrangements that are 'Hybrid', successful candidates must be based in Canada and report to a set Bell office for a minimum of 3 days a week. Recognizing the importance of work-life balance, Bell offers flexibility in work hours based on the business needs.

Service New Brunswick
Senior Business Analyst
Open Competition – Pay Band 6 (Classification under review)

Flexible location within New Brunswick

Service New Brunswick (SNB) is seeking an individual with Senior Business Analyst expertise to join the Technology Services Division in the Digital Solution Services unit. The Senior Business Analyst will join a new Agile team being established to support a strategic approach based on a common framework for portable, verifiable, and user-controlled credentials.

Working at Service New Brunswick is more than just a job — it's an opportunity to build a meaningful career. Guided by our vision of "Elevating Service Excellence", our teams provide high-quality, innovative public services for customers with a focus on value for all New Brunswickers.

Known for our people-oriented workplace culture, we foster an environment where innovation, inclusivity, and teamwork are celebrated. We are proud to be recognized as one of Atlantic Canada's Top Employers for 2026!

## What We Offer

At SNB, our people are at the heart of everything we do. We are:

• Human-Centered: We prioritize well-being and flexibility for our employees.

• Driven by Growth: We invest in your professional development and career advancement.

• Celebrating Excellence: We recognize and reward outstanding contributions.

• United by Purpose: Every project you work on makes a real difference for New Brunswickers.

• Empowered to Decide: We trust our teams to make decisions and innovate boldly.

With offices and locations in most New Brunswick cities and a wide variety of positions and job roles, SNB offers unmatched opportunities for growth and impact, including an employee recognition program, a mentoring program, training & development opportunities, employee townhalls and ongoing leadership development.

## SNB also offers a comprehensive employee benefits package.

Reporting to a Product Owner, the Senior Business Analyst collaborates with the user community in an Agile operating environment to gather business requirements and conduct workflow analysis, transforming them into features and user stories supporting the design and successful implementation of solutions across the organization.

Your responsibilities will include but are not limited to:

• Conduct product feature deconstruction and story writing

• Provide backlog refinement support by partnering with the Product Owner to manage, groom, and prioritize the Agile team's backlog.

• Participate in the planning, building and implementation of systems, upgrades and enhancements

• Accountable for the maintenance and support of these systems, including troubleshooting and issue resolution

• Ensure systems are configured to meet architectural, security, and user interface/user experience (UI/UX) standards and guidelines

• Create and implement testing approaches and processes to solve testing problems, including use of test automation approaches

• Participate and lead the development of testing strategies, test plans, and test cases to ensure smooth transition to training and deployment

• Create requirements traceability documentation

• Assist with functional, integration and user acceptance testing as required

• Coordinate and facilitate workshops to understand and develop client business processes, including current and future state analysis and gap definitions. This includes developing workshop materials, agendas and reports, as required

• Act as primary conduit by working with Agile teams, architects, and business stakeholders to analyze business needs and recommend and support development of solutions to address these needs

• Identify and document key business drivers

• Analyze and document gaps between requirements and products features and/or capabilities. Document the results of the analysis in an appropriate format including business rules, user stories, and workflow descriptions

• Support quarterly Planning Interval (PI) events by helping to map out dependencies across teams on the Agile Release Train (ART) and by clarifying requirement ambiguities so developers can confidently estimate workloads

• Work with Agile teams to define and document business benefits, outcomes and measures contribute to issue, change, and risk management processes

• Maintain a strong linkage and collaboration with project managers and other key stakeholders

• Experience within the public sector

• Experience with Enterprise Agile frameworks, including the Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe)

• Experience with Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) practices

• Possession of a Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) for Teams certification, called the SAFe Practitioner (SP). Note that incumbents without this certification must secure and maintain it as a condition of continued employment.

• Possession of active Business Analyst certifications, such as IIBA-CBAP, PMI-PBA, and IQBBA

• Experience with Azure DevOps Services

• Experience with the BrowserStack platform

• Experience with Identity and Access Management (IAM) and Identity-as-a-Service (IDaaS) platforms, such as PingOne

• Experience with decentralized identity solutions and approaches utilizing Verifiable Credentials (VCs)

• Experience with SaaS applications

• Experience with Cloud applications

• Experience with UI/UX design systems

ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS: A bachelor's degree in computer science or a related field, and a minimum of six (6) years of related technology experience. Subject to the response to this competition, an equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered.

## Written and spoken competence in English is required.

Applicants must clearly demonstrate the essential qualifications to be given further consideration. Please state your language capability on your application and ensure that preferred language for assessment is clearly identified.

Subject to the response to this competition, candidates may be required to demonstrate on their application one or more of the asset qualifications in addition to the essential qualifications in order to be given further consideration.

This position may require limited flexibility in working hours, with occasional weekday evening or weekend work.

Candidates will be required to undergo Criminal History Clearance prior to appointment.

• Analytical Thinking/Judgment

• Results Orientation

• Self-Confidence

• Written communication

• Planning and organizing skills

• Presentation skills

• Ability to use Office Technology, Software and Applications

• Use of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to implement UI/UX design systems

• High-level understanding of Object-Oriented Programming Languages

• High-level understanding of SQL

Resumes should be in chronological order specifying education and employment in months and years including part-time and full-time employment.

2240003.description:
See if you are our next:

## RECEPTIONIST | Dieppe

Working for LASIK MD (an affiliated entity of Vision Group) is to help improve people's eyesight. It is having the feeling of a mission accomplished and a job well done. It is seeing happiness in the eyes of patients and realizing that you have changed the way they see life. All of this can be achieved while having the opportunity to build a stable and rewarding career that meets your full potential.

Join our team, where our Great Place to Work® certification represents our commitment to creating a supportive and inclusive culture for every member of our organization.

## A look at your benefits

• You receive a quarterly bonus.

• You have a permanent full-time position (32-35hrs/week).

• You benefit from a free LASIK surgery, 3 weeks of vacation, 3 sick days, 1 floater & 1 wellness day.

• You benefit from group insurance, telemedicine & RRSP match.

• You work with experts in Ophthalmology & you can count yourself as a team member of one of Canada's Best Managed Companies.

## Your tasks at a glance

• You warmly welcome patients and direct them to the waiting room, ensuring that new patients complete the questionnaire to add to their files.

• You handle mail, clinic phone lines, and voicemails, and make sure to call patients to confirm their appointments.

• You are responsible for updating the medical records and appointments software after each patient's arrival and departure.

• You manage inventory and ensure the aesthetics and cleanliness of the clinic when needed.

## A clear view of your assets

• You have experience as a receptionist, medical secretary, or administrative assistant in a doctor's office or have strong customer service/patient care skills.

• You are comfortable with computers, technology, and Microsoft 365 (knowledge of EMR systems is an asset).

• You stand out for your organizational and collaborative skills as well as your ability to work with minimal supervision.

• You especially thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, and when you work as part of a team.

• You are comfortable traveling to other clinics for training or work (expenses covered by Vision Group).

• Important: You have excellent communication skills, you speak English et français également (advanced intermediate level of French required due to the nature of the tasks or interactions with our French-speaking patients).

• Schedule: You are available to work Monday through Friday, 7:00 am to 3:00 pm (flexibility required for later shifts 9:00 am to 5:00 pm.

Address: 30 Englehart St, Dieppe, NB E1A 8H3

## From our point of view

Whatever your profile, we are above all looking for someone beyond the CV, since you can benefit from in-house training. Only your motivation and your desire to learn are part of our selection criteria.

Mechanical Project Manager - Commercial Department
Moncton, NB

Black & McDonald is an integrated, multi-trade service provider that safely delivers high quality construction, facilities management, and technical solutions. We are a family -owned and family-run company that employs thousands of highly skilled and talented professionals across North America. ## CLOSING DATE
