2241068.description:
Mount Allison acknowledges, honours, and respects that the land named Sackville, NB is part of the unceded territory of the Mi'kmaq People who are the historic inhabitants, custodians, and dwellers on the land where our University is built and confirms its commitment to strengthening relationships with all Indigenous people.

Position title: Library Resources and Access Manager
Department: Libraries and Archives
Type: Full-time two-year term position
Opportunity type: Non-academic
Classification: Admin Grade 6
Salary range: $58,000 to $77,054 per annum
Supervisor's title: Dean of Libraries and Archives
Posted date: September 24, 2026

## Position description

Reporting to the Dean of Libraries and Archives, the Library Resources and Access Manager leads a team of staff responsible for technical services, access services, & resource sharing. This position oversees the acquisitions budget, has five direct reports, and manages a portfolio of ~13 individuals. The LRAM is responsible for developing and sustaining a unified approach to resource management, access, and patron services, ensuring collaboration, coordination, and communication across library departments. This position works closely with the Collections Librarian, ordering librarians, and other partners inside and outside the library. The incumbent is a member of the leadership team and serves as the staff supervisor-in-charge in the absence of the Dean.

## Responsibilities

• Under direction from the Dean of Libraries & Archives, is an active member of the leadership team and serve as the staff supervisor-in-charge in their absence

• Contribute to a positive organizational culture, facilitating collaboration, coordination, and communication within and across departments

• Hire, train, coach, and mentor supervisees, assisting the Head of Access Services & Resource sharing with the same; set goals, track progress, monitor results, and provide feedback and guidance to ensure success

• Support the Head of Access Services & Resource Sharing to ensure efficient and effective workflows and outstanding patron-oriented services

• Under direction from the Dean, oversee the library acquisitions budget and related financial processes and practices; create, input, roll-over and manage the budget (~$1mill in operating and endowments) in the library LSP (Alma); approve fund codes and expenditures; reconcile accounts, track balances, and prepare budget projections

• Oversee print and electronic resource acquisitions staff and operations, ensuring adherence to established procedures that facilitate efficient processes, responsible financial practices, and accessible library resources; ensure maintenance of up-to-date vendor files

• Coordinate the electronic resource renewals and cancellations process in consultation with the librarians and acquisitions staff; communicate with vendors and consortia as needed on issues related to ordering, invoicing, and activation

• Supervise cataloguing and metadata technician; ensure high-quality records that facilitate access and discoverability as determined by the Collections Librarian; support librarians with digital and other special projects as requested; facilitate effective and timely workflows

• Assist with the maintenance of up-to-date holdings and records information for electronic resources, ensuring accuracy and accessibility in the discovery layer and A-Z list; refer complex access and records questions to the Collections Librarian

• Serve as a member of the electronic resource troubleshooting team; assists with triaging, resolving, and delegating support tickets; communicate professionally with patrons to resolve issues and ensure access

• In collaboration with Novanet and internal team, configure the acquisitions and fulfillment modules in Alma; maintain expert knowledge of Alma functions and analytics; identify and ensure task cleanup for acquisitions and cataloguing functions

• Develop procedures and documentation to support departmental operations and make recommendations for improvement

• Run reports, gather statistics, and communicate frequently with library administration, financial services, librarians, vendors, and others; support librarians' collection and electronic resource assessment and evaluation processes as needed

• Identify, recommend, and assist with implementation and training for new systems, services, processes and skills for continuous improvement in consultation with appropriate colleagues

• Coordinate, provide, or support training for staff and student workers; supervise student workers as needed; provide backup to departmental operations as needed.

## Other Duties

• Represents the library on Novanet, CAAL, and other relevant professional committees; library staff are encouraged to participate in activities and events that promote our collections, services, and resources internally and externally

• May serve on the web services team, supporting activities that ensure accurate and timely information on the library website, assisting with the configuration of the ILS discovery layer (Primo) and other methods to improve discoverability and access; may serve on the library's public services committee, collections committee, and others as appropriate

• Stay current on and pursue relevant professional development opportunities on best practices and trends in library services and technologies; makes recommendations to the Dean or other parties as appropriate

• Work collaboratively and effectively with library colleagues on shared strategies, initiatives, and issues; positively and professionally represents the library internally and externally.

• Support the Dean with special projects, as needed

• Other duties as assigned

## Qualifications/skills

• A Bachelor's degree, Library Technician's Diploma (LIT) or equivalent, and a minimum of 5 years of library experience is required

• An equivalent combination of education, skills, and experience may be considered

• Experience in at least four of the following areas is required:
• Superior knowledge of Alma or comparable ILS

• Project management

• Library acquisitions

• Circulation/access services

• Electronic resource management

• Budget management and accounting

• Experience with creating and maintaining catalogue and metadata records

• Outstanding interpersonal, communication, and patron service skills

• Demonstrated skill as a leader, mentor, and trainer; ability to lead teams and effectively supervise work

• Advanced proficiency with spreadsheet software (e.g., Excel) and intermediate proficiency with Office products; high degree of comfort with and the ability to adapt quickly to new technologies

• Ability to run reports, track statistics, monitor trends and make informed decisions

• Ability to take initiative and manage multiple projects, priorities, deadlines, and develop/implement process improvements

• Demonstrated aptitude for investigating and troubleshooting technical and process related issues

• Attention to detail and accuracy, and ability to keep accurate financial records

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

## Duties of Position:

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Primary Care Paramedics are based on the current National Occupational Competency Profile (NOCP) for Primary Care Paramedics,Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in paramedicine or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

Required Qualifications:

• You are entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizenship, permanent resident status or work permit)

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record

• Must have a high regard for confidentiality and patient safety

• Primary Care Paramedic program/course of over six months; If you do not have one and are interested in this career, here is a list of paramedic programs in Atlantic Canada, click here

• Must be registered, active Paramedic with the Paramedic Association of New Brunswick; If you are not currently registered in New Brunswick, please visit PANB at www.panb.ca

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 4 Driver's Licence (or equivalent)

Additional requirements for your application:

• Current Resume and Cover Letter

• A copy of your PCP diploma from an accredited institution

• Proof of current registration with Paramedic Association of New Brunswick

• Proof of completion of a Physical Abilities Test (PAT) specific to working as a paramedic within the last 12 months

• Proof of valid CPR level C certification issued in the last 12 months

• Photocopy of front and back of valid Class 4 driver's license (or equivalent) with minimum one year driving experience

• Driver's abstract; issued within the last 30 days

• Copy of any valid Driver's course certificate i.e. CEVO, VFIS or NS VSP or equivalent issued within the last three years

• Criminal Record with Vulnerable Sector Check; issued within the last 30 days

• Immunization Record (Tetanus Tdap) within the last 10 years, 2 MMR vaccines (Measles, Mumps and Rubella) or lab evidenced immunity, 2 Varicella vaccines (Chicken Pox) or lab evidenced immunity, 3 Hepatitis B doses and Lab evidenced immunity, TB Skin Test (2 step) and a 1-step in the last 12 months; if reactive a follow up chest x-ray). Please note, a meeting with our Employee Health and Wellness Consultant can be scheduled, to ensure that all vaccinations are up to date by the time an offer is made

2240106.title: Hydrogeologist
2240106.employer: GEMTEC Consulting Engineers and Scientists Limited
2240106.description:
We're looking for a Hydrogeologist to join our growing team in Fredericton, NB. This role is also open to our other New Brunswick offices in Moncton, Saint John, Bathurst or Grand Falls.

At GEMTEC, we offer something different. We're a perfect sized employee-owned, 400-person multi-disciplinary consulting firm that is large enough to compete head-to-head with publicly traded engineering giants, but still small enough to maintain the culture and flexibility of a close-knit team.

Our size and hands-on management style let us move quickly, embrace new opportunities, and empower our people to shape their own careers—without getting lost in corporate bureaucracy.

A typical day on the job might look like:

• Provide technical support to a wide variety of physical hydrogeology projects and prepare proposals and reports.

• Design field investigations such as drilling, coring and test pitting logging; soil and bedrock description and characterization; monitoring well and groundwater/surface water instrumentation installation; single- and multi-well pumping tests; soil, groundwater, sediment and surface water sampling; infiltration rate testing; and private well monitoring.

• Prepare technical proposals and reports, including hydrogeological characterization assessments; impact assessments, groundwater supply and source water protection studies and approvals; quarry, mine pit and construction dewatering assessments and permitting; water balance assessments; and groundwater and surface water interaction and monitoring programs.

• Develop and maintain relationships with clients.

The good stuff you get:

• Fair pay plus extra: competitive salary with year-end profit-sharing bonus.

• Complete health & dental coverage including vision, paramedical services, and Teladoc.

• Retirement planning made easier with a 5% employer match on your contributions.

• Paid time off (vacation and sick days) plus Employee & Family Assistance Program when you need it.

• Office year-end closure (paid time off between Christmas and the New Year).

Your background and what you bring:

• Bachelor's degree in earth science, environmental science or geological/geotechnical/civil engineering with an emphasis in water resources or hydrogeology.

• Professional license in NB (i.e., P.Geo. or P.Eng.)

• 5 to 10 years of relevant professional related experience (preferably in consulting).

• Knowledge and understanding of provincial and federal regulatory frameworks for groundwater withdrawal/use, drinking water supply, contaminated sites assessment and management, and environmental assessment is required.

• Familiarity with infrastructure, pit and quarry dewatering as well as exploration and development of community water supplies is required, with specific experience in the mining industry considered an asset.

• Groundwater flow and transport modeling experience is considered an asset.

• Valid NB driver's license.

Interested individuals, click here to apply: https://gemtec.bamboohr.com/careers/350

Thank you for taking the time to consider GEMTEC. Only candidates proceeding to the next phase of the application process will be contacted at this time. We encourage you to connect with us on LinkedIn, even if this opportunity isn't for you, the next one might be!

Should you be selected for an interview and require accommodation of any kind, please kindly help us understand how we can help.

2240378.description:
## This is the life-changing opportunity you've been looking for.

Horizon Health Network in beautiful New Brunswick is looking for a Regional Director of Population Health to join our team!

Horizon Health Network (Horizon) is seeking a strategic, motivated, and agile individual to join our team as a Regional Director of Population Health. The ideal candidate will be a senior expert on population health, providing expertise and strategic support regionally on population health initiatives, system improvements and identifying and addressing health disparities within a large organization.

## Why you should work here

Working for Horizon gives you a career that provides an east coast lifestyle and the chance to make a big difference in the lives of New Brunswickers.

This position comes with competitive salary, paid time off, sick benefits, employer paid contributions into our government pension plan and a remote work policy.

Horizon is committed to enhancing our diverse and inclusive environment for our employees and patients. We believe in a healthcare system that equally supports all people regardless of race, ethnicity, national origin, social background, religion, gender identity or expression, age, disability, or sexual orientation. An environment based on a commitment to diversity and inclusion supports our goal of safe and quality patient care.

## Who you are

You hold a master's degree in health or social science discipline. A concentration of study or advanced degree on population health and/or social determinants of health is considered an asset for this position. You have the ability to work with minimal supervision and possess strong organizational and time management skills. You have 7 to 10 years progressive leadership experience with experience in human resource and financial management, problem solving and critical thinking. You have additional training in project management and organizational change/improvement and trauma informed care (an asset). Using a Two-Eyed seeing approach, you foster an environment that supports traditional Indigenous ways of knowing & healing practices with evidenced based quality care. You also possess additional experience leading collaborative initiatives in a clinical setting (asset). You have demonstrated program and project leadership skills, including expertise in planning, implementation, and evaluation of programs.

## What you will do

• Develop and execute strategic plans in addition to develop, implement, monitor, and evaluate operational plans related to Population Health services in alignment with Horizon's Strategic Plan.

• Provide strategic leadership to Horizon Health Network in the adoption of evidence-informed approaches to improve population health and effect system transformation.

• Identify and support research, best practices and projects that align with the mandate and strategic direction of the department and Horizon Health.

• Support the facilitation of a Two-Eyed Seeing approach to wellbeing and care of Indigenous clients and building these systems within Horizon Health Network.

• Serve as a strategic business partner, advisor, and leader to influence all levels of the organization by providing and executing responsive solutions.

• Work closely with Department of Health and other government departments and external stakeholders to enhance policy and strategically support the delivery of population health priorities and assure the modernization and effective delivery of population health services.

• Leads a regional approach to evidenced based practices in community engagement in collaboration with public health, primary care, addictions and mental health partners as well as other stakeholders in Horizon.

• Supervise multiple operational population health teams delivering services within Horizon and communities within New Brunswick.

• Oversee, monitor, and evaluate the quality and safety of Population Health services.

• Prepare, manage, monitor, and report on budgets and ensure fiscal responsibility within all departments.

• Develop, review, revise, monitor and report on performance indicators.

• Oversee the processes that ensure adherence with professional practice standards, policies, and procedures.

• Oversee human resource planning, skill optimization & utilization, productivity & capacity enhancements and assist with recruitment and retention activities.

• Build and maintain relationships with physicians and internal and external stakeholders, including integration of population health approaches within the overall Community portfolio and within the larger Horizon system.

• Participate/coordinate quality improvement activities and risk management processes to improve quality of care with a specific focus on taking a regional approach to improvements & increased accountability, accessibility, productivity, capacity, responsiveness.

• Provide leadership and oversight of standardization of policies and procedures across all zones in collaboration with local Directors and Managers of Population Health and Public Health.

• Address strategic priorities related to health equity and the social determinants of health by building capacity in the organization is a focus of this portfolio.

• Travel throughout the region/province as required.

## Horizon Competency

Core competencies for non-bargaining positions are based on the LEADS in a Caring Environment leadership capabilities framework: Lead Self, Engage Others, Achieve Results, Develop Coalitions, and System Transformation.

In addition to LEADS, all positions need to demonstrate compassion, patience, and professionalism in all interactions, consistently upholding a respectful and supportive environment for patients, clients, families, and colleagues. Proactively addresses concerns and responds to emerging needs with empathy and diligence, contributing to high-quality, patient/client centered care.

## Interested? Apply Today!

To learn more, visit MyHorizonCareer.ca/management-business-professionals/

Horizon Health Network (Horizon) only accepts on-line applications.

## About Horizon's Recruitment Process

We thank all applicant who apply; however, only those selected for further consideration will be contacted. All interested applicants are encouraged to apply as an equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered.

Horizon's recruitment screening process may include language proficiency testing, clerical testing and/or behavioral assessment. If you are selected for testing, you will be contacted via the email address provided on your application. The official results will be shared with the candidate, Human Resources and the requesting manager electronically and language results will be placed on the personnel file for Horizon's hiring purposes.

## Diversity Statement

Horizon is committed to enhancing our diverse and inclusive environment for our employees and patients. We believe in a healthcare system that equally supports all people regardless of race, ethnicity, national origin, social background, religion, gender identity or expression, age, disability, or sexual orientation. ## This is the life-changing opportunity you've been looking for.

Horizon Health Network in beautiful New Brunswick is looking for a Clinical Director to join our team!

Horizon Health Network (Horizon) is seeking a strategic, innovative, and motivated individual to join our team as a Clinical Director. The Clinical Director will work in partnership with the Clinical Department Head and Program Medical Directors across Horizon to provide overall responsibility and accountability for the delivery of services within allocated resources.

## Why you should work here

Working for Horizon gives you a career that provides an east coast lifestyle and the chance to make a big difference in the lives of New Brunswickers.

This position comes with competitive salary, paid time off, sick benefits, employer paid contributions into our government pension plan and a remote work policy.

Horizon is committed to enhancing our diverse and inclusive environment for our employees and patients. We believe in a healthcare system that equally supports all people regardless of race, ethnicity, national origin, social background, religion, gender identity or expression, age, disability, or sexual orientation. An environment based on a commitment to diversity and inclusion supports our goal of safe and quality patient care.

## Who you are

You have a worked as a healthcare leader for a minimum of 7 years. You have experience in healthcare administration, mentoring, leading, facilitating, team building, negotiation, decision-making and conflict resolution.

You hold a master's degree in health or business administration linked to a clinical profession.

## What you will do

The Clinical Director will:

• Lead and facilitate the delivery of quality care in close collaboration with the applicable Horizon Clinical Networks/Programs.

• Lead the coordination of daily operations and patient flow across the facility, optimizing capacity, access, and discharge processes to support safe, efficient, and timely patient care.

Leadership and Management:

• Provide visionary leadership.

• Foster a culture of teamwork, accountability, and continuous performance improvement to delivery safe, quality patient care.

• Ensure departments are fiscally responsible.

• Oversee the daily operations

Strategic Planning and Continuous Performance Improvement:

• Collaborate with the Clinical Executive Director, Program Medical Director and Regional Leadership to develop and execute strategic plans, goals, and initiatives that are aligned with Horizon's mission, vision, and values, as well as the Province of New Brunswick's Health Care Plan.

• Continuously evaluate and improve the quality and efficiency of services through established key performance indicators, project specific metrics, audits, and feedback from the teams.

Patient Safety and Quality Assurance:

• Ensure compliance with all relevant healthcare regulations, accreditation standards, and licensure requirements, maintaining documentation and records as needed.

• Implement and maintain regional protocols, policies, and quality assurance initiatives to uphold patient safety and enhance outcomes.

• Monitor incident reporting, address incidents as they arise, and implement recommendations from quality process reviews in the specified timeframe.

Staff Development:

• Collaborate in the recruitment of staff with talent acquisition.

• Foster an environment of professional growth and educational advancement.

• Address the resolution of practice, behavioral, and attendance issues in collaboration with department managers, professional practice, and human resources as appropriate.

Budget Management:

• Ensure all departments are adhering to defined budgets.

• Monitor monthly variances and expenses to identify cost-saving opportunities while maintaining the highest standards of patient care.

• Oversee the procurement, maintenance, and utilization of equipment and technology to ensure the highest level of care.

Specific Regional Health Authority Responsibilities:

• Represent the program on committees locally, regionally and provincially.

• Prepare, on request, reports for presentation to various administrative board committees, foundations, and the Department of Health.

• Assumes regular responsibility for Administrative On-Call for respective zone as per established schedule.

2239611.title: Thoracic Surgeon
2239611.description:
This is the life-changing opportunity you've been looking for. Join a division that believes in collaboration, teamwork, research, medical education, innovation, and excellence in clinical care.

Horizon Health Network is seeking a General Thoracic Surgeon to be a part of our Regional Thoracic Surgery Program at the Saint John Regional Hospital - a key component of our province-wide vision for surgical excellence grounded in national best practices.

You'll collaborate with a wide network including the New Brunswick Heart Centre, Trauma Services, and Medical and Radiation Oncology to deliver integrated, patient-centered care.

This new regional program will deliver care aligned with the Canadian Association of Thoracic Surgeons and Cancer Care Ontario's Level 1 standards, including:

• Multidisciplinary, high-volume surgical practice focused on lung, esophageal, and mediastinal pathology

• Access to advanced diagnostics, interventional radiology, endoscopy, and comprehensive cancer services

• Integration with medical oncology, radiation oncology, trauma, and pulmonary medicine

• Emphasis on rapid access and evidence-based perioperative care

• Technology & Infrastructure: A robotic surgery platform is already in place, with a Hybrid OR currently in development to further enhance the delivery of complex thoracic procedures.

• Collegial Culture: Collaborate with subspecialty teams and join an inclusive, interdisciplinary environment.

• Participation in the CATS National Database Program facilitating quality improvement and research opportunities.

## Why you should work here

New Brunswick offers a safe and welcoming community with a relaxed lifestyle and a true work-life balance, enriched by its diverse Indigenous, Anglophone, and Francophone heritage.

Horizon Health Network is the largest health authority in the region, employing dedicated professionals focused on delivering high-quality care. Our employees collaborate with community partners to provide accessible health programs and services to over half a million people through our 12 hospitals and more than 100 medical facilities and clinics.

Located on the beautiful bay of Fundy, Saint John offers coastal living, vibrant arts and culinary scenes, and quick access to wilderness—all without the big-city grind. You'll also enjoy a lower cost of living and a close-knit, welcoming community.

## Incentives & Remuneration

Remuneration for this position is based on a recently renewed, competitive New Brunswick Medicare Alternate Funding Plan for Thoracic Surgery. Base salary is $684,000 per annum with incremental increases in 2027 and 2028. There is an additional Mandated On-Call stipend of $300.00 per day. Medical education remuneration is based on set Dalhousie University rates.?Hours of work are normally provided between 0800 and 1600 Monday to Friday.

Successful applicants may be eligible to receive the following:

• Urban recruitment incentive of $50,000.00 with a 2-year return of service.

• Moving expense reimbursement is also available.

## What you will do

The Physician will provide both inpatient and outpatient thoracic surgical care and share on-call duties with the Division. A typical schedule includes:

• Access to a modern MIS suite, da Vinci Xi robot, and Illumisite bronchoscopy platform.

• Collaborative care with cardiac surgery, ICU, respiratory, oncology, radiology, ENT, and plastics.

• Ongoing capital upgrades: new ICU, hybrid OR, endoscopy suite, and oncology clinic.

• Support from a full-time Thoracic Surgery Clinical Assistant.

• Office-based and ambulatory patient care, inpatient rounds, and hospital consults.

• Assigned OR time and 1-in-3 on-call coverage, including holidays and weekends.

• Interdisciplinary collaboration and adherence to evidence-based standards.

• Active participation in education, research, and continuous quality improvement.

• Commitment to Horizon Health Network's mission, values, and AFP deliverables.

• Accurate documentation and coverage planning for absences.

Academic Affiliation: The Saint John Regional Hospital is a teaching hospital and part of Horizon's strategic plan to grow research and innovation. Members of the Division are required to be part of the medical education program partnering with Dalhousie University New Brunswick. Members are eligible for an academic appointment with Dalhousie University

## Who you are

• You possess a Medical Degree from a recognized medical school and postgraduate training in General Thoracic Surgery with Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons certification.

• You must be eligible for licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of New Brunswick.

• Written and spoken competence in English is required at an advanced level. Bilingual skills would be considered an asset.

• Proven experience in acute care settings and possess advanced MIS skills.

• Ability to perform under pressure while maintaining high standards of patient care.

• Commitment to ongoing education and research within the field of thoracic surgery.

## Interested? Apply Today!

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

## Duties of Position:

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Primary Care Paramedics are based on the current National Occupational Competency Profile (NOCP) for Primary Care Paramedics,Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in paramedicine or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

## Position Overview:

The Saint John Police Force is now accepting applications for experienced Police Officers.

Police officers are an integral part of the community, responsible for maintaining law and order and protecting members of the public. Police officers build relationships with community members and work collaboratively with them to solve problems and enhance the wellbeing of the people they serve with self-confidence, analytical thinking, while always acting at a high moral standard with honesty and integrity.

## Minimum Requirements:

To become a Sworn Police Officer, as outlined in the New Brunswick Police Act, applicants must:

• Have reached the full age of nineteen years.

• Be a Canadian citizen or a permanent resident of Canada.

• Be a graduate of the Police Science Program at the Atlantic Police Academy OR

• Be a graduate of a comparable training course offered at a police training institute approved by the Minister OR

• Have a minimum of three years of satisfactory full-time service as a member of any police force in Canada.

• Not have been convicted of an offence under the Criminal Code (Canada), the Narcotic Control Act (Canada), or the Food and Drugs Act (Canada), or if convicted, shall have received a pardon.

• Have a valid driver's license.

• Be of good character and habits.

All applicants must be security cleared and able to pass the Physical Abilities Requirement Evaluation (P.A.R.E.) to policing standards.

## Recognized Police Training Academies:

In addition to the Atlantic Police Academy located in Summerside, PEI, graduates of the following Police Training Academies are also currently recognized:

• British Columbia Justice Institute

• RCMP Training Academy

• Canadian Forces Military Police Academy

• L'Ecole nationale de police du Quebec

• Ontario Police College

Note: Community college and other college courses that include studies in law and security administration do not meet the level of training as defined under the NB Police Act.

Salary will follow the wage schedule of the Saint John Police Association collective agreement.

## Application Instructions:

Qualified applicants should submit their cover letters and resumes to:

Saint John Police Force
Attention: Human Resources

2240720.description:
Title: Truck and Transport Mechanic (Service Tech I)
Salary: $33.95 hourly
BSA: $268.03 biweekly benefit spending allowance.

## Description:

Are you a Red Seal Service Technician who takes pride in keeping essential fleets moving? Join the City of Fredericton's Fleet Services team and put your expertise to work maintaining and repairing transit vehicles that help keep our community connected every day.

The City of Fredericton is seeking skilled fleet maintenance professionals to join its Fleet Services Division. Reporting to the Foreman, Fleet Services, the Service Technician is primarily responsible for performing maintenance and repairs on the City's transit fleet, with opportunities to work on other municipal fleet equipment as operational needs require. The successful candidate will utilize their technical expertise and previous experience to perform high-quality work at the journeyman level within the Truck and Transport & Heavy Equipment section. Assignments may be provided through written or verbal instructions, and completed work is evaluated through testing and the operational performance of vehicles and equipment.

Qualifications:

We recognize that candidates bring diverse experiences and backgrounds. Applicants are encouraged to demonstrate how their qualifications meet the essential requirements of the position. Additional valued qualifications may strengthen an application but are not required.

## Essential

To be considered for this position, applicants must demonstrate the following:

• Minimum prerequisite is Journeyman Truck & Transport Mechanic (Red Seal) certification OR finishing the final block training with demonstrated eligibility to challenge the Red Seal exam.

• Valid NB driver's license, class V.

• Knowledge of standard practices and equipment of the Truck & Transport & Heavy Equipment mechanic trade(s); knowledge of the principles of operation of gasoline and diesel engines and of mechanical repair methods applicable to a variety of fleet vehicles.

• A clear Criminal Record Check as well as a clear Driver's Abstract, are required as conditions of employment.

Equivalent combinations of education, training, and experience may be considered where they provide the knowledge, skills, and abilities required to perform the essential duties of the position. Applicants are encouraged to describe how their background aligns with the requirements of the role.

## Valued

The following qualifications are not required but may strengthen an application:

• Five years of relevant experience in Truck and Transport & Heavy Equipment Repair field.

• Knowledge of occupational hazards and safety practices of the trade.

• Ability to understand and carry out oral and written instructions.

• Ability to diagnose or trouble shoot engine and electrical problems.

• Must have complete set of tools to perform the work listed above.

• Knowledge of Motor coach and Transit/Bus fleets would be an asset.

• Knowledge of Fire Suppression Assets and equipment including pumps would be an asset.

• Knowledge in Snow removal equipment and attachments, along with material spreading controls would be an asset.

## What You'll Do

• Adjust, troubleshoot, diagnose, repair or replace parts and components of heavy equipment/trucks and other related components.

• Installation of electrical equipment and accessories including 2-way radios, pay terminals, cameras, and other associated technologies.

• Perform scheduled maintenance service such as oil changes, lubrications and tune ups and tire changes.

• Complete reports to record problems and work performed.

• Other related duties as required.

Competitive, Progressive Pay Structure:
Grow your earnings with clearly defined technician levels based on experience, ability, and licensing:

• Service Tech I: $33.95/hour

• Service Tech II: $35.94/hour

• Service Tech III: $37.07/hour

• Advance your career while increasing your earning potential.

Generous Benefits Support:
Receive a biweekly Benefit Spending Allowance (BSA) of $268.03 to help offset the cost of your health and dental coverage. Any unused BSA credits can be allocated to a Health Spending Account (HSA) or taken as additional taxable earnings.

## Total Compensation Package:

A Service Tech earns approximately $77,850.36 - $84,362.17 annually, including base pay plus a biweekly benefits allowance of $268.03 with additional value from pension and comprehensive benefits.

Reliable Hours & Job Stability:
Benefit from a guaranteed 40-hour work week and long-term employment stability with a trusted employer.

Work-Life Balance You Can Count On:
Enjoy a predictable Monday-to-Friday schedule from 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., giving you the freedom to plan your personal time with confidence and make the most of your evenings and weekends. While occasional overtime may be required to support operational needs and service delivery, all eligible hours worked outside of regular business hours are compensated at the applicable overtime rate.

Expand Your Technical Expertise:
Work with a wide range of equipment and brands, giving you valuable hands-on experience that strengthens your skills and career growth.

## Build a future with an employer that supports your life today and tomorrow.

At the City of Fredericton, we believe great employers offer more than just a salary. They provide stability, purpose, flexibility, and the confidence to plan for the future. That's why our total rewards package goes beyond your base salary to support your health, well-being, financial security, and work-life balance at every stage of your career and life.

## Health & Wellness Designed Around You

Your base pay is complemented by a biweekly flexible benefit spending allowance that helps you build the coverage that best fits your needs. Choose from comprehensive health, dental, and insurance options, and access confidential support through our Employee and Family Assistance Program.

## Time to Recharge

Enjoy vacation entitlements that grow with years of service, plus the option for eligible employees to purchase additional prorated leave each year, giving you greater flexibility to balance work and life.

## Retirement Security

Build long-term financial security through a shared risk pension plan, with contributions from both you and the City.

## Meaningful Work. Lasting Impact.

Help shape a vibrant, inclusive, and growing Fredericton. Your work will play a role in delivering services that make a significant and positive difference in the community.

## Our Commitment

The City of Fredericton is an equal opportunity employer committed to a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace. We welcome applications from Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, racialized persons, and other equity-deserving groups. Qualified candidates who self-identify may receive preference in line with employment equity goals and applicable legislation.

If you require accommodation, please advise Human Resources so we can work with you to meet your needs

## Apply Now!

Please submit your application on or before October 6, 2026, at 4:30 p.m. AST.

• Extended health coverage

• Dental coverage

• Vision coverage

• Company paid pension plan

• Year-round dedicated work

• Driver incentive programs

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

## Duties of Position:

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Primary Care Paramedics are based on the current National Occupational Competency Profile (NOCP) for Primary Care Paramedics,Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in paramedicine or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

Required Qualifications:

• You are entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizenship, permanent resident status or work permit)

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record

• Must have a high regard for confidentiality and patient safety

• Primary Care Paramedic program/course of over six months; If you do not have one and are interested in this career, here is a list of paramedic programs in Atlantic Canada, click here

• Must be registered, active Paramedic with the Paramedic Association of New Brunswick; If you are not currently registered in New Brunswick, please visit PANB at www.panb.ca

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 4 Driver's Licence (or equivalent)

Additional requirements for your application:

• Current Resume and Cover Letter

• A copy of your PCP diploma from an accredited institution

• Proof of current registration with Paramedic Association of New Brunswick

• Proof of completion of a Physical Abilities Test (PAT) specific to working as a paramedic within the last 12 months

• Proof of valid CPR level C certification issued in the last 12 months

• Photocopy of front and back of valid Class 4 driver's license (or equivalent) with minimum one year driving experience

• Driver's abstract; issued within the last 30 days

• Copy of any valid Driver's course certificate i.e. CEVO, VFIS or NS VSP or equivalent issued within the last three years

• Criminal Record with Vulnerable Sector Check; issued within the last 30 days

• Immunization Record (Tetanus Tdap) within the last 10 years, 2 MMR vaccines (Measles, Mumps and Rubella) or lab evidenced immunity, 2 Varicella vaccines (Chicken Pox) or lab evidenced immunity, 3 Hepatitis B doses and Lab evidenced immunity, TB Skin Test (2 step) and a 1-step in the last 12 months; if reactive a follow up chest x-ray). Please note, a meeting with our Employee Health and Wellness Consultant can be scheduled, to ensure that all vaccinations are up to date by the time an offer is made

• Valid Official Language Assessments (oral assessment only) in both French and English from the Department of Post-secondary Education, Training and Labour. You can contact them at LS-SL@gnb.ca. Please take into account the additional time to receive your language assessment

• Additional training and/or education is highly valued.

For any questions for our HR team, please contact us at jobs-emplois@ambulancenb.ca

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

The New Brunswick Extra-Mural Program (EMP), often known as the "hospital without walls," has operated under the simple philosophy of helping New Brunswickers receive the care they need in the places where they are healthiest and happiest - their homes and communities. EMP makes a difference in the lives of those it serves by drastically reducing hospital admissions and greatly increasing patient satisfaction with its level of health care.

As part of EMP, your role is vital in our province's overall health. Join an integrated, multi-disciplinary team of health care professionals, dedicated to providing New Brunswickers with outstanding, highly coordinated primary health care.

## JOB SUMMARY

As a member of the interdisciplinary EMP team, the Occupational Therapist is responsible for coordinating and providing quality care within the scope of practice to patients and families by, promoting, maintaining and/or restoring functional performance.

## REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND OTHER JOB REQUIREMENTS:

• Bachelor's or Master's degree of Science in Occupational Therapy or equivalent approved by the Canadian Association of Occupational Therapists;

• Must be a member in good standing of the New Brunswick Association of Occupational Therapists and eligible for membership in the Canadian Association of Occupational Therapists;

• Must have a thorough knowledge of equipment and supplies utilized in the provision of occupational therapy.

• Knowledge of the target population of Extra-Mural Services and available community services;

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 5 Driver's License and good driving record (proof required);

• Submit a valid and clean criminal record check;

• Have a current CPR Level C certification that has been issued in the last 12 months, or be prepared to obtain within 3 months;

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and possess leadership and coaching skills, strong interpersonal skills, good judgment and decision making skills;

• Must be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record;

• Must have a high regard for confidentiality; and

• Must have excellent work habits and have a professional appearance.

If you are interested in working with a dynamic team of professionals and possess the necessary qualifications, please click the 'Apply Now' button to submit your resume.

2239730.title: Medical Office Administrator
2239730.description:
## Harbour Health Partners

Role: Medical Office Administrator

We are looking for a reliable Medical Office Administrator (MOA) to join our growing administration team. Our MOAs are the first point of contact for our patients and an important part of the support team for our providers. We are looking for someone who has a strong administrative foundation, takes pride in their work, is coachable, and wants to contribute to a team that cares deeply about the service and care we provide to our patients and to each other.

About us: Harbour Health Partners is a multi-physician primary care medical practice located in Millidgeville, in Saint John, New Brunswick. We have been a group practice since 2013 and currently have six practicing partners.

Our Mission: To be a medical home that patients can fully trust. This means that we are available, approachable, and provide safe, responsive, and science-based care.

## Our Values:

• Community Needs Responsiveness

• Secure Skilled Staff

• Collaborative Team Based Approach

• Inclusive Safe Environment

• Education Focused

• Innovation

## Seeking What Success in This Role Looks Like

A successful MOA at Harbour Health is dependable, professional, and engaged in their work. They learn and follow our processes, communicate effectively, work efficiently, pay attention to detail, problem-solve, and can be trusted to follow through on their responsibilities. Our team works to establish expectations for quality, communication, productivity, and timely completion of work. We regularly use data and quality improvement initiatives to help us learn, improve and evolve our processes. We value team members who are open to feedback, share ideas, and contribute to positive change as our practice evolves.

## Position Overview:

• Employment: Full-time, 40 hours/week, Monday-Friday

• Schedule: Regular hours between 7:45 a.m.-5:30 p.m.; occasional evening/weekend availability, in office only/not remote

• Compensation: $22-$25/hour, commensurate with experience; paid bi-weekly

• Vacation: 3 weeks paid vacation to start, increasing with years of service

• Benefits: Extended health, LTD, paid family needs days, additional unpaid days, and professional development opportunities

• Staff must adhere to clinic privacy, confidentiality, and Public Health requirements, including applicable immunization recommendations.

## The Person We Are Looking For

The ideal candidate is professional, caring, self-aware and adaptable, with the ability to balance competing priorities in a busy clinic environment. You should have:

• Strong organizational and time-management skills

• Strong written and verbal communication skills in English

• Experience managing telephone calls, scheduling, documentation and competing administrative priorities

• Confidence learning new software and electronic systems

• Accurate and efficient data-entry skills

• Good judgment and problem-solving abilities

• Experience handling confidential or sensitive information

• The ability to prioritize and transition between tasks efficiently

• The ability to follow established policies and procedures while exercising appropriate independent judgment

• A professional and welcoming approach when interacting with patients, colleagues and providers

• Reliability, including regular attendance and adherence to scheduled hours

• A team-focused and adaptable approach

• The ability to work independently and recognize what needs to be done

## Experience & Education Required:

• Minimum 3 years of administrative experience, preferably in a busy, client-facing professional environment

• Demonstrated experience performing a range of administrative responsibilities rather than reception duties alone

• Strong proficiency with Windows-based computer systems and standard office technology

• Experience managing confidential information

• Demonstrated ability to multitask, prioritize and problem-solve

## Assets:

• Previous experience in a medical office or other healthcare environment

• Medical Office Administration diploma or certificate

• Experience with Electronic Medical Record (EMR) systems

• Knowledge of healthcare administrative workflows such as requisitions, referrals, and results

• Bilingualism

## Essential Daily Job Functions include, but are not limited to:

• Welcome and check in patients, answer phones, schedule appointments, and respond to patient and provider requests

• Monitor and action EMR tasks, faxes, documents, and incoming patient requests accurately and promptly

• Maintain accurate electronic records, including scanning, document management, and data entry

• Monitor provider schedules and support efficient day-to-day clinic flow

• Process invoices, payments, and receipts for uninsured services

• Maintain patient privacy and confidentiality and follow clinic policies and procedures

• Assist with general office and clinic operations, including opening/closing, supplies, and maintaining organized shared spaces

• Provide additional administrative and clinic support as needed within the scope of the role and following appropriate training

• A complete job description will be provided for candidates selected for interviews

Reference Requirement - Candidates selected for an interview will be asked to bring three professional references; personal references will not be accepted.

Employment Eligibility - This position requires the successful candidate to be legally authorized to work in Canada. At this time, the employer is unable to provide work authorization or sponsorship for this position. By submitting an application, candidates confirm that they meet these employment eligibility requirements and do not require employer sponsorship to accept employment in this role.

We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

## How to Apply:

All applications should be sent directly to management@harbourhealthpartners.ca

Subject Line - Fall 2026 MOA Application - Your Name

All applications to include your contact information

All resumes to be sent as a PDF with your introductory letter in the body of your email

## Deadline to Apply: October 2nd, 2026

We will interview throughout, and will close the job ad early if we find the successful candidate

2235098.title: Senior Marine Structural Engineer
2235098.employer: GEMTEC Consulting Engineers and Scientists Limited
2235098.description:
Are you an experienced Marine Structural Engineer looking to progress your career? We're looking for a Senior Marine Structural Engineer to join our growing team. We are open to filling this position in any of our Atlantic Canada offices including Fredericton, Moncton, Saint John, Grand Falls, Bathurst, Halifax or St. John's.

At GEMTEC, we offer something different. We're an employee-owned, 400-person multidisciplinary consulting firm—not too big, not too small. We're large enough to compete head-to-head with publicly traded engineering giants, but still small enough to maintain the culture and flexibility of a close-knit team.

Our size and hands-on management style let us move quickly, embrace new opportunities, and empower our people to shape their own careers—without getting lost in corporate bureaucracy.

A typical day on the job might look like:

• Providing engineering designs for civil infrastructure projects (ports, harbours and bridges)

• Working with diverse teams of discipline managers, engineers, designers and technicians

• Managing projects and being responsible for completion on schedule and financial performance

• Acting as a technical resource and as a mentor to junior/intermediate staff

• Writing, compiling and reviewing technical reports

• Preparing fee proposals

• Being a member of site visit teams, gathering information as required to complement design activities

• Maintaining quality throughout a project and implement improvements when determined

• Preparing regular project summary reports

• Encouraging growth within the group and increasing the general knowledge base throughout the company

• Developing and sustaining long-lasting business relationships with clients

• Identifying and mitigating potential hazards in the field or onsite, promoting a safe working environment.

The good stuff you get:

• Full time permanent?salaried position

• Employee owned company with future potential to be a shareholder

• Year end profit sharing bonus

• Health and dental benefits

• Matching RRSP employer contributions up to 5%

• Paid time off (vacation starting at 3 weeks per year and 2 weeks of sick time)

• Office year-end closure (paid time off between Christmas and New Years)

• Work/life balance including a 37.5 hour work week and flexible working arrangements including hybrid options.

• Growth and development opportunities as we work on a large variety of projects so you can build your skills and experience.

Your qualifications and what you bring:

• Bachelor's degree in civil engineering from an accredited University

• Minimum of 12 years of experience in civil engineering including specific expertise in marine structures.

• Adaptability to represent GEMTEC professionally with clients, developers, or contractors

• Strong written and verbal communication skills needed to convey technical ideas clearly

• Eligibility to register or are currently registered as a Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) with one or more of the Atlantic provinces

• Proven ability to manage projects

• Ability to obtain security clearance

• Valid driver's license

Interested individuals, click here to apply: https://gemtec.bamboohr.com/careers/339

Thank you for taking the time to consider GEMTEC. Only candidates proceeding to the next phase of the application process will be contacted at this time. We encourage you to connect with us on LinkedIn, even if this opportunity isn't for you, the next one might be!

Should you be selected for an interview and require accommodation of any kind, please kindly help us understand how we can help.

2226879.title: Glass Installation
2226879.description:
html
Job Title: Commercial Glass Installation Specialist
Location: Saint John, NB
Available Shifts: Full-Time, 7:00am - 6:00pm
Pay: $20/Hour

## Assignment Information:

Commercial glazers play a vital role in the construction and renovation of commercial buildings, contributing to both the aesthetic and practical aspects of architectural design.

Advantage Personnel is seeking a skilled and detail-oriented Commercial Glass Installation Specialist/Commercial Glazer to join our customer's growing and dynamic team! As a leader in the glass installation industry, they pride themselves on delivering exceptional service and high-quality craftsmanship. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in commercial glazing, a commitment to safety, and the ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.

## Responsibilities:

• Installing glass products, including windows, storefronts, curtain walls, glass doors, and partitions in various commercial settings.

• Replacing and repairing glass.

• Working with aluminum frames and other materials to support glass structures.

• Ensuring proper alignment, secure fittings, and effective sealing of glass installations to maintain structural integrity and aesthetic appeal.

• Adhering to all safety protocols and regulations established by the company and local authorities, including the Occupational Health and Safety Act in New Brunswick.

• Conducting thorough inspections of completed work to ensure it meets quality standards and client specifications.

• Maintaining accurate records of materials used, project timelines, and client communications.

• Addressing any issues promptly and professionally to maintain high customer satisfaction.

## Candidate Qualifications:

• High school diploma or equivalent is required. Additional training or certification in glazing or construction is an asset.

• Proficiency in using hand and power tools specific to glass installation.

• Understanding of building codes, safety regulations, and best practices in glazing.

• Ability to lift heavy materials (up to 50 pounds) and perform physically demanding tasks, including climbing ladders and working at heights.

• Strong problem-solving skills and a meticulous approach to installation and repairs.

• A valid driver's license with a clean driving abstract is required, as travel to job sites may be necessary.

2241244.description:
Court Stenographer Court ServicesJustice and Public SafetyPermanent - OPENBilingualCampbellton, NB

Interested in making a difference in our province? We encourage you to Choose GNB!

## Who we are

The Department of Justice and Public Safety is dedicated to upholding the law, advocating for the greater good, and ensuring justice is served impartially. We're committed to strengthening the safety, security, and resilience of communities and citizens.

Our work has a positive impact on our communities and helps improve the everyday lives of New Brunswickers. Together, we are over 45,000 public servants who are passionate problem-solvers, who make a difference and are proud to call New Brunswick home.

The Department of Justice and Public Safety is seeking an individual to join the Court Services Branch as a Court Stenographer working in Campbellton, NB

## What does a Court Stenographer Do?

As a Court Stenographer, you'll be at the heart of the judicial process, playing an essential role in attending court and recording evidence, transcribing, preparing legal documents, and providing support to the judiciary and to court participants. It's a chance to be part of something meaningful, and to gain practical experience in the New Brunswick justice system. As a court stenographer, you will be an integral part of a vital institution that upholds the principles of fairness, impartiality, and the rule of law.

What's in it for You?

Career Growth: Take advantage of opportunities for professional development, training, and advancement within the department. Learn about the inner workings of the legal system in New Brunswick - A fantastic opportunity for those who are interested in a career in the justice system or who are aspiring to pursue a law degree in the future.

Competitive Salary: Earn between $2,361.74- $2,731.47 biweekly ($61,405.24-$71,018.22 annually).

Comprehensive Benefits: Access a comprehensive benefits package, including the Public Service Shared Risk Pension Plan, and free Employee and Family Assistance Program (EFAP) services.

A safe workplace for all: Your health & safety are important to us. GNB has implemented preventative measures across the organization to ensure your health & safety.

Paid Vacation: 1.25 days of paid vacation per month.

## Who We're Looking For

We're seeking individuals with initiative, flexibility, a passion for order, effective communication skills, and the ability to work under pressure. An individual who can thrive in an environment using technology (including video conferencing and Teams) will be the best fit for this role. Whether you're a seasoned administrative professional or a legal enthusiast looking to make your mark, we want to hear from you!

## Work environment

• Office location: Campbellton Law Courts, NB

• Standard hours of work: Monday - Friday, 8:15-4:30 with weekend rotations for remand court (see myth/fact below)

• Occasional work outside normal working hours: (Sometimes court can sit over a noon hour or past 4:30, but we offer overtime, time off in lieu).

• Occasional travel within the region when required. (Expenses covered as per the GNB Travel policy)

Facts and Myths about the court stenographer role:

Myth: You need to transcribe during a hearing, and type everything in shorthand.

Fact: You do not transcribe while court is in session (no transcribing in real-time), and you do not need to know shorthand (it`s not like the movies anymore!). Only a regular keyboard is used, and you are not tested on words per minute.

Myth: All stenographers work every weekend.

Fact: Weekend remand court runs every Saturday and Sunday (and Statutory holidays), on a rotational basis in only one (1) of eight (8) judicial districts across the province. Two (2) stenographers are paid overtime for the hours worked during weekend. These shifts are filled on a volunteer basis.

Myth: A court stenographer is in court all day everyday with no flexibility and works routinely after hours.

Fact: There is a good mix of office work and court sitting days. A court stenographer is not always in court every day each week. There are days when court might sit longer than usual, however we work as a team and one stenographer may replace another when needed.

## Requirements

• High School Diploma or GED.

• One year of post-secondary education in office administration or a related field.

• Minimum of three (3) years of related administrative and/or legal work experience.

Successful candidates will be required to undergo a criminal history clearance and security clearance check.

An equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered.

The ability to transcribe from digital audio files is required. As such, you will be required to successfully complete the Department`s court transcription test in English and/or French. (you are not tested on speed of typing).

Written and spoken competence in English and spoken competence in French is required, please state your language capability

Resumés should be in chronological order specifying education and employment in months and years including part-time and full-time employment.

## Ready to Join Us?

If you're ready to embark on a rewarding career journey, make a difference in your community, and be part of a supportive and inclusive team, then we want to hear from you!

We encourage applicants to apply on-line at www.ere.gnb.ca, by mail at the following address by mail at the following address HRcompetitions.concoursRH@gnb.ca by October 7, 2026 indicating competition number R78-2026-0862.

This competition may be used to fill future vacancies at the same level.

Position Overview: The Geographic Information System (GIS) Specialist is a member of the North Shore Mi'kmaq Tribal Council (NSMTC) Technical Services team and reports to the Geomatics Program Manager. The GIS Specialist supports the management, accuracy, and continuous improvement of NSMTC's geospatial and infrastructure asset information. The GIS Specialist is responsible for collecting, validating, maintaining, and integrating spatial and attribute data, as well as producing maps, spatial analyses, and GIS deliverables that support infrastructure planning, operations, and asset management. Working closely with the Geomatics Specialist, the GIS Specialist supports the collection of survey-precision data and high-resolution aerial imagery, contributes to data quality and GIS processes, and performs other duties as required to support organizational objectives. This position also involves working in collaboration with participating NSMTC Member Nations.

Program Location and Travel: The GIS Specialist will be based at the Natoaganeg Band Office in Natoaganeg (Eel Ground) First Nation, New Brunswick. Regular travel to participating North Shore Mi'kmaq Tribal Council (NSMTC) Member Nations is required, along with occasional travel throughout Atlantic Canada. The successful candidate must hold a valid driver's license and have access to reliable transportation.

## Key Responsibilities:

• Maintain and update GIS databases and infrastructure asset information to ensure data accuracy and integrity.

• Collect, validate, and manage spatial and attribute data from field and office sources.

• Produce maps, spatial analyses, and GIS deliverables to support infrastructure planning, operations, and asset management.

• Work closely with the Geomatics Specialist to collect, integrate, verify, and improve geospatial data.

• Support in the capture of survey-precision data and high-resolution aerial imagery.

• Other duties as required to meet organizational objectives.

## Duties and Responsibilities:

• Maintain and update GIS databases and infrastructure asset information.

• Collect, validate, and manage spatial and attribute data from field and office sources.

• Prepare maps, drawings, and GIS deliverables to support infrastructure projects and operations.

• Perform spatial analysis and provide GIS information to support planning and asset management.

• Work closely with the Geomatics Specialist to collect, integrate, verify, and improve geospatial data.

• Support the development and improvement of GIS workflows, standards, and data quality processes.

• Create, update, and standardize mapping products using Esri solutions, including ArcGIS Pro and ArcGIS Online.

• Support in the capture of survey-precision data using RTK GPS/GNSS base and rover equipment and other handheld tools for integration into geodatabases.

• Support in the capture high-resolution aerial imagery using drone and D-RTK equipment and process the data in Esri Drone2Map for accurate aerial mapping and geospatial analysis.

• Troubleshoot geospatial applications and solutions and provide training and technical support to NSMTC users.

• Build strong working relationships with NSMTC staff, leadership, NSMTC Member Nations, and government and non-government partners.

• Perform other technical and administrative duties as required.

## Qualifications and Skills:

• Diploma or degree in GIS, Geomatics, Geography, or a related field.

• Experience working with GIS data, mapping, and infrastructure assets.

• Proficiency with ESRI ArcGIS Online (AGOL) and ArcGIS Pro or similar GIS software.

• Strong understanding of spatial data, coordinate systems, and GIS databases.

• Strong attention to detail with excellent data management and quality-control skills.

• Ability to work collaboratively with the Geomatics Specialist, NSMTC technical teams, and other stakeholders.

• Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

• Demonstrated understanding of Indigenous people, traditions and socio-economic conditions is essential.

• Spoken and written English is essential; proficiency in Mi'kmaq will be considered an asset.

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centers around the Maritimes and beyond.

## Duties of Position:

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Primary Care Paramedics are based on the current National Occupational Competency Profile (NOCP) for Primary Care Paramedics,Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in paramedicine or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

Required Qualifications:

• You are entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizenship, permanent resident status or work permit)

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record

• Must have a high regard for confidentiality and patient safety

• Primary Care Paramedic program/course of over six months; If you do not have one and are interested in this career, here is a list of paramedic programs in Atlantic Canada, click here

• Must be registered, active Paramedic with the Paramedic Association of New Brunswick; If you are not currently registered in New Brunswick, please visit PANB at www.panb.ca

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 4 Driver's License (or equivalent)

Additional requirements for your application:

• Current Resume and Cover Letter

• A copy of your PCP diploma from an accredited institution

• Proof of current registration with Paramedic Association of New Brunswick

• Proof of completion of a Physical Abilities Test (PAT) specific to working as a paramedic within the last 12 months

• Proof of valid CPR level C certification issued in the last 12 months

• Photocopy of front and back of valid Class 4 driver's license (or equivalent) with minimum one year driving experience

• Driver's abstract; issued within the last 30 days

Horizon Health Network in beautiful New Brunswick is looking forPHARMACY TECHNICIANS to join our team!

If you're looking for a place where you can grow your healthcare career while building a healthy, well-rounded life, look no further.

## Why you should work here

Working for Horizon gives you flexibility in your career, an east coast lifestyle and the chance to make a big difference in the lives of New Brunswickers. At Horizon, a rewarding opportunity is as close as the ocean!

Horizon is an equal opportunity employer that values and recognizes your contributions, is dedicated to patient safety and satisfaction, has competitive pay and benefits, and offers many opportunities for professional growth. We were also recently recognized as one of Atlantic Canada's Top Employers!

## Why New Brunswick

With short commutes, the warmest ocean waters in Canada, and a rich and colourful cultural experience, New Brunswick is truly Canada's hidden gem. Situated on the Atlantic coast, the province boasts stunning landscapes ranging from pristine beaches to dense forests, providing endless opportunities for outdoor recreation such as hiking, camping, fishing, skiing and more.

New Brunswick communities offer affordable housing, a low cost of living, vibrant culture, and a rich east coast lifestyle that is never far from the city. Overall, New Brunswick provides a welcoming and inclusive environment for individuals and families looking to enjoy a balanced lifestyle amidst stunning natural surroundings, rich cultural experiences, and economic stability.

## Our Offer

Our offer comes with competitive salary, health and dental benefits, and employer paid pension contributions combined with a network of opportunities in over 100 facilities with careers in acute and community settings. There are flexible options with full-time, part-time, and casual opportunities.

Ask us about our pharmacy technician incentive program while seeing if this is the opportunity for you!

## Who we are

Horizon is Atlantic Canada's second largest health authority servicing over a half a million people. We operate 12 hospitals and more than 100 medical facilities, health care centres, clinics, and offices throughout New Brunswick. We offer services in both rural and urban areas.

Our people are the heart of our organization. We have more than 14,000 dedicated employees working with over 1,000 physicians, and play a major role in research, education, innovation and health and wellness.

## Who you are

• Registered as a Pharmacy Technician with the New Brunswick College of Pharmacist and licensed to practice in New Brunswick.

• You have written and spoken competence in English.

Does this sound like the opportunity you've been looking for? Our dedicated Talent Acquisition Specialist will work closely with you to discuss your career goals and areas of interest and specialization to find the best fit within our team. Apply below or send an email to careers@horizonnb.ca to find out more.

Horizon is committed to enhancing our diverse and inclusive environment for our employees and patients. We believe in a healthcare system that equally supports all people regardless of race, ethnicity, national origin, social background, religion, gender identity or expression, age, disability, or sexual orientation. An environment based on a commitment to diversity and inclusion supports our goal of safe and quality patient care.
