Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

## Duties of Position:

Provide pre?hospital clinical care prior to the arrival of a transporting ambulance when required. This work involves assessment, triage and managing patient care independently and collaboratively with ambulance crews when required.

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Primary Care Paramedics are based on the current National Occupational Competency Profile (NOCP) for Primary Care Paramedics, Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Paramedics are also expected to maintain and operate ambulances or clinical support unit (CSU) and related equipment in accordance with patient needs and public safety. Assesses, triages, and manages patient care until the arrival of an ambulance. Assist and collaborate with ambulance personnel with the provision of medical treatment, when necessary.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in paramedicine or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

Required Qualifications:

• You are entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizenship, permanent resident status or work permit);

• Primary Care Paramedic program/course of over six months;

• Must meet all legislated requirements for Paramedics in New Brunswick;

• Must be registered, active Paramedic with the Paramedic Association of New Brunswick; If you are not currently registered in New Brunswick, please visit PANB at www.panb.ca

• Have a minimum of two years' experience as a registered Primary Care Paramedic;

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 4 Driver's License (or equivalent)

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and possess strong interpersonal skills;

• Must be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record

• Must have excellent work habits and have a professional appearance.

• Must have a high regard for confidentiality and patient safety;

• Possess the ability to work independently;

• Displays capability of decision-making and takes initiative and;

Additional requirements for your application:

• Current Resume and Cover Letter

• A copy of your PCP diploma from an accredited institution

• Proof of current registration with Paramedic Association of New Brunswick

• Proof of completion of a Physical Abilities Test (PAT) specific to working as a paramedic within the last 12 months

• Proof of valid CPR level C certification issued in the last 12 months

• Photocopy of front and back of valid Class 4 driver's license (or equivalent) with minimum one year driving experience

• Driver's abstract; issued within the last 30 days

• Copy of any valid Driver's course certificate i.e. CEVO, VFIS or NS VSP or equivalent issued within the last three years

• Criminal Record with Vulnerable Sector Check; issued within the last 30 days

• Immunization Record (Tetanus Tdap) within the last 10 years, 2 MMR vaccines (Measles, Mumps and Rubella) or lab evidenced immunity, 2 Varicella vaccines (Chicken Pox) or lab evidenced immunity, 3 Hepatitis B doses and Lab evidenced immunity, TB Skin Test (2 step) and a 1-step in the last 12 months; if reactive a follow up chest x-ray). Please note, a meeting with our Employee Health and Wellness Consultant can be scheduled, to ensure that all vaccinations are up to date by the time an offer is made

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

Salary: As per collective agreement.

## Duties of Position:

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Emergency Medical Technicians are based on the current Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements for Emergency Medical Technician as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our emergency medical technicians provide transportation and patient care for non-urgent low acuity patients and are expected to maintain and operate ambulances and related equipment in accordance with patient needs and public safety.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in emergency medical technology or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

Required Qualifications:

• You are entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizenship, permanent resident status or work permit)

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record

• Must have a high regard for confidentiality and patient safety

• High school graduation plus an Emergency Medical Technician program/course

• Must meet all legislated requirements for Emergency Medical Technician in New Brunswick

• Must be registered, active Emergency Medical Technician with the Paramedic Association of New Brunswick; If you are not currently registered in New Brunswick, please visit PANB at www.panb.ca

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 4 Driver's Licence (or equivalent)

• Written & Spoken competency in one of the two official languages (English or French) is required and spoken competency in the other official language is preferred.

Additional requirements for your application:

• Current Resume and Cover Letter

• A copy of your EMT certificate from a recognized institution

• Proof of current registration with Paramedic Association of New Brunswick

• Proof of completion of a Physical Abilities Test (PAT) specific to working as an Emergency Medical Technician within the last 12 months

• Proof of valid CPR Level C certification issued in the last 12 months

• Photocopy of front and back of valid Class 4 driver's license (or equivalent) with minimum one year driving experience

• Driver's abstract; issued within the last 30 days

• Copy of any valid Driver's course certificate i.e. CEVO, VFIS or NS VSP or equivalent issued within the last three years

• Criminal Record with Vulnerable Sector Check; issued within the last 30 days

• Immunization Record (Tetanus Tdap) within the last 10 years, 2 MMR vaccines (Measles, Mumps and Rubella) or lab evidenced immunity, 2 Varicella vaccines (Chicken Pox) or lab evidenced immunity, 3 Hepatitis B doses and Lab evidenced immunity, TB Skin Test (2 step) and a 1-step in the last 12 months; if reactive a follow up chest x-ray). Please note, a meeting with our Employee Health and Wellness Consultant can be scheduled, to ensure that all vaccinations are up to date by the time an offer is made

• Valid Official Language Assessments (oral assessment only) in both French and English from the Department of Post-secondary Education, Training and Labour. You can contact them at LS-SL@gnb.ca. Please take into account the additional time to receive your language assessment

• Additional training and/or education is highly valued.

For any questions for our HR team, please contact us at jobs-emplois@ambulancenb.ca

If you are looking for a career that will change lives and have a direct impact on the health of our community submit your application.

2188723.description:
True North Salmon, a division of Cooke Aquaculture Inc., is a dynamic and growing east coast family company, with Platinum Member status in the Canada's Best Managed Companies program. We have an opportunity for a highly motivated individual to join our team as a Quality Assurance Lead Hand (Monitor), reporting to the QA Supervisor at our St. George, NB facility.

Cooke is a global seafood company with operations in North America, Europe, and South America. Our company's success is driven by our dynamic, highly skilled and innovative management team, supported by dedicated employees who live in coastal communities and contribute to the local area's economy and sense of community.

## The Role

The Quality Assurance Lead Hand (Monitor) is responsible for daily quality and food safety verification activities on the production floor. This position supports the QA Supervisor by conducting inspections, completing monitoring tasks, verifying compliance with procedures, identifying deficiencies, and communicating corrective actions. The QA Lead Hand acts as the first level of leadership and technical support for QA Technicians

Key Responsibilities:

Quality and Food Safety Monitoring

• Conduct a QA assessment once per week throughout processing operations.

• Complete environmental swabbing programs as scheduled and submit the environmental swab plan to the lab the week prior to swabbing.

• Perform raw material temperature verification activities.

• Complete Acceptable Quality Limit (AQL) inspections, one lot per day.

• Monitor compliance with food safety, GMP, HACCP, BRCGS, BAP, and customer requirements.

• Follow up on customer complaints and communicate inspection updates to the INspec Manager when required.

• Complete additional tasks requested by the QAM, RQAM, DQA

Root Cause Analysis (RCA)

• Participate in Root Cause Analysis investigations for quality, food safety, customer complaint, GMP, environmental monitoring, and documentation-related non-conformances.

• Complete initial fact gathering and evidence collection, including interviews, observations, records review, photographs, and trend analysis.

• Prepare and submit initial RCA documentation using the company's approved Root Cause Analysis template for QA Manager review and follow-up.

• Support the identification of immediate, contributing, and systemic causes using recognized problem-solving tools such as 5 Why Analysis, Cause-and-Effect (Fishbone) Diagrams, and trend reviews.

• Recommend corrective and preventive actions to eliminate recurrence of identified issues.

• Monitor assigned corrective actions and provide verification evidence to the QA Supervisor.

• Escalate repeat, high-risk, regulatory, customer-impacting, or food safety-related findings to the QA Supervisor and QA Manager.

One Point Lesson Development and Training

• Develop and deliver weekly One-Point Lessons (OPLs) for QA Technicians and Production employees based on audit findings, customer complaints, root cause investigations, GMP observations, environmental monitoring results, and quality trends.

• Create simple visual training materials focused on a single critical topic to improve understanding and retention.

• Conduct short coaching sessions to reinforce quality and food safety expectations, inspection methods, documentation requirements, and GMP compliance.

• Maintain records of training topics, attendee participation, and effectiveness verification activities.

• Identify recurring knowledge gaps requiring additional training and communicate recommendations to the QA Supervisor.

• Verify employee understanding through observation, questioning, and follow-up assessments.

Inspections and Verification Activities

• Complete assigned Lead Hand INspec approvals each day.

• Identify non-conformances and initiate corrective actions.

• Conduct monthly inspections, including Pest Control Program and Glass and Brittle Plastic Program inspections.

• Conduct quarterly facility/building inspections (Please use CFIA building inspection S1/S2, while zoning in on one department monthly - in addition to the quarterly inspections).

Maintenance and Continuous Improvement

• Complete bi-weekly facility infrastructure walkthroughs.

• Review maintenance work orders and identify quality-related concerns.

• Develop and submit monthly Priority #1 maintenance and infrastructure concerns to the QA Manager.

• Escalate food safety and quality risks requiring management attention.

Documentation and Administration

• Complete QA staff time sheet verification daily.

• Complete Lead Hand break checklist verification activities a minimum of twice per day.

• Maintain all records accurately and completely.

• Submit corrective action reports to QA Management as required.

Training and Procedural Compliance:

• Review one SOP and one Work Instruction per week.

• Develop and complete knowledge assessment questions based on reviewed procedures.

• Verify QA Technician understanding through verbal questioning.

• Conduct short training sessions on proper methods, forms, and sign-off requirements, and submit hard copies to the QA Manager.

• Report training results and procedural gaps to the QA Supervisor.

Back Up QA Technician

• Complete QA technician tasks when short staffed, or during staff vacations

• Conduct LH duties where practical & provide notice to QA Supervisor/ Manager of tasks that are unable to be completed due to QA Back up duties.

Skills, Qualifications & Attributes:

• Seafood processing or food manufacturing experience.

• Knowledge of HACCP, GMPs, BRCGS, SFCR, and food safety programs.

• Strong organizational and communication skills.

• Ability to perform inspections and make objective quality decisions.

• Intermediate computer and documentation skills.

• Strong attention to detail.

• Commitment to following and promoting all QA and Health & Safety regulations.

• Exceptional verbal and written communication skills.

• Proven ability to lead and work effectively in a team environment.

• Ability to perform well under pressure in a high-demand, deadline-driven setting.

• Professional, respectful, and supportive demeanor toward colleagues.

• Ability to remain calm and level-headed in all situations.

• Willingness to perform micro testing as required.

• Alignment with and respect for the Company's mission and values.

## Working Conditions:

• Work is performed in a seafood processing plant and QA support environment.

• Ability to work a Continental Night Shift schedule, with shifts beginning at 5:00 PM, including weekends, holidays, and overtime as operationally required.

• Regular presence on the production floor, processing lines, inspection areas, and refrigerated or wet environments is required.

• Exposure may include loud noise, slippery surfaces, water, cleaning chemicals, cold temperatures, and fish processing by-products.

• Standing, walking, inspecting product and equipment areas, and completing documentation are routine parts of the role.

• Use of appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) is mandatory.

*Cooke offers full time year round employment and competitive rates.

## Benefits Package:

• Health Benefits: Includes coverage for dental, vision, and extended medical care.

• Insurance: Life and disability insurance provided for financial security.

• SupportServices:Access to an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

• Financial Planning: Opportunity for RRSP matching to support your retirement savings.

• Wellness: Wellness programs.

• Career Development: Professional growth opportunities and avenues for advancement.

• Perks: Employee discounts on company products or services.

* As per company policy, a clear result from a pre-employment criminal background check is required.

## The Opportunity

The role description is just one part of the story. This is an opportunity to grow, to stretch, to work within the parameters of the role but stretch to your fullest potential. We are a team that counts performance, we reward contribution, and we recognize talent. It is about being at the center of the fastest growing company in New Brunswick and knowing you are part of that growth. The ability to bring your passion for learning, desire for growth, and energy for moving your career forward is what we offer.

## The Why

Why Cooke? Simple - we are a company that rewards initiative, resour cefulness, and work ethic. We will champion your growth and provide you with the platform to create your path, your career, and your future.

2234449.description:
Cooke is a global seafood company with operations in North America, Europe, South America and Australia. Our company's success is driven by our dynamic, highly skilled, and innovative management team, supported by dedicated employees who live in coastal communities and contribute to the local area's economy and sense of community.

Cooke is continuing to mature its digital strategy through stronger demand capture, sharper business case discipline, and clearer accountability between business outcomes and technology delivery. As the Manager, Finance Technology, you lead the technology agenda for our Finance and Accounting functions turning finance priorities into a focused capability roadmap and delivery plan, and ensuring digital initiatives deliver measurable value across the core finance and accounting processes that keep the business running, anchored by record-to-report.

## The Role

As Manager, Finance Technology, you own both the near-term (typically 12-month) technology roadmap for Finance and Accounting and the delivery of that roadmap operating within Cooke's enterprise IT governance, architecture, and delivery frameworks. Finance and Accounting spans general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, treasury, tax, and financial planning & analysis. You translate finance priorities into sequenced, executable initiatives, define scope and success criteria, and lead the team that delivers capability-specific technology work. Delivery is coordinated through the Project Manager and within approved plans; you resolve domain-specific delivery issues, and you escalate risks, cross-capability trade-offs, and decisions beyond your authority through governance.

You partner closely with the Finance leadership team as your primary business stakeholders, the Digital Strategy Analyst, Solution Architect, Project Manager and Business Systems Analyst aligned to your capability areas. Enterprise Architecture governs technical standards and patterns and the PMO governs delivery. You report to the Director, Business Technology.

## Key Responsibilities:

## Team Leadership & Delivery Management

• Lead and develop the delivery team assigned to Finance Technology (e.g., Business Systems Analysts and Project Managers), with potential to scale as the portfolio grows

• Conduct regular 1:1s, set objectives, manage performance, and own development planning for your team

• Prioritize work, manage day-to-day execution decisions, and ensure quality, compliance, and timely delivery against defined standards and commitments

• Coordinate domain-specific resources and resolve delivery issues through the Project Manager, within approved plans

• Coach team members, build a learning culture, and mentor future team leads

## Finance & Accounting Capability Roadmap

• Own and maintain a 12-month technology roadmap for Finance and Accounting, aligned to enterprise sequencing set by the Director, Business Technology

• Translate finance and accounting priorities into sequenced, executable initiatives with measurable outcomes

• Define scope, constraints, and success criteria for initiatives within the capability

• Drive continuous improvement and capability maturity across finance and accounting processes - record-to-report (R2R), plus the finance side of procure-to-pay (accounts payable) and order-to-cash (billing, accounts receivable, and collections) that Finance shares with Procurement and Sales & Marketing

## Business Stakeholder Engagement

• Act as the primary technology partner for Finance and Accounting leaders, building trust and surfacing needs, pain points, and emerging demand into the intake process

• Represent the finance domain in intake triage, prioritization, and governance discussions

• Ensure requirements are clearly linked to business outcomes and that stakeholders are aligned on the baseline

## Initiative Quality & Business Case Discipline

• Ensure each initiative has a clear problem statement, a validated business case, a measurable objective, and a named business sponsor

• Support ROI validation and confirm scope, success criteria, and product fit before initiatives are submitted for prioritization or contract

• Provide inputs to budgeting and forecasting for the finance technology portfolio

## Delivery Readiness, Handoff & Benefits

• Confirm initiatives entering delivery have validated requirements, funded scope, and clear ownership, and provide a clean transition to implementation and then support

• Stay engaged through delivery to validate readiness, sign off on business outcomes, and support benefits realization

## Governance, Escalation & Decision-Making

• Participate in intake, architecture, and stage-gate reviews for initiatives impacting Finance and Accounting

• Provide clear recommendations and decisions within your authority and within agreed governance timelines

• Escalate cross-capability trade-offs and decisions beyond your authority through PMO or enterprise governance

• Remain accountable for delivery outcomes once initiatives are approved

## What Success Looks Like

• Finance and Accounting leaders have a clear, current, and trusted technology roadmap

• Initiatives entering delivery are well-framed, well-scoped, and ready for execution

• Core finance and accounting processes (record-to-report, and the finance side of procure-to-pay and order-to-cash) are measurably more efficient and better supported by technology over time

• The team is high-performing, well-developed, and operating to CookeIT standards

• The domain delivers measurable business outcomes, not just shipped projects

## Core Skills & Capabilities

• People leadership and coaching - able to lead, develop, and get results through a team

• Governance and quality assurance across delivery processes, frameworks, and standards

• Strong organizational, prioritization, and delivery management skills

• Stakeholder management and communication with finance and IT audiences

• Ability to translate strategy into team execution and connect initiatives to business outcomes

• Business case structuring, ROI validation, and outcome-based framing

• Understanding of IT financial management concepts (e.g., TBM taxonomy, cost categorization) is an asset

## Finance & Accounting Technology (Assets)

• Familiarity with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations (D365 F&O) or Business Central would be an asset

• Familiarity with industry-standard finance processes - record-to-report (R2R), and the finance components of procure-to-pay and order-to-cash - would be an asset

• Understanding of core accounting and finance functions: general ledger, AP/AR, month-end and period-end close, consolidations, treasury, tax, and FP&A

• Awareness of finance data, reporting, and analytics needs (e.g., Power BI) and how they connect to ERP and master data

• Awareness of finance controls, audit, and compliance considerations

## Behaviors That Drive Success

• Adaptability - Anticipates change, guides the team through transitions, and adjusts plans to maintain momentum

• Collaboration & Synergy - Leads collaboration across functions; resolves conflicts constructively

• Outcome Driven - Sets stretch goals and ensures team alignment to business outcomes

• Growth Mindset - Builds a learning culture within the team and mentors others

• Business Acumen - Applies business insight to improve processes and make informed decisions

• Decisiveness - Makes timely, data-informed decisions within scope

• Digital Acumen - Applies digital insight to improve work quality and the finance user experience

• Political Savviness - Builds credibility and influence across departments

## Experience & Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Business, IT, Finance, or a related discipline (or equivalent experience)

• 5-8 years in IT or business roles, including 2-3 years in a supervisory or team lead capacity

• Demonstrated experience delivering technology for finance, accounting, or a comparable corporate function

• Experience leading BSAs and/or PMs and operating within a structured delivery and governance model

• Familiarity with capability-based planning, business case discipline, and vendor scope shaping

• Experience with project/portfolio management and reporting tools (e.g., Monday.com, MS Project) and governance frameworks

• Familiarity with D365 F&O or Business Central, and with finance processes such as record-to-report, an asset

• Comfortable engaging finance leadership and translating their priorities into technology outcomes

Join our team and enjoy the benefits of full-time year-round employment with competitive rates and a comprehensive benefits package tailored to support your well-being and career growth.

## Benefits Package:

• Health Benefits: Includes coverage for dental, vision, and extended medical care.

• Insurance: Life and disability insurance provided for financial security.

## This is the life-changing opportunity you've been looking for.

## Horizon Health Network in beautiful New Brunswick is looking for a

## Pediatric Endocrinologist to join our team!

Horizon Health Network, Saint John area (Region 2), is actively seeking a full-time Pediatric Endocrinologist, either locum or permanent, to join our collaborative team in Saint John, New Brunswick. The Saint John Regional Hospital is New Brunswick's largest tertiary care hospital, and the Department of Pediatrics has an active inpatient and outpatient unit along with a Level-3 NICU. The successful candidate will join a team of eight general pediatricians, six sub-specialty pediatricians (in the areas of Neurology and Neonatology), two diabetes nurses, one endocrinology nurse, and a pediatric dietitian. As a full-time pediatric endocrinologist, you will provide general pediatric endocrine clinics as well as a multi-disciplinary type-1 diabetes clinic. This position also includes general pediatric ward and call coverage. There is opportunity for teaching and research through Memorial University and Dalhousie University academic affiliations.

## Why you should work here

Horizon Health Network (Horizon) is proud of its dedicated team of health care professionals who are focused on delivering safe and quality care to our patients, clients, families, and communities. Horizon is a great place to work, as people are the heart of our organization, and the success of Horizon is a direct result of our employees' dedication, professionalism, and commitment.

Horizon is the largest regional health authority – and one of the largest employers – in New Brunswick, and the second-largest health authority in Atlantic Canada. Our leadership and health care providers are experts in diverse areas of health and community services and provide services to a half a million people.

Horizon has an annual budget of approximately $1.2 billion and has more than 13,000 employees, 1,100 physicians and 1,300 volunteers, as well as 17 foundations, 12 auxiliaries and 8 alumnae organizations.

## What you will do

Reporting to the Pediatric Department Head and the Medical Director for the area, the Pediatric Endocrinologist collaborates with other Physicians, Nurse Practitioners, Registered, Nurses, and other Allied Medical Staff.

• Provide ambulatory care in a clinic setting.

• Provide inpatient care as required and requested by the Clinical Department Head.

• Practice in a collaborative fashion as a member of an interdisciplinary team and consult with members of other health professions as appropriate.

• Participates in departmental medical education initiatives.

• Provide on-call services during statutory holidays, evenings, and weekends as part of the on-call schedule for the Department.

• Participate in medical practice that is compatible with the Health Authority's mission, values, and strategic directions.

• These responsibilities are basic. Additional duties may be assigned from time to time as may be necessary to the operation of Horizon Health Network.

## Hours of Work

• Hours of work are normally provided between 0800hrs – 1600hrs Monday to Friday, unless otherwise agreed upon by the Service/Department Head.

• After-hours and weekend call coverage in coordination with members of the Department.

## Remuneration

• Salaried.

• This is a Salaried position. Remuneration is based on the New Brunswick Medical Pay Plan. The current rates range between $241,748 to a maximum of $293,904 annually (locums receive 10% of the base salary in lieu of benefits) based on qualifications and experience.

• On call remuneration is Fee-For-Service which is a direct compensation between the physician and Medicare New Brunswick.

## Qualifications

• Must have a Medical Degree from a recognized medical school and postgraduate studies (residency) in the field of Pediatric Medicine.

• Certification by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada.

• Candidates must be eligible for licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of New Brunswick.

• Proficiency in English is required. Bilingual skills would be considered an asset.

• In accordance with immigration requirements, preference will be given to Canadian citizens and Permanent Residents of Canada.

• Excellent communication, interpersonal and team-building skills.

• Good attendance and work record.

• Physically able to perform assigned duties.

## Expected Start Date

• As soon as possible.

## Incentives

• Candidates may be eligible for a Provincial Recruitment Incentive with a Return of Service Agreement. (Locums not eligible.)

• Relocation reimbursement of up to $8,000.

## About the Facility

Horizon's Saint John Regional Hospital is the largest tertiary care hospital in New Brunswick and is the primary health care referral centre for this area and to all New Brunswickers for major trauma and cardiac care.

The New Brunswick Trauma Program, New Brunswick Heart Centre, and the New Brunswick Stem Cell Transplant Centre are located within the hospital, as are Radiation Oncology and Nephrology services. This site offers autologous stem cell therapy and a stem cell processing laboratory.

The Saint John Regional Hospital also serves as the centre for Dalhousie Medicine New Brunswick's distributed medical education program. The hospital services a catchment population of 170,000 people.

## About the Community

Imagine…

A playground in Atlantic Canada surrounded by fresh waterways on one side and the ocean on the other.

Connect…

With a community of Maritime and Acadian people whose rich friendly culture will include you.

Belong…

To a community where families are able to raise their children in a safe, close-knit environment with a reasonable cost of living.

The Saint John area offers you a broad range of affordable housing options, from heritage properties to executive homes within the city and in nearby Kennebecasis Valley. Saint John, a booming harbor city is Canada's oldest incorporated city (1785) and home to the country's oldest museum and farmers' market. For spouses and families, there are excellent employment and educational prospects. The nearby towns and villages, such as St. Stephen, Sussex, and Grand Manan, provide a diverse selection of recreational and sport activities that appeal to all age groups

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

## Duties of Position:

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Advanced Care Paramedics are based on the current National Occupational Competency Profile (NOCP) for Advanced Care Paramedics,Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in paramedicine or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Advanced Care Paramedic positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

Required Qualifications:

• You are entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizenship, permanent resident status or work permit)

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record

• Must have a high regard for confidentiality and patient safety

• Advanced Care Paramedic program/course of over six months; If you do not have one and are interested in this career, here is a list of paramedic programs in Atlantic Canada, click here

• Must be registered, active Advanced Care Paramedic with the Paramedic Association of New Brunswick; If you are not currently registered in New Brunswick, please visit PANB at www.panb.ca

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 4 Driver's Licence (or equivalent)

• Must be willing to participate and contribute to future pilot projects, related research initiatives and focus groups

• Must be willing to participate in community Paramedicine duties

Additional requirements for your application:

• Current Resume and Cover Letter

• A copy of your ACP diploma from an accredited institution

• Proof of current registration with Paramedic Association of New Brunswick

• Proof of completion of a Physical Abilities Test (PAT) specific to working as a paramedic within the last 12 months

• Proof of valid CPR level C certification issued in the last 12 months

• Photocopy of front and back of valid Class 4 driver's license (or equivalent) with minimum one year driving experience

• Driver's abstract; issued within the last 30 days

• Copy of any valid Driver's course certificate i.e. CEVO, VFIS or NS VSP or equivalent issued within the last three years

• Criminal Record with Vulnerable Sector Check; issued within the last 30 days

• Immunization Record (Tetanus Tdap) within the last 10 years, 2 MMR vaccines (Measles, Mumps and Rubella) or lab evidenced immunity, 2 Varicella vaccines (Chicken Pox) or lab evidenced immunity, 3 Hepatitis B doses and Lab evidenced immunity, TB Skin Test (2 step) and a 1-step in the last 12 months; if reactive a follow up chest x-ray). Please note, a meeting with our Employee Health and Wellness Consultant can be scheduled, to ensure that all vaccinations are up to date by the time an offer is made

• Valid Official Language Assessments (oral assessment only) in both French and English from the Department of Post-secondary Education, Training and Labour. You can contact them at LS-SL@gnb.ca. Please take into account the additional time to receive your language assessment

• Additional training and/or education is highly valued.

For any questions for our HR team, please contact us at jobs-emplois@ambulancenb.ca

If you are looking for a career that will change lives and have a direct impact on the health of our community, submit your application.

Ambulance NB is committed to the principle of equal opportunity in its employment practices and to providing an environment free from discrimination and harassment for all employees.

We would like to thank all candidates for expressing interest. Please note only those selected for interviews will be contacted.

2240703.description:
## This is the life-changing opportunity you've been looking for.

Horizon Health Network in beautiful New Brunswick is looking for a Materials Coordinator for the Cardiac Care program to join our team!

Horizon Health Network (Horizon) is seeking a skilled, dedicated and detail-oriented individual to join our team as a Materials Coordinator. The ideal candidate will have experience with the hospital Meditech system, purchasing processes and material management.

## Why you should work here

Working for Horizon gives you a career that provides an east coast lifestyle and the chance to make a big difference in the lives of New Brunswickers.

This position comes with competitive salary, paid time off, sick benefits, employer paid contributions into our government pension plan and a remote work policy.

Horizon is committed to enhancing our diverse and inclusive environment for our employees and patients. We believe in a healthcare system that equally supports all people regardless of race, ethnicity, national origin, social background, religion, gender identity or expression, age, disability, or sexual orientation. An environment based on a commitment to diversity and inclusion supports our goal of safe and quality patient care.

## Who you are

You have a worked in the healthcare setting for a minimum of 5 years.

Written and spoken competence in English is required at an advanced level.

## What you will do

## PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The primary purpose of the Coordinator is to develop and maintain/manage a cost effective cardiology inventory management system and to collaborate with the cardiac Program Managers, members of Materials Management/Purchasing Department, Physicians (cardiac surgeons, interventional cardiologists, electrophysiologists, cardiologists and cardiac anesthesiologists), Perfusion Medicine, Respiratory Therapy, Electrodiagnostics, Clinical Engineering and Maintenance Departments in the acquisition of appropriate major and small equipment and supplies. To be a support and resource for the Cardiac Program Managers at all sites in Horizon.

## RESPONSIBILITIES

• Resolve supply and equipment problems related to clinical use and quality to ensure the appropriate products are available when needed to provide safe patient care.

• Coordinate and direct the duties of the laboratory materials personnel.

• Determine educational needs of members of the cardiac multidisciplinary team with respect to supplies and equipment and develop strategies to ensure appropriate education is delivered.

• Provide education for cardiac program representatives on relevant materials management philosophies and processes.

• Identify for the Managers and clinicians all new equipment, instrumentation and supplies requiring staff education

• Where applicable, standardize Cardiac Program supplies and equipment and manage inventory.

• Review all products in use and work towards ensuring that only one product is used for the same purpose in all sites.

• Emphasize maintaining and enhancing existing standards of patient care while conserving resources and improving value for expenditures.

• Coordinate the standardization of products and the evaluation of new equipment, instrumentation and supplies that may be considered for future purchase and to report the results to the necessary stakeholders.

• Collaborate with ad hoc and advisory teams to develop and coordinate clinical evaluations.

• Knowledgeable about the most cost effective and efficient instrumentation, supplies and equipment available and provide this information as appropriate to Managers and necessary stakeholders.

• Meet with sales representatives to view/discuss new equipment, instrumentation and supplies.

• Prepare a cost benefit analysis for the decision makers for new equipment and supplies when stakeholders request a change in practice or procedure.

• Coordinate the purchase process of major equipment and supplies (including High Tech and Capital equipment requests) with the Program, Purchasing Department, Managers, physicians and other stakeholders such as Clinical Engineering, Respiratory, Electrodiagnostics, and Anesthesiology.

• Play an active role in the budget process (planning and analysis), providing critical information on projected cost for materials/contracts in the next fiscal year.

• Provide Managers and cardiac program representatives with the recommended standards for equipment, instrumentation and supplies.

• Act as a resource for projects involving equipment, supplies and inventory.

• Act as a resource in the development of policies and procedures as they pertain to equipment, instrumentation and supplies.

• Act as a resource on risk management issues involving equipment and/or supplies.

• Maintain knowledge of clinical procedures and techniques as they relate to supply and equipment requirements.

• Maintain current knowledge of products and equipment in the marketplace by reviewing appropriate literature, attending exhibitions related to supplies and equipment and communicating with vendors.

• Maintain current knowledge of group purchasing contracts (MedBuy) and develop strategies to ensure optimal compliance.

• Establish cardiac product inventory control by setting appropriate levels of supplies to minimize inventory holding costs and waste due to obsolescence. Develop processes to ensure appropriate inventory stocking and delivery.

• Participate in appropriate Committees or as requested

## QUALIFICATIONS

• Degree in a health-related discipline or equivalent combination of training and experience.

• Minimum five (5) years recent experience in a healthcare setting.

• Demonstrated knowledge of tertiary cardiology and general cardiology instruments, supplies and equipment.

• Formal training and/or experience in evaluation techniques are preferred.

• Knowledge of various related provincial guidelines, government acts and regulations, standard public purchasing guidelines and fair business practice preferred.

• Ability to communicate effectively including the ability to write reports, make presentations and speak to groups.

• Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving ability.

• Ability to identify, plan and compete work assignments within established time constraints.

• Ability to work as a team member and demonstrate good interpersonal skills.

• Self direction and ability to adapt to the diverse aspects of the position.

• Ability to travel as required.

• Good work and attendance record.

• Physically able to perform assigned duties.

• Advanced computer skills: Meditech, MS Office, ORSOS, MS Excel; (MS Access and MS Project – an asset).

## SPECIFIC PERFORMANCE OUTCOMES

• Uses Meditech computer software.

• Cost benefit analysis is prepared for all new initiatives and submitted as appropriate.

• Purchase requisitions for capital and high-tech equipment are submitted to purchasing by submission deadline following authorization from the Cardiac Clinical program Director.

• New equipment evaluations are conducted in collaboration with multidisciplinary team.

• Instructions and product use information are given to necessary stakeholders.

• Records are maintained for all cost benefit analysis completed and submitted to the Cardiac program Clinical Director.

• Provides documentation and information to involved stakeholders, including Quality/Risk Management on equipment or supply issues and ECRI alerts and ensures appropriate responses are taken.

• Ensures record of all repairs and tracks instrumentation/equipment history for all sites.

• Develops Business Case Plan for projects as identified by Cardiac Clinical Director.

## Horizon Competency

Core competencies for non-bargaining positions are based on the LEADS in a Caring Environment leadership capabilities framework: Lead Self, Engage Others, Achieve Results, Develop Coalitions, and System Transformation.

In addition to LEADS, all positions need to demonstrate compassion, patience, and professionalism in all interactions, consistently upholding a respectful and supportive environment for patients, clients, families, and colleagues. Proactively addresses concerns and responds to emerging needs with empathy and diligence, contributing to high-quality, patient/client centered care.

## Interested? Apply Today!

To learn more, visit MyHorizonCareer.ca/management-business-professionals/

Horizon Health Network (Horizon) only accepts on-line applications.

## About Horizon's Recruitment Process

We thank all applicant who apply; however, only those selected for further consideration will be contacted. All interested applicants are encouraged to apply as an equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered.

Horizon's recruitment screening process may include language proficiency testing, clerical testing and/or behavioral assessment. Responsibilities include but are not limited to provision of diabetes education, care and services, teaching diabetes education classes, presentations to community and professional groups and mentoring students assigned to the clinic. This position strives to improve health outcomes with best practice by enhancing clinical management, patient knowledge and self-management skills.

## ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS

• A Bachelor of Science degree in nutrition or dietetics and successful completion of an accredited internship program.

• Must be registered and a member in good standing with the New Brunswick Association of Dietitians.

• Certified Diabetes Educator (CDE)

• Ability to attend work on a regular basis.

• Full clinical assessment establishing a baseline for intervention as well as ongoing monitoring and evaluation for clients with any form of diabetes.

• Establishing effective care plans (in collaboration with primary health care provider(s) as indicated), provision of intensive counselling, education and advocacy as well as make recommendations for appropriate treatments, referrals or changes to therapy.

• Effectively demonstrating strong clinical skills in chronic disease management through daily assessment, interventions and through excellent interpersonal communication.

• Liaise with internal and external agencies to support sourcing and funding for diabetes management products.

• Collaborating and maintaining productive relationships with managers, physicians, clinic staff, patients, and families.

• Access or develop resources to support diabetes self-management.

• Supporting the patient / family in the self-management of diabetes.

• Supporting clinicians external to the diabetes clinic on best practices for diabetes management.

• Maintaining clinical records and documentation

• Preparing and presenting information and education sessions

• Providing mentoring and support for a variety of post-secondary students / interns.

• Participating in program development, including developing, maintaining and evaluating policies and procedures.

The work we do has a positive impact on our communities and helps improve the everyday lives of New Brunswickers. Together, we are over 45,000 New Brunswickers who are passionate problem-solvers, who make a difference and are proud to call New Brunswick home.

Not only is the department responsible for managing over 18,000 kilometers of provincial highways, it also manages the planning, design and construction of hospitals, schools and other government buildings.

2240384.description:
## JOB PURPOSE

The nurse practitioner (NP) is a self-directed, advanced practice-prepared nurse who functions within a collaborative practice model. The NP demonstrates a comprehensive knowledge base in an Emergency Department/Urgent Care Setting, exhibiting a high degree of clinical competence in caring for select patient groups with acute and specialized health needs. The NP scope of practice incorporates skills and knowledge from the disciplines of nursing and medicine. Working in collaboration with a physician or group of physicians, the NP manages, directs and provides comprehensive care for Emergency Patient population in an interdisciplinary team environment.

## QUALIFICATIONS

• Baccalaureate and/or Masters degree as Nurse Practitioner

• Currently registered in the province of New Brunswick as a nurse practitioner, in good standing with the College of Nursing of New Brunswick (CNNB)

• Advanced clinical knowledge in primary health care in an Emergency Department Setting.

• Recent ED experience is an asset

• Working Knowledge of CTAS Guidelines

• BLS

• Skills such as suturing, I&D, Pelvic examinations would be considered an asset

• Demonstrates team philosophy and values an interdisciplinary environment.

• Demonstrates clear ability to produce quality health documentation

• Demonstrates ability to deliver top performance in a dynamic, fast-paced work environment.

• Ability to attend work on a regular basis.

• Ability to perform the duties of the position.

• Good work record.

## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• NP provides advanced assessment and critical decision-making incorporating medical directives, the nursing process, standards of practice and the nursing code of ethical behavior.

• Performs a comprehensive health or symptom directed assessment and synthesizes data from multiple sources to make a diagnosis of a disease or disorder for patients within the Canadian Triage and Acuity Scale (CTAS) and NP Scope of Practice.

• Provides advanced clinical expertise to members of the interdisciplinary team.

• Incorporates an interdisciplinary approach to the assessment and treatment of patients, including patients returning for follow-up testing or treatment.

• Prescribes appropriate consultations and therapies consistent with the NP scope of practice.

• Acts as a clinical resource for team members, providing a specialized approach to patient care problems.

• Facilitates coordination and continuity of care

• Competently identifies, prioritizes, and orders necessary diagnostic tests and procedures as per current NANB nurse practitioner schedules for ordering.

• Reviews laboratory reports as part of the Medical Team from patients previously registered and follow-up care if further interventions are required.

• Prescribes pharmacological and other therapeutic interventions as per current NANB nurse practitioner schedules for ordering.

• Accurately documents all pertinent patient data on patient health record, referral forms, in health information system, or as per other policies and processes of patient care decree.

• Evaluates health outcomes in collaboration with team.

• Directs referrals to appropriate professionals or services.

• Maintains knowledge for, and competently performs invasive or non-invasive procedures related to clinical practice.

• Acts as a resource team member in the development of policy, procedure and /or programs related to specific patient populations. Participates in the development, monitoring, and evaluation of evidence-based protocols /guidelines/standards of care for specific patient populations, in collaboration with team members.

• Facilitates the engagement of families in the process of informed decision-making about health care and lifestyle choices.

• Acts as a preceptor to developing nurse practitioners.

• Role models continuous learning

## COMPETENCIES

• Effective and professional communication

• teamwork and collaboration

• Professional responsibility and accountability

• Leadership skills

• Patient/Client focused

• Demonstrates initiative, good judgement and ability to set priorities

• Nurse Practitioner Competencies as outlined on NANB

## CLOSING DATE

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

## Duties of Position:

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Primary Care Paramedics are based on the current National Occupational Competency Profile (NOCP) for Primary Care Paramedics,Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in paramedicine or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

Required Qualifications:

• You are entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizenship, permanent resident status or work permit)

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record

• Must have a high regard for confidentiality and patient safety

• Primary Care Paramedic program/course of over six months; If you do not have one and are interested in this career, here is a list of paramedic programs in Atlantic Canada, click here

• Must be registered, active Paramedic with the Paramedic Association of New Brunswick; If you are not currently registered in New Brunswick, please visit PANB at www.panb.ca

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 4 Driver's Licence (or equivalent)

Additional requirements for your application:

• Current Resume and Cover Letter

• A copy of your PCP diploma from an accredited institution

• Proof of current registration with Paramedic Association of New Brunswick

• Proof of completion of a Physical Abilities Test (PAT) specific to working as a paramedic within the last 12 months

• Proof of valid CPR level C certification issued in the last 12 months

• Photocopy of front and back of valid Class 4 driver's license (or equivalent) with minimum one year driving experience

• Driver's abstract; issued within the last 30 days

• Copy of any valid Driver's course certificate i.e. CEVO, VFIS or NS VSP or equivalent issued within the last three years

• Criminal Record with Vulnerable Sector Check; issued within the last 30 days

• Immunization Record (Tetanus Tdap) within the last 10 years, 2 MMR vaccines (Measles, Mumps and Rubella) or lab evidenced immunity, 2 Varicella vaccines (Chicken Pox) or lab evidenced immunity, 3 Hepatitis B doses and Lab evidenced immunity, TB Skin Test (2 step) and a 1-step in the last 12 months; if reactive a follow up chest x-ray). Please note, a meeting with our Employee Health and Wellness Consultant can be scheduled, to ensure that all vaccinations are up to date by the time an offer is made

• Valid Official Language Assessments (oral assessment only) in both French and English from the Department of Post-secondary Education, Training and Labour. You can contact them at LS-SL@gnb.ca. Please take into account the additional time to receive your language assessment

• Additional training and/or education is highly valued.

For any questions for our HR team, please contact us at jobs-emplois@ambulancenb.ca

If you are looking for a career that will change lives and have a direct impact on the health of our community, submit your application.

Ambulance NB is committed to the principle of equal opportunity in its employment practices and to providing an environment free from discrimination and harassment for all employees.

We would like to thank all candidates for expressing interest. Please note only those selected for interviews will be contacted.

2204618.title: Project Manager, Contaminated Sites Specialist
2204618.description:
## Your mission

You will play an important role in a dynamic and passionate team, collaborating on a variety of projects of all sizes and scopes in the environment, renewable energies, hydroelectricity, transportation, materials, buildings and climate change markets. Boldness, innovation and collaboration are an integral part of our daily operations .

## Englobe - Who we are

At Englobe, our rigor is matched by sincere care for our colleagues, our customers, our communities , and the environment. We are committed to making a real difference, one project at a time, and to having a positive, lasting impact. We approach our work with fresh perspectives, relying on collaboration and a diversity of voices. With an entrepreneurial spirit, we empower our customers and communities with boldness and optimism. We are determined to leave a lasting legacy for generations to come.

Does this sound like the right fit for you? Learn more about the role !

## Your main responsibilities

• Apply and promote Englobe's health and safety policies.

• Lead project teams in the planning and delivery of a range of contaminated sites projects.

• Provide consulting services in the capacity of a Senior Engineer / Professional in conjunction with phased environmental site assessments and remediation and risk management programs.

• Remain current with the requirements of local, provincial and federal agencies for the assessment and management of contaminated sites.

• Apply in-depth knowledge of engineering principles to the completion of complex and difficult projects under your responsibility.

• Mentor, direct, and collaborate with other environmental professionals and technicians.

• Work with other project managers to ensure that projects are set up and executed in full compliance with quality standards and regulations.

• Develop high-quality deliverables and proposals.

• Build and support client relationships while working in conjunction with the senior leadership team.

• Consult on matters of design, processes, and engineering techniques related to growth opportunities, business development and planning.

• Provide effective technical leadership, direction, and support for members of the team.

• Serve as a senior consultant for environmental projects, designs and deliverables.

## What makes you unique

• University degree in Environmental Engineering and/or Applied Science, or related discipline.

• Minimum of 10 years of experience in the field of environmental consulting.

• Member of Professional Engineer and/or Geoscientists association(s).

• Experience in contaminated sites is highly desired.

• Experience in natural environmental science projects.

• Experience with hazardous materials surveys.

• Experience in contaminant hydrogeology.

• Experience in managing a portfolio of projects.

• Experience working on federal client assignments is considered a strong asset.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Advanced problem solving and analytical skills.

• Willingness and ability to travel throughout the Atlantic Region.

• Demonstrated sensitivity and consideration for occupational health and safety.

## What makes Englobe unique

At Englobe, you'll have the opportunity to work on a variety of projects of every size and scope. You'll work in an organization that values you and your experience, and allows you to grow.From day one, you'll enjoy the following benefits:

• Real flexibility;

• Multiple opportunities for professional growth, mentoring and skills development;

2240019.title: Medical Science Liaison
2240019.description:
## Medical Science Liaison

Sequence Bio is a Newfoundland and Labrador-based biotechnology company conducting genetic research to discover the true biological causes of disease.

We collaborate with the people and medical professionals of Newfoundland and Labrador, and partner with leading pharma and biotech to help accelerate the development of better medicines for global unmet medical needs.

## The Opportunity

We are seeking a highly motivated Medical Science Liaison to join our team. As the Medical Science Liaison, you'll represent a peer-to-peer scientific bridge between Sequence Bio's Chief Scientific Officer / Principal Investigator and our research collaborators.

We're looking for someone who can translate complex genomic research into trusted, actionable partnerships within the Newfoundland and Labrador healthcare community. In this role, you'll build strong relationships with regional physicians and specialists, accelerate research study enrollment, and share the impact of our findings with a wide range of stakeholders. If you're driven to make a lasting, real-world difference, this is your chance to be part of something that can truly matter for patients and their families for generations to come.

The Role
What You'll Do
Responsibilities
Research & Healthcare Provider Collaboration

• Serve as the primary scientific point of contact for healthcare and research collaborators, positioning Sequence Bio as a true innovation and research partner within the provincial healthcare system.

• Build and maintain trusted, collaborative partnerships with regional specialists, general practitioners, clinical researchers and other healthcare providers within target disease areas (e.g., respirology, rheumatology, oncology).

• Collaboratively develop streamlined referral and outreach processes with research partners to optimize participant identification and accelerate enrollment across active research studies.

## Scientific Communication & Education

• Deliver compelling, objective presentations on the scientific value of Newfoundland and Labrador's founder population, genetic architecture, and the mechanics of family-based validation studies.

• Provide scientific education to clinicians on target disease cohorts (e.g., MASH, Ankylosing Spondylitis, Multiple Sclerosis) and collaborate on inclusion/exclusion criteria considerations to support study enrollment.

• Represent Sequence Bio at regional medical conferences, symposia, and working groups to engage new partners and communicate progress, abstract data, and research milestone achievements.

• Synthesize clinical insights from community healthcare providers and collaborate with internal science and research teams to align study goals with provincial healthcare infrastructure.

Who You Are
Qualifications & Skills

• Education & Experience: Bachelor's degree in Biological or Life Sciences, Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences, Healthcare and Clinical Professionals, (advanced degree like an MSc, PhD, or PharmD is an asset). A minimum of 3-5 years of experience in healthcare stakeholder engagement, research partnerships, medical affairs, or professional biotech/pharmaceutical relations.

• Regional Network: Established professional relationships within the Newfoundland and Labrador healthcare ecosystem (e.g., NL Health Services, private specialty).

• Mobility & Residency: Current residency in Newfoundland and Labrador is required, along with the ability to travel across the province's health zones as needed.

• Scientific Acumen: Strong functional understanding of genetics, human biology, and population health concepts; demonstrated ability to confidently discuss complex scientific data and research methodologies with medical specialists (e.g., Rheumatologists, Oncologists, Neurologists).

• Communication & Presentation Mastery: Advanced public speaking and presentation skills, with a proven ability to translate complex genomic research objectives into clear, engaging narratives. Comfortable presenting to diverse audiences, ranging from formal clinical panels and academic symposia to community-facing patient advocacy groups.

• Advocacy & Community Engagement: Proven track record of building trusted, collaborative partnerships with non-profit health foundations and patient advocacy groups.

• Growth Mindset & Curiosity: A proactive learner with a strong intellectual curiosity and eagerness to continually expand their knowledge of genomics, data-driven drug discovery, and emerging precision medicine trends as the company grows.

## Why Join Sequence Bio

Working with us means working for the benefit of others. Whether your job is analyzing multi-dimensional data sets or coding a research application-we're all driven by the same purpose: enable breakthrough medical discoveries to improve lives around the world.

Our Benefits
Our benefits include:

• Fair and equitable salary

• Competitive stock option plan

• Progressive health and wellness plan

• Company-matched retirement savings

• Generous PTO and parental and family leave

• Learning and professional development allowance

## Our Commitment

Ethics, privacy and security excellence is rooted in everything we do at Sequence Bio. We are transparent about our information sharing policies and practices, and are committed to returning benefits to Newfoundland and Labrador. All our employees must uphold the company's commitment in all they do and champion the company's ethics, privacy and security mindset to ensure we maintain our best-in-class approach.

Sequence Bio is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB), and recognize the importance and value of a diverse workforce. We are committed to creating a safe, inclusive and respectful environment for everyone we interact with. If you could benefit from an accommodation during any stage of our recruitment process, please share with us how we can best support you.

## Culture and Recognition

Sequence Bio has been named one of Canada's Top Small & Medium Employers for 2026. This recognition highlights our commitment to our team through supportive policies, comprehensive benefits, continuous professional development, our leadership in gender diversity, and more.

Sequence Bio is also recognized as one of Atlantic Canada's Best Places to Work for 2026 by Atlantic Business Magazine. From our inclusive culture and competitive benefits to our commitment to professional growth and employee well-being, this award highlights our commitment to putting our people first.

You will provide administrative support by managing the logistics of calendars, schedules, organizing meetings, travel arrangements and responding to incoming routine correspondence, inquiries, and phone calls. 2190271.description:
## About NLHC

The Newfoundland and Labrador Housing Corporation (NL Housing) is a crown corporation whose mandate is to develop and administer housing assistance policy and programs for the benefit of low to moderate income households throughout the province. As the largest landlord in the Province, NL Housing manages a portfolio of over 5,500 units province-wide. The services provided by NL Housing provide clients with access to safe, stable and affordable housing, which is essential to the social, financial, and physical well-being of individuals, families and communities. There is a wide range of housing needs across the province, from those facing homelessness or at risk of homelessness, to low income households needing assistance to pay rent or complete much-needed repairs on their homes. For more information on our programs and services, and strategic priorities, please visit our website www.nlhc.nl.ca.

## About the Department/Region

Context:

The Central Region maintains and supports all NL Housing rental properties in the Grand Falls and Gander areas, as well as delivering a variety of programs designed for low to moderate income households and homeowners. The region provides a wide range of services, including receiving and processing rental applications; administering rental accounts and lease compliance provisions; providing various client services and tenant relations; and monitoring, facilitating and administering property maintenance. Regional staff members are involved in the delivery of the Provincial Home Repair, Home Modification, Home Energy Savings, Partner Managed Housing, and Rent Supplement Programs.

## Position Details

Competition Number:2025/26-042-800198P

Employment Type: 1 Permanent

Department/Region: Grand Falls Winsor

Location: Central Regional Office

Posting Status: External

Closing Date: October 11, 2026

Salary Scale: $70,434 to $78,824 per annum (CG-39, $38.70 to $43.31 per hour), 35-hour work week

Duties:

Reporting to the Regional Director, the successful candidate will engage with tenants and apply NLHC's eviction prevention framework to achieve the goal of maintaining stable housing. In completing this work, the incumbent will provide individualized and on-going support to tenants from initiating contact and follow-up activities such as telephone calls and home visits. Eviction Prevention work involves engaging clients to educate on tenant's rights and responsibilities as tenants, to connect to supports and support the development of tenant action plans that will decrease the risk for eviction. The Social Worker I will also provide unplanned, short-term crisis response for clients experiencing complex needs, mental health and addictions. The incumbent will work with tenants on an ongoing basis to build capacity to be independently successful. This includes the assessment of client needs and providing connections/referrals to a variety of community groups, government agencies and health authorities. In addition, this position provides Community Development support to the regional community centre by attending quarterly program development committee meetings and ensuring compliance with funding guidelines for quarterly grants and special funding. The Social Worker I will help clients navigate systems required to improve their own mental health and well-being, while maintaining stable housing, as well as participating in case conferences and maintaining correspondence with various medical, para-medical, and government departments. This work involves collaboration with other NLHC staff, regions and departments including Housing Officers, Managers, Eviction Prevention Coordinator and the Community Partnerships and Homelessness team, to jointly support clients all along the housing continuum. Case notes, written reports and recommendations are prepared in keeping with the documentation standards of the Newfoundland and Labrador College of Social Workers (NLCSW). The successful incumbent demonstrates accountability and effective resource management by documenting and compiling monthly statistics in a quantitative and qualitative manner. Other related duties may be required.

## Screening Criteria

Bachelor of Social Work Degree

Experience in the provision of professional Social Work services

Experience in delivering services related to housing and homelessness (asset)

Experience in the delivery of non-profit housing (asset)

## Assessment Criteria

Knowledge of professional social work practice and standards (including assessment/interviewing and debriefing)

Knowledge of housing and homelessness issues and best practices

Knowledge of eviction prevention techniques and Housing First principles (asset)

Workload management skills

Written communication and documentation skills

Ability to think critically

Ability to effectively exchange information

Ability to work independently

Relationship building and networking skills

## Conditions of Employment

Conditions of Offer:

Active registration with the Newfoundland and Labrador College of Social Workers (NLCSW)

Acceptable Certificate of Conduct

Proof of class 5 driver's license

Conditions of Acceptance:

Acknowledges the requirement for travel (day and periodic overnight)

Willing to accept flexible schedule/requirement to work alternate shift schedules

The Nurse Practitioner is responsible to provide comprehensive assessment and care to clients. The Nurse Practitioner provides comprehensive and holistic nursing care to clients including health promotion, injury and illness treatment and prevention, supportive, curative and rehabilitative care in a family practice setting. The NP will provide advanced nursing care including health promotion and prevention and chronic disease management for common health issues in collaboration with physicians and other members of the multidisciplinary team.

As an advanced practitioner, the Nurse Practitioner functions in the roles of practitioner, educator and leader.
