The Valuation Services Division of the Municipal Assessment Agency is offering a great opportunity for a Commercial Assessor. The successful candidate will ensure accurate valuation of property and outstanding customer service to our clients throughout Newfoundland & Labrador.

## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Analyse market data and assign value to all properties in a portfolio of real property including but not limited to commercial, industrial, institutional, and resource-based properties.

• Collaborate with field employees to set priorities and ensure timelines are met.

• Ensure the quality of the valuation and equity of assessment through application of accepted methods and performance of prescribed quality control functions (i.e. ratio studies, equalization process, etc.).

• Review property data and inspect properties in support of the appeal process.

• Represent the agency at tribunal hearings and appear as a witness in Supreme Court to provide evidence for verification of data and valuation.

• Conduct market research on real property to keep abreast of market trends within regions.

• Investigate property transactions to determine and verify consideration, influences on price, and qualification as an open market transaction.

• Provide opinions and estimates of condition, age, and functionality of improvements using a review of maps, deeds, and surveys.

• Determine and record ownership, boundary, dimensional, topographical, and location details.

• Verify legal descriptions of properties by comparing them to current assessment records.

• Confirm building codes and zoning by-laws to determine any effects on the appraised property.

• Interview individuals familiar with the property as required.

• Provide valuation and consulting services outside the assessment function to municipalities in the form of a letter of opinion or brief narrative work.

## SCREENING CRITERIA:

• Completion of a diploma in appraisal, assessment, or a related field (equivalencies will be considered)

• Certification or designation in good standing in one of the following:
• Accredited Appraiser or Certified Residential Appraiser of the Appraisal Institute of Canada, (A.A.C.I. or C.R.A)

• Certified Assessment Evaluator of the International Association of Assessing Officers (C.A.E.)

• Residential Evaluation Specialist (R.E.S)

• Associate or Accredited (M.I.M.A. or A.I.M.A) designation through the Institute of Municipal Assessors

• Eligible for membership in the International Association of Assessing Officers, Institute of Municipal Assessors, or the Appraisal Institute of Canada

• Experience in real estate valuation, including commercial, industrial, institutional, or resource-based properties

• Experience using computer software (i.e. Microsoft Excel & Word, databases, etc.)

• Experience with related legislation (i.e. Assessment Act, 2006) (asset)

• Experience with iasWorld or similar software (asset)

• Experience in a Computer-Assisted Mass Appraisal (CAMA) environment (asset)

## ASSESSMENT CRITERIA:

• Knowledge of real commercial property assessment practices

• Knowledge of related legislation (asset)

• Proficiency with related computer programs and software

• Ability to effectively exchange information

• Ability to independently manage time and tasks

• Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships

• Problem-solving skills

• Leadership skills

• Analytical skills with attention to detail

• Client service orientation

CAA Atlantic is recognized as one of Canada's Most Admired Corporate Cultures! We're committed to supporting your development through comprehensive training programs and continuous learning opportunities - helping you advance your skills and achieve your professional goals. CAA is one of the largest, most trusted and respected consumer-based organizations in Canada. We provide emergency roadside assistance, travel services, and exclusive savings and rewards for our members. We're deeply focused on helping Atlantic Canadians travel safely and confidently, whether they are on the road close to home or planning trips around the world.

## Join Our Automotive Services Team and Help Keep Atlantic Canada Moving!

Are you someone who feels a sense of reward and satisfaction when helping others? Are you passionate about roadside safety? Do you have a strong mechanical aptitude and interested in all things automotive? If yes, we have a great career opportunity for you based in St. John's, NL!

As an Emergency Roadside Service (ERS) Technician (12 Month Term), you'll be the reassuring face of CAA Atlantic on the roadside, delivering trusted towing and roadside assistance with professionalism, safety, and care. This term position will commence in early summer 2026 with an expected end date 12 months from the start date. Term positions are based on continued business need, CAA Atlantic reserves the right to extend or end early any contract position. Should your position be terminated prior to the projected end date, CAA Atlantic will provide a minimum 30 days' notice.

Every day brings new challenges and opportunities to make a real difference - whether you're rescuing a Member with a flat tire, towing a vehicle to a repair shop, delivering fuel on a rainy night, or boosting a battery during a winter storm. We do all that and more for our Members!

In this hands-on, fast-paced role, you'll take pride in providing safe and efficient towing services while performing a wide range of roadside support, from lockouts to tire repairs and battery installations. You'll use your mechanical know-how and problem-solving skills to assess situations quickly and get Members back on their way - all while communicating clearly and courteously with Members and Dispatchers to ensure timely, dependable service.

We're looking for safety-minded, reliable team players who thrive in dynamic environments and take ownership of their work. Flexibility is key - our Members count on us around the clock, and you'll be ready to assist during evenings, weekends, and holidays when help matters most. If you're known for your positive spirit, calm under pressure, and dedication to excellent service, you'll fit right in with our trusted team of ERS Technicians at CAA Atlantic.

This position is commencing immediately and follows a shift rotation schedule: 4 days on followed by 4 days off, 12 hour shifts.

This position is classified as safety sensitive. As part of CAA Atlantic's commitment to maintaining a safe and healthy workplace, successful candidates will be required to complete and pass a pre-employment drug and alcohol test as a condition of employment.

Qualifications
• A valid driver's licence with a satisfactory driving record and criminal record.

• Strong mechanical aptitude and comfort working with vehicles.

• Excellent problem-solving and customer service skills, even under pressure.

• Willingness to work a variety of shifts, including evenings, weekends, and holidays.

• A positive, reliable, and safety-conscious attitude.

Responsibilities
• Provide safe and efficient towing services for Members.

• Deliver roadside assistance such as lockout service, tire changes and repairs, fuel delivery, and battery boosts.

• Support battery testing, sales, and installation for CAA Atlantic Battery Service Program.

• Communicate clearly and courteously with Members and Dispatchers to ensure timely service.

• Maintain company vehicles, tools, and equipment in clean and reliable working condition.

• Follow all safety, traffic, and company operating procedures.

2241311.title: Administrative Assistant
2241311.description:
Our St. John's office is looking for a proactive, digitally confident and people-focused Administrative Assistant to serve as the operational backbone of our office and municipal engineering teams. This role is critical in helping busy project teams stay organized, informed, and ready to deliver important infrastructure projects throughout Newfoundland and Labrador.

This is a visible and important in-office role. You will be one of the first people our clients, visitors and team members meet, while also working behind the scenes to coordinate calendars, travel, meetings, project documents, office logistics and changing priorities.

You do not need an engineering background. We are more interested in how you approach work: whether you take initiative, learn new technology quickly, communicate warmly and professionally, remain composed when plans change and follow through on the details that help a busy team succeed.

If you enjoy helping people, solving everyday problems and becoming the person others trust to keep things moving, this could be an excellent opportunity to build a long-term career with a leading employee-owned consulting firm.

Your Key Responsibilities:

• Act as the welcoming face of CBCL's St. John's office by creating a professional, positive and memorable experience for clients, vendors, visitors and team members.

• Manage incoming calls and enquiries and connect people with the appropriate team member.

• Coordinate meetings, shared calendars, client presentations, office events and changing schedules.

• Arrange travel and prepare clear itineraries for project managers and technical staff, including changes and expense documentation.

• Format and coordinate letters, reports, proposals, specifications and other project documents.

• Maintain organized digital project records, proposal trackers, filing systems and archives.

• Support meeting preparation, record key decisions and actions, and help ensure follow-up items are not lost.

• Support engineering and project management teams working on municipal infrastructure projects throughout Newfoundland and Labrador by helping coordinate the information, meetings, travel and documentation required to deliver successful projects.

• Keep shared office areas organized, welcoming and supplied, including coordinating routine office services and supplies.

• Assist with everyday workplace technology, such as meeting-room equipment, printer connections and basic software issues, escalating matters when appropriate.

• Look for practical ways to simplify administrative processes and improve how information is organized and shared.

Career Growth

• This role offers more than traditional administrative support. As your skills develop, you will have opportunities to take ownership of increasingly complex responsibilities including: project administration, proposal coordination, document control systems, office operations, event coordination, business development support and digital workplace initiatives. We are looking for someone who wants to grow with our team and build a long-term career within a leading employee-owned engineering consulting firm.

• You will work closely with engineering and project teams, receive practical coaching and gain exposure to the systems and processes behind consulting projects across Newfoundland and Labrador.

Your Capabilities and Credentials:

• Experience in administration, office coordination, customer service, hospitality, project support or another role involving organization and frequent interaction with people.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Practical experience with Microsoft 365 applications including Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams and SharePoint

• Demonstrated ability to quickly learn unfamiliar technology, troubleshoot routine digital and office issues, and confidently adapt to new software, systems and processes.

Assets, Not Requirements:

• Previous experience in consulting, professional services, construction, architecture, engineering or a quality-managed environment would be helpful but is not required. We will provide training on our project processes and terminology.

• Experience in formatting and preparation of reports and proposals;

• Post-secondary education in office administration, business or a related area is an asset. An equivalent combination of education, customer-service experience, administrative experience and demonstrated digital capability will also be considered.

What we can offer you:

• A competitive compensation package effective on your first day of employment:
• Comprehensive health and dental benefits

• CAAT Defined Benefit Pension Plan with employer contributions

• Generous vacation allowance commensurate with experience

• Maternity or Parental leave top-up

• Health spending account

• Wellness incentive

• Membership dues reimbursement

• Education and lifelong learning subsidization

• Community volunteering incentive

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Public transit subsidy

In addition to the above benefits, we offer:

• Ability to work paid overtime or bank time-in-lieu for future use;

• Diverse team with a wide range of experience and expertise;

• Exposure to a variety of projects;

• Support to develop skills and pursue projects related to your own interests;

• Collaboration between multiple disciplines and levels of expertise;

• Mentoring opportunities to foster your personal and professional development;

• Accessible and central offices in Atlantic Canada and Ottawa; and

• Access to training opportunities in areas ranging from technical development to leadership skills.

About Us

At CBCL our purpose is to create a positive and lasting impact on people and our planet. As an employee-owned firm, at CBCL, our people are everything. We are committed to promoting inclusivity and diversity for a workplace where everyone can thrive, and we build long-term relationships with our clients while providing them with innovative solutions.

We have earned recognition as one of Canada's Top 100 Employers and one of Canada's Best Managed Companies. Our multitalented group of professionals offer consulting in the Infrastructure, Water and Wastewater, Buildings, Industrial, and Earth and Environment sectors. We value our people, our communities, and our history and look forward to continuing our steady growth.

Along with our commitment to reducing our carbon footprint corporately, CBCL develops and implements sustainable engineering solutions that respect the current social and environmental impacts, as well as future implications of our designs.

CBCL operates from its offices in Halifax and Sydney, NS; Charlottetown, PE; Saint John, Fredericton and Moncton, NB; St. John's, NL, and Ottawa, ON.

CBCL Limited strives to provide a diverse workplace that is inclusive, accessible and celebrates individuals and what makes us unique. We are proud to be an employer partner with the Canadian Centre for Diversity and Inclusion and Pride at Work.

We are committed to creating an inclusive and accessible workplace for all. If you require accommodations at any stage of the recruitment or interview process, or while working with us, please email hr@cbcl.ca. We will work with you to meet your needs in a respectful and timely manner.

Our goal is to ensure every candidate has a fair opportunity to demonstrate their abilities. We value diverse perspectives and are dedicated to removing barriers that may prevent individuals from thriving in their roles.

We thank all applicants for their interest, but only those applicants who are selected to interview will be contacted.

2239465.title: Geoscientist
2239465.employer: Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Offshore Energy Regulator (C-NLOER)
2239465.description:
The Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Offshore Energy Regulator (C-NLOER) invites applications for the full-time permanent position of Geoscientist to join a technical offshore Geoscience Team supporting the regulation of exploration and development activities in the Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Offshore Area. This role offers the opportunity to contribute to a wide range of offshore basin activities while working within a multidisciplinary and collaborative environment.

As part of a leading regulatory organization, the Geoscientist will play a key role in land tenure administration, regulatory operations related to exploration and resource management, and engagement with operators, stakeholders and internal teams. The ideal candidate will have a strong understanding of sedimentary geological processes with an overall focus on energy sector geophysical analysis.

Reporting to the Lead, Geoscience in the Offshore Resources and Data Department, this position supports geoscience projects and regulatory activities, and is responsible for the following:

• 2D/3D seismic interpretation using advanced interpretation workflows and attribute analysis to evaluate subsurface geology.

• Conduct integrated geological and geophysical assessments to support scheduled land tenure processes and exploration-related activities in the Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Offshore Area.

• Reservoir modelling support for technical assessments.

• Participate in geoscientific studies and special projects related to petroleum exploration, development and renewable energy geosciences such as evaluating petroleum system elements and reservoir scale interpretation in the case of development projects.

• Participate in multidisciplinary evaluations and supporting oversight of regulatory approvals and authorizations alongside engineers and other geoscientists.

• Participate in the development and review of policies, guidelines, and regulatory instruments.

Geo. with PEGNL is preferred.

## Who we are:

The Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Offshore Energy Regulator (C-NLOER) is the independent agency formerly known as the Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Offshore Petroleum Board (C-NLOPB). It dates back to 1986, established by the federal and provincial governments under the Atlantic Accord Implementation Acts. Legislative amendments that came into effect in 2025 expanded our mandate to include offshore renewable energy and changed our name. The C-NLOER regulates oil and gas exploration and development and will regulate future renewable energy projects in the Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Offshore Area. 2240408.description:
Jump Recruitment, on behalf of our client Adventure Sales & Service, are seeking a Powersports Dealership Controller, to join their team in Gander, NL.

Position Summary: A Powersports Dealership Controller manages the unique financial complexities of a dealership selling Travel trailers, ATVs, UTVs, snowmobiles, boats, and trailers. Operating as a key strategic partner to the General Manager, this role maintains tight internal controls and manages high-volume inventory financing across diverse manufacturers (such as Polaris, CF Moto, Mercury Marine, TYM Tractors, Forest River, Thor Industries).

The Powersports Dealership Controller leads the financial and administrative operations of the dealership. This role oversees all accounting functions, maintains precise records, and generates timely monthly financial statements in accordance with diverse manufacturer requirements. The Controller enforces internal controls and provides critical unit-inventory and margin analyses to Management to help optimize profitability across Sales, Parts, and Service.

## Key Responsibilities:

## Inventory & Floor Plan Management

• Reconcile monthly floor plan statements across multiple powersports lenders and manufacturers (e.g., Wells Fargo CDF, Huntington).

• Track unit margins and funding closely, ensuring all units sold are paid off promptly (Paid-When-Sold compliance) to avoid interest penalties.

• Manage parts and apparel inventory accounting, coordinating regular physical counts and auditing obsolescence reserves.

## Financial Reporting & Management

• Prepare monthly financial statements according to individual powersports manufacturer formats and deadlines.

• Maintain the Daily Operating Control (DOC) to provide management with a real-time snapshot of dealership performance.

• Monitor seasonal cash flow cycles, forecasting cash needs to navigate predictable seasonal dips in inventory sales.

• Review and reconcile all scheduled accounts, including factory receivables, finance/insurance (F&I) product reserves, and co-op advertising funds.

## Operations & Team Leadership

• Design and enforce internal controls to safeguard high-value unit inventory, parts, and cash flow.

• Streamline the deal-jacket process, ensuring Sales, F&I, and Accounting workflows communicate seamlessly to speed up bank funding.

## Human Resources & Payroll Administration

• Process full-cycle payroll for all dealership employees, accurately calculating complex automotive/powersports pay plans (base pay, hourly flag rates, flat-rate service commissions, and tiered sales bonuses).

• Manage employee onboarding and offboarding, including background checks, and setting up system credentials.

• Administer employee benefits packages, handling health insurance enrollment, workers' compensation claims, and paid time off (PTO) tracking.

• Maintain digital employee files in strict compliance with federal, provincial, and local labor laws, ensuring confidentiality of medical and personal data.

• Serve as the primary HR point of contact for employee inquiries regarding pay errors, benefits questions, and company policies.

## Qualifications:

• Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or Business Administration (or equivalent progressive dealership experience).

• 5+ years of dealership accounting experience, with a strong preference for powersports, marine, RV, or Automotive environments.

• Proficiency with Powersports Management Systems (DMS) such as DX1, Lightspeed EVOX, or CDK.

• Proven track record managing a full month-end close process and handling complex, multi-line OEM accounting.

## About NLHC

The Newfoundland and Labrador Housing Corporation (NL Housing) is a crown corporation whose mandate is to develop and administer housing assistance policy and programs for the benefit of low to moderate income households throughout the province. As the largest landlord in the Province, NL Housing manages a portfolio of over 5,500 units province-wide. The services provided by NL Housing provide clients with access to safe, stable and affordable housing, which is essential to the social, financial, and physical well-being of individuals, families and communities. There is a wide range of housing needs across the province, from those facing homelessness or at risk of homelessness, to low income households needing assistance to pay rent or complete much-needed repairs on their homes. For more information on our programs and services, and strategic priorities, please visit our website www.nlhc.nl.ca.

## About the Department/Region

Context:

The Labrador Region maintains and supports approximately 250 NL Housing rental properties in the areas served by an office in Goose Bay and a sub-office in Labrador City. The region provides a wide range of services, including receiving and processing rental applications; administering rental accounts and lease compliance provisions; providing various client services and tenant relations including eviction prevention, and monitoring, facilitating and administering property maintenance. A variety of programs designed to support low to moderate income households and homeowners are also delivered. Regional staff members are involved in the delivery of the Provincial Home Repair, Home Modification, Home Energy Savings, Partner Managed Housing, and Rent Supplement Programs.

## Position Details

Competition Number:2026/27-016-900448P

Employment Type: 2 Permanent Position

Department/Region: Labrador

Location: Goose Bay

Posting Status: Internal/ External

Closing Date: September 29, 2026

Duties:

The incumbent performs skilled repair, maintenance, and refurbishment work on NL Housing residential units, including preparing vacant units for occupancy. Duties include plastering, painting, drywall repair, and general carpentry such as repairing and replacing doors, windows, flooring, siding, and cabinetry, as well as minor construction work. The role also involves basic plumbing repairs, including installing and repairing fixtures, clearing blockages, and identifying leaks. Work may include mold and mildew remediation and minor asbestos abatement in accordance with safety standards.

Additional responsibilities include completing minor electrical-related tasks, ensuring safety systems are operational, and performing interior and exterior repairs using appropriate tools and equipment. The incumbent estimates materials and labour, maintains records, and communicates professionally with tenants while working in occupied units. Other related duties, including seasonal tasks, may be required.

## Screening Criteria

Experience in residential plastering and painting.

Experience in residential carpentry, maintenance, or construction.

Experience in basic plumbing.

Knowledge of plastering and painting practices, including the use and care of tools.

Knowledge of carpentry methods and practices, including the use and care of tools.

Knowledge of basic plumbing practices, including the use and care of tools.

Knowledge of the National Building Code is considered an asset.

## Offshore Night Supervisor (NDSV)

Employer: Axis Well Technology
Work Location: St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador, with work performed offshore East Coast Canada
Number of vacancies: 1
Employment type: Full-time, temporary, project-based employment
Contract Duration: 18 - 24 months
Work Schedule: 28/28 rotation
Language of Work: English
Wage: CAD $225,000 to $275,000 per year, directly relevant experience and qualifications
Benefits: No additional benefits

## Job Description:

Reporting to the Offshore Lead Supervisor (DSV) and East Coast Drilling Superintendent, the Offshore Night Supervisor (NDSV) oversees offshore well operations during night shift activities on the Mobile Offshore Drilling Unit (MODU). The NDSV is responsible for the safe, efficient and regulatory-compliant execution of drilling, completion and well intervention operations in accordance with approved well programs, company procedures and applicable regulatory requirements. The NDSV provides operational leadership during the assigned shift and serves as the primary company representative offshore in the absence of the DSV, ensuring continuity of operations, contractor management, well integrity and safety performance.

## Key Responsibilities:

• Supervise offshore well operations during assigned shifts.

• Ensure drilling, completion and well intervention activities are executed in accordance with approved well programs, procedures and regulatory requirements.

• Coordinate drilling contractor and third-party service provider activities during night shift operations.

• Monitor operational progress and ensure activities are performed safely and efficiently.

• Identify operational risks and implement mitigation measures within approved authorities.

• Participate in shift handovers, operational planning meetings, risk assessments and SIMOPS reviews.

• Verify compliance with HSE requirements, well integrity standards and permit-to-work systems.

• Review operational data, daily reports and equipment performance to support operational decision-making.

• Escalate operational issues, non-conformances and safety concerns to the Offshore Lead Supervisor and onshore management as required.

• Support emergency response activities and incident management during assigned shifts.

• Coordinate logistics and operational readiness to minimise downtime and maintain operational efficiency.

• Ensure operational records, reports and regulatory documentation are completed accurately.

• Promote continuous improvement, safe work practices and effective communication across all offshore personnel.

## Required qualifications and experience:

• Engineering degree

• Minimum 15 Years experience in offshore drilling, well construction, well intervention, and well operations, including supervisory responsibility on offshore drilling facilities.

## DUTIES

Reporting to the Research Security Manager, the Research Security Analyst will support the advancement and implementation of research security practices at Memorial. The position will assist in strengthening processes and initiatives that safeguard research while promoting compliance with federal research security policies, guidelines, and best practices. The ideal candidate will apply knowledge of research security, legal and regulatory compliance, geopolitics, and/or national security; demonstrate a commitment to staying informed on emerging national security and geopolitical issues as they pertain to the University environment; maintain confidentiality when handling sensitive information; effectively manage priorities and changing requirements; and work within tight timelines. Duties include, but are not limited to:

• Conducting ethical, advanced, comprehensive online research while systematically documenting findings.

• Preparing detailed reports involving sensitive and complex matters.

• Developing, reviewing, and contributing to new and existing policies, procedures, guidance resources, etc.

• Applying relevant legal, regulatory, and policy frameworks to assess and mitigate research security risks.

• Assisting with the development and maintenance of website content.

• Supporting initiatives that strengthen and promote the University's research security culture.

## QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience (2-3 years) in research security, or in an academic, funding agency, government national security, or legal environment.

• A university degree in Science, Engineering, Business, Law, Political Science, International Relations, or in a field of specialization appropriate to the position

• Exceptional online research skills, including the ability to conduct ethical, comprehensive internet investigations, identify credible sources, and uncovering hard-to-find information with accuracy.

• Experience in developing policies, processes, guidelines, and informational resources.

2226537.title: Senior Case Manager - Roster
2226537.description:
Title: Senior Case Manager - Roster
Employee Working Location: Partially Virtual / Hybrid (AB, Atlantic, MB, SK)
Employment Status: Casual

The Canadian Red Cross (Red Cross) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2024, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

The Senior Case Manager provides support to individuals affected by emergencies, crises, or other challenging events by assessing needs, identifying barriers to recovery, and connecting them with appropriate internal and external resources. In addition to case management responsibilities, the Senior Case Manager serves as an escalation point for complex cases, ensuring timely resolution of urgent and high-risk situations. They provide mentorship, training, and guidance to Case Managers, supporting their professional development and ensuring consistency in service delivery. They also collaborate with leadership to enhance case management processes, contribute to best practices, and maintain alignment with operational requirements and organizational standards.

## In this role, you will:

• Provide advanced case management support by actively listening to clients, documenting their experiences, assessing their needs, and identifying gaps or barriers to recovery.

• Conduct comprehensive assessments of client strengths, vulnerabilities, and capacities, collaborating with them to develop tailored recovery plans.

• Evaluate immediate, medium, and long-term needs, identifying and recommending appropriate services from a broader range of resources beyond pre-defined options when necessary.

• Review case files and provide expert recommendations to leadership on appropriate assistance and interventions, ensuring alignment with organizational policies.

• Act as an escalation point for complex or high-risk cases, coordinating with internal experts and external partners to find appropriate solutions. Provide feedback and insights on new program design, and adaptation of programs in real time to meet needs where appropriate.

• Guide and mentor case managers, providing training and support in case management best practices, service navigation, and client engagement.

• Ensure consistent documentation of client interactions, assessments, and service plans, maintaining data accuracy and compliance with governance policies.

• Oversee case file quality, ensuring completeness, accuracy, and timely updates in the applicable system, while identifying areas for improvement.

• Lead and contribute to team briefings, debriefings, and meetings, sharing insights and best practices to enhance case management effectiveness.

• Collaborate with team members and external stakeholders to advocate for client needs, ensuring a coordinated and client-centered approach.

• Identify and analyze emerging trends related to client needs, service gaps, and capacity challenges, sharing insights with leadership to inform program improvements.

• Ensure adherence to established processes and procedures, proactively identifying opportunities for enhancement and escalating systemic challenges as needed.

## What we are looking for:

• Qualifications include a minimum of 4-5 years' experience and a 1-2 year post-secondary certification/diploma in social work, psychology, human services, social services, community or health studies or related field and/or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Experience handling complex or high-risk cases, including escalations and advocacy for vulnerable populations.

• Proficiency in standard computer applications (Microsoft Office Suite), client database software and comfortable to navigate multiple systems.

• Ability to identify, investigate and analyze problems, identify root causes and risks, and apply technical, functional and organizational knowledge to develop solutions.

• Communication skills, diplomacy and empathy to interpret information and deliver advice, clarify client or stakeholder needs, offer solutions, and resolve escalations in new or somewhat sensitive situations.

• Proven ability to manage escalations and provide expert guidance on complex, high-risk cases, ensuring appropriate intervention and resolution.

• High degree of attention to detail, and ability to simultaneously listen and type to ensure client information is accurately captured and aligns to CRC requirements.

• Fluency in English is required, French is an asset.

• Valid driver's license from a Canadian province or territory required.

• As we work with and support people (managers, colleagues, impacted households, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.

• Eligibility to work in Canada: At this time, we welcome applications from candidates eligible to work in Canada. If you are not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada, we encourage you to carefully review your visa to find out whether you are eligible to work in the job you are considering applying for. Refer to our FAQ for more information.

• If you are selected for this role, you will be required to complete a successful pre-employment screening process which includes a satisfactory Enhanced Police Information Check (E-PIC)

## Working Conditions:

• The working conditions for this role will vary depending on the specific location.

• This is a field-based role and requires deployment into affected disaster areas

• Requires intermittent travel and deployment, usually for periods of up to 3-4 weeks, to support emergency response and program activities; deployment frequency varies based on operational needs.

• Travel can be to high-stress or unstable environments / disaster-affected areas, requiring strong personal safety awareness.

• Occasional lifting of up to 5 kg.

• Periods of prolonged sitting or standing with limited breaks.

• Fast-paced and often unpredictable, with competing and time-sensitive priorities.

• Requires adaptability to frequent changes and the ability to make decisions under pressure.

• Involves managing multiple, business-critical deadlines simultaneously.

• Requires sustained concentration, attention to detail, and accuracy, including working with non-routine information and data entry.

• Involves exposure to emotionally charged situations and supporting individuals experiencing trauma.

• Work in disaster or emergency contexts may include challenging environmental conditions (e.g., noise, smoke, odors, weather) and rapidly changing situations with limited information, which can impact physical and psychological well-being.

• As we work with and support people (managers, colleagues, beneficiaries/customers, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.

• Eligibility to work in Canada: At this time , we welcome applications from candidates eligible to work in Canada. If you are not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada, we encourage you to carefully review your visa to find out whether you are eligible to work in the job you are considering applying for. Refer to our FAQ for more information.

• If you are selected for this role, you will be required to complete a successful pre-employment screening process which includes a satisfactory Enhanced Police Information Check (E-PIC).

At GEMTEC, we offer something different. We're a perfect sized employee-owned, 400-person multi-disciplinary consulting firm that is large enough to compete head-to-head with publicly traded engineering giants, but still small enough to maintain the culture and flexibility of a close-knit team.

• Have the ability to work in a fast-paced, multi-disciplinary environment

• Enjoy contributing as both a team player and a leader and thrive in a collaborative environment

• Approach your work in an organized and efficient way, with a strong focus on quality outcomes

• Are an effective communicator, with well-developed interpersonal, verbal, and written skills

• Experience leading, mentoring, or supporting others—or a strong interest in developing these skills and helping people grow.

A typical day on the job might look like:

• Provide technical support and oversight to a wide variety of physical hydrogeology projects and prepare proposals and reports in collaboration with other senior staff (including hydrogeological, contaminated sites, geotechnical, surface water, etc.).

• Lead and assist junior and intermediate staff preparing technical proposals and reports, including hydrogeological characterization assessments; impact assessments, groundwater supply and source water protection studies and approvals; quarry, mine pit and construction dewatering assessments and permitting; water balance assessments; and groundwater and surface water interaction and monitoring programs. Provide technical review of hydrogeological deliverables.

• Provide mentorship and technical coaching to junior technical staff.

• Developing and maintaining relationships with clients.

• Provide senior support and leadership within Newfoundland and Labrador operations; may include staff / team lead opportunities.

• Engage with our senior leaders in the Atlantic and Ontario business, providing input, developing and leading strategic initiatives.

The good stuff you get:

• Fair pay plus extra: competitive salary with year-end profit-sharing bonus.

• Complete health & dental coverage including vision, paramedical services, and Teladoc.

• Retirement planning made easier with a 5% employer match on your contributions.

• Paid time off (vacation and sick days) plus Employee & Family Assistance Program when you need it.

• Office year-end closure (paid time off between Christmas and the New Year).

Your background and what you bring:

• Bachelor's degree in earth science, environmental science or geological/geotechnical/civil engineering with an emphasis in water resources and hydrogeology. A post-graduate degree is considered an asset.

• Professional license in NL (i.e., P.Geo. or P.Eng.)

• Minimum 12 years of relevant professional experience (preferably in consulting).

• Thorough knowledge and understanding of provincial and federal regulatory frameworks for groundwater withdrawal/use, drinking water supply, contaminated sites assessment and management, and environmental assessment is required.

• Familiarity with infrastructure, pit and quarry, and community supply required. Specific experience in the mining industry is considered an asset.

• Groundwater flow and transport modeling experience is an asset.

• Numerical and advanced hydraulic testing experience is an asset.

• Senior project management and people management skills are required.

• Valid driver's license

The Labrador Region maintains and supports approximately 250 NL Housing rental properties in the areas served by an office in Goose Bay and a sub-office in Labrador City. The region provides a wide range of services, including receiving and processing rental applications; administering rental accounts and lease compliance provisions; providing various client services and tenant relations including eviction prevention, and monitoring, facilitating and administering property maintenance. A variety of programs designed to support low to moderate income households and homeowners are also delivered. Regional staff members are involved in the delivery of the Provincial Home Repair, Home Modification, Home Energy Savings, Partner Managed Housing, and Rent Supplement Programs.

2241196.title: Junior Civil Technologist

We have an exciting opportunity for a Junior Civil Technologist, Field Services to join our team in our St. John's NL office.

This position is intended for a recent graduate or early-career technologist who enjoys practical, hands-on work and wants to build a long-term career in surveying, construction inspection and municipal infrastructure.

You will initially work closely with our existing team of experienced civil technologists who will provide field training, technical guidance and ongoing mentorship. As your skills and confidence develop, you will take on increasing responsibility for field assignments, construction documentation, survey activities and coordination of field services work.

This is a field-focused position. Candidates should be comfortable travelling throughout Newfoundland and Labrador, working outdoors in varying weather and terrain, and supporting projects in remote or challenging locations. During periods of reduced field activity, you will support survey-data processing, Civil 3D drafting, reporting, estimating and municipal design assignments.

Your Key Field Services Responsibilities:

• Assist with and progressively lead topographic and infrastructure surveys.

• Support construction inspection and resident-services assignments under the guidance of experienced staff.

• Complete site investigations, measurements, photographs and field documentation.

• Maintain accurate daily field records, survey notes, inspection reports and construction documentation.

• Safely operate, care for and organize survey instruments and other field equipment.

• Communicate professionally with project managers, contractors, clients, property owners and members of the public.

• Travel to project sites throughout Newfoundland and Labrador, including remote locations.

• Work outdoors in varying weather, terrain and site conditions.

• Follow CBCL and project-specific health and safety requirements.

Office and Technical Responsibilities During Non-Field Periods

• Download, organize and process survey information.

• Prepare existing conditions plans and other drawings using AutoCAD and Civil 3D.

• Assist with municipal design and drafting for water, sewer, stormwater and roadway projects.

• Prepare inspection records, technical memoranda and report content.

• Assist with quantity calculations and construction cost estimates.

• Support engineers and technologists with project delivery and contract-administration activities.

Career Growth

This position is intended to develop into a key field-services resource within our St. John's office. As experience and technical abilities grow, the successful candidate will take increasing ownership of surveying, construction inspection and field-coordination activities while supporting the development of future junior staff.

Your Capabilities and Credentials:

• This opportunity is intended for a recent graduate or early-career technologist. Previous co-op, summer, survey, construction or municipal experience is helpful but not required.

• Diploma in Civil Engineering Technology, Civil Engineering Technician, Geomatics or a related program. Students completing their final academic term may also be considered.

• Introductory experience with AutoCAD and Civil 3D through education, co-op work or employment. Additional training and mentoring will be provided.

• Hold a valid driver's license and willingness to travel to job sites;

What will Help You Succeed

• A genuine interest in surveying, construction and municipal infrastructure.

• A positive attitude and willingness to learn from feedback and hands-on experience.

• Dependability, initiative and a strong work ethic.

• A safety-conscious and careful approach to field work.

• Ability to adapt to changing site conditions, schedules and project needs.

• Strong organizational skills and attention to field notes, records and equipment.

• Clear verbal and written communication.

• Ability to work both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.

• Introductory familiarity with AutoCAD or Civil 3D is helpful. Training and mentorship will be provided.

• A valid driver's license and willingness to travel throughout Newfoundland and Labrador.

• Ability and willingness to work outdoors in varied weather and terrain and depending on project needs, overnight stays.

Assets, Not Requirements

• Co-op, summer or employment experience in surveying, construction, municipal infrastructure, consulting or other field-based work would be considered an asset.

• Familiarity with survey equipment, data collectors or survey data processing.

• Exposure to GIS, quantity calculations, cost estimating or municipal piped systems.

• Safety training or previous experience on active construction sites.

What we can offer you:

• A competitive compensation package effective on your first day of employment:
• Comprehensive health and dental benefits

• CAAT Defined Benefit Pension Plan with employer contributions

• Generous vacation allowance commensurate with experience

• Maternity or Parental leave top-up

• Health spending account

• Wellness incentive

• Membership dues reimbursement

• Education and lifelong learning subsidization

• Employee Family Assistance Program

In addition to the above benefits, we offer:

• Diverse team with a wide range of experience and expertise;

About Us

At CBCL our purpose is to create a positive and lasting impact on people and our planet. As an employee-owned firm, at CBCL, our people are everything. We are committed to promoting inclusivity and diversity for a workplace where everyone can thrive, and we build long-term relationships with our clients while providing them with innovative solutions.

2236374.title: Quality Assurance Lead Hand
2236374.description:
Hermitage Processing Inc., a Division of Cooke Aquaculture Inc., a dynamic and growing east coast family company, with Platinum Member status in the Canada's Best Managed Companies Program, is offering a unique opportunity for the right individual to join the Processing Team as Quality Assurance Lead Hand.

Cooke is a global seafood company with operations in North America, Europe, and South America. Our company's success is driven by our dynamic, highly-skilled and innovative management team, supported by dedicated employees who live in coastal communities and contribute to the local area's economy and sense of community.

## The Role

The Quality Assurance Lead Hand is responsible for daily quality and food safety verification activities on the production floor. This position supports the QA Supervisor by conducting inspections, completing monitoring tasks, verifying compliance with procedures, identifying deficiencies, and communicating corrective actions. The QA Lead Hand acts as the first level of leadership and technical support for QA Technicians.

## Key Responsibilities

Quality and Food Safety Monitoring

• Conduct a QA assessment once per day throughout processing operations.

• Complete environmental swabbing programs as scheduled and submit the environmental swab plan to the lab the week prior to swabbing.

• Perform raw material temperature verification activities.

• Complete Acceptable Quality Limit (AQL) inspections, one lot per day.

• Monitor compliance with food safety, GMP, HACCP, BRCGS, BAP, and customer requirements.

Root Cause Analysis

• Participate in Root Cause Analysis investigations for quality, food safety, customer complaint, GMP, environmental monitoring, and documentation-related non-conformances.

One Point lesson Development & Training

• Develop and deliver weekly One-Point Lessons (OPLs) for QA Technicians and Production employees based on audit findings, customer complaints, root cause investigations, GMP observations, environmental monitoring results, and quality trends.

Inspections & Verification Activities

• Complete assigned Lead Hand INspec approvals each day.

• Identify non-conformances and initiate corrective actions.

Maintenance & Continuous Improvement:

• Complete bi-weekly facility infrastructure walkthroughs.

• Review maintenance work orders and identify quality-related concerns

## Expectations of the Role

• Reliability & Diligence: Consistently demonstrate reliability, punctuality, attention to detail, and accurate completion of monitoring and verification tasks.

• Hands-on QA Leadership: Lead by example on the production floor and provide day-to-day guidance and technical support to QA Technicians.

• Effective Communication: Communicate clearly and respectfully with QA Technicians, the QA Supervisor, production employees, and management representatives.

• Problem Identification: Proactively identify quality, food safety, documentation, production, and GMP concerns and escalate when required.

• Commitment to Standards: Uphold high standards for food safety, product quality, regulatory compliance, and record accuracy.

• Training Support: Reinforce procedural compliance through one-point lessons, short coaching sessions, verbal questioning, and follow-up verification.

• Adaptability: Adjust to changing production needs, inspection priorities, customer requests, and QA management direction.

## Qualifications

• Seafood processing or food manufacturing experience.

• Knowledge of HACCP, GMPs, BRCGS, SFCR, and food safety programs.

• Strong organizational and communication skills.

• Ability to perform inspections and make objective quality decisions.

• Intermediate computer and documentation skills.

## Benefits Package

• Health Benefits: Includes coverage for dental, vision, and extended medical care.

• Insurance: Life and disability insurance provided for financial security.

• Support Services: Access to an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

• Financial Planning: Opportunity for RRSP matching to support your retirement savings.

• Wellness: Wellness programs.

• Career Development: Professional growth opportunities and avenues for advancement.

• Perks: Employee discounts on company products or services.

Join our team and enjoy the benefits of full-time year-round employment with competitive rates and a comprehensive benefits package tailored to support your well-being and career growth.

*As per company policy, a criminal background check is required.

## The Opportunity

The role description is just one part of the story. This is an opportunity to grow, to stretch, to work within the parameters of the role but stretch to your fullest potential. We are a team that counts performance, we reward contribution, and we recognize talent. It is about being at the center of the fastest growing company in Atlantic Canada and knowing you are part of that growth. The ability to bring your passion for learning, desire for growth, and energy for moving your career forward is what we offer.

Why Cooke? Simple - we are a company that rewards initiative, resourcefulness and work ethic. We will champion your growth and provide you with the platform to create your path, your career and your future.

2241322.title: Social Worker I - Competition Number: 2026/27-035-700643P
2241322.description:
## About NLHC

The Newfoundland and Labrador Housing Corporation (NL Housing) is a crown corporation whose mandate is to develop and administer housing assistance policy and programs for the benefit of low to moderate income households throughout the province. As the largest landlord in the Province, NL Housing manages a portfolio of over 5,500 units province-wide. The services provided by NL Housing provide clients with access to safe, stable and affordable housing, which is essential to the social, financial, and physical well-being of individuals, families and communities. There is a wide range of housing needs across the province, from those facing homelessness or at risk of homelessness, to low income households needing assistance to pay rent or complete much-needed repairs on their homes. For more information on our programs and services, and strategic priorities, please visit our website www.nlhc.nl.ca.

## About the Department/Region

Context:

The Eastern Region maintains and supports approximately 3,500 NL Housing rental properties on the Avalon and Burin Peninsulas through offices in St. John's (Avalon) and Marystown. The region provides a wide range of services, including receiving and processing rental applications; administering rental accounts and lease compliance provisions; providing various client services and tenant relations including eviction prevention, and monitoring, facilitating and administering property maintenance. A variety of programs designed to support low to moderate income households and homeowners are also delivered. Regional staff members are involved in the delivery of the Provincial Home Repair, Home Modification, Home Energy Savings, Partner Managed Housing, and Rent Supplement Programs.

## Position Details

Competition Number: 2026/27-035-700643P

Employment Type: 1 Permanent

Department/Region: Eastern Region

Location: Avalon Regional Office

Posting Status: External

Closing Date: October 6, 2026

Salary Scale: $70,434 to $78,824 per annum (CG-39, $38.770 to $43.31 per hour), 35-hour work week

Duties:

Reporting to the Manager, Rental Housing, the successful candidate will engage with tenants and apply NLHC's eviction prevention framework to achieve the goal of maintaining stable housing. In completing this work, the incumbent will provide individualized and on-going support to tenants from initiating contact and follow-up activities such as telephone calls and home visits. Eviction Prevention work involves engaging clients to educate on tenant's rights and responsibilities as tenants, to connect to supports and support the development of tenant action plans that will decrease the risk for eviction. The Social Worker I will also provide unplanned, short-term crisis response for clients experiencing complex needs, mental health and addictions. The incumbent will work with tenants on an ongoing basis to build capacity to be independently successful. This includes the assessment of client needs and providing connections/referrals to a variety of community groups, government agencies and health authorities. The Social Worker I will help clients navigate systems required to improve their own mental health and well-being, while maintaining stable housing, as well as participating in case conferences and maintaining correspondence with various medical, para-medical, and government departments. This work involves collaboration with other NLHC staff, regions and departments including Housing Officers, Managers, Eviction Prevention Coordinator and the Community Partnerships and Homelessness team, to jointly support clients all along the housing continuum. Case notes, written reports and recommendations are prepared in keeping with the documentation standards of the Newfoundland and Labrador College of Social Workers (NLCSW). The successful incumbent demonstrates accountability and effective resource management by documenting and compiling monthly statistics in a quantitative and qualitative manner. Other related duties may be required.

## Screening Criteria

Bachelor of Social Work Degree

Experience in the provision of professional Social Work services

Experience in delivering services related to housing and homelessness (asset)

Experience in the delivery of non-profit housing (asset)

## Assessment Criteria

Knowledge of professional social work practice and standards (including assessment/interviewing and debriefing)

Knowledge of housing and homelessness issues and best practices

Knowledge of eviction prevention techniques and Housing First principles (asset)

Workload management skills

Written communication and documentation skills

Ability to think critically

Ability to effectively exchange information

Ability to work independently

Relationship building and networking skills

## Conditions of Employment

Active registration with the Newfoundland and Labrador College of Social Workers (NLCSW)

Acceptable Certificate of Conduct

Proof of class 5 driver's license

Conditions of Acceptance:

Acknowledges the requirement for travel (day and periodic overnight)

Willing to accept flexible schedule/requirement to work alternate shift schedules

Acknowledges the requirement for primary use of a private vehicle (with business insurance)

## Applicant Information

This is a CUPE Local 1860 bargaining unit position and as per the Collective Agreement, applicants internal to the bargaining unit will be processed prior to other candidates.

Newfoundland Labrador Housing values diversity in the workforce and is an equal opportunity employer.

Newfoundland and Labrador Housing recognizes the need for work life balance and offers flexible work arrangements.

Disability related accommodations are available upon request at any stage of the recruitment process by contacting recruitmentaccommodations@nlhc.nl.ca or by calling (709) 724-3002.

Preference will be given to applicants who are legally entitled to work in Canada.

Applications should be received prior to midnight Newfoundland Standard time on the closing day.

The applicant is responsible for ensuring that the application submitted clearly demonstrates the required criteria. Applications that do not clearly demonstrate the required screening criteria will be screened out.

The applicant is responsible for ensuring that the application includes accurate and current contact information, including phone number, mailing and e-mail addresses.

All information submitted as part of this application must be factual, complete and current to date of submission. Successful applicants will be required to provide proof of stated credentials as part of the selection process.

This competition may be used to fill future similar vacancies with NL Housing.

Only successful applicants will be contacted for an interview.

Do you have what it takes to help keep the lights on for our customers in communities across the province? Then joining the Newfoundland Power team could be part of your next adventure…

## Who We Are

At Newfoundland Power, we're passionate about delivering safe, reliable, and efficient electricity. Our roots in Newfoundland and Labrador go back over 140 years. Today, we're part of Fortis Inc., a leader in the regulated gas and electric utility industry in North America. As one of Atlantic Canada's Top Employers, we are proud to employ over 650 talented people who are among the best in the industry.

We are committed to ensuring a supportive, inclusive and diverse culture where everyone feels safe and valued for who they are. Together, we strive to create an environment which is free of discriminatory barriers, where everyone is treated respectfully and equitably so they can thrive and bring their whole selves to work.

Everything we do is guided by our core values: People, Safety, Service, Respect, Teamwork and Innovation. We believe in going above and beyond to serve our customers and giving back to the place we call home is a longstanding tradition held by our employees. This could be the opportunity for you to continue to grow and develop your career.

## The Opportunity

As a member of the Generation Engineering team, you will provide electrical engineering expertise and project leadership for capital upgrades and asset management initiatives across hydroelectric, thermal, and general property assets. You will lead projects through all phases, including planning, design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and contractor management.

## Key responsibilities include:

• Planning, designing, and managing electrical system upgrade projects.

• Developing technical specifications and supporting equipment procurement.

• Reviewing and approving protection and control single-line diagrams, electrical schematics, panel layouts, and related engineering deliverables.

• Supporting protection relay settings, logic development, testing, and commissioning activities.

• Providing technical support to generating station operations, maintenance programs, and asset management initiatives.

• Managing project scope, schedule, budget, quality, and contractor performance to ensure successful project delivery.

• Collaborating with multidisciplinary teams, operations personnel, consultants, and external contractors.

## Your qualifications include:

• Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering.

• Registered as a Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) with Professional Engineers and Geoscientists of Newfoundland and Labrador (PEGNL).

• Minimum of 5-7 years of progressively responsible electrical engineering experience, preferable within electric utilities, power generation, industrial facilities, or other critical infrastructure environments.

• Experience leading complex capital projects through planning, design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and closeout.

• Experience with power systems, protection and control systems, electrical design, generation assets, and asset management programs.

• Proven ability to provide technical leadership, mentor others, and effectively manage consultants and contractors.

• Strong project management, planning, analytical, organizational, and communication skills.

• Ability to work effectively both independently and within multidisciplinary teams.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.

• Valid Class 5 driver's license and ability to travel to sites as required.

Our team is seeking an Advanced Care Paramedic for a temporary call-in position. If no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics and Ambulance Operators/Attendants. We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

Duties/Job Demands:
The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will provide assistance to the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

Job Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
* Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;
* Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.
* Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.
* Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

Qualifications:
* Graduation from High School or equivalent;
* Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;
* Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;
* Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director
* Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;
* Current certification in Basic Life Support;
* Current ACLS certification (ACP only);
* Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)
* Effective oral and written communication skills;
* Critical and sound decision making skills;
* Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;
* For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.
* A satisfactory record of work performance is required;
* A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

## Salary:

* Advanced Care Paramedic - CGHSA-37 of the NAPE HS salary scale $39.14 to $46.27 per hour
* Primary Care Paramedic – CGHSA-29 of the NAPE HS salary scale $32.71 to $37.40 per hour
* Ambulance Operator/Attendant – CG-25 of the NAPE HS salary scale $23.78 to $26.19 per hour

Virtual clinical services will also be provided as necessary and
appropriate.

Occasionally uses hand tools and equipment that requires rapid physical movement and reflexes and controlled movement.
Fine finger/precision is required on a regular basis when performing work on the computer
Visual and auditory concentration is regularly required as well as higher than normal levels of attentiveness or alertness.

Current licensure with the Newfoundland and Labrador Occupational Therapy Board.
A minimum of three years of experience within the last five working as a Clinical Occupational Therapist in adult physical health is required.
Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively, with interprofessional team members, patients/residents/clients and their families in a one-to-one and group environment.
Demonstrated effective written communication skills required for client documentation, report writing and professional communications
Demonstrated ability to effectively translate and communicate knowledge in the specialized area of occupational therapy practice to others.
Proven supervisory and leadership skills.
Demonstrated ability to coach, mentor and train Clinical Occupational Therapists, Occupational Therapist Support Workers and students.
Proven ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships as a member of an interprofessional team.
Proven ability to assume professional responsibility for safe, ethical and effective practice.
Proven ability to develop positive working relationships with external stakeholders.
A valid Newfoundland and Labrador Class 5 Driver's License and the use of a private vehicle are conditions of employment.

Job Summary
The Nuclear and Molecular Medicine Technologist III is responsible for the day-to-day operations and implementation of the only Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography (PET/CT) program in Newfoundland & Labrador. This position performs specialized and advanced diagnostic imaging procedures using a PET/CT camera and involves administering radioactive materials and contrast with very specific timing/and flow rates to visualize the anatomical regions that are required. The result is a very detailed image that the Nuclear Medicine Physicians review to determine whether surgical interventions, oncology treatments, or palliative treatments are required. The results of the scans help the Oncologists to treat cancer patients, Cardiologists to treat cardiac patients, Neurologists to diagnose varying neurological conditions, and Internists to treat patients with infections in varying parts of their body. The Nuclear and Molecular Medicine Technologist IIIs are classified as Nuclear Energy Workers (NEW).

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Regularly moves or lifts objects between 10-50+ lbs. such as shielded radioactive sources and lead bricks.
Occasionally pushes and pulls objects or transports patients over 50 lbs. in wheelchairs or stretchers.
Regularly stands, walks, or sits for extended periods to perform activities.
A very high level of alertness and attentiveness is required when performing scans/procedures due to patients' condition, safety and because some scans/procedures are captured in real time.
Regularly performs fine finger/precision computer work; handling of open-source radioactivity and radioactive equipment/components requiring steadiness and accurate movement/control.
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) are a regular requirement, including gloves and gowns.

Job Qualifications
Graduation from a recognized (accredited) program in Nuclear Medicine Technology is required.
Successful completion of the CAMRT Computed Tomography (CT) Imaging or PET/CT Certificate Program is required.
Current registration and member in good standing with the Canadian Association of Medical Radiation Technologists (CAMRT).
Current BLS Certification is required.
Strong understanding of radiation safety procedures and CNSC regulations.
Proven analytical, critical thinking, problem solving, decision-making and organizational skills.
A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required.
