2240906.title: Manager, Finance and Corporate Services
2240906.description:
Position Title Manager, Finance and Corporate Services

Department Name Corporate Services

Reports to CEO

Version Dated September 21, 2026

## About Advantage St. John's Inc.

Advantage St. John's is the investment attraction agency established by the City of St. John's, the Town of Conception Bay South, and the Town of Paradise. Its mission is to amplify economic growth by enhancing investment and talent attraction, supporting business retention and expansion, and advancing economic development opportunities in Newfoundland and Labrador's capital region.

## Position Summary

The Manager, Finance and Corporate Services provides financial management, corporate services, and operational oversight to support the effective administration and long-term sustainability of Advantage St. John's. The Manager leads budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, payroll coordination, procurement controls, contribution agreement administration, funding research, grant applications, internal controls, and the preparation of quarterly and year-end financial statements for the CEO and Board of Directors. This position ensures the Agency's financial resources, systems, records, policies, and processes are managed with accuracy, accountability, compliance, and sound judgment.

In addition to leading the finance and corporate services portfolio, the Manager supervises the Executive Assistant and provides oversight across human resources, governance, risk management, information systems, property management, records management, privacy, and administrative functions. The Manager also contributes directly to Advantage St. John's investment attraction mandate by providing financial intelligence related to taxes, incentives, funding programs, and business conditions in Canada and Newfoundland and Labrador, and working collaboratively with the CEO, staff, partners, funders, and stakeholders to advance organizational and regional economic development priorities.

## Key Responsibilities

## Financial Management and Accountability

• Lead the Agency's financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, monitoring, reporting, and year-end processes in accordance with accounting standards, funding agreements, government requirements, and organizational policies.

• Prepare quarterly and year-end financial statements, reports, and supporting analysis for review by the CEO and presentation to the Board of Directors.

• Provide financial advice, analysis, and guidance to the CEO, Senior Leadership Team and Board of Directors, to support informed decision-making

• Coordinate the development, approval, and ongoing monitoring of annual operating and project budgets in collaboration with directors, funding partners, and the Board.

• Oversee day-to-day financial administration, including invoicing, accounts receivable, payment tracking, collections, deposits, and related follow-up to support timely and accurate cash flow management.

• Coordinate payroll administration and employee-related financial processes, including payroll inputs, benefits remittances, vacation or leave tracking inputs, expense claims, and liaison with external payroll or benefits providers as required.

• Administer procurement and purchasing controls by supporting requisitions, purchase approvals, vendor set-up, purchase orders, invoice verification, contract documentation, and compliance with organizational policies and funding requirements.

• Maintain complete, accurate, and secure financial records, including filing, document retention, audit support materials, banking records, remittance documentation, and confidential financial information.

• Ensure effective internal controls, financial policies, and processes are established, documented, consistently applied, and regularly reviewed.

## Grant and Funding Management

• Research and monitor municipal, provincial, federal, and partner funding programs to identify opportunities that align with the Agency's mandate, strategic priorities, operations, and project needs.

• Prepare and coordinate funding applications, proposals, business cases, supporting budgets, workplans, cash flow projections, and required documentation in collaboration with internal staff, funding agencies, and organizational partners.

• Maintain awareness of eligibility criteria, program deadlines, application requirements, reporting obligations, and funding conditions to support timely and compliant submissions.

• Administer contribution agreements and related project files, including tracking approved activities, eligible expenditures, milestones, deliverables, amendments, payments, and compliance requirements.

• Support project reporting, reimbursement claims, financial reconciliations, variance explanations, and funder communications to ensure obligations are met accurately and on schedule.

## Governance, Risk, and Human Resources

• Provide advice on financial, operational, human resource, governance, and risk matters.

• Serve as Advantage St. John's designated ATIPPA Coordinator, leading compliance with the Access to Information and Protection of Privacy Act, managing access requests, privacy matters, and serving as the primary liaison with the Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner.

• Develop and oversee policies, procedures, and best practices related to privacy, records management, information governance, retention schedules, and the protection of confidential information.

• Prepare policies, and recommendations for the CEO and Board of Directors regarding access, privacy, records management, and information governance matter.

• Manage the Agency's insurance requirements and related risk management practices, ensuring appropriate coverage, regulatory compliance, and organizational safeguards are maintained

• Promptly communicate significant, contentious, or emerging financial, operational, human resource, legal, or reputational issues to the CEO.

• Ensure human resource practices are consistent with organizational policies, employment legislation, occupational health and safety requirements, and best practices.

• Supervise, support, and provide direction to the Executive Assistant, including work planning, priority setting, coaching, performance management, and professional development.

• Maintain appropriate personnel policies, procedures, records, and confidentiality safeguards.

• Foster a respectful, collaborative, inclusive, and high-performing workplace culture.

## Property Management and Information Systems

• Ensure compliance with lease obligations and serve as the primary liaison with property management representatives regarding lease renewals, facility operations, maintenance, and office upkeep.

• Oversee office accommodation, equipment, services, safety, security, and business continuity requirements in collaboration with the Executive Assistant.

• Oversee information technology, telecommunications, software, cybersecurity, data protection, and related vendor relationships to ensure systems are reliable, secure, and appropriate for the Agency's needs.

• Plan and coordinate technology improvements that strengthen administrative efficiency, collaboration, business continuity, and information security.

• Ensure appropriate access controls, backup practices, equipment management, and technology-related policies are maintained.

## Investment Attraction Support

• Collaborate with the CEO, the Director of Economic Growth, and other team members to advance qualified investment leads, provide responsive investor support, prepare for investment attraction events, and execute investment attraction projects.

• Apply financial expertise to support investor and business client inquiries by providing research, analysis, and intelligence on relevant tax considerations, incentive programs, funding supports, and financial advantages available in Canada and Newfoundland and Labrador.

• Support the procurement processes and coordination of cross-functional project teams and external consultants to ensure deliverables are completed on time, within budget, and in accordance with funding and organizational requirements.

## Education and Experience

• A university degree in business, commerce, finance, accounting, public administration, or a related discipline from a recognized institution.

• A recognized professional accounting designation, such as CPA, is preferred.

• A minimum of five years of progressive management or leadership experience, including responsibility for financial management and staff supervision.

• Experience managing annual operating and project budgets exceeding $1 million.

• Experience with non-profit, public-sector, or government-funded financial reporting and contribution agreements is considered an asset.

• Experience in finance, human resources, privacy, information technology, risk management, governance, and policy development.

## Additional Requirements and Competencies

• Strong financial acumen, judgment, analytical ability, and attention to detail.

• Demonstrated ability to lead staff, manage competing priorities, and deliver results in a fast-paced and evolving environment.

• Excellent written, verbal, presentation, relationship-management, and stakeholder-engagement skills.

• Ability to exercise discretion and maintain confidentiality when handling sensitive financial, personnel, client, and organizational information.

• Proficiency with Microsoft 365 and financial, payroll, client relationship management, and information management systems.

• Commitment to the vision, mission, values, and regional mandate of Advantage St. John's.

• A valid driver's licence.

## Compensation

Advantage St. John's offers a competitive compensation and benefits package, including group health, life and dental coverage, a matching group retirement savings program, and professional development. The office is located in downtown St. John's and includes parking. Advantage St. John's is an equal opportunity employer and encourages applications from all qualified individuals.

## Apply

Applications should be emailed to info@advantagestjohns.ca with the subject line Application - Manager, Finance and Corporate Services. Thank you to all that apply. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

Do you have what it takes to help keep the lights on for our customers in communities across the province? Then joining the Newfoundland Power team could be part of your next adventure…

## Who We Are

At Newfoundland Power, we're passionate about delivering safe, reliable, and efficient electricity. Our roots in Newfoundland and Labrador go back over 140 years. Today, we're part of Fortis Inc., a leader in the regulated gas and electric utility industry in North America. As one of Atlantic Canada's Top Employers, we are proud to employ over 650 talented people who are among the best in the industry.

We are committed to ensuring a supportive, inclusive and diverse culture where everyone feels safe and valued for who they are. Together, we strive to create an environment which is free of discriminatory barriers, where everyone is treated respectfully and equitably so they can thrive and bring their whole selves to work.

Everything we do is guided by our core values: People, Safety, Service, Respect, Teamwork and Innovation. We believe in going above and beyond to serve our customers and giving back to the place we call home is a longstanding tradition held by our employees. This could be the opportunity for you to continue to grow and develop your career.

## The Opportunity

Reporting to the Vice President, Finance and Chief Financial Officer, the successful applicant will be responsible for leading the internal audit function of the Company. The internal audit function includes the review of the internal control systems, disclosure controls and procedures, information systems, corporate policies and risk management procedures, and governance processes.

• Preparing and executing an annual internal audit plan using a risk-based approach in accordance with professional standards and best practices;

• Reporting results of internal audits to management and the Audit & Risk Committee and ensuring implementation of recommendations;

• Managing the internal audit department and acting as a liaison with other departments;

• Testing the design and effectiveness of internal controls for various business processes;

• Coordinating internal audit efforts with the work of external auditors, as appropriate;

• Coordinating the Company's annual enterprise risk management review;

• Completing quality assurance reviews of continuous disclosure documents and regulatory filings; and

• Conducting special projects or investigations as requested by management or the Board of Directors.

## Your qualifications include:

• Bachelor's degree in Business, with a focus on Finance or Accounting.

• Chartered Professional Accountant with 8 to 12 years of internal audit, external audit, risk management and/or controls experience. A Certified Internal Auditor designation and experience with Sarbanes Oxley is considered an asset.

• 3 to 5 years in a leadership role is preferred.

• Depth of knowledge in generally accepted finance and accounting policies and IIA Global Standards.

• Sound professional judgement, attention to detail, excellent organization and analytical skills.

• Strong communication (written and oral) and relationship management/interpersonal skills.

• Experience in utility industry is preferred.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP;

• Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification;

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

## Branch Shipper and Receiver

Jump recruitment, on behalf of our client, ND Graphics is seeking a motivated and committed Branch Shipper and Receiver to become part of their warehouse team in St. John's, Newfoundland.

## About ND Graphics

Since 1981, ND Graphics has grown from a small family business into Canada's leading supplier to the sign and imaging markets. Servicing customers is our number one priority. As Canada's leading supplier to the sign, graphics, vehicle wrap, and imaging market, ND Graphics has proudly served customers in Newfoundland for many years. Due to our growing presence and commitment to the region, we are excited to establish a local warehouse, enabling us to deliver even more efficient service and support to customers across the island.

## The Role

In this role, you will contribute to operational efficiency, profitability, and exceptional customer service. Key responsibilities include order picking and preparation, stocking and organizing materials, inventory management, and maintaining a clean, safe, and well-organized warehouse.

## What You'll Do:

• Prepare and complete orders for delivery or pickup according to schedule, including loading, packing, wrapping, labeling, shipping, and inspecting products for damage or defects.

• Demonstrate strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to track inventory, maintain a clean and organized work environment, and prioritize tasks effectively.

• Meet the physical demands of the role, including standing for extended periods, lifting, pushing, and pulling materials as required.

• Coordinate freight handling by sorting and moving products to designated areas, rotating stock, and arranging disposal of damaged materials when necessary.

• Communicate effectively and follow written and verbal instructions, work orders, and safety procedures.

• Provide excellent customer service by assisting customers in person, over the phone, and responding to inquiries as needed.

• Operate office and warehouse equipment, including computer-assisted inventory systems, forklifts, and other light machinery used to move and store materials.

• Work independently while contributing to a collaborative team environment, partnering closely with the customer service team to support operational success.

• Demonstrate reliability and dependability, including punctual attendance and flexibility to support operational needs.

• Perform other related duties as assigned.

## What You Bring

• High school diploma or GED equivalent required.

• Ability to meet the physical demands of the role, including frequent lifting of 50+ lbs.

• Valid forklift training and certification required.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, and Outlook.

• Professional demeanor, strong interpersonal skills, and a commitment to maintaining a professional appearance.

## What We Offer

• Competitive compensation

• Health & dental benefits

• RRSP match

• Paid time off

If you are looking to be part of a fabulous team that spans all of Canada - this is your chance! We would love to hear from you!

Our team is seeking a Primary Care Paramedic for a full-time position. We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Primary Care Paramedic, then Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to an EMR as the next highest classification, they will be awarded as temporary full time (TFT) and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Primary Care Paramedic (or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will aid the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as a PCP or EMR;

• Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

2231106.description:
Jump Recruitment, on behalf of our client, Nu-Quest Distribution Inc., are seeking a Warehouse Shipper/Receiver to join their team in Mount Pearl, NL.

## Position Summary:

The Warehouse Shipper/Receiver is responsible for the accurate receiving, storage, handling, and shipping of products within the warehouse. This role supports inventory control, order fulfillment, warehouse organization, and occasional delivery services while ensuring compliance with company procedures, Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), and product handling requirements.

## Key Responsibilities:

Receiving Operations

• Receive incoming shipments and verify products against shipping documentation.

• Inspect all deliveries for damage and report discrepancies or shortages.

• Use handheld scanning equipment to receive inventory into the warehouse management system.

• Accurately stock products in designated locations and rotate inventory according to expiry dates, ensuring older stock is positioned for first use.

• Reconcile receiving discrepancies and communicate issues to the Warehouse Supervisor.

Shipping Operations

• Verify customer orders against invoices to ensure accuracy and completeness.

• Pick, pack, and prepare orders for shipment using appropriate packaging materials and containers.

• Apply shipping labels, identifying information, and special handling instructions as required.

• Select the most cost-effective shipping methods while maintaining service requirements.

• Obtain management approval for any additional shipping costs before releasing shipments.

Warehouse Maintenance and Inventory Support

• Assist in maintaining a clean, organized, and safe warehouse environment.

• Perform shelf organization and inventory housekeeping activities.

• Identify and remove expired, damaged, or outdated products and transfer them to the Returns Department according to company procedures.

• Support inventory accuracy through proper product handling and storage practices.

Delivery Responsibilities

• Perform occasional deliveries and pickups as required.

• Deliver products to hospitals, pharmacies, and other customers throughout the Metro area, CBS, Avondale, Pouch Cove, and the Southern Shore.

• Collect and return signed documentation, including Proof of Delivery forms and COS slips, when required.

• Ensure all products are transported safely and securely.

• Return all customer product returns, packaging, and documentation to the warehouse or office upon completion of deliveries.

• Ensure no products, returns, or packaging materials remain in company vehicles after deliveries are completed.

## Qualifications & Skills:

• Previous warehouse experience is required.

• Valid driver's license with a satisfactory driving record is preferred for delivery duties.

• Experience with inventory management systems and handheld scanners is considered an asset.

## Job Details:

• Comprehensive benefits package provided.

• Fast-paced warehouse environment.

• Frequent standing, walking, bending, and lifting.

• Ability to lift and move products weighing up to 50 lbs.

• Exposure to varying warehouse temperatures and shipping activities.

• Training provided for Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), product storage and handling, temperature-controlled shipping procedures, damaged products receiving and reporting and company warehouse policies and procedures.

Hermitage Processing Inc., a division of Cooke Aquaculture Inc., a dynamic and growing east coast family company, with Platinum Member status in the Canada's Best Managed Companies Program has opportunities for highly motivated individuals to join the Company's Processing Team based out of our facility located in Hermitage, Newfoundland. Our company's success is driven by our dynamic, highly-skilled and innovative management team, supported by dedicated employees who live in coastal communities and contribute to the local area's economy and sense of community.

We are seeking seasonal Sanitation Workers to join our team.

This position is responsible for diligently sanitizing the production lines and equipment, preparing foot and hand dips, as well as general housekeeping such as, but not limited to, sweeping, mopping, garbage disposal, and general cleaning of the common areas and as well as transporting fish.

• Clean work areas and sanitize equipment.

• Weigh fish and record weight and pack fish in ice

• Transport supplies, ice, and packaging materials throughout plant and storage area manually or with powered equipment

The Technologist also participates in research, is involved in quality control and radiation safety techniques and performs other related duties as required.

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Regularly lifts, moves, repositions, pushes, or pulls objects (i.e. supplies, equipment, cameras, lead vests, and patients), less than 10 lbs., between 10-50 lbs., and over 50 lbs.
Regularly stands or walks when performing procedures or scanning patients. Occasionally, works in awkward or cramped positions where maintaining balance is required while operating heavy machinery or equipment to perform scans.
Scanning patients requires controlled movements while physically handling cameras. Occasionally will sit to review images and use fine finger/precision movements to work on the computer, walk, and bend to give injections using fine motor skills.
Visual concentration is required when reading physicians' orders, positioning patients, drawing up radiation into syringes, calculating and measuring dosages, inserting venipuncture and intravenous (IV) lines, giving injections, examining detailed computer images, computer processing, and monitoring patients during procedures.

Job Qualifications
Graduation from a recognized (accredited) program in Nuclear Medicine Technology is required.
Current registration and member in good standing with the Canadian Association of Medical Radiation Technologists (CAMRT) in Nuclear Medicine is required.
A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required.

* Effective May 1, 2025, all Medical Radiation Technologists and X - Ray Health Professionals will require registration with the Newfoundland and Labrador Council of Health Professionals (NLCHP) in the appropriate discipline(s) in order to practice in Newfoundland and Labrador.

## About NLHC

The Newfoundland and Labrador Housing Corporation (NL Housing) is a crown corporation whose mandate is to develop and administer housing assistance policy and programs for the benefit of low to moderate income households throughout the province. As the largest landlord in the Province, NL Housing manages a portfolio of over 5,500 units province-wide. The services provided by NL Housing provide clients with access to safe, stable and affordable housing, which is essential to the social, financial, and physical well-being of individuals, families and communities. There is a wide range of housing needs across the province, from those facing homelessness or at risk of homelessness, to low income households needing assistance to pay rent or complete much-needed repairs on their homes. For more information on our programs and services, and strategic priorities, please visit our website www.nlhc.nl.ca.

## About the Department/Region

Context:

The Central Regional Office maintains and supports all NL Housing rental properties in

the Grand Falls and Gander areas, as well as delivering a variety of programs designed for low

to moderate income households and homeowners. The region provides a wide range of

services, including receiving and processing rental applications; administering rental accounts

and lease compliance provisions; providing various client services and tenant relations; and

monitoring, facilitating and administering property maintenance. Regional staff members are

involved in the delivery of the Provincial Home Repair, Home Modification, Home Energy

Savings, Partner Managed Housing, and Rent Supplement Programs.

## Position Details

Competition Number:2026/27-039-800859P

Employment Type: Permanent

Department/Region: Central Region

Location: Grand Falls-Winsor

Posting Status: Internal

Closing Date: September 30, 2026

Salary Scale: $55,993 to $61,984 (CG-28 $26.92 to $29.80 per hour) 40-hour work week

Duties:

Reporting to the Regional Maintenance Manager, the Occupational Health and Safety Officer will support the effective implementation and ongoing administration of the Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) programs, policies, procedures, and safe work practices. The officer will promote awareness of and compliance with established OH&S requirements and applicable federal and provincial legislation, regulations and standards and will ensure staff are informed of the relevant updates or changes to policies, procedures and safe work practices throughout the Central Region. The officer will identify hazards and emerging safety concerns and recommend new or revised safe work practices where required to address workplace risks. The incumbent will develop and deliver OHS training to staff; conduct workplace inspections, safety audits, assessments and provide guidance to managers and employees on health and safety requirements and responsibilities. The Officer will work collaboratively with employees, supervisors, managers, and contractors to address safety concerns, investigate incidents, promote safe work practices, and ensure compliance with applicable requirements. The Officer will also prepare hazard assessments, daily logs, and technical reports; conduct industrial hygiene and environmental assessments where applicable; investigate workplace hazards; and provide recommendations to address safety concerns. The officer will also serve as an active member of the OH&S Committee and contribute to the identification and resolution of the workplace health and safety issues. The Officer will maintain current knowledge of OHS legislation, standards, and best practices through ongoing training and professional development and contribute to the continuous improvement and promotion of a safe and healthy workplace.

## Screening Criteria

Completion of a 2- or 3-Year Diploma in Safety Engineering Technology (Equivalencies may be considered)

Experience working with occupational health and safety regulations and legislation

Professional safety designations such as the CHSC or CRSP (asset)

## Assessment Criteria

Knowledge of business application software (Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook) and document management systems

Knowledge of Occupational health and safety regulations and legislation industry standards, and safe work practices.

Knowledge of incident investigation, workplace inspections, hazard/risk assessments, corrective actions, and safety program administration

Administrative and organizational skills

Ability to effectively exchange information

Ability to work independently while managing time and tasks

Attention to detail

Relationship building

## Conditions of Employment

Conditions of Offer:

Acceptable Certificate of Conduct

Valid class 5 driver's license

Proof of required diploma/designation

Conditions of Acceptance

Acknowledges the requirement for day travel (constant)

Acknowledged requirement for overnight travel (periodic)

Use of private vehicle with business insurance

## Applicant Information

This is a CUPE Local 1860 bargaining unit position and as per the Collective Agreement, applicants internal to the bargaining unit will be processed prior to other candidates.

Newfoundland Labrador Housing values diversity in the workforce and is an equal opportunity employer.

Newfoundland and Labrador Housing recognizes the need for work life balance and offers flexible work arrangements.

Disability related accommodations are available upon request at any stage of the recruitment process by contacting recruitmentaccommodations@nlhc.nl.ca or by calling (709) 724-3002.

Applications should be received prior to midnight Newfoundland Standard time on the closing day.

The applicant is responsible for ensuring that the application submitted clearly demonstrates the required criteria. Applications that do not clearly demonstrate the required screening criteria will be screened out.

The applicant is responsible for ensuring that the application includes accurate and current contact information, including phone number, mailing and e-mail addresses.

All information submitted as part of this application must be factual, complete and current to date of submission. Successful applicants will be required to provide proof of stated credentials as part of the selection process.

The NP works independently in an Urgent Care/Emergency environment, conducting rapid assessment and diagnosis on a walk-in basis, which necessitates individual follow-up at times. 2239860.title: Professional Standards Coordinator
2239860.description:
Professional Standards Coordinator

Professional Engineers and Geoscientists Newfoundland and Labrador (PEGNL) regulates the engineering and geoscience professions in the public interest in accordance with the NL Engineers & Geoscientists Act 2008 (Act), NL Engineers & Geoscientists Regulations 2024 (Regulations) and By-Laws.

With more than 5,000 individual and 600 corporate members throughout the province, and beyond, PEGNL is accountable to the public through the provincial Department of Government Services to ensure licensed, competent and ethical practice of the professions.

Reporting directly to the Director, Professional Standards, and supporting the Director, Legal Services, the Professional Standards Coordinator ensures legislative compliance, that members are practicing ethically and competently, and that professional standards and guidelines are developed and enforced.

## Duties & Responsibilities

Specific duties of this role as required and directed by PEGNL include, but are not limited to:

## Compliance

• Conduct ongoing compliance monitoring.

• Document compliance actions and results in the compliance database and distribute compliance correspondence at the request of the Director, Legal Services.

• Oversee the professional liability insurance renewal requirement processes for permits to practice, ensuring processes are followed and completed correctly, managing timelines and ensuring timely resolution and ensure permit holder compliance.

• Respond to professional liability insurance renewal related enquiries.

• Process permit to practice applications for review by the Director, Professional Standards.

## Discipline & Enforcement

• Provide support to the Director, Legal Services with complaints filed for unethical or incompetent practice.

• Provide support to the Director, Legal Services with files referred to the Complaints Authorization Committee (CAC) and with files referred by the CAC to an adjudication tribunal.

## Standards

• Assist in the development of professional standards and guidelines.

• Support the Director, Professional Standards promoting awareness of the Act, Regulations and By-Laws among members and act as a resource for Memorial University on professional practice.

## Professional Development

• Coordinate the PD program (including annual audit).

• Research and develop regulatory learning modules.

• Manage PEGNL's learning platform and suggest learning module additions and modifications.

• Provide support to members on compliance with the requirements of PD reporting.

• Manage equity, diversity and inclusion (EDI) initiatives.

## Administration

• Champion the company's values.

• Respond to general inquiries from members and the public, received via phone, email or in-person.

• Assist members and permit holders with account enquiries.

• Assist with the annual renewal process.

• Prepare trademark confirmations and letters.

• Approve and revoke digital seals.

• Represent PEGNL on a national EDI committee.

• Support the Director, Professional Standards and Director, Legal Services, with work for PEGNL Committees and National Groups.

• Attend trade shows and other industry events.

• Assist with the annual greenhouse gas (GHG) assessment.

## Qualifications

• Professional Engineering or Geoscience (P. Eng. or P. Geo.) designation preferred.

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering or Geoscience.

• 3 to 5 years of relevant experience is preferred.

• Previous experience in a legal or legislative environment would be an asset.

• Strong oral and written communication skills.

• Strong organization, prioritization, and time management skills.

• Strong interpersonal skills.

• Comfortable dealing with members of the public.

• Computer proficiency (Microsoft Office preferred) and the ability to learn new software as required.

• Ability to effectively work within a team and independently, to review and process sensitive material with complete confidentiality.

Applications can be submitted to: recruitment@pegnl.ca

Deadline: Friday, October 2, 2026

While we thank all applicants for their interest, please note that only candidates selected to move forward in the recruitment process will be contacted.

The Centre of Health Excellence is an innovative organization in the local healthcare landscape. We are bringing a new way of thinking about how primary and outpatient medicine can be delivered. This is a great opportunity for the right candidate to join an exciting and growing health care organization.

Our Patient Care Coordinator plays an important role in creating an efficient, welcoming, and professional experience for our patients. Working closely with physicians and clinical team members, the Patient Care Coordinator helps prepare patients for their appointments, gathers and documents important information, supports patient education, and helps ensure the clinic operates smoothly.

This is a casual position with a primary focus on Sunday shifts from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., with the potential for additional shifts and opportunities as the clinic continues to grow.

The Perks
• Be part of a growing and innovative health care organization with opportunities for the role to expand in the future.

• Enjoy a great office environment that values engagement, teamwork, and a healthy workplace.

• Gain valuable experience working alongside physicians and other health care professionals.

• Work in a modern, paperless clinic environment.

• Receive training and support to learn our systems, processes, and patient care protocols.

What you will be doing
• Welcoming patients and helping create a friendly, professional, and positive patient experience.

• Reviewing and documenting patient information in the electronic medical record (EMR) using established scripts, formats, and clinic protocols.

We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic.

If the competition is awarded to a PCP as the next highest classification, they will be awarded as temporary full time (TFT) and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of Emergency Services. The primary base for this service is located in located in Happy Valley-Goose Bay/Sheshatshiu, NL.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP or PCP;

• Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

We are a provincial health authority responsible for delivering quality health care to approximately 550,000 people in Newfoundland and Labrador. Guided by the vision of the Health Accord NL, we offer a range of health-care programs and services through a wide network of facilities, clinics, and community services across five zones: Central, Eastern-Rural, Eastern-Urban, Labrador-Grenfell, and Western.

Jump Recruitment, on behalf of our client, CSN Baker's Autobody. is currently seeking a skilled Auto Body Technician to join their team. In this role, you'll restore vehicles to pre-accident condition, all while ensuring quality standards and safety are maintained.

If you're a detail orientated individual, who has a passion for automotive repair and thrives on putting your valuable skills to use - this opportunity is for you!!

## ABOUT CSN Baker's:

Founded in 2002 by a group of four successful collision repair owners, CSN Collision was established to assist independent collision repair facilities to improve their operations through performance assessments, ongoing training, and marketing initiatives. Today, CSN Collision is one of Canada's most advanced networks of independently owned and operated collision repair facilities. Our independence is our strength in that our licensees have a vested interest in the company and their communities.

Baker's Autobody is a staple in the Clarenville community and a leader in collision repair. We pride ourselves on providing the highest level of customer service and treating your vehicle as if it's one of our own. Our trained technicians will repair your vehicle properly to pre-accident condition so that you can get back on the road safely.

## WHAT YOU'LL DO:

• We are looking for an experienced and reliable Auto Body Technician with experience in collision and auto-body repair.

• Assess vehicle damage accurately and determine appropriate repair methods and procedures.

• Repair and replace damaged vehicle panels, frames, and structural components using a variety of hand and power tools.

• Perform dent removal, sanding, painting, and finishing work to restore vehicles to manufacturer and industry standards.

• Safely operate equipment and utilize proper lifting techniques to move vehicles, parts, and materials as required.

• Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment to support operational efficiency and workplace safety.

• Adhere to all company safety policies, industry regulations, and quality standards throughout the repair process.

• Collaborate with team members to ensure repairs are completed efficiently and within established timelines.

The philosophy of a Family Care Team (FCT) is to deliver care that is patient-centered, comprehensive, team-based, culturally safe, coordinated, accessible, and focused on quality and safety. This philosophy supports providers and care teams to meet clients where they are using an inter-professional collaborative approach where care is provided in the right place, at the right time, by the right provider in a manner that best suits the client’s need. The team will ensure clients are treated with respect, dignity, and compassion, and enable strong and trusting relationships with providers and staff. FCT’s will enable the delivery of a range of quality care for clients within their own communities while facilitating interdisciplinary work amongst healthcare providers. The FCT for the Brookfield/ Centreville will include the geographical areas of Brookfield and Centreville.

Definition of work:
The Primary Health Care Program is seeking an advanced professional Clinical Dietitian II for the Brookfield/ Centreville FCT. The Clinical Dietitian II is responsible for the provision of nutrition care (i.e. screening, assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation) to clients of the FCT as well as the planning, implementation, coordination and evaluation of nutrition services. The principles of the FCT align with the patient health home model of care; using a collaborative health care team approach, from various health disciplines, in the provision of primary health care services to clients.

This position functions with a high degree of independence and initiative. The successful incumbent will report to the Regional Manager of the Exploits Family Care Team, Primary Health Care Program and will maintain accountability to the Regional Professional Practice Consultant for Dietitians for integrity and professional practice issues.

Nutrition services will include (but is not limited to) health promotion, disease prevention, nutrition counselling (group and individual) and chronic disease management. In this role, the Dietitian will support the development, implementation and evaluation of nutrition practice, program and quality improvement initiatives within the FCT; participate in evidence informed practice, education and community capacity building; and play a lead role in the development of primary health care initiatives using a nutrition lens.

Clients in this primary health care setting have diverse nutritional needs and may include frail elderly, clients with acute and/or chronic disease and those at risk for malnutrition; as such the dietitians practice will reflect the needs of the clients/community. Care will be provided face to face and virtually as necessary and appropriate. The dietitian will apply their skills of advocate and change agent to support the FCT's mission; collaborate with the FCT team in the provision of care; engage with acute care and community supports in the provision of care; assist clients with navigation through the health system; and mentor other dietitians and team members.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements. Travel throughout the region may be required.

Required qualifications:
• Successful completion of Bachelor’s Degree specializing in Applied Human Nutrition or equivalent field of science as approved by the NLCD, supplemented by a 1-year internship and a Registered Dietitian (RD) professional designation.
• Registration with the Newfoundland and Labrador College of Dietitians is required.
• Two (2) years’ experience within the last five (5) as a Clinical Dietitian.
• Thorough knowledge of nutritional health promotion strategies; nutritional interventions to prevent and manage acute and chronic disease; clinical nutrition care processes; behavior change theory; primary care nutrition risk screening strategies and pathways; clinical nutrition presentations requiring referral to secondary health care services; and the broader health system and community supports.
• Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with inter-professional team members, patients/residents/clients and their families in a one-to-one and group environment.
• Demonstrated effective written communication skills required for client documentation, report writing and professional communication
• Demonstrated ability to assume professional responsibility for safe, ethical and effective practice.
• Demonstrated supervisory and leadership skills.
• Demonstrated ability to function effectively in a diverse and changing environment.
• Demonstrated ability to lead practice initiatives within the nutrition/dietetics community of practice.
• A valid Newfoundland and Labrador Class IV Driver's License.
• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position.
• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority.

Job Summary
The Clinical Psychologist III provides an advanced and specialized psychology service to the clients of the Mental Health and Addictions Program in the Eastern Rural Zone in NLHS. This position acts on referrals from clients themselves, general practitioners, specialists and other healthcare providers. Standardized assessment and therapeutic interventions are provided to patients across the lifespan, with a wide range of complex needs including, but not limited to, anxiety, depression, obsessive-compulsive disorder, eating disorders and personality disorders.

The responsibilities include designing, implementing and evaluating the psychological interventions provided to patients and families; conducting advanced, independent diagnostic interviews to expedite the formulation of an appropriate treatment approach; formulating and communicating psychiatric diagnosis using DSM-5-TR; selecting and administering comprehensive psychometric tests where appropriate, including but not limited to, intellectual assessment, personality assessment, neuropsychological screening, memory assessment and vocational/aptitude testing; interpreting psychological data for diagnostic purposes; conducting group facilitation; and monitoring/prioritizing patient wait lists according to clinical needs. The Clinical Psychologist may have involvement in DBT groups.

As a clinical leader, the Clinical Psychologist provides supervision to Psychology residents, Doctoral students and provisionally registered Psychologists. This position reports to the Division Manager and maintains accountability to the Professional Practice Consultant for Psychology for professional integrity issues.

Job Demands
Occasionally, there is lifting or physical strength required, less than 10 lbs. for files, boxes, or equipment.
Regularly sits; occasionally works in awkward/cramped positions, and stands to facilitate or teach groups.
Uses fine finger/precision work when on the computer and visual concentration is required when in sessions with patients (i.e. reviewing patient charts/notes, tests and for documenting work, and when reading or researching information).
Visual concentration is required to interpret patient observations and integrate into patient evaluation.
Auditory concentration is constantly required in sessions with patients to listen attentively, to be alert and to obtain and interpret information correctly.
A higher-than-normal level of attentiveness is required when assessing high risk patients.

Job Qualifications
Graduation with an approved/recognized Master's Degree in Clinical Psychology is required.
Graduation with an approved/recognized Doctorate Degree in Clinical Psychology is preferred.
Current and continuing registration or provisional registration with Newfoundland and Labrador Psychology Board is required.
Graduate course work and supervised experience in psychological assessment including cognitive and diagnostic assessment with children, adolescents and adults is required.
Graduate course work and supervised experience in evidence based therapy with individuals, families and groups with a specific focus on mental health issues is required.
Previous experience supervising Doctoral level residents is preferred.
Exhibited strong communication, program development and evaluation skills.
Possessed strong leadership and supervisory skills that are focused on engaging others and developing coalitions.
Demonstrated ability to provide strong and comprehensive clinical support, training and mentorship to other psychologists and supervisees.
Possessed strong analytical, critical reasoning, collaboration, problem solving, decision-making and organizational skills.
Demonstrated ability to effectively translate and communicate knowledge in the specialized area of psychology practice to others.
Demonstrated ability to conduct research, deliver lectures/clinical education sessions and provide clinical direction and consultation within an interprofessional environment.
Ability to work autonomously, prioritizing caseloads and client needs.
Demonstrated ability and willingness to participle in the clinical training activities of the psychology discipline.
Demonstrated strong awareness of ethical principles and standards of professional conduct.

2240815.description:
Higher Talent is excited to conduct an executive search for a strategic, hands-on, entrepreneurial Director of Finance for Fort Amherst Healthcare, in St. John's, NL.

## WHO WE ARE:

Fort Amherst Healthcare, a subsidiary of Fort Amherst Properties, is an investment company headquartered in St. John's focused on the development of high-quality seniors housing and health care services. The company currently owns and operates approximately 400 personal care home suites across the province, consisting of both licensed personal care homes and independent living seniors' apartments. Facilities under management include Bishops Gardens (St John's), Westbury Estates (Southlands), Mountain View Retirement Centre (Corner Brook), Cambridge Estates (St. John's).

With happiness, health and wellness as top priorities, we strive to offer an extensive range of services, living options, and lifestyle choices to meet individual needs - whether highly active, needing a little assistance day-to-day, or requiring a custom-designed care plan.

To learn more about us, please visit Fort Amherst Healthcare.

## THE ROLE:

The Director of Finance is a strategic, hands-on finance leader with a strong accounting foundation and demonstrated experience managing the financial operations of a complex, people-focused organization. The successful candidate will build and professionalize the finance function, establish scalable corporate systems and partner closely with the President, Director of Operations, site leadership, the Board, lenders and external advisors.

## RESPONSIBILITIES:

Reporting to the President, the Director of Finance will lead accounting, financial reporting, planning and analysis, treasury, banking, tax, audit coordination, lender and Board reporting and financial controls. The role will also oversee defined corporate-support functions including information technology, insurance, contracting, procurement, supply-chain governance, vendor administration and shared-service coordination.

## Financial Leadership & Reporting

• Lead accounting and financial reporting across all properties and legal entities.

• Own monthly close, budgeting, forecasting, cash flow, financial controls and scenario analysis.

• Standardize accounting practices, policies, controls and reporting processes.

• Translate financial results, risks and opportunities into actionable recommendations for the President and Board.

## Treasury, Tax & Risk

• Oversee cash management, banking, treasury, tax, audit coordination and lender reporting.

• Support financing, lender diligence, covenant compliance and transaction requirements.

• Oversee insurance, risk management and related regulatory requirements.

## Systems & Business Operations

• Modernize financial systems, reporting and workflow automation.

• Oversee technology infrastructure, cybersecurity, continuity and third-party providers.

• Establish scalable processes for contracts, procurement, vendors and shared services

## Systems & Business Operations

• Modernize financial systems, reporting and workflow automation.

• Oversee technology infrastructure, cybersecurity, continuity and third-party providers.

• Establish scalable processes for contracts, procurement, vendors and shared services.

## Growth & Integration

• Support M&A diligence, financing and transaction execution.

• Lead finance, banking, insurance, systems and vendor integration for acquisitions and new entities.

• Build scalable shared-service processes as the organization grows.

## Leadership & Partnership

• Serve as a trusted financial and business advisor to the President.

• Partner closely with the Director of Operations and site leadership.

• Strengthen financial understanding and accountability across the organization.

• Lead and develop finance and business-support personnel as the function grows.

## ABOUT YOU:

• CPA designation.

• 7+ years of progressive financial leadership experience; experience in healthcare, long-term care, seniors living, or another regulated, multi-site environment is an asset.

• Degree or diploma in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related discipline.

• Strong experience in budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, cash flow management, and financial controls.

• Strong business acumen with the ability to connect financial performance to operational realities.

• Exceptional analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills with strong attention to detail.

• Proven leadership experience with the ability to mentor, develop, and motivate a team.

• Experience with accounting/ERP systems and advanced Microsoft Excel skills.

• Proactive, hands-on approach with the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

• Knowledge of government funding programs and regulatory requirements is an asset.

## WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT:

An attractive total compensation package, including a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits package, employer matched RRSP, personal time off, professional development and growth opportunities.

## HOW TO APPLY:

If you are financially rigorous, commercially minded, and comfortable moving seamlessly between detailed execution and executive-level decision-making, this is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact. Bring your sound financial judgment, integrity, accountability, and leadership to Fort Amherst Healthcare-and take the next step in your career.

Our team is seeking an Advanced Care Paramedic for a temporary call-in position. If no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics and Ambulance Operators/Attendants. We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

Duties/Job Demands:
The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will provide assistance to the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

Job Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
* Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;
* Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.
* Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.
* Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

Qualifications:
* Graduation from High School or equivalent;
* Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;
* Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;
* Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director
* Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;
* Current certification in Basic Life Support;
* Current ACLS certification (ACP only);
* Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)
* Effective oral and written communication skills;
* Critical and sound decision making skills;
* Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;
* For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.
* A satisfactory record of work performance is required;
* A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

## Salary:

* Advanced Care Paramedic - CGHSA-37 of the NAPE HS salary scale $39.14 to $46.27 per hour
* Primary Care Paramedic – CGHSA-29 of the NAPE HS salary scale $32.71 to $37.40 per hour
* Ambulance Operator/Attendant – CG-25 of the NAPE HS salary scale $23.78 to $26.19 per hour

Ability to work autonomously, prioritizing caseloads and client needs.
Demonstrated ability and willingness to participle in the clinical training activities of the psychology discipline.
Demonstrated strong awareness of ethical principles and standards of professional conduct.

The Newfoundland and Labrador Housing Corporation (NL Housing) is a crown corporation whose mandate is to develop and administer housing assistance policy and programs for the benefit of low to moderate income households throughout the province.
