## Full careers. Full lives.

## Join the Medavie Health NL Team

Are you looking for a fulfilling career that makes a meaningful impact on your life, and the lives of others? As the provider of emergency medical services and medical communications operations across Newfoundland and Labrador, Medavie Health NL (MHNL) is proud to offer career opportunities for professionals who share our strong commitment to delivering healthcare to communities throughout Newfoundland and Labrador.

If you're a passionate professional seeking a unique and meaningful career, MHNL is your destination. Join our team and achieve your full potential in a supportive and dynamic environment.

Working Hybrid and reporting to the Lead, Provincial Scheduling, the Scheduler is responsible for the creation, management, and review of all operational schedules, including but not limited to Ground Operations, Mobile Integrated Health, Fleet, Air Ambulance, and the Communication Centre. This position balances the availability and resources against incoming requests to ensure all tasks are completed on time and adjust schedules as necessary to accommodate changes in priorities or deadlines. This position is also responsible for managing payroll processes, maintaining accurate employee records, approving leave, and serving as the primary point of contact for relief staff. The Scheduler ensures compliance with collective agreements and organizational policies while providing high-quality customer service to employees and managers across multiple healthcare sites.

This position is critical in ensuring precise and effective scheduling to ensure MHNL can meet the obligations of our contracts for service. The Scheduler will be responsible for ensuring an exact capture of all unionized employee hours worked to support Payroll in providing accurate pay for all employees.

This role requires strong attention to detail, discretion, and the ability to work independently in a fast-paced, high-volume environment. The Scheduler also contributes to employee wellness, supports HR processes, and helps maintain operational efficiency across the organization.

## Professional Qualifications & Competencies:

• Completion of a one-year business college program.

• Minimum of two years' experience in scheduling and using scheduling software complemented by two years of administrative experience.

• Advanced knowledge of Vector Solutions software considered a strong asset.

• Extensive knowledge of the policies, structure and functions of internal administrative systems and practices applicable to private industry.

• Require superior diplomacy and interpersonal skills in dealing with difficult situations.

• Proficiency in Microsoft office including Word, Excel, Access, PowerPoint, and Outlook, etc.

• Prior experience working with databases and knowledge of medical terminology is an asset.

• Must maintain very close attention to detail.

• Superior diplomacy in professionalism and confidentiality required.

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

• Self-starter that can work independently but also be a strong team player.

• Highly organized with strong time management skills and proven ability to prioritize.

• Some independent judgment and initiative required in the follow-up for special assignments, programs and issues if requested.

• Maintains corporate confidentiality in accordance with all Provincial, Federal, or corporate regulations or policy.

• Ability to solve problems, meet deadlines and effectively manage multiple tasks.

• Demonstrate excellent organizational and time management skills to adequately prioritize workload.

• Ability to work well under pressure, often under strict time deadlines.

• Demonstrate self-direction, good judgment, and decision-making skills to prioritize incoming work, composing correspondence, and dealing with other employees and the public.

• Demonstrate effective listening skills and the ability to follow instructions.

• Knowledge of online scheduling software.

• Knowledge of payroll procedures and familiarity with the NL Labour Standards.

• Strong understanding of collective agreements and HR policies

• Excellent organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills

## Salary Range

• $45,000 to $55,500 annually.

The Base Pay range may vary depending on the successful candidate or other relevant job-related factors such as knowledge, skills, qualifications, experience and education/training. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Medavie employees may participate in various performance-based incentive programs. Payments under these programs are discretionary and subject to both individual and organizational results.

While Medavie may use automated tools, including AI, to support application screening, candidates are expected to complete all recruitment interactions independently-without AI assistance-to ensure a fair and equitable process.

## Who we are

MHNL is the selected proponent to design, manage and operate a single, integrated road and air ambulance service in Newfoundland and Labrador. We are an incorporated, wholly owned NL-based subsidiary of Medavie Health Services (MHS), the largest contracted provider of emergency management services in Canada and a national leader in primary health care solutions, including mobile integrated health and community paramedicine programs.

Together with Medavie Blue Cross, MHS is part of Medavie, a national health solutions partner and innovative leader in benefits management, health management, and healthcare delivery. Backed by our team of over 8,200 dedicated professionals, we exist to improve the wellbeing of Canadians so that every life can be lived to the fullest.

We're one of Canada's Most Admired Corporate Cultures, one of Canada's Top 100 Employers, and certified Rainbow Registered as an organization that champions diversity, equity and inclusion. We foster a culture of caring where people are celebrated beyond their roles and valued for who they are and what they contribute.

If you share our mission of improving the wellbeing of Canadians, join our team.

## What it's like to work with us

We are more than just a workplace - we are a people-focused, visionary organization dedicated to fostering well-being and making a meaningful impact on the lives of our employees and the Communities we serve.

We celebrate individuality and value the diverse perspectives and skills our employees contribute. We go beyond providing competitive pay and comprehensive benefits by offering opportunities for personal and professional growth, meaningful experiences, and supportive leadership. At Medavie, you'll find more than just a job - you'll find a pathway to a full and rewarding career.

## We welcome diversity

We believe our employees should reflect the communities we serve and welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds. To provide the best experience possible, we will support you with accommodations or adjustments at any stage of the recruitment process. Simply inform our Recruitment team of your needs. We are committed to making sure recruitment, retention, advancement, and compensation are fair and accessible while following all relevant human rights and privacy laws .

## We put safety first

Employees of MHNL are accountable to our patients and coworkers by participating in and supporting all safety-related initiatives, as well as acting in a manner that fosters a culture that focuses on patient safety and a safe workplace.

Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

If you experience any technical issues throughout the application process, please email: humanresources@medaviehs.com.

BENEFITS: Benefits Package Applicable, Foreign Service Premium (applicable when employee is travelling outside of Home Country)

LOCATION: Offshore Newfoundland, Canada

TYPE OF RIG: DP3 6th Generation Ultra-Deepwater Semi-Submersible, Hercules

ROTATION: Equal Rotation

TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT: Contract, Full Time

CONTRACT: Long Term Contract; Estimate 400 Days + 300 Day Option

NUMBER OF POSITIONS: Four (4)

JOB SUMMARY: Organize the execution of drilling and well operation in a safe manner according to plans and procedures and actively follow up the ongoing operation in the field. Toolpusher is delegated duties for day-to-day operational planning and execution of lifting operations in their work area.

## PRE-REQUISITES/QUALIFICATIONS:

• Drilling Technical Courses or Equivalent

• 1 year experience as Toolpusher on a 6th Generation Deepwater AKMH Semi-Submersible

• 2+ years' experience as Driller on a 6th Generation Deepwater Semi-Submersible

• 6+ years previous experience in a role on a 6th Generation Deepwater Semi-Submersible

• 5+ years previous experience with AKER and MHWirth equipment

• HPHT Experience (while in leading offshore position)

• Knowledge of all technical calculations required for the safe operation of the drilling equipment

• Structured and organized mindset

• High level of integrity

• Analytical ability

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English

• Must pass Physical, Drug Screen and Background/Pre-Employment Screening Checks

## DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Leadership:

• Supervise the drilling and well operation in accordance with Odfjell's vision and values.

• Maintain good working relations between the drill crew and all other personnel onboard.

• Know your Driller.

• Ensure that all are familiar with the operational plans and own tasks.

• Take necessary action against unacceptable behaviour.

• Monitor relations between the drill crew members and other personnel.

• Assign tasks to the Driller.

• Correct unacceptable behaviour.

Competence:

• Perform/ensure on the job training.

• Be in accordance with competence requirements at all times.

• Know status on your crew members vs. competence assurance system.

• Ensure acceptable level of crew competence and act when insufficient.

• Decide correct tempo on the operation based on crew competence.

Operations:

• Hands on supervision of the drilling and well operation.

• Supply written instructions (DDIs) to the Driller as required.

• Ensure that checklists are ticked off and preparations are made in due time.

• Verify quality of pipe tally, calculations, trip sheets and other paperwork required for well operations.

• Organize and follow up the first line maintenance system for drilling equipment.

• Relieve the Driller as required.

• Prepare daily drilling report.

• Ensure that the drilling equipment is operated in a proper manner within its capacity limits and at the correct tempo.

• Ensure good communication between all involved in the ongoing operation.

• Ensure that the drill crew are trained, and the equipment is set up to handle emergency situations (e.g. well control, loss of position, heavy weather).

• Ensure correct performance and reporting of jobs done in the First Line Maintenance system for drilling equipment.

• Instruct the Driller.

• Emergency duties according to the unit's emergency organization.

• Perform other duties as assigned.

The above is intended as a summary of the key requirements for the position and is not intended to be a complete list of all duties and responsibilities.

It is the objective of Odfjell Drilling to ensure employment equity within the workplace. We encourage applications from Indigenous peoples, visible minorities, women, and persons with disabilities having the capability, qualifications, and experience to make application for this position. Qualified residents in Newfoundland and Labrador will be given first consideration in the staffing of these positions.

2228852.title: IT Network Security Analyst
2228852.description:
Challenge, reward and opportunity - the PAL Group of Companies offers all three. If you are a motivated, energetic and challenge-driven individual who is eager to succeed, you will fit in great with our corporate culture. With a proud history in the aviation industry for nearly 40 years, our company has grown and expanded to become international leaders in aerospace and aviation.

Supporting the PAL Group of Companies, we are looking for a IT Network Security Analyst to join our team in St. John's, NL.

## Responsibilities:

• Monitor network traffic for security incidents and events.

• Install and operate firewalls, encryption programs, and other security software.

• Fix vulnerabilities.

• Assist with information technology security, including LAN/WAN, firewalls, logging, web filtering, intrusion detection/prevention systems, etc.

• Enforcement of information security plans and policies, ensuring they meet all contractual and regulatory requirements.

• Assist with the development of Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery Plans.

• Adhere to security compliance programs such as ISO27001.

• Regular review of system events and audit logs to ensure policy compliance.

• Conduct risk analysis of new information systems and make recommendations.

• Awareness training of the workforce on security standards, policies, and best practices.

• Conduct periodic network and vulnerabilities scans.

• Conduct periodic simulated cyber attacks on information systems, networks, and end-users to find exploitable weakness.

• Conduct periodic configuration reviews of existing systems to ensure policy compliance.

• Investigation of security incidents & security breaches.

• Review of all requested information system configuration changes.

• Other duties as assigned.

## Qualifications:

• University degree or college diploma in Computer Science or related field.

• 7+ years of IT Security administration experience.

• Strong experience with networking systems: LAN, WAN, switches, routers, protocols, firewalls, VPN, wireless networks, security appliances, and network access security.

• Experience with CrowdStrike antivirus and SPLUNK monitoring software.

• Completion of Cisco and Microsoft certifications would be considered an asset.

• Palo Alto Networks Certified Cybersecurity Associate (PCCSA) would be considered an asset.

• Systems Security Certified Practitioner (SSCP) would be considered an asset.

The centre is associated with Golden Heights Manor, a 70-bed Level 3 long-term care facility.

The referral site is Dr. G.B. Cross Memorial Hospital in Clarenville, approximately 110 km away, offering a full range of specialist services including anesthesia, general surgery, internal medicine, obstetrics, gynecology, psychiatry, radiology, pediatrics, and 24-hour emergency (Category A).

ABOUT NLHS
NL Health Services offers the full continuum of health and community services including public health, long-term care, community services, hospital care and unique provincial programs and services. To do that, we employ qualified, competent, and caring individuals who are dedicated to their professions and to our vision of Healthy People, Healthy Communities.

ABOUT CENTRAL ZONE
Central Zone is the second largest health zone in Newfoundland and Labrador Health Services, serving approximately 90,000 people (17 per cent of the province’s population) living in 176 communities. With a geographical area encompassing more than half the total land mass of the island, the Central region extends from Charlottetown in the east, Fogo Island in the north, Harbour Breton in the south, to Baie Verte in the west. Central Zone provides a variety of primary, secondary, long-term care, community health, and other enhanced secondary services.

JOB SUMMARYNL Health Services Central Zone invites applications from Family Physicians to join the Family Care Team Program in a full-time salaried position in the Kittiwake Region.

NLHS is pleased to support Family Care Team in achieving its goals of providing exceptional and high-quality care to patients in the Central region. The Family Care Team (FCT) mandate is to provide patients without a primary care provider with access to primary health care services. Services will be provided using an inter-professional collaborative approach where patients will see the right provider at the right time and right place. The team may include physicians, NPs, RNs including diabetic nurse educator, clerical supports, LPNs, pharmacists, social workers, dietitian, physiotherapist and occupational therapist. All health care providers, including physicians, will be expected to practice to their full scope of practice to meet patient needs and requirements. The FCT aims to provide continuity of care to improve health outcomes and patients’ quality of life.

We are seeking physicians to manage a roster of patients in addition to supporting the work at the Category B Facility within the community. Additional support of other services, such as Long-Term Care and Personal Care Home services, is also part of the responsibilities as part of the team supporting that facility. Our ideal candidates will have a strong patient focus and excellent communication skills with a keen interest in practicing in a collaborative team approach. Hours of work may need flexibility to offer clinics during the daytime or coverage of Category B Emergency. After hours and/or weekend coverage may be required. The successful Physicians will provide care using the EMR platform.

Newfoundland and Labrador Health Services (NL Health Services) brings together five former separate health entities - Eastern Health, Central Health, Western Health, Labrador-Grenfell Health, and the Newfoundland and Labrador Centre for Health Information. The creation of a provincial health authority was announced following recommendations from Health Accord NL.

NL Health Services is responsible for delivering health and community services to more than 528,000 people living in Newfoundland and Labrador and employs over 21,000 people. NLHealthServices.ca

Job Summary
The Clinical Dietitian II is part of an inter-disciplinary team responsible for the monitoring and licensing of Personal Care Homes. This includes the monitoring of activities and reports related to nutrition and food service for assigned Personal Care Homes to ensure compliance to the Personal Care Home Program Operational Standards and the Personal Care Home Regulations 2001. There is a possibility of after-hours/weekend monitoring that may be required as part of the monitoring process. The Clinical Dietitian II collaborates with the inter-professional health care team in the provision of nutrition care; provides counselling/education to residents and staff of Personal Care Homes; participates in interdisciplinary team meetings, annual review meetings and investigations of complaints and completion of inspections which may require visits after hours and on weekends; and completes monthly statistical reports as required. The Clinical Dietitian II will engage in practice, program and quality improvement initiatives. Our team is seeking a Primary Care Paramedic for a full-time position. If no Primary Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Ambulance Operators/Attendants (also known as Emergency Medical Responder (EMR)). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Primary Care Paramedic, then Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to an EMR as the next highest classification, they will be awarded as temporary part time (TPT) and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Primary Care Paramedic (or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will aid the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

Headquartered in Atlantic Canada with a global presence in over 60 countries and a dedication to special missions excellence for over 50 years, the PAL Aerospace team thrives at the forefront of aviation technology and expert crew skills. As a rapidly growing company, we've built a reputation for delivering airborne special mission solutions that enable our customers to address today's complex security, safety, economic, and environmental threats. On the PAL Aerospace team, you're working alongside a tight-knit group of talented professionals who help make the world a safer and more sustainable place.

• Must be flexible to work all shifts and adapt to fluctuations in shift times due to operational and/or unforeseen situations.

• Strong leadership and organizational skills

• Effective communication and problem-solving abilities

## Great benefits:

At PAL Aerospace, we know that compensation isn't the only factor in choosing a company. That's why we're proud to offer comprehensive perks and benefits.

• Commuting: Pilots may commute from Gander, NL or Deer Lake, NL to PAL Aerospace's primary operating bases in St. Johns and Goose Bay, with travel and accommodations covered by PAL Aerospace.

• Rotational Schedule: PAL Aerospace offers a rotational (2 weeks on / 2 weeks off), allowing for meaningful rest, travel, and family time away from work.

• Competitive Total Rewards: In addition to a competitive salary, PAL Aerospace is also happy to offer:
• Comprehensive health benefits including medical, dental, vision, and life insurance

• Pension Plan with employer matching

• Employee Stock Purchase Plan

• Tuition Assistance Program

• Personal travel privileges with PAL and interline agreements with multiple airlines

• Employee and Family Assistance Program

• Industry discounts (hotels, rental cars, etc.)

PAL Aerospace is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment that celebrates and encourages diversity, equity, and inclusion whereby individuals are recognized, supported, and respected. Candidates of all backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

Only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. Thank you.

## Recreation Services Coordinator - Permanent

Department: Recreation & Community Services
Competition Number: #26-03
Closing Date: September 29, 2026
Wage: $28.95 per hour / 35 hours per week (flex schedule)

The Town of Pasadena is seeking an energetic, well-organized and community-minded individual to join its Recreation & Community Services Department as a permanent Recreation Services Coordinator.

Reporting to the Director of Recreation & Community Services, the Recreation Services Coordinator is responsible for supporting the planning, development, coordination, delivery and evaluation of sport, recreation and leisure programs and community special events for residents of all ages and abilities.

The Recreation Services Coordinator works collaboratively with community organizations, groups, agencies, volunteers and other partners to help ensure a diverse range of recreational, social and community opportunities are available within the municipality while minimizing duplication and barriers to participation.

The position also supports the promotion of programs and events, recruitment and coordination of activity leaders and volunteers, community-initiated programming, assessment of community recreation needs, grant funding applications, and the development of recommendations for consideration by the Director of Recreation & Community Services.

This position operates on a 35-hour flexible work schedule and will require some scheduled evening and weekend work as part of the regular work schedule to support programs, special events and other departmental activities.

## Key Responsibilities

The Recreation Services Coordinator will:

• Promote the Town's vision, values, priorities and objectives and foster positive working relationships based on professionalism, mutual respect, accountability and service to the community.

• Support and promote a culture of wellness, inclusion, accessibility and safety.

• In consultation with the Director of Recreation & Community Services, assist with the development and implementation of social, recreational and community programs and services based on identified community needs and a community development philosophy.

• Plan, coordinate, implement and evaluate recreation programs, initiatives and community special events.

• Conduct ongoing analysis of community recreation and leisure needs and identify opportunities for new or enhanced programs and services.

• Communicate and collaborate with community organizations, groups, agencies and individuals to strengthen cooperation and coordination of programs and services and avoid unnecessary duplication.

• Identify and develop potential partnerships with public sector organizations, private businesses and not-for-profit organizations to respond to identified community needs.

• Provide information, resources and support to community organizations, groups and individuals to assist with the enhancement of existing programs and development of new recreation and community opportunities.

• Research and maintain awareness of Provincial, Federal and other grant and funding opportunities and prepare funding applications as required or directed by the Director of Recreation & Community Services.

• Assist with the preparation of operating budgets for recreation programs, services and special events and monitor program-related revenues and expenditures as required.

• Assist with the preparation and completion of seasonal recreation program information, schedules, promotional materials and other publications.

• Assist in coordinating promotional and marketing activities relating to Recreation & Community Services programs, special projects and community events.

• Maintain complete and accurate program, event and activity records, participation statistics and related documentation.

• Assist with recreation facility bookings and maintain accurate documentation relating to the use of Recreation & Community Services facilities.

• Assist with the design, coordination and delivery of recreational and community programs offered by the Recreation & Community Services Department.

• Recruit, coordinate and support instructors, activity leaders and volunteers as required for recreation programs and special events.

• Assist and support Town staff on matters relating to recreation and community services.

• Ensure the safe operation and use of equipment associated with assigned duties and report unsafe acts, equipment or conditions to the Director of Recreation & Community Services.

• Perform duties in accordance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act and Regulations and applicable Town policies and procedures.

• Maintain and enhance professional knowledge and skills and participate in training or obtain certifications relevant to the position as requested by the Town.

• Perform other related duties and responsibilities as required.

The above statements describe the principal functions of the position and are not intended to be a complete description of all duties and responsibilities.

## Qualifications

A university degree with a major concentration in Recreation or Business Administration; two (2) years' related experience in the recreation field; demonstrated proficiency in computers and applicable software applications; proven interpersonal, leadership, written and verbal communication skills; demonstrated ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships; attention to detail and the ability to meet deadlines and work effectively under pressure; hold and maintain a valid Class 5 Newfoundland and Labrador Driver's Licence; hold and maintain a clear Vulnerable Sector Check; capable of being insured and maintaining continuity under the Town's insurance policy; capable of being bonded and maintaining bondability; or any equivalent combination of education, experience and training acceptable to the Town.

To apply for this opportunity, please submit a resume and cover letter (PDF file format) to hr@pasadena.ca, referencing Competition #26-03, by September 29, 2026.

The Town of Pasadena is an inclusive employer and invites applications from all qualified individuals. We thank all applicants in advance for their interest; however, only those selected for further consideration will be contacted. If you are unsuccessful, please accept our appreciation for your interest. This position is restricted to those legally entitled to work in Canada.

If there are no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics (PCP) and Ambulance Operators/Attendants (also known as Emergency Medical Responder (EMR)). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to a PCP or EMR as the next highest classification, they will be temporarily awarded the position for the same number of hours indicated above and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.
The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.
The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.
The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.
The Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will aid the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

What if your next career move gave you the opportunity to do more than manage engagements?

Jump Recruitment is excited to conduct a search for an experienced and driven Senior Manager on behalf of our client, located in St. John's, NL.

Our client is an established and growing accounting firm seeking an experienced Senior Manager to join its team. You may have built a strong technical foundation at a national or large regional accounting firm. Now, you may be looking for an environment where your experience is more visible, your client relationships are deeper, and your contributions can have a more direct impact.

• Expand your exposure beyond compliance and into meaningful advisory work.

• Have greater visibility and influence within the organization.

• Mentor and develop the next generation of accounting professionals.

## Closing date:

## Full careers. Full lives.

## Join the Medavie Health NL Team

Are you looking for a fulfilling career that makes a meaningful impact on your life, and the lives of others? As the provider of emergency medical services and medical communications operations across Newfoundland and Labrador, Medavie Health NL (MHNL) is proud to offer career opportunities for professionals who share our strong commitment to delivering healthcare to communities throughout Newfoundland and Labrador.

If you're a passionate professional seeking a unique and meaningful career, MHNL is your destination. Join our team and achieve your full potential in a supportive and dynamic environment.

Reporting to the Manager, Communications & External Relations, the Communications Advisor plays a key role in supporting internal and external communications, employee engagement, and organizational initiatives across Medavie Health Services operations in Newfoundland and Labrador.

Working closely with leaders, project teams, and colleagues across MHNL, the successful candidate will help plan and deliver communication strategies that inform, engage, and connect employees while supporting key business priorities, organizational change, and operational initiatives. The ideal candidate is a strong writer and relationship-builder who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys collaborating with interest groups, and can manage multiple priorities with confidence and professionalism.

## Responsibilities include:

• Developing and delivering communication plans and strategies that support organizational priorities, business initiatives, operational updates, and key projects across MHNL .

• Creating, editing, and coordinating content for a variety of communication channels, including newsletters, employee updates, presentations, key messages, speaking notes, website content, social media posts, and other communication materials.

• Supporting employee engagement and internal communication initiatives by ensuring employees receive clear, timely, and relevant information that aligns with organizational objectives.

• Providing communications support for change management, organizational projects, and cross-functional initiatives, working closely with leaders and project teams to develop and implement effective communication approaches.

• Building strong relationships internally to gather information, identify communication needs, and provide strategic communications advice and support.

• Monitoring of key regional and national news media to identify issues that may impact the operations and/or reputation of the organization and providing media support as needed.

• Coordinating and supporting employee meetings, leadership communications, town halls, and other engagement activities.

• Ensuring communications are consistent, aligned with organizational priorities, and reflect Medavie's brand, values, and culture.

• Monitoring emerging issues, trends, and developments that may impact employees, operations, or organizational reputation, and providing communications support as needed.

• Collaborating with communications colleagues across Medavie to share best practices, support enterprise initiatives, and contribute to the development of integrated communication strategies.

• Tracking, measuring, and reporting on communication activities and outcomes to support continuous improvement.

## Professional Qualifications & Competencies:

• Minimum of 3-5 years of progressive experience in a strategic communications role.

• Post-secondary education in Communications, Public Relations, or another related field.

• Have excellent verbal and written communication skills, and strong attention to detail.

• Demonstrate the ability to translate corporate vision into targeted communications strategies and deliver those initiatives.

• Proven delivery of communications strategies in a fast-paced environment with tight timelines.

• Team player with a focus on supporting colleagues, trying new approaches and delivering results.

• Strong interpersonal, project management and relationship-building skills, with an ability to work with various stakeholder teams in a fast-paced environment, across locations and operating companies.

• A self-starter and problem-solver who works independently and as part of a geographically dispersed team.

• Understanding of communications strategies; in emergency medical services and/or the healthcare industry.

• Flexibility to work outside of normal hours and open to occasional travel.

Salary Range: $70,000 to $85,000

The Base Pay range may vary depending on the successful candidate or other relevant job-related factors such as knowledge, skills, qualifications, experience and education/training. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Medavie employees may participate in various performance-based incentive programs. Payments under these programs are discretionary and subject to both individual and organizational results.

While Medavie may use automated tools, including AI, to support application screening, candidates are expected to complete all recruitment interactions independently-without AI assistance-to ensure a fair and equitable process.

## Who we are

MHNL is the selected proponent to design, manage and operate a single, integrated road and air ambulance service in Newfoundland and Labrador. We are an incorporated, wholly owned NL-based subsidiary of Medavie Health Services (MHS), the largest contracted provider of emergency management services in Canada and a national leader in primary health care solutions, including mobile integrated health and community paramedicine programs.

Together with Medavie Blue Cross, MHS is part of Medavie, a national health solutions partner and innovative leader in benefits management, health management, and healthcare delivery. Backed by our team of over 8,200 dedicated professionals, we exist to improve the wellbeing of Canadians so that every life can be lived to the fullest.

We're one of Canada's Most Admired Corporate Cultures, one of Canada's Top 100 Employers, and certified Rainbow Registered as an organization that champions diversity, equity and inclusion. We foster a culture of caring where people are celebrated beyond their roles and valued for who they are and what they contribute.

If you share our mission of improving the wellbeing of Canadians, join our team.

## What it's like to work with us

We are more than just a workplace - we are a people-focused, visionary organization dedicated to fostering well-being and making a meaningful impact on the lives of our employees and the Communities we serve.

We celebrate individuality and value the diverse perspectives and skills our employees contribute. We go beyond providing competitive pay and comprehensive benefits by offering opportunities for personal and professional growth, meaningful experiences, and supportive leadership. At Medavie, you'll find more than just a job - you'll find a pathway to a full and rewarding career.

## We welcome diversity

We believe our employees should reflect the communities we serve and welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds. To provide the best experience possible, we will support you with accommodations or adjustments at any stage of the recruitment process. Simply inform our Recruitment team of your needs. We are committed to making sure recruitment, retention, advancement, and compensation are fair and accessible while following all relevant human rights and privacy laws .

## We put safety first

Employees of MHNL are accountable to our patients and coworkers by participating in and supporting all safety-related initiatives, as well as acting in a manner that fosters a culture that focuses on patient safety and a safe workplace.

Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

If you experience any technical issues throughout the application process, please email: humanresources@medaviehs.com.

2241059.description:
Management Analyst II (Continuous Improvement & Internal Audit)
Permanent Position / 35 Hours per Week / Public Opportunity

The Municipal Assessment Agency is required to provide municipalities with real property values (or assessments) in accordance with the terms and conditions of the province's Assessment Act, 2006. We are responsible for providing property assessment services to over 240 municipalities within Newfoundland & Labrador.

LOCATION: Any regional office (St. John's, Gander, or Corner Brook)

The Municipal Assessment Agency is committed to providing their employees with training and overall professional growth. We provide great rewards including, but not limited to, comprehensive health benefits, flexible working arrangements, pension and leave benefits, learning and development opportunities, an employee & family assistance program, and challenging work.

## THE ROLE:

The Municipal Assessment Agency is seeking a Management Analyst II (Continuous Improvement & Internal Audit) within the Continuous Improvement & Client Services Division.

Reporting to the Director, Continuous Improvement & Client Services, this position supports the Agency's continuous improvement and internal audit functions. The role is responsible for assisting with the development and execution of audit plans, conducting audit research and data analysis, maintaining audit schedules, and preparing comprehensive audit reports. The position also supports the identification and implementation of continuous improvement opportunities through process analysis, stakeholder engagement, and performance measurement.

## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

## Internal Audit

• Plan, coordinate, and complete internal process and policy audits in accordance with established audit schedules.

• Participate in pre-audit and post-audit meetings, collaborating with stakeholders to discuss audit plans, findings, recommendations, and continuous improvement opportunities.

• Review process documentation and develop audit plans to assess compliance with approved policies, procedures, and process requirements.

• Conduct research and perform data collection, sampling, testing, and analysis to evaluate process effectiveness and levels of compliance.

• Execute audit testing activities in accordance with audit plans and quality assurance standards.

• Prepare audit reports, findings, and recommendations to support compliance, risk mitigation, and continuous process improvement.

## Continuous Improvement

• Support the development and implementation of internal controls, risk assessments, assurance plans, and Continuous Improvement initiatives.

• Document and map business processes, facilitate focus groups, and collaborate with stakeholders to identify and validate process improvement opportunities.

• Analyze business processes, conduct root cause analyses, and recommend solutions to improve efficiency, effectiveness, and quality controls.

• Develop and implement data collection methodologies, performance measures, and key metrics to monitor organizational performance and Continuous Improvement outcomes.

• Design, administer, and analyze surveys and other data-gathering tools, compiling results in tracking tools and spreadsheets to support decision-making and performance measurement.

• Analyze qualitative and quantitative data to identify trends, risks, inefficiencies, and opportunities for improvement.

• Prepare reports, presentations, and recommendations for management, and support the implementation and monitoring of improvement initiatives.

## SCREENING CRITERIA:

• An undergraduate degree in Business Administration or Commerce (equivalencies will be considered)

• Experience in business process auditing and process mapping tools and techniques

• Experience developing reports, presentations, and recommendations for management

• Experience collaborating with stakeholders

## ASSESSMENT CRITERIA:

• Knowledge of process auditing and process mapping tools and techniques

• Proficiency with information management and reporting systems

• Ability to effectively exchange information

• Ability to manage time and tasks and work independently

• Ability to think critically

• Stakeholder engagement skills

• Attention to detail and analytical skills

• Professionalism

SALARY: CG-30 ($51,615 - $57,330 per annum) as per the NAPE GS Collective Agreement (classification under review)

CLOSING DATE: Sunday, October 4th

Applications, quoting competition number MAA.MAII.11.2026, must be submitted to careers@maa.ca

Job Summary
This position works within the Nurse Practitioner’s (NP) scope of practice in the following stream of practice: Family/All Ages or Adult. This is an advance practice role providing professional, analytical and an autonomous comprehensive range of health services to clients and patients including but not limited to health assessments and diagnosis diseases, disorders, injuries and conditions, treating and managing acute and chronic illnesses and identifying health risks and needs within a holistic model.

This is an advanced nursing position that involves the planning and provision of both generalized and advanced nursing services. The NP will provide comprehensive care to clients using principles of primary health care within a health promotion, population health and self-help framework. This work involves treating those requiring medical withdrawal management involving withdrawal protocols. In the provision of comprehensive primary health care services, the NP collaborates with an interdisciplinary heath care team including community physicians.

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Constantly moves, lifts, or operates equipment/machinery up to 10 lbs. and regularly is required to lift/move equipment, books and supplies, up to 25 lbs.
Occasionally, may have to reposition a patient over 50 lbs.
Physical effort also includes regular sitting to conduct patient histories, performing work on the computer and when assessing patients, regularly stands or walks.
When performing procedures, regularly uses fine finger/precision work and hand tools (i.e. medical instruments, computer mouse, stethoscope, dopplers, etc.) requiring accurate control and steadiness.
Visual concentration is required when performing physical assessment and procedures, completing charts/reports, observing patients, reading equipment/monitors, and completing work-related correspondence on the computer.

Job Qualifications
Completion of an approved/recognized Nurse Practitioner program is required.
Current and continuing registration with the Newfoundland and Labrador College of Nurses (NLCN) and Licensed (or eligible for licensure) as a Nurse Practitioner (Family/All Ages or Adult) with the NLCN.
A minimum of five years clinical experience in the last seven in mental health and/or addictions is required.
Current BCLS Certification is required.
Possessed strong abilities in the areas of collaboration, clinical reasoning, professional development, interpersonal effectiveness, conflict management and teamwork.
Demonstrated progressive clinical leadership skills.
Possessed strong communication, problem solving, decision-making, and teaching skills.
Demonstrated ability to function autonomously in an advanced practice role.
Support and participate in research to improve practice and client outcomes.
Demonstrated skills in computer and database management skills.
A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required.

If no applicants have the required experience in mental health, applicants with experience in other areas will be considered.

The philosophy of a Family Care Team (FCT) is to deliver care that is patient-centered, comprehensive, team-based, culturally safe, coordinated, accessible, and focused on quality and safety. This philosophy supports providers and care teams to meet clients where they are using an inter-professional collaborative approach where care is provided in the right place, at the right time, by the right provider in a manner that best suits the client’s need. The team will ensure clients are treated with respect, dignity, and compassion, and enable strong and trusting relationships with providers and staff. FCT’s will enable the delivery of a range of quality care for clients within their own communities while facilitating interdisciplinary work amongst healthcare providers. This position will support the FCT for the Coast of Bays area. There is also housing available for this position.

## Definition of work:

As part of the collaborative team, the Nurse Practitioner will be expected to practice to their full scope of practice in order to provide comprehensive assessment and care to clients and provide clinic leadership. The FCT aims to provide continuity of care to improve health outcomes and quality of life through client attachment and client paneling to clinic providers, with the support and wrap around services of the full team. The successful applicant works independently in diagnosing conditions, prescribing medications, performing or ordering diagnostic tests and treatments, evaluating treatments and providing follow-up care in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team. The Nurse Practitioner provides comprehensive and holistic nursing care to clients including health promotion, injury and illness treatment and prevention, supportive, curative and rehabilitative care in a primary care practice setting. The Nurse Practitioner will document using the Electronic Medical Record (EMR). In this leadership role, the Nurse Practitioner will contribute to the ongoing program development, implementation, and evaluation of the FCT including client and clinician engagement. The role will encompass participating in clinic evaluations and continuous quality improvement processes based upon current best practice guidelines. Flexible hours are required (combination of days, evenings, and weekends required). The Nurse Practitioner will report to the Regional Director of Primary Health Care & Community Nursing in the Central Zone.

As an advanced practitioner, the Nurse Practitioner functions in the roles of practitioner, educator and leader. As governed by provincial regulations, he/she practices independently, collaborating with the primary care physicians in the area for issues outside the Nurse Practitioner scope of practice. Travel throughout the region may be required. The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

## Required qualifications:

• Graduation from a Nurse Practitioner program approved by Central Health.

• Current registration as a Nurse Practitioner with the Association of Registered Nurses of Newfoundland and Labrador.

• Current BLS certification.

• Demonstrated knowledge of home and community health services.

• Demonstrated exceptional leadership qualities and problem-solving skills as well as oral and written communication skills.

• Demonstrated ability to work well independently and in an interdisciplinary team environment.

• A valid Newfoundland and Labrador Class 5 Driver’s License.

• Consistent demonstration of NLHS core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position.

• A satisfactory Certificate of Conduct from the RCMP or local police authority.

## Preferred Qualifications:

• Demonstrated skill in using health care-based computer systems (CRMS, Meditech, EMR).

• Experience in the care and management of patients with diabetes, COPD, heart failure, and/or mental health disorders is an asset.

• Experience working in a Primary Health Care setting is an asset.

* Electronic Medical Records (EMR) training is required and will be provided upon hire.

Our team is seeking an Advanced Care Paramedic for a full-time position. If there are no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics (PCP). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic.
If the competition is awarded to a PCP as the next highest classification, they will be awarded as temporary full time (TFT) and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.
The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.
The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.
The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required. \

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP or PCP;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

ABOUT NLHS
NL Health Services offers the full continuum of health and community services including public health, long-term care, community services, hospital care and unique provincial programs and services. NL Health Services prides ourselves on providing the highest quality care and service possible to the people in our communities, in our region, and in the province. To do that, we employ qualified, competent, and caring individuals who are dedicated to their professions and to our vision of Healthy People, Healthy Communities.

ABOUT CENTRAL ZONE
Central Zone is the second largest health zone in Newfoundland and Labrador Health Services, serving approximately 90,000 people (17 per cent of the province’s population) living in 176 communities. With a geographical area encompassing more than half the total land mass of the island, the Central region extends from Charlottetown in the east, Fogo Island in the north, Harbour Breton in the south, to Baie Verte in the west. Central Zone provides a variety of primary, secondary, long-term care, community health, and other enhanced secondary services.

JOB SUMMARYNL Health Services Central Zone invites applications from Family Physicians to join the Family Care Team Program in a full-time salaried position in the Coast of Bays Region.

NLHS is pleased to support Family Care Team in achieving its goals of providing exceptional and high-quality care to patients in the Central region. The Family Care Team (FCT) mandate is to provide patients without a primary care provider with access to primary health care services. Services will be provided using an inter-professional collaborative approach where patients will see the right provider at the right time and right place. The team may include physicians, NPs, RNs including diabetic nurse educator, clerical supports, LPNs, pharmacists, social workers, dietitian, physiotherapist and occupational therapist. All health care providers, including physicians, will be expected to practice to their full scope of practice to meet patient needs and requirements. The FCT aims to provide continuity of care to improve health outcomes and patients’ quality of life.

We are seeking physicians to manage a roster of patients in addition to supporting the work at the Category B Facility within the community. Additional support of other services, such as Long-Term Care and Personal Care Home services, is also part of the responsibilities as part of the team supporting that facility. Our ideal candidates will have a strong patient focus and excellent communication skills with a keen interest in practicing in a collaborative team approach. Hours of work may need flexibility to offer clinics during the daytime or coverage of Category B Emergency. After hours and/or weekend coverage may be required. The successful Physicians will provide care using the EMR platform.

See more information on the Family Care Teams by visiting Family Care Teams NL - Home Page

Our team is seeking an Advanced Care Paramedic for a full-time position. If there are no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics (PCP) and Ambulance Operators/Attendants (also known as Emergency Medical Responder (EMR)). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to a PCP or EMR as the next highest classification, they will be awarded as temporary full time (TFT) and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

Job Summary:
The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of Emergency Services. The primary base for this service is located in located in Happy Valley-Goose Bay/Sheshatshiu, NL.

Duties/Job Demands:
The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will aid the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

Job Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;

• Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director

1888637.title: Aircraft Maintenance Engineer (AME M1/M2 or Military equivalent)
1888637.description:
Requisition ID: 554

Why Choose IMP Aerospace & Defence:
IMP Aerospace & Defence's Canadian Search and Rescue Helicopter program has provided all aspects of support to Canada's fleet of Cormorant Search and Rescue (SAR) CH-149 helicopters for over twenty years. Operating from across Canada at three Main Operating Bases, Gander NL, Greenwood, NS, and Comox, BC and headquartered in the Cormorant Support Centre in Halifax, NS, the program provides comprehensive, turnkey In-Service Support to Canada's Cormorant helicopters. This unique program provides the RCAF with a full suite of all levels of support to this critical 24/7/365 mission.

Position Overview:
The Aircraft Maintenance Engineer performs first and second line aircraft maintenance on the Cormorant Helicopter in support of our Canadian Search and Rescue operations. Duties include servicing, inspection, removal, cleaning, repair, installation, adjustment, flight testing and certification (release) of aircraft mechanical, structural and electrical systems and components and ground support equipment.

What You Will Do:
• Perform First and Second Level maintenance on aircraft mechanical, structural and electrical systems and components, and ground support equipment.

• Ramp duties will include but not be limited to pre/post flight inspection and support, marshalling, parking, towing, fueling/defueling and installation/removal of required mission equipment and crash and salvage response.

• Perform ground runs of auxiliary power units, where qualified and authorized.

• Fly as necessary in support of maintenance, ferry and deployment operations

• Travel and work at other main operating bases, deployments in support of operations at remote sites, mobile repair parties and ferry flights.

• Provide on-the-job-training to other employees.

• Attend training for trade and personnel development and for qualifications, recertification, and authorization purposes.

• Sweep and clean hangar, shop, stores and office areas, remove all debris accumulated by tasks performed and maintain a clean, safe work area.

• Adhere to policies, procedures and directives established by the Company.

• Provide supervision to other employees.

• Perform other tasks as may be required from time to time.

What You Will Bring:
• Graduate of a recognized aircraft maintenance course or apprenticeship program and hold a current Aircraft Maintenance Engineers license or be qualified as an aircraft aviation technician within the Canadian Armed Forces or equivalent commercial experience.

• A minimum of 3 years' experience in aviation maintenance is required.

• Thorough knowledge of aircraft systems, including, but not limited to, power plants, flight controls, dynamic systems, hydraulics, pneumatics, environmental, basic structures and power generation and distribution systems.

• Knowledge of use of special tools and equipment.

• Knowledge of corrosion control techniques.

• Capable of reading and interpreting technical documentation such as maintenance manuals, work packages, drawings, blueprints and Standard Plant Procedures.

• Capable of performing Non-destructive Inspection.

• Ability to use standard computer programs and such specialized ones as may be necessary in the performances of the duties.

• Valid Class 5 Drivers License, with the ability to drive vehicles, tow tractors and support vehicles.

• Must be eligible to meet requirements for Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP), and Secret Level II Security Clearance through PSPC- Contract Security Program.

What We Will Do For You:
• All of IMP's benefits become effective on your first day of work, regardless of your position

• We offer a comprehensive Benefits Package, including RRSP Program

• Climate controlled workspace

• All tools and necessary PPE provided by IMP

• Free parking onsite

• Attractive working hours

• Tuition Reimbursement Program

• Long Service Awards

• Volunteer Grant Program

• Scholarship Program

IMP is committed to Employment Equity and our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative at all job levels. We welcome applicants from Indigenous People, Visible Minority Groups, Persons with Disabilities and Women in occupations or positions where they are under-represented. If you are a member of one of these equity groups, you are encouraged to self identify on either your cover letter or resume.

COMPANY/CLIENT: Puglisevich on behalf of Odfjell Drilling

CONTACT: careers@puglisevich.com

REPORTS TO: Offshore Installation Manager
