ROTATION: Equal Rotation

TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT: Contract, Full Time

CONTRACT: Long Term Contract; Estimate 400 Days + 300 Day Option

NUMBER OF POSITIONS: Four (4)

## JOB SUMMARY:

• Manage the deck department and bridge/control room and monitor that the operations are conducted in a safe manner according to plans and procedures.

• Actively follow up the ongoing operation in the field.

• The MSL is the Chief Officer of the unit and has the responsibilities and authority as outlined in maritime legislation and international conventions.

• Ensure that all equipment and systems in own department are maintained, functioning and in accordance with COF/OA and current regulations.

• Operational responsible person for lifting operations on the unit; ref. applicable national regulation and standards. Responsible for the unit's stability, and to ensure that stability calculations are up to date.

• OIM's deputy.

• Ship security officer and responsible for safety equipment.

## PRE-REQUISITES/QUALIFICATIONS:

• High School Diploma or Equivalent

• Canadian Barge Supervisor License MOU Surface or STCW Equivalent

• Canadian Chief Mate License MOU Surface or STCW Equivalent

• 1 year experience as a Marine Section Leader on a 6th Generation Ultra-Deepwater Semi-Submersible

• 1.5 years experience as a Dynamic Positioning Operator on a 6th Generation Ultra-Deepwater Semi-Submersible

• 5 years previous experience in a role on a 6th Generation Ultra-Deepwater Semi-Submersible

• 4 years experience from Posmoor ATA operations on Semi-Submersible

• DP Unlimited Certificate

• Structured and organized mindset

• High level of integrity

• Analytical ability

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English

• Must pass Physical, Drug Screen and Background/Pre-Employment Screening Checks

## DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Leadership:

• Supervise the marine operations in accordance with Odfjell's vision and values.

• Through delegation oversee operational planning and execution of lifting operations on the unit. Day to day planning and execution of lifting operations is delegated to the supervisors leading work in the different areas/departments on the unit: Drilling Section Leader, Toolpusher, Technical Section Leader and Assistant Technical Section Leader.

• Secure and monitor good working environment.

• Cooperate with other departments and third parties.

• Promote Odfjell's values and a just culture.

• Set the standard for tidiness and cleanliness and ensure compliance.

• Know your crews, and how they relate to each other.

• Ensure that all are familiar with the operational plans and own tasks.

• Act upon unsatisfactory behaviours and/or crew compositions.

• Assign tasks to members of the deck department.

• Correct unacceptable behaviour.

• Nominate candidates for promotion.

Competence:

• Ensure that the Competence Assurance System is functioning.

• Promote on the job training on all levels in own department.

• Identify and follow up deviations from Odfjell's competence requirements in own department.

• Ensure that all personnel conducting any work within own department are qualified.

• Ensure that the crews are trained to handle emergency situations (e.g. well control, fire, loss of position, heavy weather, etc.)

• Nominate candidates for external training/education.

• Restrict access to perform any work within own department based on complexity and competence evaluation.

• Plan and conduct regular emergency drills in accordance to drill matrix.

Operations:

• Organize and follow-up daily and long-term operations and ensure availability of required equipment ready for use within own department.

• Ensure detailed planning in accordance with requirements and that operations within own department are conducted in accordance with valid requirements, procedures, and plans.

• Ensure that stability and ballast operations are conducted in accordance with valid requirements and procedures.

• Ensure that structural loads on the unit are within acceptable limits during any operations.

• Keep track of all loading and unloading of cargo and conduct daily stability calculations.

• Ensure that required logbooks within one's department are maintained.

• Perform navigation and conduct navigational watches.

• Instruct DP operators, Control Room Operators and deck crew and relieve the DPO/CRO as required.

• Spend time in the field and monitor daily operation.

• Cooperate with other departments, customer and third parties.

• Report non-compliances to the OIM.

• Stop any operation if considered unsafe.

• Emergency duties according to the unit's emergency organization.

Equipment and systems:

• Organize and follow-up on daily and long-term maintenance within own department.

• Ensure updated documentation, procedures and instructions on equipment and systems within own department are available.

• Ensure that marine equipment and systems are correctly set-up and operated in a proper manner within operating limits and procedures.

• Ensure that maintenance is carried out on all systems and equipment according to the maintenance system.

• Keep workplace and work areas in a tidy condition at all times.

Cold Ocean Salmon Inc., a division of Cooke Aquaculture Inc., a dynamic and growing east coast family company with Platinum Member status in the Canada's Best Managed Companies Program, is offering a unique opportunity for a highly motivated individual to join the company's team as Contract Saltwater Aquaculture Worker.

## Responsibilities:

• Configure, deploy, and maintain multi-site networking across global sites.

• Configure, deploy, and maintain network equipment and connectivity such as firewalls, Switches/Routers, VPN, and Wi-Fi infrastructure.

• Ensuring compliance through network device lifecycles, hardware refresh, and firmware updates.

• University degree or college diploma in Computer Science or related field.

• 5+ years experience providing enterprise / large network support and implementation.

• Extensive experience with network and routing protocols such as VRFs, NAT, OSPF, BGP, IPsec, L2 WAN, QoS, VLANs, multicast, private and public addressing.

• Strong experience with networking systems: LAN, switches, routers, protocols, firewalls, VPN, wireless networks, security appliances, and network access security.

• Experience with virtual networking technologies: firewalls, VRTR, vswitch

• Experience with WAN technologies such as VPLS, VXLAN, VPN, site-to-site networking.

• Experiencing working with Palo Alto firewalls, Aruba switches and Aruba wireless, Cisco Meraki, Cisco Nexus and Catalyst switches, and Ubiquiti Wireless.

• Experience administrating and supporting a Microsoft Windows environment, VMWare, Network/Server administration and application support.

• Experience with network architecture and design.

• Excellent customer service skills and communication skills.

## About NLHC

The Newfoundland and Labrador Housing Corporation (NL Housing) is a crown corporation whose mandate is to develop and administer housing assistance policy and programs for the benefit of low to moderate income households throughout the province. As the largest landlord in the Province, NL Housing manages a portfolio of over 5,500 units province-wide. The services provided by NL Housing provide clients with access to safe, stable and affordable housing, which is essential to the social, financial, and physical well-being of individuals, families and communities. There is a wide range of housing needs across the province, from those facing homelessness or at risk of homelessness, to low income households needing assistance to pay rent or complete much-needed repairs on their homes. For more information on our programs and services, and strategic priorities, please visit our website www.nlhc.nl.ca.

## About the Department/Region

Context: The Human Resources Department is responsible for planning, directing and implementing the various human resources policies, procedures, and programs in support of the organization's mandate. The department provides support, interpretation, and advice to departments, regional offices, and senior management in the areas of employee relations, staffing, job evaluation, compensation, staff development, safety, payroll and benefits administration.

## Position Details

Competition Number:2026/27-046-650071P

Employment Type: Permanent

Department/Region: Human Resources

Location: Head Office, St. John's

Posting Status: Internal/External

Closing Date: September 28th, 2026

Salary Scale: $76,087 to $101,767 per annum on the Management Pay Plan

587 Points, 35-hour work week

Duties: Reporting to the Director, Human Resources the Manager, Occupational Health and Safety will develop, implement, and maintain an Occupational Health and Safety (OH&S) Program to ensure a safe work environment and compliance with provincial OH&S legislation. As the Corporation's primary OH&S resource, the incumbent will provide guidance and support to safety officers, managers and employees, in fulfilling their legislated responsibilities as prescribed by the OH&S Act of Newfoundland and Labrador. This position will work with safety officers to develop safe work practices as required based on job hazard assessments. The incumbent will conduct needs assessments to identify training requirements and develop and deliver training that cannot be outsourced. The incumbent will ensure all workplace incidents are reported to WorkplaceNL in accordance with legislation, regulations and reporting requirements. The incumbent will be an active member of the emergency management committee and will act as the lead fire warden chairing the Fire Warden Committee. The position will monitor OH&S performance through data analysis of incident, injury and illness to enable the provision of quarterly and annual reports. The incumbent is also responsible for OH&S programs related to safety orientation. The role demands a high degree of independence, working closely with NLHC stakeholders, Workplace NL (to meet PRIME incentive requirements) and external safety organizations.

## Screening Criteria

Completion of post-secondary degree and/or diploma in Occupational Health and Safety, Safety Technology, Environmental Health, or a related field (equivalencies may be considered)

Experience developing OH&S programs and related policies and procedures

Experience conducting hazard assessments, workplace inspections, and accident/incident investigations

Experience in emergency planning and response coordination

Experience using a Human Resource Information System (HRIS) for data collection, record keeping and statistical analysis

Experience with PRIME requirements through Workplace NL and understanding of NL Provincial OH&S legislation (asset)

## Assessment Criteria

Knowledge of OH&S legislation, safety standards (e.g., CSA, ANSI), and best practices

Proficiency conducting safety audits, inspections and accident investigations

Ability to develop and manage OH&S programs, policies and procedures

Ability to develop, conduct and source training

Analytical skills for data analysis and reporting on safety statistics

Ability to promote a safety-focused culture, transitioning from reactive to proactive practice

Ability to work independently while maintaining time and tasks

Decision making skills, a proactive approach to problem solving and risk management

Ability to effectively exchange information

Stakeholder engagement and client service orientation

## Conditions of Employment

Conditions of Offer:

Acceptable Certificate of Conduct

Conditions of Acceptance

Acknowledges the requirement for travel (occasional)

Acknowledges requirement to carry a corporate smart phone

Acknowledges the requirement for overnight travel (occasional)

Acknowledges requirement for use of a private vehicle (with business insurance)

## Golf Professional - St. John's

Higher Talent is seeking an experienced and customer-focused Golf Professional to lead the day-to-day golf operations at GlenDenning Golf Course in St. John's. Reporting to the General Manager, the Golf Professional will oversee all aspects of golf operations, including the Pro Shop, tournaments, leagues, golf instruction, merchandising, practice facilities, and member services.

The successful candidate will play a key leadership role in delivering an exceptional golf experience by managing staff, developing instructional programs, coordinating tournaments and member events, and driving player engagement through innovative programming and community outreach. This individual will also collaborate closely with the General Manager to support marketing initiatives, enhance the club's online presence, and promote GlenDenning as a premier golf destination.

## The Job

• Responsible for the overall day to-day operations and services of the golf course, including the Pro Shop, leagues, tournaments, practice facilities and cart fleet.

• Responsible for the coordination of golf instruction, golf schools, tournaments, and golf merchandising.

• Working with the GM, coordinate marketing programs to promote GlenDenning's services to potential players and oversee member events and daily play.

• Work with the GM to create content and keep the website and social media platforms updated and informative.

• Perform other duties as directed by the GM.

• Must be CPGA certified and be trained from a recognized Post Secondary Institution.

## Golf Operations

• Enforce all operational rules and policies governing the use of the golf course and practice facility.

• Operate and maintain a reputable golf instruction business and practice range, staffed with competent personnel.

• Facilitate the operation of a handicap system for all golfers.

• Develop a program to attract new golfers and guests, through golf instruction and player development.

• Maintain a close working relationship with the Course Superintendent and maintenance staff.

• Maintain a close working relationship with all managers. Attend regular meetings for updates on tournaments, group bookings, events, and golf.

• Handle specific complaints in all areas of golf operations and regularly report to the GM.

•

## Pro Shop Operations

• Hire, manage, train, schedule and supervise Pro Shop Staff, Back Shop Staff, Marshalls, Starters, etc. in the day to-day performance of their jobs.

• Become very knowledgeable with the Company's operating software and be able to train staff in its use.

• Maintain the online store including fulfilling online orders.

• Order inventory and sell merchandise in the Pro Shop, featuring quality merchandise.

• Ensure Pro Shop is always staffed and properly maintained in a clean and presentable condition.

• Provide a profitable and efficient merchandising plan, ensuring minimum inventory levels and maximum profits.

• Order and maintain merchandise levels to meet customer demands.

• Ensure proper controls are in place for the order, delivery, receiving and stocking of merchandise; supervise weekly and monthly physical inventories of merchandise.

• Coordinate product promotions, instore displays, etc.

• Stay current with golf markets trends in fashion and product.

• Create material to display golf course policies and rules.

• Ensure the proper ordering and stocking of pro shop staples such as scorecards, pencils, forms, ball mark repair tools, cart keys and tags.

• Perform club repair, custom fitting, and club regripping.

## Tournament & League Operations

• Responsible for all, Club Member Events and Tournaments

• Develop and administer tournament activities, in collaboration with the Managers.

• Be present at the tournaments to greet organizers and golfers and to provide general support to golf operations staff as required.

• Responsible for the organization, execution, and communication for the following: Ladies' League & Men's League

• Other events that will be the full responsibility of the Golf Pro and are as follows: Club Championship & Members Day

• Must work closely with the GM to obtain new sponsors for specific events and tournaments.

## Golf Academy Operations

• Familiar and trained in the CPGA First Tee program

• Develop programs for teaching golfers of all skill levels.

• Administer and develop weekly clinics for men, women, and junior golfers.

• Develop a local junior program.

• Create material for integrated marketing of GlenDenning golf academy.

• Develop and create instructional booklets for new students.

• Responsible for recruiting teaching assistants and volunteers.

• Responsible for all golf academy operations from setup to execution and administration.

• Approach possible sponsors during the offseason to work with GlenDenning in the development of junior programs and golf schools.

• Provide community outreach through area schools and other social programs to promote GlenDenning Golf and its programs.

Brendan Hagerty | Vice President & General Manager | brendan@highertalent.caHigher Talent | www.jumpcareers.ca

Job Summary
As a member of an interdisciplinary team, the Nurse Practitioner provides quality care to clients of the Family Care Team, providing services to residents in the Clarenville region, with potential service to alternate sites using a hub and spoke model. The principles of the Family Care Team align with the patient health home model of care; using a collaborative health care team approach, from various health disciplines, in the provision of primary health care services.
This position works within the Nurse Practitioner's (NP) scope of practice in the following category of practice: (Family/All Ages). This is an advance practice role providing professional, analytical and an autonomous comprehensive range of health services to clients and patients including but not limited to health assessments and diagnosis diseases, disorders, injuries and conditions; treating and managing acute and chronic illnesses and identifying health risks and needs within a holistic model. The NP in this position may complete home visits and provide virtual care.

The Family Care Team mandate is to provide patients without a primary care provider of the Clarenville region with access to health care services. Services will be provided using an inter-professional collaborative approach where patients will see the right provider at the right time and right place. All health care providers, including NPs, will be expected to practice to their full scope of practice in order to meet patient needs and requirements. The Family Care Team aims to provide continuity of care to improve health outcomes and patient quality of life through patient attachment and patient paneling to individual NPs, with the support and wrap around services of the full team. Flexible hours may be required (Combination of days, evenings, and weekends required).

This position reports to the Regional Primary Health Care Program Manager responsible for the service.

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Constantly moves, lifts, or operates equipment/machinery up to 10 lbs. and regularly is required to lift/move equipment, books, supplies, and sometimes children up to 25 lbs. (may need to be deleted or added depending on the position). Occasionally, may have to reposition a patient over 50 lbs.
Physical effort also includes regular sitting to conduct patient histories, performing work on the computer and when assessing patients, regularly stands or walks.
When performing procedures, regularly uses fine finger/precision work and hand tools (i.e. medical instruments, computer mouse, stethoscope, dopplers, etc.) requiring accurate control and steadiness.
Visual concentration is required when performing physical assessment and procedures, completing charts/reports, observing patients, reading equipment/monitors, and completing work-related correspondence on the computer.

Completion of an approved/recognized Nurse Practitioner program is required.
Current registration with the College of Registered Nurses of NL and Licensed (or eligible for licensure) as a Nurse Practitioner (Family/All Ages) with the CRNNL.

The Occupational Therapist II is an integral member of the Flexible Assertive Community Treatment Team (FACT) that provides intensive mobile services to individuals with severe and persistent mental illness and concurrent related complexities of mental health issues/disorders. The Occupational Therapist II is responsible for the development, organization and implementation of vocational and career development strategies, assessing overall client functioning and implementing strategies to improve functioning in activities of daily living. ## ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

NL Health Services – Eastern Rural Zone has two (2) full-time Emergency Medicine positions available at Carbonear General Hospital in Carbonear, NL. These positions are fee-for-service and available immediately.

ER shifts are allocated in an equitable and predictable templated format. Emergency MD shifting is solo, with ER Nurse Practitioner support from 8:00am–4:00pm on weekdays. Second Emergency MD shifting is also utilized during peak periods. The position involves a minimum of 13 shifts per month — day shifts are 10 hours (8:00am–6:00pm) and night shifts are 14 hours (6:00pm–8:00am).

Core generalist specialty support resources are in place. A dedicated portable ultrasound is based in the ER and 24-hour emergent CT scanning is available on site. Specialty services include Anesthesia, General Surgery, Orthopedics, Obstetrics/Gynecology, Internal Medicine, Psychiatry, Pediatrics, Family Medicine (Hospitalist), and 24-hour Emergency coverage. ## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification;

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete;

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

Definition of Work:
Work involves providing nursing care and treatment services for the physically ill, disabled and/or cognitively impaired clients under the direction of a Registered Nurse. The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

Physical Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
• Constantly moves/lifts up to 10-15lbs, regularly moves/lifts up to 50lbs; required to restrain/reposition/move/lift up to, or above, 50lbs with co-worker assistance and repetitively required to complete pushing/pulling with medium force (22-44lbsF).
• Constantly stands/walks. May work in awkward or cramped positions to assist with care. Work repetitively involves reaching/stretching, bending/twisting and repeated bouts of low-level postures such as squatting, crouching or stooping.
• Potential for exposure to blood, bodily fluids and/or other contagion. May be exposed to patients/residents with potential risk for aggressive behavior.
• Work Environments present potential for exposure to scented/chemical products and/or other allergens within publicly accessible areas.

Required qualifications:
• Graduation from a practical nursing program approved by Central Health.
• Current BLS certification.
• Current registration with the College of Licensed Practical Nurses of Newfoundland and Labrador.
• Demonstrated effective interpersonal and communication skills.
• Consistent demonstration of NLHS core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (I CARE)
• Demonstrated competency in working to the full scope of practice (as per the CLPNNL and Central Health’s policies and procedures) and standards of care relevant to designated client population.
• Completion of other skills and post basic competencies as required.
• Work collaboratively as a member of an interdisciplinary care team and support the Registered Nurse in caring for clients with unpredictable outcomes as required.
• Work under the direction of a Registered Nurse for patients where the acuity or complexity of care requires an advanced level of knowledge and skill beyond the scope of practice for Licensed Practical Nurses.
• Completion of Central Health's Admissions Module for LPNs, or willingness to complete prior to commencement of the position.
• Completion of Central Health's Peripherally Inserted Catheters (PICC) Module for LPNs, or willingness to complete prior to commencement of the position.
• Demonstrated proficiency in Wound Care Management and Medication Administration including IM, IV and subcutaneous injections.
• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position.
• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority.

Preferred Qualifications:
• Experience in licensed practical nursing.

Job Summary
The Nurse Practitioner (NP) in the Community Urgent Care Clinic works within the NP scope of practice in the following category of practice: (Family/All Ages). This is an advanced practice role providing professional, analytical and comprehensive health services to clients/families including, but not limited to, health assessments and diagnoses of diseases, disorders, injuries and conditions, treating and managing acute and chronic illnesses and identifying health risks and needs within a holistic, episodic care model.

The NP works independently in an Urgent Care environment, conducting rapid assessment and diagnosis, which may necessitate individual follow-up at times. This is supported by scheduled, weekly administrative time in order to review results and provide additional client care and necessary follow-up via in-person, telephone or virtual visits. The NP will also work collaboratively with other providers and staff at the clinic. The successful applicant will be supported to become proficient in the use of virtual care technologies.

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Constantly moves, lifts, or operates equipment/machinery up to 10 lbs. and regularly is required to lift/move equipment, books, supplies, and sometimes children up to 25 lbs. Occasionally, may have to reposition a patient over 50 lbs.
Physical effort also includes regular sitting to conduct patient histories, performing work on the computer and when assessing patients, regularly stands or walks.
When performing procedures, regularly uses fine finger/precision work and hand tools (i.e., medical instruments, computer mouse, stethoscope, etc.) requiring accurate control and steadiness.
Visual concentration is required when performing physical assessment and procedures, completing charts/reports, observing patients, reading equipment/monitors, and completing work-related correspondence on the computer.

Job Qualifications
Completion of an approved/recognized Nurse Practitioner program is required.
Current and continuing registration with the Newfoundland and Labrador College of Nurses (NLCN) and Licensed (or eligible for licensure) as a Nurse Practitioner (Adult or Family/All Ages) with the NLCN.
A minimum of five years' nursing experience within the last seven years, including two years' experience working as a Nurse Practitioner in Primary Health Care, Emergency Room, Urgent Care or a similar clinic setting providing care to Family/All Ages, is required.
Current BCLS Certification is required.
Knowledge of urgent care/episodic care model.
Demonstrated exceptional critical thinking and clinical judgement skills.
Possessed strong abilities in the areas of collaboration, clinical reasoning, professional development, interpersonal effectiveness, conflict management and teamwork.
Demonstrated progressive clinical leadership skills.
Possessed strong communication, problem solving, decision-making, and teaching skills.
Demonstrated ability to function autonomously in an advanced practice role.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively within an interprofessional team.
Support and participate in research to improve practice and client outcomes.
Demonstrated skills in computer and database management skills
A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required.

*The successful applicant must complete Electronic Medical Records (EMR) Training at the first available opportunity.

## ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

NL Health Services – Central Zone invites applications from Family Physicians to join the Family Care Team (FCT) Program in a full-time salaried position in the Lewisporte Region.

Central Zone is the second largest health zone in NL Health Services, serving approximately 90,000 people across 176 communities. The region extends from Charlottetown in the east, Fogo Island in the north, Harbour Breton in the south, to Baie Verte in the west — encompassing more than half the total land mass of the island of Newfoundland.

The Family Care Team mandate is to provide patients without a primary care provider with access to primary health care services using an interprofessional collaborative approach, where patients see the right provider at the right time and place. The team may include physicians, Nurse Practitioners, Registered Nurses including a diabetic nurse educator, clerical support, LPNs, pharmacists, social workers, dietitians, physiotherapists, and occupational therapists. All health care providers, including physicians, are expected to practice to their full scope of practice to meet patient needs. The FCT aims to provide continuity of care to improve health outcomes and patients' quality of life.

The successful candidate will manage a roster of patients in addition to supporting work at the Category B facility within the community. Additional support of Long-Term Care and Personal Care Home services is also part of the responsibilities. Hours of work may require flexibility to offer clinics during daytime or coverage of Category B Emergency. After-hours and/or weekend coverage may be required. Care will be provided using the EMR platform.

For more information on the Family Care Teams visit: https://familycareteamsnl.ca/

Job Summary
The Nuclear and Molecular Medicine Technologist III is responsible for the day-to-day operations and implementation of the only Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography (PET/CT) program in Newfoundland & Labrador. This position performs specialized and advanced diagnostic imaging procedures using a PET/CT camera and involves administering radioactive materials and contrast with very specific timing/and flow rates to visualize the anatomical regions that are required. The result is a very detailed image that the Nuclear Medicine Physicians review to determine whether surgical interventions, oncology treatments, or palliative treatments are required. The results of the scans help the Oncologists to treat cancer patients, Cardiologists to treat cardiac patients, Neurologists to diagnose varying neurological conditions, and Internists to treat patients with infections in varying parts of their body. The Nuclear and Molecular Medicine Technologist IIIs are classified as Nuclear Energy Workers (NEW).

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Regularly moves or lifts objects between 10-50+ lbs. such as shielded radioactive sources and lead bricks.
Occasionally pushes and pulls objects or transports patients over 50 lbs. in wheelchairs or stretchers.
Regularly stands, walks, or sits for extended periods to perform activities.
A very high level of alertness and attentiveness is required when performing scans/procedures due to patients' condition, safety and because some scans/procedures are captured in real time.
Regularly performs fine finger/precision computer work; handling of open-source radioactivity and radioactive equipment/components requiring steadiness and accurate movement/control.
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) are a regular requirement, including gloves and gowns.

Job Qualifications
Graduation from a recognized (accredited) program in Nuclear Medicine Technology is required.
Successful completion of the CAMRT Computed Tomography (CT) Imaging or PET/CT Certificate Program is required.
Current registration and member in good standing with the Canadian Association of Medical Radiation Technologists (CAMRT).
Current BLS Certification is required.
Strong understanding of radiation safety procedures and CNSC regulations.
Proven analytical, critical thinking, problem solving, decision-making and organizational skills.
A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required.

* Due to safety requirements this position will rotate through the PET/CT and Nuclear Medicine sections of the Nuclear and Molecular Medicine Division. Please note that shift start and stop times may change subject to operational requirements as the PET/CT program develops.

** The successful applicant must be eligible for Nuclear Energy Worker (NEW) status.

Effective May 1, 2025, all Medical Radiation Technologists and X - Ray Health Professionals will require registration with the Newfoundland and Labrador Council of Health Professionals (NLCHP) in the appropriate discipline(s) in order to practice in Newfoundland and Labrador.

## ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

NL Health Services – Eastern Rural Zone invites applications for two (2) permanent full-time General Internists within the Internal Medicine Program at Dr. G.B. Cross Memorial Hospital in Clarenville, NL.

The successful candidates will work collaboratively with family physicians and other specialists to provide a multidisciplinary approach to patients in clinic settings, consultations, inpatient care, and on-call coverage. Outpatient assessments take place at Dr. G.B. Cross Memorial Hospital and 5 Coish Place, with space shared with other specialists.

The collaborative model of care at Dr. G.B. Cross Memorial Hospital involves the Hospitalist on-call, Inpatient Nurse Practitioner, and Internists. All Internal Medicine and Hospitalist ER consultations are handled by the on-call Internist, who will conduct the initial consultation and outline a treatment plan. The NP and Hospitalist are responsible for all floor issues and rounds, working collaboratively with the Internist. After hours, the Hospitalist is responsible for floor pages. The Internist on-call is responsible for patients admitted until they are handed over to the Hospitalist in the morning. ICU remains the responsibility of the Internist. On-call including holidays and weekends is shared equitably among site General Internists.

Dr. G.B. Cross Memorial Hospital provides services to a catchment area of approximately 20,000 people. The hospital has 41 acute care beds including palliative care, medical/surgical, obstetrics, pediatric, and ICU beds, as well as 9 ER beds and 44 long-term care beds. Services include anesthesia, chemotherapy, family practice, general surgery, gynecology, obstetrics, ICU/Cardiac, internal medicine, laboratory, palliative care, pathology, pediatrics, psychiatry, radiology, respiratory therapy, ultrasonography, and 24-hour emergency (Category A). Visiting clinics include neurology and ophthalmology.

## Work Environment

Clarenville is a vibrant service centre in eastern Newfoundland offering an exceptional quality of life. The town is near a national park, downhill and cross-country ski lodges, two golf courses, and hunting and fishing opportunities. Community amenities include a stadium, swimming pool, theatre, soccer pitch, running track, softball fields, playgrounds, hiking trails, and snowmobile trails. For more information visit: https://clarenville.ca/

## Job Summary:

The Primary Care Paramedic (or Ambulance Operator/Attendant),works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

Duties/Job Demands:
The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

Job Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
* Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;
* Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.
* Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.
* Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

Qualifications:
* Graduation from High School or equivalent;
* Graduation from an approved Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;
* Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as a PCP or EMR;
* Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director
* Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;
* Current certification in Basic Life Support;
* Effective oral and written communication skills;
* Critical and sound decision making skills;
* Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;
* For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.
* A satisfactory record of work performance is required;
* A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

Salary:
* Primary Care Paramedic – CGHSA-29 of the NAPE HS salary scale $32.71 to $37.40 per hour

Competition Number: VAC0020466

Posted Date: 2026-01-20

Closing Date: Open until filled.

Our team is seeking an Advanced Care Paramedic (ACP) for a full-time position. If no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics (PCP) and Ambulance Operators/Attendants/Emergency Medical Responder (EMR). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR).

If the competition is awarded to a PCP or Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) as the next highest classification, they will be awarded as temporary full time (TFT) until the ACP position is filled.

Job Summary
The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of Paramedicine. The base for this service is located at Witless Bay AB Base.

Duties/Job Demands
The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will provide assistance to the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;
• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.
• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.
• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

Qualifications
• Graduation from High School or equivalent;
• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;
• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;
• Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director
• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;
• Current certification in Basic Life Support;
• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);
• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)
• Effective oral and written communication skills;
• Critical and sound decision making skills;
• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;
• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.
• A satisfactory record of work performance is required;
• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

## The Role

Reporting to the Zone COO, the Sr. Director - Primary Health Care and Community Services is a member of the senior leadership team with responsibility for primary care and for improving the value of care. The Sr. Director - Primary Health Care and Community Services is ultimately responsible and accountable for all primary and community care core programs and services within the assigned portfolio for the Zone, which may include, but not limited to: Primary Health/Chronic Diseases, Community Health/Supports, Mental Health and Addictions, Long Term Care, Rural Health and other services, as required by regional operations.

The Sr. Director - Primary Health Care and Community Services will provide leadership on strategic and operational issues in an integrated health service environment ensuring optimum accessibility, efficiency, and effectiveness, while supporting the overall standards, policies, and direction of the Zone. The Sr. Director - Primary Health Care and Community Services has responsibility for implementing an effective quality and safety program within their portfolio. This position works in collaboration with the Sr. Director Hospital and clinical services to support seamless care across the continuum to meet the health care needs of the people of the zone.

The Sr. Director - Primary Health Care and Community Services will have responsibility for areas that include:

• Strategic Leadership: Serving as a member of senior leadership team, leads region-wide strategic planning efforts and addresses organization-wide policy and management issues for the assigned program in alignment with their provincial counterparts. The Sr. Director focuses on mid- to long-term planning activities including annual or triennial strategic planning, in consultation with executive leaders, including the development of goals and objectives that link to the organization's mission and vision; plans, with key providers, and implements an appropriate model of support to patient care; participates in decisions and policymaking, and shares overall accountability with other members of the senior leadership team.

• Service Delivery and Quality Improvement: Responsible for directing and organizing administration, education, and service delivery of Primary Care Services. They have responsibility to develop, implement, and evaluate Primary Care programs and policies to ensure the efficient and effective delivery of these services and an optimized integration of them across the continuum of care. Promotes a high standard of care. Plans, implements, and evaluates the risk management agenda and continuous quality improvement programs and projects within the zone.

• Legislative and Provincial Alignment: The Sr. Director - Primary Health Care and Community Services promotes a high standard of care in the delivery of Primary Care Services, aligning organizational programs and policies to provincial health legislation, as required. They foster the development, implementation, and evaluation of an integrated model through collaborative processes that cross zones and communities.

• Delivery of Services: Ensures the delivery of programs and services that respect the principles of universality, comprehensiveness, and accessibility so that the Zone operational and strategic plans of Zone Health are realized.

• Client and Patient Relationship Management: The Sr. Director - Primary Health Care and Community Services deals directly with patient/family, staff and physician complaints that cannot be resolved at the program/department level.

• Stakeholder Relationship Management: The Sr. Director - Primary Health Care and Community Services represents the zone and work with external stakeholders such as other the Department of Health and Community Services, local community groups and national organizations pertaining to matters within the portfolio. The Sr. Director maintains a relationship with internal stakeholders such as HR, Finance, Hospital and Information System and Internal Credential Management, and other programs and services.

• Talent Management and Employee Engagement: The Sr. Director - Primary Health Care and Community Services provides leadership and mentorship to staff to:

o Promote professional development, staff engagement, and retention.
o Champion a healthy, safe, diverse, and respectful workplace.
o Practices sound human resources management by attracting, recruiting, and retaining high calibre talent.
o Provide ongoing learning and development opportunities.
o Promote teamwork, and ensuring employees have the tools and resources they require to perform at their best.
o Foster the development of others by supporting and promoting the achievement of professional and personal goals and creating a culture of continuous learning.

• Financial Stewardship and Accountability: Develops and oversees the annual operating and capital budget for the portfolio; prepares and reviews funding proposals; recommends the allocation of resources in consideration of the needs of in zone Health and the delivery and delivery of health services.

• Visible Leadership, Partnership and Relationships: Ensures consistent translation of NLHS culture, mission, values, policy, and leadership expectations within the zone. Provides visible and accessible leadership within the Zone. Orchestrates and champions transformational change by actively leading the change process to achieve program goals and objectives while fostering a culture of accountability, responsibility and continuous learning amongst the Leadership team and staff to ensure compliance with national, provincial, and institutional regulations, policies, and directives.

• Transition to Provincial Health Authority: The Sr. Director - Primary Health Care and Community Services will be establishing and supporting a unified provincial system for programs assigned to their portfolio. This will include working with the VP/COOs, Senior Directors and other leaders from across the five regions to amalgamate and integrate existing departments, staff and services, develop provincial policies and standards, increase efficiency, and enhance quality.
Transforming our health system is a collective responsibility. Senior leaders will be expected to play a variety of roles and adapt to changes as we progress through the process of integration. All senior leaders will share responsibility for culture which includes a commitment to safety and physiological wellbeing. Members of the Senior Management Team may be assigned responsibility for programs, departments, or projects within the organization, as determined by the Zonal COO.

## Requirements of the Role

The ideal candidate will draw on 3-5 years of experience at a senior leadership level responsible for one or more clinical care services. Candidates must be able to demonstrate experience in a health system setting. Candidates should have a Bachelor’s Degree in a Health or Business Related Disciple with a masters preferred. The successful candidate will have extensive credentials as a senior administrator, strategist, and policy developer and have exceptional communication skills both with internal and external stakeholders. The individual must also have demonstrated leadership ability, high ethical standards, integrity, effective engagement as a member of a team; the ability to facilitate and lead change; and commitment to the health care community and the organizational development, goals, and objectives of Newfoundland and Labrador Health Services.

The successful candidate is a passionate, empathetic leader with exceptional business acumen, and interpersonal skills, as well as a commitment to the LEADS Framework. They must also demonstrate the key skills, behaviors, abilities, and knowledge outlined in the five domains of the LEADS in a Caring Environment framework.

Our Commitment
Newfoundland and Labrador Health Service?values the diversity of the people it hires and serves. Diversity, inclusion, and belonging at our organization means fostering a workplace in which individual differences are recognized, appreciated, respected, and responded to in ways that fully develop and utilize each person’s talents and strengths.

We are committed to providing a safe, healthy, and inclusive work environment that inspires respect. Newfoundland and Labrador Health Services welcomes applications from women, visible minorities, Indigenous people, persons with disabilities, and LGBTQ2+ persons. We are committed to providing persons with disabilities equal opportunities and standards and goods and services.

Successful candidates will be expected to reside within Central Zone.

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. Our team is seeking an Advanced Care Paramedic for a full-time position. If no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics and Ambulance Operators/Attendants. We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to a PCP or Ambulance Operator/Attendant as the next highest classification, they will be awarded as temporary full time (TFT) for a period of one year, with possibility of extension.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

Duties/Job Demands:
The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will provide assistance to the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

Job Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
* Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;
* Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.
* Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.
* Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

Qualifications:
* Graduation from High School or equivalent;
* Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;
* Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;
* Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director
* Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;
* Current certification in Basic Life Support;
* Current ACLS certification (ACP only);
* Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)
* Effective oral and written communication skills;
* Critical and sound decision making skills;
* Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;
* For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.
* A satisfactory record of work performance is required;
* A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

## Salary:

* Advanced Care Paramedic - CGHSA-37 of the NAPE HS salary scale $39.14 to $46.27 per hour
* Primary Care Paramedic – CGHSA-29 of the NAPE HS salary scale $32.71 to $37.40 per hour

We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP or PCP;

• Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

## Salary:

## Job Summary

Reporting to the Provincial Manager of the Provincial Medical Communications Centre (PMCC), the Clinical Support Paramedic works within the NL Health Services’ PMCC Clinical Hub. This role, in collaboration with the Medical Transport Physician, is responsible for assessing the clinical needs of interfacility emergency and urgent transfers, as well as 911 calls from patients in the community. As the Clinical Hub evolves, so too will the role of the Clinical Support Paramedic, which includes providing clinical advice and triage to both internal and external partners. The position requires the use of professional clinical judgment and active collaboration with clinicians and health care facilities at all levels across Newfoundland and Labrador, in a dynamic, fast paced environment. In addition, the Clinical Support Paramedic contributes to broader initiatives that support the ongoing development and success of both the Clinical Hub and the PMCC program.

## Job Demands

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Occasionally lifts or moves objects weighing less than 25 lbs.

• Regularly required to sit at a workstation for extended periods of time.

• Constantly uses fine finger precision work while working on a computer.

• Higher than normal levels of attentiveness or alertness for the health and safety of others is required at all times.

• Time pressures, interruptions, deadlines and lack of control over work pace are experienced when dealing with medical emergencies, managing competing tasks, while using telephone technologies and entering information into the computer.

## Job Qualifications

• Successful completion of an approved/recognized Advanced Care Paramedic (ACP) program is required.

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP.

• A minimum five years experience, with at least the last three years in a frontline patient care role within a high call-volume, performance-based EMS system, is required.

• A well-established record of clinical competence, including safe, effective, and evidence-based patient care, is required.

• Successful completion of CritiCall aptitude testing is required. Testing will be administered by Human Resources.

• Current certification in ACLS, ATLS, PTLS, and PALS is required. Instructor-level certification is considered an asset.

• Previous training or certification in clinical support roles or critical care paramedicine is considered an asset.

• Emergency Medical Dispatcher (EMD) certification with the International Academy of Emergency Dispatch (IAED) is considered an asset.

• Computer literacy in a Windows environment is required; strong general computer skills are essential to set foundation for competency in Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) and communication center technologies (e.g., telecommunications equipment, audio recorders) is required.

• Excellent interpersonal, leadership, clinical assessment, communication skills (both oral and written) as well as customer service skills are required. Demonstrated commitment to professional conduct and ongoing professional development, including participation in quality improvement initiatives within a system-based care model.

• Familiarity with ground and air ambulance operations, as well as the associated operational and clinical policies, procedures, and protocols relevant to paramedicine and medical transport, is expected.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required.

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

The philosophy of a Family Care Team (FCT) is to deliver care that is patient-centered, comprehensive, team-based, culturally safe, coordinated, accessible, and focused on quality and safety. This philosophy supports providers and care teams to meet clients where they are using an inter-professional collaborative approach where care is provided in the right place, at the right time, by the right provider in a manner that best suits the client’s need. The team will ensure clients are treated with respect, dignity, and compassion, and enable strong and trusting relationships with providers and staff. FCT’s will enable the delivery of a range of quality care for clients within their own communities while facilitating interdisciplinary work amongst healthcare providers. The FCT for the Baie Verte/ Springdale Family Care Team will cover both communities and the surrounding areas. This position will be based in Springdale.

Definition of work:
As part of the collaborative team, the Nurse Practitioner will be expected to practice to their full scope of practice in order to provide comprehensive assessment and care to clients and provide clinic leadership. The FCT aims to provide continuity of care to improve health outcomes and quality of life through client attachment and client paneling to clinic providers, with the support and wrap around services of the full team. The successful applicant works independently in diagnosing conditions, prescribing medications, performing or ordering diagnostic tests and treatments, evaluating treatments and providing follow-up care in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team. The Nurse Practitioner provides comprehensive and holistic nursing care to clients including health promotion, injury and illness treatment and prevention, supportive, curative and rehabilitative care in a primary care practice setting. The Nurse Practitioner will document using the Electronic Medical Record (EMR). In this leadership role, the Nurse Practitioner will contribute to the ongoing program development, implementation, and evaluation of the FCT including client and clinician engagement. The role will encompass participating in clinic evaluations and continuous quality improvement processes based upon current best practice guidelines. Flexible hours are required (combination of days, evenings, and weekends required). The Nurse Practitioner will report to the Regional Director of Primary Health Care & Community Nursing in the Central Zone.
As an advanced practitioner, the Nurse Practitioner functions in the roles of practitioner, educator and leader. As governed by provincial regulations, he/she practices independently, collaborating with the primary care physicians in the area for issues outside the Nurse Practitioner scope of practice. Travel throughout the region may be required. The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

Required qualifications:
• Graduation from a Nurse Practitioner program approved by Central Health.
• Current registration as a Nurse Practitioner with the Association of Registered Nurses of Newfoundland and Labrador.
• Current BLS certification.
• Demonstrated knowledge of home and community health services.
• Demonstrated exceptional leadership qualities and problem-solving skills as well as oral and written communication skills.
• Demonstrated ability to work well independently and in an interdisciplinary team environment.
• A valid Newfoundland and Labrador Class 5 Driver’s License.
• Consistent demonstration of the core values of NL Health Services: Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect, and Excellence (I CARE)
• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position.
• A satisfactory Certificate of Conduct from the RCMP or local police authority.

Preferred Qualifications:
• Demonstrated skill in using health care-based computer systems (CRMS, Meditech, EMR).
• Experience in the care and management of patients with diabetes, COPD, heart failure, and/or mental health disorders is an asset.
• Experience working in a Primary Health Care setting is an asset.

*Electronic Medical Records (EMR) training is required and will be provided upon hire.
