If the competition is awarded to a PCP or EMR as the next highest classification, they will be temporarily awarded the position for the same number of hours indicated above and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will aid the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

## FACILITIES SERVICES TECHNICIAN (BAND LEVEL 3)

This competition may be used to fill identical positions in this unit within three (3) months of the closing date

All qualified employees are welcome to apply, however preference is given to CUPE members

The University will consider applications from qualified permanent staff who may be interested in a temporary assignment, subject to departmental approval

## DUTIES

Reporting to the Laboratory Services Supervisor, the Facilities Services Technician (FST) is responsible, on an after-hours shift basis (nights, weekends, holidays, University closures), for systems monitoring and caretaker work related to the Department of Ocean Sciences' buildings, laboratories, and live animal facilities. The successful candidate will conduct physical rounds to monitor ongoing experiments and equipment to ensure the integrity of experimental parameters and stored samples in cooperation with the Facilities Management utilities annex. The FST will also monitor facility systems via an electronic building information system (EBI) to ensure the integrity of the water supply and various building functions. Other duties include conducting regular and special checks of all live animal holding facilities and laboratories; providing system adjustments and reporting any situations likely to lead to flooding, facility damage, or loss of animals or equipment; detecting electrical interruptions and properly resetting laboratory equipment, ultralow freezers, and water treatment equipment following these events; admitting pass holders to the buildings after hours, reporting after-hours issues to Principal Investigators or designates, Facilities Management, and Department of Ocean Sciences on-call personnel as appropriate; and performing other related duties as required. Weekday overnight shift coverage is 14 hours; weekend shifts are 12 hours; and holiday shifts are 10 hours.

This position will share leave coverage for three full-time with one part-time Facilities Services Technicians for annual, sick, and family leave, statutory holidays, and other University closures.

## QUALIFICATIONS

Experience (minimum 2 years) in the performance of caretaker work in a non-medical research environment, including some experience in the care and handling of live animals; graduation from high school is required; or an equivalent combination of experience and training may be considered. The ability to multi-task and work independently with minimal supervision, effective communication and problem-solving skills, and proficiency with computer use are essential. General knowledge of plumbing, electrical, and mechanical systems would be definite assets.

## CURRENTLY HIRING

Competitive Day Rate-Offshore Newfoundland

Start Date: ASAP

Employment Type: Ad Hoc / Temporary

JOB SUMMARY: Responsible for all tasks and duties of Systems Control / Instrumentation Technician / Electronic Technician discipline including but not limited to, installation or maintaining electrical control and instrumentation systems, i.e. electronics, programmable controllers, telecommunications, transmitters, and hydraulic, pneumatic systems.

## PRE-REQUISITES/QUALIFICATIONS:

• High School Diploma or Equivalent

• Inter-Provincial Journeyman's Certificate (Instrumentation) or Diploma in Instrumentation Technology

• 1+ years previous experience in an Instrumentation/Systems role on an offshore drilling rig

• Previous High Voltage and Low Voltage Experience

• Read and understand electrical drawings, schematics, and diagrams. Able to proficiently use electrical testing meters and equipment. Able to operate software application as applicable to position.

• Good verbal and written communication skills in English

• Must pass Physical, Drug Screen and Background/Pre-Employment Screening Checks

## DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Ensure that all instruments/PLC's/control networks/electrical equipment is maintained and repaired promptly. To investigate defects and submit reports as required

• Maintain a preventative maintenance programme in accordance with the Company's repair and preventative maintenance procedures as directed by immediate supervisor

• Ensure that all equipment under their control complies with statutory requirements and is maintained at all times in a safe condition or is otherwise completely withdrawn from service

• Monitor any instruments/PLC's/electrical equipment supplied by other contractors or sub-contractors to ensure that it is suitable for use

• Plan maintenance and repair tasks so as to minimize the effect on the drilling operation

• Carry out tasks as part of a multi-discipline maintenance team as operational requirements dictate

• Ability to read, update or modify any drawings, sketches or information on existing and replacement equipment as required or provides such information to management

• Other duties as required

The above is intended as a summary of the key requirements for the position and is not intended to be a complete list of all duties and responsibilities.

It is the objective of Puglisevich to ensure employment equity within the workplace. We encourage applications from Indigenous peoples, visible minorities, women, and persons with disabilities having the capability, qualifications, and experience to make application for this position. Qualified residents in Newfoundland and Labrador will be given first consideration in the staffing of these positions.

## ABOUT NL HEALTH SERVICES

We are a provincial health authority responsible for delivering quality health care to approximately 550,000 people in Newfoundland and Labrador. Supported by over 23,000 employees and physicians, our team works together to improve the health and well-being of every person, in every community. Guided by the vision of the Health Accord NL, we offer a range of health-care programs and services through a wide network of facilities, clinics, and community services across five zones: Central, Eastern-Rural, Eastern-Urban, Labrador-Grenfell, and Western.

At NL Health Services, we believe that our people — employees, doctors and volunteers — make it a great place to work. Every individual brings valuable knowledge, experience and perspective. It is in this diversity that we find strength. We are committed to embracing the distinct and complementary characteristics of our members, as we seek to eliminate health disparities, and ensuring we provide fair, equitable and quality health care to everyone.

If you are passionate about making a difference and providing exceptional health care, we want to hear from you. Join our team and be part of something extraordinary.

????????????????????????????????????????

## ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

The Surgical Services Perioperative Program of NL Health Services – Eastern Urban Zone invites applications for a full-time Cardiac Anesthesiologist at Health Sciences Centre in St. John's, NL, with a start date of June 20, 2026.

The successful candidate will join a group of six (6) Cardiac Anesthesiologists at HSC, working with the entire group of 22 Anesthesiologists including cardiac. The Anesthesiologist will function as a key member of the perioperative team, responsible for the provision of anesthetic services to surgical patients. Practice will be at least 50% in the provision of cardiovascular anesthesia, with direct involvement in the care of patients pre- and post-operatively, including responsibility for pre-admission anesthesia clinics and post-operative pain management.

Health Sciences Centre runs 14–16 operating rooms per day across the following surgical specialties: General, Cardiac, Neuro-Surgery, Plastic, Orthopedic, Gynecology/Gyne-ONC, Cath Lab, Neuro-Interventional Radiology, Ophthalmology, and Urology. Anesthesiologists also provide support to ECT, Endovascular Treatment of Stroke, and Acute Pain Services.

On-call coverage averages two (2) times per month, with additional second-call coverage for APS, EVT, and second team averaging one to two times per month. Members of the Cardiac Anesthesia group provide specific coverage for cardiovascular anesthesia on call and transesophageal echocardiography for the perioperative program on call.

Health Sciences Centre is a teaching hospital affiliated with the Faculty of Medicine at Memorial University of Newfoundland and Labrador, providing opportunities to engage in educational experiences with anesthesia residents and undergraduate medical students.

## Work Environment

St. John's is a vibrant, historic city on the eastern tip of North America, offering a warm and welcoming community, a thriving arts and culture scene, and easy access to the stunning natural landscapes of the Avalon Peninsula — including whale watching, hiking, and some of the most dramatic coastlines in Canada.

????????????????????????????????????????

## QUALIFICATIONS

• Medical Degree (MD) from a recognized institution

• Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada Certification in Anesthesiology (or pending certification)

• Subspecialty fellowship training in Cardiac Anesthesia required

• Successful certification of competency in advanced perioperative transesophageal echocardiography (NBE or equivalent examination)

• Demonstrated recent experience and expertise in anesthesia for Cardiac, Neuro-Surgery, Cath-Lab, Neuro-Interventional Radiology, and Urology surgical services

• Priority given to candidates with recent clinical experience at the HSC site

• Eligible for licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Newfoundland and Labrador (www.cpsnl.ca)

• Must satisfy credentialing and privilege requirements of NL Health Services including a satisfactory criminal record check and vulnerable sector check

????????????????????????????????????????

## DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

• Provide anesthetic services to surgical patients with at least 50% of practice in cardiovascular anesthesia

• Deliver pre-operative anesthesia clinic services and post-operative pain management

• Provide anesthetic coverage across General, Cardiac, Neuro-Surgery, Plastic, Orthopedic, Gynecology/Gyne-ONC, Cath Lab, Neuro-Interventional Radiology, Ophthalmology, and Urology

• Provide support to ECT, Endovascular Treatment of Stroke, and Acute Pain Services

• Provide cardiovascular anesthesia on-call coverage and transesophageal echocardiography for the perioperative program on call

• Participate in on-call coverage averaging two (2) times per month plus second-call coverage averaging one to two times per month

• Contribute to teaching and education of anesthesia residents and undergraduate medical students through the Memorial University affiliation

• Support person- and family-centered care; promote patient and worker safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks, and implementing improvements

Closing Date: Open until filled.

The philosophy of a Family Care Team (FCT) is to deliver care that is patient-centered, comprehensive, team-based, culturally safe, coordinated, accessible, and focused on quality and safety. This philosophy supports providers and care teams to meet clients where they are using an inter-professional collaborative approach where care is provided in the right place, at the right time, by the right provider in a manner that best suits the client’s need. The team will ensure clients are treated with respect, dignity, and compassion, and enable strong and trusting relationships with providers and staff. FCT’s will enable the delivery of a range of quality care for clients within their own communities while facilitating interdisciplinary work amongst healthcare providers. The FCT for the Exploits Area will include the geographical areas of Buchans, Grand Falls-Windsor, Bishops Falls. This position will support the FCT for the Exploits Area in the Bishop Falls Satellite.

Definition of work:
As part of the collaborative team, the Nurse Practitioner will be expected to practice to their full scope of practice in order to provide comprehensive assessment and care to clients and provide clinic leadership. The FCT aims to provide continuity of care to improve health outcomes and quality of life through client attachment and client paneling to clinic providers, with the support and wrap around services of the full team. The successful applicant works independently in diagnosing conditions, prescribing medications, performing or ordering diagnostic tests and treatments, evaluating treatments and providing follow-up care in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team. The Nurse Practitioner provides comprehensive and holistic nursing care to clients including health promotion, injury and illness treatment and prevention, supportive, curative and rehabilitative care in a primary care practice setting. The Nurse Practitioner will document using the Electronic Medical Record (EMR). In this leadership role, the Nurse Practitioner will contribute to the ongoing program development, implementation, and evaluation of the FCT including client and clinician engagement. The role will encompass participating in clinic evaluations and continuous quality improvement processes based upon current best practice guidelines. Flexible hours are required (combination of days, evenings, and weekends required). The Nurse Practitioner will report to the Regional Director of Primary Health Care & Community Nursing in the Central Zone.
As an advanced practitioner, the Nurse Practitioner functions in the roles of practitioner, educator and leader. As governed by provincial regulations, he/she practices independently, collaborating with the primary care physicians in the area for issues outside the Nurse Practitioner scope of practice. Travel throughout the region may be required. The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

Required qualifications:
• Graduation from a Nurse Practitioner program approved by Central Health.
• Current registration as a Nurse Practitioner with the Association of Registered Nurses of Newfoundland and Labrador.
• Current BLS certification.
• Demonstrated knowledge of home and community health services.
• Demonstrated exceptional leadership qualities and problem-solving skills as well as oral and written communication skills.
• Demonstrated ability to work well independently and in an interdisciplinary team environment.
• A valid Newfoundland and Labrador Class 5 Driver’s License.
• Consistent demonstration of NLHS values, Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (I CARE)
• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position.
• A satisfactory Certificate of Conduct from the RCMP or local police authority.

Preferred Qualifications:
• Demonstrated skill in using health care-based computer systems (CRMS, Meditech, EMR).
• Experience in the care and management of patients with diabetes, COPD, heart failure, and/or mental health disorders is an asset.
• Experience working in a Primary Health Care setting is an asset.

* Electronic Medical Records (EMR) training is required and will be provided upon hire.

Job Summary:
The Primary Care Paramedic works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.
The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.
The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

Duties/Job Demands:
The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

Job Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;
• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.
• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.
• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

Qualifications:
• Graduation from an approved Primary Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;
• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as a PCP;
• Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director
• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;
• Current certification in Basic Life Support;
• Effective oral and written communication skills;
• Critical and sound decision making skills;
• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;
• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.
• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;
• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;
• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;
• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

The Primary Care Paramedic (or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Job Summary
The Pastoral Care Clinician identifies, organizes and assists with pastoral care and ethics services for patients, families and/or staff for the Acute Care program. Support services include visitation, pastoral care, grief and bereavement, and crisis intervention in emergencies. The Pastoral Care Clinician assists and supports denominational chaplains in their involvement with patients and families; provides compassionate spiritual care in a multifaith and multicultural context; liaises within a comprehensive network of internal disciplines, programs, and external agencies that facilitate the continuum of care; supports and participates in discipline-specific education and liaises with educational organizations; organizes pastoral care services with team and community groups; provides grief and bereavement counselling to clients; participates and represents the discipline of pastoral care in team meetings; participates in the development, implementation and evaluation of approved Pastoral Care and Ethics goals, objectives and strategies; and participates in organizational accountability systems such as workload measurement, written reports, and performance review sessions. The Pastoral Care Clinician will also assist with the Ethics program of NL Health Services.

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Job occasionally results in fatigue, requiring periods of rest.
Occasionally lifts supplies, materials or equipment weighing up to 10 lbs.
Fine finger precision work, sitting, standing, walking, and driving are regularly required.
Visual concentration or alertness is constantly required while counselling. Pastoral care requires eye contact and focus on the client/patient/resident, observing body language, surroundings and being aware of the patient/client/resident's safety or Clinician's safety.
Auditory concentration is constantly required when counselling individuals in noisy areas or when counselling weak/ill clients who speak softly or may have ailments restricting their ability to talk.
Alertness to the health and safety of others is constantly required for the emotional and spiritual health of clients, patients, residents, family members and other staff.
Lack of control over the work pace occurs when emergency issues arise, deadlines and time pressures exist.

Job Qualifications
Master’s Degree in Theology, Ministry, Pastoral Studies or a related field, and clinical pastoral training as accredited by the Canadian Association of Spiritual Care (CASC), or as approved by the employer, is required.
Approved formal ministry designation is required.
Knowledge of pastoral care and counselling needs for patients/clients within long-term care, rehabilitation and community.
Knowledge and ability to provide pastoral care to clients with cognitive impairments.
Knowledge of mental health and addictions issues and how it relates to pastoral care needs.
Knowledge and ability to plan regularly scheduled spirituality discussion sessions suitable for a multi-faith context.
Demonstrated strong communication and interpersonal skills, and the ability to function as an educator and facilitator.
Demonstrated ability to work with a high degree of independence and initiative.
Demonstrated strong time management skills.
Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships.
A Condition of employment includes a valid Class 5 Newfoundland Driver's License and the use of a personal vehicle.
A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required.

2240266.description:
September 16, 2026

## BUILDING FACILITIES TECHNICIAN (BAND LEVEL 3)

Labrador Campus

(Contractual Position to January 19, 2027; Possibility of Extension)

(Part-Time; 23 Hours per Week)

## This position is based in Happy Valley-Goose Bay, Labrador

This competition may be used to fill identical positions in this unit within three (3) months of the closing date

All qualified employees are welcome to apply, however preference is given to CUPE members

The University will consider applications from qualified permanent staff who may be interested in a temporary assignment, subject to departmental approval

## BACKGROUND

The Labrador Campus is the newest campus of Memorial University, established in January 2022. Home to the School of Arctic and Subarctic Studies and the Pye Centre for Northern Boreal Food Systems, the Labrador Campus is a vibrant centre for Northern-focused, Northern-inspired, and Northern-led research, education, and community partnerships. As part of this exciting and historic transformation, the Labrador Campus is developing undergraduate, graduate, and post-graduate degrees, diplomas, certificates, and professional development learning opportunities, expanding its research activities; and developing new infrastructure. The campus is currently hiring a Building Facilities Technician to support operations related to buildings, fleet, and safety.

## DUTIES

The Building Facilities Technician will be responsible for the performance of building operational work (such as caretaking, coordinating access and security, maintenance and monitoring, storage and warehousing) related to the Labrador Campus buildings and facilities. Duties include, but are not limited to, conducting regular and special checks of facilities throughout the building, including classrooms, entrances and exits, and the library; adjusting and reporting situations that could lead to issues or loss; admitting staff, students, and users to buildings and verifying their eligible access; locking, closing, and securing buildings at night; transporting Labrador Campus vehicles to various locations; removing snow and ice from vehicles and stairs; moving and rearranging furniture to set up rooms for use; transporting materials; coordinating maintenance work with contractors; and performing other related duties as required. This position requires occasional evening work.

## QUALIFICATIONS

Experience (1-3) years in the performance of building and/or caretaker work and/or experience in a vocational trades environment; graduation from high school is required; or an equivalent combination of experience and training may be considered. Experience with building security, access, and maintenance; demonstrated strong communication skills; and the ability to use Microsoft Office (particularly email) are essential. Candidates must possess a valid Class 5 driver's license issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador. The successful candidate will be required to provide a satisfactory Certificate of Conduct.

SALARY $25.85 - $30.32 per hour (CUPE Local 1615)

Plus applicable Northern Allowance

CLOSING DATE October 1, 2026 by 5:00 p.m. NST

All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, preference will be given to applicants who are legally entitled to work in Canada. Memorial University is committed to employment equity and diversity and encourages applications from all qualified candidates, including women; 2SLGBTQIA+ people; persons whose gender identity or gender expression is nonbinary or otherwise not cisgender; Indigenous peoples; racialized people; Black persons; and persons with disabilities. Memorial is committed to providing an inclusive learning and work environment.

If there is anything we can do to ensure your full participation during the application process, please contact equity@mun.ca directly and we will work with you to make appropriate arrangements.

The personal information requested in your application is collected under the authority of the Memorial University Act (RSNL 1990 c M-7) for the purpose of identifying and recruiting candidates; assessing applicant qualifications; and maintaining records pertaining to the administration of employment with Memorial University of Newfoundland.

If you are a successful candidate, this information will form part of your permanent employment record and will be used for other activities related to the employment process. This information may be disclosed to government departments and agencies as legally required; and to third party service providers, as necessary to administer programs and activities.

If you have any questions about the collection, use and disclosure of the information on this form, please contact MyHR, Department of Human Resources, at recruitment@mun.ca.

## Please be advised that we are unable to provide updates on current competitions.

We thank all applicants for their interest, however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

2240150.title: Market Economics Research Analyst
2240150.description:
Jump Recruitment, on behalf of our client, the Association of Seafood Producers is currently seeking a Market Economics Research Analyst to join their team. This is a one-year position, with the potential for a longer-term opportunity following a review.

This role involves navigating the Fishing Industry Collective Bargaining Act (FICBA) and the Master Collective Agreement between the Association and the Fish, Food and Allied Workers-Unifor Union (FFAW-Unifor) to support the negotiation of raw material prices and conditions of sale with the FFAW, the union representing fish harvesters.

## ABOUT THE ASSOCIATION OF SEAFOOD PRODUCERS:

The Association of Seafood Producers (ASP) is a not-for-profit industry trade association representing seafood processors across Newfoundland and Labrador.

The Association was founded in November 2003 as the province's leading voice for seafood processors and legislated industry representative for all collective bargaining. Over the years, we've built strong, collaborative relationships with all levels of government and industry. These partnerships have been built on mutual respect, shared goals, and a commitment to the long-term success of our shared natural resources.

We're more than a voice. We walk the walk, working collaboratively to strengthen the future of Newfoundland and Labrador's seafood industry - through sound public policy, sustainable practices, and responsible resource management. Together with our members, we're building a resilient, forward-looking seafood sector - one that supports good jobs, strong communities, and sustainable fisheries for generations to come.

## WHAT YOU'LL DO:

In this highly confidential role, you will support NL seafood producers and will routinely access, analyze, and manage proprietary business information, collective bargaining strategies, market intelligence, pricing data, operational metrics, and commercially sensitive information provided by ASP member companies. Maintaining strict confidentiality and exercising sound professional judgment are essential requirements of this role. The incumbent will be required to sign a confidentiality and non-disclosure agreement and adhere to all ASP data management and privacy protocols.

Your key responsibilities will be:

## Market Analysis:

• Track seafood pricing, wholesale/retail buying habits, import/export trade data, and global market trends, analyzing international market data, currency trends, and production yields to justify, determine, and set competitive prices.

## Economic Forecasting:

• Research mathematical and bio-economic models that forecast future seafood supply, demand, and inventory and pricing models.

## Policy & Regulatory Assessment:

• Evaluate the financial and socioeconomic impacts of processing license management, fisheries management, conservation measures, and international trade regulatory changes and policies on processors, plant workers and coastal communities.

## Reporting:

• Translate complex economic datasets into simplistic documentation that can be utilized as part of Standing Fish Pricing Panel submissions; support policy papers, and presentations for industry or government policymakers.

## Confidential Information Management:

• Collect, maintain, analyze, and safeguard highly sensitive commercial, financial, pricing, production, and market data obtained from ASP member companies and collective bargaining processes. Ensure all information is handled in accordance with ASP confidentiality policies and data security requirements.

## WHAT YOU BRING:

• Education: A bachelor's or master's degree in economics, Resource Management, Statistics, or Business.

• Industry Knowledge: Understanding of commercial fishing, marine resource policies, and global seafood supply chains.

• Experience: Experience working with proprietary datasets, strategic business information, labour negotiations, or confidential economic analysis would be considered a strong asset.

• Analytical Skills: Proficiency in statistical and econometric databases, and software (Advanced Excel, Expana, etc.)

• Communication Skills: High proficiency in both oral and written communication, must be able to translate complex economic datasets into simplistic documentation used as part of collective bargaining submissions; to support policy papers, and presentations for industry or government policymakers

• Professional Integrity and Confidentiality: Demonstrated ability to manage highly confidential and commercially sensitive information with discretion.

## WHAT WE OFFER:

• A competitive salary to commiserate with experience.

• A flexible, supportive, and collaborative work environment.

If you're looking to be a part of building a resilient, forward-looking seafood sector - one that supports good jobs, strong communities, and sustainable fisheries for generations to come, this opportunity is for you!

achieve its strategic goals. This position will develop effective working relationships and communicate regularly with a wide range of internal and external stakeholders. This will require excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including
sensitivity, tact and diplomacy and the ability to appropriately handle contentious conversations.

In that capacity, this position will:
• Contribute and maintain supplier management framework to support the development and ongoing maintenance of strong supplier relationships.

• Evaluate contract effectiveness and inform Sourcing and Contracts of potential changes to terms and conditions of future competitive bidding and contract documents to ensure positive stakeholder relationships.

are not performing. This includes: mediating disputes between suppliers, Public Procurement Agency, and end-users to ensure compliance to contracts, Public
Procurement Act, and minimize legal risks.

• Develop and maintain constructive relationships across three Supply Chain provincial divisions in a “pod” that would include employees from: Sourcing & Contracts, Purchase Operations, and Supplier Relationship Management divisions, and work within these pods to identify efficiencies that could impact Supply Chain’s services to its customers, and commodities being ordered and delivered, including making recommendations to improve supplier performance, manage the legal landscape impacting procurement, and provide increased bid opportunities.
• Manage supplier and product complaints and use business acumen to recognize issues, analyze options and recommend course of action to work complaint to resolution.
• Analyze internal and third-party data to identify risks related to supply chain sustainability including potential disruptions in the current and projected future supply chain, and monitor threats to supply availability and NLHS operations.
• Evaluate and promote Environmental Social Governance (ESG) initiatives in NLHS in relation to supply chain and SRM including collaborating with suppliers to implement sustainable practices and monitor their progress, and promote diversity and inclusion within the supply chain;
• Promote the Supplier Relationship Management function and associated customer/end user satisfaction goals internally.
• Interpret and communicate Supply Chain policies and procedures and provincial legislation and works with end users to provide advice and ensure compliance.
• Assist with the management and coordination of product recalls, warranties and supplier complaints.
• Complete special projects as required.

•Strong business and legal acumen to build, deliver and maintain strategic supplier relations and support fiscal stewardship on behalf of NLHS.
•Experience working in pods supporting complex purchasing/supply chain environment, where analytics, projects, and relationship management is integral to
success.
• Minimum 2 years experience in managing suppliers, leading difficult conversations, navigating amongst multiple parties with differing perspectives, decision making, and project management.
• Minimum 2 years specific supply chain experience in: business and supply chain strategy; contract and formal legal document writing and management, supplier engagement, performance monitoring, execution management; supplier relationship management, and risk management.
• Experience in working within the ESG space particularly in monitoring impacts on supplier relationships.
• Very proficient in preparing electronic reports, analysis, data management, and communications.
• Strong writing and formatting skills to develop, proof-read, edit, and format legally binding content is required. And, must have the ability to communicate, both orally and written, with internal customers, departments, vendors, and other external stakeholders such as Public Procurement Agency and legal counsel to ensure there is a clear understanding of the requirements.

We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to an Ambulance Operator/Attendant as the next highest classification, they will be awarded as temporary full time (TFT) for a period of one year, with possibility of extension.

## Job Summary:

The Primary Care Paramedic (or Ambulance Operator/Attendant),works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine. The base for this service is located at Lewisporte Ambulance Base, Lewisporte.

Duties/Job Demands:
The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will provide assistance to the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

Job Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;
• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.
• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.
• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

Qualifications:
• Graduation from High School or equivalent;
• Graduation from an approved Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;
• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as a PCP or EMR;
• Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director
• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;
• Current certification in Basic Life Support;
• Effective oral and written communication skills;
• Critical and sound decision making skills;
• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;
• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.
• A satisfactory record of work performance is required;
• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

Duties/Job Demands:
The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will provide assistance to the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

Job Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
* Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;
* Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.
* Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.
* Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

Qualifications:
* Graduation from High School or equivalent;
* Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;
* Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;
* Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director
* Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;
* Current certification in Basic Life Support;
* Current ACLS certification (ACP only);
* Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)
* Effective oral and written communication skills;
* Critical and sound decision making skills;
* Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;
* For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.
* A satisfactory record of work performance is required;
* A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

## Salary:

* Advanced Care Paramedic - CGHSA-37 of the NAPE HS salary scale $39.14 to $46.27 per hour
* Primary Care Paramedic – CGHSA-29 of the NAPE HS salary scale $32.71 to $37.40 per hour
* Ambulance Operator/Attendant – CG-25 of the NAPE HS salary scale $23.78 to $26.19 per hour

## Job Summary:

The Primary Care Paramedic (or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

Duties/Job Demands:
The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will provide assistance to the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

Job Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
* Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;
* Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.
* Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.
* Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

Qualifications:
* Graduation from High School or equivalent;
* Graduation from an approved Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;
* Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as a PCP or EMR;
* Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director
* Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;
* Current certification in Basic Life Support;
* Effective oral and written communication skills;
* Critical and sound decision making skills;
* Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;
* For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.
* A satisfactory record of work performance is required;
* A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

## Salary:

* Primary Care Paramedic – CGHSA-29 of the NAPE HS salary scale $32.71 to $37.40 per hour
* Ambulance Operator/Attendant – CG-25 of the NAPE HS salary scale $23.78 to $26.19 per hour
* A financial recruitment incentive may apply to this position for new hires in exchange for a return in service. If so, the recruiter will discuss with you.

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

The Cancer Care Program has a provincial mandate to deliver cancer care to the people of Newfoundland and Labrador. It operates the Dr. H. Bliss Murphy Cancer Centre (DHBMCC) in St. John's, and regional cancer centres in Corner Brook, Gander and Grand Falls. The DHMBCC has four linear accelerators, an orthovoltage unit, an HDR Brachytherapy unit, two CT-Simulators, Eclipse Treatment Planning System and ARIA Radiation Oncology information system. The cancer centre in Corner Brook is a satellite site with one linear accelerator and one CT simulator and will be offering a full complement of radiation therapy techniques. NLHealthServices.ca

Job Summary
The Dosimetrist is responsible for:

o Performing highly specialized and clinical work as a member of the radiation oncology team in the development of treatment plans for oncology patients undergoing radiation therapy treatment, and in accordance with established policies and standards of practice.
o Clinical activities in the CT simulator, and radiation treatment units.
o Consulting with physicians regarding goals of treatment, including treatment volumes and organs at risko Performing image registration/fusion.
o Contouring organs at risk for treatment and devising optimal radiation beam arrangements.
o Organizing workload and coordinating resources in the department to ensure all aspects of a patient's radiation treatment plan are completed prior to treatment.
o Performing quality assurance checks of the Electronic Medical Record by following established policies and procedures, maintaining records of check, and taking appropriate action when necessary.
o Performing quality assurance checks of treatment plans created by non-certified Dosimetrists.
o Consulting with Radiation Therapists, Medical Physicists and Radiation Oncologists on optimal treatment parameters.
o Facilitating weekly Planning Quality Assurance Rounds and Radiation Oncologist Peer Reviews.
o Providing support, teaching and technical advice to non-certified Dosimetrists, Radiation Therapists and Students.
o Working in mould room fabricating patient specific radiation therapy accessories such as custom beam modifying devices.

Dosimetrists report to the Provincial Manager of Medical Physics.

**At the Corner Brook location, Dosimetrists may be required to perform all radiation therapist duties including CT simulator and/or the radiation treatment unit.

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Work is subject to time pressures and deadlines.
Regularly requires a higher-than-normal level of attentiveness/alertness for visual and auditory concentration
Regularly requires fine finger/precision work and sitting at a computer.
Occasionally lifts or moves objects less than 10lbs, occasionally objects between 10-50 lbs. and occasionally over 50 lbs.
Required to regularly stand, walk, or sit for extended periods and fine finger or precision work is regularly required.

Job Qualifications
Graduation from an approved/accredited degree/diploma in Radiation Therapy is required.
Current and continuing certification with the Canadian Association for Medical Radiation Technologists (CAMRT) in Radiation Therapy is required.
Successful completion of the CAMRT Dosimetry Certificate (CDC) OR current and continuing registration as a Certified Medical Dosimetrist (CMD) with the Medical Dosimetrist Certification Board (MDCB) is required.
A minimum of three years' experience within the last five years working in Radiation Therapy or Dosimetry is required.
In-depth knowledge of treatment planning and the physical principles of dose calculation.
Comprehensive knowledge of departmental, organizational, and professional standards.
Demonstrated ability to work independently with a high degree of autonomy, ability to prioritize workload, strong time management skills, and strong decision-making skills.
Demonstrated ability to build and maintain successful working relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to teach and mentor others.
Demonstrated commitment to NL Health Services' values of innovation, compassion, accountability, respect, and excellence.
Satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required.

*Effective May 1, 2025, all Medical Radiation Technologists and X - Ray Health Professionals will require registration with the Newfoundland and Labrador Council of Health Professionals (NLCHP) in the appropriate discipline(s) in order to practice in Newfoundland and Labrador. The successful applicant is required to achieve registration by May 1, 2025.

Title: Senior Manager, Publishing - Prevention & Safety

Employee Working Location: Partially Virtual / Hybrid (Canada)

Employment Status: Temporary Full-time (18 Months)

The Canadian Red Cross (Red Cross) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

## In this role, you will:

• Lead a multidisciplinary team responsible for the design, development, maintenance, and improvement of accessible learning program products in print, digital, and online formats.

• Provide strategic direction on product design and production to the Leadership Team, while providing coaching, resource planning, and operational oversight to ensure design and production priorities are aligned with organizational objectives and products are delivered efficiently and meet established quality and product standards.

• Lead team annual budget planning and oversee ongoing budget monitoring, forecasting, and resource allocation to ensure effective stewardship of financial resources and alignment with organizational priorities.

• Make decisions on hiring, promotion, and performance with senior leadership approval, fostering teamwork and innovation, operating within financial guidelines, and contributing to budget planning and financial reporting.

• Address complex product, workflow, and resourcing challenges by analyzing business needs, evaluating options, and developing practical solutions that balance user needs, organizational priorities, and operational constraints, with escalation for alignment with business unit goals.

• Manage the design, development, maintenance, and governance of accessible products to support effective project planning and delivery, including content development and architecture, visual and production design, UX, UI design, digital asset creation and management, content strategy, creative direction, art direction, and English, French, and multilingual deliverables.

• Coordinate with the team, our team partners within Prevention & Safety, and stakeholders to assess the readiness of projects for product and publication development (including resourcing and timelines) and define product and publication requirements to deliver cohesive, branded, accessible, and user-centred learning experiences across digital, print, online, and blended formats.

• Oversee team to develop, maintain, and follow standards for creating accessible, inclusive, useful, usable, and relevant products, and grow the team's expertise in creating and delivering user-friendly products across our offerings (online courses, in-person courses, printed and digital products, audio and visual products, etc.).

## What we are looking for:

• A minimum of 6 to 9 years of experience and a 3-year college diploma or university degree in product design, publication design, publishing, user experience, instructional design, communications, multimedia, or a related field and/or equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Requires expertise in a specialized discipline or broad experience across fields, along with an understanding of interconnections between processes and business units to provide effective leadership.

• Deep understanding of learning programs and their product development, lifecycle management, and risk management across print, digital, online, and blended formats, including deep understanding of accessibility and inclusivity, user experience and usability principles, Agile and Waterfall delivery approaches, and product and publication governance, quality assurance, and operational processes.

• Leadership and team management skills with the ability to resolve conflicts and inspire, motivate, and engage teams to achieve program objectives.

• Proficiency with collaboration, project management, content authoring, and learning technology platforms such as Microsoft 365 (including Teams and SharePoint), Atlassian tools (Jira and Confluence), Adobe Acrobat, Articulate Rise, D2L Brightspace, Vimeo, and related publishing technologies.

• French language comprehension would be an asset in this role, as well as familiarity with instructional design and learning experience design, content strategy and information architecture, digital asset management, multimedia production and creative direction.

## Working conditions:

• Requires significant attention to detail and concentration and ability to mentally process large amounts of information.

• The work pace is often unpredictable with significant time pressures.

• Ability to adapt to frequent and often urgent changes in priorities, make decisions under pressure, and work at an unpredictable pace.

• Some domestic or international travel to safe locations.

• Work requires the ability to work to multiple, conflicting deadlines.

• As we work with and support people (managers, colleagues, beneficiaries/customers, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.

• Eligibility to work in Canada: At this time, we welcome applications from candidates eligible to work in Canada. If you are not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada, we encourage you to carefully review your visa to find out whether you are eligible to work in the job you are considering applying for. Refer to our FAQ for more information.

• If you are selected for this role, you will be required to complete a successful pre-employment screening process which includes a satisfactory Enhanced Police Information Check (E-PIC).

Cold Ocean Salmon, a division of Cooke Aquaculture Inc., a dynamic and growing east coast family company, with Platinum Member status in the Canada's Best Managed Companies Program, has an opportunity for a highly motivated individual to join our Wharf Crew based out of Hermitage, Newfoundland. Cooke is a global seafood company with operations in North America, Europe, and South America. Our company's success is driven by our dynamic, highly skilled, and innovative management team, supported by dedicated employees who live in coastalcommunitiesand contribute to the local area's economy and sense of community.

Receive, store, and issue materials and supplies.

Fulfill orders from different departments.

Keep the feed room clean and organized.

It is about being at the center of the fastest growing company in Atlantic Canada and knowing you are part of that growth. The ability to bring your passion for learning, desire for growth, and energy for moving your career forward is what we offer.

Why Cooke? Simple - we are a company that rewards initiative, resourcefulness, and work ethic. We will champion your growth and provide you with the platform to create your path, your career, and your future.

We are a provincial health authority responsible for delivering quality health care to approximately 550,000 people in Newfoundland and Labrador. Supported by over 23,000 employees and physicians, our team works together to improve the health and well-being of every person, in every community. Guided by the vision of the Health Accord NL, we offer a range of health-care programs and services through a wide network of facilities, clinics, and community services across five zones: Central, Eastern-Rural, Eastern-Urban, Labrador-Grenfell, and Western.

At NL Health Services, we believe that our people — employees, doctors and volunteers — make it a great place to work. Every individual brings valuable knowledge, experience and perspective. It is in this diversity that we find strength. ## ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

The Pathology & Laboratory Medicine Program of NL Health Services – Eastern Urban Zone invites applications for a permanent full-time Clinical & Academic Genitourinary Pathologist at Health Sciences Centre in St. John's, NL.

The successful candidate will join an established and collaborative Pathology team providing comprehensive genitourinary pathology services in a tertiary care and teaching hospital setting. The position includes both clinical and academic responsibilities and is formally affiliated with the Faculty of Medicine at Memorial University of Newfoundland and Labrador. Opportunities for teaching, research, and scholarly activities are an integral part of this role.

St. John's is a vibrant, historic city on the eastern tip of North America, offering a warm and welcoming community, a thriving arts and culture scene, and easy access to the stunning natural landscapes of the Avalon Peninsula — including whale watching, hiking, and some of the most dramatic coastlines in Canada.

ABOUT CENTRAL ZONE
Central Zone is the second largest health zone in Newfoundland and Labrador Health Services, serving approximately 90,000 people (17 per cent of the province’s population) living in 176 communities. With a geographical area encompassing more than half the total land mass of the island, the Central region extends from Charlottetown in the east, Fogo Island in the north, Harbour Breton in the south, to Baie Verte in the west. Central Zone provides a variety of primary, secondary, long-term care, community health, and other enhanced secondary services.

## JOB SUMMARY

NL Health Services Central Zone is inviting applications from Family Physicians to join the Family Care Program in a full-time salaried position in the Gander/Gander Bay Region.

NLHS is pleased to support its Primary Health Care Clinic in achieving its goals of providing exceptional and high-quality care to patients in the Central region. The PHC Family Care Team (FCT) mandate is to provide patients without a primary care provider of the Central region with access to primary health care services. Services will be provided using an inter-professional collaborative approach where patients will see the right provider at the right time and right place. The team includes physicians, NPs, RNs including diabetic nurse educator, clerical supports, LPNs, pharmacists, social workers, dietitian, physiotherapist and occupational therapist. All health care providers, including physicians, will be expected to practice to their full scope of practice to meet patient needs and requirements. The FCT aims to provide continuity of care to improve health outcomes and patients quality of life.

We are seeking physicians to manage a roster of patients. There are other services in the area of the FCT which the physician is encouraged to consider participating in including: Hospitalist Services, Emergency Department Services, Long-Term Care, Palliative Care, and other opportunities. Our ideal candidates will have a strong patient focus and excellent communication skills with a keen interest in practicing in a collaborative team approach. Hours of work may need flexibility to offer clinics during the daytime, after-hours and on weekends to meet patient needs. The successful Physicians will provide care using the EMR platform.

In this role the nurse practitioner performs all activities utilizing a harm reduction approach within the primary health care framework.

The PHC Team mandate is to provide low barrier access to harm reduction focused, primary health care services for individuals who are homeless or precariously housed. Many of these individuals are navigating complex mental health and/or substance use conditions and often experience marginalization because of their circumstances; many have trouble accessing traditional health care services.

The NP will work to full scope of practice providing care to the vulnerable population through a walk-in clinic and/or outreach to various locations (Mobile Clinics, community partner locations etc.) They will also be involved in the Managed Alcohol Program (MAP) and a Palliative approach Care for vulnerable populations, in collaboration with other providers and team members.

The nurse practitioner is a member of the Downtown Healthcare Collaborative and harm reduction teams of health professionals including, but not limited to, registered nurses, pharmacist, occupational therapist, community outreach workers, social worker, peer support workers and others, working across programs and services to provide the best possible care. Health services in this context are provided in a variety of ways including street reach and mobile clinics, home visits, PHC walk-in clinics, community partnerships, and acute care partnerships.

The nurse practitioner, as a member of the team, provides for the presenting needs of the client and includes all routine primary health care and treatment as well as Hepatitis C, HIV, latent TB, STBBI testing and treatment, mental health single session counselling, client education, and is a satellite site for provision of SWAP supplies. All services are intended to reach the most vulnerable, underserved individuals in our community.

In keeping with NL Health Services Values, the harm reduction team members operate in an environment of mutual respect where the contribution of every team member, regardless of personal or professional background, is considered when providing care to clients. Team members are supported and encouraged to use their education, knowledge, strengths, experience, and expertise to practice to their full scope in the performance of their work, in support of the client, and in support of one another. Low barrier access to care is the foundation of service, meeting individuals wherever they are in their life journey and regardless of their personal circumstances. By working with the individual to address concerns impacting their personal health, the team endeavors to attach clients to permanent providers wherever possible and to connect them with long term services when necessary.

Our team is seeking an Advanced Care Paramedic for a temporary position. If no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics. We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from High School or equivalent;

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP or PCP;

• Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance is required;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

## Salary:

• Advanced Care Paramedic - CG-37 of the NAPE HS salary scale $39.14 to $46.27 per hour

• Primary Care Paramedic – CG-29 of the NAPE HS salary scale $32.71 to $37.40 per hour

• A financial recruitment incentive may apply to this position for new hires in exchange for a return in service. If so, the recruiter will discuss with you.
