As a member of an interdisciplinary team, the Nurse Practitioner provides quality care to clients of the Family Care Team, providing services to residents in the Clarenville region, with potential service to alternate sites using a hub and spoke model. The principles of the Family Care Team align with the patient health home model of care; using a collaborative health care team approach, from various health disciplines, in the provision of primary health care services.

This position works within the Nurse Practitioner's (NP) scope of practice in the following category of practice: (Family/All Ages). This is an advance practice role providing professional, analytical and an autonomous comprehensive range of health services to clients and patients including but not limited to health assessments and diagnosis diseases, disorders, injuries and conditions; treating and managing acute and chronic illnesses and identifying health risks and needs within a holistic model. The NP in this position may complete home visits and provide virtual care.

The Family Care Team mandate is to provide patients without a primary care provider of the Clarenville region with access to health care services. Services will be provided using an inter-professional collaborative approach where patients will see the right provider at the right time and right place. All health care providers, including NPs, will be expected to practice to their full scope of practice in order to meet patient needs and requirements. The Family Care Team aims to provide continuity of care to improve health outcomes and patient quality of life through patient attachment and patient paneling to individual NPs, with the support and wrap around services of the full team.

Flexible hours may be required (Combination of days, evenings, and weekends required).

This position reports to the Regional Primary Health Care Program Manager responsible for the service.

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Constantly moves, lifts, or operates equipment/machinery up to 10 lbs. and regularly is required to lift/move equipment, books, supplies, and sometimes children up to 25 lbs. (may need to be deleted or added depending on the position). Occasionally, may have to reposition a patient over 50 lbs.
Physical effort also includes regular sitting to conduct patient histories, performing work on the computer and when assessing patients, regularly stands or walks.
When performing procedures, regularly uses fine finger/precision work and hand tools (i.e. medical instruments, computer mouse, stethoscope, dopplers, etc.) requiring accurate control and steadiness.
Visual concentration is required when performing physical assessment and procedures, completing charts/reports, observing patients, reading equipment/monitors, and completing work-related correspondence on the computer.

Job Qualifications
Completion of an approved/recognized Nurse Practitioner program is required.
Current and continuing registration with the Newfoundland and Labrador College of Nurses (NLCN) and Licensed (or eligible for licensure) as a Nurse Practitioner (Adult or Family/All Ages) with the NLCN.
A minimum of five years clinical experience in the last seven in Primary Health Care is required.
Current BCLS Certification is required.
Possess strong abilities in the areas of collaboration, clinical reasoning, professional development, interpersonal effectiveness, conflict management and teamwork.
Demonstrated progressive clinical leadership skills.
Possessed strong communication, problem solving, decision-making, and teaching skills.
Demonstrated ability to function autonomously in an advanced practice role.
Support and participate in research to improve practice and client outcomes.
Demonstrated skills in computer and database management skills.
A valid Newfoundland and Labrador Class 5 Driver's license and use of private vehicle are conditions of employment.
A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required.

## Job Summary:

Reporting to the Director level, the Registered Midwife is an autonomous primary maternity care professional providing comprehensive care to individuals and their newborns during the childbearing period. The Registered Midwife provides comprehensive care during pregnancy, conducts births in the hospital and community setting, and continues with postpartum care to individuals and their newborns for at least six weeks after birth.

The Registered Midwife has the ability to admit and discharge in hospital and works collaboratively with obstetricians, nurses, family physicians, pediatricians, anesthetists, lactation consultants and other members of the healthcare team. The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person- and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety, and partner with all team members to improve staff and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements. The Registered Midwife contributes to NLHS policies and educational sessions. The Registered Midwife works as part of a small team sharing clients and on-call coverage.

• A Master's degree is an asset;

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

Duties/Job Demands:
The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will provide assistance to the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

Job Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
* Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;
* Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.
* Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.
* Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

Qualifications:
* Graduation from High School or equivalent;
* Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;
* Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;
* Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director
* Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;
* Current certification in Basic Life Support;
* Current ACLS certification (ACP only);
* Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)
* Effective oral and written communication skills;
* Critical and sound decision making skills;
* Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;
* For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.
* A satisfactory record of work performance is required;
* A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

* Primary Care Paramedic – CG-29 of the NAPE HS salary scale $32.71 to $37.40 per hour

The NP Cardiovascular and Stroke Program provides comprehensive patient care in collaboration with other members of the interdisciplinary health team within the Cardiology Services, this includes performing comprehensive health assessment based on a thorough history, physical examination, and additional assessment strategies individualized to patient needs and practice setting; utilizing critical appraisal skills in decisions related to the use of clinical and diagnostic investigations, interventions and the management of care including but not limited to addressing emergent clinical needs for patients; demonstrating evidence-based clinical decision-making through the critical examination and application of evidence from clinical research integrated with clinical expertise, patient input, family involvement, and existing resources; performing diagnostic procedures and therapeutic interventions; coordinating activities and functions regarding patient care, progress and outcomes; exercising flexibility in clinical decision-making depending on need to negotiate with other healthcare provider(s) to determine a course of action in the absence of other resources or providers; and directs patient care to ensure continuity across the continuum. ## Definition of Work:

This position will support the Primary Care Neighborhood (PCN) in the Coast of Bays. A Primary Care Neighborhood is a geographic area where all community based primary healthcare providers function as an interconnected team in delivering the care patients require. As a member of the PCN, the successful candidate will work collaboratively to provide team based comprehensive, patient centered, and culturally safe healthcare to meet the needs of patients and communities. PCNs will enable the delivery of a range of quality care for patients within their own communities while facilitating interdisciplinary work amongst healthcare providers.
The philosophy of a Primary Care Neighborhood is to deliver care that is patient-centered, comprehensive, team-based, coordinated, accessible, and focused on quality and safety. This philosophy of health care encourages providers and care teams to meet patients where they are. The Primary Care Neighborhood is a place where patients are treated with respect, dignity, and compassion, and enable strong and trusting relationships with providers and staff. This is a model for achieving primary care excellence so that care is received in the right place, at the right time, and in the manner that best suits a patient's needs.
Definition of Work:
This physiotherapy position is a highly independent clinical position with the primary purpose of facilitating optimal physical performance of clients with a wide variety of physical, or environmentally induced impairments utilizing the models of best practice and developed pathways. Proficiency in all practice areas will be required as this is a multifaceted position. In consultation with the primary care team, clinical work involves screening of referrals, client assessment, development of client centered goals and intervention plans, coordination of other services and completion of all required documentation. This position may also require travel and the utilization of virtual technologies in supporting the clientele within the neighborhood.
The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care; demonstrate a commitment to continuous quality improvement and demonstrate a commitment to safety partnering with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

If there are no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics (PCP) and Ambulance Operators/Attendants (also known as Emergency Medical Responder (EMR)). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to a PCP or EMR as the next highest classification, they will be awarded as temporary full time (TFT) and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will aid the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients.

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

## ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

The Pathology & Laboratory Medicine Program of NL Health Services – Eastern Urban Zone is seeking a qualified and highly motivated Hematopathologist to join the Hematopathology Division at Health Sciences Centre in St. John's, NL.

The successful candidate will join three (3) other Hematopathologists and work in collaboration with molecular and diagnostic pathologists, clinical and medical microbiologists, genetics scientists, and clinical chemists, providing the province with tertiary and quaternary laboratory care.

The Division of Hematopathology offers transfusion medicine, bone marrow pathology, flow cytometry, hematology core lab, coagulation, and hemoglobinopathy services. It also provides training to medical laboratory technology students, medical students, anatomic pathology, and other medical residents. Hematopathologists are supported by molecular pathology and cytogenetics laboratories providing testing for various myeloid and lymphoid neoplasms, and by immunohistochemistry laboratories.

This full-time position will also share responsibilities in providing medical oversight in hematopathology and transfusion medicine to rural hospitals and community health centres across NL, offering basic hematology, coagulation, and transfusion medicine testing and transfusion services. The position will provide consultative services for a wide variety of patient programs including hematology, bleeding and coagulation disorders, bone marrow transplantation, and blood transfusion.

## Definition of Work:

Reporting to the Director of Patient Flow and Site Operations. The Acute Care Nurse Practitioner (NP) works collaboratively with the hospitalist service, site lead physicians and interdisciplinary team members. The NP participates in interdisciplinary patient care planning, handover discussions, collaborative inpatient management, patient assignment and workload coordination, and discharge planning activities in partnership with the hospitalist service and healthcare team. The NP’s primary role provides clinical care to inpatients at James Paton Memorial Regional Health Centre, with presentations that include various acute and chronic health conditions. Operational requirements may necessitate support in other clinical areas (including but not limited to personal care homes, long-term care and community settings) consistent with the NP’s competencies and organizational need. The successful candidate will work collaboratively with unit-based nursing staff, leaders, allied health team members, subspecialists, the Hospitalist Team and administration to provide comprehensive, holistic, patient-family centered care. The NP will participate in the regular morning huddle with the site-operation team and work with the multidisciplinary team to facilitate patient flow and discharges.

The Nurse Practitioner is expected to perform advanced comprehensive health assessments; order, interpret and perform diagnostic tests; provide input related to primarily ALC and medically discharged patients; however, may need to manage active inpatients within their scope of practice in acute care settings in collaboration with both hospitalist and other providers. The successful candidate will communicate assessment findings, diagnoses, including outcomes and prognoses; prescribe appropriate pharmacological, medical, and other therapies; utilize complex reasoning to safely coordinate and manage patient care while promoting continuity across the continuum of care.

The position will contribute to collaborative inter-professional patient care through advanced clinical practice, consultations, referrals, leadership, education, research, and other related duties as required. This position will require strong

interpersonal skills, the ability to build collaborative, trusting relationships and will demonstrate skills in the organization, conflict resolution, advanced problem solving, critical thinking, change management and interdisciplinary leadership. A passion for caring and advocating for patients with advanced medical complexity, and their families, is essential.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

• CNA certification in either Gerontology, Hospice Palliative Care, Medical-Surgical and willingness to complete at least one of these within two years after commencing in the role.

Posted Date: 2026-06-04

Closing Date: Open until filled.

Our team is seeking a Primary Care Paramedic for a full-time position. If no Primary Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Ambulance Operators/Attendants (also known as Emergency Medical Responder (EMR)). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Primary Care Paramedic, then Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to an EMR as the next highest classification, they will be awarded as temporary full time (TFT) and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Primary Care Paramedic (or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will aid the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as a PCP or EMR;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

Job Summary
The Psychologist works closely with the interdisciplinary team (Developmental Pediatrician, Social Worker, Physiotherapist, Occupational Therapist, Speech-Language Pathologist, and other specialties) providing services to children and their families aged 0-18. The Child Development Team Psychologist serves a very diverse population of children and adolescents: including learning, behavioural, developmental and cognitive challenges.

This position functions autonomously and uses critical thinking and independent analysis/judgment in the application of specialized psychological knowledge and principles in clinical practice. The incumbent is responsible for the provision of psychological/cognitive assessment, standardized psychometric testing, formulation of the diagnosis based upon the DSM-5 criterion, and therapeutic intervention for children/adolescents and their families within a chronic illness and physical disability framework. The incumbent provides/supervises specialized therapy in situations where the application of professional analysis based upon a broad range of theoretical frameworks in complex practice situations is essential. The clinician has a specialty area of children and adolescents with neuro/developmental conditions and functions autonomously using independent judgment in determining appropriate assessment, diagnosis and interventions and then developing, implementing, and evaluating/analyzing treatment plans. Work involves providing clinical education and consultation to physicians and other professional personnel; mentoring; coaching and clinical consultation to enhance the delivery of client care patients; provision of leadership direction for professional development; clinical education and consultation with other organizations and agencies; research and evaluation of services; ensuring compliance with professional standards; and development and implementation of psychology policies as they affect population groups. The Psychologist responds to broader systems issues impacting on services to specific client populations.

This position also includes advanced clinical supervisory and leadership responsibilities in the discipline of psychology. The Psychologist provides supervision across the range of training experiences offered at Eastern Health. This may include advanced doctoral-level clinical supervision, training, and consultation to masters- and doctoral-level provisionally registered Psychologists seeking registration with the Newfoundland and Labrador Psychology Board (NLPB); to senior doctoral-level graduate students in clinical Psychology; and Pre-Doctoral Psychology Residents during their placements/rotations at the Development and Rehabilitation Division. Furthermore, the Psychologist has an integral role in the development and ongoing maintenance of training in clinical psychology within the Development and Rehabilitation Division and the broader system of Eastern Health.

This position reports to the Division Manager for Children's and Women's Health and maintains accountability to the Clinical Psychologist Professional Practice Consultant for integrity and professional practice issues.

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Occasionally, there is lifting, or physical strength required, less than 10 lbs for files, boxes, or equipment.
Regularly sits; occasionally works in awkward/cramped positions, and stands. The psychologist may provide services in conjunction with other disciplines and as such, may be required to sit or stand in alternative environments (e.g. physiotherapy pool, occupational therapy bathroom).
Uses fine finger/precision work when on the computer and visual concentration is required when in sessions with patients (i.e. reviewing patient charts/notes, tests and for documenting work, and when reading or researching information).
Visual concentration is required to interpret patient observations and integrate into patient evaluation.
Auditory concentration is constantly required in sessions with patients to listen attentively, to be alert and to obtain and interpret information correctly.
A higher-than-normal level of attentiveness is required when assessing high risk patients.
Travel to outlying regions is required.

Job Qualifications
Graduation with an approved/recognized Master's Degree in Clinical Psychology is required.
Doctorate Degree in Clinical Psychology is preferred.
Registration or provisional registration with Newfoundland and Labrador Psychology Board is required.
Graduate course work and supervised experience in psychological assessment, particularly cognitive and adaptive functioning assessment, and treatment with individuals and families, with a specific focus on children and adolescents with neurodevelopmental conditions.
Exhibited strong communication, program development and evaluation skills.
Possessed proven analytical, critical reasoning, collaboration, problem solving, decision-making and organizational skills.
Demonstrated ability to direct, supervise and mentor students.
Demonstrated ability to effectively translate and communicate knowledge in the specialized area of psychology practice to others.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively within an interprofessional environment and provide clinical consultation.
Ability to work autonomously, prioritizing caseloads and client needs.
Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain a constructive working rapport with clients.
Demonstrated strong awareness of ethical principles and standards of professional conduct.
A satisfactory record of work performance is required.

Job Summary
This position works within the Nurse Practitioner's (NP) scope of practice in the following category of practice: (Pediatric with specialized education relevant to Neonatology). This is an advanced practice role providing professional, analytical and an autonomous comprehensive range of health services to patients including, but not limited to, resuscitation, stabilization and management of ill infants, health assessments and diagnosis of diseases, disorders, injuries and conditions; treating and managing acute and chronic illnesses; and identifying health risks and needs within a holistic model.

In collaboration with the interdisciplinary health care team, the NNP will manage, direct and provide comprehensive care for a select patient population with acute and specialized neonatal and newborn health care needs. This includes performing comprehensive health assessment based on a thorough history, physical examination, and additional assessment strategies individualized to patient needs and practice setting; utilizing critical appraisal skills in decisions related to the use of clinical and diagnostic investigations, interventions and the management of care; demonstrating evidence-based clinical decision-making through the critical examination and application of evidence from clinical research integrated with clinical expertise, and existing resources; performing diagnostic procedures and therapeutics; coordinating activities and functions regarding patient care, progress and outcomes.

The NNP will have a key leadership role within the NICU, performing quality improvement work; participating in policy and procedure development, facilitating educational support for patients, families and staff and will be a critical member of the clinical leadership team supporting high quality evidence-based care for high-risk neonatal patients. The NNP must also be able to identify the need for change related to clinical, educational or research issues in clinical practice and initiate appropriate action while promoting staff and patient/family satisfaction within a philosophy of family-centered care.

The NNP clarifies relevant research questions, collaborates, initiates and disseminates research activities; provides leadership in the development, implementation and evaluation of evidence-based practice; and promotes the use of research to evaluate the outcomes of care while acting as a leader, resource person, preceptor and mentor for nurses, students and other professionals.

The NICU is a 30 bed Level II and Level III, tertiary referral center for all neonatal services for the province of Newfoundland and Labrador as well as for the French islands of St. Pierre and Miquelon.

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Constantly moves, lifts, or operates equipment/machinery up to 10 lbs. and regularly is required to lift/move equipment, books, supplies, and sometimes children up to 25 lbs. Occasionally, may have to reposition a patient over 50 lbs.
Physical effort also includes regular sitting to conduct patient histories, performing work on the computer and when assessing patients, regularly stands or walks.
When performing procedures, regularly uses fine finger/precision work and hand tools (i.e. medical instruments, computer mouse, stethoscope, etc.) requiring accurate control and steadiness.
Visual concentration is required when performing physical assessment and procedures, completing charts/reports, observing patients, reading equipment/monitors, and completing work-related correspondence on the computer.

Job Qualifications
Completion of an approved/recognized Neonatal Nurse Practitioner program is required.
Current and continuing registration with the College of Registered Nurses of NL (CRNNL) and Licensed (or eligible for licensure) as a Nurse Practitioner (Pediatric- with specialized education relevant to neonatology) with the CRNNL is required.
A minimum of five years' nursing experience within the last seven years working in neonatal intensive care is required.
Current BCLS Certification is required.
Current Neonatal Resuscitation Program (NRP) Certification is required.
Demonstrated exceptional critical thinking and clinical judgement skills.
Possessed strong abilities in the areas of collaboration, clinical reasoning, professional development, interpersonal effectiveness, conflict management and teamwork.
Demonstrated progressive clinical leadership skills.
Possessed strong communication, problem solving, decision-making, and teaching skills.
Demonstrated ability to function autonomously in an advanced practice role.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively within an interprofessional team.
Demonstrated commitment to support and participate in research to improve practice and client outcomes.
Demonstrated skills in computer and database management skills

We are a provincial health authority responsible for delivering quality health care to approximately 550,000 people in Newfoundland and Labrador. Guided by the vision of the Health Accord NL, we offer a range of health-care programs and services through a wide network of facilities, clinics, and community services across five zones: Central, Eastern-Rural, Eastern-Urban, Labrador-Grenfell, and Western.

## ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

NL Health Services – Central Zone invites applications for five (5) permanent full-time Internal Medicine Physicians at James Paton Memorial Regional Health Centre in Gander, NL.

The successful candidates will provide comprehensive Internal Medicine services to patients across the Central Zone, working within a collaborative and well-supported interdisciplinary team. The position includes both inpatient and outpatient Internal Medicine care, with on-call coverage shared equitably among the physician group.

Central Zone is the second largest health zone in NL Health Services, serving approximately 90,000 people across 176 communities. The region extends from Charlottetown in the east, Fogo Island in the north, Harbour Breton in the south, to Baie Verte in the west — encompassing more than half the total land mass of the island of Newfoundland.

James Paton Memorial Regional Health Centre is the primary acute care facility for the Central Zone, serving as a regional referral centre for the zone and providing a broad range of secondary services to the communities of central Newfoundland.

NL Health Services is affiliated with the Faculty of Medicine at Memorial University of Newfoundland and Labrador, and academic interests are encouraged and supported.

## Work Environment

Gander is a welcoming and well-serviced community in central Newfoundland, known for its friendly residents, rich aviation heritage, and easy access to the natural beauty of the region — including world-class salmon fishing, hiking, and stunning wilderness landscapes.

• Must satisfy credentialing requirements of NL Health Services including a satisfactory criminal record check and vulnerable sector check

About Us
Newfoundland and Labrador Health Services (NL Health Services) brings together five former separate health entities - Eastern Health, Central Health, Western Health, Labrador-Grenfell Health, and the Newfoundland and Labrador Centre for Health Information. The creation of a provincial health authority was announced following recommendations from Health Accord NL.

NL Health Services is responsible for delivering health and community services to more than 528,000 people living in Newfoundland and Labrador and employs over 21,000 people. NLHealthServices.ca.

Job Summary
The Nuclear Medicine Technologist IIA is responsible for performing standardized and complex diagnostic and therapeutic Nuclear Medicine procedures. This includes preparing, measuring, dispensing, and administering radiopharmaceuticals and radioisotopes for diagnostic and therapeutic use, assessing patients for exams and explaining procedures and tests, and performing quality control testing on all equipment. The Technologist also participates in research, is involved in quality control and radiation safety techniques and performs other related duties as required.

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Regularly lifts, moves, repositions, pushes, or pulls objects (i.e. supplies, equipment, cameras, lead vests, and patients), less than 10 lbs., between 10-50 lbs., and over 50 lbs.
Regularly stands or walks when performing procedures or scanning patients. Occasionally, works in awkward or cramped positions where maintaining balance is required while operating heavy machinery or equipment to perform scans.
Scanning patients requires controlled movements while physically handling cameras. Occasionally will sit to review images and use fine finger/precision movements to work on the computer, walk, and bend to give injections using fine motor skills.
Visual concentration is required when reading physicians' orders, positioning patients, drawing up radiation into syringes, calculating and measuring dosages, inserting venipuncture and intravenous (IV) lines, giving injections, examining detailed computer images, computer processing, and monitoring patients during procedures.

Job Qualifications
Graduation from a recognized (accredited) program in Nuclear Medicine Technology is required.
Current registration and member in good standing with the Canadian Association of Medical Radiation Technologists (CAMRT) in Nuclear Medicine.
A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. The Ambulance Operator/Attendant will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will provide assistance to the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

* A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

Newfoundland and Labrador Health Services (NL Health Services) brings together five former separate health entities - Eastern Health, Central Health, Western Health, Labrador-Grenfell Health, and the Newfoundland and Labrador Centre for Health Information. Our team is seeking an Advanced Care Paramedic (ACP) for a full-time position. If no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics (PCP) and Ambulance Operators/Attendants/Emergency Medical Responder (EMR). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR).

If the competition is awarded to a PCP or Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) as the next highest classification, they will be awarded as temporary full time (TFT) until the ACP position is filled.

Job Summary
The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of Paramedicine. The base for this service is located in Marystown.

Duties/Job Demands
The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will provide assistance to the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

## Qualifications

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;

• Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory record of work performance is required.

## ABOUT NL HEALTH SERVICES

We are a provincial health authority responsible for delivering quality health care to approximately 550,000 people in Newfoundland and Labrador. Supported by over 23,000 employees and physicians, our team works together to improve the health and well-being of every person, in every community. Guided by the vision of the Health Accord NL, we offer a range of health-care programs and services through a wide network of facilities, clinics, and community services across five zones: Central, Eastern-Rural, Eastern-Urban, Labrador-Grenfell, and Western.

At NL Health Services, we believe that our people — employees, doctors and volunteers — make it a great place to work. Every individual brings valuable knowledge, experience and perspective. ## Definition of work:

This service is fast paced and includes a patient population with high acuity in addition to a chronic stable population. The nursing position in the hemodialysis setting requires the ability to deliver high quality, safe patient care both independently and collaboratively. The registered nurse must apply advanced technical skills through operation of specialized equipment and must display the ability to interpret technical information to provide safe, appropriate clinical interventions. Hemodialysis offers both an exciting and challenging professional work environment. Work involves providing nursing care and treatment services for the Hemodialysis Unit in the James Paton Regional Health Centre.

Under the NLHS model of nursing care, the RN is required to provide comprehensive patient care that includes pre-dialysis patient assessment, completing a plan of care, initiating treatment, monitoring and ongoing assessment during dialysis treatment, discontinuing treatment, post dialysis assessment, evaluation, and appropriate documentation. Significant critical thinking and problem-solving abilities are required. On a continual basis throughout the workday, the successful candidate will be responsible to critically assess patients and make appropriate decisions to ensure safe patient outcomes.

The registered nurse will be accountable and responsible to function independently within the daily patient assignment in addition to participating as a collaborative interdisciplinary team member. The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centred care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

## Required qualifications:

• Graduation from an accredited school of nursing.
• Current registration with the Association of Registered Nurses of Newfoundland and Labrador.
• Current BLS certification for health care providers from the Heart and Stroke Foundation.
• Current Health Assessment certification or willingness to complete next available course.
• Two (2) years of clinical experience in Dialysis in the last five (5) years.
• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Services core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect, and Excellence (ICARE)
• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position.
• A satisfactory Certificate of Conduct from the RCMP or local police authority.

Posted Date: 2026-03-19

Closing Date: Open until filled.

Our team is seeking an Advanced Care Paramedic to this position. If there are no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics (PCP). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic.
If the competition is awarded to a PCP as the next highest classification, they will be awarded as temporary full time (TFT) and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

Job Summary:
The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.
The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.
The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

Duties/Job Demands:
The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.
The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

Job Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;
• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.
• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.
• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

Qualifications:
• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;
• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP or PCP;
• Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director
• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;
• Current certification in Basic Life Support;
• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);
• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)
• Effective oral and written communication skills;
• Critical and sound decision making skills;
• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;
• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.
• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;
• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;
• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;
• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

Job Summary
The Nuclear and Molecular Medicine Technologist III is responsible for the day-to-day operations and implementation of the only Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography (PET/CT) program in Newfoundland & Labrador. This position performs specialized and advanced diagnostic imaging procedures using a PET/CT camera and involves administering radioactive materials and contrast with very specific timing/and flow rates to visualize the anatomical regions that are required. The result is a very detailed image that the Nuclear Medicine Physicians review to determine whether surgical interventions, oncology treatments, or palliative treatments are required. The results of the scans help the Oncologists to treat cancer patients, Cardiologists to treat cardiac patients, Neurologists to diagnose varying neurological conditions, and Internists to treat patients with infections in varying parts of their body. The Nuclear and Molecular Medicine Technologist IIIs are classified as Nuclear Energy Workers (NEW).

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Regularly moves or lifts objects between 10-50+ lbs. such as shielded radioactive sources and lead bricks.
Occasionally pushes and pulls objects or transports patients over 50 lbs. in wheelchairs or stretchers.
Regularly stands, walks, or sits for extended periods to perform activities.
A very high level of alertness and attentiveness is required when performing scans/procedures due to patients' condition, safety and because some scans/procedures are captured in real time.
Regularly performs fine finger/precision computer work; handling of open-source radioactivity and radioactive equipment/components requiring steadiness and accurate movement/control.
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) are a regular requirement, including gloves and gowns.

Job Qualifications
Graduation from a recognized (accredited) program in Nuclear Medicine Technology is required.
Successful completion of the CAMRT Computed Tomography (CT) Imaging or PET/CT Certificate Program is required.
Current registration and member in good standing with the Canadian Association of Medical Radiation Technologists (CAMRT).
Current BLS Certification is required.
Strong understanding of radiation safety procedures and CNSC regulations.
Proven analytical, critical thinking, problem solving, decision-making and organizational skills.
A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required.

* Due to safety requirements this position will rotate through the PET/CT and Nuclear Medicine sections of the Nuclear and Molecular Medicine Division. Please note that shift start and stop times may change subject to operational requirements as the PET/CT program develops.

** The successful applicant must be eligible for Nuclear Energy Worker (NEW) status.

Effective May 1, 2025, all Medical Radiation Technologists and X - Ray Health Professionals will require registration with the Newfoundland and Labrador Council of Health Professionals (NLCHP) in the appropriate discipline(s) in order to practice in Newfoundland and Labrador.

If there are no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics (PCP) and Ambulance Operators/Attendants (also known as Emergency Medical Responder (EMR)). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to a PCP or EMR as the next highest classification, they will be temporarily awarded the position for the same number of hours indicated above and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will aid the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

## ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

NL Health Services – Eastern Urban Zone invites applications for a salaried Float Family Physician to join the Family Care Team (FCT) in the St. John's metro region.

The Primary Health Care Family Care Team mandate is to provide patients without a primary care provider in the St. John's and metro region with access to primary health care services. Services are delivered using an interprofessional collaborative approach where patients see the right provider at the right time and place. The team includes physicians, Nurse Practitioners, Registered Nurses including a diabetic nurse educator, clerical support, LPNs, pharmacists, social workers, dietitians, physiotherapists, and occupational therapists. All health care providers, including physicians, are expected to practice to their full scope of practice to meet patient needs.

Should no providers be on leave across the Family Care Teams, the incumbent will provide care at the Community Walk-In Clinic or the Mobile Primary Health Care Clinic. Job Summary
The Community Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports and the presence or absence of valid complaints. Advanced Community Care Paramedics report directly to the Manager of Community Paramedicine.

The Community Advanced Care Paramedic in this role also preforms community and palliative care and participates in other care initiatives as required. The duties and responsibilities of this position will include, but are not limited to: collaboration with other health care teams in the community setting including physician and nursing groups; education s of patients, families, and health care professionals on the scope of the Community Paramedicine Program; and collection of patient and key stakeholder feedback to support evolvement of the program.

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Regularly moves, lifts, or carries patients or equipment ranging from 10 to 50 pounds and occasionally in excess of 100 lbs. in challenging environments and which is not always conducive to proper ergonomics. Constantly bending, stretching, kneeling or pushing/pulling of stretchers (which require up to 35 lbs. of push/pull force or greater per employee as the terrain and weather conditions; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

Lack of control over work pace occurs due to unpredictable situations and/or call volume.

## Job Summary:

The Primary Care Paramedic, works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Primary Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as a PCP;

• Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

About the Role
The Youth Outreach Worker (YOW) is a frontline prevention and early intervention position within Mental Health & Addictions. Working with youth and young adults up to age 29, the Youth Outreach Worker provides community-based outreach, brief intervention, mental health promotion, addictions prevention, system navigation, and connection to services.

This position focuses on building trusting relationships with youth where they live, learn, work, and gather. Services are delivered through schools, community organizations, recreation settings, virtual platforms, and other community locations. The Youth Outreach Worker supports youth experiencing early signs of mental health, substance use, social, emotional, or life challenges and helps connect them to appropriate supports before concerns escalate into crisis.

Key Responsibilities
Build trusting, strengths-based relationships with youth and young adults.
Provide brief supportive interventions, risk assessments, safety planning, and referrals.
Support youth experiencing mental health concerns, substance use issues, social and emotional challenges, or other life stressors.
Facilitate youth-centred workshops, awareness initiatives, and group programming focused on mental wellness, resilience, life skills, and healthy coping.
Support youth in navigating health, education, social, and community systems.
Collaborate with families, schools, Indigenous organizations, municipalities, and community partners.
Maintain documentation, workload statistics, and reports in accordance with organizational standards.
Participate in multidisciplinary consultation, community development initiatives, and service planning activities.
Contribute to program development, quality improvement, and evaluation activities to support the ongoing enhancement of youth services.

Required Qualifications
Degree or diploma in Child and Youth Care, Social Work, Human Services, Psychology, Sociology, Community Studies, or related field.
Specialized education or training in mental health, addictions, youth engagement, harm reduction, suicide prevention, and/or brief intervention would be considered an asset.

Required Experience
Experience working with children, youth, young adults, and families.
Experience delivering community-based programs, outreach services, education sessions, or youth engagement initiatives.
Experience supporting individuals experiencing mental health, addictions, trauma, or social challenges would be considered an asset.

Required Knowledge and Skills
Demonstrated ability to engage and build rapport with youth.
Knowledge of child and adolescent development.
Knowledge of mental health promotion, addictions prevention, and harm reduction practices.
Understanding of trauma-informed, culturally safe, and youth-centred approaches.

Strong communication, facilitation, and presentation skills.
