2241463.description:
J.J. MacKay Canada Limited (MacKay Meters), an industry leader in the design, development and manufacturing of innovative industrial grade parking solutions and equipment, is currently seeking an Accounts Payable Clerk to join our dedicated accounting team at our corporate headquarters in New Glasgow, Nova Scotia, Canada.

Reporting to the Controller, the Accounts Payable Clerk is responsible for maintaining all phases of the accounts payable function, including entering and balancing accounts, and preparing payments.

## Responsibilities:

• Review and process all invoices received from vendors, reconcile vendor statements, deal with vendor inquiries, and resolve any discrepancies between invoice and purchase order.

• Enter invoices and expense reports into accounting software, ensuring that they have proper internal approvals and support. Code each of these to ensure they are being booked to the correct general ledger account.

• Code purchase orders/receipts with the appropriate general ledger account numbers and descriptions for analysis, ensuring inventory is being directed to the proper locations.

• Post receiving batches daily.

• Help ensure that all payment deadlines are met, coordinate payments on a weekly basis, this can include electronic payments or the weekly cheque run.

• Maintain and monitor the Accounts Payable Subledger and Filing System, maintain monthly expense analysis spreadsheet for various accounts, and prepare monthly close reports.

• Participate in year end audit by responding to auditor enquiries and preparing relevant reports as necessary. This includes but is not limited to the Aged Accounts Payable Subledger Report, Subsequent Disbursement Report, and Receiving Report After Inventory.

• Other duties as necessary.

## Qualifications:

• Completion of at least a one- or two-year business program

• Three to five years of experience in an accounting or accounts payable role

• A basic knowledge of bookkeeping and accounting principles

• Accounting experience in a light manufacturing environment is an asset

• The initiative to work independently and as part of a team with all levels of staff and management

• A solid track record of personal and professional integrity

• Good oral and written communication skills

• Ability to manage multiple tasks, prioritize, and work under tight deadlines

• Ability to carry out general administrative duties

• Experience with Microsoft® Dynamics Great Plains or a similar accounting software is an asset

• Proficiency in Microsoft® Excel, Microsoft® Word and email applications.

## Additional Information:

This is a full-time position offering group insurance benefits, company RRSP and salary commensurate with experience and qualifications.

The successful candidate must provide a satisfactory criminal records check.

## How to Apply:

Please send your cover letter and résumé/CV, indicating relevant experience for this position, to hr.mgr@mackaymeters.com. Please no telephone inquiries.

We thank all applicants for their interest, however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

## About J.J. MacKay Canada Limited:

J.J. MacKay Canada Limited is a Nova Scotia based company and an industry leader in the manufacture and supply of innovative parking equipment and parking solutions. We have been providing our parking products, services and solutions to Canadian, US, and international clients for over 60 years. The parking IT solutions we provide include traditional client/server applications with associated databases installed at our client sites as well as products that require customized software development, mobile applications, web based (remote) applications and client data hosting. Our web site is https://mackaymeters.com.

Department: Public Works

Location: NEW GLASGOW

Type of Employment: Term

Union Status: NSGEU - NSPG

Closing Date: 13-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
The Building Services Division of the Department of Public Works is responsible for the operation and maintenance of 2,200 provincial buildings and structures across Nova Scotia. We maintain various buildings including museums, core government buildings, office buildings, correctional centers, and justice centers. Daily, we are responsible for ensuring these buildings are best served, including all matters related to building operations, building systems maintenance, renovations, and new construction.

Who are we Looking For
Are you a problem solver? Do you thrive in a team environment? Are your best days spent in the field making sure buildings and associated equipment are operating safely and appropriately? Working with your hands to get the job done intrigues you?

If you are driven, customer-focused and eager to learn, then this role is for you.

About the Role
Your role is pivotal in supporting the safety and efficiency of our provincial building infrastructure. Your role involves overseeing the daily operation, reporting and maintenance of building infrastructure in various government buildings under the direction of your Supervisor. This responsibility is crucial to ensuring uninterrupted services provided by our government.

You will need to be familiar with the Occupational Safety General Regulations and the Occupational Health and Safety Act. Working knowledge of the National Building Code and the National Fire Code will be integral to success in your role as Building Operator.

What You Will Be Doing
As the Building Operator, you will be responsible for:

• Using your various skills and expertise to identify potential problems, determine solutions, and physically complete minor carpentry, mechanical, and electrical repairs and develop solutions to inefficiencies.

• Assisting with enhancing and administering a scheduled preventative maintenance program, while prioritizing work efficiently to minimize disruption to building tenants.

• Ensuring all equipment performs and operates properly and provides a safe, secure, effective, and efficient work environment daily.

• Completing and arranging for completion of buildings assigned PMWO's & reactive WO's (if a work order requires a specialized tradesperson or contractor to complete the BO is to assure it gets completed).

• Establishing and maintaining effective communication and coordination with other divisions, project teams, facility clients, other government departments, consultants, and contractors related to expected and unexpected changes in operations.

You will have an opportunity to work on:

• Plumbing infrastructure; (such as heating systems, pumps, condensers, condensate tanks and air separators).

• Mechanical / HVAC equipment (such as boilers, chillers, air handling equipment, pneumatic and electronic controls, diesel/electric generators, cooling towers, sprinkler pumps and air compressors).

• Electrical systems (such as electronic monitoring systems, security systems and computerized fire alarm systems); automated systems (Building automation systems).

Qualifications, Experience & Skills
High School completion and five (5) years of related experience in operating and maintaining commercial or institutional buildings is required.

An equivalent combination of education, training and experience will be considered.

• Familiarity in a computerized environment, including spreadsheet, word processing, and email applications, is essential.

• Experience with a computerized building maintenance management system and familiarity with government procurement policy and tendering procedures are considered an asset.

You demonstrate a sound knowledge of all aspects of building construction and operation, including:

• Architectural, plumbing, electrical, fire suppression and HVAC systems; and

• Reading and interpreting various specifications and drawings.

We will assess all qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
An equivalent combination of training, education and experience will be considered. Related equivalencies may include, but are not limited to:

• Power Engineer 3rd or 4th Class certificate and four (4) years of related experience

2241478.title: General Manager & Regional Governance Modernization Lead
2241478.description:
General Manager & Regional Governance Modernization Lead
Yarmouth, Nova Scotia
Reference #JL-MDY-9785

The Yarmouth Area Industrial Commission (YAIC) is a regional economic development organization focused on supporting sustainable growth and prosperity throughout the Yarmouth region. Through strategic management of key assets, stakeholder partnerships, and economic development initiatives, YAIC plays an important role in advancing opportunities that benefit businesses, residents, and communities.

YAIC is seeking a collaborative and strategic leader to serve as General Manager & Regional Governance Modernization Lead. This unique position combines operational leadership of the Commission with a regional mandate to coordinate governance modernization initiatives across three municipal partners.

## The Role

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the General Manager & Regional Governance Modernization Lead is responsible for the overall management and strategic direction of YAIC. The role provides leadership in operational planning, financial stewardship, stakeholder relations, contract management, and governance support while ensuring the organization achieves its strategic objectives.

Approximately 70% of the role is dedicated to General Manager responsibilities, including oversight of port operations, leases, financial management, and organizational performance. The remaining 30% is focused on advancing a regional governance modernization initiative, supporting municipal partners as they explore opportunities to strengthen collaboration, service delivery, and regional governance models.

This position operates within a service delivery model that utilizes contracted and outsourced expertise for selected administrative, financial, legal, engineering, and technical services. The General Manager maintains accountability for oversight, performance management, and coordination of all external service providers.

## Duties & Responsibilities:

• Provide strategic advice and operational leadership to the Board of Directors.

• Oversee port operations, leases, tenant relationships, and related business activities.

• Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory, contractual, and governance requirements.

• Lead organizational financial planning, budgeting, reporting, and risk management activities.

• Manage relationships with government partners, tenants, community stakeholders, and industry representatives.

• Represent YAIC in meetings, public engagements, and regional initiatives.

• Develop and manage service agreements with contracted providers and consultants.

• Monitor outsourced services to ensure quality, timeliness, cost-effectiveness, and compliance with organizational expectations.

• Oversee contract administration and performance management of external service providers.

• Identify opportunities to optimize service delivery through a balance of internal and outsourced resources.

• Coordinate and advance regional governance modernization initiatives involving multiple municipal partners.

• Support research, analysis, policy development, and implementation planning related to governance modernization.

• Prepare reports, recommendations, and presentations for municipal and organizational stakeholders.

• Coordinate consultants, funding opportunities, project timelines, and stakeholder engagement activities.

• Support change management efforts and facilitate collaboration among participating organizations.

• Track progress toward strategic objectives and modernization milestones.

## Qualifications & Experience:

• Degree in public administration, business administration, finance, economics, governance, or a related discipline. Equivalent experience will also be considered.

• Progressive leadership experience within municipal government, economic development, public sector organizations, not-for-profit entities, or related environments.

• Experience in governance, financial management, contract administration, and strategic planning.

• Demonstrated success managing outsourced or vendor-delivered service models.

• Strong understanding of public sector governance, stakeholder engagement, and organizational accountability.

• Experience leading projects that involve multiple organizations, partners, or levels of government.

• Strong financial and analytical skills with experience interpreting budgets, reports, and performance metrics.

• Exceptional communication, relationship-building, and facilitation skills.

• Political acumen and the ability to navigate complex stakeholder environments.

• Proven ability to manage competing priorities and deliver results in a dynamic environment.

## What Success Looks Like:

• Effective oversight and delivery of outsourced services within budget and established performance expectations.

• Advancement and achievement of regional governance modernization milestones.

• Strong financial stewardship and operational performance.

• Positive stakeholder relationships and successful regional collaboration.

• High levels of Board confidence and satisfaction with organizational leadership and strategic direction.

## To express interest in this opportunity please apply online directly here.

If you have any questions, please contact Kate Spares, Recruitment Specialist, at kspares@kbrs.ca or Jeff Lanthier, Partner, at jlanthier@kbrs.ca. If you require accommodation to participate in the recruitment process, please let us know.

Meridia Recruitment Solutions connects leading organizations with top talent by building strong relationships and creating ideal matches with candidates because we are only successful when you are. We appreciate your interest in this opportunity.

To learn more about Meridia Recruitment Solutions, our job opportunities, and career advice we invite you to explore our site and subscribe for career alerts.

Competition # : 50012

Department: Cyber Security & Digital Solutions

Location: HALIFAX

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: NSGEU - NSPG

Closing Date: 13-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
At CSDS, we prioritize people—both within our team and in the communities we serve. Our mission is to redefine how Nova Scotians engage with government by creating accessible, reliable digital solutions centered around user needs.
In today's tech-driven world, CSDS empowers government departments with essential digital solutions to meet Nova Scotians' expectations. As a trusted partner across government, we enable departments to fulfill their mandates with secure, user-friendly services. From healthcare and education to public safety, we collaborate to transform how services are designed and delivered.
We don't just implement technology; we modernize outdated systems and reimagine processes. Our agile, data-driven approach ensures that digital services are both efficient and adaptable to Nova Scotia's evolving needs.
Joining CSDS means contributing to work that makes a real difference. From providing vital tech support to healthcare professionals to strengthening cybersecurity and developing scalable digital platforms, you'll play a key role in building a more inclusive, responsive government for Nova Scotians.
Together, we're setting new standards for digital public service, delivering resilient solutions that meet today's needs—and anticipate tomorrow's challenges.

About Our Opportunity
As a Technical Architect in the Integration & Security team, you will design, support, and optimize the integration platforms that enable enterprise applications to communicate and exchange data securely and reliably. The role provides technical leadership for middleware technologies, APIs, web services, and system integrations, ensuring the availability, performance, and security of critical business applications. Responsibilities include troubleshooting complex integration issues, supporting application deployments and upgrades, performance tuning, security assessments, and providing technical guidance on system architecture and integration solutions. The position plays a key role in maintaining and enhancing the digital services that support business operations across the organization.
Your work will support government departments, agencies, boards, and commissions, as well as Nova Scotia Health and the IWK Health Centre. You will collaborate with different teams and build trusted relationships with a wide range of clients and partners to integrate solutions, implement governance around accounts and access, and resolve problems through clear communications.
This role requires deep expertise with a focus on understanding interactions between different systems and interdependencies in the delivery of enterprise Integration & Security services.

Primary Accountabilities
To succeed in this role, you must be objective, professional, thorough, data-driven, and have clarity of thought and purpose. Your technical competence, work ethic, and communications will ensure that the government Integration & Security services are secure, resilient, and user friendly.
In this role, you will:

• Serve as a subject matter expert for the Integration & Security team.

• Design, implement, and support application integrations, APIs, and web services.

• Maintain and optimize middleware platforms and integration services.

• Troubleshoot and resolve complex application and data integration issues.

• Perform application configuration, patching, performance tuning, and technical support.

• Conduct security reviews and implement mitigation measures for integrated solutions.

• Provide technical consulting and guidance on system architecture and integration design.

• Support critical enterprise applications and data exchange services.

• Manage incidents, service requests, changes, and problems, implementing corrective and preventive actions as needed.

• Coach and mentor team members to promote knowledge sharing, consistency, and operational excellence.

Qualifications and Experience
To be successful in this role, you will have a Bachelor of Science in Computer Science plus a minimum of 5 years' experience, or graduation from a recognized Information Technology program plus 5 years and 6 months experience, or an acceptable equivalent combination of training and experience.
Requirements

• System Administration - particularly with Red Hat Enterprise Linux

About Us
Building and maintaining our provincial infrastructure is no small job.
The Building Services Division of the Department of Public Works is responsible for the operation and maintenance of 2,200 provincial buildings and structures across Nova Scotia. We maintain various buildings including museums, political core buildings, office buildings, fishery centres, correctional centres, and justice centres. Daily, we are responsible for ensuring these buildings are best served; including all matters related to building operations, building systems maintenance, renovations, and new construction.

About Our Opportunity
As the Building Operator 4, you are pivotal in supporting the overall safety and efficiency of our provincial building infrastructure. You will be responsible for supervising Building Operators in the performance of operation, repair, maintenance and installation duties; ensuring work requirements are achieved in safe and timely manners, within budgets. You will prepare work schedules, evaluate work performance, and provide technical guidance to your supervised staff.
You are critical in ensuring that the daily operation and maintenance of building infrastructure in various government buildings are safe, efficient, and that there are no interruptions to services provided by our government as a result of building equipment issues or failures.
As the ideal candidate you build relationships and demonstrate leadership qualities which promote teamwork; communicating vision and fostering a safe work culture that encourages new ideas and innovative solutions. You have proven and professional communication skills, both oral and written, for collaborating with your staff and clients. You have well developed planning and organizational skills, coupled with the ability to multi-task and adapt in this fast-paced environment with competing priorities. Consistently, you maintain a courteous disposition and hold a high standard for client and customer service.

This position provides the opportunity to collaborate with various government Departments and staff, vendors, contractors and consultants to ensure all construction projects, equipment installations and system upgrades minimize building disruptions.

Primary Accountabilities
Using your various skills and expertise, you will complete minor carpentry, mechanical, and electrical repairs and develop solutions to inefficiencies. You will also assist with enhancing and administering a scheduled preventative maintenance program, all the while prioritizing work efficiently to minimize disruption to building tenants. Daily, you ensure all equipment performs and operates properly and provides a safe, secure, effective and efficient work environment.
You'll have the opportunity to work on:

• Special projects as assigned;

• Plumbing infrastructure;

• Mechanical equipment (such as boilers, chillers, pneumatic and electronic controls, diesel/electric generators, cooling towers, sprinkler pumps and air compressors);

• Electrical systems (such as electronic monitoring systems, security systems and computerized fire alarm systems); and

• Automated control systems.

Qualifications and Experience
High school completion plus a Power Engineer 3rd Class certificate and five (5) years of related experience in the operation and maintenance of commercial or institutional buildings is required. An equivalent combination of education, training and experience will be considered.
Previous experience supervising a team, along with demonstrated leadership qualities, is required. You must demonstrate the ability to effectively organize and plan, schedule, prioritize and assign work to ensure effective use of resources and to minimize building disruptions.
You demonstrate a sound knowledge of all aspects of building construction and operation, including:

• Architectural, plumbing, electrical, fire suppression and HVAC systems;

• Reading and interpreting various specifications and drawings;

• Working knowledge of the National Building Code and the National Fire Code;

• Familiarity with the Occupational Safety General Regulations and the Occupational Health and Safety Act; and

• Familiarity in a computerized environment including spreadsheets, word processing and email applications.

Experience with the following are considered assets:

• Collective agreements and unionized work environments;

• Computerized building maintenance management systems; and

• Government procurement policy and tendering procedures.

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
An equivalent combination of training, education and experience will be considered. Related equivalencies may include, but are not limited to:

• Power Engineer 3rd Class certificate and six (6) years of related experience

Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
This is a labour-intensive opportunity requiring physical strength and dexterity. At times, you are subject to various environmental and temperature extremes. Overtime is often necessary when installations and maintenance requires disruption or shutting down of power supply and other services that would disrupt building activities.
The successful incumbent must be available to respond to emergency calls, at any time, when building systems fail or building security is compromised.

As travel is a component of this position, you must have a valid driver's license and access to a reliable motor vehicle.

2241473.title: Francophone Workforce Development Officer/Agent(e) de développement de la main-d'œuvre, Bilingue
2241473.employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
2241473.description:
## Numéro de concours 50050

Francophone Workforce Development Officer/Agent(e) de développement de la main-d'œuvre, Bilingue, Permanent, HALIFAX

## Education & Early Childhood Development

Date de clôture : 13-Oct-26 (Les candidatures sont acceptées jusqu'à 23 h 59, heure de l'Atlantique)

Notre objectif est d'avoir une main-d'œuvre diversifiée représentative de la population que nous servons, et ce, à tous les niveaux d'emploi. Le gouvernement de la Nouvelle-Écosse a adopté une politique d'équité en matière d'emploi, et nous invitons les demandes de personnes autochtones, afro-néo-écossaises et d'autres groupes raciaux visibles, de personnes handicapées et de femmes pour des emplois ou des postes où ces personnes sont sous-représentées. Si vous êtes membre d'un de ces groupes, nous vous encourageons à l'indiquer dans votre formulaire de demande, votre lettre d'accompagnement ou votre curriculum vitæ.

À notre sujet
La Direction des programmes et services en français du ministère de l'Éducation et du Développement de la petite enfance (MEDPE) soutient l'avancement de l'éducation en français et de l'apprentissage du français langue seconde en Nouvelle-Écosse. Guidée par les principes d'équité linguistique, d'inclusion et de vitalité culturelle, elle veille à offrir aux communautés acadiennes et francophones un accès à des programmes et à des services éducatifs de grande qualité dans leur langue.

En collaboration avec des partenaires gouvernementaux, communautaires, provinciaux, nationaux et internationaux, la Direction développe et met en œuvre des initiatives, des programmes et des partenariats qui contribuent au rayonnement de la langue française, au développement de la main-d'œuvre éducative francophone et à la pérennité de l'éducation en français. Son travail favorise notamment le recrutement et l'intégration et la rétention de professionnels qualifiés au sein du système éducatif néo-écossais.

La Direction appuie également les occasions d'apprentissage du français pour les élèves anglophones de la province, contribuant ainsi au bilinguisme, à la compréhension interculturelle et à la dualité linguistique canadienne. Par son leadership et ses actions stratégiques, elle contribue à bâtir un système d'éducation inclusif, équitable et culturellement riche qui soutient l'épanouissement des communautés acadiennes et francophones tout en bénéficiant à l'ensemble des Néo-Écossaises et des Néo-Écossais.

Au sujet de cet emploi
Sous la supervision de la Direction de partenariats des programmes et services en français, la personne titulaire assure un leadership stratégique dans le développement de la main-d'œuvre francophone en éducation en Nouvelle-Écosse.

Elle planifie, développe, coordonne et évalue des stratégies et des initiatives visant à renforcer le recrutement, l'accueil, l'intégration, le perfectionnement et la rétention du personnel éducatif francophone. Son mandat comprend notamment le soutien aux enseignants formés à l'étranger, aux enseignants immigrants, aux assistants de langue et aux autres professionnels appelés à travailler dans les milieux éducatifs francophones et d'immersion française.

La personne titulaire mobilise les partenaires gouvernementaux, éducatifs, communautaires, postsecondaires, nationaux et internationaux afin de répondre aux besoins actuels et émergents du secteur. Elle contribue à la création de parcours durables vers les professions en éducation, à la reconnaissance et à la valorisation des compétences ainsi qu'au développement d'un environnement accueillant, inclusif et favorable à la rétention du personnel francophone.

Responsabilités principales
Élaborer une stratégie de développement de la main-d'œuvre
Élaborer, mettre en œuvre et évaluer des stratégies visant à répondre aux besoins actuels et futurs en personnel éducatif francophone et francophile dans les milieux scolaires et éducatifs de la Nouvelle-Écosse.

Analyser les besoins et les tendances du marché du travail
Réaliser des recherches, des consultations et des analyses afin de cerner les pénuries, les besoins émergents, les obstacles au recrutement et à la rétention ainsi que les possibilités de développement de nouveaux bassins de main-d'œuvre.

Développer des initiatives de recrutement ciblées
Concevoir et coordonner, en lien avec le CSAP et les CRE, des initiatives provinciales, nationales et internationales permettant d'attirer des enseignants, des assistants de langue et d'autres professionnels qualifiés vers les milieux éducatifs francophones et d'immersion française.

Soutenir l'accueil, l'intégration et la rétention: Développer des mesures d'accompagnement favorisant l'établissement professionnel, culturel et communautaire des nouvelles recrues, notamment les enseignants formés à l'étranger, les enseignants immigrants et les assistants de langue.

Créer des parcours vers les professions en éducation Collaborer avec les universités, les collèges, les établissements scolaires, les organismes de réglementation et les partenaires communautaires afin de faciliter l'accès à la formation, aux stages, à la certification, au perfectionnement professionnel et aux carrières en éducation.

Mobiliser des partenariats stratégiques Établir et entretenir des partenariats avec les ministères provinciaux et fédéraux, les établissements postsecondaires, les employeurs du secteur éducatif, les organismes communautaires et les organisations de la francophonie afin de coordonner les efforts et des pistes communes liés à la main-d'œuvre.

Développer des projets de mobilité et de coopération internationale Concevoir et coordonner, avec le Consulat général de France, l'Ambassade de France au Canada et d'autres partenaires internationaux, des projets de recrutement, de mobilité professionnelle, de stages, d'échanges d'expertise et de coopération éducative.

Gérer les projets Assurer la gestion complète des initiatives liées à la main-d'œuvre, y compris la planification, les budgets, les échéanciers, la mesure des résultats et la reddition de comptes.

Fournir des conseils stratégiques et produire la documentation requise Conseiller la direction sur les enjeux de recrutement, d'intégration et de rétention, et préparer des notes d'information, des analyses, des recommandations, des demandes de financement, des présentations, des ententes et des rapports.

Représenter le ministère et évaluer les résultats Représenter le ministère auprès des comités, des réseaux et des tables de concertation liés à la main-d'œuvre francophone en éducation, tout en évaluant l'efficacité, l'incidence et la pérennité des initiatives mises en œuvre.

À votre sujet
La personne recherchée est une personne professionnelle bilingue et mobilisatrice qui possède une expérience en développement de la main-d'œuvre, en gestion de projets et en création de partenariats stratégiques. Elle comprend les réalités de l'éducation en français en milieu minoritaire et en français langue seconde ainsi que les enjeux liés au recrutement, à l'intégration, à la certification et à la rétention du personnel éducatif francophone.

Elle possède un diplôme universitaire dans un domaine pertinent et au moins cinq années d'expérience connexe, ou une combinaison équivalente de formation et d'expérience. Elle sait notamment :

-concevoir et coordonner des initiatives visant à accroître la disponibilité de personnel qualifié en éducation francophone;

-mobiliser des partenaires gouvernementaux, éducatifs, communautaires et internationaux;

-appuyer le recrutement, l'intégration et la rétention du personnel éducatif;

-comprendre les processus de certification professionnelle ainsi que les programmes d'immigration et de mobilité internationale;

-gérer des projets complexes, des ententes de financement, des budgets et des exigences de reddition de comptes;

-analyser des données et formuler des recommandations stratégiques;

-animer des consultations et des tables de concertation;

-communiquer efficacement en français et en anglais, à l'oral comme à l'écrit.

Son leadership, son jugement et sa capacité à établir des relations de confiance lui permettent de contribuer concrètement au renforcement de la main-d'œuvre en éducation francophone et à la vitalité des communautés acadiennes et francophones de la Nouvelle-Écosse.

Exigences linguistiques
Vous devez posséder un niveau avancé de bilinguisme (français et anglais), tant à l'oral qu'à l'écrit, ainsi qu'une capacité démontrée à travailler et à communiquer efficacement dans les deux langues officielles.

Our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative, at all job levels, of the citizens we serve. The Government of Nova Scotia has an Employment Equity Policy and we welcome applications from Aboriginal People, African Nova Scotians and Other Racially Visible Persons, Persons with Disabilities and Women in occupations or positions where they are under-represented. If you are a member of one of the equity groups, you are encouraged to self-identify, on your application form, cover letter, or on your resume.

About Us
The French Programs and Services Branch of the Department of Education and Early Childhood Development (EECD) supports the advancement of French-language education and French second-language learning in Nova Scotia. Guided by the principles of linguistic equity, inclusion, and cultural vitality, the Branch works to ensure that Acadian and francophone communities have access to high-quality educational programs and services in their language.

In collaboration with governmental, community, provincial, national, and international partners, the Branch develops and implements initiatives, programs, and partnerships that contribute to the promotion of the French language, the development of the francophone education workforce, and the sustainability of French-language education. Its work notably supports the recruitment, integration, and retention of qualified professionals within Nova Scotia's education system.

The Branch also supports opportunities for English-speaking students across the province to learn French, thereby contributing to bilingualism, intercultural understanding, and Canada's linguistic duality. Through its leadership and strategic actions, it helps build an inclusive, equitable, and culturally rich education system that supports the growth and well-being of Acadian and francophone communities while benefiting all Nova Scotians.

About Our Opportunity
Reporting to the Director of French Program Partnerships within the French Programs and Services Branch, the successful candidate provides strategic leadership in the development of the francophone education workforce in Nova Scotia.

The incumbent plans, develops, coordinates, and evaluates strategies and initiatives aimed at strengthening the recruitment, onboarding, integration, professional development, and retention of francophone education personnel. This includes supporting internationally educated teachers, immigrant teachers, language assistants, and other professionals working in francophone and French immersion educational settings.

The incumbent mobilizes governmental, educational, community, post-secondary, national, and international partners to address current and emerging workforce needs. They contribute to the creation of sustainable pathways into education professions, the recognition and promotion of skills and qualifications, and the development of a welcoming, inclusive environment that supports the retention of francophone personnel.

Key Responsibilities

## Develop a Workforce Development Strategy

Develop, implement, and evaluate strategies that address current and future workforce needs for Francophone and Francophile educational personnel across Nova Scotia's schools and educational settings.

## Analyze Workforce Needs and Labour Market Trends

Conduct research, consultations, and analyses to identify workforce shortages, emerging needs, recruitment and retention barriers, and opportunities to develop new talent pools.

## Develop Targeted Recruitment Initiatives

Design and coordinate, in collaboration with CSAP and Regional Centres for Education (RCEs), provincial, national, and international recruitment initiatives aimed at attracting teachers, language assistants, and other qualified professionals to francophone and French immersion educational settings.

## Support Onboarding, Integration, and Retention

Develop support measures that facilitate the professional, cultural, and community integration of new hires, particularly internationally educated teachers, immigrant teachers, and language assistants.

## Create Pathways into Education Professions

Collaborate with universities, colleges, schools, regulatory bodies, and community partners to facilitate access to education, practicums, certification, professional development, and careers in education.

## Mobilize Strategic Partnerships

Establish and maintain partnerships with provincial and federal government departments, post-secondary institutions, education sector employers, community organizations, and francophone organizations to coordinate workforce-related efforts and shared initiatives.

## Develop International Mobility and Cooperation Projects

Design and coordinate recruitment, professional mobility, internship, knowledge-exchange, and educational cooperation projects with the Consulate General of France, the Embassy of France in Canada, and other international partners.

## Manage Projects

Provide full project management for workforce initiatives, including planning, budgeting, scheduling, performance measurement, and reporting.

## Provide Strategic Advice and Produce Required Documentation

Advise management on recruitment, integration, and retention issues, and prepare briefing notes, analyses, recommendations, funding applications, presentations, agreements, and reports.

## Represent the Department and Evaluate Results

Represent the Department on committees, networks, and collaborative tables related to the francophone education workforce while evaluating the effectiveness, impact, and sustainability of implemented initiatives.

About You
The ideal candidate is a bilingual, collaborative, and results-oriented professional with experience in workforce development, project management, and strategic partnership building. They understand the realities of French-language education in minority settings and French second-language education, as well as the challenges related to the recruitment, integration, certification, and retention of francophone educational personnel.

The successful candidate has a university degree in a relevant field and at least five years of related experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. They can:

• Design and coordinate initiatives aimed at increasing the availability of qualified personnel in francophone education.

• Engage government, education, community, and international partners.

• Support the recruitment, onboarding, integration, and retention of educational personnel.

• Understand professional certification processes, as well as immigration and international mobility programs.

• Manage complex projects, funding agreements, budgets, and accountability requirements.

• Analyze data and develop strategic recommendations.

• Facilitate consultations and stakeholder engagement tables.

• Communicate effectively in both French and English, verbally and in writing.

The candidate's leadership, judgment, and ability to build trusted relationships enable them to make a tangible contribution to strengthening the francophone education workforce and supporting the vitality of Nova Scotia's Acadian and francophone communities.

Language Requirements
You must demonstrate an advanced level of bilingualism (French and English), both written and spoken, and have proven ability to work and communicate effectively in both official languages.

This combination of skills and experience will enable the incumbent to contribute effectively to the Department's priorities related to French-language education, francophone workforce development, international cooperation, and the vitality of Nova Scotia's Acadian and francophone communities.

2241052.title: Lease Administration Coordinator
2241052.description:
The Franchise Management Group of Companies (FMI) is one of the largest restaurant franchisees in North America. We currently own and operate more than 400 Pizza Hut, KFC, Taco Bell, Burger King, and Panera Bread locations across 20 different provinces and states. With presence in all 10 provinces and 11 states, FMI is proud to employ over 6,500 people. All operations are administered from our Support Center in Woodstock, New Brunswick.

The Lease Administration Coordinator will be responsible for the preparation, coordination, administration and execution of commercial lease documentation using approved templates and standard forms, including proposals, new leases, renewals, amendments, assignments, consents, notices and other related documentation. The position will also support the administration of our leases throughout their lifecycle, including maintaining accurate lease records and system data and working closely with Legal, Operations, Property Management, Development, Finance and other internal and external stakeholders. This position will report directly to our Manager of Commercial Leasing and Property Administration.

Qualifications

## What Will You Bring to the Role?

The successful candidate should have a sound understanding of commerical lease documentation, commercial real estate terminology and the lease-administration process. The candidate should also have:

• Strong organizational and administrative coordination skills;

• Excellent attention to detail and a high regard for accuracy and confidentiality;

• The ability to manage a high volume of files and competing priorities independently;

• The ability to read and understand commercial lease provisions and accurately administer the resulting obligations;

• Strong written and verbal communication skills;

• Strong analytical, problem-solving and critical-thinking abilities;

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office, specifically Excel;

• Experience with lease-administration or document-management systems, such as LeaseQuery, as an asset; and

• French/English bilingualism as an asset.

The starting salary for this position is $59,000 annually. Education and experience will be considered.

Responsibilities

## What Will You Do?

The primary responsibilities of the Lease Administration Coordinator include, but are not limited to, the following:

• Manage lease files from the offer stage through execution of the final lease documentation.

• Prepare and coordinate leases, renewals, amendments, assignments, consents, notices and other commercial lease documentation using approved forms and templates.

• Coordinate signatures, approvals and execution of lease documentation and proactively follow up with the relevant stakeholders to keep matters moving.

• Abstract executed lease documents and accurately maintain key lease information, financial terms, rent schedules, notice requirements and critical dates within LeaseQuery or other applicable lease administration systems.

• Maintain complete and accurate electronic lease files, including executed agreements, approvals, correspondence, lease abstracts and supporting documentation.

• Ensure lease documentation and records are maintained in accordance with FMI's document-management and records-management requirements.

• Track lease expiries, renewal and termination periods, rent adjustments, notice periods and other recurring or critical obligations.

• Maintain rent schedules and reports and assist with the administration of recurring rent and other occupancy charges.

• Conduct an initial review of routine landlord invoices, operating-cost reconciliations, property-tax charges and other additional-rent items against the applicable lease documentation.

• Maintain property-tax records and related lease and property information.

• Monitor and organize the leasing inbox, acknowledge and route requests, maintain open-item tracking and follow up on outstanding documentation and administrative matters.

• Ensure fully executed documentation and relevant lease information are distributed to Finance, Operations, Property Management and other required departments.

• Prepare and maintain critical-date reports, lease-status reports, documentation metrics and other lease-administration reporting.

• Escalate material discrepancies, missed or uncertain deadlines, lease interpretation issues, disputes, defaults, and other matters as appropriate.

• Perform other related duties as required.

## Why Work for FMI?

• You'll surround yourself with a team whose members are committed to being the best at what they do.

• You'll have a flexible work environment.

• You can enroll in our comprehensive benefits package and RRSP contribution plan.

• You'll enjoy quarterly meals cooked by our Leadership Team, as well as monthly events for all staff!

• Career growth, development, and continuous learning opportunities within a positive and inclusive work culture.

• Opportunity to be involved in FMI events that give back to our community.

• Perkopolis discounts for various vendors across Canada and Discounts at all our brands.

• Educational assistance plan & Bursary Program.

## ABOUT NL HEALTH SERVICES

We are a provincial health authority responsible for delivering quality health care to approximately 550,000 people in Newfoundland and Labrador. Supported by over 23,000 employees and physicians, our team works together to improve the health and well-being of every person, in every community. Guided by the vision of the Health Accord NL, we offer a range of health-care programs and services through a wide network of facilities, clinics, and community services across five zones: Central, Eastern-Rural, Eastern-Urban, Labrador-Grenfell, and Western.

At NL Health Services, we believe that our people — employees, doctors and volunteers — make it a great place to work. Every individual brings valuable knowledge, experience and perspective. It is in this diversity that we find strength. We are committed to embracing the distinct and complementary characteristics of our members, as we seek to eliminate health disparities, and ensuring we provide fair, equitable and quality health care to everyone.

If you are passionate about making a difference and providing exceptional health care, we want to hear from you. Join our team and be part of something extraordinary.

????????????????????????????????????????

## ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

NL Health Services – Eastern Rural Zone invites applications for two (2) permanent full-time Fee-For-Service Hospitalist Physicians at the Burin Peninsula Health Care Centre in Burin, NL. These positions are available immediately.

The Burin Peninsula Health Care Centre provides health care services to a catchment area of approximately 18,000 people and serves as an important regional health centre for the Burin Peninsula, while also supporting two local Category B hospitals — the U.S. Memorial Health Centre in St. Lawrence and the Dr. S. Beckley Health Care Centre in Grand Bank.

Hospitalist physician coverage is generally solo, with Nurse Practitioner support from 8:30am–4:30pm on weekdays. Hospitalist shifts are 24 hours of coverage for 7 consecutive days, with handover occurring Monday mornings. Physicians will work an average of 1–2 weeks per month.

A shared 0.5 FTE appointment may potentially be considered as an alternative to a full-time position, or in combination with other clinical duties such as emergency room coverage, chemotherapy clinics, or family medicine clinic.

The hospital has access to comprehensive specialist and hospital-based support including General Surgery, Anesthesia, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Paediatrics, Psychiatry, Internal Medicine, and the Hospitalist Program.

## Work Environment

Live, work, and play on Newfoundland and Labrador's beautiful Burin Peninsula — known locally as "The Boot" and the "Sunny South." The Burin Peninsula offers a unique combination of welcoming coastal communities, spectacular ocean scenery, and year-round outdoor recreation including hiking and walking trails, sandy beaches, kayaking, paddleboarding, fishing, camping, golfing, and boating. The region also offers a rich cultural and maritime history, vibrant local communities, local restaurants, festivals, and community events. For a unique weekend adventure, the ferry from Fortune to Saint-Pierre and Miquelon offers the opportunity to visit France just off Newfoundland's south coast. For more information visit: www.burinnl.ca

2238282.title: Operations Manager, MCC
2238282.description:
Position Type:
Permanent
*

Closing date:
2026-10-05
*

## Full careers. Full lives.

## Join the Medavie Health NL Team

Are you looking for a fulfilling career that makes a meaningful impact on your life, and the lives of others? As the provider of emergency medical services and medical communications operations across Newfoundland and Labrador, Medavie Health NL (MHNL) is proud to offer career opportunities for professionals who share our strong commitment to delivering healthcare to communities throughout Newfoundland and Labrador.

If you're a passionate professional seeking a unique and meaningful career, MHNL is your destination. Join our team and achieve your full potential in a supportive and dynamic environment.

Reporting to the Manager, Provincial Medical Communications Centre (PMCC), the MCC Operations Manager (OM) is responsible for managing staff and systems within the Medical Communications Centre to ensure efficient, safe, and effective operations that align with organizational and provincial standards.

Major operational components of this position include overseeing shift activities, supporting staff performance and development, ensuring operational readiness, and addressing escalated concerns from staff, hospitals, and partner agencies. The OM also manages payroll and staffing needs, validates reporting, and contributes to system-level improvements in collaboration with leadership and clinical partners. Assessing and reporting overall performance, both current and long-term, to meet service objectives is expected.

The fundamental management skills required include demonstrated leadership, planning, organizing, directing, and motivating staff. The incumbent will work collaboratively with operations management and other system partners to ensure the overall operational status of the PMCC remains fully functional while meeting or exceeding service expectations. The OM fosters a culture of accountability, patient safety, and teamwork by modeling professionalism, self-awareness, and the same high standards expected of staff.

## Duties and Responsibilities

## Clinical & Operations

• Oversee day-to-day shift operations, ensuring operational readiness in collaboration with Senior Communications Officers (SCOs) (staffing, systems, and resources).

• Address escalated operational issues with hospitals, partner agencies, or field staff.

• Monitor Stat and Urgent Transfer requests in collaboration with the Clinical Hub and Medical Transport Physician.

• Validate and review daily shift reports, ensuring accuracy and follow-up as required.

• Partner with leadership and QA/QI to identify and implement service delivery improvements.

• Contribute to integration efforts with Field Operations, Critical Care, and Community Paramedic Programs to strengthen system effectiveness.

## Human Resources

• Supervise and support Senior Communications Officers (SCOs) and Medical Communications Officers (MCOs), ensuring KPIs are met.

• Provide mentoring, coaching, and performance feedback to staff; escalate significant issues to QA/QI or senior leadership as appropriate.

• Process payroll, overtime, and staff leave/vacation requests while ensuring adequate staffing levels are maintained.

• Participate in staff development initiatives, recruitment, and retention strategies to support long-term workforce stability.

## Administrative & External

• Serve as point of contact for escalated concerns from SCOs, Team Leads, hospitals, or partner agencies.

• Ensure clear and consistent communication across staff, leadership, and external stakeholders.

• Attend operational huddles and monitor system communication tools.

• Participate in working groups, committees, and outreach initiatives with system partners as required.

• Support organizational goals by contributing to research, reporting, and continuous improvement initiatives.

## Professional Qualifications and Competencies

• Successful completion of an approved/recognized ACP or PCP program, or equivalent education and experience in medical communications, EMS, health care, or a related field, is required.

• Current and ongoing registration, certification, or professional designation in the applicant's respective field, where applicable, is required.

• A minimum of three years of progressive experience in a high-volume EMS, Medical Communications Centre, emergency communications, or related operational environment is required.

• Emergency Medical Dispatcher (EMD) certification with the International Academy of Emergency Dispatch (IAED) is required.

• Current Emergency Medical Dispatcher (EMD) certification through the International Academy of Emergency Dispatch (IAED) is required.

• Demonstrated leadership experience in Medical Communications, EMS, health care, emergency communications, dispatch, quality management, or a related operational environment is required.

• Strong knowledge of Medical Communications Centre operations, ambulance dispatch, patient transport, ground and air ambulance operations, and applicable clinical and operational policies is required.

• Knowledge of Newfoundland and Labrador geography as it relates to ambulance operations is required.

• Strong computer skills and demonstrated ability to work with CAD, telecommunications, electronic documentation, and other Medical Communications technologies are required.

• Excellent interpersonal, leadership, communication, and decision-making skills, with a demonstrated commitment to professional conduct, continuous learning, and quality improvement, are required.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required.

• Possession of a valid Class 4 driver's licence and clear driver's abstract is required.

• A bachelor's degree in a health-related, leadership, communications, emergency management, or related field is preferred.

## Salary Range

• $105,000 to $115,000 annually.

The Base Pay range may vary depending on the successful candidate or other relevant job-related factors such as knowledge, skills, qualifications, experience and education/training. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Medavie employees may participate in various performance-based incentive programs. Payments under these programs are discretionary and subject to both individual and organizational results.

While Medavie may use automated tools, including AI, to support application screening, candidates are expected to complete all recruitment interactions independently-without AI assistance-to ensure a fair and equitable process.

## Who we are

MHNL is the selected proponent to design, manage and operate a single, integrated road and air ambulance service in Newfoundland and Labrador. We are an incorporated, wholly owned NL-based subsidiary of Medavie Health Services (MHS), the largest contracted provider of emergency management services in Canada and a national leader in primary health care solutions, including mobile integrated health and community paramedicine programs.

Together with Medavie Blue Cross, MHS is part of Medavie, a national health solutions partner and innovative leader in benefits management, health management, and healthcare delivery. Backed by our team of over 8,200 dedicated professionals, we exist to improve the wellbeing of Canadians so that every life can be lived to the fullest.

We're one of Canada's Most Admired Corporate Cultures, one of Canada's Top 100 Employers, and certified Rainbow Registered as an organization that champions diversity, equity and inclusion. We foster a culture of caring where people are celebrated beyond their roles and valued for who they are and what they contribute.

If you share our mission of improving the wellbeing of Canadians, join our team.

## What it's like to work with us

We are more than just a workplace - we are a people-focused, visionary organization dedicated to fostering well-being and making a meaningful impact on the lives of our employees and the Communities we serve.

We celebrate individuality and value the diverse perspectives and skills our employees contribute. We go beyond providing competitive pay and comprehensive benefits by offering opportunities for personal and professional growth, meaningful experiences, and supportive leadership. At Medavie, you'll find more than just a job - you'll find a pathway to a full and rewarding career.

• Support strategic planning and governance activities that advance provincial digital health priorities.

• Develop and report on performance measures, outcomes, and benefits realization.

• Prepare briefing materials, recommendations, and governance documentation for senior leadership.

• Support initiatives that strengthen digital health services and health system transformation.

Company: Nova Scotia Power

Department: Work in Asset Management - Customer & Grid Intelligence

Location: Halifax, Nova Scotia

Are you passionate about improving business processes, solving operational challenges, and delivering technology solutions that make a real impact? As the Product Owner, Work and Asset Management (WAM), you will play a key role in shaping and enhancing the systems that support Regional Operations teams and field work execution.

In this role, you'll serve as the bridge between operational users, business stakeholders, and technical teams, ensuring that WAM solutions evolve to meet changing business needs while delivering maximum value to the organization. You'll have the opportunity to influence how work is planned, scheduled, and managed, driving initiatives that improve efficiency, strengthen user experience, and support operational excellence.

This is an ideal opportunity for someone who enjoys combining business analysis, product ownership, stakeholder engagement, and continuous improvement. You'll collaborate with cross-functional teams, lead meaningful change, and help translate complex operational needs into practical technology solutions that support employees, contractors, and customers alike.

Key elements of this role include:

• Champion the end-user experience for Regional Operations teams by optimizing WAM solutions and related business processes.

• Partner with operational stakeholders, subject matter experts, and technical teams to identify needs and develop effective solutions.

• Gather, analyze, and translate business requirements into system enhancements, configurations, and solution designs.

• Prioritize initiatives and product improvements that deliver the greatest operational and business value.

• Lead workshops, discussions, and working sessions to uncover opportunities for process improvement and innovation.

• Assess business impacts, troubleshoot system challenges, and recommend solutions that improve operational effectiveness.

• Support solution delivery through user acceptance testing, validation activities, and issue resolution.

• Conduct business impact assessments related to system and process changes.

• Develop and contribute to training, user support materials, and change adoption activities that help teams successfully embrace new processes and technologies.

• Build strong relationships across the organization, facilitating collaboration, alignment, and informed decision-making.

• Manage stakeholder expectations and provide updates on initiatives and outcomes.

• Apply project management principles to plan, coordinate, track, and deliver initiatives.

• Coordinate and support cross-functional projects, providing progress updates, managing priorities, and helping deliver successful outcomes.

These skills will make you successful:

• Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Business, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Minimum 6 years of relevant experience in product management, business analysis, and product ownership role, with experience supporting Energy Delivery processes within an electric utility environment.

• Experience working with Agile and Scrum methodologies, with the ability to gather requirements, analyze business processes, and translate business needs into effective technology solutions.

• Experience with Work and Asset Management (WAM) solutions and related technologies such as Maximo, CIS, Salesforce/Field Service, particularly within utility or field operations environments is considered an asset.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and collaboration platforms.

• Experience leading cross-functional initiatives and applying project management practices to drive results.

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills with the ability to evaluate information from multiple sources.

• Excellent communication, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build consensus among diverse groups.

• Experience supporting organizational change, user training, and solution adoption initiatives.

• Ability to facilitate workshops and build collaborative relationships across teams.

• Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and deliver results in a fast-paced environment.

If you're energized by improving operational performance, influencing technology strategy, and partnering with teams to create better ways of working, we'd love to hear from you. This is an opportunity to make a visible impact while helping shape the future of Work and Asset Management solutions across the organization.

The Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration works to provide fairness, safety and prosperity for all Nova Scotians by helping them live, learn and work to their highest potential. Together, we support workplace safety, apprenticeship, adult education, workforce development and other services that affect everyday life in Nova Scotia.
The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency supports and advances apprenticeship training and certification across the province. Working with industry, training providers, communities, regulatory authorities and provincial, territorial and federal partners, the Agency develops and maintains occupational standards, curriculum standards, examinations, training pathways and policies that contribute to a highly skilled workforce.
We are seeking an innovative, collaborative and highly skilled education professional to join the Standards and Examinations team as Education Consultant, Apprenticeship Agency.

About Our Opportunity
Reporting to the Manager, Program Standards, the Education Consultant provides leadership and direction for the development, implementation and continuous improvement of a portfolio of skilled trades training and certification products. You will design, develop and maintain occupational and curriculum standards, assessments, examinations and flexible training pathways that respond to industry needs and support quality apprenticeship programming across Nova Scotia.
You will work with business, industry, labour, education providers, communities, equity groups and government partners to identify emerging needs and develop new programs and initiatives. You will also provide evidence-informed advice on whether proposed training pathways or initiatives should proceed and may contribute to workforce development initiatives aligned with Government and Agency priorities.

Primary Accountabilities
As the Education Consultant, you will:

• Write, review, edit and validate occupational standards, curriculum standards, competencies, learning outcomes, assessments and examinations for assigned skilled trades.

• Determine short- and long-term priorities for the development, review and revision of trades training and certification products.

• Design innovative, flexible and accessible training pathways and resources for in-person, online and other delivery models, including pathways for new trades or trades without established training options.

• Apply expertise in curriculum development, adult education, Universal Design for Learning, cultural responsiveness, equitable learning principles, assessment design and examination-item development.

• Recruit, screen and support subject matter experts, instructors and industry practitioners participating in development and validation activities.

• Plan and facilitate provincial, Atlantic and national workshops involving subject matter experts, instructors and apprenticeship representatives.

• Chair or support committees, task teams and steering committees, and represent the Agency on provincial, regional and national initiatives, including work undertaken through the Atlantic Apprenticeship Council and the Canadian Council of Directors of Apprenticeship.

• Build and maintain effective partnerships with business, industry, labour, education providers, youth and equity groups, communities, and federal, provincial and territorial governments.

• Ensure published standards, examinations and communications meet applicable Atlantic and national standards and comply with government legislation, regulations, policies and quality requirements.

• Maintain alignment and consistency among occupational standards, curriculum documents, assessments and examinations.

• Monitor occupational, technological, industry and labour market trends; research policies, programs and leading practices in Canada and internationally; and recommend new or revised programming.

.
• Conduct examination-item and statistical analyses to support the validity, reliability and continuous improvement of assessments and programs.

• Support the development, annual review and evaluation of transfer-credit agreements with secondary and post-secondary education providers, including approximately 50 external certificate and diploma programs.

• Provide expert guidance on recognition of prior learning, transfer credit, cross-trade credit and credential-recognition matters.

• Lead or support policy development related to apprenticeship training and certification, including consultation and jurisdictional research.

• Prepare proposals, reports, briefing notes, issue papers, surveys, presentations and other internal and external communications, and present information to diverse audiences.

• Monitor project expenditures, follow procurement requirements, manage contracts with technical writers or development consultants, and coach contracted resources.

• Contribute to labour market and workforce planning initiatives, including analysis related to education and training programs, recruitment, retention, succession planning and workplace culture.

• Perform other related duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Experience
As the successful candidate you have a master's degree in education, as well as 8 years of experience in the design, development, implementation and evaluation/monitoring of training standards, curriculum, examinations, policies and/or programs, or an equivalent combination of training and experience. Experience in online course development and delivery is required.
You also have:

• Significant experience developing, reviewing or implementing curriculum, occupational standards, competency frameworks, assessments or examinations.

• Demonstrated knowledge of adult learning, Universal Design for Learning, culturally responsive and equitable education practices, and valid and reliable assessment principles.

• Experience leading complex projects involving multiple partners, competing priorities and firm timelines.

• Experience conducting research, analyzing and synthesizing complex information, and developing practical recommendations, policies or program options.

• Strong facilitation, consultation and consensus-building skills, including experience working with subject matter experts and diverse partner groups.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with demonstrated ability to prepare clear reports, briefing notes, standards, presentations and other technical or strategic materials.

• Strong organizational, project-management and attention-to-detail skills, including the ability to maintain consistency across interconnected standards, curriculum and assessment products.

• Demonstrated cultural competence and the ability to work respectfully and effectively with diverse communities, equity-deserving groups, industry, labour, educators and government partners.

• Proficiency with word processing, spreadsheets, presentation, scheduling, organizational and database software.

• A valid Nova Scotia driver's licence, or the ability to travel as required.

The Following Would Be Considered Assets
• Experience in apprenticeship, skilled trades training, certification, workforce development or a regulatory environment.

• Knowledge of the Canadian Red Seal Program, Atlantic apprenticeship harmonization or interprovincial apprenticeship systems.

• Experience with recognition of prior learning, transfer credit, credential assessment or competency-based assessment.

• Experience developing examination items, conducting item analysis or applying statistical methods to assessment quality.

• Experience managing procurement processes, contracts, consultants or project budgets.

• Experience designing or implementing online, blended, community-based or other flexible training models.

• French-language proficiency.

This is an opportunity to shape skilled trades training and certification in Nova Scotia and contribute to provincial, Atlantic and national workforce priorities. About Us
The Safety Branch of the Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration delivers regulatory programs that protect workers and the public. Through education and outreach, inspection and enforcement, equipment registration, permits and licences, more than 130 employees located across Nova Scotia support compliance with provincial safety requirements. The Branch uses a compliance pathway that includes setting and promoting requirements, verifying compliance and taking enforcement action when necessary.

About Our Opportunity
Reporting to the Executive Director, Occupational Health and Safety, the Senior Director Compliance and Inspection provides strategic direction, quality-management oversight, operational planning expertise and leadership for the provincial delivery of workplace occupational health and safety compliance, inspection, enforcement and investigation programs and regulatory activities.
The Senior Director provides timely, informed advice to senior leadership and Regional Directors, leads major province-wide compliance and inspection initiatives, supports continuous improvement, and contributes to legislative and regulatory reform in response to emerging workplace-safety issues. The role may exercise authorities delegated under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, as determined by the Executive Director.

Primary Accountabilities
• Lead the development, execution and continuous improvement of comprehensive regional operational plans, performance measures and service-delivery frameworks that meet legislative requirements and align with departmental priorities.

• Provide provincial oversight of inspections, investigations, enforcement actions, administrative penalties, prosecutions and case management to support the clear, consistent and fair application of occupational health and safety legislation, policies and procedures.

• Monitor regional performance, inspection and enforcement practices, emerging risks and service-delivery gaps, and provide strategic direction and decision support to Regional Directors and compliance and inspection staff.

• Review files, make recommendations on enforcement actions and intervene when appropriate enforcement action has not been taken or requires correction.

• Lead change initiatives for province-wide regional inspection and compliance operations, including the development and implementation of standards, programs, processes and service-delivery improvements.

• Represent Nova Scotia on provincial, regional and national working groups concerned with regulatory harmonization, labour mobility, emerging issues, regulatory development and compliance planning.

• Build and maintain strategic relationships across the Safety Branch, government departments and agencies, other levels of government, professional associations, communities, the Workers' Compensation Board and the private sector.

• Provide advice and background information to senior and elected officials and, when required, respond to media inquiries concerning occupational health and safety inspections, investigations and serious incidents.

• Lead the effective planning and management of human and financial resources, including performance objectives, coaching, succession planning, employee development, respectful workplace practices, procurement and budget forecasting.

Qualifications and Experience
This may be the right opportunity for you if you have a university degree relevant to occupational health and safety, coupled with several years of leadership experience in a related field. An acceptable combination of education, training and experience may be considered.
You have demonstrated knowledge and experience in occupational health and safety compliance, inspection, enforcement, investigation, program delivery and the development of solutions that affect workplace health and safety. Experience working with various levels of government and diverse partners is required.
You possess exceptional interpersonal, written and verbal communication, negotiation and conflict-resolution skills. You can provide clear strategic advice, manage sensitive and high-profile issues, and establish effective relationships with a diverse range of individuals and organizations. Experience responding to media inquiries on sensitive matters is considered a strong asset.
You are proficient in Microsoft Office applications and possess strong organizational and analytical skills. You work accurately, pay close attention to detail and balance competing priorities in a fast-paced environment. You quickly synthesize new information and provide advice grounded in sound judgment and professional expertise.
A valid driver's licence is required.
