2241566.description:
The Opportunity

Company, Department: Nova Scotia Power, Customer & Grid Intelligence

Location: Halifax, Nova Scotia

Type of Employment: Permanent, Full-Time

Closing Date: October 13, 2026

Are you passionate about transforming data into meaningful insights that drive business decisions? As a Data Analyst on the Data Insights & Analytics team within Customer & Grid Intelligence, you'll play a key role in helping the organization leverage data to improve operational performance, enhance customer outcomes, and support strategic decision-making.

In this role, you will work with a wide range of data sources, including smart meter, asset, customer, among others, turning complex information into actionable intelligence. You'll collaborate with business and technical teams to develop dashboards, reports, and analytical solutions that support operational efficiency, data quality, and continuous improvement.

This is an excellent opportunity for a curious and analytical professional who enjoys solving problems, working with large datasets, and translating business needs into impactful data-driven solutions. You'll have the chance to influence decision-making across the organization while expanding your technical, analytical, and stakeholder engagement skills.

Key elements of this role include:

• Develop dashboards and visualizations that provide meaningful insights and support business decision-making.

• Create, maintain, and enhance reports using large and complex datasets to address operational and strategic needs.

• Analyze data sources, workflows, and business processes to identify trends, opportunities, and actionable recommendations.

• Ensure the accuracy, integrity, and availability of critical business and smart meter data.

• Develop and maintain data models, data dictionaries, and data catalogs that improve data accessibility and governance.

• Perform data validation, testing, and quality assurance activities to support reliable reporting and analytics.

• Write and optimize complex SQL queries across multiple data sources to support analysis and reporting requirements.

• Partner with stakeholders to understand business challenges and translate requirements into effective data solutions.

• Create ad hoc reports to address emerging business needs.

• Support data transformation activities and the development of data-driven solutions.

• Contribute to requirements gathering, data modelling, and workflow development aligned with business processes.

• Communicate analytical findings and technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

• Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance reporting capabilities, business processes, and operational performance.

These skills will make you successful:

• Bachelor's degree in Data Analytics, Computer Science, Information Systems, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, Business Analytics, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• 2-4 years of experience in data analysis, reporting, data modelling, business intelligence, or a related analytical role.

• Advanced experience working with SQL and relational databases.

• Experience developing dashboards and reports using Tableau and working with large, complex datasets.

• Knowledge of data modelling, data transformation, data quality management, and data validation methodologies.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify trends and translate data into actionable insights.

• Experience gathering and interpreting business requirements to develop practical, data-driven solutions.

• Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to diverse audiences.

• Familiarity with Python, statistical analysis, machine learning concepts, or similar analytical tools is considered an asset.

• Experience working with smart meter technologies, customer information systems, work management systems, ServiceNow, ITIL, or ITSM processes is considered an asset.

If you're excited by the opportunity to work with complex data, build impactful analytics solutions, and help drive informed business decisions, we'd love to hear from you.

Come build a career as unique as you are: making an impact from Atlantic Canada to the world. Your experience and perspective will help us to safely deliver cleaner, more reliable energy to our customers.

If working in an innovative environment, challenging yourself, and shaping a cleaner energy future inspires you, we want to hear from you. Apply by Tuesday, October 13, 2026 and let us know why this role is right for you.

The perks of joining our team? We offer:

• Competitive Compensation: Short-term incentive plan and a Defined Contribution Pension Plan.

As one of Atlantic Canada's largest publicly traded companies, we are ranked one of Canada's Top 100 Employers, Top Employers for Young People and Top Diversity Employers. About Us
Nova Scotia is rich in natural resources, including biodiversity, forests, provincial parks, and the land we manage. The Department of Natural Resources is responsible for the development, management, conservation and protection of forest, parks and wildlife resources, and the administration of the province's Crown land. Together we are working with Nova Scotians to build a better future through sustainable natural resource management as we all benefit from the natural health and wealth of the province.

The Shubenacadie Wildlife Park is one of Nova Scotia's top tourist destinations and has attracted millions of visitors over the past 72 years. The 331-hectare park has enchanted Nova Scotians and visitors alike and provides a wide range of outdoor recreational and educational opportunities.

About Our Opportunity
Do you enjoy working with people and creating positive visitor experiences? The Shubenacadie Wildlife Park is seeking Visitor Experience Clerks to serve as the first point of contact for visitors and help ensure every guest receives exceptional customer service.

## Visitor Experience Clerks take pride in:

• Professionally welcoming visitors and processing admissions
• Providing information about the Wildlife Park, programs, exhibits and surrounding area
• Operating point-of-sale systems and processing sales transactions
• Answering questions and resolving customer concerns
• Maintaining a clean, safe and welcoming admissions area for staff and

• Balancing cash and preparing daily deposits
• Cleaning and maintaining admissions facilities and public washrooms
• Assisting with inventory control and merchandise displays
• Supporting special events and visitor programs
• Assisting with weather-related activities including sweeping, sanding and snow removal as required

As a Visitor Experience Clerk, you will work under the supervision of the Visitor Experience Supervisor.

You will be responsible for:

• Processing admissions, merchandise sales and other financial transactions
• Maintaining accurate cash handling and accounting records
• Balancing and preparing daily revenue deposits
• Providing accurate information regarding the Wildlife Park and local attractions
• Maintaining a safe, clean and welcoming visitor environment
• Working independently while prioritizing tasks and responding to operational requirements as they arise

Qualifications and Experience
You've completed Grade 12 or have an equivalent combination of training and experience.

To be successful in this role, you should possess, confirm in your cover letter, and be prepared to demonstrate:

• Experience working with cash transactions, balancing, deposits, and basic accounting procedures
• Experience operating cash registers and point-of-sale systems
• Excellent customer service and communication skills
• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail
• Ability to work independently with minimal supervision
• Strong problem-solving abilities and sound judgment
• Ability to stand for extended periods and work in a fast-paced environment.

The following are considered assets:

• Previous tourism, hospitality, retail, admissions, or visitor services experience
• Knowledge of the Shubenacadie Wildlife Park and local tourism attractions
• Knowledge of park directives, departmental policies and procedures
• Knowledge of Occupational Health and Safety requirements
• Experience working with public education or recreation facilities

We will assess the above qualifications using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

• Periods of high visitor volume require sustained concentration, accuracy and customer service excellence.
• Employees may occasionally be required to perform light groundskeeping, cleaning and weather-related duties.
• Ability to work independently while maintaining a high level of professionalism is essential.

Additional Information
Currently, there is a casual position available from October to May, primarily as weekend and evening shifts, often outdoors in all weather conditions.

The Wildlife Park welcomes approximately 100,000 visitors annually, making the Visitor Experience Clerk an important ambassador for both the Park and the Department.

• Meaningful work contributing to one of Nova Scotia's most visited attractions.

• Opportunities for future seasonal and casual employment.

When you apply, you'll be considered not only for the current opening but also for upcoming bilingual Case Manager roles over the next year.

Reporting to a dedicated Claims Management leader, you are responsible for a broad range of responsibilities including assessing the needs of individual workers and administering the benefit provisions of the Workers' Compensation Act. They also exercise leadership in the development of a goal-oriented return-to-work plan; liaising with employers, health-care providers, unions, and other service providers to ensure access to appropriate medical and vocational rehabilitation services. Other responsibilities include managing assigned caseloads, preparing reasoned plain language decisions, adhering to procedures for return-to-work management and approving/authorizing services and benefits for injured workers on an ongoing basis.

## Salary And Hours Of Work:

• Hours of work are those required to perform the assigned tasks but shall not be less than 35 hours per week, 7 per day. Monday to Friday between 8:00-5:00 PM.
• The pay scale for this position is $92,248.80 to $108,528.00 annually.

## Responsibilities

• Experience in building strong trusting relationships with clients and external service providers to promote early and safe return to work outcomes.
• Exercise leadership in the development of a goal-oriented return-to-work case plan, by proactively managing a timely and safe return-to-work process through the active participation of the injured worker and employer.
• Work in a high pace environment without losing sight of the Safe and Early Return to Work Goal.
• Work collaboratively with injured workers, employers, and health-care professionals, in the development of the return-to-work plan.

2241565.title: Inclusion Coach - Lawrencetown - September 29, 2026
2241565.employer: Nova Scotia Early Childhood Development Intervention Services
2241565.description:
## Inclusion Coach

## Annapolis Valley Region – Lawrencetown Location

NS Early Childhood Development Intervention Services (NSECDIS) provide province-wide specialized services to families of young children between birth and school entry, who either have a biological risk for or a diagnosis of, developmental delay in NS. Consultation, information, support and services designed to meet the individual needs of each child and family are delivered in the child's home and may extend to community based programs. Services emphasize the enhancement of skills and ability through planned interactions to promote child development and family capacity.

Early Childhood Development Intervention Services (ECDIS) also facilitate early childhood educator capacity building through the delivery of inclusion coaching to childcare and pre-primary program settings, utilizing the Pyramid Model. The Pyramid Model for Supporting Social Emotional Competence in Infants and Young Children is a conceptual framework of evidence-based practices for promoting young children's healthy social and emotional development.

## Requiring: 1 Full Time Inclusion Coach

## Annapolis Valley Region – Lawrencetown Office

Through the implementation of Pyramid Model evidence-based practices, the Inclusion Coach provides professional development and program coaching to build the capacity of early childhood educators and childcare centres to support young children's social emotional and behavioural competency.

Coaching definition: Coaching is an interactive process based on a collaborative relationship. It is intentionally designed to promote sustainable growth in attitudes, skills and knowledge to effectively implement best practices for optimal development of young children and their families. Through observation, discussion, reflection and collaborative planning the coach promotes the early childhood educator's abilities to grow toward their identified goals.

## Duties and Responsibilities

## Program Planning

• build relationships and establish an environment and culture of best practices

• observe coachee and program to gather information for the coachee's profile and coaching and development plan

• assist coachees and programs to identify priorities and functional/meaningful outcomes based on their identified needs

• respond sensitively to the coachee's cultural diversity and individual preferences

• provide guidance and support to the program data coordinator on measures, collecting data, and using data for making decisions

• provide ongoing support to program leadership teams by attending their meetings and assisting with data-use and decision making as required

## Program Delivery

• provide training and support to early childhood educators and other staff on Pyramid Model and inclusive practices

• identify resources and supports in accordance with individual coaching plans

• plan, implement and document regularly scheduled coaching visits/consultations and meetings

• inform coachees of available options to support their professional growth and development in accordance with their own styles and preferences, including preferred levels of involvement in the intervention process

• organize and conduct regular reviews and revisions of the coaching and development plan with coachee and program

• support the implementation of individualized strategies and supports based on the coachee's and program's identified strengths, resources, priorities and concerns

• support the coachee and program to reflect on observations of their progress and to connect child development theories to practice in a clear, meaningful and practical manner

• assist the coachee and program in critically evaluating services and supports that are best for their program

• provide guidance, development and support to the program's internal coaches on practice-based coaching and tools for assessing a classroom implementation strengths and needs

• provide data, information and documentation to the Provincial Leadership team as required

• participate in training (in person/online), research and program evaluations as required

• maintain an on-going commitment to learning and professional development

## Community Connection

• provide support to other Inclusion Coaches and Developmental Interventionists as needed

• maintain knowledge base of community-based services, resources, and programs

• facilitate and maintain partnerships with local service providers to create networks of community supports for early childhood educators and families

• make recommendations for referrals to appropriate services/programs, as needed

• assist the coachee and program to find and access community resources to support their program

• attend community events and meetings with community partners as required

• communicate with other intervention, education and health professionals in order to

learn of emerging professional consensus and approaches

• participate in NSECDIS centre-based programming

• participate on community-based committees where appropriate

## Administration

• support/mentor other Inclusion Coaches and Developmental Interventionists, regarding service delivery and caseload problem solving

• continue/maintain own professional development (e.g., goal setting, reading, course work, sharing information with other professionals in the field)

• expand professional knowledge base through ongoing education and the critical evaluation of emerging research and professional literature

• participate in the preparation and presentation of public relations materials as required.

• participate in program development and evaluation

• maintain and report any statistics, records, data, etc. required by the organization and leadership team

• collect and maintain data on each coachee and child care/pre-primary program's progress and prepare written reports as needed

## Required Qualifications and Skills

## Education

• a minimum Bachelor's degree in early childhood development or the equivalent combination of training and experience

## Work Experience

• experience working with children from birth to school age and their families is essential

• experience within early childhood education settings and a knowledge of policies and systems that affect early childhood services

## Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

• competency and knowledge in early childhood development, social emotional learning, family-centred practice, and family systems theory

• demonstrated ability to implement developmentally appropriate practices, use adult

education principles, and deliver community-based programming

• strong planning, organizational, and time-management abilities

• knowledge/experience using observational assessment tools

• excellent communication (oral and written) and interpersonal skills, with the demonstrated ability to create and maintain effective relationships with children, families, early childhood educators and other community partners

• demonstrated knowledge of current trends, best practices, and research regarding early childhood development, and ability to apply theory to practice

• experience with underserved communities in the region (e.g., African Nova Scotian, First

Nations, new immigrant, Francophone/Acadian) and ability to communicate in other

languages an asset

• proficiency in the use of computers including word processing, e-mail, internet, digital calendars, file sharing programs, online data entry and video conferencing

• obtain valid First Aid Certification (Standard Child Care First Aid & CPR)

## Personal Attributes

• empathic, sensitive approach in communicating with children and families

• highly motivated and organized

• professional with the highest ethical standards

• able to work independently and within a team

• strong communicator verbally and in writing

• commitment to family-centred practice

• awareness of professional boundaries in working with families

## Working Conditions

• flexibility for some evening and weekend work when required

• regular travel (to childcare and pre-primary programs, other service provider locations, etc.) and access to own vehicle and valid driver's license is required

Salary: $34.20/hour plus Benefit Package

Our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative of the families we serve. We welcome applications from Acadian Francophones, Aboriginal People, African Nova Scotians, new immigrants and other racially visible persons and persons with disabilities. If you are a member of one of the equity groups, you are encouraged to self-identify on your cover letter or resume.

2241592.title: Mill Operator 6
2241592.description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is transforming the future?

## Who We Are

We are Vale Base Metals – a global supplier of the critical minerals transforming the future.

With industry-leading reserves of copper and nickel in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia, and state-of-the-art infrastructure in the U.K., Canada, and Japan, VBM delivers a secure and responsible supply of high-quality products to customers across Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

Global demand for critical minerals is growing exponentially. From energy to aerospace, batteries to magnets, robotics to artificial intelligence, a secure and responsible supply of critical minerals is fundamental to power modern technologies. And at Vale Base Metals, we are transforming our business to provide a secure and responsible supply of these minerals.

Join our diverse team of 13,000 talented individuals committed to providing mineral security to a world in transition. We invite you to put your skills to work, driving meaningful and enduring change while enjoying a rewarding career.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking a Mill Operator 6 to join our Concentrator Team in Voisey's Bay, Labrador, a fly-in fly-out operation.

These are permanent on-site positions, working a 2 week on, 2 week off rotation.

As a Mill Operator 6, you operate one of the nine circuits: crushing, grinding, flotation, dewatering, reagents, paste plant, tailings and water management, concentrator central control room, and/or paste plant control room.

Additionally, in this position you will:

• Perform pre-operational checks and operate equipment according to standard operating procedures and monitor equipment and processes.

• Conduct troubleshooting activities when problems arise and interact with the Control Room Operator and the Supervisor as required to correct.

• Perform plant housekeeping activities, minor equipment repairs, and support maintenance activities as required.

• Complete operator reports and ensure that equipment deficiencies and operational issues are communicated to the supervisor.

• Use overhead cranes and lifts to move operational supplies around the plant.

• Participate in crew safety meetings.

## What We Offer You

• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare

• Online training and career development opportunities

• Chartered flights within Newfoundland & Labrador

• Access to recreational facilities and social activities (cardio/weight room, gymnasium, music room, movie theatre, etc.)

• Accommodations are equipped with cable TV, internet, and unlimited long-distance calling

• All Personal Protective Equipment is provided upon hire. Employees are given a safety boot allowance and receive a 100% reimbursement for prescription safety glasses

## About You

## Education:

• Completed a minimum of Grade 10 or equivalent.

## Experience:

• Minimum of 6 months of operating experience in a mineral processing plant.

• Previous experience in Voisey's Bay would be considered an asset.

## Skills:

• Basic understanding of mineral processing theory and practice.

• Familiar with the process flowsheet and with the equipment and its function.

• Familiar with the safe work practices and standard operating procedures of the concentrator.

• Detailed knowledge of one area of the concentrator and can operate the equipment autonomously at the completion of the training period.

• Able to recognize hazards in an industrial workplace and understands his or her role in assessing and managing risk.

• Able to apply logical thinking to solve problems and "trouble-shoot" abnormal situations to correct mechanical or process problems.

• Has mechanical aptitude and is able, with appropriate instruction, to perform basic equipment repairs.

• Able to communicate effectively with operations and maintenance personnel while carrying out duties.

• Familiar with operating a computer and running Windows-driven applications.

## Why Newfoundland and Labrador

Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada's easternmost province, is known for its rugged coastline, rich cultural heritage, and significant natural resources. The province's economy is bolstered by a robust mining sector, where our operations play a crucial role.

At Long Harbour, we operate a state-of-the-art processing plant, which refines nickel concentrate from the Voisey's Bay mine into finished nickel, copper, and cobalt products. This plant is a cornerstone of our commitment to value-added processing in Canada. Meanwhile, the Voisey's Bay mine, located in Labrador, is one of the world's most substantial nickel deposits. It provides high-quality nickel, copper, and cobalt, essential for the 21st century economy.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people feel comfortable to be themselves. Vale encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

Vale recognizes the Impacts and Benefits Agreements with the Innu Nation and the Nunatsiavut Government in which Innu and Inuit workers have first preference for employment at the Voisey's Bay Mine Site. This is guided by an adjacency principle that first gives preference to those who live on the coast of Labrador, followed by those residing in the rest of Labrador, those residing on the island of the province, followed by the rest of Canada.

Next, priority will be given to Newfoundland and Labrador residents. We also welcome those who are willing to relocate back home and those looking to make NL their permanent home.

Accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Innu Nation members and Nunatsiavut beneficiaries can submit their application to their Vale Aboriginal Employment Coordinator.

Employees engaged by the Company must be lawfully able to work for the Company in the country where the role is located. The Company does not provide immigration, work permit, or permanent residence sponsorship or assistance.

Interested applicants must submit their application online at https://vale.eightfold.ai/careers.

Apply by: Thursday October 15th, 2026.

## #ValeBaseMetals

2241594.title: Provincial Trails Coordinator
2241594.description:
## Provincial Trails Coordinator

## Department of Natural Resources

## Pay Band 5

## Open Competition

## Fredericton

Interested in making a difference in our province? We encourage you to Choose GNB!

## Who we are:

The Department of Natural Resources is seeking an individual to join the Crown Lands Branch, as the Provincial Trails Coordinator, located in Fredericton.

The Department of Natural Resources is responsible for protecting and managing the forests, fish, and wildlife, and for overseeing the development of mineral resources in New Brunswick. The Crown Lands Branch is responsible for the administration and management of Crown lands across New Brunswick, ensuring responsible use and sustainable development. The branch oversees land tenure and land use authorizations supporting a wide range of commercial, recreational, and resource-based activities on Crown lands, including the management of the Former Railway Line and other corridors for the development and management of a recreational trail network.

## What you will do:

As a member of the Approvals Section and reporting to the section Manager, the selected candidate will be responsible for coordinating the development of both motorized and non-motorized trails on Crown lands with the objective to ensure the safe, sustainable and strategically located public recreational trail opportunities that maximizes the economic, social and environmental benefits to the province.

## Key responsibilities:

• Developing and maintaining a positive working relationship with the main trail user groups and relevant staff from other departments with similar trail mandates;

• Creating and maintaining Geographic Information Systems (GIS) data to support activities related to motorized trail applications;

• Participating as Chairperson of the Provincial Trail Planning Committee, with responsibility for agendas and minutes and related liaison functions, including trail application processes for development, use and maintenance of all trail networks;

• Providing functions associated with the operation of the Trail Management Trust Fund including all processes and protocols as established by the Minister, necessary for the disbursement of funds in accordance with the Off-Road Vehicle Act;

• Participating in process improvement related initiatives;

• Working with project managers and other branch staff to ensure trail priorities are met and clients receive timely responses to trail applications, including making recommendations with respect to policies, procedures, regulation and/or legislation, as they relate to Crown land use and trails;

• Performing other related duties as required.

## Who you are:

• You have excellent written and verbal communication skills.

• You excel at providing high-quality client services.

• You are at your best when challenged and thrive on getting results.

• You are recognized for your attention to detail, organizational skills, and ability to prioritize deliverables.

• You are effective in working independently and collaboratively with colleagues and clients.

Your attitude, skills and interests are just as important as your area of study. We are looking for diverse backgrounds that bring a combination of the following.

Essential Qualifications:

• A University degree in Forestry, Engineering, Recreational Studies, Environmental Studies, Geography, or Planning.

• A minimum of five (5) years of progressively more responsible experience in land management, resource management, or outdoor recreation such as planning, development, management and delivery of nature-based recreational programs, tourism products, or infrastructure.

• A minimum of one (1) year of experience working collaboratively with multiple organizations.

An equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered.

Written and spoken competence in English is required. Please state your language capability on your application.

Applicants must clearly demonstrate the essential qualifications to be given further consideration. Please ensure that preferred language for assessment is identified on your resume. Resumes should be in chronological order specifying education and employment in months and years including part-time and full-time employment.

## Asset Qualification(s):

• Preference may be given to candidates that demonstrate experience using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) mapping software.

Subject to the response to this competition, candidates may be required to demonstrate on their application one or more of the asset qualifications in addition to the essential qualifications in order to be given further consideration.

Behavioural Competencies: The successful candidate will possess the following behavioural competencies:

• Analytical Thinking/Judgment

• Effective Interactive Communication

• Relationship/Network Building

• Results Orientation

• Teamwork and Cooperation

Technical Competencies: The successful candidate will possess the following technical competencies:

• Knowledge of applicable legislation and the Department¿s policies and procedures;

• Ability to use office technology, software and applications;

• Planning and organizing skills;

• Project management skills;

• Written communication.

## Wage: Pay Band 5 - $68,276 to $95,342 annually

## Operational Requirement(s):

• Must be prepared to: travel throughout the province as required; and possess a valid class 5 driver licence as issued by the Province of New Brunswick, or equivalent.

## Work environment:

• Office location: Hugh John Flemming Forestry Centre, 1350 Regent Street, Fredericton, New Brunswick.

• Work hours: Monday to Friday / 8:15 to 4:30; 36.25 hours per week.

• We promote a scent-reduced environment.

## What can GNB offer you?

• Comprehensive benefits package which includes paid vacation, Health and Dental Plan, Life Insurance, and the New Brunswick Public Service Pension Plan.

• Opportunities for career growth, professional development, and training.

• Free access to Employee and Family Assistance Program (EFAP) and services.

• One paid volunteer day per year to give back to your community.

Providing a safe workplace for all. Your health and safety are important to us. GNB has implemented preventative measures across the organization to ensure your health and safety. We promote a scent-reduced environment.

We encourage applicants to apply online at www.ere.gnb.ca, by email at Brenda.Nicholson@gnb.ca, or by mail at the following address, by October 16, 2026, indicating competition number DNR-26-12. This competition may be used to fill future vacancies at the same level.

2241596.title: Implementation Specialist
2241596.description:
Work Location: 6080 Young Street, Halifax, NS (On-site, 5 days per week)

Department: Engineering

Reports To: Manager, Business Implementation

Employment Status: Full time, 40 hours per week

Our Business Implementation team is looking for an organized and customer-focused Implementation Specialist to help bring our business solutions to life. Reporting to the Manager, Business Implementation, you’ll coordinate the implementation of customer-specific Voice, Data and Video solutions, from planning through to completion. Working with teams across Eastlink, as well as customers or external partners, you’ll help ensure projects are delivered on time, within budget and in line with the approved design.

This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys coordinating moving pieces, building relationships, solving problems and seeing a project through to successful delivery.

What You'll Be Doing

Manage Customer Implementation

• Manage multiple customer implementation projects simultaneously, coordinating activities and key milestones from planning through to completion.

• Work closely with Customer Solutions Engineering to ensure solutions are implemented according to the approved engineering design.

• Manage project timelines, budgets and quality objectives, ensuring spending remains aligned with forecasts.

Coordinate Across Teams

• Partner with cross-functional teams to coordinate the efficient delivery of customer solutions.

• Work with Procurement and suppliers to ensure required equipment and materials are available when needed.

• Identify risks, roadblocks and potential delays, working with the appropriate teams to resolve issues and keep projects moving forward.

Keep Customers and Teams Connected

• Serve as a key point of contact throughout the implementation, providing customers and key partners with clear and timely updates and coordinating with the right teams to address questions or concerns.

• Prepare project status updates outlining progress, risks, key milestones and upcoming activities.

• Maintain accurate project records and tracking tools, including progress updates and anticipated completion dates.

What We're Looking For

• Post-secondary education in a related field; an engineering degree is considered an asset.

• Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to effectively manage multiple projects and competing priorities.

• Strong verbal and written communication skills and the ability to build effective working relationships with customers, colleagues and external partners.

• A customer-focused mindset with a commitment to delivering a positive experience.

• A proactive approach to problem-solving, with the ability to take initiative and adapt as priorities change.

• Telecommunications knowledge or experience is preferred, particularly with Internet, Data, Voice and Cable TV services.

• Knowledge of network infrastructure and design, including structured cabling, fibre optic and hybrid fibre-coaxial (HFC) systems, is considered an asset.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.

• A valid driver’s license, with the ability to travel locally and regionally, as required.

About Eastlink

Eastlink is proudly family-owned and headquartered in Halifax, Nova Scotia. After more than 50 years, we’ve grown from a small-town startup into one of Canada’s Best Managed companies without losing our entrepreneurial edge. We move fast. We try new things. We care about doing right by our customers, and we’re not afraid to take a different approach to make that happen.

Why Work with Us

We could say we’re not your typical telecom, but what makes us different is how we operate day to day. At Eastlink, we’re a tight-knit team all working toward common goals. We’re big enough to do meaningful work, but small enough that you can actually make your mark. You won’t get stuck waiting for layers of approval or years of tenure to make an impact! We believe in getting involved, speaking up, and figuring things out together. We’re always listening, learning, and adapting because our customers (and our people) expect us to. And just like we invest in our network, we invest in you, with intention and for the long run.

We’re committed to building a workplace where everyone feels they belong. We embrace diversity, inclusion, equity, and accessibility throughout all levels of the organization and encourage members of equity groups to self-identify during the application process. Need an accommodation during the hiring process? We encourage you to reach out and let us know how we can support your participation.

Do you have what it takes to help keep the lights on for our customers in communities across the province? Then joining the Newfoundland Power team could be part of your next adventure…

## Who We Are

At Newfoundland Power, we're passionate about delivering safe, reliable, and efficient electricity. Our roots in Newfoundland and Labrador go back 140 years. Today, we're part of Fortis Inc., a leader in the regulated gas and electric utility industry in North America. As one of Atlantic Canada's Top Employers, we are proud to employ over 650 talented people who are among the best in the industry.

We are committed to ensuring a supportive, inclusive and diverse culture where everyone feels safe and valued for who they are. Together, we strive to create an environment which is free of discriminatory barriers, where everyone is treated respectfully and equitably so they can thrive and bring their whole selves to work.

Everything we do is guided by our core values: People, Safety, Service, Respect, Teamwork and Innovation. We believe in going above and beyond to serve our customers and giving back to the place we call home is a longstanding tradition held by our employees. This could be the opportunity for you to continue to grow and develop your career.

## The Opportunity

As a valued member of our Operations Team at our Whitbourne location, you will be responsible for:

• Installing and maintaining energized and de-energized power lines at various voltages;

• Interpreting single-line drawings and specifications;

• Inspecting and maintaining tools, equipment, and vehicles used to carry out line work; and,

• Performing other duties related to this position.

## Your qualifications include:

• A Powerline Technician Operating Red Seal Certificate

• A valid Class 3 motor vehicle driver's license with air brake endorsement. Powerline Technician Red Seal candidates who do not possess a valid class 3 motor vehicle drivers' license with air brake endorsement may be considered if they are able to obtain this certification prior to starting work or as a condition of employment.

• Excellent knowledge and solid understanding of utility safety procedures, standards and work methods.

• Strong computer skills and the ability to execute technical tasks with precise attention to detail.

• You possess excellent planning and organizational skills and consistently display initiative and productivity in your job duties.

• You are a highly-motivated team player with a strong commitment to safety and customer service, an excellent work ethic, and effective interpersonal and communication skills.

There is a residency requirement for this position, whereby your primary residence must be within 40 km of the Whitbourne office.

Compensation is as per the current Collective Agreement.

If you require accommodation for any reason during the interview process, please let us know what you need, and it will be kept in confidence. 2241598.title: Learning Ecosystem Support Specialist
2241598.description:
Title: Learning Ecosystem Support Specialist

Employee Working Location: Partially Virtual / Hybrid (Canada)

Employment Status: Temporary Full-time (12 months)

The Canadian Red Cross (Red Cross) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

Reporting to the Director of Product Management, the Learning Ecosystem Support Specialist provides advanced technical support for the Canadian Red Cross Learning Ecosystem, including the external administration portal, eCommerce platform, Brightspace LMS, CRM integrations, identity services, and related applications. The role serves as the primary technical escalation point for cross-platform issues, integration failures, and end-to-end transaction troubleshooting across the learning technology ecosystem.

## In this role, you will :

• Investigate, diagnose, and resolve web-layer technical issues within D2L Brightspace, admin portal and eCommerce platform including HTTP errors, rendering glitches, and application timeouts.

• Review browser developer tools, console logs, network payloads, and application logs to identify front-end and back-end performance bottlenecks.

• Investigate authentication and access issues, including Single Sign-On (SSO) and integration access problems.

• Review application logs, integration logs and API transactions to determine if an issue is internal or vendor related.

• Collaborate closely with development team and vendors to gather technical details required to resolve complex issues.

• Spot check high-level HTML, CSS, and JavaScript issues logged in console or custom widgets that impact accessibility or mobile responsiveness.

• Diagnose and resolve issues reported by customer service related to system configurations.

• Coordinate with internal Technology Group and D2L support to ensure issues are assigned to the appropriate support group.

• Maintain clear and concise case notes documenting the issue, investigation, actions taken and resolution details for each support ticket.

• Ensure internal stakeholder are informed of the ticket status, progress, and resolution activities while coordinating with the Customer Service Escalation Specialist to maintain macros/scripts.

• Document system configurations, troubleshooting playbooks, and root-cause analyses for the internal knowledge base.

• Develop a strong understanding of the Prevention& Safety business and delivery service model.

• Ensure all established processes and quality controls have been completed prior to ticket closures.

• Interact with Product Owner, D2L Technical Advisor Manager (TAM) and internal Technology Group team to validate product software issues and assist in their resolution.

• Take ownership of the support tickets assigned and be responsible for them until resolution and for communication with internal staff.

• Maintain a current skill set on third Party D2L applications used by external customers and internal staff.

• Train Tier 2 staff on high-level troubleshooting steps to provide sufficient details in support ticket.

## What we are looking for:

• College degree in Computer Science, Information Technology or related field or 2 + years of previous technical support experience or equivalent experience.

• 7 + years of experience administering, configuring or supporting web eCommerce, admin portals or D2L Brightspace platform.

• Strong technical understanding of web infrastructure, including HTTP/S protocols, web servers, DNS, and SSL/TLS certificates

• Proficiency in using web browser debugging tools (Chrome DevTools) to analyze network traffic and console errors.

• Experience with Microsoft D365 (e.g. CRM & F&O) or related is required.

• Practical knowledge of web standards and coding in (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript) and API integrations (REST, JSON, LTI 1.3).

• Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities with demonstrated comprehensive troubleshooting tactics.

• Ability to tailor explanations of technical concepts to the end user audience.

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills are a must.

• Proficiency in English oral and written, is required.

• Familiarity with Vue.js is preferred but not required.

## Working Conditions:

• Ability to work from home as the primary workspace.

a) Completion of a diploma/certificate program from a recognized institution in Office Administration/Management, Secretarial Science, or an acceptable equivalent obtained through relevant job training and experience;

2241513.title: Senior Health System Specialist, Strategic Growth & Partnerships - Full-time
2241513.description:
## ## Requisition Details:

Employment Status: Regular, Full-time (1.0 FTE)
Program Name: Strategic Growth & Partnerships
Number of Hours Bi-Weekly: 75
Work Schedule: Days
On Call: No
Existing Vacancy: Yes - we're currently hiring candidates for an existing vacancy in this position.

## Job Summary:

Reporting to the Director, Strategic Growth & Partnerships (SG&P), the Sr. Health Systems Specialist, Strategic Growth & Partnerships (Sr. Specialist) is a key member of the Engagement & Philanthropy team responsible for strategic growth, including analytical, advisory and consultative services, reporting, program development, program implementation and advocacy. The Sr. Specialist manages the development and deployment of provincial strategic programs and is responsible for the evaluation and successful delivery of program outcomes.

## Key Responsibilities:

Strategic Health System Analytics, Advisement and Communications

• Performs environmental health system scanning activities which include the interpretation of issues, assessment of risks and identification of potential impacts on strategic growth priorities. Provides recommendations and key insights to drive corporate strategy.

• Monitors provincial healthcare systems' objectives, emerging trends, and challenges; leads program analysis options; provides strategic advice; identifies issues and trends; and provides recommendations on existing and future funding opportunities within the province to their Director and other leaders in the organization as required.

• Provides strategic growth advisory services to senior management, including the preparation and creation of briefing/issue notes, position papers and reports

• Manages strategic planning that anticipates and absorbs complex, mid to large scale issues and recognizes the interdependencies of Policy and Legislative implementation as it relates to strategic growth

• Identifies and manages contentious issues demonstrating sound judgement, sensitivity and a high degree of political acuity in the setting of priorities

• Supports organizational planning by addressing gaps and aligning growth with VON's strategic goals and priorities

Program Development

• Using a deep understanding of the health system, environment and VON funder/payer goals, the Sr. Specialist will partner with provincial and regional leadership to support the development of funder, payer and advocacy organization submissions, reports and presentations and other documentation that promote the value of existing and new VON programs, models and associated program funding

• Develops reports, key messaging, proposals, presentations, and other documents to support the communication of VON program value to our funders, payers, and advocacy organizations. This includes analyzing and interpreting statistical data and monitoring quality, performance indicators, and benchmarks.

• Follows business development methodology and supports and monitors the consistent use of this methodology within the organization.

• Supports organizational capacity by using a standard approach for proposals created for external stakeholders, partners, funders, and payers and developing templates that operations and teams can utilize.

• Supports the operation and corporate teams with relevant information, strategy, positioning, and documentation to help them succeed in their business development endeavours.

• Collaborates with departments/sites across the organization in identifying and developing program and service business opportunities

• Builds internal and external partnerships, influences, and negotiates between partners to achieve a shared optimized goal.

Program Management

• Manages a provincial portfolio of strategic growth projects and initiatives to produce high quality results on time through team-based approaches utilizing Lean and project management principles

• Establishes program outcome measures and evaluation criteria aligned with the requirements of funders, payers and strategic partners. This includes the use of qualitative and quantitative methods to meet the quadruple aim

• Leads the successful implementation of the project and/or initiative and ensures that the project/initiative remains within scope, is delivered on time, and within budget as determined through the agreement between the funder and VON

• Provides leadership to projects and small teams to bring the program design to life and ensure a sustainable transition to the operating teams

## Common Responsibilities:

• Promotes the goals and values of VON and their role as an integrated community care provider

• Promotes a safe and healthy workplace, ensuring workplace conduct and activities are in accordance with the provincial Occupational Health and Safety Act and Regulations.

• Abides by all VON policies and work practices

• Abides by all confidentiality and protection of personal information policies, regulations and practices and ensures appropriate safeguards are in place within their role

• Works in collaboration with other staff in a team approach to service delivery

## External and Internal Relationships:

• Liaises with and presents to internal and external stakeholder groups, including governmental agencies in both Ontario and Nova Scotia and other system partners.

• Establishes effective working relationships and communications with VON national and regional leadership teams to execute priority growth opportunities, partner engagements and business development

• Identifies and develops working relationships with key external stakeholders and represents VON on consultations, negotiations and working groups; and,

• Works closely with external project stakeholders in launching of programs, paying close attention to process and approach for project evaluation and outcomes.

## Education, Designations and Experience:

• Post-secondary degree in a Health Care Profession, Social Sciences, Business Administration, Health Policy or related field. Master's degree preferred.

• Minimum of 5 years' experience in program planning, health policy, project management, and/or strategic planning (in a health-related environment preferred).

• Knowledge of Provincial health care systems, objectives, emerging trends, and challenges.

• A strong understanding of LEAN principles and methodologies, LEAN certification (minimum Green Belt) is preferred.

• Project Management designation or certification considered an asset.

• Proven experience leading projects and work teams, from program ideation to delivery and iteration, to solve and meet strategic growth objectives.

• Demonstrated analytical, problem solving, conflict resolution, negotiation, strategic and systems thinking and decision-making skills.

• Experience working with qualitative and quantitative data and ability to analyze information to identify priorities and emerging issues.

• Experience conducting literature reviews, environmental scans, and appraisal and synthesis of research and other information to inform service delivery.

• Experience in policy analysis, development, modernization processes and implementation.

• Advisory and consultation skills to discuss and resolve diverse and competing policy and program related issues.

• Prior experience working in a Home and Community organization considered an asset.

• Prior experience in business development considered an asset.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Suite applications, internet, email, and the ability to use health information systems for decision support.

## Skill Requirements:

• Strategic thinker who has a strong understanding of funding opportunities within the Health and Community sector, keeps current on trends and industry developments, understands home and community care operations and can articulate a plan and translate it into strategies to support the achievement of organizational objectives

• Provides a positive example to VON by acting as a change champion, modelling an openness to learning new things and exploring new possibilities.

• Embeds a people-centered approach to program development and implementation • Ability to exercise innovation and initiative in solving problems and identifying opportunities

• Strong project management skills.

• Strong planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.

• Strong interpersonal skills, including the ability to relate effectively with people and resolve conflict with both internal and external parties.

• Ability to work collaboratively to resolve issues and negotiate changes and shifts in priorities.

• Excellent change leadership skills.

• Strong active listening and critical thinking skills.

• Strong research and investigative skills.

• Excellent written, presentation and oral communication skills.

• Strong organizational skills, including the ability to organize and manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines

• Ability to manage multiple priorities and ambiguity in a time-sensitive environment.

## Other

• A current and original satisfactory Criminal Records Check is required upon the start of your employment

• A Vulnerable Sector Search and/or Child Abuse Registry Check may be required

• Travel and irregular work schedules as required

Working conditions and physical demands: This role requires a detail-oriented approach in a dynamic environment, with physical activity including lifting, carrying (using proper techniques), bending, reaching, kneeling, and other movements that emphasize good body mechanics. Individuals in the role are required to walk, sit, stand, and climb stairs throughout the day, with some tasks requiring fine hand movements.

2241648.title: Business Architect
2241648.description:
## WHO WE ARE:

Mariner innovates always and everywhere, turning novel ideas into practical solutions. From products and services to venture creation, we build better futures powered by people. We partner with people embracing change, leveraging data, cybersecurity, cloud, and change management to drive successful business outcomes that matter to our customers.

Mariners build for change. Like SHIFT Energy, our energy management and decarbonization company. Or East Valley, created to scale social economic impact in our communities through investment and mentorship of emerging change-makers and their companies.

Mariner s purpose has always been to be a great, everlasting technology company and the core values that guide us every day are:

## OUR VALUES

• We care for our team.

• We care about the impact we have on our community.

• We serve by solving complex problems.

• We grow because growth fuels opportunities.

• We innovate always and everywhere.

• We build a business that lasts.

OVERVIEW OF THE ROLE:
Our client is seeking an experienced Business Architect to support a major business transformation initiative. This is an on-site contract opportunity based in Moncton, New Brunswick, with an anticipated 12-month term and strong potential for extension. The successful candidate will focus on understanding and optimizing business capabilities, end-to-end processes, and cross-functional dependencies to enable improved business outcomes.

Working closely with business stakeholders, you will analyze current-state operations, identify opportunities for improvement, and help shape future-state processes that drive efficiency, alignment, and organizational success. This role requires a strategic thinker with hands-on experience in business architecture, process mapping, gap analysis, and facilitating cross-functional discussions to achieve desired business outcomes.

WHAT YOU LL BE DOING IN THE ROLE:
• Lead business capability and end-to-end process mapping across multiple business functions.

• Document and assess current-state business processes, workflows, and operational dependencies.

• Facilitate future-state design sessions and workshops with business stakeholders.

• Identify process, data, and organizational gaps impacting business performance.

• Analyze upstream and downstream dependencies to ensure alignment across business areas.

• Facilitate cross-functional discussions to define business needs, challenges, and desired outcomes.

• Develop recommendations for process improvements and business transformation initiatives.

• Create process maps, business architecture artifacts, and supporting documentation.

• Collaborate with business leaders to prioritize opportunities and support implementation planning.

• Ensure business requirements and recommended solutions align with strategic objectives.

WHAT SKILLS / QUALIFICATIONS YOU LL NEED TO DO THE JOB:
• 7+ years of experience in Business Architecture, Business Analysis, Process Improvement, or a related discipline.

• Demonstrated experience with business capability mapping and business architecture frameworks.

• Strong experience with end-to-end process mapping and process optimization.

• Proven ability to perform current-state assessments, future-state design, and gap analysis.

• Experience identifying process, data, and dependency issues within complex organizations.

• Strong stakeholder engagement and workshop facilitation skills.

• Ability to translate business challenges into practical, actionable recommendations.

• Excellent communication, documentation, and presentation skills.

Preferred Qualifications
• Experience supporting large-scale business transformation or modernization initiatives.

• Knowledge of business architecture methodologies and best practices.

• Experience with process modeling tools such as Visio, Lucidchart, ARIS, or similar platforms.

• Business Architecture Guild, CBAP, Lean Six Sigma, TOGAF, or related certifications are considered assets.

## AND YOU ARE...

• Always improving your skills and knowledge: you want to be the best at what you do

• Curious and creative; comfortable taking on new problems and challenges

• A self-starter with the ability to recommend priorities to the project leader

• Comfortable working through problems and figuring things out with minimal supervision

• Great problem-solving skills: thorough and reliable

• Able to work in a team: share knowledge and assist other team members

• A good communicator: able to explain your ideas and recommendations

• Well organized and dependable under pressure: you manage your time effectively

• Energized by our company values!

## MARINER OFFERS YOU:

• A values-driven workplace where people really matter.

• Competitive salary, retirement savings program, and rewards program

• Comprehensive health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance plans and access to e-health care

• Paid vacation, maternity/parental leave, paid sick leave and paid Mariner MyLife days

• Unlimited training

## WHY MARINER?

We believe in making a positive impact in the communities where we live and work! Not only are we passionate about nurturing a thriving technology sector here in Atlantic Canada, but we are also committed to solving technology challenges that will make an impact worldwide. Technology is everlasting, and we take pride in connecting world class talent to world class projects and business solutions.

If you are an IT Professional, Software Professional, or Management Consultant, that is passionate about career development, data, and problem solving, we want to hear from you! If this sounds like someone you know, share this with them so they do not miss the opportunity to experience Mariner!

To achieve this, we know we need to be all in on training and development of our team so we can continue to move the needle in the technology sector together. Of course, we offer competitive compensation and benefits packages to our team, but our competitive edge is the development and training that our team experiences every day.

Be part of our vibrant community that values diversity and embraces inclusion at every level. We are committed to fostering a culture where individuals from all backgrounds and walks of life feel empowered to contribute their unique perspectives. Our collaborative environment celebrates the richness of ideas and experiences, and we believe that by embracing diversity, we can achieve greater innovation and excellence together. Come and help us create a workplace that reflects the beautiful tapestry of our global community.

## Join our growing team!

2241650.title: Industrial Electrician
2241650.description:
Job Title: Industrial Electrician

Location: Baie-Sainte-Anne, NB
Job Type: Full-Time
Wage: $40-$45/hour
Schedule: Monday to Friday, 8am-5pm or 2pm-10pm, weekends as needed

## About the Position

We are looking for an experienced Industrial Electrician to join our team. The successful candidate will be responsible for installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing electrical systems and industrial equipment while ensuring all work is completed safely and in accordance with applicable electrical codes and company standards.

## Responsibilities

• Install, maintain, troubleshoot, and repair industrial electrical systems and equipment

• Diagnose electrical faults and perform preventative maintenance

• Read and interpret electrical drawings, schematics, and wiring diagrams

• Install and maintain motors, controls, PLCs, sensors, and related equipment

• Perform electrical testing and inspections

• Respond to equipment breakdowns and minimize production downtime

• Maintain accurate maintenance and service records

• Follow all company safety procedures and applicable electrical codes

• Work with maintenance, operations, and other trades to resolve equipment issues

• Participate in planned shutdowns and occasional overtime as required

## Qualifications

• Red Seal Industrial Electrician certification or equivalent provincial certification

## This is the life-changing opportunity you've been looking for.

Horizon Health Network in beautiful New Brunswick is looking for a HR Business Partner to join our team!

The HR Business Partner (HRBP) is a strategic advisor and trusted partner to business leaders, responsible for aligning HR strategies with organizational and departmental goals. This role drives talent management, performance and culture, workforce planning, and compliance while leveraging data?driven insights to support informed decision?making. The HRBP plays a critical role in building organizational capability, fostering employee engagement, supporting change, and ensuring HR practices enable sustainable business performance.

## Why you should work here

Working for Horizon gives you a career that provides an east coast lifestyle and the chance to make a big difference in the lives of New Brunswickers.

This position comes with competitive salary, paid time off, sick benefits, employer paid contributions into our government pension plan and a remote work policy.

Horizon is committed to enhancing our diverse and inclusive environment for our employees and patients. We believe in a healthcare system that equally supports all people regardless of race, ethnicity, national origin, social background, religion, gender identity or expression, age, disability, or sexual orientation. An environment based on a commitment to diversity and inclusion supports our goal of safe and quality patient care.

## Who you are

• Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or related field.

• 5+ years of progressive HR experience, including at least 2 years in a business partner or advisory role.

• Strong knowledge of HR policies, employment law, and HR best practices.

• Experience in performance management, workforce planning, and talent acquisition.

• Proficiency in HR analytics and data?driven decision?making

## What you will do

• Strategic Alignment: Partner with leaders to translate business strategy into HR initiatives, align workforce planning with organizational goals, and advise on organizational design and restructuring.

• Talent Management: Support talent acquisition, onboarding, succession planning, leadership development, and retention strategies; identify and develop high?potential talent.

• Performance & Culture: Support performance management processes, including coaching and corrective actions; promote a high?performance, inclusive culture and embed company values.

• Workforce Planning & Analytics: Develop workforce plans and use HR data, reporting, and analytics to identify trends, risks, and opportunities that inform business decisions.

• Employee Relations & Coaching: Serve as a trusted advisor on employee relations matters; coach leaders on conflict resolution, people management, and policy application.

• Change Management: Support and guide organizational change initiatives, assessing impacts and driving communication, readiness, and adoption strategies.

• Compensation & Rewards: Advise on compensation decisions, reward programs, and recognition strategies to ensure internal equity and market competitiveness.

• Compliance, Safety & Risk Management: Ensure compliance with labor laws, policies, and safety standards; mitigate HR?related risks and partner with legal/Labour Relations on complex cases.

• Stakeholder Collaboration: Build strong relationships with leaders and HR partners; collaborate with Centers of Excellence and HR Operations to deliver integrated HR solutions.

## Skills and Competencies

• Strategic thinking and business acumen.

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

• Ability to influence and build strong relationships with leaders.

• Analytical mindset with experience in HR metrics and reporting.

• Problem-solving and conflict resolution skills.

In addition to LEADS, all positions need to demonstrate compassion, patience, and professionalism in all interactions, consistently upholding a respectful and supportive environment for patients, clients, families, and colleagues. ## JOB PURPOSE

Provide exceptional leadership and clinical expertise within the Emergency Department, ensuring the highest standards of patient care and staff performance. The incumbent will demonstrate strong leadership abilities, motivate and mentor staff, and exhibit excellent communication and problem-solving skills. Responsibilities include maintaining clinical competencies, staying current with nursing trends, developing patient care assignments, and collaborating with management and clinical nurse educators on education and resource utilization. The role also involves supporting staff, promoting a professional practice environment, and ensuring compliance with privacy legislation and health authority policies. This position reports to the appropriate Critical Care Director.

## QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor of Nursing or eligible for same

• Active registration within the province of New Brunswick

• At least 5 years of clinical nursing experience within the Emergency Department in the last seven years

• Demonstrated strong leadership abilities. Must be able to motivate staff and have excellent positive communication skills

• Demonstrate ability as a role model/mentor/leader within the interdisciplinary team

• Demonstrate ability to incorporate nursing theory and evidence-based practice into the provision of patient care

• Demonstrate competence in clinical expertise in relevant clinical area

• Demonstrate ability to support, adapt and facilitate change within the health network

• Demonstrate team building skills and ability to evaluate work performance

• Good previous work and attendance record

• Mentally and physically capable of performing the duties. Able to physically manage assignments in all areas of the Emergency Department

• Previous experience in supervisory or managerial roles is recommended but not required.

## KEY RESPONSIBILITES

• Attend workshops and in-services as applicable and relay information to other staff members

• Maintain certification of clinical skills required on the unit

• Maintain an awareness of recent trends and issues related to the nursing profession and Emergency nursing care

• Strengthen professional self-development through relevant continuing education

• Motivate others

• Consistently exhibit excellent and positive communication skills. Be a good listener and consider all points of view.

• Be objective and fair

• Delegate tasks appropriately and prioritize care

• Develop daily patient care assignments based on patient needs, continuity of care and staff development

• Participates in orientation of new staff

• Provide support and guidance to staff with decision making

• Collaborate with Nurse Manager and Critical Care Educator regarding the need for staff education, counselling and conflict resolution

• Participate in performance appraisals

• Act as a role model to promote a professional practice environment and high standard of care

• Work collaboratively with Nurse Manager to ensure appropriate utilization of finances within the unit

• Maintain awareness of the need for cost containment and relay information to staff (i.e.. suggest alternate material and human resources that are more cost effective)

• Coordinate the maintenance and repair of equipment in collaboration with Nurse Manager

• Demonstrate adherence to all privacy legislation and Health Authority policies to ensure all confidential patient, business, financial and employee information is accessed on a need to know basis only (for required job duties) and is disclosed only to those authorized to receive it.

• Assist Nurse Manager with quality improvement initiatives and collection of relevant data to support nursing in the care of patients.

## COMPETENCIES

• Communication and Interpersonal Skills

• Emotional Intelligence

• Assessment skills

• Patient/client focus

• Planning and prioritizing work

• Decision making

• Critical thinking

• Problem solving

• Teamwork and collaboration

• Professionalism

• Positive attitude

• Organizational ability

• Strong leadership and decision-making skills
