About Us
The Correctional Services division of the Department of Justice is responsible for the administration and operation of community and custody-based programs and services for adults and young persons. Within the Correctional Services core business area there are two programs: community corrections & correctional facilities. Each of these program areas is broken down into closely related activities that have a specific impact on the program's target group.
Community Corrections has 22 offices across the province from Yarmouth to Sydney and is responsible for the supervision of both adult and young persons serving community-based sentences. The sentences include probation, conditional sentence, custody and supervision, conditional supervision and Intensive Rehabilitative Custody and Supervision. Probation officers also supervise those released from custody on conditional releases and prepare pre-sentence investigations to assist the Courts in the sentencing process. Evidence based Program facilitation and supports to specialized courts in areas of domestic violence, mental health and wellness are also part of the role of a Probation Officer as well as Restorative Justice casework and collaboration with community justice agencies.
Four (4) adult correctional facilities and one (1) youth centre provide the safety and security of person in custody while providing programs that address dynamic criminogenic factors to assist with their successful, reintegration back into the community.
Nova Scotia Correctional Services utilizes an evidence-based approach in both Community Corrections and custodial facilities. Core Correctional Practices (CCP) is the foundational practice that drives reintegration and rehabilitation practices deployed within Correctional Services. Utilizing CCP, Correctional Services staff can effectively interact, manage behavior, and help facilitate change, within target populations.
For more information on the Department of Justice Correctional Services please visit our website: https://novascotia.ca/just/Corrections/

About Our Opportunity
As the Captain, you are responsible for supervising Correctional Workers/Officer and ensuring the custody, care and control of individuals in custody. Your responsibilities include regular security and maintenance inspections of the facility to ensure that proper cleanliness and security standards are being maintained. The incumbent is responsible for the development and evaluation of subordinate staff. This includes implementing necessary correction and developmental action, attendance management, shift scheduling, participation in the recruitment process and correctional programming. As the Captain you will conduct special projects, investigations and fine calculations, working regularly with Correctional Services policies and procedures, standing orders, and directives.

Primary Accountabilities
• Maintain the administration and operation of a provincial correctional facility including the safety of individuals in custody, staff and the public

• Maintain the daily facility schedule and ensure these are delivered consistent with schedules (i.e. cleaning, group program activities, etc.)

• Manages the admission and discharge of individuals in custody ensuring the validity of warrants produced

• Ensures the effective management of human and financial resources

• Assigns and delegates work assignments, workloads and directives as well as participates in the recruitment, selection, placement and retention of staff

• Chair of the Unit Review Boards for transfers of individuals in custody in accordance with the Corrections Act and Policy and Procedures

• Investigate and gather information linked to disciplinary levels for the Provincial Adjudicator

• Participate in the Institutional Review Board for participation of individuals in custody in programs and Temporary Leaves of Absence in the community

• Supervises the operation of mechanical and electrical systems

Qualifications and Experience
You will have a High school diploma, completion of a Correctional Officer certificate program and several years of experience as a Correctional Officer or Corrections Youth Worker. You will have previous supervisory experience and a university degree from a recognized institution. An acceptable equivalent combination of education, training and experience in other areas of Corrections, Criminal Justice, Policing, or Court Services may be considered. Experience keyboarding and working in a computerized environment would be an asset.
During the interview, you as the successful candidate will demonstrate knowledge and understanding of currently accepted correctional strategies and philosophies all in the aspects of correctional facility operations. You understand custody management, crisis management and prevention, safety and security, administrative routines and allocation of human and material resources. You as the incumbent will also have effective communication and interpersonal skills with strong leadership abilities to support the development of rapport with institutional staff and individuals in custody. Sound decision-making and problem-solving abilities are also a requirement.
You as the successful candidate will demonstrate an attitude towards individuals in custody and the criminal justice system that is compatible with the objectives the Department of Justice, the Correctional Services Division and the goals of the Correctional Facility.
The Government of Nova Scotia has adopted the LEADS Leadership Framework. During the interview, candidates will be expected to express how they have demonstrated the key behaviours and capabilities required to effectively lead in a caring and inclusive environment. LEADS Domains includes Leads Self, Engage Others, Achieve Results, Develop Coalitions and Systems Transformation.
Please follow LEADS (novascotia.ca) for more information.
We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
An acceptable equivalent combination of education, training and experience in other areas of Corrections, Criminal Justice, Policing, or Court Services may be considered. Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions

• Approximately 95% of your time is spent inside the facility consisting of physical rounds, interviewing, conducting meetings, planning, or overseeing operations including team interventions

• Under constant pressure to meet deadlines, make decisions, frequently must deal with members of the public, staff and individuals in custody

Additional Information

Our eight Financial Advisory Services (FAS) units work directly with departments, Crown corporations, and other public service entities, providing support in budgeting, forecasting, and program-related financial advice. Interested in making a difference in our province? We encourage you to Choose GNB!

## Who we are

The work we do has a positive impact on our communities, and helps improve the everyday lives of New Brunswickers. Together, we are over 45,000 New Brunswickers who are passionate problem-solvers, who make a difference and are proud to call New Brunswick home.

The Department of Justice and Public Safety is dedicated to the rule of law, the promotion of the public interest, and the impartial administration of justice and works to improve the safety, security and resiliency of communities and citizens.

The Attorney General is the law officer of the Executive Council and is responsible to see that the administration of public affairs is in accordance with the law and to ensure protection of the public interest. The Legal Services Branch provides civil and constitutional legal advice and representation to all provincial government departments and related agencies.

The Office of the Attorney General is seeking an individual to join the Legal Services Branch as Lawyer 1 or 2 within the Legal Advice Services Group.

## What you will do

The successful candidate will be responsible for conducting research in a wide variety of areas of the law and for providing legal opinions to government departments and agencies on matters of statutory interpretation and general advice with respect to the conduct of government affairs and operations.

2241798.title: Marketing and Events Coordinator
2241798.employer: Chartered Professionals in Human Resources New Brunswick
2241798.description:
Marketing and Events Coordinator

Full-Time / Remote

Based in New Brunswick with Travel Requirements

Salary: $55,000-$62,000 Annually Based on Experience, Qualifications and Skills

CPHR New Brunswick is seeking a Marketing and Events Coordinator to help grow our reach, strengthen relationships with members and partners, and create experiences that bring New Brunswick's HR and business communities together. This role brings together marketing strategy, sponsorship development and hands-on event delivery. The coordinator will have the independence to lead projects from planning through execution while working closely with colleagues, volunteers and partners. This role will suit someone who enjoys meeting people, building relationships and bringing energy to in-person events. While much of the planning and marketing work happens remotely, the coordinator will regularly connect with members, sponsors and partners and be on-site to deliver events throughout New Brunswick.

## What We offer

Flexibility is one of the things we value most. We offer remote work and flexibility in organizing the workday, with the trust to manage responsibilities while making room for life outside work. Events and meetings require availability at set times, but outside those commitments, there is room to establish a working rhythm that supports both professional responsibilities and personal life.

Our small, collaborative team provides an environment where everyone has a voice. The coordinator will have ownership of their portfolio and the independence to lead it, with colleagues who share ideas, offer support and figure things out together. We also offer a competitive compensation package and benefits that support employee well-being. As CPHR New Brunswick grows, the coordinator will have opportunities to shape the role and see the impact of their work on our members and workplaces across the province.

## Responsibilities

• The coordinator will develop and lead a marketing strategy that identifies key audiences, sets clear priorities and supports CPHR New Brunswick's goals. This includes creating campaigns for membership, professional development, partnerships and events, and coordinating content in English and French across email, social media, the website and other channels.

• The role includes establishing and managing marketing KPIs, tracking progress and using findings to guide decisions.

• Business development is an important part of this position. The coordinator will proactively identify and pursue new sponsorship opportunities while also growing relationships and opportunities with existing partners. This includes identifying prospective sponsors, conducting outreach, developing proposals, securing commitments and cultivating strong, long-term partner relationships.

• Throughout the year, the coordinator will plan and deliver multiple events, managing everything from budgets and suppliers to promotion and the on-site experience, while building connections across New Brunswick's HR and business communities.

## Qualifications & Skills required

• Experience developing and implementing successful marketing strategies that support organizational business goals.

• Experience creating content for and managing organizational social media accounts, including planning, publishing, community engagement and performance tracking.

• Demonstrated success proactively securing new sales, sponsorships or comparable partnerships, as well as growing existing partner relationships.

• Experience planning and delivering events, including managing competing priorities and responding to changes on event day.

• Advanced written and spoken communication skills in both English and French. These skills will be assessed during the selection process.

• Strong organizational skills and the ability to make decisions and move work forward independently.

• A collaborative approach and demonstrated ability to build strong professional relationships.

Applicants whose experience has provided the skills to succeed in this role are encouraged to apply.

## Location, Travel and Work Authorization

This is a remote position based in New Brunswick, with regular travel throughout the province and occasional travel outside New Brunswick. Occasional evening and weekend work is required to support events, with scheduling adjusted accordingly. The coordinator will need to be available to attend and deliver events as planned. Reasonable work-related travel expenses will be reimbursed in accordance with CPHR New Brunswick's travel and expense policy.

The ability to travel throughout New Brunswick, including to locations that may not be accessible by public transportation, is required. The role requires the ability to carry out the physical requirements associated with event setup and teardown, with accommodation where required. This includes transporting and carrying marketing materials to and from events, lifting, bending and assembling pop-up marketing displays and other event materials.

The successful candidate must be legally authorized to work in Canada and reside in New Brunswick by the start date of the role. CPHR New Brunswick is unable to provide immigration sponsorship for this position.

## How to Apply

Please submit a résumé to tina@cphrnb.ca by October 15, 2026.

CPHR New Brunswick welcomes applications from people of all backgrounds and identities and is committed to an accessible and inclusive hiring process. Accommodations are available at any stage of recruitment. Applicants are encouraged to let us know what would support their participation.

2241806.description:
## Recreation Programmer

The Birches Nursing Home in Musquodoboit Harbour, NS, Canada
Facility: The Birches Nursing Home
Location: 7702 HWY 7, Musquodoboit Harbour, Nova Scotia
Job Category: Nursing, Healthcare
Position Available: Permanent Full-Time

## Facility Description:

As a Community Governed Organization and part of the Musquodoboit Harbour community since 1979, The Birches is home to 42 long term care residents who benefit from our focus on resident-centered care and honouring each person's lifelong routine.

This is made possible through the dedication of fantastic staff from a variety of disciplines, including nursing, continuing care assistants, recreation, maintenance, food services, laundry, housekeeping, and administrative support. Active volunteers also complement our day-to-day work. The Birches is committed to the highest standards of support and services and promotes a health workplace for its 100 staff. The organization fosters a healthy work life balance and uses the latest best practice information at all levels.

## JOB SUMMARY:

The Recreation Programmer is responsible for planning, implementing and evaluating leisure/ therapeutic recreation on an individual basis and/or group program. The Recreation Programmer must demonstrate an understanding of the cognitive, physical, emotional, intellectual, spiritual and psycho-social benefits that therapeutic recreation provides in maintaining and/or enhancing the quality of life for residents.

## QUALIFICATIONS:

• A post-secondary degree in Recreation/Leisure Studies OR a two (2) year community college diploma in Recreation. Preference given to those with bachelor's degree in Therapeutic Recreation and certification with NCTRC.

• Gerontology Certificate an asset.

• Minimum one year work experience in providing leadership in recreation planning and implementing of programs in a long-term care setting an asset.

• An active membership with the Nova Scotia Therapeutic Recreation Association and keep with current new programming approaches and trends in the field is an asset.

• Must possess the following characteristics and skills: strong interpersonal skills, including active listening and empathy; effective oral and written communication skills; excellent organizational and planning skills; creative problem-solving and good assessment skills.

• Basic computer skills required.

• Must provide valid criminal record check and vulnerable record check.

## The Birches Offers:

• Free Parking

• Comprehensive Benefits Package

• Comprehensive Orientation

• A supportive work environment

Salary Range: In accordance with current collective agreement between The Birches and C.U.P.E. Local 3199

HOURS OF WORK: Schedule is flexible, includes weekends, days/evenings and availability for special events.

## Please note:

• This facility is not located on a bus route. Reliable transportation is required.

• Please be aware that The Birches is a pet friendly environment.

• If the full application form is not completed with all applicable information, your application will not be reviewed.

2241807.description:
Evergreen Home for Special Care - Children's Centre one 0.6 permanent part time job openings for continuing care assistants ( NOC 33102)

Evergreen Home for Special Care is a privately owned continuous care provider located in the beautiful Annapolis Valley.

The facility is comprised of a Children Centre which is licensed to provide 24-hour nursing coverage for 20 children and a Seniors Centre consisting of 98 residents. All residents receive multi-disciplinary care based on a holistic approach to ensure physical, mental and spiritual wellbeing while recognizing the right to individuality, respect, and dignity.

Programming in the Children Centre is conducted on an individual basis and some of the children attend school outside the facility. Full and part time professional nursing care is provided to children of all ages and respite care is available to families in need.

## Responsibilities:

• Assisting clients with various personal care activities (e.g., bathing, dressing, grooming).

• Perform light housekeeping duties.

• Assist clients with meals and between meal refreshments.

• Provide respite for families and care givers.

• Documentation (e.g., reporting client concerns, progress notes, incident reports).

• Engage residents/families in leisure/recreational programs.

## Core Requirements:

• Provincial Continuing Care Assistant Certification

• Persons with related education and/or work experience and are enrolled in or are eligible to be enrolled in CCA RPL Program

• Students in nursing, CCA programs, and international educated nurses will be considered.

Continuing Care Assistant in Training means a person employed as a Continuing Care Assistant who is

• Hired on a conditional basis in accordance with the Educational Requirements for Entry to Practice of Non-Licensed Care Staff Policy.

2239845.title: Supervisor, Maintenance
2239845.description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is growing?

## Who We Are

We are a global mining company dedicated to safely delivering nickel, copper, cobalt, and platinum group metals essential for the world's energy transition.

Our mission is to improve lives and shape a better future together.

From utensils to cellphones to satellites, our operations simplify daily life and enhance connectivity. Our metals are integral to life-saving medical equipment and the electric vehicles driving the fight against climate change – our work truly matters.

Join our diverse team of 15,000 talented individuals committed to transforming critical minerals into prosperity and sustainable development in countries like Canada, Brazil, Indonesia, the United Kingdom, and Japan. We invite you to use your skills with us and contribute to something meaningful and enduring.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking a Supervisor, Maintenance (Mobile) to join our Copper Cliff South Mine team in Sudbury, Ontario.

This is a permanent onsite position. The work schedule is days/nights on a 5/4 rotation.

As a Supervisor, Maintenance (Mobile) you will be accountable for continuously improving the work team performance through the effective use of established processes and procedures at South Mine. Your experience and skills will establish and maintain work relationships with the various key plant stakeholders including supervisors, planners, schedulers, superintendents, crew members, etc.

Additionally, in this position you will:

• Adhere to maintenance business processes as outlined in Maintenance Planning and Control (MPC) by using approved systems (SAP, Prometheus, etc.), tools, and standards.

• Review and promote/reject all new Urgent notifications in your work center through the group approval process.

• Ensure planned work orders are closed with proper time confirmations completed. Identify and escalate all critical issues that threaten the successful execution of work orders for completion by their Required End Date.

• Monitor KPIs and actively strive toward plant targets.

• Work within assigned budgets and escalate to management should a budget be exceeded.

• Establish and maintain work relationships with the various key plant stakeholders including supervisors, planners, schedulers, superintendents, crew members, etc.

2241815.title: Supervisor, Logistics
2241815.description:
## Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is growing?

## Who We Are

We are a global mining company dedicated to safely delivering nickel, copper, cobalt, and platinum group metals essential for the world's energy transition.

Our mission is to improve lives and shape a better future together.

From utensils to cellphones to satellites, our operations simplify daily life and enhance connectivity. Our metals are integral to life-saving medical equipment and the electric vehicles driving the fight against climate change – our work truly matters.

Join our diverse team of 15,000 talented individuals committed to transforming critical minerals into prosperity and sustainable development in countries like Canada, Brazil, Indonesia, the United Kingdom, and Japan. We invite you to use your skills with us and contribute to something meaningful and enduring.

## The Opportunity

We are seeking a Logistics Supervisor to join our Commercial Logistics team in Sudbury, Ontario.

This is a permanent position supporting Vale Base Metals logistics operations across Ontario and other North American locations. The role is based in Sudbury and reports to the Manager, Supply Chain Americas. The Logistics Supervisor is responsible for leading a team of Logistics Administrators and overseeing the movement, storage, and distribution of nickel finished products, copper products, purchased feeds, intermediate products, and reagents. The position plays a critical role in ensuring the safe, reliable, and cost-effective execution of transportation and logistics services across multiple modes including trucking, rail, ports, vessels, and containerized shipments. The successful candidate will provide leadership in logistics execution, contract management, inventory oversight, stakeholder engagement, and continuous improvement initiatives while ensuring alignment with production plans, customer requirements, and Vale's commitment to safety and operational excellence.

## About You

You are a collaborative and results-oriented logistics professional with demonstrated leadership experience in transportation, supply chain, or materials management environments. You thrive in a fast-paced operational setting where balancing business priorities, stakeholder expectations, safety requirements, and service excellence is critical. You bring strong knowledge of logistics operations, contractor management, transportation networks, and inventory controls. Your ability to build relationships, solve complex operational challenges, and lead teams through changing priorities allows you to consistently deliver reliable business outcomes.

## In this role, you will:

• Lead, coach, mentor, and develop a team of Logistics Administrators to ensure safe and effective execution of daily, weekly, and monthly logistics activities.

• Oversee logistics operations supporting more than 50,000 tonnes of nickel finished products, 178,000 tonnes of copper products, 100,000 tonnes of purchased feeds, and other intermediate materials.

• Coordinate and schedule transportation requirements involving trucking, rail, containers, vessels, and port operations to support production and customer commitments.

• Manage inventories at Vale facilities and third-party locations to ensure inventory accuracy, product availability, and operational efficiency.

• Collaborate with Operations, Technical Services, Finance, Sales and Marketing, Procurement, and external service providers to support business and production objectives.

• Develop, review, and modify logistics-related scopes of work and service requirements for transportation and logistics contracts.

• Support the negotiation, implementation, and management of logistics contracts to ensure reliable and cost-effective services.

• Monitor contractor performance, conduct audits, manage non-conformances, and work closely with Procurement on sourcing activities, change orders, and escalations.

• Provide logistics expertise related to freight options, transportation lanes, and cost estimates to support changing business requirements.

• Develop and implement contingency plans to minimize operational disruptions resulting from service interruptions, labour disputes, or transportation challenges.

• Lead communication and coordination with key internal and external stakeholders to ensure safety, production, and customer service objectives are achieved.

• Ensure compliance with company policies, regulatory requirements, environmental standards, and transportation legislation.

• Participate in internal and external audits and drive continuous improvement initiatives across logistics operations.

• Support budget management and execution plans while identifying opportunities for service optimization and cost reduction.

• Promote a culture of safety, teamwork, accountability, ethical conduct, and operational excellence.

## Experience

• Minimum 5–7 years of progressive experience in logistics, transportation, supply chain, materials management, operations, or contract management.

• Previous supervisory or team leadership experience in an industrial, manufacturing, mining, transportation, or supply chain environment.

• Experience coordinating multimodal transportation services including trucking, rail, warehousing, and port operations.

• Demonstrated experience managing contractor performance, service agreements, and stakeholder relationships.

• Experience working within complex operational environments with multiple internal and external stakeholders.

## Education

• Bachelor's degree in supply chain management, Logistics, Business Administration, Engineering, Commerce, or a related discipline.

• Supply Chain certifications such as CSCP, CLTD, SCMP, or equivalent are considered assets.

• Completion of Vale's Supervisor Training Program is considered an asset.

## Skills & Competencies

• Strong leadership, coaching, and team development capabilities.

• Sound knowledge of transportation logistics, rail operations, trucking, warehousing, port services, and inventory management.

• Strong contract administration and contractor performance management experience.

• Excellent problem-solving, decision-making, and organizational skills.

• Strong communication and stakeholder management abilities.

• Ability to manage competing priorities and make critical operational decisions in a dynamic environment.

• Knowledge of safety management systems, environmental compliance, and regulatory requirements.

• Strong analytical and financial acumen with the ability to evaluate logistics costs and identify optimization opportunities.

• Proficiency with logistics, inventory, transportation, and enterprise business systems.

• Strong commitment to continuous improvement, operational excellence, and customer service.

## What Makes This Role Unique

• Lead a team of five unionized Logistics Administrators supporting critical logistics activities for Vale Base Metals operations.

• Manage logistics movements across multiple Canadian provinces and international destinations.

• Support transportation requirements involving approximately 6,900 truck movements annually, including approximately 2,700 direct-to-customer deliveries.

• Oversee more than 12 logistics service contracts with an annual value exceeding CAD $30 million.

• Play a key role in supporting the movement of strategically important nickel and copper products that contribute to the global energy transition.

## What We Offer You

• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans, and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare online

• Online training and career development opportunities

## Why Sudbury

Sudbury is one of Canada's premier mining centres and a global leader in mining innovation, technology, and sustainability. Home to world-class mining operations and a highly skilled workforce, Sudbury provides unique opportunities to work on industry-leading projects that support the growing demand for critical minerals worldwide. Working in Sudbury offers access to excellent outdoor recreation, strong community connections, and a high quality of life while contributing to the future of responsible resource development and the global energy transition.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people feel comfortable to be themselves. Vale encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all.

We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other

fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

Accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

2241810.title: Event Services Coordinator
2241810.description:
## Event Services Coordinator

At St. John's Sports & Entertainment Ltd. (SJSEL), we operate two of Newfoundland and Labrador's iconic venues: Mary Brown's Centre and the St. John's Convention Centre. Together, we host everything from concerts and sporting events to conventions, trade shows, meetings, and community celebrations.

Our vision is constant: Reimagining Events. Igniting Connection. Moving People.

Our Event Services Coordinators help bring that vision to life. As a member of the team, you'll work with clients and internal teams to plan, coordinate, and deliver events across both venues. You'll be responsible for the details that connect planning to execution, ensuring events are organized, operationally ready, and delivered to a high standard.

This is a one year contract position reporting to the Manager, Event Services, you'll serve as a key point of contact throughout the event lifecycle, helping transform confirmed bookings into successful experiences for clients, guests, performers, exhibitors, and more.

## About SJSEL:

Based in the heart of downtown St. John's, we welcome guests from across Newfoundland and Labrador and beyond for live entertainment, sport, business events, and community gatherings.

The experiences we help create contribute to the cultural, social, and economic vibrancy of our province. Guided by a commitment to innovation and continuous improvement, our team works behind the scenes to reimagine what's possible and deliver events safely, efficiently, and professionally.

## Key Responsibilities:

• Serve as the primary point of accountability for event execution of the assigned events at the Mary Brown's Centre and St. John's Convention Centre, managing relationships from contract through post-event follow-up and ensuring expectations are met. Oversee end-to-end event planning and delivery across events of varying scope and scale, with accountability for integrated operational readiness.

• Exercise judgment in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment by directing operational priorities, allocating resources, and resolving event-related issues across two facilities.

• Act as Manager on Duty for assigned events, providing onsite operational leadership and decision-making authority for client, staffing, safety, and operational matters.

• Lead and oversee the Event Services casual employees as it relates to the assigned event, serving as the primary point of accountability for performance, event staffing schedules, skill development, coaching, and issue resolution, in alignment with the Manager of Event Services to support consistency and effectiveness across the team.

• Create, review, and approve Event Services staffing schedules.

• Determine and communicate event-specific cleaning and maintenance requirements to the applicable department, ensuring operational needs are clearly defined.

• Interpret client, promoter, and tenant requirements and convert them into comprehensive operational plans and event documentation escalating contractual or policy issues when necessary.

• Lead cross-department communication to clarify expectations, align resources, and ensure consistent execution by internal teams and external partners.

• Support booking and sales activity for the Mary Brown's Centre.

• Receive confirmed bookings for the St. John's Convention Centre from the Sales team and assume responsibility for the event, including managing contract updates when changes are required.

• Prepare event pre-settlements, initiate billing processes, track financial information, and work in conjunction with the Manager of Finance to support accurate invoicing and compliance for events at the Mary Brown's Centre.

• Prepare and finalize client invoices for events at the St. John's Convention Centre with full accountability for accuracy.

• Assume responsibility for reviewing and approving time & attendance for Event Services during the Manager of Event Services' absence.

• Liaise with Technical Operations Manager to ensure the appropriate level of building access is provided related to the event. Maintain accurate and complete event records, files, and documentation across event management systems and digital and paper records.

• In accordance with the organization's policies and procedures, identify and report safety, cleaning, and maintenance issues.

• Preparation and communication of ticket breakdown, seating manifests, pricing structures, holds, discounts, presales, reporting, promoter updates, and on-sale logistics.

• Serve as backup to the Coordinator Ticketing & Client Services, with responsibility for completing ticket builds, ensure the financial accuracy of fees and surcharges, and meeting critical timelines for event announcements and on-sales.

• Participates in strategic planning processes as it relates to Event Services.

## Qualifications:

Education:

• Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Hospitality Management, Marketing, or a related field.

Specific Skills/Certifications:

• Strong strategic thinking and planning skills, with the ability to translate high-level direction into actionable plans, measurable outcomes, and cross-departmental initiatives.

• Proven ability to plan and execute large scale, complex, multi faceted events effectively with a strong attention to detail.

• Skilled in all processes of the ticketing module and other accredited software approved by SJSEL.

• Excellent computer skills including Microsoft Office, with a proficiency in using Microsoft Excel.

• Effectively use SJSEL's booking and event management software, and other management tools, and be willing and able to learn various software programs related to providing ticketing and technology-based event services as required to implement events.

• Ability to lead, and direct staff.

• Ability to deal with a variety of situations in a tactful and professional manner.

• Superior interpersonal and communication (verbal and written) skills, with a collaborative approach to working across departments and with external stakeholders.

• Ability to take initiative and make informed decisions while maintaining professionalism in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

Relevant Experience:

• Minimum of three (3) years event services management experience with knowledge of hospitality industry practices.

• Experience in large upscale event planning.

Not checking every box? We encourage you to apply. We recognize that valuable experience can be gained through many different paths, and candidates with an equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.

## Work Environment:

At SJSEL, successful events are built through collaboration, trust, and a shared commitment to delivering exceptional experiences.

This role works closely with clients, promoters, tenants, vendors, guests, and colleagues across multiple departments. No two events are exactly alike, and success requires strong communication, adaptability, and teamwork.

Our venues are active, high-profile environments where planning and preparation are just as important as event-day execution. You'll spend your time coordinating event details, supporting stakeholders, and helping ensure events are delivered successfully.

SJSEL is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a qualified workforce that reflects the diversity of the communities we serve. We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package, including:

• Competitive salary

• Healthy work-life balance

• Cost shared group insurance plan

• Generous paid leave program

## Scheduling Requirements:

• Ability to work varying shifts including early mornings, late nights, weekends and holidays.

## How to Apply:

The region provides a wide range of services, including receiving and processing rental applications; administering rental accounts and lease compliance provisions; providing various client services and tenant relations including eviction prevention, and monitoring, facilitating and administering property maintenance. Employment Opportunity- Town Manager

The Town of Deer Lake is perfectly located within the province of Newfoundland and Labrador as it serves as the central hub between Labrador and the Island of Newfoundland. Beautifully situated at the top of the Humber Valley, Deer Lake serves as the gateway to Gros Morne National Park, Northern Peninsula and Labrador. Home to approximately 5,000 residents, our thriving Town of Deer Lake offers endless freshwater beaches, a thriving regional airport, and is commonly affirmed as the snowmobile hub of the island.

The Town Council of Deer Lake is pursuing to hire a Town Manager to provide leadership and direction and shall bear the responsibility for the overall administration of the Town's organization including labour relations, risk management; budgeting; financial analysis and executing all municipal policies and bylaws set forth by Council. In addition, the manager shall provide broad policy and general guidance to department heads related to operations, fiscal and general management function; and to provide close general supervision to personnel within the administrative department.

Reporting to Council, this position is responsible for:

• Delivering a safe, respectful and welcoming workplace by providing leadership and direction for all staff, departments and divisions.

• Providing advice to Council regarding policy, governance and operational matters.

• Developing and managing annual budgets and financial plans including capital works.

• Serving as a strong liaison between Deer Lake Search and Rescue, and Deer Lake Airport Authority.

• Ensuring staff remain motivated and committed to delivering a high level of public service while overseeing human resources and staff performance.

• Ensuring compliance with applicable legislation, regulations and Town bylaws.

• Building and maintaining a positive relationship with residents, businesses, community groups and government agencies.

• Coordinating all special projects for the Town including capital infrastructure projects, management studies, new initiatives, programming and various professional services; and

• Developing a respectful relationship with Union representation of the Town's employees by overseeing negotiations and executing existing collective agreements in a fair and unbiased manner.

The Ideal candidate shall possess:

• A bachelor's degree in business administration, commerce, public administration, engineering or related field with minimum of five (5) years progressive senior managerial expertise in the public-sector

• Consideration will be given to candidates with a combination of education and experience acceptable to the Town;

• Professional, ethical with good character and integrity;

• Strong planning and economic development skills;

• Strong financial management and budgeting skills;

• Sound understanding of municipal governance, legislation and administration.

• Effective interpersonal, written and oral communication skills;

• An ability to manage a diverse team of subordinates and department heads;

• Proficient knowledge of with Microsoft Suite programs.

Hours of Work:

This is a salaried position. The incumbent will be expected to attend all scheduled council meeting (public or non-public) which regularly occur within the evening hours. In addition, the incumbent shall be in a rotation with department managers for on-call for emergency services to relieve all other departmental managers.

Salary:

Salary shall be commensurate based on experience and qualifications. A competitive benefits package shall compliment the commensurate package.

If you are interested in opportunity to become part of a dedicated team responsible for providing effective and efficient municipal services and programs for the residents of Deer Lake, please submit a cover letter and resume electronically to the undersigned by 3:00PM on October 23rd, 2026.

## October 2, 2026

## MARINE GEOMATICS SPECIALIST (HYDROGRAPHER)(RTP V)

School of Ocean Technology, Centre for Applied Ocean Technology

Marine Institute

(2-year contractual position)

A campus of Memorial University, the Fisheries and Marine Institute (MI) is North America's most comprehensive marine institute dedicated to education, training, applied research, industrial response, and technology transfer supporting ocean industries. Operating within MI's School of Ocean Technology, the Centre for Applied Ocean Technology (CTec) provides research and development support, industry outreach, and scientific and technical advisory services to clients and partners, with expertise spanning ocean observation, ocean mapping, remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), aerial drones, autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs), and autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs). The Centre is based at The Launch, MI's ocean innovation centre and a cornerstone facility in Canada's ocean innovation ecosystem, located in Holyrood, Newfoundland and Labrador, approximately 35 minutes from St. John's. This team works at the cutting edge of ocean technology, in collaboration with a wide range of marine sectors locally, nationally, and internationally, to enhance the safety, efficiency, sustainability, and profitability of maritime pursuits through the application of technology.

## DUTIES

The successful applicant will work as part of a multidisciplinary team of engineers, technologists, researchers, and instructors supporting MI's ocean mapping and ocean observation education and training programs and undertaking client projects, industry outreach, and collaborative applied research and development with university, government, and industry partners. Clients span the fisheries, aquaculture, marine environmental monitoring, energy, marine transportation, and defence sectors. This role will also require the provision of technical support to instructors and students during field and laboratory-based activities in MI's ocean mapping and other programs, including equipment preparation, system demonstrations, and survey operations.

Duties include mobilizing, integrating, operating, troubleshooting, calibrating, and maintaining hydrographic, oceanographic, and remote-sensing systems used in teaching, applied research, and client projects. The successful applicant will also plan and conduct field surveys; acquire, process, edit, assess, and validate hydrographic, oceanographic, and geospatial data; apply quality-control procedures in accordance with applicable standards and project specifications; and prepare technical documentation, processing reports, data summaries, maps, surfaces, charts, and other project deliverables.

The successful applicant will work directly with ocean-sector clients, researchers, university partners, and technology developers and will contribute to or lead project scoping, proposal and budget development, field execution, data management, technical reporting, and deliverable production. Elements of travel, both within and outside Newfoundland and Labrador, can be expected, as well as participation in at-sea surveys and field programs on MI or external client vessels. The position involves travel within and outside Newfoundland and Labrador and participation in at-sea surveys and field programs aboard MI and external client vessels. This position is based at The Launch in Holyrood, NL.

## QUALIFICATIONS

Applicants must have three to five years of relevant experience in marine surveying and a post-secondary diploma or undergraduate degree in hydrography, ocean mapping, geomatics, GIS, remote sensing, ocean technology, or a related discipline; an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience will be considered. Applicants must demonstrate practical knowledge of and experience with multibeam, sidescan, and other hydrographic sonar systems, including survey planning, system integration, data acquisition, processing, quality control, and deliverable production; proficiency with hydrographic acquisition software and with CARIS HIPS and SIPS or equivalent hydrographic processing software, including data editing, quality control, and surface generation; and proficiency with ArcGIS Pro and related GIS tools for spatial data management, analysis, visualization, and survey deliverable production is required. Experience with single-beam or sub-bottom sonar, oceanographic instrumentation, remote-sensing systems, or data acquisition using ROVs, aerial drones, ASVs, or AUVs would be an asset. Experience operating small vessels in support of hydrographic or oceanographic surveys, or a willingness to undertake appropriate vessel-operation training and certification, would also be an asset. A valid Newfoundland and Labrador Class 5 driver's licence, or an equivalent licence from another jurisdiction, is required. Possession of a valid Marine Emergency Duties (MED) A1 certificate or equivalent marine-safety certification is an asset.

SALARY: $66,626 to $86,520 per annum (Research and Technical Personnel V, NAPE Local 7405)

Reporting directly to the Owner, the Controller will take ownership of the firm's financial operations, including accounting and financial reporting, banking and cash management, taxation, budgeting, payroll, receivables, payables, and financial controls. This is a growth-oriented opportunity for a recently designated CPA who wants to develop a deep understanding of a growing business, work closely with its owner, and progress toward greater financial leadership responsibility over time.

## Key responsibilities include:

Financial Reporting & Accounting

• Lead the preparation, review and finalization of quarterly and annual financial statements, MD&A, press releases and the Annual Information Form.

• Oversee property-level accounting across the company's office, hotel and residential assets, ensuring accuracy, consistency and compliance with IFRS.

• Maintain accounting policies and documentation for significant judgment areas and lead technical accounting research for complex transactions.

• Support business combinations, including business acquisition reports and purchase price allocations.

Valuation, Controls & Compliance

• Oversee complex quarterly fair value analyses, including valuation methodologies, key assumptions, third-party valuations and related financial statement disclosures.

• Oversee 52-109 internal controls over financial reporting and disclosure controls.

• Coordinate with external auditors and respond to regulator, lender and investor reporting inquiries.

Leadership, Planning & Special Projects

• Lead and mentor accounting and finance team members, with a focus on continuous improvement, efficiency and building a high-performing team.

• Prepare and review monthly, quarterly and annual Board reporting.

• Support corporate department budgets, the annual consolidated budget and business plan.

• Lead various projects and contribute to other value-add initiatives across the organization.

The ideal candidate will possess:

• A CPA designation, ideally recently obtained, with approximately 1-5 years of accounting experience.

• Strong knowledge of accounting, financial reporting, taxation, and financial controls.

• Exceptional attention to detail with a strong commitment to accuracy and accountability.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate financial information into useful management reporting.

• A highly organized and dependable approach, with the ability to take ownership of key financial processes.

• An interest in understanding how a growing business operates and contributing to its continued growth.

• Experience in a law firm or with trust accounting is considered an asset but is not required.

This is an exciting opportunity to take on meaningful responsibility within a growing firm, with the opportunity to expand your expertise and progress into a senior financial leadership role as the firm grows.

To express interest in this opportunity please apply online at: https://meridiarecruitment.ca/Career/17909571780350000008xft

For more information about this exciting opportunity please contact Heather Labucki, Partner, or Sara Morey, Senior Consultant at smorey@kbrs.ca. If you require accommodation to participate in the recruitment process, please let Sara know.

Meridia Recruitment Solutions connects leading organizations with top talent by building strong relationships and creating ideal matches with candidates because we are only successful when you are. We appreciate your interest in this opportunity.

To learn more about Meridia Recruitment Solutions, our job opportunities, and career advice we invite you to explore our site and subscribe for career alerts.

2241817.title: Director, Marine Engineering
2241817.description:
Port Saint John is seeking a Marine Engineer to join its Infrastructure, Assets and Engineering team. This role leads and supports marine infrastructure projects that enable safe, efficient and sustainable port operations.

The Marine Engineer provides technical and project management expertise for piers, berths, wharves, navigation channels, turning basins, dredging and other marine assets. The position is the Port's technical lead for capital dredging and supports the operational dredging program while collaborating with internal teams, consultants, contractors, regulators and port users.

Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree in civil, marine, coastal, ocean, geotechnical or structural engineering, or a related engineering discipline.

• Seven to ten years of progressive engineering experience, preferably involving marine or port infrastructure, dredging, coastal works, heavy civil infrastructure or major capital projects.

• Demonstrated experience with project delivery, procurement, construction, contract administration, consultant management and contractor oversight.

• Strong technical judgment, project management, communication, collaboration and problem-solving skills.

• Registration as a Professional Engineer, or eligibility for registration, with the Association of Professional Engineers and Geoscientists of New Brunswick.

• Eligibility to obtain the required Transport Canada security clearance and possession of a valid Class 5 New Brunswick driver's license, or equivalent.

• Project management or related marine construction, dredging, environmental, safety or asset management credentials are considered assets.

You will thrive in this role if you:

• Put safety and wellness first, using a safety-first approach to guide your decisions.

• Show initiative, embrace innovation and persevere when facing obstacles.

• Treat others with respect and build trust through honesty, openness and accountability.

• Commit to continuous learning and support the development of your colleagues.

• Include others by building strong relationships and engaging meaningfully with

Responsibilities
• Plan and deliver marine infrastructure projects from scope development and procurement through construction and close-out.

• Lead the capital dredging program and support operational dredging, including technical review, permitting, budgets, schedules, risk and stakeholder coordination.

• Review engineering drawings, specifications, studies, estimates, tender documents and contractor deliverables.

• Assess navigation channels, vessel accommodation, under-keel clearance, mooring systems, berth loading and related operational requirements.

• Support inspections, condition assessments and lifecycle planning for Port-owned marine assets.

• Coordinate consultants, contractors, regulators, terminal operators and other stakeholders while ensuring compliance with safety, environmental, contractual and regulatory requirements.

• Prepare project updates, reports, recommendations, funding documentation and organized technical records.

Port Saint John operates on the traditional and unceded territory of the Wolastoqey, Mi'Kmaq, and Peskotomuhkati Nations. Our commitment to truth and reconciliation is grounded in respect for Indigenous cultures and heritage and in building meaningful relationships.

Port Saint John connects people and markets by building partnerships and developing innovative solutions that create economic and social value. With links to more than 350 ports worldwide and direct access to central Canadian markets through Canadian National and Canadian Pacific rail networks and the Trans-Canada Highway, the Port is a key facilitator of trade within Canada's Atlantic Gateway. Our transportation infrastructure provides a marine gateway to global markets while supporting prosperity and sustainability.

Help shape the future of marine infrastructure at Port Saint John. If your experience and values align with this opportunity, we invite you to apply.

The application deadline is October 19th.

2241824.title: Bilingual Marketing and Communications Coordinator (Bilingual French and English)
2241824.description:
Bilingual Marketing and Communications Coordinator (Bilingual French and English)

Location: Fredericton
Job Type: Full-time Hybrid/Remote with Regional Travel

## About Us

Behind every person living with Alzheimer's disease and other dementias, there are hundreds of people dedi-cated to helping them. The Alzheimer Society is the leading not-for-profit health organization working nation-wide to improve the quality of life for Canadians affected by Alzheimer's disease and other dementias while ad-vancing the search for a cause and cure. Since 1987, the Alzheimer Society of New Brunswick (ASNB) has been committed to supporting individuals living with dementia, their families, care partners, healthcare profession-als, and communities through education, advocacy, and support.

## Job Summary

As a Marketing and Communications Coordinator, you will play a key role in strengthening the Alzheimer Soci-ety of New Brunswick's brand presence, awareness initiatives, fundraising campaigns, and community engage-ment efforts throughout the province. Reporting to the Manager of Brand and Philanthropy, you will support the development and execution of strategic marketing and communications activities across multiple platforms.

Working collaboratively with all departments, you will create compelling bilingual content, manage digital com-munications channels, support media relations and marketing campaigns, and help share the impact of ASNB's work with donors, volunteers, care partners, healthcare professionals, and the broader community.

## Distinguishing Characteristics

The ideal candidate is a creative and detail-oriented communications professional who is passionate about storytelling, community impact, and mission-driven work. They are an exceptional writer and communicator in both English and French and have experience creating engaging content for a variety of digital and print platforms.

The successful candidate demonstrates initiative, adaptability, strong organizational skills, and sound judgment. They are comfortable managing multiple projects simultaneously, analyzing marketing performance metrics, working collaboratively across departments, and representing the Alzheimer Society of New Brunswick in a pro-fessional and positive manner.

## Typical Duties and Responsibilities

## Marketing and Communications

• Support the development, implementation, and evaluation of internal and external marketing and com-munications activities aligned with ASNB's strategic priorities.

• Contribute to annual communications and marketing plans that increase awareness, engagement, fund-raising success, and brand recognition.

• Create compelling bilingual (English/French) content and graphics for a variety of platforms, including:
• Social media

• Website

• Email marketing and newsletters

• Advertisements

• Press releases

• Promotional materials

• Donor and stewardship communications

• Event and campaign materials

• Maintain and update website content, including landing pages, event information, and key program re-sources to ensure accuracy, accessibility, and alignment with brand standards.

• Monitor and analyze website performance metrics and provide recommendations for optimization and improvement.

• Manage social media platforms including Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, and YouTube, with responsibil-ity for content planning and scheduling, graphic creation, community engagement, monitoring mes-sages, comments, and mentions, performance tracking and reporting.

• Monitor and analyze social media metrics such as reach, engagement, impressions, clicks, shares, and audience growth.

• Coordinate the production of marketing collateral and branded materials in collaboration with internal teams and external vendors.

• Assist in the promotion of programs, services, events, fundraising campaigns, awareness initiatives, and advocacy activities.

• Co-lead one of ASNB's IG Wealth Management Walk for Alzheimer's volunteer organizing committees.

• Collaborate with staff across departments to gather impact stories, client experiences, program out-comes, and organizational updates for external communications.

• Support media relations activities through the development of press releases, media materials, media lists, and coverage tracking.

• Monitor emerging issues, trends, and reputational risks that may affect communications activities and recommend appropriate responses.

• Support internal communications initiatives that promote organizational alignment, information sharing, and employee engagement.

• Ensure brand consistency and compliance across all communications and marketing activities.

## Administration and Professional Development

• Assist with reporting, data entry, administrative tasks, and other duties that contribute to organizational success.

• Support donor stewardship and fund development activities through the identification of potential do-nors, volunteers, community partners, and corporate supporters.

• Participate in provincial and national initiatives as required, including collaboration with Federation part-ners and national working groups.

• Collaborate with the Executive Director and team members to ensure person-centred approaches are reflected throughout organizational activities.

• Foster a culture of philanthropy by supporting awareness, engagement, and fundraising efforts across the organization.

• Participate in ongoing professional development opportunities and stay informed of emerging trends and best practices in marketing, communications, and nonprofit engagement.

• Travel throughout New Brunswick as required.

## Qualifications

• Must be fully bilingual in English and French.

• Post-secondary education in Marketing, Communications, Public Relations, Journalism, Digital Media, or a related field.

• Minimum one years of experience in marketing, communications, public relations, journalism, digital marketing, or a related field.

• Experience working within the nonprofit, healthcare, community service, or charitable sector is consid-ered an asset.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills in both English and French.

• Strong storytelling abilities with experience creating content that engages diverse audiences.

• Demonstrated ability to adapt messaging, tone, and content for different communication channels and audiences.

• Experience managing social media platforms and creating engaging digital content.

• Proficiency with Canva or similar graphic design platforms and basic video editing software.

• Experience using marketing and communications tools, including: Meta Business Suite, Mailerlite or sim-ilar email marketing platforms, website content management systems such as Drupal, analytics and re-porting tools.

• Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office and online collaboration tools.

• Demonstrated commitment to equity, diversity, and inclusion.

• Sensitive to the impact of dementia on individuals, families, and care partners.

• Strong interpersonal skills with a positive, collaborative, and professional approach.

• Ability to work independently while contributing effectively as part of a team.

• Valid New Brunswick driver's license with the ability to travel throughout the province.

• Ability to work occasional evenings and weekends to support events, campaigns, and organizational ac-tivities.

• Criminal Record Check and Vulnerable Sector Check required.

## What We Offer

• A supportive, mission-aligned team environment.

• Collaborative culture.

• Opportunities for professional learning and career development.

• Comprehensive benefits package including health and dental coverage, wellness initiatives, paid time off, and retirement contributions.

• Mileage and travel reimbursement for approved travel.

## Equity Statement

The Alzheimer Society of New Brunswick is committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcomed, respected, and valued. We encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds and are com-mitted to providing an accessible recruitment process. Accommodations are available upon request throughout the hiring process.

## How to Apply

If you are passionate about making a meaningful difference in the lives of people living with dementia and their families, we'd love to hear from you. Please submit your resume and cover letter outlining your qualifications and interest in the position to info@alzheimernb.ca.

Located in the heart of New Brunswick, Mount Carleton Provincial Park is a breathtaking destination committed to preserving and showcasing the natural beauty of the Appalachian Mountain Range. As the highest peak in the Maritimes, Mount Carleton offers visitors a unique experience, with over 42,000 acres of pristine wilderness to explore.

Our park is a haven for outdoor enthusiasts, offering opportunities for hiking, camping, fishing and stargazing in one of the darkest skies in Eastern Canada. With a rich cultural history and a deep commitment to conservation, Mount Carleton is more than a scenic retreat - it's a place to connect with nature, to explore diverse ecosystems and to enjoy unforgettable experiences.

Joining our team means becoming part of a community dedicated to providing exceptional service to visitors, promoting environmental stewardship, and sharing the wonders of New Brunswick's natural heritage.

Capital Planning & Operations is a team of approximately 130 employees that take tremendous pride in the campus and deliver exceptional service that supports the University of New Brunswick's mission, vision, and values. • Ability to read and interpret drawings and to work from sketches and diagrams.

Department: Finance & Corporate Services

Reports To: Accounting Manager

Employment Status: Full time, 40 hours per week

At Eastlink, Financial Analysts are driven by curiosity, accuracy, and the opportunity to help the business make informed decisions. By analyzing financial results, identifying trends, and providing meaningful insights, they play an important role in supporting operational performance and business success.

In this role, you'll support a variety of operating departments by providing financial reporting, forecasting, budgeting, and analysis. Working closely with Accounting and business partners, you'll help ensure financial information is accurate, actionable, and supports effective decision-making.

What You’ll Be Doing

As a Financial Analyst, you'll help provide the financial insights that support planning and performance across the organization. Your responsibilities will include:

• Preparing monthly financial reports, variance analysis, and commentary on departmental operating expenses.

• Supporting the development of annual budgets, monthly forecasts, and long-range financial projections.

• Partnering with business leaders to review financial results and forecast assumptions.

• Preparing expense allocations, journal entries, and balance sheet reconciliations.

• Analyzing financial performance, investigating variances, and identifying trends and opportunities.

• Providing reporting and ad hoc analysis to support business and operational decisions.

• Contributing to process improvements that enhance the accuracy and efficiency of financial reporting.

What We’re Looking For

We're looking for someone who enjoys working with numbers, solving problems, and understanding the story behind the financial results. You'll succeed in this role if you:

• Have strong analytical and critical-thinking skills.

• Are detail-oriented and enjoy digging into data to understand variances and trends.

• Can manage multiple priorities and consistently meet deadlines.

• Communicate effectively and build strong working relationships across teams.

• Take initiative and look for opportunities to improve processes and ways of working.

• Are committed to continuous learning and expanding your business knowledge.

You’ll Also Bring

• A Bachelor of Commerce degree with a focus in Accounting.

• Three to five years of experience in an accounting or financial analysis role.

• Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and strong spreadsheet skills.

• Experience preparing financial reports, budgets, forecasts, and account reconciliations.

• Strong organizational, problem-solving, and time management skills.

• Enrollment in a professional accounting designation program is considered an asset.

• A collaborative approach and commitment to contributing to a positive team environment.

About Eastlink

Eastlink is proudly family-owned and headquartered in Halifax, Nova Scotia. After more than 50 years, we’ve grown from a small-town startup into one of Canada’s Best Managed companies without losing our entrepreneurial edge. We move fast. We try new things. We care about doing right by our customers, and we’re not afraid to take a different approach to make that happen.

Why Work with Us

We could say we’re not your typical telecom, but what makes us different is how we operate day to day. At Eastlink, we’re a tight-knit team all working toward common goals. We’re big enough to do meaningful work, but small enough that you can actually make your mark. You won’t get stuck waiting for layers of approval or years of tenure to make an impact! We believe in getting involved, speaking up, and figuring things out together. We’re always listening, learning, and adapting because our customers (and our people) expect us to. And just like we invest in our network, we invest in you, with intention and for the long run.

When you join Eastlink, you'll enjoy:

• Opportunities for internal growth and promotion

• Paid vacation and holidays

• Comprehensive health and dental benefits

• Company pension plan with employer contributions

• Employee discounts on Eastlink products and services

We’re committed to building a workplace where everyone feels they belong. We embrace diversity, inclusion, equity, and accessibility throughout all levels of the organization and encourage members of equity groups to self-identify during the application process. Need an accommodation during the hiring process? We encourage you to reach out and let us know how we can support your participation.

## Newfoundland and Labrador Health Services

Newfoundland and Labrador Health Services (NL Health Services) is the provincial health authority responsible for delivering quality healthcare to more than 550,000 people across Newfoundland and Labrador. Supported by over 23,000 employees and physicians, the organization works collaboratively to improve the health and well-being of every person in every community throughout the province.

Through a broad network of hospitals, health centres, clinics, and community-based services across the Central, Eastern-Rural, Eastern-Urban, Labrador-Grenfell, and Western zones, NL Health Services is committed to providing an accessible, equitable, innovative, and sustainable healthcare system.

NL Health Services is seeking a strategic and collaborative leader to serve as Senior Director, Provincial Budgeting, Sustainability and Data Quality.

This is an exceptional opportunity to provide province-wide financial leadership and advance the organization's commitment to fiscal sustainability, accountability, performance excellence, and data-informed decision-making.

## The Role

Reporting to the Vice President, Corporate Services and Chief Financial Officer, the Senior Director, Provincial Budgeting, Sustainability and Data Quality is a member of the senior leadership team responsible for providing strategic leadership and oversight of provincial budgeting, forecasting, financial planning, performance reporting, sustainability initiatives, and data quality across NL Health Services.

The Senior Director plays a critical role in the preparation, management, and monitoring of the operating budget and the delivery of accurate, timely, and meaningful financial and performance information to Executive Leadership, the Board of Trustees, and the Department of Health and Community Services.

Working collaboratively with senior leaders throughout the province, the Senior Director will support organizational decision-making through robust financial analysis, business intelligence, performance measurement, and strategic resource allocation while helping ensure a sustainable healthcare system for the people of Newfoundland and Labrador.

## Key Accountabilities

## Strategic Leadership

• Provide strategic leadership for provincial budgeting, sustainability, business intelligence, performance measurement, and data quality functions.

• Contribute to enterprise-wide strategic planning and organizational transformation initiatives.

• Partner with Executive Leadership to establish long-term financial strategies and priorities aligned with NL Health Services' mission, vision, and strategic objectives.

• Participate in organizational policy development, planning, and decision-making as a member of the senior leadership team.

## Provincial Budgeting and Financial Planning

• Lead the development, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of the operating budget across the organization.

• Oversee forecasting processes and provide strategic financial advice to Executive Leadership and senior management.

• Support informed decision-making through comprehensive financial analysis, scenario planning, resource modelling, and reporting.

• Ensure budget processes and reporting comply with relevant legislative, governmental, regulatory, and professional accounting requirements.

## Financial Sustainability and Resource Stewardship

• Advance financial sustainability initiatives that support high-quality, patient-centred care.

• Ensure effective stewardship of financial resources through responsible planning, allocation, monitoring, and reporting.

• Support long-term business planning and operational sustainability initiatives.

• Promote evidence-based resource allocation decisions that align with organizational priorities and service delivery requirements.

## Performance Measurement and Business Intelligence

• Lead the development and implementation of performance measurement frameworks, scorecards, dashboards, and key performance indicators.

• Leverage business intelligence tools and organizational data to support decision-making, accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement.

• Provide actionable insights that support clinical, operational, human resource, and financial performance.

• Ensure performance data is meaningful, timely, accurate, and aligned with organizational objectives.

## Data Quality and Corporate Reporting

• Provide leadership for provincial data quality initiatives to strengthen the integrity, consistency, and reliability of organizational information.

• Establish standards, processes, and controls that support high-quality financial and operational reporting.

• Collaborate with clinical, operational, and corporate leaders to ensure the accuracy and integrity of performance information.

• Support enterprise reporting requirements through the delivery of accurate and timely financial and statistical information.

## Continuous Improvement and Integration

• Lead initiatives that standardize and modernize budgeting, reporting, and performance management processes across the province.

• Develop provincial policies, standards, and operating procedures that improve consistency, efficiency, and service quality.

• Identify opportunities for process improvement and innovation through the effective use of technology, data, and analytics.

• Support ongoing health system integration efforts and the establishment of unified provincial services.

## Relationship Management and Communication

• Foster productive partnerships with Executive Leadership, operational leaders, government stakeholders, clinicians, and external partners.

• Develop effective communication strategies to support the dissemination of financial, performance, and organizational information.

• Present complex financial and operational information clearly and effectively to diverse audiences.

## Talent Leadership

• Build and lead a high-performing, diverse, and engaged team.

• Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, inclusion, continuous learning, and employee well-being.

• Support workforce planning, succession planning, leadership development, and performance management.

• Ensure employees have the resources, support, and development opportunities required to succeed.

## Transforming Healthcare Together

Transforming Newfoundland and Labrador's healthcare system is a collective responsibility. As a member of the senior leadership team, the Senior Director will contribute beyond their portfolio and be adaptable to evolving organizational needs and priorities.

All senior leaders share responsibility for fostering a culture of safety, inclusion, collaboration, accountability, and psychological well-being.

## Qualifications

The ideal candidate will possess:

• A Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation or an equivalent combination of education and senior leadership experience.

• A minimum of 5 years of progressive senior leadership experience in budgeting, financial planning, forecasting, business intelligence, performance measurement, reporting, analytics, and organizational strategy.

• Demonstrated experience leading large-scale financial planning and reporting functions within a complex organization

• Experience leading organizational transformation, change management, and continuous improvement initiatives.

• Exceptional leadership, communication, relationship-building, and stakeholder engagement skills.

• Demonstrated ability to think strategically while driving operational excellence and measurable results.

• A commitment to the principles of equity, inclusion, accountability, and public service.

The successful candidate will demonstrate the capabilities described within the LEADS in a Caring Environment Framework, including:

• Lead Self

• Engage Others

• Achieve Results

• Develop Coalitions

• Systems Transformation

## Our Commitment

NL Health Services is committed to fostering a workplace where every employee, patient, and stakeholder feels respected, valued, and included. Diversity strengthens our organization, and we are committed to ensuring equitable opportunities for all applicants.

Accommodation is available throughout the recruitment process. Applicants requiring accommodation to participate in the application, assessment, or interview process are encouraged to recrruitmentservicees@nlhealthservices.ca

## Additional Information

Location: St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador (On-Site)

## How to Apply

To apply, please submit:

Applicants who do not provide the required documentation may not be considered.

For further information regarding this opportunity, please contact recruitmentservices@nlhealthservices.ca in confidence
